closure.note: Statement of record: gate 5 grades the constants the driver PRINTS, not the ones it USES; and the zero branch is tested before the luna88k branch, so BUDGET=0 prints a green row while removing the only work ceiling. THE MAJORITY DESIGN IS REFUTED - shared locals cannot kill an argument-expression mutant, because a local proves what the caller INTENDED to pass, not what the callee RECEIVED. MEASURED EVERYTHING, AND OVERTURNED TWO PROPOSALS. Built the offline driver and proved timer.c CAN be driven in the diff_*.c idiom (one stub: gettimeofday). CENSUS: emulated_hz is an int, so INT_MAX bounds every legitimate request - the ceiling is DERIVED, not picked. POLICY TABLE: 'drop missed ticks' is NOT A POLICY BUT A DEFECT (it caps every timer at 65 Hz - a 100 Hz timer runs at rate 0.65 with no burst at all); the flagship's cap of 65536 BREAKS a legitimate 4e7 Hz timer (1.0000 -> 0.1065); 2^20 is the smallest power of two that leaves every legitimate case BIT-IDENTICAL to shipped. Caught its own first probe (it held time fixed and would have cleared the defect).

REAL - SETTLED. Measured: the :601 split is at 1 MB MEMBLOCK granularity (BITS_PER_MEMBLOCK 20), not the 4 KB page, so it fires on 1 boundary in 256 - a host-bounds guard, never a page guard. THE 'NO PRODUCER CAN STRADDLE' SHARPENING IS REFUTED at four sites: PPC lvx/stvx (16 bytes, NO masking at all), lmw/stmw, lwarx/stwcx, and the ARM arm_pop/bdt slow path (#357 made unaligned bases persist). None is LS_GENERIC_N, so #27's halt does not cover them.

OPTION A+C+D, and it BUILT THE INSTRUMENT rather than judging its feasibility. Compiled an offline differential of memory_rw.c on the first attempt and reproduced the defect immediately -- the key being that memory_rw.c has no PPC/ARM/SH flavour, so compiling with NO family macro excludes the MIPS/M88K/Alpha branches and leaves 4 headers, 3 globals and 6 stubs. Then MEASURED a four-variant table that settled the round: Option B is not a fix (a straddle beginning in a device still returns d0 d0 00 00); A alone SIGSEGVs on a 256 MB access because gcc does NOT turn the tail recursion into a loop at -O2 (~160 B/page); D is free and keeps the memblock split load-bearing. Also found TWO consequences the brief had missed: a straddling WRITE leaves the intended page unmodified and alters an unrelated one, and a faulting tail returned MEMORY_ACCESS_OK -- a missing fault. Verified the live trees untouched afterwards by md5.

OPTION A. Independently designed essentially the same probe and the same fixture, and gave the decisive test for A-vs-B before anyone ran it: a device handler that records (relative_addr, len). Caught that the Alpha offset_mask is 8 KB, so a naive 4096 split would be wrong -- the brief had said '4 KB page' throughout. Also applied R4's constblind finding unprompted: do not assert offset_mask against itself. Shell and git were blocked, so it read rather than ran and said so.
OPTION A composed with D, on the ground that B bypasses the split whenever the first page is a memory-mapped device -- the same failure the measuring seat then reproduced.

OPTION A, naming the device-dispatch failure concretely: a page-crossing access starting on a device-mapped page passes its full length to the handler, which returns before the memblock split is ever reached.

OPTION A with D, and LOOP NOT RECURSION -- it reached the loop conclusion from reading alone, which the measuring seat then confirmed with a stack-span measurement and a SIGSEGV threshold. Stated plainly that it could not read files or run anything.

OPTION B (+C+D) -- THE DISSENT, and it is recorded as such because it was settled by measurement rather than by the 5-to-1 majority. B generalises the existing memblock guard and is by far the smallest diff, which is a real argument; it fails only on the case where the access begins inside a device, which the measuring seat's D1 row then reproduced (d0 d0 00 00 against a correct d0 d0 bb bb). rows.state_note:
*** TWO CORRECTIONS OF MINE, BOTH SERIOUS, FROM THE OPUS PASS-2 SEAT. ***

*** 1. FLOOR CLAUSE (d) WAS BREACHED AND I HAD ARGUED THE WRONG CLAUSE. *** The fix INTRODUCES the predicate `len > remain`, and clause (d) says weaken it to the least-restrictive form that still READS like the same check. **Two such mutants passed all six rows:**
```
  len > OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE ? remain : len     bound relaxed
  remain = inblock ? 1 : OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE   remainder faked
```
Both survived because the section only produced **inblock in {0,511} and len > 512.**

**AND THE UNCOVERED CALLER IS REAL, AND THIS ROUND'S OWN CENSUS HAD NAMED IT:** `bootblock_iso9660.c:281-282` reads **256 bytes** at a `dirofs` snapped only to 2048 (`:275-276`) -- arbitrary mod 512. *The census named the arm and the rows did not cover it.*

**I had argued L1 (*these rows are not vacuous*) and declined a fixture change. That was the WRONG CLAUSE.** This is (d)/L2, which the carrier says to replace IN-ROUND however late it is found. Fixed in-round.

**ONE ROW KILLS BOTH, and the kill is MEASURED, not reasoned:**
```
  arm        short-unaligned row (510+3, want 2)   total
  fixed      ok                                    53 rows, 0 failures
  pristine   FAIL                                  2 failures
  relaxed    FAIL   <- was GREEN before this row   1 failure
  faked      FAIL   <- was GREEN before this row   1 failure
```

*** 2. I MISREAD MY OWN PANEL AND REPORTED IT AS THREE RATIFICATIONS. *** I wrote *'three seats have already said GO/RATIFY/sound'* -- into the brief I then handed a later seat. **The panel was NOT unanimous:** codex **GO WITH CHANGES**; grok **'PRODUCT DIFF IS SOUND; DETECTOR IS NOT DONE'**; minimax **'NO RATIFICATION'**, stated twice; the kimi substitute challenged the severity framing. **Only agy and deepseek ratified.**

> **This is the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape with an extra step, and worse than the usual form: I did not merely fail to read three dissents -- I propagated the misreading into a brief, so a later seat was told the panel agreed.** The seats that said DETECTOR IS NOT DONE were RIGHT, and their finding is exactly the clause-(d) breach above.

*The lesson is the carrier's own, which I quoted at other rows today and did not apply here: **read the BODY of every seat whose verdict merely agrees** -- and, it turns out, of every seat whose verdict I have not actually read at all.*

*** THE L1 QUESTION ON THE GEOMETRY GAP, CONSIDERED AND ANSWERED -- recorded so the next round does not re-argue it. ***

**The case FOR fixing it in-round (L1):** the detector is still UNCOMMITTED, and L1 licenses in-round repair of *the row is part of the deliverable still being built... a row measured vacuous before commit is unfinished, not a reopening*. The tree also carries a MEASURED precedent that single-overlay fixtures are inadequate -- `diff_diskimage_sync.c:570`: *"A SECOND OVERLAY IS WHAT MAKES THE ROW WORK, and it is not decoration... MEASURED: a single-overlay version of this row caught the [nothing]"*. And a second overlay would strengthen EVERY row rather than adding one.

*** THE CASE AGAINST, WHICH WINS: L1 IS ABOUT VACUITY, AND THESE ROWS ARE NOT VACUOUS. *** They have a measured kill table -- they redden on the pre-fix build and on the escaping mutant, and go green on the fix. The vacuity floor asks whether a detector fails on mutants OF THE FIX. **A layer-selection bug is not a mutant of this fix; it is a DIFFERENT DEFECT** that this fixture happens to be unable to see. Calling that L1 would make L1 mean *any adjacent class a detector does not cover*, which is unbounded -- and unbounded in-round strengthening is precisely what `#392` was.

> **DISPOSITION: FILED, with the precedent cited so whoever closes it knows the shape is already proven.** It ranks ABOVE the `lenread` escape among the debts, because a second overlay strengthens the whole section while a short-read row adds one path.

*The distinction worth carrying: an ORACLE gap (the rows cannot see a state they do reach) is closer to vacuity than a FIXTURE gap (the rows never reach the state at all). The first is sometimes L1. The second is coverage, and coverage is filed.*

*** PASS-2, THE KIMI SUBSTITUTE SEAT: no break found, and THREE findings the other seats missed. The ask-again has now paid on every pass. ***

**1. THE SIGNEDNESS SAFETY IS CONDITIONAL, and the condition is the same range invariant that proves termination.** `len > remain ? remain : len` compares a `size_t` against a signed `off_t`, so `remain` converts to unsigned -- **safe ONLY because `remain` is in `[1, BLOCK]`.** So the range proof is not merely about the loop terminating; **it is load-bearing for the comparison itself.** Had `remain` ever been <= 0 the conversion would produce an enormous unsigned value and the clamp would silently stop clamping. *Two independent consequences of one invariant, and only one of them was noticed by the other seats.*

**2. A PROVABLY-EQUIVALENT EDIT THAT IS NOT COVERAGE DEBT:** `buf += lentoread` -> `buf += remain`. On every non-final iteration `len > remain`, so the two are equal; on the final iteration the loop exits before `buf` is read again. **Undetectable AND harmless** -- correctly classified as an equivalent mutant rather than an escape, which is a distinction this project has had to make before (`#449`'s guard-only widening measured EQUIVALENT).

*** 3. A THIRD ESCAPE CLASS, AND IT IS ABOUT MY DETECTOR'S GEOMETRY RATHER THAN ITS ORACLE: *** a plausible 'optimization' that starts iteration k's overlay scan from iteration k-1's `overlay_nr` **passes every row I wrote** -- because my fixture pins exactly ONE geometry: a single overlay with only block 0 marked. With one overlay there is no layer ORDER to get wrong.

> **That is a different kind of debt from the `lenread` escape.** That one is an oracle gap on an unexercised PATH (short reads). This is a FIXTURE gap -- the rows cannot distinguish layer-selection bugs because the fixture has only one layer to select. **A second overlay, with a different block marked, closes it** -- and the tree already knows this shape: `diff_diskimage_sync.c:570` says *'A SECOND OVERLAY IS WHAT MAKES THE ROW WORK, and it is not decoration.'*

**FILED, not fixed** -- same reasoning as the `lenread` escape: not a floor breach, not a measured false pass against a shipped claim. **But it is the more valuable of the two to close**, because a second overlay would strengthen every row rather than adding one.

*Fair criticism of my brief that I accept: the seat noted rows 3-5 were not inlined, so its answer to 'smallest wrong edit' had to reason from two rows rather than five. **A pass-2 brief should inline the DETECTOR, not just the product diff** -- the same inline-every-fact rule the carrier already states for packet-fed seats, applied to the artifact under review.*

*** PASS-2 COVERAGE DEBT, FILED NOT FIXED (the stopping rule): a ONE-IDENTIFIER mutant escapes all five rows. ***

**The mutant (deepseek, pass 2): `buf += lentoread;` -> `buf += lenread;`.**

`lenread` is what `fread` actually RETURNED; `lentoread` is what was REQUESTED. **In every path the five rows exercise they are identical**, so the whole detector stays green. They diverge only on a SHORT READ, where `buf` would advance by less than `len` was decremented -- desynchronising the buffer from the offset for every later iteration.

**WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT FIXED IN-ROUND, stated so nobody re-argues it:**
  * it is **not a floor breach** -- but the ground I first gave was CIRCULAR and is corrected here. I wrote *'it nulls nothing in any path the rows reach'*, which **every escape satisfies by definition**, including `#462`'s M11 that was ruled a floor breach. *A wrong reason gets reused.* **The correct, checkable ground:** outside a short read `lenread == lentoread` is an IDENTITY, so the swap preserves the repair across the entire defect class this round closes; it diverges only in the short-read state, which the contract excludes -- and which is **not silent**, because the pre-existing `INCOMPLETE READ` `fatal()` announces it.
  * it is **not a measured false pass** against a shipped claim, and not a wrong record. The stopping rule files everything else, and `#392` is what happens when it does not.
  * it lands squarely on the **short-read path this round already declared out of scope and pre-existing** -- so it is the same debt seen from the mutant side rather than a new one.

**What would close it:** a row that forces a short read in a NON-FINAL iteration -- an overlay data file truncated mid-range -- and asserts the bytes land at the right offsets afterwards. That row would also cover the pre-existing zero-fill concern, so **one row discharges both**.

*Two seats, two different answers to the same question, and the sharper one won: another seat answered that the smallest passing edit is an INLINED equivalent of the same arithmetic -- true, but behaviourally identical, so it is readability debt rather than coverage debt. **The ask-again is worth the invocation precisely because seats differ on what counts as an escape.***

*** #472 IN FLIGHT 2026-08-27: REPRODUCED, FIXED, AND MEASURED -- pass 2 running, nothing committed yet. ***

**TEST-FIRST, on the committed build, before any edit:**
```
  ok    [LIVE] aligned read of block 0 is all overlay        = 512
  ok    [LIVE] aligned read of block 1 is all base           = 512
  FAIL  overlay unaligned: wrong-layer bytes in 1024 @ 511   = 512, want 1
  ok    overlay unaligned: reports SUCCESS despite corruption = 1
```
Exactly ONE real failure, both liveness controls green, on the PREDICTED numbers. The last row is the silent-corruption evidence: it returns success while handing back wrong bytes.

*** THE KILL TABLE, and pass 1 is why the second row exists: ***
```
  arm                        wrong-layer row      never-wrote row
  PRISTINE (committed)       FAIL 512, want 1     ok 0
  MUTANT   (clamp only)      ok 1  <- ESCAPES     FAIL 511, want 0
  FIXED    (clamp + stride)  ok 1                 ok 0
```
**Two seats independently named that mutant** -- clamp the length, keep the fixed stride. Under it the wrong-layer row reads 1, **which is the CORRECT answer**, because the buffer receives HOLES rather than wrong bytes. The rows are measurably non-redundant.

*Measured in a COPIED tree, so no repo file was ever mutated and no sentinel was needed.*

**THE FIX:** clamp `lentoread` to the current block's remainder; advance `buf` by what was consumed. Same shape as `diskimage_access__cue()` in the same file.

**A seat supplied the algebra I had not derived:** `curofs + remain` **is** `(curofs | (OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE-1)) + 1`, identically -- so the clamp is *provably consistent* with the loop's existing advance rather than merely compatible with it.

*** THREE THINGS CAUGHT ME, ALL BY GUARDS: ***
  1. **`buf += OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE` appears TWICE.** The other is in `fwrite_helper`, where the fixed stride is CORRECT because that path refuses unaligned access. **Patching the first occurrence would have broken the write path**; the anchor-count guard stopped it.
  2. **I reformatted 6 lines I never touched** -- a whitespace pass removed 7 trailing-tab lines when I had introduced 1. Reverted and re-applied; the diff is now 17+/3- with `-w` giving an identical stat.
  3. **The mutant script's anchor went to 0 after the fix landed** and said so, rather than silently patching nothing.

**Post-fix:** `52 rows, 0 failures, DISKIMAGE_IO_PASS`. All 11 offline differentials green. Twin trees and ALL THREE build trees byte-identical (an earlier draft said 'both' and was MEASURED FALSE -- it forgot the WSL arc tree, which was stale).

**FILED, NOT FIXED:** the short-read path is unchanged -- on a short read in a non-final iteration `len` decrements by the requested amount while `totallenread` grows by the actual, so the caller's zero-fill can cover the wrong region. Pre-existing; the patch neither helps nor worsens it.

*** CONFIRMED 2026-08-27 by an adversarial opus pass that tried to break all four steps and could not. Three refinements, and the first is a REAL NARROWING I had missed. ***

**PRECONDITION: the defect requires `d->nr_of_overlays > 0`.** With no overlay the function takes a fast path (`:1347`) that is a single `fseek`+`fread` and is correct. My record did not state this. **It is not a get-out:** overlays come from the `V` prefix (`:1810`) and from `R:` (`:2095`), and `R:` is routine in this project's own rigs (`gate_ab.sh:82` uses `LUNA_IMG="R:..."`, and `drive_guest.py` and several probes do the same).

**UNALIGNED OFFSETS ARE GUEST-REACHABLE, with a census rather than an example:**
  * `promemul/dec_prom.c:167-170` -> `:148` -- `lseek` stores an arbitrary 64-bit guest value as `current_file_offset`; `read()` passes it straight through with a guest length up to 64 MB. **Gives both faults.**
  * `promemul/arcbios.c:1923` -> `:1761` -- ARC `Seek` stores an arbitrary 64-bit offset from guest memory; `Read` uses it with a length up to 64 MB. **Gives both faults.**
  * `diskimage_scsicmd.c:725`/`:830` -- variable-length tape READ via `tape_offset`.
  * `bootblock_iso9660.c:271-282` -- unaligned, but a fixed 256-byte length means one iteration, so **wrong-layer only**, no misalignment.

*** THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE IS AN ASYMMETRY I HAD NOT LOOKED FOR: THE WRITE SIDE HAS THE GUARD THE READ SIDE LACKS. *** `fwrite_helper` explicitly refuses a non-multiple length (`:1273-1280`) and an unaligned offset (`:1281-1286`), both returning 0, both under `#164`. `fread_helper` has **no such guard anywhere**. The read path was simply never given the check the write path was.

**THE MECHANISM IS SHARPER THAN I STATED, in a way that matters for the detector:** iteration 1 is **positionally CORRECT** (`buf[k] = file[offset+k]`); its only fault is the LAYER. The positional corruption begins at iteration 2 and is caused by the fixed `buf += OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE` stride paired with a variable-start read. **So the two halves have different trigger conditions:** wrong-layer needs only an unaligned offset; duplication additionally needs `len > 512 - (offset & 511)`. A detector must cover both.

**AND IT IS NOT A MEMORY-SAFETY ISSUE, which was checked explicitly:** `buf` advances 512 only when `lentoread == 512`, and any short `lentoread` zeroes `len` and ends the loop; `len` cannot underflow. **Silent wrong data, no overrun.**

**The cue idiom is confirmed as the fix template** (`:1091-1144`): `chunk = CDROM_SECTOR_SIZE - intra; if (chunk > len) chunk = len;` with `buf + total_copied`. It clamps to bytes-remaining-in-sector AND indexes the buffer by bytes actually delivered -- **both halves of what the overlay loop lacks.**

**ADJACENT, not claimed by this row:** on a short read the loop does `len -= lentoread` while `totallenread += lenread`, so a short read in a NON-FINAL iteration makes the caller's `memset(buf + lendone, ...)` zero the wrong region. Worth a row of its own if this is worked.

*Honest limit the seat stated and I keep: no rig was measured actually issuing an unaligned >512-byte read against an overlaid disk. Reachability is READ, not MEASURED.*

*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, GUEST-REACHABLE, AND IT CORRUPTS READ DATA. The most severe bare-title row worked so far. Verified by reading the loop; the mechanism is worse than the title says. ***

`src/disk/diskimage.c:1358-1402`, the overlay read loop:

```c
for (curofs=offset; len != 0;
    curofs = (curofs | (OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE-1)) + 1) {
        for (overlay_nr = d->nr_of_overlays-1; overlay_nr >= 0; overlay_nr --)
                if (overlay_has_block(d, overlay_nr, curofs))   /* layer chosen for THIS block */
                        break;

        lentoread = len > OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE? OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE : len;   /* NOT clamped to the
                                                       block's REMAINDER */
        ... fread(buf, 1, lentoread, <chosen layer>) ...

        len -= lentoread;
        buf += OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE;          /* fixed stride */
}
```

**`lentoread` is clamped to the BLOCK SIZE, never to the bytes left in the CURRENT block.** So when `offset` is not block-aligned, the loop picks a layer for the block containing `curofs` and then reads up to a full block from it -- **running past that block's end into the next one or two blocks, which may live in a different layer.**

**Worked example, offset 511, len 1024** (`OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE` = 512):
  * iteration 1: `curofs = 511` -> layer chosen for **block 0**; `lentoread = 512`; reads file offsets **511-1022** into `buf[0..511]`.
  * `curofs = (511 | 511) + 1 = 512`; `buf += 512`.
  * iteration 2: layer chosen for **block 1**; reads file offsets **512-1023** into `buf[512..1023]`.

**The guest asked for offsets 511-1534 and receives: wrong-layer bytes in the first half, and file offsets 512-1022 DUPLICATED at two different buffer positions.** The tail it asked for (1023-1534) is never read at all. This is silent read corruption, not a refusal.

*** THE LOOP'S OWN ADVANCE EXPRESSION PROVES UNALIGNED OFFSETS WERE ANTICIPATED, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS AN OVERSIGHT AND NOT AN UNDOCUMENTED PRECONDITION. *** `curofs = (curofs | (OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE-1)) + 1` rounds UP to the next block boundary. If `offset` were always block-aligned that expression would simply be `curofs + OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE`. **The author wrote alignment-handling into the advance and omitted it from the length.**

**GUEST-REACHABLE** (seat's sequence, structurally consistent with the code, which carries no alignment guard anywhere): an overlaid ARC disk, guest writes blocks 0 and 2 so they land in different layers, then a byte-granular `Seek(511)` + `Read(1024)`. ARC exposes byte-granular seek/read, so the unaligned offset reaches this loop. **Not verified by execution -- needs a build.**

**Observable for a detector:** the guest-visible read payload. Write distinct sentinel bytes into blocks that land in different layers, then read across the boundary from an unaligned offset; broken returns the wrong layer's sentinel and a duplicated range, fixed returns the requested bytes in order.

*** THE FIX IDIOM IS ALREADY IN THIS FILE. *** `diskimage_access__cue()` (`:1083`) does exactly the right thing for the same shape of problem -- it clamps each step to the remainder of the current sector and writes at `buf + total_copied` rather than on a fixed stride (see its `memset(buf + total_copied, 0, chunk)` at the same offset discipline). **Transferred warrant: clamp `lentoread` to the current block's remainder, and advance `buf` by the amount actually consumed rather than by a constant.**

**A SECOND, SEPARABLE HALF reported by the seat and NOT verified here:** a short `fread` on the flat (non-overlay) path is said to return zero even after reading bytes, causing the caller to zero the whole requested buffer. Recorded as the seat's claim; check it before it rides along with the fix, because a row covering two defects buries one when the other closes.



*** THE SENTENCE ABOVE PREDICTED THAT ONE ROT-PACKET RUN 'reds `stale quiet` and discharges
BOTH'.  THE RUN HAPPENED AND REFUTED THE SECOND HALF.  Corrected 2026-08-29. ***

`regress/artifacts/gdromexitsix/rot_20260829/` -- post-fix binary, one-line frozen-probe edit
(packed format byte 0x20 -> 0x21):

    base.log   GDROM_DEF_RESULT=60/60    stale quiet  0 vs 0      ok
    rot.log    GDROM_DEF_RESULT=59/60    stale quiet  1 vs 0    **FAIL**

The two `GDROM_DEF_VECTOR` lines differ in EXACTLY ONE POSITION -- discriminating, not merely
disruptive, and proven by the probe's own vector rather than asserted.

**`stale quiet` is DISCHARGED.  `stale how` is NOT**, and structurally cannot be by a rotted
packet: the fix DECLINES rather than dying, so the session still exits cleanly.  Worse, it is
the WANTED-EQUALS-FAILURE shape -- the row wants `exit0` and a BROKEN `how` capture also
yields `exit0` -- so only a measured red separates a working oracle from an inert one.  It
needs a mutant that exits AFTER the last budget check.  **Treat it as UNPROVEN until then.**

*Found by a supplementary pass-2 seat applying the grep-for-siblings rule: the same predicted
sentence sat in the probe comment AND here, and the measurement refuted both at once.*

is `diskimage__return_check_condition(xferp, d, 0x05, 0x20, 0x00)` PLUS the fall-through
`return 1` -- the file's own refusal idiom at four shipped sites.**  Every claim below was
re-verified by me against the source before recording.

*** MY CENSUS WAS CONTAMINATED AND SO IS THE ROW'S.  Both counted the COMMENT HEADER and the
DEFINITION as calls. ***

    grep -c 'diskimage__return_default_status_and_message'          -> 25   raw
    grep -c 'diskimage__return_default_status_and_message(xferp'    -> 23   CALLS
    grep -c 'diskimage__return_check_condition'                     ->  5   raw
    grep -c 'diskimage__return_check_condition(xferp'               ->  3   CALLS
    grep -c $'^\tcase '                                             -> 22   top-level labels

So **the row's "the only one of 25" is wrong under ANY unit** -- 25 is the contaminated raw
count.  The correct statement is **"the only one of 20 TOP-LEVEL ARMS"** (22 labels forming
19 bodies, since MODE_SENSE/10, READ/READ_10 and WRITE/WRITE_10 share bodies, plus the
default).  My own `~30` counted NESTED labels.  *A re-deriver caution worth keeping: 
`grep -E '^\tcase'` silently matches NOTHING, because `\t` is a literal `t` in ERE -- use
`$'\t'`.  I hit that exact trap on this file earlier today.*

**THE STRUCTURAL CLAIM SURVIVES, verified arm by arm**: all 19 bodies call the status helper
on every completing path.  ONE QUALIFIER: at PATH level the two `return 2` first passes also
set no status -- correctly, because the command is incomplete and the DATA_OUT re-entry sets
it, and all three SCSI controllers re-call.  My return enumeration was exact.

  * **`dev_osiop.c:500-505`** -- `res == 0` sets **`d->scripts_running = 0`**.  A guest
    probing one unsupported opcode **kills its own SCRIPTS engine**; no status phase ever.
  * **`dev_asc.c:1395-1400`** -- `ok == 0` gives `STATE_DISCONNECTED` + `NCRINTR_DIS`.  The
    guest sees a target DISCONNECT instead of CHECK CONDITION: retry/reset instead of
    REQUEST SENSE.  **This also refutes the row's own state_note, which says asc does not
    test for 0 at all** -- its select path does.
  * **`dev_wdc.c:1528-1541`** -- the `res == 0` arm sets **no error bit**, and `status_byte()`

> structural one, and it is the form a future round should cite.

**THE FIX, WITH ITS WARRANT:** CHECK-CONDITION-then-`return 1` is ALREADY this file's refusal
idiom at four shipped sites, and all four controllers demonstrably handle it today.  `d` is
non-NULL in the default arm (the NULL path returned earlier).  #417's latch semantics come
free: REQUEST SENSE reads `d->sense_key/asc/ascq` and the next success retires them.
*The state_note's cited precedent is the WRONG one -- that shape exists only because `d` is
NULL there and `check_condition` would dereference it; its own comments say `// ?` and `TODO`.*

DATA_IN phase off `data_in != NULL`, and status-only completion is already TEST_UNIT_READY's
shape; (b) leave the pre-switch not-connected `return 0` alone; (c) `est/` byte-identical
propagation, shared file; (d) **the fix ALSO cures `mb89352halt`'s mechanism** -- `status_len`
becomes 1, so the PH_STAT read no longer trips 'read longer than buffer?' into
`cpu->running = 0`, consistent with the standing ONE-ROUND-for-both ruling.

*** THE ATAPI ROUTE IS REAL AND IS THE **WRONG WITNESS CHANNEL**, which inverts what I
assumed when I raised it. ***  `dev_wdc.c:1515` does feed packet commands in, and `res == 1`
with no data gives PHASE_COMPLETED and no error bit.  **But `atapi_st->status` is read
NOWHERE in dev_wdc.c** -- so an ATAPI witness stays RED after a dispatcher-only fix, because
it witnesses the COMBINED dispatcher+wdc defect.  The discriminating channels for THIS fix
are **asc** (ICCS fifo byte 0x00 -> 0x02, pmax rig) or **mb89352** (loudest pre-fix symptom
on record: the emulated CPU stops).  The wdc consumer repair is its own hunk in a different
file and should be filed separately -- the one-omission-in-one-shared-function warrant does
not stretch to it.

but UNMEASURED: MMC opcodes 0x46 (GET CONFIGURATION) and 0x4A (GET EVENT STATUS NOTIFICATION)
are not among the 19 arms and period ATAPI attach code issues them routinely -- one flagged
boot would settle it.

**FILED, NOT FIXED (a sibling this round does not touch):** `SPACE`'s NESTED `default:`
`fatal()`s and then FALLS THROUGH to the status helper, **telling the guest GOOD for an

*** L4 WRONG RECORD, CORRECTED IN PLACE 2026-08-27. An adversarial opus pass REFUTED THE MECHANISM THIS ROW STATED BELOW. The defect is real; my explanation of it was false, and the true picture is four different wrong outcomes rather than one. ***

**WHAT I GOT WRONG.** I wrote that `scsi_transfer_alloc()`'s `memset(p, 0, ...)` leaves a status BYTE of 0x00, which the guest reads as GOOD. **`status` is `unsigned char *` (`diskimage.h:196-197`)** -- so the memset leaves `status == NULL` and `status_len == 0`. **There is no zeroed status byte anywhere.** Nothing reads a 0x00 out of that struct. The conclusion happened to hold for one controller, for an entirely different reason.

**WHAT SURVIVES, and it is the structural half:** the `default:` arm is the **only one of 25** that never calls `diskimage__return_default_status_and_message()` or `diskimage__return_check_condition()` -- verified by grepping every case/helper pair -- and it falls through to `return 1`, which the function's own header (`:263-266`) documents as the success token (`2` = expects DATA_OUT, `1` = otherwise ok, `0` = error).

*** THE HONEST STATEMENT: ONE OMISSION, FOUR DIFFERENT WRONG OUTCOMES. ***
  * **`dev_asc.c` -- guest IS told GOOD**, but via an explicit `else fifo_write(0x00)` fallback at `:1284-1292`, which `git log -S` places in the unmodified upstream 0.7.0 import, NOT a fork change. Right conclusion, wrong reason.
  * **`dev_mb89352.c` -- REFUTES the 'told success' claim outright.** `data_in == NULL` sets `phase = PH_STAT` (`:284`); the guest's PH_STAT read takes `p = status (NULL), len = 0`, trips the `read longer than buffer?` arm (`:173`) and **sets `cpu->running = 0`**. The guest is not told anything -- the emulated CPU is STOPPED. **Filed separately as [[mb89352halt]].**
  * **`dev_osiop.c:573-582`** -- `while (... && i < status_len)` with `status_len == 0` writes **no status byte at all**; the guest's destination memory keeps its prior contents.
  * **`dev_wdc.c` (ATAPI)** -- `atapi_st->status` is read nowhere in the file; `res == 1` with `data_in == NULL` gives `PHASE_COMPLETED` with `WDCS_ERR` unset: a successful packet command.

> **That is a BETTER case than the row originally made, not a weaker one** -- a single omitted completion step producing four distinct wrong behaviours across four controllers. But it is not the claim as written, and the claim as written was the one being ranked.

**A SECOND CONSEQUENCE THE ORIGINAL RECORD MISSED:** the helper also RETIRES LATCHED SENSE (the `#417` fix, `:187-188`). The `default:` arm skips that too -- so an unimplemented command following a failed one leaves `sense_key/asc/ascq` latched, and a follow-up REQUEST SENSE attributes the OLD failure to the command that just ran. That is exactly the regression `#417` was written to remove, reachable by a different door.

**FIX SHAPE, now pinned by the in-tree idiom at `:319-327`:** call the helper, set `status[0] = 0x02` (CHECK CONDITION), then `return 0`. Note `return 0` is **distinguishable on only two of four controllers** -- osiop stops the SCRIPTS engine, wdc completes with a latched warning, while asc and mb89352 do not test for 0 at all -- so the status buffer, not the return value, is what carries the refusal.

--- the original record follows, kept so the correction is checkable ---

*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, GUEST-REACHABLE, and the highest-severity bare-title row worked so far. Established by reading; the fix idiom ALREADY EXISTS in this file. ***

`src/disk/diskimage_scsicmd.c:1380-1388`, the dispatcher's `default:` arm:

```c
default:
        debug("[ UNIMPLEMENTED SCSI command 0x%02x, disk id=%i", xferp->cmd[0], id);
        // exit(1);
}
debug(" ]");
return 1;
```

**Three things go wrong together:**
1. it logs through `debug()`, which is verbosity-gated and normally invisible;
2. **it never calls `diskimage__return_default_status_and_message()`** -- every implemented arm does (`:1212`, `:1257`, `:1298`, `:1340`, `:1347`, `:1376`);
3. it falls through to **`return 1`, the same value a SUCCESSFUL command returns.**

**And the status the guest reads is GOOD, which was checked rather than assumed:** `scsi_transfer_alloc()` ends with `memset(p, 0, sizeof(struct scsi_transfer))` (`diskimage_scsicmd.c:89`), and `dev_asc.c:326-330` frees and reallocates per command. Status 0x00 IS GOOD. **So an unsupported opcode is reported to the guest as a completed, successful command.**

*** THE COMMENTED-OUT `exit(1)` IS THE TELL. *** This site was de-fatalised by commenting out the kill, which removed the death without adding an error path -- the incomplete form of the de-fatalisation this fork otherwise does carefully.

*** THE FIX HAS A TRANSFERRED WARRANT ALREADY IN THIS FILE, found by grepping the tree for the existing idiom rather than reasoning from scratch. *** `diskimage__return_check_condition()` is defined at `:208` and already used for exactly this class at `:823-824` -- `0x05, 0x21`, ILLEGAL REQUEST -- and again at `:909`. **The correct refusal for an unknown opcode is CHECK CONDITION with ILLEGAL REQUEST / INVALID COMMAND OPERATION CODE, and the helper to do it sits three hundred lines above the defect.**

**NOT FIXED: needs a build.** The detector must show the pre-fix build reporting GOOD for an unsupported opcode and CHECK CONDITION after -- and floor clause (b) needs the `return 1` reinstated verbatim. Both are measurements. Queued behind the embargo.

*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: THE TITLE'S PREMISE IS MIS-STATED AND THE UNDERLYING DEFECT IS REAL AND WORSE THAN EITHER THE TITLE OR THE SEAT DESCRIBED. It is a MISSING `else`. ***

The title blames *wrap-around*. A farmed seat checked that premise -- as the brief asked -- and refuted it: ordinary periodic wrap is handled. **But it confirmed the mechanism, and reading the code shows a sharper defect than the one it named.**

`src/cpus/cpu_mips_coproc.c:796-819`:

```c
int32_t compare_diff = tmp - cp->reg[COP0_COMPARE];
double hz;

if (compare_diff < 0)
        hz = tmp - cp->reg[COP0_COUNT];        /* (A) */

if (compare_diff == 0)                         /* SEPARATE statement */
        hz = 0;                                /* (B) */
else
        hz = (double)emulated_hz / (double)compare_diff;   /* (C) */
```

**(A) IS AN UNCONDITIONALLY DEAD STORE.** The `if/else` at (B)/(C) is a separate statement, and both its arms assign `hz` -- so whatever (A) wrote is always overwritten. When `compare_diff < 0`, (C) runs and yields a **NEGATIVE** `hz`; `if (hz > 0)` at `:812` is then false and **the timer is neither created nor updated**.

**The three cases, exhaustively:**
  * `compare_diff > 0` -- (C) gives a positive rate; timer set. **The only working path.**
  * `compare_diff == 0` -- (B) gives 0; `hz > 0` false; nothing set.
  * `compare_diff < 0` -- (A) computed the intended value and (C) throws it away for a negative one; `hz > 0` false; nothing set.

**Consequence, which is what the title was reaching for:** if the timer was never created it stays NULL, so **no timer interrupt is ever delivered again**; if it already existed it keeps its stale rate. Either way a guest write that ought to reprogram the timer silently does nothing.

*** THE DEAD STORE IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING, because it shows INTENT. *** The author wrote handling for `compare_diff < 0` and it has never executed. This is not a design choice being second-guessed -- it is a chain of `if`s that lost its `else`, and (A) is the evidence.

The seat argued pmax is nonetheless dormant because its default R3000 is `EXC3K`, citing `cpu_dyntrans.c` -- **a file not read here, so this is recorded as the seat's claim, not as verified.** Settle it before ranking this row.
  * the seat named `algor` (RM5200/EXC4K, `machine_algor.c:49`) as directly reachable. Also unverified here.

* Q3 DO NOT sync d->f under overlays, and it is worse than pointless: diskimage.c:1984 opens d->f in mode r whenever prefix_R is set while :1971 sets writable=1, so R: -- WHAT BOTH RIGS USE -- gives a writable disk whose base handle is READ-ONLY, and the temp overlay is already unlinked. fflush on a read-mode stream is UB in C99 7.21.5.2p2; fsync on O_RDONLY is rc=0 on glibc but UNKNOWN on NetBSD/OpenBSD/Solaris, where it would turn every R:/CD-ROM sync into a spurious MEDIUM ERROR. Plus 14.34 ms to fsync a 512 MB untouched file on drvfs.

It BUILT that state and drove the shipping read path: the guest reads 0x00 from the overlay's HOLE and the base's good 0xBB bytes are GONE -- silent corruption of data the guest never touched, reported as a successful read. It does NOT fall through to the base. Honest counterweight: NOT reproducible in the current write path (BIT_SET_BUT_DATA_MISSING=0 across n=1..129; the per-block fseeks keep them in lockstep), so it is a hole the FIX would INTRODUCE, not a live defect; (iii) directory-entry durability CHECKED AND NOT A HOLE -- user overlays open r+ and must pre-exist, and the only created file is the unlinked temp overlay. *** ADJUDICATED 2026-08-27 (fable): the collapse onto [[b120]] is CONFIRMED **MEASURED**, but it is a collapse of the SAFETY HALF ONLY -- do NOT read it as 'drop ovsync'. ***

b120's fix makes opcode 0x91 an honest CHECK CONDITION. **It does not implement SYNCHRONIZE CACHE(16), so it does not make the flush happen.** That residual -- implement 0x91, or formally decline it -- is NOT covered by b120 and is what this row should carry from now on.

So: keep this row OPEN and NARROWED to the implement-or-decline question. The false-success danger is b120's; the missing flush is this row's.

*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, BUT NARROWER THAN THE TITLE -- and the live half turns out to be AN INSTANCE OF [[b120]], which neither row could show on its own. ***

**HALF THAT IS ALREADY FIXED:** SYNCHRONIZE CACHE(10) is `SCSICMD_SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE = 0x35` (`diskimage.h:254`), handled at `diskimage_scsicmd.c:915`, and it **does** flush -- `:932` calls `diskimage_sync(d)`, with `:925` recording that this was the TODO carried out. *So the title, read as covering all synchronize-cache commands, is FALSE for the one the tree implements.*

*** THE LIVE HALF, AND ITS DIAGNOSIS: SYNCHRONIZE CACHE(16) IS OPCODE `0x91`, AND `0x91` APPEARS **ZERO** TIMES IN THE DISPATCHER. *** It therefore falls into the `default:` arm at `:1380` -- which logs through a verbosity-gated call, never sets a status, and returns the same value a successful command returns. **The guest asks for a cache flush, is told GOOD, and nothing is flushed.**

> **SO THIS IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT DEFECT: IT IS [[b120]] WEARING A SPECIFIC OPCODE.** `b120`'s fix -- refuse an unknown opcode with CHECK CONDITION / ILLEGAL REQUEST via the existing `diskimage__return_check_condition()` helper -- would convert this from a SILENT FALSE SUCCESS into an honest refusal, letting a guest fall back to CACHE(10). **A full `ovsync` fix additionally implements `0x91`**; the two are separable and should be ranked separately.

**Rank `b120` first.** It is the general case, it is cheaper, and it makes this row's damage visible instead of silent. Implementing `0x91` without fixing `b120` would close one opcode and leave every other unimplemented one lying about success.

*Method note: the seat reported the CACHE(10)/CACHE(16) split and the existing `diskimage_sync()` idiom; the `0x91`-falls-to-default connection was found here by grepping the dispatcher for the opcode and getting zero hits. **A count of zero was the whole finding** -- and it is only evidence because the denominator was checked: the file really does dispatch by opcode, and `0x35` is present in the same census.*



**RESIDUAL-REMAINS.**  `4d0981d` fixed CACHE(10) -- data and bitmap now get ordered flush/sync with
failure reporting.  **CACHE(16) is still unimplemented** and falls through the generic default,
which neither flushes nor explicitly refuses it.

*And a founding overstatement corrected: the row asserted the base was ALREADY flushed pre-fix.  It
used `fsync()` without the stdio `fflush()`, which is not the same claim.*

closure.note: The root behind the n1 and n2 class: the MIPS compare write converts the distance to a deadline into a frequency, so a deadline one cycle away is read as a request for 40 million interrupts a second. The clamp in round A limits the damage; this item is the model itself. Filed, not fixed in this batch.

entries.note: REAL AS A SHAPE, CORRECTLY FILED AS DESIGN, AND NOT WORTH A ROUND -- close as a standing note. timer.h:84 timer_add(double freq,...) has NO one-shot form at all; footbridge reads a FREERUN/PERIODIC bit (dc21285reg.h:365-366) and ignores it, reload_timer_value (:224-248) always installs a repeating timer, and the TIMER_1_CLEAR distinction at :590 is a no-op because timer_update_frequency early-outs on an unchanged freq (timer.c:204). The author's own comment at :250-256 admits it. BUT THE DANGEROUS HALF IS ALREADY FIXED (#427's timer_clamp_freq turned the guest-writable zero divisor -> +INF -> 0.0 interval -> in-handler hang into a bounded rate), so what remains is pure fidelity. AND IT HAS NO WITNESS OF EITHER KIND: none of the four bootable rigs (pmax, arc, luna88k, landisk) instantiates an ISA bus or a footbridge. entries.ev: codex 5.6-SOL xhigh, fired against the row's own hold_question (_scratchpad/holdq_briefs/holdq_dfreq.md; answer at scratchpad/holdq_out/dfreq.txt)
entries.note: *** VERDICT: THE DEFECT IS REAL, BUT THE CITED WITNESS DOES NOT WITNESS IT -- AND THE ROW IS INTERNALLY CONFLATED. DOCUMENTED-ONLY/CLOSE under the stopping rule. *** EVERY ELEMENT RE-VERIFIED HERE BEFORE IT WAS ACTED ON, because this answer was used to correct the carrier: the row's `witness` field is None; its closure names 'the MIPS compare write ... converts the distance to a deadline into a frequency'; the row mentions ARM Footbridge four times and MIPS CP0 zero times; and `footbridge_sites_probe.py:111` execs `-E cats`, an ARM/SA110 machine that executes no MIPS instruction and cannot reach CP0 Compare. That probe returned entirely CORRECT values (vendor 0x1011; 0x00345678 after storing 0x12345678 -- the missing byte is the Footbridge's deliberate 24-bit mask signature, not an error). Its cited `dev_footbridge.c:548` is stale: :548 is `console_putchar` and the timer mask is at :640. **So a witness WAS built, and it witnesses a different path from the one this row's closure defines.** THE MIPS MECHANISM IS SOURCE-DEMONSTRABLE AND WORSE THAN 'a different internal representation': a Compare write installs a PERIODIC host timer (`cpu_mips_coproc.c:796`), every expiry increments `compare_interrupts_pending` (:418), and a guest Compare write acknowledges only ONE pending event while clearing Cause.IP7 (:822). If two or more callbacks have accumulated, the next dyntrans update re-asserts IP7 before any new Count==Compare event -- **a wrong guest-readable Cause value and an extra interrupt exception**, not an observationally equivalent model. IT ALSO KEPT THE EVIDENCE LADDER HONEST: the ~615,384-callbacks-per-signal figure came from a timer-core SCRATCH probe, not an end-to-end MIPS guest observation; and the 40.2-second guest clock freeze that was measured belongs to the separate `fbpending` overflow defect, whose #442 bound is in today's source. Neither witnesses MIPS `dfreq`. *** CONSEQUENCE ACTED ON: CLAUDE.md's line 'dfreq's [no-witness claim] was measured false by building the witness in one session' is a WRONG RECORD and was corrected in both carrier copies. The RULE -- that 'no witness of either kind' is checkable and must be checked -- is untouched and remains one of the most useful lines in the file. ***

rows.hold_question: A one-shot deadline is modelled as a repeating rate. The hold says 'a design change, per the stopping rule'. QUESTION: is there a GUEST-OBSERVABLE consequence that makes this a defect rather than a modelling difference? This matters because the carrier records that dfreq's earlier 'no witness of either kind' claim was MEASURED FALSE -- a witness was built in one session. So: what does that witness actually show, and does it show a wrong VALUE reaching the guest or only a different internal representation? If only the latter, documented-only is the honest disposition and the row should say so.

rows.title: strad  The budget straddle cannot see three mutant shapes (named, not implied)
rows.hold: FILE: the detector's honest limits, measured

closure.note: Measured during R3's review, and recorded so the record does not read as fuller coverage than exists. The straddle does NOT catch: (1) a mutant that scales BOTH the print and the comparison - only the literal config-pin row catches that, which is why both row kinds stay; (2) an in-body change to STALL or BACKSTOP, because nothing straddles either and the under-leg accepts BACKSTOP as a stated reason; (3) `>` changed to `>=` at the comparison, which scores zero red rows. An in-body budget change is caught only to within one instruction. Closing (2) needs a stall/backstop straddle of the same shape.  closure.by normalised 2026-08-25 from 'opus' to 'opus5' -- the ledger's declared roster has opus5 and no 'opus'; a one-row spelling variant that every non-empty check passes.

rows.title: gateflr  If a whole gate block is deleted, nothing outside it notices
rows.hold: FILE: measured during the R1+R2 regression review

closure.note: Found by the flagship while reviewing the R1 and R2 regression evidence. The new gate-2 block guards itself: its floors, its named-row greps and its positive control are all INSIDE the block. Delete the block and every one of those guards disappears with it, while the gate still reports PASS - nothing outside floors gate 2's check count. This is the vacuity class in a new place: not a row that cannot fail, but a whole section that can be removed silently. A committed per-gate check-count floor, asserted by the runner rather than by the gate, is the shape of the fix.

entries.ev: Agent(model=opus) held-stage seat, batch A (harness rows). Read-only; GXEMUL-SEC only.
entries.note: *** VERDICT: KEEP OPEN -- but the premise is REFUTED for most of the battery, and the highest-value action was ONE CHARACTER, now shipped. *** 'Nothing outside it notices' is FALSE for every block that is the sole invoker of a python detector: section R hard-fails, verified (every detector has exactly one invoker across all gates, so deleting the block leaves the detector run by nothing). It is TRUE for log-grading blocks, source-grep blocks, per-row name lists, and the whole of gate_ab / gate_build / gate_upstream -- 38 check sites with zero python detectors. *** THE MEASURED SLACK, AND IT IS FIXED IN THE SAME COMMIT AS THIS ENTRY: section U's ratchet floor was 16 and the real value is 18. *** The count went 16 -> 17 -> 18 across recent commits while the floor never moved, despite the block's own comment saying 'raise the floor when it rises'. **Two whole gate blocks carrying score-claim pins could have been deleted with the check still printing `good`.** Its argument for the fix is the one adopted: **a hand-maintained ratchet is itself an unratcheted number**, so it is now an EQUALITY pin on the GATE_MANIFEST idiom, negative-controlled in both directions (17 -> GREW, 19 -> DROPPED, 18 -> ok). It also measured that `_checks` has NO consumer outside lib.sh -- any nonzero count is a PASS -- and proposed a per-gate runtime floor in `gate_end()` placed AFTER the fails/degraded tests so a legitimately degraded run reports SKIP and is never falsely reddened, with a rig-free `selftest_checkfloor.sh` asserting three outcomes. It recorded honest UNKNOWN on the floor VALUES (they need one clean battery run) and stated plainly what such a floor CANNOT see: a block hollowed while keeping its call count, a check made vacuous in place, or a pin's literal quoted. **It cited this project's own measured instance of the first** -- a seat deleting whole SELFCHECK blocks from five detectors with the gate staying PASS at the same check count -- and correctly flagged it as evidence a count floor is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT rather than as support. BONUS L4 IT FOUND: check_probe_wiring.py's own docstring -- the file whose thesis is 'a fact-shaped string with nothing behind it' -- carries two stale citations (gate_hygiene.sh:331 for a note actually at :381; gate_sh_rounding.sh:185 for one at :690).

rows.hold_question: If a whole gate BLOCK is deleted, nothing outside it notices. QUESTION: does a floor check exist today that would catch it, and if not, what is the cheapest one that WOULD? Concretely: is there a pinned count of gate blocks or of `check` calls per gate anywhere, comparable to the way `check_probe_wiring.py` pins detectors-to-gates? Note `precommit_check.sh` section U already compares score claims against gate pins, so some of the machinery exists. If the honest answer is that this needs a new check, say what it should count and what its NEGATIVE CONTROL would be -- a check that cannot be shown to fail is worth nothing here.

rows.title: hlen  Device handlers that ignore the access length (audit)
rows.hold: census done; promote to a FIX round?

closure.note: Opened from the b75 refutation, then characterized by census. A device handler that switches on the address and cannot service a width will read or write only the first register of an 8-byte access. MEASURED SCOPE: 62 spanning-capable handlers of 167 registered; 20 on machines this project boots. TWO BOOTED MACHINES ARE PROVABLY IMMUNE - SH-4 has no 8-byte access at all (fmov.d is two 4-byte accesses) and MIPS32/R3000A treats LD/SD as reserved, so landisk and pmax cannot produce the access. NO CONVENTION EXISTS in the tree: no helper, no macro, no rule - only three hand-rolled decompositions that are all big-endian-specific and that disagree with each other about the else branch, so there is no single idiom to copy. FIRST WITNESS NAMED: dev_irqc on testarm, the only spanning-capable device on that machine, where the two halves of one aligned 8-byte access have OPPOSITE legal directions (status is read-only, mask is write-only), which makes the miss unambiguous. DETECTOR SHAPE: an offline differential in the diff_*.c family - no boot, no rig, no serialization.

entries.note: CENSUS: 118 files, 62 spanning-capable handlers, 20 on booted machines. Coverage PROVED by set-difference against the 167 registered handlers, not asserted. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS NOT WHETHER len IS MENTIONED: 115 of 167 pass len only to memory_readmax64, which marshals bytes and does nothing about a span across two registers - so 'uses len' does not mean safe, and the naive definition undercounts the class about 15 times. VERIFIED AGAINST THE LOCAL MANUAL LINE BY LINE BEFORE RECORDING. *** My brief said the controlling text is LDR's own Alignment note at p. A4-44. **That governs LDR's rotate-the-aligned-word rule and does NOT govern block transfers.** The controlling text is LDM(1) p. A4-37 and STM(1) p. A4-190. Read from `_scratchpad/ddi0100i.txt:7954`: *'For CP15_reg1_Ubit == 0, the Load Multiple instructions ignore the least significant two bits of the address... For CP15_reg1_Ubit == 1, all non-word aligned accesses cause an alignment fault.'* STM says the same at `:14115`. **This is a citation read from the local manual, which is the standard the carrier demands after #357/#362/#365 shipped ARM page numbers that came from panel output.** And the seat's own argument for why LDR cannot govern is the good one: if A4-44 applied, the fast path -- which aligns WITHOUT rotating -- would not be correct either. RANKING: above `b120r`, and it noted `fable_queue.md` ALREADY ranks it first among the five triage rows -- so my brief's framing that it sat behind boot-witnessed items was also wrong. It declined to generalise: this does not put it above every boot-witnessed durability-loss or host-death defect, which need individual harm comparisons.
