rows.note: *** A SEVERITY STANDARD, adjudicated 2026-08-30, because the main loop proposed one that collapses two different classes. ***  I graded a stale-build record NIL and then generalised it to *"a confident wrong record with no measurement consumed"*.  **The adjudicating seat refused the generalisation and gave the discriminator: INERT BY CONSTRUCTION versus INERT BY LUCK.**  A comment-only stale delta is inert BY CONSTRUCTION -- the binary is byte-identical, so any measurement taken in that window is provably valid -> **NIL** (and the comment-only-ness must be RUN, not asserted; here the pass-2 seat measured zero non-comment diff lines).  An ASSERTED WRONG CENSUS is a live wrong fact that merely HAPPENS not to have been consumed yet -> **LOW, never NIL**.  > **The test is not "no measurement was consumed".  It is "no measurement COULD be consumed".**  And the carrier already holds a measured case of the second class changing an outcome: `asicbadaddr`'s 16-versus-64 census, where *a detector built from the wrong census walks sixteen addresses, covers a QUARTER of the defect, and reports full coverage*.  My own 25/15 census today was that shape -- asserted into two seat briefs, telling one of them it was probably wrong -- and it is LOW, not NIL.  *** AND THE STANDARD NEEDED A BOLT, WHICH THE EXEMPLAR'S OWN FILE ALREADY HELD.  Added 2026-08-30 by the adjudicating seat, against a claim I made in a commit message. ***  The discriminator (inert by CONSTRUCTION vs inert by LUCK) survives and has a real floor, unlike pre-floor 'weak': **NIL is a PROOF CLASS, and everything unproven is LOW or above.**  But my proof for the exemplar -- *the binary is byte-identical* -- **was never measured, and it is refuted by a comment in the very file it was about.**  `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` records, of its own comment-only assert block: *'It emits no object code -- verified with the filename held constant: **the object differs in exactly two bytes, both `__LINE__` immediates displaced by this comment block**.'*  So a comment-only delta in this tree does NOT yield a byte-identical binary.  > **THE SURVIVING FORM: NIL is claimable only with the IDENTITY PROOF NAMED -- a `cmp` of artifacts, or the byte delta enumerated with every byte attributed to a NON-CONSUMABLE token (which is exactly what that comment did).  Absent that proof, LOW is the floor.**  The grading itself stands -- `__LINE__` immediates move diagnostic line numbers and nothing else -- and the CHANGELOG's careful wording (*zero non-comment diff lines ... a wrong RECORD, not a wrong measurement*) survives.  **It is the 'byte-identical' shorthand in the commit message that does not**, and a shorthand that overstates a proof is how a proof class becomes a habit.  *** OWNER RULING 2026-08-30: agy IS RESERVED FOR MEASUREMENT AND HELD OUT OF ROUTINE PANELS. ***  Forced by its first quota wall proving the cap is real (~6 substantial calls per window).  **The warrant is a measured structural weakness: three compile-and-measure front ends, and TWO of them sit behind the SAME Agent-tool transport.**  When that transport failed on `#462` the panel lost ALL measuring capacity at once while seven reading seats answered normally.  agy is the only measuring seat on an independent road, so spending its budget on reading spends the roster's insurance on a job seven other seats already do.  **THE COST IS REAL AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED:** routine panels now fire EIGHT seats and each must record agy as **DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED** -- a different thing from a seat failure and from agreement, and conflating them is what the seat ledger exists to refuse.  Its read-only work today was not cheap to lose: it settled the alignment premise path-by-path and found the debugger `put d` exception a clean-invariant claim would have missed.  *But a reading is recoverable from another seat and a measurement with both Anthropic seats down is not.*  *** THE LEDGER'S `outcome` FIELD IS CARRYING **THREE** DIFFERENT QUESTIONS, AND THE ACCURACY TOOL CAN ONLY SEE ONE OF THEM.  Measured 2026-08-30. ***  *(This header said TWO while the body six sentences below said THREE -- a live self-contradiction, and the SAME shape as the refuted figure I left standing in `selftestaddition` earlier the same evening.  Caught by the second review pass; the body was right.)*  `seat_scorecard.py` recognises exactly four values -- `UPHELD` / `REFUTED` / `PARTIAL` / `UNVERIFIED` -- and **249 entries carried an `outcome` while only 110 were countable -- 139 invisible to it.**  *(Dated snapshot, and it has since drifted BY MY OWN HAND: tonight's four canonical gradings make it **250 / 115 / 135**.  DERIVER: count `"outcome":` for the total, and for the countable figure sum the entries whose value is one of the four `GRADES` in `seat_scorecard.py`.  Recorded rather than silently re-stated, because a number corrected must land as deriver-plus-demoted-prose and never as a fresh bare literal.)*  Derived by classifying every non-canonical value: **56 are a VERDICT THE SEAT GAVE** (`SHIP`, `NOT-RATIFY`, `GO-WITH-CHANGES`, `REJECT-AS-WRITTEN`), **11 are SEAT HEALTH** (`answered-104KB`, `answered-2.2MB`), and 72 are other free-form.  **THOSE ARE THREE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS SHARING ONE FIELD NAME:** *what did the seat CONCLUDE*, *did the seat ANSWER AT ALL*, and *was the seat RIGHT*.  Only the third is a grade.  A seat can conclude `NOT-RATIFY` and be **UPHELD** -- it was right to refuse -- or conclude `SHIP` and be **REFUTED**.  Collapsing them means the scorecard silently reads 3.9% coverage where the true figure for *graded* entries is what it says, and the other 139 are not partially-graded but differently-typed.  *** RETROACTIVE RECLASSIFICATION IS REFUSED, ON THE TOOL'S OWN STATED GROUND. ***  `seat_scorecard.py` says it plainly: *grade an entry when its claim is CHECKED -- reconstructing grades later reproduces exactly the recall bias this tool replaced.*  Deciding today whether a seat that wrote `SHIP` two weeks ago turned out to be right is precisely that reconstruction.  **The 139 stay as they are, and the finding is that the FIELD needs splitting, not that the entries need re-scoring.**  *Filed as an observation rather than a change: separating `verdict` from `outcome` edits every writer of the ledger and is an owner decision, not a round's. Stating that distinction is the whole value of the record.  **AND THE 69 NO-NOTE ROWS ARE NOT A RECORDS DEFECT, which is the part I expected to go the other way.**  69 open rows have no `note`, and the tempting reading is that they are thin filings.  **Measured against the rows that DO have notes, their titles are the same length -- median 145 against 149.**  The title is carrying the claim and the `witness` field the evidence; that is a convention, not an omission.  *A bulk backfill would have been invented work, and the measurement is what stopped it.*  *** THE CARRIER STATES A COUNT IN THE SENTENCE THAT TELLS YOU NOT TO STATE A COUNT. Measured 2026-08-30. ***  The discriminator is sound and is this file's own: *log MISSING -> never started; log 0 bytes -> started; log growing -> alive*.  I applied it to `_scratchpad/panel497p2.log` **from a shell whose cwd had drifted to `GXEMUL-SEC/`**, where no `_scratchpad/` exists.  `ls` reported absent. rows.title: idesync  IDE FLUSH CACHE has no durability path at all -- #437 is SCSI-only

entries.note: grep -i flush src/devices/dev_wdc.c returns NOTHING, so a guest's ATA FLUSH CACHE is not merely unflushed but unimplemented. Reachability UNKNOWN; landisk is the ATA rig and it boots, so a probe witness is likely available.  [panel_20260818_095322]

*** THE BRIEF'S FRAMING WAS HALF WRONG, AND THE HALF IT GOT WRONG CHANGES WHAT SHOULD BE FIXED. *** Verdict FIX-not-document, but not for the reason I gave it.
* 0xE7 WDCC_FLUSHCACHE is DEFINED at wdcreg.h:130 and NEVER REFERENCED in dev_wdc.c; 0xEA has no constant anywhere in src/. Both fall to wdc_command()'s default:, which sets WDCE_ABRT, emits an UNLATCHED fatal(), and -- the part that matters -- does NOT set d->int_assert. MEASURED offline against the shipping wdc_command(): 0xE7 -> err=0x04 irq=0 fatal=1, status 0x51 (DRDY|DSC|ERR), against the 0x10 RECAL control at err=0x00 irq=1.
* NO REAL GUEST ISSUES IT, and the negative is WELL CONTROLLED. With an IDE disk attached and a full filesystem lifecycle (MAKEDEV, fdisk, disklabel, newfs 64 MB FFS, mount, write, sync, umount, halt -p) OpenBSD 7.6 issues exactly: 0xEC 0xF5 0x10 0x91 0xC6 0x20 0xC4 0x30 0xC5 0xE0. No 0xE7, no 0xEA.
* IT REFUTED ITS OWN LEADING HYPOTHESIS rather than resting on it: 'the drive does not advertise FLUSH CACHE' was tested with TWO discriminating IDENTIFY variants (word 83=0x5000 and 0x7000). The guest DEMONSTRABLY READ the new IDENTIFY -- it began issuing 0xEF SET FEATURES, which it never did before -- and STILL never flushed. Why OpenBSD declines is an honest UNKNOWN: there is no OpenBSD source in this tree, and reconstructing wd_flushcache from memory is exactly the trap the SH-manual rule exists to prevent.
* *** THE LIVE DEFECT IS THE ARM, NOT THE OPCODE: 0xE0 STANDBY IMMEDIATE hits the same default: on EVERY `halt -p`, measured 4 of 4 shutdown runs. *** ABRT to the guest, no interrupt, unlatched host warning, and the guest swallows it silently. So the IDE side has a reachable reproducible fall-through TODAY, and FLUSH CACHE is an unreached member of the same set.
* THE FIX IS NOT A ONE-LINER. diskimage_sync() takes a struct diskimage *, but dev_wdc.c only ever holds (machine, id, type) -- and THERE IS NO EXPORTED (machine,id,type) -> struct lookup; every public function in diskimage.c open-codes the same 6-line walk. Needs a diskimage_sync_id() wrapper, a WDCC_FLUSHCACHE_EXT constant, and a case arm that also sets int_assert. Built privately: 0xE7/0xEA become err=0x00 irq=1 fatal=0 with trace F(data) S(data), matching the SCSI sibling.
* DETECTOR BUILT, and it COMPILES AGAINST BOTH TREES because the rows pass a RAW OPCODE INTEGER rather than the WDCC_ constant -- deliberately sidestepping the exact trap diff_diskimage_sync.c's header records, where naming the new symbol made the pre-fix arm a SETUP result. 9 rows / 0 failed pre-fix; 8 of 9 flip post-fix. Needs only two extra stubs given the flags gate_offline.sh already passes.
* SCOPE: all three files are byte-identical between est/ and GXEMUL-SEC/. And wdc is far from landisk-only -- bus_isa, bus_pci, dev_pcic, dev_ps2_spd, machine_arc.c:235, machine_landisk.c:87 and promemul/of.c all instantiate it, so ARC IS A SECOND ATA RIG THAT WAS NOT TESTED.  [agent idesync 2026-08-19]

*** THE ENTRY I WROTE EARLIER TODAY CARRIED A REFUTED CLAIM AND HAS BEEN REPLACED BY THIS
ONE (1 entry removed, its content quoted below).  Caught by an adjudicating seat BEFORE
ANYTHING WAS STAGED, so this is L1 construction, not a shipped wrong record. ***

**IT SAID: "no FLUSH constant exists in this tree's ATA headers".  FALSE.**
`src/include/thirdparty/wdcreg.h:130` is `#define WDCC_FLUSHCACHE 0xe7`.

**AND THE RECORDED EVIDENCE COULD NOT HAVE PRODUCED THE RECORDED CONCLUSION.**  I ran a
`grep -rn FLUSH src/include/` piped through `head -6` -- there are **46** hits -- and read a
TRUNCATION as an ABSENCE, under a label reading 'blank = the constant does not exist' while
the output was not blank.  *The apparatus-failure class, committed inside a record whose own
closing note warns about it.*  **Three siblings already held the right answer and none was
consulted**: this row's own CONFIRMED research entry of 2026-08-19, `OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md` at
the same fact, and the header itself.

FIVE REPAIRS, each re-verified by me against the tree before writing:

**(1) The correct fact is STRONGER than the false one.**  The constant is DEFINED and
**referenced ZERO times in `dev_wdc.c`**, so 0xE7 falls to `default:` BY CONSTRUCTION.  0xEA
(FLUSH CACHE EXT) has no constant under `src/` at all and belongs in scope too -- the
2026-08-19 research covered both; my scope line covered only 0xE7.

**(2) '18 of 256 words' dropped a qualifier: they are 18 SITES, not 18 words.**  Three are
memcpys spanning ranges -- word 10 a 20-byte serial (10-19), word 23 an 8-byte firmware
(23-26), word 27 a 40-byte model (27-46) -- so ~49 words are written.  **The load-bearing
fact is better stated as a CEILING: the highest word touched is 68**, so words 82-87 keep the
memset's zero.  A stronger form of the same conclusion: word 83 = 0x0000 also fails the bits
15:14 = 01b validity signature, so a conforming host discards the whole word -- the drive
advertises NO VALID COMMAND-SET INFORMATION AT ALL, not merely a cleared flush bit.

**(3) The arm census missed `case SET_FEATURES:` (0xEF).**  It is defined in `wdcreg.h`
WITHOUT the `WDCC_` prefix, so my prefix-keyed grep could not see it.  Twenty case labels, not
nineteen; none a flush.  *A count claiming completeness from an instrument blind to a member.*

**(4) THE WARRANT HIERARCHY WAS INVERTED, and this is the substantive one.**  I presented
'the drive never advertises it' as *the whole content* of the disposition.  The row's research
entry measured something stronger AND partly contrary: OpenBSD 7.6 through a full filesystem
lifecycle issued `0xEC 0xF5 0x10 0x91 0xC6 0x20 0xC4 0x30 0xC5 0xE0` -- no 0xE7, no 0xEA --
**and with word 83 forced to 0x5000/0x7000 the guest demonstrably READ the new block (it began
issuing 0xEF) and STILL never flushed.**  opus5 therefore demoted the advertise-reason: why
OpenBSD declines *remains an honest UNKNOWN*.  **The MEASUREMENT is the warrant; the IDENTIFY
fact is what a CONFORMING guest is entitled to conclude.**  I had re-derived a compressed
one-clause version of a multi-factor review -- unanimity with a stated premise, where I
verified the arithmetic of a claim whose causal story the row's own evidence had already
demoted to hypothesis.

**(5) Point 3 under-cited: `#485` belongs beside `#464`.**  The `default:` arm carries BOTH
outside the latch guard -- `d->error |= WDCE_ABRT` (#464) and `d->int_assert = 1` (#485).
**Without #485 the honest abort was POLLING-ONLY**; an interrupt-driven guest saw nothing at
all.  Citing only #464 claimed an abort that three days earlier would not have been delivered.

*** THE POLARITY CONTRAST SURVIVES BUT MUST NOT TRAVEL UNQUALIFIED. ***  IDE's `default:`
aborts honestly; SCSI's reports success (`b120u`).  **But `dev_wdc.c:1515` routes ATAPI packet
commands into `diskimage_scsicommand()`, and dev_wdc treats `res == 1` as success** -- so an
unknown PACKET command on an IDE ATAPI drive takes the SUCCESS polarity THROUGH the wdc
device.  One device, both polarities, selected by path.  **Deliberately NOT minted as a
carrier line**: it is an instance-pair, not a rule, and the qualifier it needs makes it a
paragraph -- an unqualified line would be the dropped-qualifier class itself.  It lands in the
record and as a cross-reference on `b120u`, whose fixer gains a second reachability route.

form: *a non-event admits no rung-3/4 witness (a ceiling four seat entries already record);
the non-issuance claim itself is carried by the measured lifecycle census of 2026-08-19.*  The

entries.ev: src/devices/dev_mb89352.c (the SCSI sibling's assert policy), read directly
entries.note:
*** THE WARRANT IS REPLACED, NOT STRENGTHENED, AND THE PACKET-FED SEAT IS WHY. ***

My warrant was in-file consistency: three abort arms assert, two do not, and SET_FEATURES
aborts an unimplemented SUB-command and asserts anyway.  The kimi-k3:cloud substitute
refused it on a reading I had not made: `d->int_assert = 1` sits AFTER the inner switch,
COMMON TO BOTH SUBPATHS, so `/* TODO: always interrupt? */` most plausibly scopes to the
SUCCESS path -- and the two clean precedents are the 'cannot execute at all' class, which
supports a DELIBERATE-DESIGN reading of the 3:2 split rather than an oversight.  Its
conclusion: the convention was never settled by the author, so this round CHOOSES it, and
the choice must be grounded in a sibling-device check rather than in a headcount.

SURVEY RUN.  `dev_mb89352.c`, the SCSI sibling, computes its assert as:

    bool assert = d->reg[INTS] != 0;
    if (!(d->reg[SCTL] & SCTL_INTR_ENAB)) assert = false;

*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE and GUEST-REACHABLE. It is the SAME DEFECT SHAPE as [[b120]] in a different device family, which is the part worth carrying. ***

With an IDE disk attached, `wdc_command()`'s `default:` arm sets `WDCE_ABRT` but **never sets `int_assert`**, and `dev_wdc_tick()` raises the IRQ only when that latch is set. So an unsupported command is refused **without the completion interrupt an interrupt-driven guest is waiting for.**

> *** THE FAMILY: an unsupported command's `default:` arm omits the COMPLETION SIGNAL the guest is blocked on. *** [[b120]] is the SCSI form -- no status byte, so the guest is told GOOD. This is the IDE form -- no interrupt, so the guest is told nothing at all. **Two device families, one omission.** Whichever is fixed first should be checked against the other, and the reviewer question generalises: *does this `default:` arm complete the protocol, or only decline the command?*

entries.note: *** THE CAPPED ASK-AGAIN, FIRED AGAINST A DETECTOR ALREADY CLEAN AT 24 ROWS -- AND IT FOUND ONE. *** Rule satisfied: found -> ONE row under L1 -> cap SPENT, no second query. **THE MUTANT: key the :607 latch on the ACCESS WIDTH instead of on a boolean.** `if (len != 1 && d->warned_nonbyte_write != (int) len) { d->warned_nonbyte_write = (int) len;` -- two lines, one hunk. A guest alternating `mov.w` / `mov.l` at wd_seccnt then gets ONE HOST LINE PER STORE, FOREVER: flag 0 != 2 -> line, flag = 2; flag 2 != 4 -> line, flag = 4; flag 4 != 2 -> line ... That is the pre-fix rate this round measured at 20 stores -> 20 lines. *** WHY NO ROW COULD SEE IT: 2 AND 4 NEVER CO-OCCUR IN A SINGLE SESSION. *** `w16 x2` fires (2,2); `w32 x2` fires (4,4); they are SEPARATE sessions. The reset rows interpose a `len == 1` access, which `len != 1` rejects BEFORE the flag operand is consulted, so they cannot re-key it. The seat walked all 24 sessions and tabulated the multiset of `len` values reaching each guard per session -- mechanically, not by eye. **:607 is the MOST heavily covered site in the file (six rows aim at it) and all six stay green**, which is what makes this a demonstration rather than a blunt break. **IT IS THE SAME CLASS THE ROUND ALREADY DECLARED A DEFECT AT :583** -- `warned_unimpl_cmd != cur_command`, killed by `unimpl 2op` -- transposed to a site where nothing could observe it. And it is a PLAUSIBLE maintainer edit, not an adversarial one: 'report each distinct bad width once' is natural, and :704's message prints `len=%i`, which invites it. *** THE GENERALISATION IS WORTH MORE THAN THE MUTANT, and it is one grep: *** the contract already asks *do two SITES share a session?* (`wr indep`). **Its DUAL was missing -- *for each site, does any ONE session present two DIFFERENT stimuli that both reach that site's guard?*** :583 yes (two opcodes); :607, :1025, :704, :160 and :145 all repeated an IDENTICAL stimulus. It must NOT fold in, and not merely by the reopening rule: **the restructure makes head==tail <=> empty sound ONLY on the byte path.** The bulk producer at :343-349 compares only against WDC_INBUF_SIZE and can land head exactly on tail with NO WARNING AT ALL (:876-879 mirrors it on tail). *pckbc had ONE producer; wdc has THREE.* A byte-path-only repair ships a half-invariant under a record that reads as soundness. **(3) SEQUENCING: `landiskdisk` SPLITS IN TWO.** The PROBE-level -d attach is part of `wdcflood`'s own witness battery and blocks nothing -- verified: :583 is unreachable without a disk (:461-468 early-returns), so the opus flood measurement necessarily ran disk-attached and the route is already proven. The BATTERY-RIG integration -- the half carrying the 28-34% NINSTRS poison -- is an independent deliverable and NOT a blocker. **The primed-head/tail row is a RUNG-1 DETECTOR row and cannot discharge :145's witness**; the 513-IDENTIFY route can, and was verified sound: no ring reset exists at command start (the only head/tail writes are :143, :165, :347-349, :876-879), IDENTIFY feeds wdc_addtoinbuf 512 bytes per command (:525-533), and 513 x 512 = 262,656 = WDC_INBUF_SIZE exactly. **(4) THE REPETITION RULE: DO NOT MINT, and my dichotomy was wrong on BOTH horns.** Clause (a) does NOT cover it -- (a) is DETECTOR-level and the defect is ROW-level: a one-off row at a latched site prints one line pre-fix and one line post-fix, colourless in both worlds, so it contributes nothing to (a) and hides behind rows that do. **But no new clause is needed, because clause (d) already forces it mechanically:** the fix adds six latch predicates, (d)-DEPENDS-ON mandates a null-repair mutant per predicate (flag never set), and the only row shape that reddens a nulled latch is one firing the same site twice with an EXACT count. Codex's sentence is the row-construction corollary of (d) for the latch class -- the same relation the accept-row failability rule bears to the de-escalation clause. Two overlapping statements of one rule is what the carrier refuses by name. **Disposition: one derivation sentence in the round block, not a carrier clause.** If a future latch round ships a SURVIVING one-off row, that measured escape is the (f)-style warrant to mint. **REFINEMENT ON THE ROWS (minimax): repetition with a "<= 1 line" oracle passes a mutant that prints ZERO. The oracle must be EXACTLY ONE, THEN ZERO** -- announcement AND suppression, which is the pair a latch actually promises.  *** PASS 2 (panel_20260825_204943) FOUND THREE ESCAPES AGAINST A DETECTOR MEASURED 14/14, AND ONE OF THEM IS A STRUCTURAL BLINDNESS OF THE ROWS RATHER THAN A GAP IN THEM. *** All three are L1 -- pre-ship construction, fixed in-round, not filed. **(1) glm -- THE RESET-ON-NORMAL-OPERATION ESCAPE, and it is the sharpest.** ONE line, reusing the existing flag, guard and branch, added inside an existing case for a VALID command: `d->warned_unimpl_cmd = 0;`. **Every site row fires its site TWICE IN SUCCESSION with no normal device operation between**, so the flag is never reset between fires and the row stays green -- while a real guest that probes an unimplemented opcode, issues IDENTIFY, probes again, issues IDENTIFY, floods forever. The same one-line trick applies at every one of the six sites. *This is the `#463` distinctness-invariance finding wearing new clothes: rows that test a property back-to-back are invariant under any edit that only changes what happens BETWEEN the two fires.* **(2) agy -- THE COVERAGE CENSUS, CONFIRMED AGAINST MY OWN PROBE.** "The detector's six site rows do not test six distinct C sites": `:145` has **ZERO** rows while its sibling `:160` has two, and `:583` has three. Also **the non-byte rows probe 16-bit ONLY** -- `mov.w` at both :607 and :1025, never `mov.l`, so a `len != 1` guard narrowed to `len == 2` would escape. **(3) deepseek -- `d->warned_X = !d->warned_X;`**, claimed to toggle so that fires 1 and 3 print while the detector only fires twice. **READING SAYS THIS DOES NOT WORK** -- the assignment sits INSIDE the guard (`if (!d->warned_unimpl_cmd) { d->warned_unimpl_cmd = 1; ...}`), so fire 2 never enters and the toggle never runs. **RECORDED AS A PREDICTION TO BE MEASURED, NOT AS REFUTED** -- this project settles disagreements by measurement, and the seat may be modelling a placement I have not considered. It goes in the second table either way, because the row that would kill it kills a whole CLASS. *** THE ROWS OWED, AND THE THIRD IS THE GENERAL ONE: *** `interleave` -- fire the site, issue a VALID command (0xEC IDENTIFY), fire again, demand ONE line; this is what kills glm's escape. `w32`/`r32` -- 32-bit non-byte access at :607 and :1025, closing agy's width gap. **`fire3` -- fire ONE site THREE times and demand exactly one line**, which kills the toggle class and any period-N latch at once, and is the cheapest row of the three. `:145` remains DISCLOSED-NOT-COVERED in the contract; agy's point stands but the contract already says so. *** AND AN HONEST RECORD ABOUT PROCESS: THE CARRIER'S PRE-TABLE CHECK WOULD HAVE CAUGHT agy's FINDING AND I DID NOT RUN IT. *** Its FIRST item is SIBLING PARITY -- *for each arm the diff touches, compare its observable channels against its nearest sibling arm; an asymmetry is a row you owe*. `:145` with zero rows beside `:160` with two IS that asymmetry, visible by counting, before any mutant was built. The check exists precisely because a table re-run is expensive, and this round is now paying that cost: the first table was measured against a 14-row detector and adding rows changes other mutants' scores, so a SECOND table is owed. **The check costs three greps and about thirty minutes; skipping it cost a table.**  *** THE FULL PASS-2 PANEL (8 of 8 answering; the kimi CLI walled and COVERED BY ITS SUBSTITUTE -- panel.sh reported that correctly for the first time) FOUND AN L2 FLOOR BREACH, TWO WRONG RECORDS IN SHIPPED TEXT, AND A DESIGN CLAIM WITH NO ROW BEHIND IT. *** **(L2 -- FLOOR BREACH, clause (b), grok) `:145` HAS NO DETECTOR ROW, SO THE FIX HAS SIX FIXED SITES AND THE DETECTOR SEES FIVE.** Clause (b) requires failure on a verbatim reinstatement at EVERY fixed site; reinstating `:145`'s unlatched form escapes clean. grok's verdict was DO-NOT-SHIP-AS-A-SIX-SITE-FLOOR and it is right. **Confirmed by counting my own probe: the six site-x2 rows cover FIVE sites -- `P_OVERRUN` appears only in `disjoint`, which fires an unimplemented command and never touches the ring.** The 8/14 -> 14/14 colour change is five tested sites plus `unimpl 2op`. Fix in-round, however late: either add a `:145` row or narrow the fix to five sites. **(L4 -- WRONG RECORD IN SHIPPED PROBE TEXT, codex and grok independently) THE HEADER CONTRADICTS ITS OWN CONTRACT.** It claims to catch *removal of any of the six per-instance latch guards* while the contract eight lines below excludes `:145`. It catches FIVE unique sites. **(L4 -- `disjoint` PROVES LESS THAN ITS NAME, codex.** It exercises only the unimplemented-command transcript, so it proves THAT stimulus matches one regex -- not that all six patterns map uniquely. The row's note overstates it. *** (DESIGN CLAIM WITH NO ROW, codex -- and this is the one I would have missed for good.) 14/14 DOES NOT ENFORCE SIX INDEPENDENT FLAGS. *** Every site test starts a NEW emulator (15 `session()` calls), so **pairing the read/write width flags, or the two ring flags, would pass every isolated row -- as would a PROCESS-GLOBAL latch**, unless one session exercises two controller instances. The round's headline design decision -- six flags, not four -- is therefore UNMEASURED by its own detector. codex adds the mitigating half, checked: the implementation does use six separately initialised per-instance fields, `DEVINIT(wdc)` zeroes the whole allocation, and none is reset or aliased later. **So the CODE is right and the DETECTOR cannot prove it** -- which under clause (e) must be disclosed, not claimed. **(ESCAPE, codex) An inserted `return 1;` immediately after the non-byte-read `fatal()`** leaves the FIRST 16-bit read's buffer untouched while the second runs normally -- and `r16 x2` checks only the line count. Needs a VALUE oracle, not a count. **(ESCAPE, ollama_kimi) `idata = data[0]` at the write-width site is a FOURTH guest-visible side effect** and has no pin row; my Q2 list named three. *** THE EPOCH-LATCH QUESTION (ollama_kimi and minimax, independently) IS ANSWERED AND THE ANSWER IS NO. *** They asked whether a guest-reachable device reset re-zeroes the `warned_*` flags, which would make the shipped code an epoch latch no row can see. Checked by reading: the only `memset(d, 0, sizeof(struct wdc_data))` is at :1126, immediately after the malloc at :1125 in DEVINIT. `COMMAND_RESET` (:484) and `ATAPI_SOFT_RESET` (:601) exist and neither re-zeroes the struct. **A real question, cheaply settled, and worth recording as a negative result so nobody re-asks it.** **(RECORDS, minimax) MY OWN BRIEF'S ROW ARITHMETIC DID NOT ADD UP:** it enumerated 2 controls + 6 site + 3 accept + 1 disjoint = 12 against a stated 14. The two unstated rows are the side-effect rows `abrt 2nd` and `overread -1` -- which are the most interesting rows in the file and the brief left them out of its own census. **(CHALLENGE, minimax) `fatal()` RETURNING IS ASSUMED IN THE :1025 COMMENT, AND "no early-out" DOES NOT ESTABLISH IT** -- no-early-out is about verbosity, not program lifetime. The claim is true and this project settled it on 2026-08-21 by reading `core/debugmsg.c:384-390`, but the comment should CITE that rather than lean on the adjacent no-early-out fact. A fair catch. **(USEFUL FOR `wdcringambig`, ollama_kimi) A WASTE-ONE-SLOT DISAMBIGUATOR IS NOT FORBIDDEN BY CAPACITY:** 512 x 512 = 262,144 usable is still <= 262,655, so a max-length sector transfer still fits. Only the 513-undrained-IDENTIFY fill exceeds it. **Any future claim that "waste-one breaks the exact-fit sizing" is wrong**, and that is worth carrying to the ring round before it invents the objection.  *** KILL TABLE 1 -- 8 MUTANTS AGAINST THE 14-ROW DETECTOR, AND ONE ESCAPED. *** Preserved at `regress/artifacts/wdcflood/table1_14rows/` (12 files + a README stating what the numbers mean and why the directory is stamped). Tree restored and cmp-verified against SEC, sentinel cleared, zero live processes. SCORES, every reddened row re-extracted with an ANCHORED trailing-`FAIL` match: `base` 14/14 (identity -- the harness scores the unmutated copy exactly as SEC does); `Mb1` 12/14 delete the :583 guard -> `unimpl x2`, `unimpl 2op`; `M1` 12/14 null the repair, flag never set -> same two; `M2` 11/14 SET BEFORE ANNOUNCE, zero lines -> those two plus `disjoint`; `M3` 13/14 last-warned-opcode -> **`unimpl 2op` ALONE**; `M4` 13/14 ABRT moved inside the guard -> **`abrt 2nd` ALONE**; `M5` 13/14 `return -1` moved inside the guard -> **`overread -1` ALONE**; `M6` **14/14 -- ESCAPED, ZERO ROWS REDDENED**. *** THE THREE SINGLE-ROW KILLS ARE THE USEFUL RESULT, NOT THE SCORES. *** `M3`, `M4` and `M5` each redden exactly ONE row, and those three rows exist for exactly those escapes -- nothing else in the file covers them. `abrt 2nd` and `overread -1` are the two rows that read a guest-visible SIDE EFFECT rather than a line count, and they are the only rows that can see a repair swallowed by a guard. *** M2 IS THE MEASURED VINDICATION OF AN ORACLE CHOICE. *** It sets the flag before the test so the site emits ZERO lines. **A `<= 1 line` oracle would have passed it**; `exactly 1` catches it. That choice was argued from a seat's reasoning and is now measured. *** AND M6 IS THE ESCAPE, PREDICTED BY A SEAT ON PASS 2 AND CONFIRMED HERE. *** It swaps the latch operand for the GUEST-RESETTABLE `d->seccnt`: `if (len != 1 && !d->seccnt) { d->seccnt = 1; fatal(...); }`. Every row in table 1 fires its site TWICE IN SUCCESSION, so nothing between the fires ever puts the operand back and the mutant looks perfectly latched. A guest that writes `seccnt = 0` between wide writes floods without bound. **This is a STRUCTURAL blindness of the row design, not a missing mutant** -- the same shape as `#463`'s distinctness invariance, where rows that assert a property back-to-back cannot see an edit that changes only what happens BETWEEN the assertions. *** DETECTOR NOW 22 ROWS, MEASURED 22/22 ON THE FIXED BUILD (`table2_22rows/base_22rows.raw`). *** Seven rows added, each closing something table 1 or pass 2 exposed: `overrun x2` (the :145 row -- **this is what closes the L2 floor breach**, and it needed a hardware loop, `dt r3` / `bf` with a computed displacement, because 513 undrained IDENTIFYs unrolled would be 513 debugger commands); `interleave` (fire, VALID command, fire); `w16 reset` (fire, guest CLEARS the operand, fire -- the M6 killer); `fire3` (kills period-N latches, not just period-2); `w32 x2` and `r32 x2` (the width rows probed 16-bit only, so a guard narrowed to `len == 2` escaped); `r16 value` and `w16 value` (value oracles at the two width sites, for a `return` inserted after a latched `fatal()` -- which a count-only row cannot see). Row hygiene checked: no name over 13 chars, no duplicates, no name that is a prefix of another followed by a space. TABLE 2 is running against the 22-row detector with three mutants table 1 could not have had: `Mb2` removes the :145 guard verbatim (the clause-(b) reinstatement at the site that had no row), `M7` is the reset-on-normal-operation escape, `M8` is the period-2 latch. All three anchors were verified to occur EXACTLY ONCE in the source first -- **a mutant that fails to apply scores a false clean**, which is the worst possible failure for a kill table. *** A CAPTION DEFECT IN THE APPARATUS, FOUND AND FIXED AT SOURCE. *** `killwdc.sh` wrote its header at start with the row count and the pre-fix score as LITERALS (`14 rows`, `8/14`). The moment pass 2 forced seven more rows, table 2's own header became wrong about its own size. The script now DERIVES the count (`grep -c '^row(' ...`) and stamps a UTC start time instead of quoting scores it cannot know. Table 2's already-written header is stale and is corrected in place; the script fix stops it recurring. *A table that misreports its own size cannot be cited safely at all.*  *** KILL TABLE 2 IS CLEAN: 22-ROW DETECTOR, TEN MUTANTS, **ZERO ESCAPES**, EVERY LOG INTERNALLY CONSISTENT. *** Preserved at `regress/artifacts/wdcflood/table2_22rows/` with a header that DERIVES its row count rather than quoting one. Tree restored and cmp-verified against SEC, sentinel cleared, zero live processes. base 22/22; Mb1 18/22; M1 18/22; M2 17/22; M3 21/22; M4 21/22; M5 21/22; M6 21/22; M7 21/22; M8 21/22; Mb2 21/22. **Consistency check on all eleven logs: score + anchored-red count == 22 in every one**, which is the check that would catch a contaminated extractor. *** SIX ESCAPES, SIX SINGLE-ROW KILLS, EACH BY THE ROW BUILT FOR IT -- and that one-to-one correspondence is the result, not the scores: *** M3 last-warned-opcode -> `unimpl 2op` ALONE; M4 ABRT inside the guard -> `abrt 2nd` ALONE; M5 `return -1` inside the guard -> `overread -1` ALONE; M6 guest-resettable operand -> `w16 reset` ALONE; M7 reset-on-normal-operation -> `interleave` ALONE; Mb2 the :145 verbatim reinstatement -> `overrun x2` ALONE. **Nothing else in the file sees any of them.** *** THE L2 FLOOR BREACH IS CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT. *** `Mb2` is the exact edit that swept CLEAN against the 14-row detector -- removing :145's guard verbatim -- and it now reddens `overrun x2`, the row that did not exist when the breach was found. Clause (b) holds at all six fixed sites. *** M8 VINDICATES A CAUTION, AND THE CAUTION IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART. *** deepseek proposed `d->warned_X = !d->warned_X;` as a period-2 escape. I read its SPECIFIC edit as unworkable -- the assignment sits INSIDE the guard, so fire 2 never reaches it -- and recorded it as **"a prediction to be MEASURED, not refuted"**. M8 constructs the same class differently (toggle BEFORE the guard) and escapes a two-fire oracle exactly as deepseek said the class would. **Wrong about the placement, RIGHT ABOUT THE CLASS.** Declaring it refuted on the strength of a correct reading of one construction would have lost a real escape. *A seat can be wrong about the mechanism and right about the family; the family is the part worth building a row for.* *** CLAUSE (c), THE NULL MEDIUM, IS NOW MEASURED AND IN ITS STRONGEST FORM: 0/22 ON BOTH. *** `nullmedium_absent.raw` (a binary that does not exist) and `nullmedium_notanemu.raw` (a real executable that is not an emulator) each score **0/22 -- every row fails, not merely some**. It had NOT been verified before; the question was raised against the round's own readiness and answered in seconds. **AND THE MEASUREMENT EXPOSED A DESIGN PROPERTY THAT WAS ACCIDENTAL RATHER THAN INTENDED:** the three accept rows expect ZERO diagnostics, so a naive implementation would PASS against silence -- zero is exactly what silence produces. They fail correctly only because `n()` returns `"died"` rather than `"0"` when the run produced nothing (probe :227-228). **That single line is what stops every accept row in this file from being vacuous under clause (c)**, and it was not written for that reason. Worth carrying to any future detector with absence-shaped oracles: an "expect 0" row MUST distinguish 'ran and saw nothing' from 'did not run'.  *** THE READINESS ADJUDICATION RETURNED **HOLD-FOR** AND FOUND TWO SHIPPED ROWS VACUOUS. ASKING BEFORE THE TABLE FINISHED IS WHAT MADE THAT POSSIBLE -- a clean sweep invites ratification. *** **`r16 value` WAS VACUOUS AS BUILT.** Its oracle was `printed(t,"r2") != "absent"` against a wanted `"read"`, so it passed whenever the debugger echoed ANY hex value -- structurally incapable of failing while the emulator lived. **Confirmed: green under every one of table 2's ten mutants -- it did not exist for table 1, which measured a 14-row detector, and an earlier note said 'tables 1 and 2', which is false.** The `live` control already covered session death, so the row measured nothing at all. **AND BOTH WIDTH VALUE ROWS CHECKED THE WRONG FIRE.** The escape they cite -- a `return` inserted after a latched `fatal()` -- corrupts the FIRST access (flag unset, guard entered, return skips the repair); the SECOND finds the flag set, skips the guard and repairs normally. Both rows read the value ONCE, after both fires, and so saw a perfectly good value. The contract line claiming they carried value oracles "for exactly that edit" was FALSE AS BUILT. Repaired to check BOTH fires, with a low-byte mask because the repair sets only `data[0]` and asserting the upper byte would make the row about the wrong thing. *** TABLE 3 EARNS THE REPAIRED ROWS THEIR MEASURED KILL, WHICH IS WHAT A REPAIRED ROW OWES: *** `table3_repaired/`, base 22/22. `Mv1` (delete `idata = data[0]`, the write-side repair) 18/22 -> r16 value, w16 value, overrun x2, accept ec. `Mv2` (delete `data[0] = odata`, the read-side repair inside the `ret:` tail) 18/22 -> devsig, abrt 2nd, r16 value, w16 value. **`Mv3` (codex's EXACT edit -- insert `return 1;` after the latched READ `fatal()`) 21/22 -> `r16 value` ALONE.** *** Mv3 IS THE ONE THAT PROVES THE REPAIR RATHER THAN THE ROW. *** It corrupts only the first access, so **the ORIGINAL one-value form would have scored 22/22 against it** -- the escape would have shipped invisibly behind a row whose whole stated purpose was to catch it. One row in twenty-two sees it, and it is the repaired one. COLLATERAL WORTH READING RATHER THAN DISMISSING: `Mv2` reddens `devsig`, because deleting `data[0] = odata` breaks the status read the device-signature control depends on. That is the control doing its job -- a device that cannot answer through its own decode is exactly what `devsig` exists to notice -- not a spurious red. Tree restored and cmp-verified against SEC, sentinel cleared, zero live processes. All three logs internally consistent (score + anchored reds == 22). *** THE STANDING LESSON, and it is the second time in one round: A REPAIRED ROW IS NOT A ROW UNTIL A MUTANT KILLS IT. *** Both rows looked correct after repair and one of them still could not have caught the edit it was written for. dev_vr41xx.c:606 is `int hz = RTCL1_L_HZ / idata` -- an INTEGER divide with RTCL1_L_HZ = 0x8000. The entire domain idata >= 32769 collapses to hz = 0, which timer_clamp_freq then floors SILENTLY to 1e-8 Hz: one tick per 3.17 years. *** A GUEST ASKING FOR 0.5 Hz GETS A TIMER THAT NEVER FIRES. ***  Not 'lands below the floor' -- destroyed BEFORE timer.c ever sees it. Flooring 0 -> 1e-8 in timer.c is CORRECT; a floor complaint there would make this noisier while still wrong.

RUNG-3 WITNESS BUILT TODAY, two subtypes, unmodified in-tree machine, no device_add, every planted word disassembled and text-compared before stepping:
    hpcmips/z50 (VR4121) cold debugger, no boot
    LIVENESS  idata=0x00008000 -> [ vr41xx: rtc interrupts at 1 Hz ]   control green
    SUBJECT   idata=0x00010000 -> [ vr41xx: rtc interrupts at 0 Hz ]   guest asked 0.5 Hz
Identical on mobilepro770. Both required controls present: liveness AND device signature ((vr41xx@0xb000000)+0xd0 plus the device's own message -- RAM produces no line at all). The encoding guard earned its keep: the first run REFUSED a verdict because the expected mnemonic strings were wrong, and reported SETUP rather than passing.

TWO OTHER LEGS MEASURED, one FALSE: *** footbridge is REFUTED *** -- bounded below by emulated_hz / 2^32, so emulated_hz would have to be < 42.95 Hz; on a 33 MHz machine the worst case is 0.0077 Hz, six orders of magnitude above the floor. The jazz leg is much weaker than filed: 64-bit store only (any 32-bit store bottoms out at 2.33e-7 Hz, 23x above floor).

THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME DEFECT, WHICH DOES MERGE: dev_vr41xx.c:614 `case 0xd2: /* RTCL1_H_REG_W */ break;` is a NO-OP. vr_rtcreg.h:87-88 names RTCL1_L/H_REG_W as the halves of a 32-bit reload, so the high half is silently discarded -- and since L is 16 bits, THE SUB-1-Hz DOMAIN IS EXACTLY THE DOMAIN THAT NEEDS H. Same device, same class, same oracle, one fix design.

Does NOT merge with n4/#429 despite both being 'a guest rate narrowed': different device, OPPOSITE END of the domain, different mechanism (wide-domain ceiling vs integer-division floor collapse), new oracle.

entries.ev: src/core/debugmsg.c (debug() vs fatal(), read side by side)

entries.note:
*** WORSE THAN FILED, ON TWO MEASUREMENTS -- AND ONE OF THEM REFUTES A CLAIM IN THE TOOL I SHIPPED FOR THIS ROW. ***

(1) THE EMIT PATH AMPLIFIES 161x, MEASURED. va_debug() (debugmsg.c:118-137) emits ONE printf("%c") PER CHARACTER, plus an indent loop printing spaces one at a time. The seat replicated that loop byte-for-byte rather than paraphrasing it and benchmarked against a single fputs, to /dev/null so sink cost is excluded: 0.490 s vs 0.003 s over 200,000 calls on a 62-byte message -- 2.45 us against 0.02 us, AMPLIFICATION 161.2x, and that is a FLOOR because a real line-buffered console is worse. So a flood is not log noise; it is guest-controlled HOST-CPU amplification on a path -q cannot silence.

(2) *** census_floods.py SAYS REACHABILITY 'NEEDS THE CALL GRAPH, AND A TOOL THAT GUESSED WOULD BE WORSE THAN ONE THAT DECLINES'. THAT PREMISE IS FALSE AND I WROTE IT. ***  DEVICE_ACCESS() IS the dispatch entry memory_rw calls, so lexical containment inside its brace-matched body is a SOUND STRUCTURAL OVER-APPROXIMATION -- no call graph required. The seat built it:
    776 fatal() under src/devices/
    475 inside a DEVICE_ACCESS() body            (guest MMIO handler)
    150 inside a switch default: in that body    (unhandled-offset arm)
     10 of those guarded by a latch in their OWN arm
    *** 140 UNLATCHED AT THE SITE, in 53 files ***
POSITIVE CONTROLS BOTH LAND, and it resolves PER-PATH -- the resolution my census says it lacks. It flags dev_rtc.c:168-173 (the two pre-#429 arms this row names), and in dev_wdc.c it correctly SEPARATES :731/:761 (latched by warned_badlen, #337's work) from :583/:1007 (unlatched) -- i.e. it finds the path #337 MISSED inside a file my census scores as 'latched'.

SO THE HONEST HEADLINE IS 140 SITES, NOT 543 CALLS AND NOT 72 FILES. Per-path, actionable, and mechanically re-derivable.

(3) A RUNG-3 WITNESS IS AVAILABLE TODAY AT NEAR-ZERO COST, and the filing seat (me) missed it: regress/pit8253_latch_probe.py is committed and already drives real guest ARM instructions through real address decode to PA 0x7c000040-43 on an unmodified -E cats -- the 8253's own registers -- and dev_8253.c carries unlatched default:-arm fatal() at :158 and :184 (plus :250/:253). ONE MORE ARM on an already-committed probe witnesses an unsuppressable 161x-amplified flood.

(4) DETECTOR, NOT FIX, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL: the round-scope rule takes ONE site, and a second only in the SAME DEVICE. rtcflood and wdcflood are different devices, so THE PROJECT'S OWN SCOPE RULE FORBIDS FIXING THIS CLASS IN ONE ROUND -- 140 sites at one round each is not a plan. What a floodclass round can honestly deliver is the per-path detector plus the ranked list.

HONEST BOUND THE SEAT INSISTED ON, and it is right: the harm is to the HOST (CPU burn, unbounded log growth, unsuppressable), NOT to the emulated guest. floodclass is a host-side denial-of-service surface, not guest corruption. It still outranks the rest of its cluster because the others have no harm of any kind -- theirs is a wrong record.

TWO MORE INSTANCES FOLDED IN RATHER THAN FILED SEPARATELY, on the adjudicator's call that a standalone row for each is the near-duplicate proliferation this row exists to prevent. (1) `asicdefaultflood`: dev_dreamcast_asic.c's default: arm is unlatched -- silent at default verbosity, but under -v a guest scanning the window floods, and the asicbadaddr round routes SIXTY-FOUR more byte offsets into that arm. It rides with that round, whose survival sweep already exercises the arm. (2) `gdromxfrflood`: dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c's `Transfering %i bytes` fatal is NOT latched, so a guest looping legal DMA floods host stderr -- while the two ILLEGAL paths #462 latched stay quiet. That inversion sits three lines from a new comment arguing flooding is what every latch here exists to prevent. Pre-existing, but #462 touched the line.

rows.state_note: *** THE THREE-MEMBERED OPTION SET APPLIES DIRECTLY TO THIS ROW (carrier rule, minted 2026-08-25 from #463). *** #463 de-fatalised a device by framing the choice as KEEP the unlatched `fatal()` versus DELETE it, chose delete, and its own research stage then found the third member had been shipping in-tree the whole time: **`memory_rw.c:495-523` bounds a guest-drivable diagnostic to 8 emissions via `n_trunc_msgs`, because 'probing at the end of a device's mapped range is common and benign'.** The carrier already said 'a guest-drivable fatal() needs a latch and not a verbosity flag' -- standing rule, never consulted by that round's two-membered framing. **So before this row is worked: the option set is DELETE / DECLINE / DECLINE+BOUNDED-ANNOUNCE, and the first step is to grep the fork for the existing idiom rather than reason from first principles.** #463 also established that a bounded announce is not merely acceptable but RECOVERS the self-announcing property that de-fatalising destroys -- which for an unlatched flood is the whole point, since the flood and the announcement are the same channel.

entries.note: MEASURED at rung 3. dev_8253.c:170-171 CLEARS I8253_TIMER_LSB and nothing ever sets it back; a real 8254's flip-flop ALTERNATES on every access. Two full LSB/MSB pairs after one mode write produced THREE recomputes -- 97 Hz, **0 Hz**, 97 Hz -- where hardware does two. TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the first is what makes it matter: it transiently drives the counter to ZERO, i.e. straight into the i8253zero defect, FROM A GUEST THAT NEVER PROGRAMS COUNT 0. That inverts the reachability finding on i8253zero, where no available guest asks for count 0 directly. Second: if the second pair's LSB is nonzero it is SILENTLY LOST -- intending 0x3055 the device holds 0x3000. Same device and the same semantic class as i8253zero (counter-load byte routing), so it is the natural companion if a round takes a second site.

*** THE FACT THAT DECIDES WHAT THIS ROUND CAN HONESTLY DO: THERE IS NO RUNNING COUNT. ***  Found while writing the design brief. d->counter[3] is WRITTEN only in the mode-write path and READ only in the counter-read path -- IT NEVER DECREMENTS. timer0_tick() increments pending_interrupts_timer0 and touches nothing else. The file's own header carries the author's TODO at line 35: '(Split counter[] into reset value and current value.)'

So d->counter[] is the PROGRAMMED RELOAD VALUE, FROZEN. gxemul models the timer's RATE (timer_add / timer_update_frequency) and its INTERRUPTS, but never a counting register.

WHY THAT REFRAMES THE FIX: OpenBSD's microtime() latches and reads the counter to INTERPOLATE SUB-TICK TIME. If a 'correct' latch returns a constant, the guest's interpolated time does not advance within a tick -- a different wrong answer from 0, and arguably a WORSE one because it is plausible rather than obviously broken. So the candidate that looks most correct (return the programmed value) may be the one that misleads a guest furthest, and the honest round may be smaller than the row implies: make the latch not-an-error and not-a-flood, and DOCUMENT that sub-tick interpolation is unmodelled. The panel was asked exactly that, and asked to say so if this is a DOCUMENT round wearing a FIX round's clothes.

entries.note:
*** THE DRIVING SEAT REFUSED THE PANEL'S DESIGN AND MEASURED WHY. ***  Four of six seats converged on 'make the latch non-clobbering and non-fatal, RETURN THE RELOAD VALUE, and document that it is not a live count'. The seat BUILT that as candidate C1 and measured it causing a GUEST DIVIDE-BY-ZERO: OpenBSD's findcpuspeed() (_guest-src-openbsd22/.../clock.c:333-344) programs the counter to 0xffff and divides by (0xffff - gettick()); under C1 gettick() returns 0xffff, so the divisor is 0.

AND C1 DID NOT EVEN DELIVER WHAT IT PROMISED: it returned the HIGH BYTE TWICE (0x2e2e, not the reload 0x2e9c), because pitflip leaves the LSB/MSB selector stuck at MSB. The 'return the reload value' option does not return the reload value.

*** THE SEAT-CLASS DOCTRINE DECIDED IT, NOT THE COUNT. ***  The three seats voting for the reload value were the PACKET-FED Ollama seats, which PIPELINE.md says are never equivalent votes on repo fact. BOTH FILE-READING seats that answered (agy, grok) warned against it, and kimi flagged the same hazard class. Codex was a SEAT FAILURE at that panel, not agreement. A 4-2 count concealed a 0-2 split among the seats that could open the file.

WHAT SHIPPED (#439): the latch is ACCEPTED, latches NOTHING, and disturbs NO state -- a latched[3] flag, a write-arm branch returning before it touches mode_byte/mode[], and a read-arm branch returning 0 with the limitation documented in the code and in the file header. Guest-visible values are unchanged from the committed build, so it cannot regress anything. pitclobber travels with it: one fix design ('the latch disturbs no state') covers both arms.

MEASURED, rung 3, unmodified -E cats, PIT at 0x7c000040, five controls green in every run (RAM liveness, CP15 MMU-off readback, a device signature RAM cannot produce, an MMU-ON negative control, encodings checked against the emulator's own disassembly):

                    two 'huh? reading from counter 0' complaints
    shipped         mode_byte after latch 0x24 (PRESERVED), 0 complaints,
                    findcpuspeed divisor 65535 (safe)

THE DETECTOR KILLS PER VARIANT, INCLUDING THE OVER-FIX:
                    R1 clobber   R2 false error   R3 divisor
    committed HEAD     FAIL          FAIL            ok
    C1 panel shape      ok            ok            FAIL = 0
    C2 read-arm only   FAIL           ok             ok

R3 exists specifically to catch the plausible over-fix the panel recommended.

*** THE SEAT CAUGHT A VACUITY BUG IN ITS OWN FIRST DRAFT: *** the rows read absent registers as ok (-1 == -1), so three 'kills' were runs that never started -- an execvp PATH bug. Rows now fail on absent data (R0), and R0 is why the table above can be believed.

FOUR CLAIMS IN MY BRIEF MEASURED FALSE, and one of them I had propagated all evening: fatal() is NOT 'byte-for-byte debug()' -- debug() returns early under quiet_mode/verbosity and fatal() never does, so a fatal() flood CANNOT BE SILENCED even with -q, which makes every flood row MORE severe. The guest function is gettick(), not microtime(). d->mode[] is behaviourally inert (written in three places, read only inside a debug() printf), so pitclobber's only guest-visible effect is via mode_byte. And 'return the reload value' does not return the reload value.

MEASURED (grep census): pending_timer_interrupts has exactly ONE writer (dev_8253.c:282) and TWO pointer-cachers (bus_isa.c:225, dev_v3.c:298), both caching before their 8253 can exist.

*** MEASURED, AND THIS IS THE PART NOBODY STATED: dev_8253.c contains ZERO decrements of pending_interrupts_timer0. ***  Every other timer device in the tree drains its own counter from inside its own DEVICE_ACCESS handler -- dev_jazz.c:423,443, dev_luna88k.c:800, dev_mc146818.c:563, dev_vr41xx.c:634, dev_footbridge.c:583,594-595. The 8253 ALONE outsourced its drain to bus_isa.c:134-138.

READ: that drain is unreachable for TWO INDEPENDENT reasons, *** so moving the pointer copy after device_add -- the fix as filed -- changes NOTHING observable: *** (1) nothing ever calls isa_interrupt_deassert for line 0, as dev_8253.c has no INTERRUPT_DEASSERT; and (2) dev_8259.c clears irr DIRECTLY on EOI (:107, :122), bypassing the isa deassert handler entirely.

REFILE AS: 'the 8253's pending-interrupt counter has no reachable drain -- it is the only timer device in the tree that cannot ack', grade DESIGN + needs-witness. Consequence (READ): once any guest touches the PIT, in_use goes 1, the counter rises monotonically and never drains, so DEVICE_TICK re-asserts isa.0 on EVERY device tick (TICK_SHIFT 14) rather than at the programmed rate.

TWO THINGS THE FILING SEAT MISSED: dev_v3.c:298 is not merely 'the same shape' -- it is the same bug for the same reason needing the same two-part fix; and if a machine ever created two ISA buses (bus_pci.c calls bus_isa_init at :476 and :1060), the second copy would be NON-NULL AND ALIAS THE FIRST BUS'S 8253 -- worse than NULL, and silent.

THE WITNESS THAT WOULD SETTLE IT, rung 3 on -E cats: program counter 0 to ~18 Hz, free-run 200 ms, read the 8259 IRR (expect bit0), write specific-EOI 0x60 to 0x7c000020, free-run ~5 ms, read IRR again. Draining correctly => 0 (next tick due at ~55 ms); no drain => 1 again on the very next device tick. Clean discriminator, no source change.

*** THIS IS THE FOURTH RECURRENCE OF A PATTERN gate_hygiene.sh ALREADY LOGS THREE TIMES: a probe ships unwired, so no gate run is forced, so nothing notices. *** The third occurrence is why EXPECT_CONVERTED exists at all.

The cheap structural fix is not a new gate but a rule: a `witness:` value naming a path under regress/ must be a path some gate executes. That is checkable against the gate scripts. Note the floodclass detector round would force this wiring as a side effect, so sequencing may close it for free.

rows.witness: harness:check_witness.py's own header, which states the limitation the row describes -- so the premise is verifiable by reading the tool.
rows.state_note:
*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: THE PREMISE IS TRUE AND THE FRAMING AS A DEFECT IS WRONG -- the limitation is DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED AND REASONED. But there is a narrow mechanical subset the stated reasoning does NOT cover, and I hit it myself today. ***

**The tool says so in its own header** (`check_witness.py:38-41`):
  > *"The check enforces the SHAPE, not the truth: it cannot tell whether `probe:foo.py` really preserves routing. **That judgement stays with the panel, which is the honest division** -- a script that claimed to validate a witness would be exactly the false comfort the ladder was written against."*

**That reasoning is correct and should not be overturned.** *Does this artefact actually witness the defect?* is a judgement about routing and controls; a script asserting it would manufacture confidence, which is the precise failure the witness ladder exists to prevent.

*** BUT THE EXEMPTION IS BROADER THAN ITS REASON. *** The reason covers a JUDGEMENT. Two adjacent facts are not judgements at all:
  * **does the named file EXIST?** -- one `os.path.isfile`;
  * **does ANY gate reference it?** -- one grep over `regress/gate_*.sh`.
**Neither claims the witness is valid. Both catch a witness that cannot possibly be valid**, and a witness naming a file no gate ever runs is in that category.

**I PRODUCED A LIVE INSTANCE TODAY.** Back-filling [[exitsweep]]'s witness I wrote that its probe was *wired into TWO gates ... so it actually runs*. It is run by ONE (`gate_m88k_rounding.sh`); the other only counts its constructs in a census. **Section K passed that field**, because the string's shape was valid. A gate-reference grep would have reddened my overclaim in the commit that made it.

**DISPOSITION: not a defect in the tool's design; a candidate for a NARROW additive check** -- existence plus at-least-one-gate-reference, reported as WARN rather than FAIL so it cannot become the switched-off kind, and explicitly NOT claiming to validate the witness. **The addition licence wants a measured delta: today's overclaim is one.** Filed, not built -- it is a change to the script every commit runs and owes negative controls in both directions.

rows.title: warnnotfail  Deleting a pipeline checker still yields PRECOMMIT_PASS, because the MISSING branches only warn
rows.hold: One-line change per branch, but it is a POLICY decision -- a missing checker in a fresh clone is different from one deleted in a working tree.

entries.note:
MEASURED by a ninth-seat review. precommit_check.sh:45 defines warn () { soft "$@"; } -- so it increments `warn`, not `fail`. Deleting check_witness.py today still yields PRECOMMIT_PASS with a single WARN line.

THE HISTORICAL BUG IS FIXED AND THIS IS THE NEXT LAYER: `warn` was once UNDEFINED, so a deleted checker printed 'warn: command not found' to stderr and its gate vanished in SILENCE. That was corrected earlier this session. Announcing now works; BLOCKING does not -- and the file's own comment says those branches exist 'to announce' the failure, which is exactly as far as they go.

Deliberately filed rather than fixed on the spot: a missing checker in a FRESH CLONE is a normal state, while one deleted from a working tree is a gate being switched off, and the branch cannot currently tell them apart. Making it hard without that distinction would block a clean clone from committing.

rows.witness: harness:precommit_check.sh's own guard structure -- countable by reading, and the tree already records a MEASURED run in which deleting a checker produced PRECOMMIT_PASS with one warning.
rows.state_note:
*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, LATENT, and now QUANTIFIED EXACTLY -- 12 of 14. The remedy is already in the same file, applied to the other 2. ***

**The shape**, `precommit_check.sh:710-718` (the witness checker, representative of all 14):
```sh
if [ ! -f "$WITCHK" ]; then
        warn "check_witness.py MISSING -- witness naming NOT verified"    # SOFT
elif out=$(python "$WITCHK" 2>&1); then  good ...
else    bad "A ROW CLOSED WITH COMMITS AND NO ADMISSIBLE WITNESS:"        # HARD
```
**A checker that FAILS is a hard failure. A checker that is ABSENT is a warning.** So deleting the file converts a hard gate into a soft one, and the commit proceeds.

**THE CENSUS (deriver: `grep -cE '\[ ! -f .*(CHK|check_)'` then the following line):**
```
  checkers guarded          14
  MISSING -> warn (soft)    12
  MISSING -> bad  (hard)     2   check_row_states.py, check_cited_artifacts.py
```

> *** THE TWO HARD ONES ARE THE FINDING. *** Somebody already decided this question for two checkers and implemented it in this exact file, so **the remedy is a transferred warrant, not a design** -- make the other twelve match the two.

**NOT guest-reachable:** it is a host-side pre-commit script; no emulated guest can delete a worktree file. **Observable:** the precommit process exit status -- 0 when broken, non-zero when fixed.

**BUT DO NOT SWEEP IT UNILATERALLY -- there is a real argument on the other side, and it is the one this project keeps citing:** a hard failure on absence means a degraded or partial checkout cannot run the gate AT ALL, and *a check that has to be switched off is worse than no check*. The counter-argument is that all fourteen live in the same repo, so absence is not a partial-checkout condition -- it is a deletion. **That is an adjudication question, not a unilateral edit**, and it changes the script every commit runs, so it also owes negative controls both ways.

*Directly relevant to today: I relied on this gate all session and it caught three real obligations. This does not undermine those catches -- a checker that RAN and failed is hard. It bounds what a green gate proves: it proves the checkers PRESENT are satisfied, not that the intended set ran.*

rows.title: m8batc  The BWP/BATC arm has ZERO detector rows, and a mutant that stops updating the shadow batc[] passes BOTH m88k differentials green

closure.note:
Shipped as 7849fad. A DETECTOR round -- nothing in the model was wrong, the BWP/BATC arm simply had zero executable rows, measured: the deleted-shadow mutant left both differentials at 25/0 and 27/0 before the change.

39 real mutants plus a negative control, 39/39 killed. The oracle asks the REAL m88k_translate_v2p() what an address resolves to rather than re-implementing the BATC formula -- computing the right answer in the detector and comparing it against the device's array asserts something strictly weaker, which is the fixed-point-oracle shape the flagship pass named as escape family #1 the same morning.

*** IT WAS CLOSED ONE COMMIT LATE AND DELIBERATELY: *** the first attempt wrote commits='PENDING_M8BATC' and the placeholder check added earlier that day REFUSED IT, correctly. A row is not closed until its hash exists.

entries.note:
*** OUTRANKS ALL SEVEN ROWS OF THE M88K CLUSTER, AND IT WAS IN NONE OF THEM. ***  MEASURED by a seat that built the mutant.

grep -c for BWP|bwp|batc gives 2 in diff_m8invread.c (both PROSE IN COMMENTS) and 0 in diff_m8820x.c -- no executable row anywhere. The mutant: delete `batc[i] = idata;` at dev_m8820x.c:479, leaving regs[...] = idata so read-back still works. *** BOTH DIFFERENTIALS STAY FULLY GREEN, 27/27 and 25/25. ***

The shadow batc[] is what m88k_translate_v2p reads at memory_m88k.c:152 -- BEFORE the PATC and BEFORE the walk -- so a stale entry silently returns a wrong physical address for a 512 KB block. The guest programs it: pmap.c:761-772 pmap_map_batc(), live code.

Of the THREE arms in this device that touch translation inputs, two are covered and the third has zero rows. This is the counter-vs-ground-truth class that m8invground claimed falsely, at the arm where it is ACTUALLY TRUE -- and the same seat measured both, which is why the pair is worth reading together.

*** THE ORACLE DESIGN IS THE POINT: it asks the REAL m88k_translate_v2p() what an address resolves to, rather than re-implementing the BATC formula in the detector. ***  Computing the right answer in the harness and comparing it against the device's array asserts something STRICTLY WEAKER than 'the device's array is what translation reads' -- which is exactly the fixed-point-oracle shape the flagship pass named as escape family #1 this morning. Three controls rather than one, so 'the expected paddr came back' cannot be a constant.

*** FINDING 1: A MUTANT ESCAPED EVERYTHING, AND THE ROUND'S OWN HARDENING CREATED IT. ***  Widening the translator's virtual match from 0xfff80000 to 0xfff00000 survived all 45 rows and both differentials. The first port table used CONSECUTIVE LBAs (0x100..0x107), which caught that mutant BY ACCIDENT -- port n's address hit port n-1's entry. Scattering the LBAs to close a DIFFERENT hole (a masked top bit no row could see) SILENTLY REMOVED THAT ACCIDENTAL COVERAGE, and only re-running the whole census after the fixture change surfaced it.

That is a general lesson worth more than the row: A FIXTURE CHANGE CAN DELETE COVERAGE NOBODY KNEW THEY HAD, and no row goes red to say so. Closed by F17, which asserts the block boundary EXPLICITLY -- first byte in, last byte in, byte below, byte above, per port -- instead of relying on an occupied neighbour. F17 is currently the ONLY row defending that property.

FINDING 2: the seat's own chosen mutant escaped -- c-> vs cpu-> on the purge callback POINTER -- and it graded it honestly as an EQUIVALENT MUTANT and a SHAPE PIN rather than a live defect, because cpu_m88k.c:121-122 gives every m88k cpu the same function with no branch. But it checked whether that is ARCHITECTURAL and found it is not: cpu_mips.c:120-133 and cpu_ppc.c:122-135 install DIFFERENT callbacks per cpu width. Closed with a second spy and row J6.

It also SIMULATED selfmutant.py's tree shape exactly -- symlink mirror plus one real file -- to prove the new #include resolves and both row-ids still name exactly one row, WITHOUT running a gate. Build 0.74 s against a 120 s limit.

That is the exact shape #433 removed from dev_m8820x.c, in the same device family, left behind because the sweep was scoped to the device file rather than the translation path.

rows.witness: none, and none can exist without first changing the function: both `exit(1)` sites are unreachable by the enclosing function's own control flow (see the note). A witness would have to add a `goto exception` that skips the status assignment, which is laundering, not witnessing.
rows.state_note:
*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: the CALLS EXIST (claim true) but BOTH SITES ARE UNREACHABLE. This is dormant defensive code, NOT a live host kill -- a real severity downgrade, and the point of establishing it is to stop a round being opened on 'a surviving exit(1)'. ***

`src/cpus/memory_m88k.c` contains exactly **two** `exit(1)` calls, both inside the `switch (pfsr_status)` that runs after the `exception:` label:
  * `:390-394` -- `case CMMU_PFSR_SUCCESS:`, whose own diagnostic reads *"HUH? CMMU_PFSR_SUCCESS:, but exception? TODO"*;
  * `:408-413` -- `default:`, *"Internal error in memory_m88k?"*.

**Both are internal-invariant assertions, and the invariant holds structurally.** `pfsr_status` is initialised to `CMMU_PFSR_SUCCESS` at `:118`, which is what makes the first case look live. But the exception block is reached ONLY through the `exception:` label at `:373`, and:

  * there are **seven** `goto exception` sites -- `:173`, `:213`, `:267`, `:275`, `:300`, `:309`, `:341` -- and **each is preceded, ONE LINE ABOVE, by a fault assignment** at `:172`, `:212`, `:266`, `:274`, `:299`, `:308`, `:340`. Seven gotos, seven assignments, gap of 1 in every case.
  * **control cannot FALL THROUGH into the label**: `:370` is `return (accumulated_flags & PG_RO)? 1 : 2;`, immediately above it.

So `pfsr_status` is never `CMMU_PFSR_SUCCESS` at `:388`, and the `default:` arm is unreachable for the same reason -- the seven assigned values are exactly WRITE, SFAULT, SUPER and PFAULT, and all four have their own cases at `:397-406`.

**DISPOSITION: assessed, NOT a live defect, and it ranks BELOW anything guest-drivable.** The fork de-fatalises sites a guest can drive; these are sites a guest cannot reach without a code change. That is the distinction the queue ordering depends on, and the row previously read as though this were an ordinary surviving host kill.

**WHAT WOULD RE-OPEN IT, stated so the absence record is falsifiable:** any new `goto exception` that does not assign `pfsr_status` first, or any new writer of `pfsr_status`. The check is the same one run here and it is mechanical -- **the seven gotos and seven assignments must stay paired.** If that pairing is ever broken, the `SUCCESS` case becomes live and a guest-triggered fault kills the host.

*Method note: the pairing was derived by matching each `goto exception` to the nearest preceding non-SUCCESS assignment, then confirming no fall-through path into the label. Both halves are needed -- the gap check alone would miss a fall-through, and the fall-through check alone would miss an unassigned goto.*

rows.title: hpcabort  Three of eight hpcmips subtypes ABORT at construction, and no gate covers hpcmips at all

closure.note:
Shipped as a29f87b. *** THE ROUND DID NOT FULLY CLOSE THE MACHINES AND SAYS SO: *** fixing the abort exposed a second layer it had been masking -- the three subtypes now exit 1 with 'More than one console input is in use', because dev_vr41xx_init already adds an ns16550 with in_use=1. Two remedies are measured working (8/8 each) and NEITHER was applied, because choosing between them needs a judgement the round cannot ground: which of the two UARTs is the console on real hardware. Pinned by a fail-closed allowlist row (EXPECT_X_ONLY = 3), to be edited to 0 by whatever closes it -- pinned, not hidden.

Also weighed: VRIP_INTR_SIU is a JUDGEMENT, not a measurement -- there is no VR41xx datasheet in this tree, the same gap as SH. The FORM is measured; the line number is not, and the code comment says which is which.

entries.note:
MEASURED on the committed build/gxemul while establishing reachability for the vr41xx site:
    e105  rc=134 (SIGABRT, core dumped)      z50                   rc=0
    be300 rc=134 (SIGABRT, core dumped)      mobilepro770          rc=0
    vr3   rc=134 (SIGABRT, core dumped)      mobilepro780/800/880  rc=0
gdb: interrupt_handler_lookup() -> abort(), 'interrupt_handler_lookup("0") failed', from devinit_ns16550 <- device_add <- machine_setup_hpcmips.

CAUSE IS IN THE SOURCE: machine_hpcmips.c:84 and :114 pass irq=0 -- a bare "0", not an interrupt path like machine[0].cpu[0].2 -- and :242 passes irq=%i with an integer. Those three lines map to exactly BE300 (:72), E105 (:102), VR3 (:223). *** THREE BAD SITES, THREE ABORTING SUBTYPES, 1:1. ***  The /* TODO: irq? */ above :114 is the author's own flag. Upstream defect, inherited: git log shows only 39748e3. Identical in est/ and SEC.

*** GATE BLIND SPOT: hpcmips APPEARS NOWHERE UNDER regress/ *** -- no construction row, no grep, nothing. The shipped binary advertises eight subtypes in -H and core-dumps on three of them, and no gate can say so.

Rung 2 and VALID: this IS a construction-time defect, which is exactly the case rung 2 licenses. Already reproduced. FIX + DETECTOR (the first hpcmips construction row in regress/). Ranked SECOND behind the vr41xx narrowing, deliberately: the silent defect outranks the loud one by this project's own dev_footbridge.c:136-141 reasoning -- a guest waiting forever on a tick that never comes is worse than a loud recoverable fault.

*** WITNESS BUILT AND REPRODUCED, 24/24, deterministic across two runs. ***  The failing call is INTERRUPT_CONNECT(devinit->interrupt_path, d->irq) at dev_ns16550.c:342, reached only via device_add() from the machine-setup switch.

RUNG 2 IS THE CEILING, NOT A SHORTCUT, and the seat argued it rather than asserting it: a rung-3 cold-debugger probe needs a CONSTRUCTED machine and construction is what aborts; rung 4 needs that plus an image, and there is no hpcmips image in _images/. The rung-1 exclusion is respected -- nothing is #included, no function called directly, no stub substituted. Strip the machine description and this measures nothing, BECAUSE THE MACHINE DESCRIPTION IS THE DEFECT'S CARRIER. That is exactly the case the ladder licenses rung 2 for.

    subtype                      rc            class           failing name
    be-300                       -6 SIGABRT    ABORT_LOOKUP    "0"
    e-105                        -6 SIGABRT    ABORT_LOOKUP    "0"
    agenda (vr3)                 -6 SIGABRT    ABORT_LOOKUP    "17"
    workpad, mobilepro770/780/800/880   0      CONSTRUCTED_OK  --

*** THE STRONGEST CONTROL IS DERIVED FROM SOURCE CALL ORDER RATHER THAN HARDCODED, and it is also the fix-design measurement: ***  BE-300 and E-105 call device_add BEFORE dev_vr41xx_init, so the process prints SIX handlers (machine[0].cpu[0].2-7, no vrip.); VR3 calls dev_vr41xx_init first, so it prints SIXTY-FOUR including vrip.*. Both predictions matched. A DISCRIMINATION control also passes: -E mvmeppc -e mvme1600 really does SIGABRT, with a different message, and classifies ABORT_OTHER -- 'the process died' is not the same claim as 'it died HERE'.

*** A BUFFERING TRAP BIT IT FIRST, and it is worth carrying: abort() does not flush stdio, so with output to a pipe the diagnostic VANISHED and be-300 produced a 43-BYTE FILE. ***  The probe now requires stdbuf -o0 -e0 and rows go red if an aborting run's diagnostic did not arrive. A probe that reads an empty file as 'no diagnostic' would have mis-attributed the defect entirely.

LINE NUMBERS RE-DERIVED AT RUN TIME rather than remembered -- and this time the brief's were RIGHT (:84, :114, :242, cases :72, :102, :223), which is worth recording given that the previous round's brief had five wrong. Two corrections: the /* TODO: irq? */ appears above TWO of them (:83, :113), not one, and VR3 has a different TODO at :237-238. VRIP_INTR_SIU = 9 at vripreg.h:284, so VR3's 8+VRIP_INTR_SIU is 17.

THE FIX DESIGN IS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED -- and two obvious 'fixes' are measured WRONG.

The five working hpcmips subtypes are no model: THEY ADD NO ns16550 AT ALL. The tree's idiom is at 14 sibling sites (machine_cobalt.c:73 irq=%s.cpu[%i].5, machine_evbmips.c:74, machine_arc.c:156/161, machine_sgi.c:394/400). The registered names come from dev_vr41xx.c:691-702: "%s.cpu[%i].vrip.%i", i = 0..25. Probed on a CONSTRUCTED z50 through the same device_add -> DEVINIT -> INTERRUPT_CONNECT path:
    irq=machine[0].cpu[0].vrip.9    ACCEPTED, device added, rc=0
    irq=machine[0].cpu[0].vrip.25   accepted (last registered line)
    irq=machine[0].cpu[0].vrip.26   ABORTS  <- boundary control, so acceptance is a real lookup
    irq=0 / irq=17                  abort (matches construction)
    omit irq= entirely              *** ABORTS *** -- device.c:281-282 defaults to
                                    machine[0].cpu[0], which is NOT registered on MIPS
    irq= (empty)                    *** ABORTS *** -- interrupt.c:174-179 has NO return; the
                                    'No interrupt' branch fills the template and then FALLS
                                    INTO the scan loop and aborts anyway

*** SO 'JUST DELETE THE irq=' IS NOT A FIX, MEASURED TWICE OVER. ***  The fix is irq=%s.cpu[%i].vrip.%i with machine->path, machine->bootstrap_cpu, VRIP_INTR_SIU -- AND BE-300/E-105 MUST MOVE device_add AFTER dev_vr41xx_init, which the six-versus-sixty-four handler count proves is necessary rather than tidy.

UPSTREAM, NOT THIS FORK: git log --all on machine_hpcmips.c shows exactly one commit, 39748e3 'Import GXemul 0.7.0', and git blame attributes every line of all three sites to that boundary commit.

HONEST LIMIT the seat insisted on: whether vrip.9 is the CORRECT hardware line for these UARTs is NOT measurable here -- there is no VR41xx datasheet in _scratchpad/ (the same gap as SH). VRIP_INTR_SIU is the tree's own name for the serial unit and the source's TODO is explicitly unsure. Treat the line number as a judgement and the FORM as measured.

entries.note:
DETECTOR SHIPPED: regress/hpcmips_ctor_probe.py, 26 rows, ~8 s, 26/26 fixed and 17/26 pre-fix. Seven mutants; five die to behavioural rows.

*** TWO OF THEM ARE THE FINDING, AND THEY COMPILE TO THE IDENTICAL BINARY. ***  vrip.10 IS registered, so a wrong-but-well-formed interrupt line connects IN COMPLETE SILENCE -- the first version of the detector scored that mutant 26/26. VRIP_INTR_SIU+1 and VRIP_INTR_WRBERR both resolve to 10 and produce byte-identical binaries, which is itself the proof that NO RUN-BASED ROW COULD EVER SEPARATE THEM FROM THE FIX.

Closed by tightening S1 from 'mentions the symbol' to 'passes VRIP_INTR_SIU itself, whole, as one argument, with no arithmetic on it' -- a SOURCE-TEXT row, and the file says so. The justification is historical rather than invented: THE DEFECT BEING FIXED WAS AN ARITHMETIC ADJUSTMENT OF THIS CONSTANT (8+VRIP_INTR_SIU). Catching it behaviourally needs a guest load reading back which VRIP line latched -- a rung-3 probe and separate work.

*** A TRAP WORTH CARRYING: MAX_CMD_BUFLEN = 72 (debugger.c:107) TRUNCATES A DEBUGGER COMMAND LINE IN SILENCE. ***  Two probe commands were 73 and 78 characters; the path's trailing digits were eaten and one row read as a failure OF THE FIX. Only the row that compares the failing name against the exact string it SENT caught it -- which is why it does that.

*** BIG-ENDIAN SH-4 IS CONSTRUCTIBLE TODAY, and the naive fix is measurably wrong on it: *** byte_order(big) with in-tree type("landisk") gives a real BE CPU, and there `idata & 0x3ffd` takes the WRONG halfword -- the guest's 16 bits land in the top half and read back as 0. Design shipped as recommended: service the register's own two bytes in the guest's byte order, diagnose once PER SITE, len < 2 early-out. rows.title: rtclen  A one-token edit to dev_rtc.c:92 re-creates #429's own ADD-becomes-REMOVE defect and passes all 18 detector rows
rows.hold: Detector round: give wr_hz a len, have the stub honour it, add a 2^32 row at len 8. Rolls up rtcbranch/rtczero/rtccore cheaply -- same file, same oracle.

entries.note:
*** THE SMALLEST EDIT THAT BREAKS #429 AND SURVIVES ITS ENTIRE TABLE. ***  MEASURED.

    src/devices/dev_rtc.c:92
    idata = memory_readmax64(cpu, data, len);  ->  idata = memory_readmax64(cpu, data, 4);
On a little-endian guest a 2^32 write yields idata = 0 -> d->hz = 0 -> *** THE ADD BECOMES A REMOVE, *** the exact mechanism diff_rtc_range.c's own header describes. Result: 18 rows, 0 failures, RTC_RANGE_PASS. Invisible because the STUB returns stub_in whole and never looks at len. #427's clamp in timer.c cannot mask it -- the timer is GONE, not clamped.

It came out of a full census over the HZ write path (18 statement deletions + 12 substitutions) which found TEN survivors. The other nine worth naming: `>` -> `>=` (see [[rtcbranch]]); deleting `if (d->timer != NULL)` (:141); deleting `d->timer = NULL` (:144); deleting `d->pending_interrupts = 0` (:145); deleting the `else` at :151; `idata == 0` -> `idata == 1` (a guest asking 1 Hz gets the timer REMOVED -- the 'zero keeps its meaning' rows do not pin that ONLY zero stops it); the 32-bit mask on the pass-through (a true no-op, correct to pass); and timer_add / timer_update_frequency fed raw idata.

THREE STUBS ARE UNFAITHFUL AND EACH HIDES A SURVIVOR: memory_readmax64 ignores len AND cpu (the real one dereferences cpu->byte_order and reads exactly len bytes); timer_remove accepts NULL silently, where the real one (timer.c:155-175) walks to cur == NULL, finds `cur == t` TRUE, then dereferences cur->next -- *** a guaranteed NULL deref that the table survives because no row writes 0 with d.timer == NULL, the ordinary reset path; *** and memory_writemax64 is a no-op with no row doing a MEM_READ, so the guest readback (dev_rtc.c:110) is asserted nowhere.

fatal is faithful in the respect that matters -- debugmsg.c:384 calls va_debug and does not exit -- so pass 3's 'REFUTED BY SOURCE' record is correct.

rows.title: pitcount  The 8253 models no decrementing count, so OpenBSD's delay() never returns -- under every design discussed, INCLUDING the one that shipped
