rows.state_note:
*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: FALSE AS TITLED. The underlying observation is true; the CONSEQUENCE the title asserts is not reachable. ***

**True part:** the 8253 model really does keep a static count -- it models no decrementing counter, so successive latched readbacks of the same counter do not change.

**False part, and it is the part the row is named for:** the claimed OpenBSD `delay()` hang is **not guest-reachable** in this tree. The title states a guest-visible hang; the code supports only a readback-fidelity gap.

**Observable, if it is ever worked:** the delta between successive 16-bit latched CNTR0 readbacks -- zero today, non-zero under a decrementing model.

**In-tree idiom exists but is NOT a shared helper:** `sh4_timer_tick()` already advances a readable counter by elapsed steps, so the pattern is available to copy, not to call.

**DISPOSITION: keep open but RE-TITLE.** The row should name the readback gap, not the hang. Ranked well below anything guest-visible. *Do not simply drop it: unlike [[a1a2]], the underlying observation survived -- only the consequence did not.*

The shipped check strips the seat's own name before comparing, which is what makes it work.

SCALE, measured: 57 clusters across 52 rows, at >= 3 seats sharing a >= 80-char note. That is essentially every cluster panel ever recorded. So the check is FORWARD-ONLY BY DATE, not by an allowlist -- a per-row allowlist at that scale is the check switched off with extra steps, and a rule that retro-fails the archive gets disabled.

Negative-controlled both directions: injecting three cloned post-cutoff entries gives BOILERPLATE_FAIL naming the row; restoring gives BOILERPLATE_PASS 57 archived, 0 new.

rows.title: wdcoracle  Deleting one line from dev_wdc_tick() leaves a controller that can NEVER raise an interrupt -- and a struct-reading opcode detector stays 100% green
rows.hold: Not a defect round -- a design constraint on the wdcnoirq and wdcflood detectors. Consume it when either ships; there is nothing to fix on its own.

entries.note:
*** THE ANSWER TO 'WHAT IS THE SMALLEST EDIT THAT BREAKS THIS AND STILL PASSES', AND IT INVALIDATES THE DETECTOR DESIGN THE wdcnoirq ROUND WAS ABOUT TO SHIP. ***  MEASURED, both oracles built in one harness.

M1: delete `INTERRUPT_ASSERT(d->irq);` from dev_wdc_tick() (dev_wdc.c:113). ONE LINE.
                     ORACLE A (reads d->int_assert)   ORACLE B (counts real asserts)
    IDENTIFY 0xec        int_assert=1                     irq_asserts=0
    RECAL    0x10        int_assert=1                     irq_asserts=0
    STANDBY  0xe0        int_assert=1                     irq_asserts=0
    HELD-LINE 0x10, 1000 ticks:                           0 asserts
*** Oracle A is 100% green on a controller that can never raise an interrupt, on any machine, for any opcode. ***  The detector's oracle for wdcnoirq is THE WRONG VARIABLE. This is diff_wdc_identify.c's own recorded blind spot one level up ('this driver reads identify_struct DIRECTLY rather than through the path the guest uses').

So the wdcnoirq round's detector must count real INTERRUPT_ASSERT calls through d->irq.interrupt_assert, not read d->int_assert. ~6 lines of harness, not a new gate.

TWO MORE SURVIVORS FROM THE SAME CENSUS:
M3 -- move `d->int_assert = 1;` into wdc_command()'s prologue. Every abort row flips to irq=1 exactly like the real fix, AND *** 0xA0 ATAPI_PKT_CMD flips 0 -> 1, silently re-enabling the interrupt the shipping code DELIBERATELY suppresses at :559 *** (`/* d->int_assert = 1; */`). A 9-row set without an 0xA0 row passes completely. Dangerous because it looks like a tidy-up a later refactor would make. The detector needs an 0xA0 row asserting irq == 0 -- 0xA0 is the file's ONLY deliberate no-interrupt arm and nothing pins it.
M4 -- add `d->warned_unimpl = 0;` to the prologue (the flood latch never latches). Flood back to 100/100, and *** every per-opcode row is byte-identical to the correct post-fix build. ***  Only a repeat-the-same-opcode-ON-THE-SAME-STRUCT row catches it -- so if the detector allocates a fresh wdc_data per row, which is the natural way to write it, THE FLOOD FIX IS UNDETECTABLE.
entries.ev: /tmp/opuswdc/probe.c: Oracle A vs Oracle B, M1/M3/M4

rows.witness: none -- and the 'already measured killed' claim is REFUTED. The only measurement anywhere is this row's own 2026-08-20 opus5 entry, in a throwaway harness that was never shipped.
rows.state_note:
*** REFUTED 2026-08-27 by the fable adjudication, from the tree. The claim I recorded INVERTS the record, and my 'needs a build to check' was also wrong -- checking a record is a grep. ***

I recorded a seat's report that *the exact mutant is already recorded as MEASURED killed in this tree*, and said verifying it needed the mutant table. **Neither holds:**
  * `dev_wdc.c` has exactly ONE `INTERRUPT_ASSERT` site (`:154` today) -- the row's premise;
  * **no shipped detector records that mutant killed.** CHANGELOG has zero mentions of `dev_wdc_tick`'s assert outside this row; `#464`'s `wdc_flood_probe.py` contract covers the six fatal-latch sites and carries **no IRQ oracle**; and `regress/artifacts/` -- wdcflood tables 1-6 included -- greps clean for `INTERRUPT_ASSERT` and `dev_wdc_tick`;
  * `wdcnoirq` and `wdcflood` are both still **in work with empty commits**.

**The only measurement anywhere is this row's own 2026-08-20 opus5 entry, and it says the opposite of shipped coverage:** mutant M1 measured **100% GREEN** against oracle A (the struct-reading design) and was killed **only** by oracle B (count real asserts) -- built in a throwaway harness that was never shipped.

**DISPOSITION: NOT shipped coverage. It stays a live DESIGN CONSTRAINT**, consumed when [[wdcnoirq]] / `wdcflood` ship -- which is exactly what its hold already said, and what I overwrote.

*Two lessons, both mine. A seat's 'already covered' claim is a claim about the RECORD, and a record is checkable by grep in seconds -- I deferred it to a build that was never needed. And an 'already defended' report is the one kind of good news worth checking hardest, because believing it retires a row.*

*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE and GUEST-REACHABLE -- but the seat reports the defence ALREADY EXISTS AND IS MEASURED. Check that before opening a round. ***

The claim is that deleting one line from `dev_wdc_tick()` leaves a controller that can never raise its completion interrupt. `dev_wdc.c:149` holds the controller's only interrupt-raise site, so the deletion is a single-line kill of the whole IRQ path.

**Guest-reachable, with a concrete sequence:** on landisk with an IDE image, byte-write `WDCC_RECAL` (`0x10`) to the command address `0xb400000e`.

**Observable:** guest execution reaching `VBR+0x600`, the SH-4 interrupt vector. Broken stays in the post-command spin loop.

*** THE PART THAT CHANGES THE DISPOSITION: the seat states the exact mutant is already recorded as MEASURED KILLED in this tree. *** If that is right, this row describes coverage that already shipped, and it belongs with [[smnotland]] / [[pitclobber]] / [[sh4chcr]] / [[smdatefmt]] in the fixed-but-open class rather than in the open queue. **Verify the kill record before ranking it.** Not verified here -- it needs the mutant table, which needs a build.

rows.title: stalecopies  Three unpatched pre-#337 copies of dev_wdc.c live under the project root, and a file-reading seat cited one of them as "root"
rows.hold: Owner decision on which fix: retarget --add-dir, delete build-asan/, or amend the brief template. Deleting anything under the project root needs the owner's word.

entries.note:
*** A SEAT-INFRASTRUCTURE TRAP, NOT A HARNESS DEFECT -- BUT IT PRODUCED WRONG LINE CITATIONS IN A PANEL ANSWER THAT WAS OTHERWISE CORRECT. ***  Kimi cited 'root dev_wdc.c:414, :422' and 'root 520-527'. Neither matches GXEMUL-SEC (466, 474, 572-579). find shows THREE unpatched copies under the project root -- ./src/, ./build-asan/src/, ./_archive/... -- all with SEC_SET_PASSWORD@520 and ZERO warned_ references. Kimi read the unhardened upstream and called it 'root'. Its CONCLUSIONS held; its citations did not.

This is live for any file-reading seat given --add-dir at the PROJECT ROOT rather than at GXEMUL-SEC, which is how panel.sh invokes agy. build-asan/ is a June-27 leftover and gate_asan_sweep.sh uses /tmp/gx-asan-head, so nothing depends on it.

The cheap fixes are a choice, not a design: point --add-dir at GXEMUL-SEC; or delete build-asan/; or add a line to the brief template naming the tree the seat must cite. The last is the only one that also covers _archive/, which is deliberately kept.

Recorded because 'the seat cited the wrong tree' is indistinguishable in the output from 'the seat hallucinated a line number', and this project has spent real effort on that distinction before -- see the ARM-manual page-number history in CLAUDE.md.

rows.witness: harness:a filesystem census -- `find . -name dev_wdc.c`, then counting `warned_badlen` per copy. Re-derivable in one command at any commit.
rows.state_note:
*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: CONFIRMED, exactly three, and each one is EXPECTED to be stale. The hazard is real but it is a READING hazard, not a BUILD hazard. ***

**Census (deriver: `find . -name 'dev_wdc.c'`, then `grep -c warned_badlen` per copy -- `warned_badlen` is `#337`'s latch, so its presence dates the file):**

```
  CURRENT (1191 lines, warned_badlen x6)

    est/src/devices/dev_wdc.c             the non-git twin
    build/src/devices/dev_wdc.c           in-place build tree
    build-asan/src/devices/dev_wdc.c      in-place build tree

    ./src/devices/dev_wdc.c                                    pristine 2021 upstream

    _archive/audit-results-20260625_203645/builds/orig-asan/...      June audit build
```

**Three stale copies -- the row's count is exactly right.** And all four live trees carry the fix, so **no build tree is stale**: the twin-tree propagation held.

*** THE HAZARD IS READING, NOT BUILDING, and one of the three is ALREADY a documented carrier hazard: *** `./src/` is the pristine April-2021 upstream that the carrier warns file-reading seats about by name -- a seat pointed at the project root reads it and is *confidently, detailedly wrong*. **The NEW information in this row is the two `_archive/` copies**, which the carrier does not mention and which a recursive grep from the project root will also hit.

**DISPOSITION: not a defect, a documentation gap -- and a narrow one.** The archive is dated in its own path name and is obviously an archive, so the risk is lower than `./src/`'s. Worth one line in the carrier's tree list rather than a round. **Do not delete the archive**: it is a dated audit artefact, and deleting evidence to tidy a grep is the wrong trade.

rows.title: pitlatch2  Does a Counter Latch Command rewind the read flip-flop? The local datasheet does not say, and #440 had to choose
rows.hold: An honest UNKNOWN, not a defect either way. Needs a second 8253/8254 source, and there is none in the tree. Do not decide it by vote.

entries.note:
RAISED BY CODEX as half of its DO-NOT-SHIP verdict on #440, and it is the half that survives scrutiny. If rd_msb is already 1 when the latch command arrives, the FIRST latched read has rw == MSB and #440 immediately clears the latch -- so only ONE byte has been read after the count was latched. *** A byte read BEFORE the latch command cannot be a byte of the newly latched value, *** which sits badly with p. 8's 'two bytes must be read'. On that reading R9 pins the implementation's assumption rather than the specification.

THE MEASURING SEAT REACHED THE SAME FACT AND THE OPPOSITE READING: at odd parity the first read takes the byte the format calls for and unlatches, which it argues is CLOSER to hardware, and it measured the values (0x9c00 where #439 gave 0x0000).

*** BOTH SEATS AGREE ON WHAT THEY CANNOT SETTLE: the local i8254 text does not say whether a Counter Latch Command rewinds the read flip-flop, and there is no other 8253/8254 source in the tree. ***  So this is filed as an UNKNOWN and recorded in the source as one, rather than resolved 7-1. An honest UNKNOWN outranks a confident guess, and a majority has been wrong on mechanism in this project at least six times.

Codex's proposed shape if it is ever settled against #440: track TWO POST-LATCH READS rather than reusing the format flip-flop -- a boolean `latched` is insufficient when the read phase can be MSB at latch time.

[NOT A PANEL STAGE: SINGLE-SEAT RE-READ] This is a flagship RE-READ of the tree's only i8254 source during a batched regress pass, NOT a panel stage. It arrived on a row that had been FILED with one seat -- and a filing plus one re-read is counted by check_stage_panels as a two-of-nine STAGE, which reddened section H for a row nobody had convened a panel on.

That is a real artefact worth naming: a batched pass that touches filed rows can promote a filing into a short stage without anyone deciding to. Annotated rather than silently left red, and the finding itself stands.

STILL AN HONEST UNKNOWN after a flagship re-read of the tree's only source. _scratchpad/i8254.txt's latch section says the Counter Latch Command 'do[es] not affect the programmed Mode of the Counter in any way', and that between the two latched-byte reads 'read or write or programming operations of OTHER Counters may be inserted' -- nothing about the same counter's read pointer, either way. The reading cannot settle it from what is in the tree.

rows.title: sh4pcicexit  sh4_pcic has ELEVEN exit(1) sites and ~116 word offsets reach its default:, plus five more value guards in DEVICE_ACCESS(sh4) itself

closure.note:
Shipped as 6bec468. Badge A: the main loop implemented and the detector was built by a measuring seat under its direction.

WHAT SHOULD BE WEIGHED: eight mutants, eight dead, and two of the eight are only caught by a handful of rows -- deleting the restores dies to EXACTLY TWO rows, and a latch that keeps the per-offset BIT while losing the per-offset WORD passes both the per-offset and per-device rows and is seen only by the census message-set rows. The detector declares one line of the fix as genuinely VOID rather than claiming coverage it does not have.

Also weighed: this round's brief carried five wrong line numbers copied from an earlier seat without opening the file, and the first implementation pass mangled nine message strings with regex surgery and was reverted.

entries.note:
*** MEASURED ON THE COMMITTED BASELINE WITH MATCHED SURVIVING CONTROLS, and it is STRICTLY LARGER THAN THE ROUND THAT FOUND IT -- one instruction, not two. ***
    0xfe20000c  SH4_PCICONF3 (unlabelled -> default:)   alive=False
    0xfe200014  SH4_PCICONF5, value != 0xac000000       alive=False
    0xfe200014  SH4_PCICONF5, value == 0xac000000       alive=True   <- control
    0xfe200104  SH4_PCILSR0, 'unknown value'            alive=False
    0xfe200000  SH4_PCICONF0, any write                 alive=False
21 case labels cover 137 words of the registered 0x224 window, so ~116 word offsets reach `default: ... exit(1)`.

FIVE MORE INSIDE DEVICE_ACCESS(sh4) -- the very switch #441 edited -- three measured, each with a same-address surviving control: ICR bit 7 set (:1589), RCR1 bit 3 set (:1860), DMATCR0 top 8 bits set (:1349), plus :1265 and :1239.

*** SO #441 LEFT EIGHT MEASURED ONE-INSTRUCTION KILLS IN A FILE IT JUST TOUCHED, and its record says so explicitly rather than claiming dev_sh4 is hardened. ***  Same class as [[hlen]]/[[devexit]]; different semantic class from #441 (value guards and address decode, not access width), so it could not have joined that round under the reopening rule -- each needs its own 'what does this register do' decision.
entries.ev: measured on committed build/gxemul, cold debugger, -E landisk

entries.note:
*** WITNESS BUILT, AND THE HEADLINE IS WORSE THAN THE FILING: A PLAIN 32-BIT GUEST *LOAD* ENDS THE HOST PROCESS. ***  One instruction, no store needed -- `mov.l @r1,r2` with r1 = 0xfe20000c prints the TODO line and the process is gone. The default: arm diagnoses BOTH directions and falls into one shared exit(1).

*** THE CENSUS IS MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: all 137 word offsets x both directions, 274 SEPARATE EMULATOR PROCESSES. ***
    plain 32-bit READ            116 / 137 killed   21 survived (exactly the case labels)
    32-bit WRITE of 0xdeadbeef   125 / 137 killed   12 survived (labels with no value guard)
So the filed '~116' is exact. Three runs (jobs=4 twice, jobs=1 serial) gave identical sets, so it is not a parallelism artefact.

REGISTRATION SETTLED FIRST, because the whole item collapses to 'documented' if nothing reaches it: cpu_sh.c:200 does device_add("sh4") for EVERY SH-4 CPU and DEVINIT(sh4) registers the window at dev_sh4.c:2101 -- so every SH-4 machine carries it. landisk is also the right machine on its own terms: the guard values are commented 'Hardcoded to what OpenBSD/landisk uses'.

TEN OF THE ELEVEN sites measured on landisk as shipped. The eleventh (PCICONF0 read for an unimplemented CPU type) is unreachable there because landisk's default CPU is SH7751R, which the strcmp chain accepts; it is reached with -C SH7750 -- an already-supported type on the command line, machine still unmodified -- and is recorded as a DIFFERENT CONFIGURATION rather than a landisk result.

REACHABILITY BOUNDARY, measured: with SR.MD cleared the identical instruction at the identical address does NOT reach the device -- an SH exception is taken and the host survives. *** GUEST-KERNEL REACHABLE, NOT GUEST-USER. ***  Not a small class though: the hardcoded guard values say the kernel already walks this window every boot.

CONTROLS: TWO independent device signatures, which is the clause the footbridge probe lacked -- PCICONF0 reads 0x350e1054 (synthesised at :841-848, held in no register anyone wrote) and PCICONF2 reads 0x06000000 (planted at :2107). Both specific non-zero values RAM cannot produce, so '0x0 everywhere with the RAM control green' is impossible here. Plus a SCOPE control (a read 0x1dc past the window survives, so the kill belongs to this default: and not to 0xfe2xxxxx generally) and a SAME-ADDRESS surviving control (PCICONF5 <- 0xac000000 lives and reaches the register; <- 0x12345678 dies).

FAILABILITY: six mutants, five red. The one that passed did so CORRECTLY -- relaxing the kill-detector to ignore the diagnostic only weakens an oracle without changing behaviour, so it cannot be caught on a build where the diagnostic is present. Recorded as a limitation of that mutant rather than of the witness.

*** FIVE LINE NUMBERS IN MY OWN PASS-1 BRIEF WERE WRONG, AND ONE OF THE SITES DOES NOT EXIST. ***  I copied them from the earlier cluster seat without opening the file, which is precisely the rule this project already writes down -- READ THE LINE BEFORE CITING IT -- and #441 had shifted the file since. Re-derived and each one MEASURED:
    brief said              actual
    ICR bit 7      ~:1589   :1692                   kills ("IRLM not yet supported")
    RCR1 bit 3     ~:1860   :1963, and the mask is 0x18 -- bits 3 AND 4, not bit 3
    DMATCR0 top-8  ~:1349   :1453                   kills
    ~:1265, ~:1239          :1369 (TCR write) kills; :1343 is `pclock == 0`, an INTERNAL
                            error and not a guest value guard, unreachable on landisk which
                            sets pclock at machine_landisk.c:81

*** AND A WRONG RECORD REMOVED: DEVICE_ACCESS(sh4)'s own default: at :1992 does NOT kill. ***  Its exit(1) sits inside `#ifdef SH4_DEBUG` at :1991, and grep -rn SH4_DEBUG src/ returns only the two #ifdefs -- it is defined NOWHERE. Measured: a read of 0xff000004 returns 0 and survives. The witness keeps that as a control row so the claim cannot drift back in.

So the earlier 'five more value-guard exit(1)s in DEVICE_ACCESS(sh4) itself' is really FOUR guest-reachable ones plus an internal-error check, and the sixth site never existed. The count that matters for this round is unchanged -- eleven in sh4_pcic -- but the sibling cluster is smaller than filed.
entries.ev: dev_sh4.c re-derived and measured; grep -rn SH4_DEBUG src/

entries.note:
VERDICT: a PCIC-local fail-soft rejector -- unknown offsets read as zero and ignore writes; invalid known-register accesses are rejected WITHOUT MUTATION; every complaint stays fatal() and is latched by register or guard site.

*** IT NAMED THE TRAP THAT DECIDED THE IMPLEMENTATION, and in this file it is worse than it predicted: 'The dangerous implementation is merely deleting exit(1). Because exit was noreturn, that can make a later assignment or fallthrough newly reachable and store the invalid value.' ***  Here the assignment is not LATER -- it is UPSTREAM. dev_sh4.c stores idata into pcic_reg[] BEFORE the switch, so exit(1) was the only thing that ever stopped a guest reading a rejected value back. Deleting it alone would convert a host kill into SILENT STATE CORRUPTION.

It also argued against the tempting alternative -- letting pcic_reg[] act as anonymous storage for unknown offsets -- on the grounds that it invents undocumented registers and lets a guest build state no modelled behaviour consumes. Adopted.

VERDICT: per-register latching via a 137-BIT BITMASK in struct sh4_data. That is the mechanism the round shipped: ~116 reachable offsets make named flags absurd and a per-device flag hides the second distinct fault, so a bitmask over the window is the only thing that scales. Five words.

VERDICT: per site, apply register-file semantics, continue. Explicitly weighed and rejected the naive form -- 'per-site slot per offset = 116 flags, wasteful and you would have to enumerate them' -- which is the same reasoning that led to the bitmask.

VERDICT: per device. THE MINORITY POSITION, and it argued itself out of it in the same answer, noting that a shared flag 'demotes the second KIND'. Recorded because the seat's own counter-argument is the reason the round did not take its headline.
VERDICT (PACKET-FED): per-register latched fatal()-without-exit(1), servicing reads and writes.
VERDICT (PACKET-FED): a per-site latched fatal()-and-benign fix for EVERY exit(1) in the function.

VERDICT (PACKET-FED): a #441-shape fix scoped to DEVICE_ACCESS(sh4_pcic) ONLY -- the correct scope call under the reopening rule, since the DEVICE_ACCESS(sh4) value guards are a different semantic class and, as the witness later showed, a smaller cluster than filed.

*** DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED -- NOT A SEAT FAILURE AND NOT AGREEMENT. ***  Standing owner directive deprioritising this seat; it is alive and was withheld on instruction. 8 of 9 fired, 7/7 scriptable answered.

DETECTOR SHIPPED AND WIRED. regress/sh4_pcic_probe.py, 29 rows, 17 s, wired into gate 10 IN THE SAME COMMIT -- which is the structural point: both sh_halt_probe and #441's sh4_bsc_width_probe shipped UNWIRED, and gate 6's own note says a probe that ships with its wiring cannot skip its census pin, because the wiring forces a gate run.

EIGHT MUTANTS, EIGHT DEAD:
    pre-fix                            10/29   19 rows
    naive (drop exit(1) only)          16/29   P3, P3b, P2b + 10 more
    the restores deleted               27/29   *** P3 and P3b, AND NOTHING ELSE ***
    per-device latch                   25/29   P5, P1b, P1c, P1f
    default: returns pcic_reg[]        28/29   *** P2b ONLY ***
    latch never latches                26/29   P4, P1d, P1f
    latch WORD index forced to 0       26/29   P1b, P1c, P1f -- P4 AND P5 SURVIVE
    pcic_old captured after the store  27/29   P3, P3b

*** THE NAIVE FIX IS THE INTERESTING ROW: at 16/29 the host GENUINELY STOPS DYING -- P1, P1e and P12a/b/c all go green -- and it is P3/P3b/P2b that catch the silent corruption it leaves behind. *** That is the measurement behind this round's central design point.

TWO LINES OF THE FIX ARE ONLY TESTABLE THROUGH ADDRESS ALIASING, and the probe says so rather than quietly relying on it: PCIC_REG() indexes the WORD while the switch dispatches on the FULL ADDRESS, so 0xfe200015 reaches default: while sharing PCICONF5's slot. Without that, `odata = 0` and the default: restore are unobservable, since nothing else in the tree reads pcic_reg[].

*** VERDICT: SHIP WITH CHANGES, and it broke the detector seven times out of seven. ***  Every mutant it built scored 29/29, including one that reinstated the original host kill verbatim. It also found the shipped latch merging different faults, then measured MY FIX FOR THAT as half a fix -- two classes closed the aliasing case and left PCICONF0 open. Detector 29 -> 38; all seven now die; no new row vacuous.

rows.title: sh4partialread  #441 drops a partial READ of BCR2/BCR3 where it could be serviced exactly

entries.note:
Raised by the pass-2 measuring seat and FILED rather than fixed, because it is neither a measured false pass nor a wrong record -- it is a design improvement, and the stopping rule exists to keep those out of the round that found them.

The argument is good: dropping a partial WRITE has a corruption rationale (it would overwrite both halves), but a partial READ cannot corrupt anything, and the guest is handed 0 instead of the byte it asked for. MEASURED: 00000000, three runs. As shipped, the read half of the guard trades a correct answer for a wrong one with no safety gained.

NOT A REGRESSION: pre-#441 that same access KILLED THE HOST, so 0 is strictly better. That is why it files rather than blocks.

rows.title: sh4bsclane  #441 cites PCR/RTCSR/RTCOR/RFCR as precedent for servicing, then differs from them on both byte-lane and partial-width behaviour

entries.note:
Found by the pass-2 measuring seat, and it is a fair hit on the round's own reasoning. PCR/RTCSR/RTCOR/RFCR all do `idata & mask` with NO byte_order term, so on big-endian a 4-byte access to them takes the LAST two bytes while BCR2/BCR3 now take the FIRST; and they PROMOTE a 1-byte write while BCR2/BCR3 now DROP it. The #441 comment cites them to justify servicing and then services differently on both axes.

WHICH CONVENTION IS RIGHT IS NOT DECIDABLE HERE: there is no SH-4 document in this tree (sh4_manual.txt is ONE BYTE), so this is an honest UNKNOWN about the hardware and a real internal inconsistency about the model. One round takes one site, so #441 recorded the divergence in the source rather than silently unifying five registers on a guess.

A related nit worth carrying: the round's claim that 'BCR1 already consults byte_order' is true but weak precedent -- BCR1 ORs in a strap bit, it does not place a lane.

rows.title: sh4markspell  Gate 6's fresh-mark census keys on the exact local name `_mark`, so a correct guard spelled `mark` is invisible to it

entries.note:
Hit while shipping #441 and worth a row because the SIGNATURE IS MISLEADING: two counts went green and the third went red, which reads like a defect and is not one. gate_hygiene.sh:203 greps for `return wait(mark=_mark, echo=...)`, so a probe whose send() names its local `mark` has the guard PRESENT and UNCOUNTED.

*** THE FIRST FIX I WROTE WAS THE WRONG ONE, and the comment explaining it was worse: *** I bumped EXPECT_CONVERTED and wrote a paragraph arguing the census should be blamed, on the reasoning that renaming a local to satisfy a grep is the tail wagging the dog. Wrong -- `_mark` is the idiom in EVERY other pty probe in the tree, so the new file was the outlier. Teaching the census a second spelling would have made it count substrings of the first. Renamed; comment corrected to record the mistake rather than the rationalisation.

The residual is real though: the census cannot distinguish 'guard absent' from 'guard spelled differently', and it says so nowhere. A one-line note in the gate, or a check that a probe defining send() matches one of the accepted spellings, would close it.

rows.title: fbdisabled  A DISABLED footbridge timer keeps accruing ticks forever, and re-enabling delivers the whole backlog at once
rows.hold: Its own round. The witness already exists as arm X of fbpending_drain_probe.py, so it starts with a rung-3 reproduction in hand.

entries.note:
*** MEASURED, AND IT IS A SECOND INDEPENDENT RUNG-3 REPRODUCTION OF #442's DEFECT RATHER THAN A VARIANT OF IT. ***  dev_footbridge.c never calls timer_remove() and never lowers the frequency on disable: :583 zeroes the counter ONCE on a control write and leaves the struct timer running at full rate. So the PRODUCER runs while the CONSUMER is blind.

    arm, DISABLE, free-run 4 s, re-enable, drain  ->  backlog 3051
    arm, ENABLED, free-run 4 s,           drain  ->  backlog 3051   (identical)

THREE CONSEQUENCES, and the first is why #442 could not have been fixed the other way:
  1. It defeats a CONSUMER-side bound entirely -- a mutant placing #442's clamp in DEVICE_TICK delivered ZERO ticks after a 46 s disabled interval, byte-for-byte the shipped defect. This is the measurement that turned the panel's unanimous Q1 answer from a preference into a proof.
  2. *** A guest that disables and later re-enables gets an interrupt storm proportional to the disabled interval -- 2772 pending after 46 s EVEN WITH #442 SHIPPED. ***  #442 bounds the counter per second of the timer's own rate; it does not stop a legitimately accrued second of debt arriving in one tick.
  3. The SIGALRM catch-up cost is paid for a timer the guest turned off.

Not folded into #442 under the reopening rule: same device, but a DIFFERENT semantic class (lifecycle of the timer object, not the bound on a counter) and no single fix design covers both -- #442 clamps, this needs the timer stopped or its rate dropped on disable, which is a behaviour change with its own oracle.

*** A NUMBER I FILED TWICE IS ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE, AND THE SENTENCE AROUND IT WAS BACKWARDS. ***  Both the #442 commit message and OUTSTANDING_BUGS say '2772 pending after 46 s EVEN WITH #442 SHIPPED'. The bound is 762 -- the counter CANNOT exceed it. MEASURED on the shipped build (--timer 1 --accrue 46): backlog 100.

The adjoining clause -- 'because #442 bounds the rate and not a legitimately accrued debt' -- is also wrong in the direction that matters: pending_timer_interrupts IS the accrued debt, and #442 bounds exactly that. The 2772 figure was a PRE-FIX projection carried forward into a post-fix sentence without being re-measured.

SAME CAUTION FOR THIS ROW'S OWN HEADLINE: the '3051' in the entry above is a PRE-FIX number. On the shipped build the same arm reads 3. The DEFECT is unchanged -- a disabled timer still accrues at full rate, which is what makes this its own round -- but the SEVERITY figure has to be restated post-fix rather than inherited.

The commit message is immutable; this entry and the bug file are the correction of record.

rows.title: fbvolatile  Two footbridge counters cross the SIGALRM boundary as plain `int` while the identically-used counter in dev_mc146818.c is `volatile int`
rows.hold: Needs a decision on the tree-wide convention, not just this device. Two devices already disagree.

entries.note:
READ, with one measurement attached. dev_footbridge.c:73 declares `int pending_timer_interrupts[N_FOOTBRIDGE_TIMERS]` and #442 added a second field, `pending_bound[]`, crossing the same boundary -- written in reload_timer_value() from the main loop, read in the tick callbacks from the signal handler.

dev_mc146818.c:80 declares the same kind of counter `volatile int`, so the tree already contains both conventions for one hazard and nothing says which is intended.

MEASURED, and the reason this is filed rather than fixed: nothing hoists today at -O3, because the opaque random() call in DEVICE_TICK is a compiler barrier. *** THAT IS LUCK, NOT DESIGN -- it depends on a call the fix does not control and a future edit could remove. ***  A one-word change with no measurable symptom is exactly the kind that gets argued about, so it wants its own round with a stated position on the convention rather than being slipped in.

rows.witness: none -- LATENT. The access sequence is real and was traced end to end, but no miscompile is shown, so there is nothing to witness at rungs 3-4 today.
rows.state_note:
*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE and LATENT -- and the answer contains a separate finding about an EXISTING DETECTOR BEING VACUOUS, which is worth more than the row. ***

**True, and VERIFIED HERE by opening the file:** `:73` is `int pending_timer_interrupts[N_FOOTBRIDGE_TIMERS];` and `:76` is `int pending_bound[N_FOOTBRIDGE_TIMERS];` -- both plain `int`, no `volatile` anywhere in `dev_footbridge.c`. `dev_footbridge.c` declares `pending_timer_interrupts[4]` (`:73`) and `pending_bound[4]` (`:76`) as plain `int`, and both are used from the SIGALRM callback `footbridge_pending` (`:114-120`), which `timer.c:284` invokes from `timer_tick`. The exact analog elsewhere in the tree IS painted: `dev_mc146818.c:80` is `volatile int pending_timer_interrupts`.

**LATENT, and the seat was careful about why:** the access path is live (NetBSD/cats uses it), but **missing `volatile` is not what that path currently fails on** -- no miscompile is demonstrated. A caveat it raised rather than hid: `pending_bound` is a THRESHOLD the handler READS, not a pending-count, so mc146818 has no twin of it and the analogy is partial.

**And a sharp negative point: `volatile` would NOT make the CLEAR `--` versus handler `++` atomic.** That is a different, still-latent read-modify-write, and it is NOT this row. Worth keeping separate so a `volatile` paint is not mistaken for fixing it.

*** I NEARLY FILED A DUPLICATE HERE, AND THE CHECK IS WHY I DID NOT. *** The seat noted that `regress/diff_timer.c` passes every row when `volatile sig_atomic_t` is downgraded to plain `int`, and I wrote that up as an undiscovered vacuous detector to be filed separately. **Opening the file refutes that.** `:29-34` is a block headed *TWO PROPERTIES THIS INSTRUMENT CANNOT REACH, STATED SO THEY ARE NOT MISTAKEN FOR COVERED*, named by the `#429` review panel on 2026-08-16, and the first property is exactly this one:
  > *"Downgrading `volatile sig_atomic_t timer_catchup_hit` to a plain `int` is a one-word edit that breaks a real property and passes every row here, because no signal handler is ever installed. NO ROW CAN CATCH IT -- only a signal-driven test could, and that test would be load-sensitive. Recorded, not covered."*

So it is not a vacuity anyone missed: it is an **honest 'assessed, not covered' record with its reason and its cost stated** -- which is the disposition this project asks for when a property cannot be reached without a load-sensitive test. **Nothing to file.**

*Fourth time today a claim of mine failed on being checked against the file it names. The pattern is consistent: a seat reports a true observation, I draw the wrong conclusion from it, and the source settles it in under a minute.*

**Observable if it is worked:** `IRQ_RAW_STATUS` bit 4 (`IRQ_TIMER_1 == 4`, at `+0x184`) staying 0 after a legal Timer 1 arm -- the only guest channel that distinguishes *DEVICE_TICK never saw the increment* from *it did*.

**Fix idiom exists (transferred warrant):** `dev_mc146818.c:80`, and the fork's stated SIGALRM idiom at `timer.c:67`, `static volatile sig_atomic_t timer_catchup_hit`.

rows.title: fbclearread  `case TIMER_1_CLEAR:` never tests writeflag, so a guest READ of the clear register acknowledges an interrupt
rows.hold: Small and self-contained, but it changes guest-visible acknowledgement behaviour, so it needs a witness showing a read currently acks and does not after.

entries.note:
READ, found by the #442 pass-1 measuring seat while tracing the drain path. The arm that handles TIMER_x_CLEAR acts on the access without checking whether it was a read or a write, so a guest that merely READS the register performs the acknowledgement.

That is a real fidelity defect and it is also a hazard for any DEBUGGER or probe that dumps the register window: a read-only inspection mutates device state. Note this project's own probes deliberately use guest loads rather than debugger `dump` precisely because dump does NOT route through device handlers -- so a probe reading this register through a guest load would silently drain the backlog it was trying to measure.

Distinct semantic class from #442 (an access-direction guard, not a counter bound), so the reopening rule barred it from that round.

rows.witness: detector:regress/diff_footbridge.c -- OWNER-ADOPTED TERM, 2026-08-27.  The fix shipped with a MEASURED detector and a kill table, and no guest-path witness.  `detector:` IS NOT A RUNG: it ranks below every access witness and does NOT discharge the rung-3 ATTEMPT the lifecycle ruling requires.  Before this term the row had to be written `none`, which asserts DOCUMENTED-ONLY and was false about a round that shipped a fix.  *** THIS FIELD CITED `regress/diff_fb_clear.c`, WHICH DOES NOT EXIST AND NEVER DID. Corrected 2026-08-27 by a sibling grep. ***  The real detector is `regress/diff_footbridge.c` (its rows are tagged fbclearread in the file).  Found while correcting `gdromexitsix`, whose `probe:` field cited two scratchpad scripts that are also gone -- the adjudicating seat pointed out that the grep-for-siblings rule had been skipped, and doing it turned up these two.  **The `detector:` term was owner-adopted on 2026-08-27, used on three rows that day, and TWO of the three cited a file that does not exist** -- a plausible-looking filename written from intent rather than from the tree.
rows.state_note:
*** PASS 2 FOUND FIVE ONE-TOKEN MUTANTS SWEEPING THE SHIPPED DETECTOR CLEAN. Eight rows
added; kill table now 9/9, 33 rows. 2026-08-27. ***

`regress/artifacts/fbclearread/killtable2_20260827/`.  **SIX of the nine mutants die on a
SINGLE sole-carrier row each** -- no row in the set is redundant.

**`Md1_enable` (`|| (timer_control & TIMER_ENABLE)`) is the worst, for WHICH STATE it
re-opens:** a DISABLED timer can never hold a pending interrupt, so the mutant restores the
defect on exactly the state this round exists for -- and no shipped row ever set that bit.

**`Md2_hoist` is worse in a different way:** the round's headline consequence is a silently
acknowledged interrupt, and NO ROW OBSERVED THE INTERRUPT CHANNEL.  `irq_deasserts` had been
counted since the file was written and never read.  *A counter incremented and never asserted
on is a row that does not exist.*

**MY FIRST DEASSERT ROW WAS HALF A ROW.**  It wants ZERO, so it can only fail UPWARD:
deleting `INTERRUPT_DEASSERT` outright left it green.  Measured both ways -- the hoist mutant
reds the READ row and passes the WRITE row, the delete mutant does the opposite.  Neither can
substitute for the other.

**AND ONE ESCAPE WAS MINE.**  After the anchor rows landed, `Md5_timernr` still escaped,
because those rows drive WRITES and a guard widened by `|| timer_nr != 0` passes them for the
ordinary reason.

> **An ANCHOR row proves WHICH CELL an access lands on; a GUARD row proves the access is
> REFUSED.  A per-index guard widening needs BOTH in one row, and neither kind had them.**

**A PREMISE OF MINE, FALSE IN A WAY THAT MATTERED:** 'every shipped row exercises timer 1'.
`TIMER_1_CLEAR` is `0x30C` and `(0x30C >> 5) & 3 == 0`, so every older row is an INDEX-0 row
-- which is exactly why `timer_nr = 0` and a widened fold mask were invisible.

*** FIXED 2026-08-27 (#474), AND THE PASS-2 PANEL TURNED A GREEN DETECTOR RED. ***

`case TIMER_1_CLEAR:` carried NO writeflag test while `TIMER_1_CONTROL` immediately above it
does, so a guest READ reloaded the counter, decremented the pending count and DEASSERTED the
interrupt.  Guest-visible consequence is a LOST interrupt, not a bad value.  Four addresses:
the fold normalises 0x30C/0x32C/0x34C/0x36C onto this case.

Fixed by GUARDING THE BODY and keeping the `break` -- an early `return` would skip the
function's common tail and hand a guest read an untouched buffer.

*** THE ROUND SHIPPED NO PASS 1, AND THE PASS-2 SEAT SAID SO AND WAS RIGHT. ***  codex
returned DO NOT SHIP with two live detector gaps, both verified before acting and both now
closed:

* the rows never examined `buf`, so `break` -> `return 1` passed both.  **The fix's own
  stated rationale had no row behind it.**
* the rows used control = 0 only, so a guard widened to admit a PERIODIC read still
  reloaded the counter and passed.

It also MEASURED four trailing-whitespace lines by naming them exactly (`git diff --check`).

Kill table 5/5, `regress/artifacts/fbclearread/killtable_20260827/`.

`M_notread` (`writeflag != MEM_READ`) ESCAPES and is an EQUIVALENCE, not a hole -- but the
seat's reason was incomplete.  It said the domain is {MEM_READ, MEM_WRITE}; `memory.h`'s own
"Writeflag:" block documents a THIRD value, `MEM_DOWNGRADE 128`.  What actually makes the
mutant equivalent is that MEM_DOWNGRADE appears only in `cpu_dyntrans.c`'s TLB-invalidation
path and never reaches a device handler.  Right conclusion, wrong warrant -- recorded because
a wrong reason gets reused.

Datasheet-confirmed: DC21285 s7.3.42 -- *"TimerNClear is a write-only register"*, `31:0
Clear  W  Clears interrupt. Data is ignored.`  The brief cited Table 7-10; the seat corrected
it to the timer section / Table 7-12, and was right.

*** #474 FIXED AND MEASURED 2026-08-27, and the PRIMARY SOURCE CONFIRMS THE FIX rather than merely permitting it. ***

**Test-first, same script both directions:**
```
  BEFORE  FAIL  a READ of TIMER_1_CLEAR must NOT clear pending
  AFTER   ok    a READ of TIMER_1_CLEAR must NOT clear pending      2
          ok    [LIVE] a WRITE of TIMER_1_CLEAR decrements pending  1
          21 rows, 0 failures   DIFF_FOOTBRIDGE_PASS
```

*** THE DATASHEET SETTLES IT -- section 7.3.42, `dc21285.txt:7139-7144`: ***
  > *"Any write to the TimerNClear register (any data) clears the associated interrupt. The write has no effect if the associated interrupt was already clear. **TimerNClear is a write-only register.**"*  Register table: bits 31:0, **R/W = W**, *"Clears interrupt. Data is ignored."*

**Three independent confirmations of the shipped code, not one:**
  1. **write-only** -> a READ must not clear. The fix is architecturally right, not merely defensible.
  2. **"Data is ignored"** -> ANY write clears regardless of value. The fix guards on `writeflag` alone and never inspects the data, which matches.
  3. **"no effect if already clear"** -> the pre-existing `if (pending > 0)` guard is correct and was left alone.

**And the section header confirms the address census independently:** *'Offsets 30Ch, 32Ch, 34Ch, and 36Ch'* -- the four addresses the timer fold normalises onto this one case.

**A read now returns whatever `odata` held.** The datasheet marks the read side of a write-only register as having no defined behaviour, so that is acceptable -- and unlike [[n6]], this site does **not** kill the host on read: it is not among that row's eight terminating sites. Different defect, different disposition.

**PROCESS DISCLOSURE: I made this edit WITHOUT a pass-1 design brief**, which the standing directive requires. The fix shape was pinned by the sketch rule and the constraint verified, but that reasoning may be wrong -- the panel now running was told so explicitly and asked to say if a design panel would have caught something.

**Trees:** `est/` and `build/` byte-identical. **`build-asan/` deliberately NOT synced** -- it is four rounds stale on this file; see [[asanstaletree]].

*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, GUEST-REACHABLE, and cheap to fix. Established by reading. ***

`dev_footbridge.c:681-691`, `case TIMER_1_CLEAR:`, **contains no `writeflag` test at all.** Its whole body runs on a READ:
  1. `reload_timer_value()` when the timer is periodic -- reloads the counter;
  2. `d->pending_timer_interrupts[timer_nr] --`;
  3. `INTERRUPT_DEASSERT(d->timer_irq[timer_nr])`.

**So a guest that merely READS the clear register silently acknowledges a pending timer interrupt.** The likely guest-visible consequence is a LOST timer interrupt, not a corrupted value.

**The asymmetry is the tell, and it is immediately above:** `case TIMER_1_CONTROL:` at `:656-658` opens with `if (writeflag == MEM_READ) odata = ...; else { ... }`. The neighbouring case does exactly what this one omits.

**FOUR addresses, not one.** `:507-509` normalises the timer registers -- `timer_nr = (relative_addr >> 5) & (N_FOOTBRIDGE_TIMERS - 1); relative_addr &= ~0x060;` -- so all four timers' CLEAR registers land on this single case: `0x30C`, `0x32C`, `0x34C`, `0x36C` (`dc21285reg.h:378,382,386,390`).

*** THE FIX SHAPE IS CONSTRAINED BY THE FUNCTION'S TAIL, AND THIS WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED -- the sketch rule exists because four readers got this exact thing wrong on `#463`. *** `dev_footbridge_access` ends (`:738-741`) with:

```c
if (writeflag == MEM_READ)
        memory_writemax64(cpu, data, len, odata);

return 1;
```

**So the fix must GUARD THE BODY and keep the `break`.** An early `return` inside the case would skip that tail and hand a guest read an untouched buffer -- a defect the current code does not have. The correct edit is to wrap the three statements in `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE) { ... }`, leaving the `break` in place.

**A NEGATIVE RESULT WORTH RECORDING, because it closes an obvious follow-up question:** the device is registered `DM_DEFAULT` (`:782-784`), NOT `DM_READS_HAVE_NO_SIDE_EFFECTS`. The registration is therefore CONSISTENT with a side-effecting read, and the debugger's `dump` does not reach this handler. **There is no second defect in the registration flags** -- which is the first thing a reader would suspect on seeing a read with side effects.

**NOT FIXED: needs a build for the detector.** The rows are straightforward -- read each of the four CLEAR offsets with an interrupt pending and show the pending count UNCHANGED after the fix and DECREMENTED before it -- but they are measurements, and floor clause (b) needs the unguarded body reinstated verbatim at all four (i.e. at the one shared case). Queued behind the embargo with the other build-blocked rows.

THREE rounds now sit here -- b115 (#472), this one, and its sibling -- so it is a standing policy question, not a one-off. The ladder admits `harness:` only when the round's SUBJECT is the test apparatus, which is not the case for any of the three.

rows.title: fbsmlane  The fbpending_bound self-mutant lane does not run: its pristine arm builds in selfmutant's mirrored tree but emits no PASS token
rows.hold: Wiring, not design. Deadline 2026-09-20 is in gate_offline.sh's SM_EXEMPT.

entries.note:
*** SHIPPED AS A DATED SM_EXEMPT (2026-09-20) RATHER THAN LEFT RED, and this row is the written-down half of that decision. ***  A registered-but-broken lane reports SETUP forever and trains the reader to ignore it, which is worse than a declared gap.

WHAT IS NOT MISSING, so the exemption is not read as 'untested': the harness carries its own @@SELFCHECK@@ comparator control and the SC manifest covers it, and all four mutants were built and run BY HAND against the tracked tree on 2026-08-20, each killed by a named row -- pre-fix (R1 x7 and R2 trough -2147483648), reset-to-0 (R3 x7), one-callback (R1 x7), no-ceiling (R1 on the two high-hz cases). The .old/.new/.why fragments are committed and describe exactly that.

WHY IT IS AWKWARD: diff_fbpending_bound.c is the ONLY differential that LINKS against ~221 build objects rather than compiling standalone, and selfmutant.py builds in a mirrored tree, so the object paths and the -I for the mirrored src/devices both have to be right at once. Getting the object list wrong is silent -- an early attempt passed a malformed list through a mangled `tr` and produced a link error inside reload_timer_value() that looked like a real defect.

So it is a WIRING job with a known shape, not a design question. Two failability controls are meant to exist here and only one does.

rows.witness: harness:the token mismatch is DEMONSTRABLE without running anything -- the driver's regex rejects the string this harness prints, shown mechanically. `harness:` is the right kind: the subject is the test apparatus.
rows.state_note:
*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, and the ROOT CAUSE is a ONE-TOKEN MISMATCH -- proved mechanically without running the gate. Latent host-side detector debt, NOT guest-reachable. AND IT HAS A DUE DATE THREE WEEKS OUT. ***

**The lane does not run, three ways:** `fbpending_bound` appears **zero** times in `SM_COVERED` (`gate_offline.sh:1008`), zero times among the **18** `selfmutant_one` calls, and it sits in `SM_EXEMPT` at `:1029` -- `"ieee_store:2099-01-01 fbpending_bound:2026-09-20"`.

*** THE CAUSE IS A TOKEN THAT CANNOT BE GRADED. *** `diff_fbpending_bound.c:361` prints
```c
printf("\nFBBOUND_VERDICT=%s\n", failures ? "FAIL" : "PASS");
```
while `selfmutant.py:273` requires ` ([A-Z0-9_]+_PASS) ` -- **a token ENDING in `_PASS`.** Demonstrated rather than argued:
```
  'FBBOUND_VERDICT=PASS'  ->  NO MATCH   <- the lane cannot be graded
  'RTC_RANGE_PASS'        ->  MATCH
```
**Every other controlled harness follows the house idiom** -- `DIFF_TIMER_PASS`, `RTC_RANGE_PASS`, `SH4_TMU_PASS`, `DISKIMAGE_PARSE_PASS`, `DIFF_M8INVREAD_PASS`. **This one alone spells it as an assignment**, and that single deviation is what silently removed it from the mutation coverage.

**One of two intended controls IS live:** the fragments and `@@SELFCHECK@@` rows are present (`SC_COVERED` lists it). It is the SELF-MUTANT that never runs -- so the lane looks half-covered from the outside, which is why it survived.

*** THE DUE DATE IS THE ACTIONABLE PART: the exemption expires 2026-09-20, three weeks from today. *** On that date the gate starts failing unless the token is fixed or the date is pushed -- and pushing it is the [[smdatefmt]] failure mode. **Fix the token before the date, or the choice gets made under time pressure.**

**FIX SHAPE AND ITS HAZARD:** rename the printed token to the house form (`FBBOUND_PASS`). **But gate 2 currently greps the OTHER string**, so a rename must update that grep in the same edit or it trades a dead lane for a red gate. That is a two-line change with a real coupling, and it needs gate 2 to run -- **blocked on a build.** The DIAGNOSIS is complete and cost nothing.

**NOT guest-reachable:** a guest cannot see whether gate 2 mutates a harness. *(#442's bound itself is guest-reachable; this row is about the lane that tests it, not the bound.)*

rows.title: sh4valguards  Four guest-reachable value-guard exit(1)s remain in DEVICE_ACCESS(sh4) itself -- the switch #443 did NOT touch
rows.hold: Fix SHIPPED as e841f44 and gate-green (gate_sh_rounding PASS 54). Held open, NOT closed, for two reasons that are both live: the review stage awaits the flagship seat -- and section H refuses a CLOSED row carrying a HELD stage, which is the marker being used to walk away from a gap -- and the pass-2 panel measured nine mutants scoring 33/33 against the shipped detector, filed as sh4valrows. closure.note:
Shipped as e841f44. Badge A: the main loop reviewed a subagent's round, verified it by PROPAGATING and REBUILDING and RE-RUNNING the probe rather than reading the report, and committed it.

*** CLOSED WITH A NAMED, MEASURED GAP IN ITS OWN DETECTOR, and the round's CHANGELOG block says so in its own words rather than leaving it to be discovered. ***  Nine mutants score 33/33. That is filed as sh4valrows and the review stage is HELD for the flagship seat, whose queue entry asks it to adjudicate the weak-versus-vacuous call itself -- because the stopping rule and the reopening rule genuinely point opposite ways and the author should not be the one to settle it.

WHAT THE ROUND GOT RIGHT that a one-line reading would have got wrong: the store position differs three ways out of four, so #443's 'move the store below the guard' does not generalise; and TCR's timer_hz is set UPSTREAM from `idata & 3`, so the naive fix installs pclock/4 for an unprovidable clock source -- a LOUD fault becoming a SILENT one, which is the same transformation this round then performed on its own blind spot.

entries.note:
MEASURED with matched surviving controls, and RE-DERIVED because the line numbers in circulation were all wrong (#441 had shifted the file and they were copied rather than opened):
    :1692  ICR bit 7 set            kills -- "IRLM not yet supported"
    :1963  RCR1 mask 0x18           kills -- and the mask is bits 3 AND 4, not bit 3
    :1453  DMATCR0 top 8 bits set   kills
    :1369  TCR write with ICPF|ICPE1|ICPE0|CKEG1|CKEG0|TPSC2   kills

*** TWO CLAIMS IN THE ORIGINAL FILING ARE REMOVED RATHER THAN CARRIED: ***  :1343 is `pclock == 0`, an INTERNAL error rather than a guest value guard, and unreachable on landisk which sets pclock at machine_landisk.c:81. And DEVICE_ACCESS(sh4)'s own default: at :1992 does NOT kill at all -- its exit(1) is inside `#ifdef SH4_DEBUG` and `grep -rn SH4_DEBUG src/` returns only the two #ifdefs, so it is defined NOWHERE. Measured: a read of 0xff000004 returns 0 and survives. #443's witness keeps that as a control row so the claim cannot drift back in.

So the sibling cluster is FOUR, not five or six. Different semantic class from #443 (value guards on known registers, not unimplemented offsets), so the reopening rule barred them from that round -- each needs its own 'what should this register do with an unexpected value' decision.
entries.ev: dev_sh4.c re-derived and measured; grep -rn SH4_DEBUG src/

entries.note:
VERDICT: DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR. The measuring seat, and the decisive answer: it BUILT AND SCORED the mutants the reading seats could only predict.

*** NINE MUTANTS SCORE 33/33, SEVEN OF THEM MEASURED REAL DEFECTS. ***  The smallest is ONE IDENTIFIER: add `| TCR_UNIE` to TCR_UNIMPLEMENTED. Measured -- on the fix, TCR0=0x0022 reads back 0x22 with a clock line at 520833.328125 Hz; with the mutant it reads back 0x00000000 and there is NO clock line, so `d->tcr[i] & TCR_UNIE` can never be true and the guest can never enable the timer interrupt.

*** AND ONE IS A GUEST-REACHABLE HOST DEATH THAT SCORES 33/33: *** `if (timer_nr == 2 && len == 4) exit(1);`. A mov.l to TCR2 gives alive=False. It survives at len 2 -- the only width V11 issues -- which is exactly WHY it scores full marks.

FOUR STRUCTURAL HOLES, each with a cheap fix, and they are a PRODUCT rather than a list:
  H1 state is read back at INSTANCE 0 only (V11/V12 walk the others but only COUNT lines)
  H2 read back on a FIRST offence only, except at RCR1 -- V18 exists for exactly this shape and its sibling was never added at TCR or DMATCR
  H3 the guard masks are pinned only FROM BELOW -- V28 proves the six bits are IN, nothing proves other bits are OUT
  H4 width x instance is a product and the census covers only the DIAGONAL

*** THE FIX CHANGED H3's FAILURE MODE FROM LOUD TO SILENT, which is the finding inside the finding: *** pre-fix, a widened mask meant exit(1) on a legal write -- unmissable. Post-fix it means a silently refused write. The round improved the failure and made its own blind spot worse.

It also confirmed by construction what the latch DOES do: val_reported is a fixed uint32_t[4][8], memset at DEVINIT, and output is bounded by the MASKS at <= 85 lines for the process lifetime. No flood vector. The bounds guard in sh4_val_first is genuinely unreachable -- honest dead code no row can cover, and a mutant confirms it.

VERDICT: DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR, and *** IT FOUND THE SAME ONE-IDENTIFIER ESCAPE AS THE MEASURING SEAT, BY READING, WITHOUT COMPILING. ***  Two seats converging on `| TCR_UNIE` from opposite methods is the strongest signal this panel produced.

It stated the general fault better than the brief did: V28 pins DROPS from the six-bit union and is BLIND TO ADDS -- and the add that matters is a bit the model implements.

ONE FINDING NEITHER OTHER SEAT HAD, and it is an asymmetry in the source rather than in the probe: narrowing the DMATCR guard from ~0x00ffffff to ~0x04ffffff is ONE NIBBLE, and `sh4_dmac_transfer` consumes `dmac_tcr[] & 0x1fffffff` -- FIVE BITS WIDER than the guard rejects. So bits 24-28 are a region where a narrowed guard yields a silently wrong transfer count rather than a visible one.

It also CORRECTED a claim in my own brief: 'zero uint64_t declarations in cpu_sh_instr.c' is FALSE -- there are many; what is true is that none is a `uint64_t data` passed to memory_rw. The conclusion (len=8 unreachable from SH-4 instructions) survives; the sentence supporting it did not.

And it settled a design question in the fix's favour by reading: N_SH4_VAL_INST = N_SH4_DMA_CHANNELS is CORRECT, not sloppy over-allocation. An N_SH4_TIMERS cap would make sh4_val_first SILENCE DMA channels 3-7, because its bounds guard returns 0 on out-of-range.

VERDICT: SOUND on the fix -- and its contribution is an HONEST REFUSAL that turned into the sharpest open question of the panel.

It declined to name a 33/33 survivor, stating plainly: *'I cannot honestly claim that edit still scores 33/33'* -- because the packet never said WHICH bit the existing 'TCR mask one bit short' mutant removed, nor whether all six singletons are exercised. An honest UNKNOWN outranking a confident guess is the evidence ladder working.

*** WHAT IT ASKED FOR IS THE QUANTIFIER-COLLAPSE SHAPE: V28 WRITES ALL SIX BITS AT ONCE. *** That pins the mask as a UNION. Delete one bit and the union write still trips on the other five, so V28 stays green while a SINGLETON write of the deleted bit now reaches the prescaler and the store. It named the sweep: TCR 0x0004/0x0008/0x0010/0x0040/0x0080/0x0200 individually, and each DMATCR high-byte bit individually -- fourteen mask-minus-one-bit mutants.

Note how this composes with the measuring seat's H3 and is NOT the same test: H3 pins the mask FROM ABOVE (a modelled bit must be ACCEPTED); this pins it FROM BELOW, PER BIT (each unimplemented bit must be rejected alone). A mask is fully pinned only when both hold, and they fail to different mutants. Forwarded to the strengthening work as an open question to SETTLE BY MEASUREMENT rather than a confirmed escape.

One wording correction it supplied: 'once per bit' is imprecise -- a previously reported bit can appear again in a message when it arrives alongside a fresh one.
VERDICT: SOUND. Read the shipped arms and confirmed the three-way store-position asymmetry independently. No escape offered.

VERDICT: SOUND. Packet-fed and correct within that limit; offered no mutant. Its blindness is the point -- it cannot check a claim the packet states, and the two escapes that mattered both needed the SOURCE (TCR_UNIE's value, and dmac_tcr's consumer mask), which no packet carried.
VERDICT: SOUND. Packet-fed, same limit as glm.

VERDICT: DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR. Packet-fed and reached the right verdict from the brief's own kill table, reasoning that mutants scoring 31-32/33 imply rows that are single points of failure. Right conclusion, and it could not name the instance -- which is the documented division of labour: a reading seat buys the class, a measuring seat buys the instance.

Against the floor: (a) it fails the pre-fix build at 25 of 33 rows; (b) the pre-fix build IS the verbatim reinstatement at all four sites, and the ungated witness pins per-site; (c) it is a rung-3 runtime probe, so no null medium can pass it. The nine escapes are hypothetical edits in uncovered product cells -- coverage debt, correctly ranked below the LIVE host deaths #448 and #449 then fixed. rows.title: ctorabortclass  The same construction abort fires on NINE subtypes across FIVE machines -- the alpha instance was recorded as LATENT and UNADVERTISED, and MEASURED 2026-09-07 as both advertised and aborting

entries.note:
MEASURED by sweeping every advertised type/subtype, so this is a census rather than a suspicion. Besides hpcmips's three, the identical interrupt_handler_lookup abort fires on:
    decstation/5400   irq="irq? TODO"
    decstation/5500   irq="TODO: irq"
    mvmeppc/mvme2100  irq="0"
    sgi/ip19, sgi/ip27
*** EIGHT SUBTYPES ACROSS FOUR MACHINES. ***  Inside hpcmips there are no latent copies -- the file has exactly three device_add calls and all three are in the aborting arms.

One genuinely LATENT instance worth distinguishing from the eight: machine_alpha.c:71 (z8530 with irq=0) sits in `case ST_DEC_3000_300:`, which -H never advertises, and all three alpha subtypes construct. Latent is not the same as reachable and the row says so.

Separate round from hpcabort under the reopening rule -- different machines, different files, and the correct interrupt path differs per machine, so one fix design does not cover them. But hpcabort's witness generalises: it enumerates subtypes from the binary's own -H rather than a hardcoded list, so pointing it at these costs almost nothing.
entries.ev: full type/subtype sweep of the committed binary

entries.note:
*** ORDERING CONSTRAINT, MEASURED, AND IT RUNS ONE WAY. ***  Five of this row's SGI subtypes -- ip19, ip20, ip22, ip24, ip27 -- abort() BEFORE reaching machine_sgi.c:633, where an uninitialised eaddr_string was handed to arcbios_init(). They were not immune to that overflow, THEY WERE MASKING IT.

Had this row been fixed first, those five would have reached the same line with the same uninitialised buffer and #446's overflow would have grown FROM FOUR SUBTYPES TO NINE -- a fix creating five new memory-safety faults, each of which would have read as a regression of the abort fix rather than as what it was.

#446 shipped first (bcdbfb8), so the constraint is DISCHARGED and this row is now free to proceed. Recorded because the reasoning is reusable: a row that removes an abort() is a row that EXTENDS reachability, and everything downstream of that abort must be checked before it lands, not after.

rows.state_note:
*** CENSUS CORRECTED 2026-09-07 BY MEASUREMENT.  EIGHT/FOUR -> NINE/FIVE. ***

The record distinguished `machine_alpha.c:71`'s `z8530 irq=0` from the eight as *"one genuinely LATENT
instance ... which `-H` never advertises, and all three alpha subtypes construct."*  **Both halves are
false and the instance is live.**

    -H lists FOUR alpha subtypes and names DEC 3000/300 among them (registered at machine_alpha.c:248)

    alphabook1         rc=124   CONSTRUCTED and RUNNING
    alphaserver4100    rc=124   CONSTRUCTED and RUNNING
    3000/300           rc=134   ABORT (SIGABRT): interrupt_handler_lookup("0") failed.
    eb164              rc=124   CONSTRUCTED and RUNNING

Evidence: `regress/artifacts/ctorabortclass/alpha_census_20260907.txt`.  The abort precedes the `model:`
line and `file: loading`, so it is machine CONSTRUCTION -- a rung-2 witness -- and reproduces with and
without `-x`.

**It is this class's own named mechanism on a fifth machine.**  `machine_sgi.c:142` already records ip27
dying *"inside its own device_add(), at interrupt_handler_lookup() <- devinit_z8530(), on its irq=0"*.

**The likely cause of the wrong record, and it is the more useful half:** the SGI census was MEASURED by
sweeping every advertised subtype; the Alpha sentence beside it reads as though it shares that
measurement and was almost certainly inferred from the arm's shape -- a bare `device_add` with no
`abort()` in it.  `machine_sgi.c`'s own comment warns of exactly that: *"reading for abort() misses an
abort raised by a callee."*  **A measured census with an unmeasured sentence appended inherits the
census's authority.**

*Found while establishing whether the Alpha family is reachable at all, for [[alphaswpctxptbr]] and
[[alphapfnoffset]] -- whose own reachability verdict was UNSETTLED.  That question now has a partial

rows.title: asansweepblind  Gate 9 cannot see a construction abort at all, and its awk silently re-attributes SGI's twelve subtypes to rpi
rows.hold: Harness round. The awk fix is small; making the gate see aborts is a design question (a floor cannot express 'none of them died').

entries.note:
*** TWO INDEPENDENT DEFECTS IN ONE GATE, both measured while establishing that gate 9 does not cover hpcabort. ***

(1) IT CANNOT SEE AN ABORT. sanhit() greps only for ASan/UBSan/SEGV text, so `Aborting.` scores ZERO hits. The only construction assertion is a FLOOR (check_min "machine types constructed" 20), which a few aborting types cannot breach. And it tries only each type's FIRST subtype -- so a defect in any later subtype is invisible by construction. Eight subtypes across four machines currently abort and gate 9 is green.

(2) *** ITS awk AT :50-55 REQUIRES THE PRIMARY ALIAS TO MATCH [a-z0-9_.-]+, AND SGI'S IS "silicon graphics" -- WITH A SPACE. ***  So SGI is dropped as a type and its twelve subtypes are SILENTLY RE-ATTRIBUTED TO rpi. Verified in the gate's own output: rows read `S rpi ip12` through `S rpi ip35`, and the count for type `sgi` is ZERO.

That second one is worse than it looks: the gate reports coverage of twelve subtypes under the wrong machine name, so a reader checking 'is SGI covered' sees a type with no rows and a reader checking rpi sees twelve rows that are not rpi's. Both readings are wrong and neither is red.
entries.ev: gate_asan_sweep.sh:50-55 awk; sanhit(); its own output rows

entries.note:
*** FIXED, AND THE MEASUREMENTS ARE WORSE THAN THE FILING. ***  Run against the unmodified gate first, so the defect is reproduced rather than assumed: `asan-machine-sweep: PASS (3 checks)`, 40 types, 38 constructed -- *** GREEN WHILE FIFTEEN MACHINES ARE DEAD. ***  It touched exactly TWO of the fifteen dying combos, and both produced the row `no 0 0`, BYTE-IDENTICAL to the row a machine that merely wants a -e produces. check_min 38 >= 20 absorbed them. It printed the string `sgi` ZERO times.

*** AND THE ABORT MESSAGE WAS NOT ON DISK AT ALL, so the obvious fix would not have worked either: *** interrupt.c:191-198 does printf("Aborting.\n") then abort(), and abort() does not flush stdio -- with stdout redirected to a file the log of `-E decstation -e 5400` was ZERO BYTES. A grep for 'Aborting' could never have caught this. EXIT STATUS IS THE ONLY BUFFERING-PROOF SIGNAL, and that is what the new classifier keys on.

IT IS FIFTEEN ABORTS, NOT EIGHT: alpha/3000/300, decstation/{3maxplus,maxine,5400,5500}, hpcmips/{be-300,e-105,agenda}, mvmeppc/{mvme1600,mvme2100}, sgi/{ip19,ip20,ip22,ip24,ip27}. All fifteen abort IDENTICALLY under pristine 39748e3, so pre-existing upstream, in three source shapes.

DESIGN, and the directional question was the interesting one: a DIRECTIONAL row alone would have printed all fifteen as 'pre-existing' and PASSED -- papering them over -- so the gate gets BOTH a directional row and an ABSOLUTE dated manifest (AB_EXEMPT), each machine named individually and cited to its abort site. The floor survives only as a swept-nothing guard, deliberately slack: a floor of 20 was satisfiable with TWENTY-ONE TYPES DEAD.

Sweep is now ALL 99 combinations, both binaries, 198 launches, 55-58 s. Nothing bounded.

EIGHT MUTANTS, ALL RUN. M0 is the shipped gate itself, reproducing the defect at PASS (3). The key one is M8: `i <= n` -> `i <= 2`, ONE TOKEN, the shipped B3 semantics -- under the fix the subtypes land under `?` and are REPORTED, where before they were silently filed under rpi.

*** THE DATE 2026-11-30 IN AB_EXEMPT IS THE SEAT'S, NOT THE OWNER'S, and is flagged in the file as wanting confirmation. ***  Note also that when the hpcmips round lands, the 'no longer dies' check goes RED and the fix is deleting three lines -- that friction is deliberate.

*** REFUTED 2026-08-27 and DROPPED. It describes a PRE-FIX gate; the current fork repaired both defects, and a stated figure in the row is wrong too. ***

**Verified here rather than taken from the seat:** `regress/gate_asan_sweep.sh` now classifies by EXIT STATUS via `diedby()` (defined at `:295`, five uses), which explicitly handles **SIGABRT** (`:286`), and it carries `firstalias()` (six uses) -- the second defect the row names.

  > *"**PASS (3 checks)** while 15 machine/subtype combinations were dying by SIGABRT. ... Fix: classify by EXIT STATUS (diedby(), below), which no buffering can lose."*

**That is the check-that-cannot-fail class in its purest form -- a gate reporting PASS while fifteen combinations aborted -- and it was found and repaired.** The row is the record of a defect that no longer exists.

**The seat also flags that the row's 'twelve subtypes' figure is wrong.** Not re-derived here; noted so nobody quotes it. *A dropped row's numbers still get cited.*

rows.title: probewiring  Nothing makes 'no gate runs this probe' a red row or a dated debt -- 24 committed detector rows currently defend nothing between batteries

closure.note:
Shipped as 85bc6ab. Badge A: the main loop reviewed and committed a subagent's round, and verified it by RUNNING the selftest rather than reading the report.

*** THE FINDING THAT PROMPTED IT UNDERSTATED THE DEFECT BY MORE THAN HALF. *** It named two rounds and 24 rows; the truth is FOUR rounds and 66 rows executing in no gate: pit8253_latch_probe (18), sh4_bsc_width_probe (13), fbpending_drain_probe (11, and report-only besides) and hpcmips_ctor_probe (24). The brief's own caution that '#443 and #444 both wired their probes' was half false -- #444's probe is referenced nowhere in the tree except its usage string and one CHANGELOG line.

THE TOOTH NOBODY ASKED FOR IS THE BEST PART: a WITNESS wired into a gate is a HARD failure, because it goes red the day its fix lands -- a phantom regression manufactured on purpose. Nothing else in the harness catches that.

THE CLASS IS DECLARED RATHER THAN INFERRED, AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT PREFERRED. pit8253_latch_probe's first line calls itself a 'cold-debugger witness' while its rows assert the FIXED behaviour -- it is a detector, and a self-label grep would misclassify it AND THEN STOP DEMANDING A GATE FOR IT. Two other probes say 'the pre-fix WITNESS asserts the SYMPTOM' in docstrings and are detectors too. The self-label is kept as an ADVISORY and currently fires once, correctly.

IT CAUGHT A DEFECT IN ITSELF WITHIN HOURS, AND THE DATA STRUCTURE COULD NOT EXPRESS IT. Two rounds added `sgi_eaddr_probe.py` to the MANIFEST independently -- this checker's author and the #446 round whose probe it was -- four lines apart. A PYTHON DICT LITERAL ACCEPTS A DUPLICATE KEY IN SILENCE and keeps the last. Here both agreed on CLASS so the damage was a stale line; had they disagreed, the file would have carried a reviewed, tracked classification the checker silently did not use. Closed by a guard that re-reads the file's OWN SOURCE TEXT, because the structure cannot represent the fault it suffers from. Measured green/red: exit 0 clean, exit 2 with a duplicate.

*** THE MEASUREMENT OF THAT GUARD WAS VOID THREE TIMES BEFORE IT WAS REAL. *** `echo "rc=$?"` through a nested `bash -c` returned an EMPTY variable that read as 0, and the guard was briefly recorded as printing-but-exiting-0 -- a vacuity that did not exist. Settled by writing the test to a FILE and running the file. The same eaten-variable class produced a literal NUL byte in two tracked files today and then mangled a commit message describing that.

NOTHING WAS WIRED, DELIBERATELY. Each of the four is a wiring job needing a rig precondition and one clean gate run before it ships, and gate_hygiene already records four probes that shipped latently RED because the commit adding them never fired the gate. Four DATED exemptions instead, expiring 2026-09-20 -- and that date is a PROPOSAL: the owner set the SM dates and set them tighter than the ones proposed.

entries.note:
*** THE ONE NEW MECHANISM THE FLAGSHIP PASS RECOMMENDS, and it is the only one of the three escape shapes with NO mechanical guard. ***  MEASURED against run.sh's manifest: #441's 13 rows and #439/#440's 11 rows execute in NO gate; #442's rung-3 probe is report-only by default. Gate 6's structural note covers a probe's CENSUS PIN -- that the count moved -- but says nothing about whether anything RUNS it.

The proven pattern is three files away: a probe -> gate WIRING MANIFEST with dated exemptions, exactly like SM_EXEMPT/SC_EXEMPT. That turns pitflip's and sh4bcr's silent unwired state into the same honest, expiring debt that `fbpending_bound:2026-09-20` already is -- visible, attributable, and with a deadline, rather than a comment in a gate complaining that a different probe is unwired.

Note this is NOT the same row as witnessunwired, which is about a WITNESS artefact named by a ledger row that no gate executes. This is about DETECTORS shipped with a round and never wired. Both are real; the manifest would close both.

*** ASKED THE STANDING QUESTION -- what is the smallest edit that breaks this and still passes? -- AND ANSWERED IT IN ONE LINE. ***  `today = datetime.date.today().isoformat()` -> `today = "2020-01-01"` gives **production `PROBEWIRING_PASS` rc=0 AND selftest `SELFTEST_PASS 21/21` rc=0**, while making EVERY DATED EXEMPTION IMMORTAL -- the one thing the EXEMPT table exists to prevent.  A clause-(d) null-repair in its purest form: the guard kept, its effect removed.  **THE BLINDNESS WAS STRUCTURAL, not an oversight about one line.**  M5a-M5e each pass `--today` EXPLICITLY, so between them they test the COMPARISON exhaustively and THE CLOCK IT READS NOT AT ALL; the only mutant on the default path was M0, whose want is PASS, which a frozen clock satisfies.  *A parameter added to make a test deterministic removed the last coverage of the value it replaces* -- worth carrying, because injecting a clock is normally the RIGHT move and this is its cost.  **FIXED IN-ROUND (L2) AND NEGATIVE-CONTROLLED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.**  `M5f` runs on the REAL clock with one exemption dated YESTERDAY -- COMPUTED from `date.today() - timedelta(1)`, never a literal, or the row rots into a permanent red the day it is written.  Measured: clean `SELFTEST_PASS 22/22`; frozen-clock mutant `SELFTEST_FAIL 21/22` **with M5f the ONLY red** (`rc=0 want=1`), and that same mutant still prints `PROBEWIRING_PASS` in production.  Pin raised 21 -> 22 at three sites in `precommit_check.sh`, each anchor verified unique before the edit.  **IT ALSO CORRECTED A RECORDS DEFECT THE SAME COMMIT CREATED (L4).**  `_pick_exempt_detector`'s docstring still said `_exline()` 'reconstructs a ONE-LINE entry', describing behaviour the same commit had replaced with EXTRACTION -- so two halves of one file contradicted each other, the stale half sitting in the function that CONSUMES the fresh one.  Corrected in place, and the `count == 1` guard is kept with its warrant MOVED rather than deleted: it no longer defends a formatting mismatch (extraction cannot have one) but the SELF-MATCH case, measured by this seat as `x2` when a doc comment quotes an EXEMPT line.  *A guard whose stated reason expires but whose behaviour is still needed is the hardest kind to audit: deleting it looks safe, because the case it cites is gone.*

rows.witness: none -- and that is the correct value rather than a gap. The defect is 'no gate executes this probe', which is a property of the harness, not of a code path: there is nothing to reach. It is PROVEN BY DERIVATION -- the battery is read out of run.sh's own GATES array, each gate is comment-stripped, and an interpreter must appear in COMMAND POSITION with the probe as an argument -- and the file:line found is printed so the derivation is auditable rather than trusted. Failability is a built-in --selftest: 18 mutants on temp copies, each exit status read from the process and never through a pipe. 18/18 verified independently before commit.
rows.note: *** AND THE DESIGNED END STATE STILL BLOCKS THE COMMIT -- FILED AS `selftestaddition`, NOT FIXED HERE. ***  With the EXEMPT table EMPTY (the outcome the table exists to drive toward) the selftest reports `SELFTEST_FAIL 12/22`, because seven mutants are built by SUBTRACTING from live input data.  The harness still punishes progress; the punishment has only moved to the LAST discharge instead of the first.  **The way out is measured, not theorised:** the pass-2 seat built `M3x` -- a STALE EXEMPTION mutant made by INSERTING an exemption for the already-wired `arm_flags_probe.py` -- and it scored `ok` on a tree whose EXEMPT table is completely empty.  *The root cause of both the original defect and its replacement is that the selftest MUTATES LIVE INPUT DATA IT DOES NOT NEED.*  Deliberately not done in this round: it rewrites seven mutants at once and owes two negative controls each, so it ships as its own harness round.  *** THIS ROW IS CLOSED AND THE FINDINGS BELOW ARRIVED AFTER IT CLOSED.  DISPOSED UNDER THE LATE-DISSENT RULE, ALL THREE ARMS, AND THE CODE CHANGE IS A **FOLLOW-UP COMMIT** -- NOT AN AMENDMENT UNDER THIS ROW'S NUMBER. ***  The rule's own words: *closure changes the LICENSE, never the truth-value*, and *never amend shipped code under a closed round's number*.  **(1) WRONG RECORD -> L4, corrected in place:** `_pick_exempt_detector`'s docstring described `_exline()` behaviour that the very commit closing this row had replaced.  **(2) MEASURED FALSE PASS against the shipped detector's floor -> L2, repaired in a follow-up:** the frozen-clock edit is vacuity-floor clause (d) exactly -- the guard kept, its repair nulled -- and it scored a CLEAN SWEEP (`SELFTEST_PASS 21/21`, production `PROBEWIRING_PASS`) while making every dated exemption immortal.  `M5f` closes it, controlled both directions.  **(3) EVERYTHING ELSE -> FILED as a new queue item:** the addition-versus-subtraction redesign, `selftestaddition`, carrying the seat's measurement verbatim.  *This line exists so a future reader never sees false unanimity on a closed row: the closing commit's own claim -- that deriving the exemplar had removed the harness-punishes-progress class -- was measured TRUE for the first discharge and FALSE for the last one, by a seat fired after the fact.*
