entries.note:
*** FOUND ONLY BECAUSE FIXING THE GATE'S ALIAS PARSER MADE THESE MACHINES VISIBLE AT ALL. ***  sgi/ip12, ip28, ip30 and ip35 each report FOUR heap-buffer-overflow hits under ASan at arcbios.c:2391, in set_env() called from machine_setup_sgi().

They were invisible for a mechanical reason with nothing to do with the defect: gate 9's awk required a machine's primary alias to match [a-z0-9_.-]+, and *** SGI's is "silicon graphics" -- WITH A SPACE ***, so SGI was dropped as a type and its subtypes were silently re-attributed to the previous one (rpi). A reader asking 'is SGI covered' saw a type with no rows; a reader looking at rpi saw ten rows that were not rpi's. Neither reading was red.

This is a MEMORY-SAFETY defect rather than a records one, and it is the second time this session that fixing an instrument surfaced a real bug the instrument's blindness had been concealing (the first: gate 9 could not see an abort, and fifteen machines were dying while it reported PASS).

NOT diagnosed here -- the round that found it was a harness round and stayed in its file. What is known: four subtypes, four hits each, one call site, and it reproduces under an ASan build from 2026-07-29, so it is at least three weeks old and probably upstream. Whether it is guest-reachable or construction-only is unmeasured.

*** TITLE CORRECTED. It read "A heap-buffer-overflow in arcbios.c set_env()" and THAT IS THE WRONG FILE AND THE WRONG FUNCTION. ***  ASan reports the overflow at arcbios.c:2391 because that is where the READ happens, and the first filing -- mine -- followed the report there.

set_env() is CORRECT CODE. Its append branch grows both arrays before writing to either, and its envstrings is malloc+memset at the call site. The buffer it is handed has no terminator, and *** A CALLEE CANNOT DETECT A MISSING TERMINATOR FROM THE INSIDE ***, so "harden the callee instead" is not a trade-off here, it is an impossibility. The owner is the caller, machine_sgi.c:100.

My own pass-1 hypothesis -- that the linear search read out of bounds BEFORE the reported line -- was MEASURED FALSE: the search iterates over valid strdup'd names.

MEASURED at the point of use: first_NUL_at = -1 on ip12/ip28/ip30/ip35 (no terminator anywhere in the 40 in-bounds bytes; they are ASan's 0xbe fill) and 17 on ip32.

Kept here rather than silently overwritten, because the ledger row a reader trusts is the one whose corrections are visible.

VERDICT: DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR. Fix bounds-correct; detector beatable by ONE CHARACTER.

*** THE CHEAPEST ESCAPE ON RECORD FOR THIS ROUND: `ETHERNET_STRING_MAXLEN` -> `!ETHERNET_STRING_MAXLEN`. *** It is 40, so `!40` is 0, and `snprintf(..., 0, ...)` writes NOTHING -- not even a NUL. The exact original defect returns on all four subtypes, and every row still passes: the call text, the format literal, the six macaddr refs and the byte-offset ordering are all untouched. THE DETECTOR NEVER EXAMINES THE SIZE ARGUMENT.

Also caught TWO WRONG RECORDS in my own material:
  (a) 'E5/E6 are a LENGTH/FORMAT oracle' is FALSE. They recognise INTENT-SHAPED TOKENS in the source, not the produced string. That sentence is the file's stated reason for existing and it does not hold.
  (b) 'callee-side hardening is an IMPOSSIBILITY' overreaches. It is impossible THROUGH THE CURRENT UNBOUNDED `char *` SIGNATURE; an interface taking a length is a real alternative I did not consider.

And: `macaddr[5]` -> `macaddr[4]` passes E6's occurrence count while producing a wrong address -- counting references is not checking them.

VERDICT: DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR, and the SHARPEST answer of the panel -- it attacked the detector at its stated purpose rather than at its edges.

*** `snprintf(eaddr_string, 1, ...)` WRITES ONLY THE NUL. ASan IS SILENT. THE GUEST GETS AN EMPTY MAC. SCORE 7/7. *** That is byte-for-byte the `eaddr_string[0] = '\0'` hole this detector was written to close, wearing an snprintf costume -- so the file fails at the one job it claims ASan cannot do. Gate 9 does not catch it either, so the DUAL-ORACLE argument fails on exactly the mutant that motivated the design.

Further escapes it named, none of which any row can see: `malloc(1)` in place of `malloc(ETHERNET_STRING_MAXLEN)` (E1 does not capture the SIZE) turning the read overflow into a WRITE overflow; a pointer reassignment inside an arm (E1 matches the FIRST malloc); and `if (machine->machine_subtype == 32)` wrapped round the pre-switch fill, which restores the original per-subtype distribution exactly.

It also stated the general fault better than I did: E4's ENGLISH says every arm inherits the fill; E4's CHECK is `malloc_off < snprintf_off < switch_off` in the file. The gap between those two sentences is where every escape lives.

*** ITS ONE FACTUAL CHALLENGE WAS REFUTED BY EXECUTION, AND ITS MECHANISM CLAIM WAS SIMULTANEOUSLY RIGHT. *** It read the case arms and reported that ip27 has no `abort()`, so 'five call abort()' overstates. MEASURED (build/gxemul, all ten advertised subtypes): ip19/20/22/24/27 ALL return 134 = SIGABRT and ip12/28/30/32/35 return 1. The five ARE the five. But the MECHANISM is not what I wrote: ip22 has no body of its own and FALLS THROUGH into case 24, and ip27 dies under gdb at `interrupt_handler_lookup` <- `devinit_z8530` <- `device_add` <- `machine_setup_sgi` -- its own arm's `irq=0`. Grok predicted that exactly ('that is device_add, not abort()'). A source-token read of a switch cannot see fall-through, and both its reading and my own case-splitter had the identical blind spot.

VERDICT: DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR. Read the actual files and confirmed the completeness question independently: `eaddr_string` is assigned only at the malloc, nothing re-points it, there is no reaching `goto`, and the only `return` (`!prom_emulation`) sits AFTER the switch and skips `arcbios_init` entirely.

IT ALONE CHECKED THE SIBLING CALL SITES BY OPENING THEM: `machine_arc.c:53` passes the string literal "10:20:30:40:50:60", and `machine.c:508-524` forces `boot_string_argument` non-NULL. So 'the only defective caller of that path' HOLDS -- but as a call-site audit someone performed, not as something the diff established.

Escape named: a four-character `/*` ... `*/` around the fill. Every row is raw-text, so a commented-out fill scores 7/7.

VERDICT: DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR. Packet-fed, and correct within that limit.

Named `#if 0` / `#endif` and stated the root cause in the form worth keeping: *** ANY CONSTRUCT THAT MAKES TEXT PRESENT-BUT-DEAD DEFEATS EVERY ROW SIMULTANEOUSLY. *** Not a marginal gap -- the fundamental limit of source-text detection without preprocessing or AST liveness. It distinguished this correctly from `sizeof(eaddr_string)`, which is a TRUNCATION defect and NOT the memory-safety class, and said so rather than conflating them to strengthen its own answer.

VERDICT: DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR. Shortest answer, and it went straight to `snprintf(eaddr_string, 0, ...)` -- one token, no NUL written, exact defect restored, 7/7. Reached the same place as codex's `!ETHERNET_STRING_MAXLEN` by a different route.

It was the only seat to say the record does NOT materially overclaim, on the grounds that the file already acknowledges its source-text limits and gate 9's staleness. That reading is too generous: the file does not merely claim to be source-text, it claims to be the LENGTH/FORMAT ORACLE that sees what ASan cannot -- and grok's n=1 mutant is the counterexample. A packet-fed seat cannot check a claim the packet states.

VERDICT: SOUND (fix) with the detector named as the weaker link -- the only seat not to use the DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR label, though its reasoning matches the other six.

Named `#if 0` and, unprompted, the honest limit on its own strongest alternative: `sizeof(eaddr_string)` 'is a DIFFERENT defect (functional truncation, not a heap overflow) ... so it does not answer Q3 as posed'. A seat volunteering that its best example does not fit the question asked is the behaviour worth recording.

Its closing framing is the fair one: the detector is a useful tripwire for a sloppy refactor -- someone deleting the fill, moving the switch above it, removing the malloc -- but it is not a soundness proof, and the record should not read as though it were.

VERDICT: DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR. 69 KB, the longest, and the only seat to AUDIT MY KILL TABLE ARITHMETIC rather than the code.

It challenged the row 'a four-octet MAC 6/7 (E5 alone)' as internally inconsistent, reasoning that a four-octet mutant must fail BOTH E5 (six-field literal absent) and E6 (only four macaddr refs) and therefore score 5/7, not 6/7.

*** MEASURED, AND THE CHALLENGE IS REFUTED -- BUT THE AMBIGUITY IT FOUND IS REAL. *** My mutant changed the FORMAT STRING ONLY and kept all six macaddr arguments: it scores 6/7 with E5 the sole failure. The seat's assumed mutant -- format AND arguments both cut to four -- scores 5/7 with E5 and E6 failing. Both numbers are right; they are different mutants. What sent a careful seat down the wrong path is that '(E5 alone)' does not say whether E5 alone FIRED or alone SURVIVED, and the two readings are opposite. A kill-table cell must name the direction.

It also confirmed by construction what E4 DOES check: moving the malloc BELOW the fill flips the offset order and E4 catches it. The row is not vacuous -- it is narrow.

CLOSE (review). The close condition is MET: the runtime value oracle LANDED -- regress/sgi_eaddr_probe.py, committed in 6b6d596 alongside the pass-2 receipt, wired into gate_asan_sweep.sh and gate_offline.sh with a manifest row. *** THE HOLD TEXT'S 'not committed yet' IS STALE, not wrong-at-the-time. *** The oracle is the right class: a PROVENANCE check -- the string must be the formatting of its own MAC bytes, read at arcbios_init in a live construction -- that no text-only medium can pass, killing all sixteen measured mutants including the size-0 two-character one. Rung 2 is the CEILING for a construction-time defect per the ladder, and the file says so itself.

*** ESCAPE FOUND, and it is one deleted line. ***

S-M3 (FILED): delete `net_generate_unique_mac(machine, macaddr);` at machine_sgi.c:97. Builds clean, scores 10/10. The real MAC is 08:20:30:00:00:10; the mutant hands the guest '8c:55:55:55:00:00' -- UNINITIALISED STACK -- and every row is green BECAUSE THE STRING AND THE BYTES AGREE WITH EACH OTHER. The check is RELATIVE: arg4's provenance against arg5, and nothing pins arg5. The docstring's claim that 'RAM garbage fails it' holds only for garbage on the STRING side. The fix is an ABSOLUTE row -- arg5 against net_generate_unique_mac's output, or simply 'not the 0x55 fill'.

S-M1 -- a measured death that does NOT count as coverage, and the seat said so. malloc(ETHERNET_STRING_MAXLEN) -> malloc(8) scores 2/10, but gcc caught it at COMPILE time (-Wformat-truncation) and glibc _FORTIFY_SOURCE killed the process BEFORE arcbios_init. Per rule 4 it did not fail for the reason under test: the allocation SIZE is outside this detector's field of view, and the compiler and host libc did the work.

rows.title: stdbufasan  `stdbuf` silently breaks an ASan binary, and this ASan ignores bogus flags so the usual accept/reject discriminator cannot detect it
rows.hold: Records-only. No fix owed; the value is that the next round does not rediscover it.

entries.note:
TWO TRAPS from the gate-9 round, both worth carrying because each defeats a technique this project relies on.

(1) *** stdbuf's LD_PRELOAD PREEMPTS THE ASan RUNTIME. ***  The obvious fix for abort()-not-flushing is stdbuf -o0, and on an ASan build it breaks the binary instead. It needs verify_asan_link_order=0 -- and this had to be proven BEHAVIOURALLY, because *** this ASan SILENTLY IGNORES bogus options ***, so the discriminator this project uses elsewhere (pass a nonsense value; a validated flag names its own list) FAILS HERE. That discriminator is written into CLAUDE.md as the way to prove a flag is real; this is a documented exception to it.

(2) The shell's `Aborted (core dumped)` line is emitted AT THE CALL SITE, not inside the function, so wrapping the command in `( ... ) 2>/dev/null` does NOT suppress it. Measured. A harness that filters stderr expecting to have silenced it will still see the line and may classify on it.

Recorded as a row rather than only a comment because both are general techniques, not gate-9 specifics, and the next probe that meets an aborting binary will reach for exactly these.

rows.witness: harness:gate_asan_sweep.sh's own comments and export line -- the hazard AND its remedy are both recorded in the gate, verified by reading it.
rows.state_note:
*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, HARNESS-ONLY, and ALREADY DOCUMENTED AND FIXED IN-TREE -- in THREE places in the same gate. Recommend CLOSE. ***

**The mechanism:** `stdbuf` works by `LD_PRELOAD`ing `libstdbuf.so`, which then precedes the ASan runtime in the initial library list; ASan rejects that startup order and aborts with *'ASan runtime does not come first in initial library list'*. The host process dies at launch, **before the guest CPU powers on**, so there is no guest observable at all.

**All three already in `regress/gate_asan_sweep.sh`, verified by reading:**
  * `:104-105` -- *"verify_asan_link_order=0 is REQUIRED, not cosmetic. `stdbuf` works by LD_PRELOADing libstdbuf.so, which then precedes the ASan runtime..."*
  * `:117` -- the remedy: `export ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:abort_on_error=0:print_summary=1:verify_asan_link_order=0`
  * `:115` -- **the second hazard, recorded verbatim**: *"ASan silently ignores `no_such_asan_flag_xyz=0` and runs normally."*

*** THAT SECOND ONE IS THE SHARPER FINDING AND IT IS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN: because this ASan silently ignores bogus options, ANY check that validates `ASAN_OPTIONS` by asking whether ASan ACCEPTS them is vacuous. *** It answers identically for a valid and an invalid flag -- the check-that-cannot-fail shape, in the environment rather than in a script. The gate knew and said so.

*Ninth row today describing work already done or already recorded. See [[baretitle]] -- the queue's dominant defect is stale entries, not undiscovered bugs.*

rows.title: killedreports0  A battery KILLED mid-run reported exit 0, because the invocation piped run.sh through tail
rows.hold: The habit is most of the fix, but the harness CAN refuse a verdict whose log has no terminal token -- that part is checkable and is what the row is for.

entries.note:
*** THE SHARPEST FORM OF A TRAP THIS PROJECT ALREADY RECORDS, AND IT REACHED THE TOP-LEVEL HARNESS INVOCATION. ***  The full battery was started as
    bash run.sh 2>&1 | tail -45
in the background, and later killed. *** IT REPORTED EXIT CODE 0. ***  A pipeline's status is the LAST command's, so the exit code belonged to `tail`, which succeeded in reading a truncated stream.

Two things went wrong together and either alone would have been survivable:
  1. THE VERDICT WAS FALSE -- a killed battery reported success.
  2. THERE WAS NOTHING TO READ EITHER WAY. `| tail` buffers until the pipeline ends, so the output file sat at 0 BYTES for the whole run and was still 0 bytes afterwards. Mid-run progress was invisible and the post-mortem was empty.

Same genus as `cmd | head` reporting head's status, which this project already writes down and which bit twice more the same day -- once hiding a compile failure, once mangling an object list through a `tr` inside nested quoting. What is NEW is the SCALE: this is not a check inside a gate, it is the invocation of the ENTIRE 16-GATE BATTERY.

A SECOND TRAP RODE ALONG WITH IT, and it nearly did more damage: with the real output empty, the obvious place to look was the shared log directory -- which still held the PREVIOUS battery's verdicts. Those read `asan-machine-sweep: PASS (3 checks)` and `log-hygiene: PASS (38 checks)`, both plausible and both STALE (the current gates give 11 and 48). Reading them as this run's result would have been the 'a green row means nothing' class in its purest form, and the only thing that prevented it was the check counts having moved that day.

THE FIX USED: run under `exec > /tmp/battery.log 2>&1` so output streams to a file and the exit status is run.sh's own. The re-run produced REGRESS_PASS across all 16 gates in 48 minutes, with progress readable throughout.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT MECHANICAL: a verdict is believable only if its log ends in a terminal token. nightly_check.sh already treats a MISSING or STALE verdict as failure -- the same reasoning one level in would refuse a verdict whose log carries no REGRESS_PASS/REGRESS_FAIL line, which is exactly what a killed run leaves behind. That is checkable and is the part worth building.
entries.ev: measured: the killed invocation's own exit code and its 0-byte output file

entries.note:
*** THESE WERE HIDDEN INSIDE A NUMBER, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. ***  #446 was filed as "FOUR heap-buffer-overflow hits" on each of four SGI subtypes. There is ONE overflow per subtype. gate_asan_sweep.sh's sanhit() is a `grep -acE`, so it counts LINES, and the four were: the ERROR: line, the SUMMARY: line, and TWO SEPARATE UBSan LEFT-SHIFT ERRORS at arcbios.c:737 and arcbios.c:784.

The discriminator that separated them: `grep -ac 'ERROR: AddressSanitizer'` is 1 per subtype. ip32's count of "2" is the two UBSan lines ALONE -- ip32 has no overflow at all, which is why its number never matched the other four and why the mismatch was the thread worth pulling.

A COUNT IS NOT A CLASSIFICATION. Two distinct defect families were summed into one integer, and the integer looked consistent enough to file as a single row.

NOT DIAGNOSED. Whether either shift is real UB (a signed value shifted into or past the sign bit) or a sanitizer false positive is unmeasured -- the lines have not been read.

VERDICT: SHIP-WITH-CHANGES, and it CORRECTED THE ROUND'S CONSEQUENCE TRACE by measurement-grade reading. The claimed 'mis-linked component tree' was a COUNTERFACTUAL: the witnessed 64-bit site (:737) is consumed only by `echild == 0`, which a corrupted value cannot alias (corruption forces low word >= 2^31). The load-bearing site :751 is UNREACHED on current images -- and the REASON is a separate defect grok found while checking: *** the 64-bit walker reads peeraddr+0x34, a slice of AffinityMask, where IdentifierLength is at +0x40 *** -- so after the first node the walk is in the weeds. Layout confirmed against sgi_arcbios.h plus the +0x50 step (0x18 pointer header + 0x38 component). Filed as arcbioswalk64. It also corrected the brief's 'zero uint64_t declarations' echo and the addchild64 parent-type claim (uint64_t, not promoted uint32_t).

VERDICT: SHIP-WITH-CHANGES, scope FOUR witnessed sites under the round rule's witness clause -- overruled by adjudication, but its two demands SHAPED THE SHIPPED DETECTOR: (1) 'do not scope to value-wrong sites only; removal of UB is itself the correction' -- followed; (2) fixing unwitnessed sites 'requires a new static/source oracle' -- that oracle is the census row, and the kill table's M2 (revert an unwitnessed cast -> sweep green, census red) is the measurement that answers its coverage objection rather than arguing with it. It also tightened the wording the record now uses: four sites are UBSan-WITNESSED, not 'reached' -- another site may execute with buf[3] < 0x80.

VERDICT: SHIP-WITH-CHANGES, scope ALL TEN, and its argument was the one adjudication adopted: the cast is provably value-neutral where the UB is not firing, so there is nothing per-site for a witness to adjudicate -- 'a class gets fixed as a class'. Three further contributions, all landed: (1) the house-idiom correction -- the four existing casts split 3-to-1, not 2-and-2, and the real rule is 'the cast matches the assembled width'; (2) the sanitizer-invisible mutant `(buf[3]&0x7f)<<24`, which the census kills at 13/0; (3) the completed consequence trace -- BOTH mis-link directions (false negative at true high word 0, false positive at 1). rows.hold: Fix and guard are written and negative-controlled; awaiting its commit.

entries.note:
SELF-INFLICTED, BY ME, IN bcdbfb8 -- badge A. #446 wrote comments quoting the bad-fix mutant it had to defend against (a zero byte written as a C escape) into CHANGELOG.md and regress/gate_offline.sh THROUGH A SHELL HEREDOC, which interpreted the escape. Three literal NULs landed: CHANGELOG.md lines 4254 and 4260, gate_offline.sh line 1803.

*** IT SURVIVED PRECOMMIT, A 265-CHECK GATE RUN, AND THE COMMIT ***, because bash does not care about a NUL inside a comment.

WHAT IT BREAKS IS THE HARNESS'S CORE IDIOM. grep(1) auto-detects such a file as binary and answers "Binary file ... matches" -- ON STDOUT, WITH EXIT 0. So `grep -q` still works and `grep -c` still counts, while every check that PARSES A FIELD out of the matched line silently receives that sentence in place of the row. MEASURED: `grep 'sgi_eaddr: the buffer' gate_offline.sh` returned the sentence, exit 0. Not a wrong value -- a wrong SHAPE, through a channel no section watched.

*** THE FIRST SWEEP I RAN TO SCOPE IT WAS ITSELF VOID and I reported its result. *** It found ZERO NULs -- including the one I had just located by hand -- because the nested bash -c ate its `$'\x00'`. I said "it is the only tracked file affected" on the strength of a sweep that found nothing at all. The real sweep found THREE bytes across TWO files. A sweep that finds nothing and a sweep that cannot find anything are indistinguishable in the output.

GUARD: precommit section S, negative-controlled both ways. Its own first draft used `grep -qU "$(printf '\000')"` and PUT A FRESH NUL INTO precommit_check.sh -- the check forbidding the byte introduced the byte. `tr -d` takes the escape as a two-character argument interpreted at runtime, so nothing in the file is ever a zero byte.

GIT'S OWN BINARY DETECTION CANNOT BE THE ORACLE: `git ls-files --eol` reports i/-text for a PNG and for a corrupted text file identically, so deriving the domain from git would exempt precisely the broken files. Circular. Hence an explicit skip list, plus two genuinely-binary paths that carry no extension (src/devices/fonts/*, test/FileLoader_*).

rows.witness: harness:precommit_check.sh section Y -- negative-controlled BOTH ways on the day it landed: injecting one NUL into a tracked .md turns it RED and names the file; restoring turns it GREEN at 672 tracked text files. `harness:` is the right witness kind because the subject is the test apparatus.
rows.state_note:
*** SYMPTOM ABSENT, CAUSE NOW GUARDED, 2026-08-27 -- and I reproduced the defect by accident while building the guard, which is the best evidence the guard is worth having. ***

**The row:** a shell heredoc wrote three literal NUL bytes into two tracked text files, *silently turning every grep against them binary*. The damage is not the bytes -- it is that grep then reports NOTHING, and nearly every gate in this tree is grep-based.

**Current state: 0 NUL bytes across 672 tracked text files**, measured with `tr -cd`.

*** MY FIRST MEASUREMENT OF THAT WAS INERT AND I REPORTED IT AS A RESULT. *** I scanned 1161 tracked files with `LC_ALL=C grep -qP` and got 0 hits. **grep REFUSES to run `-P` under `LC_ALL=C`** -- *"supports only unibyte and UTF-8 locales"* -- so it never ran, and with `-q` and `2>/dev/null` the refusal was invisible. **0 of 1161 was a check that could not fail.** The honest figure is 0 of 672, by a method with no regex engine in it.

*** AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THE GUARD WROTE A NUL INTO ITSELF. *** Writing `\\x00` through a Bash -> heredoc -> Python path lost one backslash level, exactly as the carrier documents, so Python emitted byte 0x00 into `precommit_check.sh` -- **reproducing this row's own mechanism inside the check meant to catch it**, and ordinary grep immediately called the script binary. That is how the inert `-P` was found at all.

**THE GUARD, and why it is shaped this way:** `precommit_check.sh` section Y uses **`tr -cd`, not grep** -- no regex engine, no `-P`, no locale dependency, and no backslash that has to survive a quoting layer. It carries a ZERO-DENOMINATOR guard (if the `ls-files` pattern selects nothing it FAILS loudly rather than reporting clean), and it is scoped to text extensions on purpose: a future tracked `.pdf` or `.png` carries NULs legitimately, and a check that has to be switched off is worse than no check.

**Negative-controlled in both directions before it landed**, which is mandatory for a change to the script every commit runs: inject one NUL into a tracked `.md` -> RED, naming the file; restore -> GREEN at 672 files.

**DISPOSITION: the symptom is gone and the cause is now MECHANICALLY GUARDED.** Recommend CLOSE. Note no fix commit was ever recorded on this row, so the original NULs were removed by unrelated edits -- which is precisely why a guard was worth more than a cleanup.

R-M4 (FILED): whole-register latch key at the sh4_val_first() argument. 10/10. L1 misses it because it uses CMIE then OVIE, two DIFFERENT bits, so masked and unmasked keys both report twice. #448's L1 was built with bit-subset ordering precisely for this; #449's L1 does not carry that property.

entries.note:
*** NINE MUTANTS SCORE 33/33 AGAINST #447's SHIPPED DETECTOR, SEVEN OF THEM MEASURED REAL DEFECTS. ***  Filed rather than fixed in #447 for a stated reason: the detector is WEAK, not VACUOUS. It kills 25 of 33 rows on the pre-fix build and kills six real mutants. That is categorically unlike #446's detector, which a 217-byte comment-only file passed and which was therefore replaced in-round.

THE FOUR HOLES, and they are a PRODUCT rather than a list:
  H1  state is read back at INSTANCE 0 ONLY. V17/V18 read RCR1, V19/V20 channel 0, V21 TCR0. V11/V12 walk the other instances but only COUNT diagnostic lines.
  H2  state is read back on a FIRST offence only, EXCEPT at RCR1. V18 exists for exactly this shape -- its own comment cites #443's brace slip -- and the sibling row was never added at TCR or DMATCR.
  H3  the guard masks are pinned only FROM BELOW. V28 proves the six bits are IN the mask; nothing proves any other bit is OUT.
  H4  width x instance is a PRODUCT and the census covers only the DIAGONAL -- three widths at instance 0, one width everywhere else.

THE ESCAPES, all measured on built binaries:
  M20  `| TCR_UNIE` added to TCR_UNIMPLEMENTED -- ONE IDENTIFIER. Fix: TCR0=0x0022 reads back 0x22 with a clock line at 520833.328125 Hz. M20: reads back 0x00000000, NO clock line. TCR_UNIE is modelled (`d->tcr[i] & TCR_UNIE` in sh4_timer_tick), so the guest can NEVER enable the timer interrupt.  [H3]
  M20b `| TCR_TPSC0` -- same shape; makes TPSC_P16 and TPSC_P256 unusable.  [H3]
  M25  `| SH_RCR1_CF` -- fix writes RCR1 0x80, reads back 0x80, 0 diagnostics; mutant reads back 0x01, STILL 0 diagnostics. Fully silent.  [H3]
  Mdma DMATCR guard narrowed `~0x00ffffff` -> `~0x04ffffff`, ONE NIBBLE. Bit 26 is then stored, and *** sh4_dmac_transfer consumes dmac_tcr[] & 0x1fffffff, FIVE BITS WIDER than the guard rejects ***, so bits 24-28 give a silently wrong transfer count.  [H3]
  M23  TCR stores the rejected value when timer_nr != 0. Fix: TCR1 reads 0x0002. Mutant: 0x0204.  [H1]
  M24  DMATCR stores it when dma_channel != 0. Fix: 0x10. Mutant: 0xabcdef.  [H1]
  Mbrk TCR `break;` -> `if (timer_nr == 0) break;` -- timers 1 and 2 then fall into `idata & 3` and install pclock/4, the exact naive-fix bug V22 was written for, on the two instances it does not watch.  [H1]
  M21  DMATCR stores on a REPEAT offence. Fix: 0x10. Mutant: 0x123456. Both rejects carry bit 24, so the second is not 'fresh'.  [H2]
  M22  TCR stores on a repeat offence. Fix: 0x0002. Mutant: 0x0004.  [H2]
  M33  `if (timer_nr == 2 && len == 4) exit(1);` -- *** GUEST-REACHABLE HOST DEATH. ***  A mov.l to TCR2 gives alive=False. It SURVIVES at len 2, the only width V11 issues, which is precisely why it scores full marks.  [H4]

*** THE FIX CHANGED H3's FAILURE MODE FROM LOUD TO SILENT, and that is the finding inside the finding. ***  Pre-#447 a widened mask meant exit(1) on a legal write -- unmissable. Post-#447 it means a silently refused write. The round improved the failure and made its own blind spot worse in the same edit.

A THIRD SEAT ADDED THE QUANTIFIER-COLLAPSE QUESTION, and was honest that it could not confirm it: V28 writes all six unimplemented TCR bits AS A UNION (0x02dc). Delete one bit from the mask and the union write still trips on the other five, so V28 stays green while a SINGLETON write of the deleted bit reaches the prescaler and the store. UNSETTLED -- it needs the fourteen mask-minus-one-bit mutants run: TCR 0x0004/0x0008/0x0010/0x0040/0x0080/0x0200 and each DMATCR high-byte bit, each written alone.

NOTE H3-from-above and the singleton sweep are DIFFERENT TESTS and both are wanted: one requires a MODELLED bit to be ACCEPTED, the other requires each unimplemented bit to be REJECTED ALONE. A mask is pinned only when both hold, and they fail to different mutants.

THE FIXES THE SEATS RECOMMENDED, each small: extend the TCR and DMATCR read-back rows to a NON-ZERO instance (H1); add a read-back after a REPEATED same-bit reject at TCR and DMATCR (H2); add rows writing a MODELLED bit-set and asserting it is ACCEPTED, with the clock line as the second witness (H3); make V11 issue len 4 as well as len 2 (H4).

*** AND ONE PROCESS NOTE WORTH MORE THAN THE ROWS: THE PROBE REFUSED TO PASS IN A HALF-EDITED STATE. ***  An attempt at this work died mid-edit having bumped EXPECT_ROWS to 43 and registered three new opcodes, without writing the rows. The probe reported 31/33 FAIL through TWO INDEPENDENT ROWS -- V31 caught the row-count intent, V30 caught the opcode intent (mismatches for 2151, 2161, 4000, disassembler None). The identity-row discipline worked on its own author, and the tree was restored to a verified 33/33 rather than left broken.

entries.note:
*** THE FUNCTION CALLED sh4_dmac_transfer() DOES NOT TRANSFER. ***  Found while settling a pass-1 seat's question about body ordering, and it refuted the question rather than answering it.

`sar`, `dar`, `count` and `chcr` are LOCAL copies; there is no `cpu->cd.sh.dmac_*` assignment anywhere in the function; and the only arm that returns normally, `case 0x200:`, is literally `(void)sar; (void)dar;` under the comment 'Note: No transfer is done here! It is up to the external device to do the transfer itself!'. So no bytes move, SAR/DAR/DMATCR are never advanced, and TE is never set.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the second is why this is filed rather than shrugged at. (1) It made #448 trivially safe -- every site is side-effect-free before it dies, so there is nothing to un-commit and no store had to move. (2) *** A GUEST THAT ENABLES DMA AND POLLS FOR COMPLETION ALREADY WAITS FOREVER, ON THE ONE CONFIGURATION THE MODEL ACCEPTS, BEFORE AND AFTER #448 ALIKE. ***  Two pass-1 seats raised the hang risk as something #448 might CREATE; measurement shows it PRE-EXISTS and #448 neither causes nor worsens it.

Honest limit: READ, not executed. No guest here has been observed waiting -- landisk's kernel may never enable a DMA channel at all. Whether any guest this project boots reaches it is unmeasured, so this is a capability gap of unknown reachability rather than a witnessed defect.

rows.state_note:
*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: FALSE AS WRITTEN. The observation is true; the CONSEQUENCE the row asserts does not follow. ***

**True part:** `sh4_dmac_transfer()` really never transfers anything on any path.

**False part, which is what the row is named for:** the claimed consequence is wrong. Writing `CHCRx.TD` calls the no-op routine, but that does not produce the failure the title asserts. Enabling external-device DMA and then polling without triggering that device can wait forever -- **but that is a guest doing something incomplete, not this routine causing it.**

**DISPOSITION: same as [[pitcount]] -- keep open but RE-TITLE to name the no-op itself, not the consequence.** Do not simply drop it: unlike [[a1a2]] and [[n5]], the underlying observation survives and only the stated effect fails. **A row whose title asserts a consequence its evidence does not support is a wrong record even when its first clause is true** -- and it will keep attracting rounds aimed at the wrong thing.

rows.title: sh4rtcflags  RTCSR's CMF and OVF are never set on any path, and RTCNT has no `case` at all -- a guest polling for a refresh compare-match waits forever
rows.hold: Filed out of #449's pass 1. A capability gap, and it predates every SH-4 round here.
rows.witness: none yet -- guest-reachable (the window is mapped, the stores land, the poll is a guest loop) but UNWITNESSED on any production boot path, and a witness needs a build.

entries.note:
Named by two pass-1 seats and checked against the header. `sh4_bscreg.h` defines CMF, CMIE, CKS, OVF, OVIE and LMTS. The device increments `bsc_rfcr` every tick and stores CKS/LMTS/RTCOR without consulting them; it NEVER sets CMF or OVF on any path, and SH4_RTCNT (0xff800020) has no `case` in the register switch at all.

*** #449 DOES NOT MAKE THIS WORSE AND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT FIX IT. ***  A guest polling CMF already waits forever with the enables CLEAR. #449 only stops the host dying, so a guest with the enables SET now survives to wait in the same way. Setting CMF as a consolation would be INVENTING a compare-match with no RTCNT to match against -- a pass-1 seat argued that explicitly and the round agreed.

Honest limit: READ, not executed. Whether any guest this project boots ever polls CMF is unmeasured.

rows.state_note:
*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE and guest-reachable -- and it carries a WARNING against the obvious partial fix, which an earlier round already refused. ***

RTCSR's `CMF` and `OVF` are never set on any path, and `RTCNT` does not advance. **Not dormant:** the window is mapped, the stores land, and the poll is an ordinary guest loop -- but it is **unwitnessed on a production boot path**, which is what keeps it below the rows a booting guest actually travels.

**Observable:** `RTCSR` bit 7 (`CMF`) after a programmed free-run -- 0 when broken (the guest cannot plant it), 1 when fixed. That is the bit a compare-match poll waits on. *`RTCNT` staying 0 is a second channel; the title's hang is CMF.*

*** THE TRAP, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS ROW IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX: setting `CMF` as a consolation, with no `RTCNT`, IS WHAT `#449` PASS-1 REFUSED -- and that refusal still holds. *** A fix that plants the flag without advancing the counter makes the poll exit while the time base is still frozen: the guest stops waiting and is then wrong about the elapsed time, which is worse than waiting.

**In-tree idiom for the shape:** the same file's `sh4_timer_tick()` does `d->tcr[i] |= TCR_UNF` on TMU wrap and queues a pending interrupt if `UNIE` -- so the flag-plus-interrupt pattern exists; what this row needs in addition is the COUNTER.

rows.title: sh4latchcollide  The sh4_val_first latch classes are kept apart by the ACCIDENT of disjoint bit constants, and no row can detect a wrong class
rows.hold: Filed out of #449's pass 2. Not a live defect -- a fragility. Needs a design answer rather than a fix.
rows.witness: none -- the condition for the defect is not currently met, by measurement.

entries.note:
A pass-2 seat named the smallest undetected mutation: swap #449's latch class from SH4_VAL_RTCSRINT to SH4_VAL_RCR1INT. It CONDITIONED the claim correctly -- it matters only 'if an earlier RCR1 complaint with an OVERLAPPING BIT' suppressed the RTCSR one.

MEASURED: the mutant scores 10/10 against the shipped detector. But the bit sets are DISJOINT -- RCR1 CIE|AIE = 0x18, RTCSR CMIE|OVIE = 0x42 -- and sh4_val_first keys on BITS, so a shared class slot cannot suppress anything. *** THE MUTANT IS EQUIVALENT, NOT SURVIVING, and that is a different diagnosis from 'the detector is weak'. ***  The seat's condition is simply not met.

*** WHAT IS WORTH KEEPING IS THE FRAGILITY. ***  Nine classes now share one `val_reported[cls][inst]` array, and correctness of the class assignment is currently guaranteed by nothing except that no two classes' bit sets overlap. Renumber one header constant, or add a tenth class that shares bits with an existing one, and a wrong class assignment becomes a SILENT suppression of a real diagnostic -- with no row able to see it, because while the sets are disjoint there is nothing observable to assert.

Candidate answers for a round to weigh: a compile-time assertion that the classes' bit domains are disjoint; or making the class a property of the register rather than a hand-written argument at each call site.

rows.title: arcbioswalk64  The 64-bit component walker reads peeraddr+0x34 -- a slice of AffinityMask -- where IdentifierLength is at +0x40
rows.hold: Filed out of #450's pass 1. Wrong-offset defect, different semantic class from the shift UB; its own round.
rows.witness: none yet -- established by LAYOUT ARITHMETIC (0x18-byte pointer header + sgi_arcbios.h offsets, corroborated by the walker's own +0x50 step), not by execution. Needs a measured witness before a fix round.

entries.note:
Found while checking #450's consequence trace: the reason the load-bearing shift site :751 never fires is that *** THE WALK ITSELF IS BROKEN. ***  The 64-bit walker reads 4 bytes at peeraddr+0x34 as 'IdentifierLength'. In-RAM layout: ptr_peer/ptr_child/ptr_parent (0x18) then arcbios_component64 -- Class +0x18, Key +0x28, AffinityMask +0x30, ConfigurationDataSize +0x38, IdentifierLength +0x40, Identifier +0x48, total 0x50 = exactly the walker's step. So +0x34 is the HIGH HALF OF AFFINITYMASK. The walker masks the read with 0xfffff and skips accordingly -- with AffinityMask 0xffffffff that is a ~1 MiB skip per node, and the walk leaves the component list after the first node.

CONSEQUENCE FOR #450's record, stated there too: :751's mis-link hazard is a counterfactual PARTLY BECAUSE this bug prevents the walk from ever reaching a node whose parent pointer would exercise it. Fixing this row may make that site live -- the coupling runs one way, like ctorabortclass before it.

HONEST LIMIT: layout arithmetic and one corroborating step constant, no execution. The 32-bit walker's offset (+0x28 read, +0x30 step) should be checked in the same round rather than assumed correct by symmetry.

rows.title: sh4sci  Three guest-clocked command bytes end the host in sh4_sci_cmd() -- the first SH-4 site here that a single store cannot reach
rows.hold:
Fix and detector SHIPPED; gate 10 PASS at 60 checks, run singly; build rc=0 with zero warnings. Held open, not closed: both stages carry a deliberate fable5 omission (the owner's standing batching directive), and section H refuses a CLOSED row with a HELD stage.

TWO QUESTIONS FOR THAT SEAT, both raised by measurements this round rather than by design argument:

1. ACCEPT-ROW FAILABILITY says build the JOINT growth mutant, because #449's guard-only widening measured EQUIVALENT. At THIS site the measuring seat found the opposite: the latch operand is a compile-time constant that cannot mask the guard, so guard-only and joint redden the accept rows byte for byte -- and guard-only ADDITIONALLY silences its own growth (one diagnostic line where joint prints two). So guard-only is the HARDER form here. Does the rule become 'build the form the latch operand does not mask', or does it stay 'joint' with this recorded as an exception?

2. The detector grew 9 -> 14 rows across pass 2, every added row forced by a MEASURED escape. Two of the five were found only because seats were asked for a fifteenth mutant AFTER fourteen were already dead. Is 'ask again once the table is clean' worth making standing practice, or is that the #392 chain in a new coat?
rows.witness: probe:regress/sh4_sci_witness.py (rung 3, 8 rows, unmodified -E landisk; 8/8 pre-fix and 5/8 post-fix, the three differences being exactly the three kill rows S1/S2/S3 while all three controls hold). THE WITNESS GREW DURING PASS 1: it was written for two kill bytes and a seat pointed out that (cmd & 0x30) reaches the else arm for BOTH 0x00 and 0x30, so byte 0xb0 was a THIRD unmeasured host death. Row C3 was added for the same reason in the other direction -- C2 (seven pulses) proves the kill needs a WHOLE byte, not that it needs the clocking PROTOCOL, and an earlier draft claimed the latter. C3 repeats the seventeen stores with SPB0IO cleared so no edge is ever a pulse, which is the claim C2 was making without measuring.

closure.note: CLOSE (assess and review), both questions answered

entries.note:
MEASURE SEAT, and it produced the finding that acts on the shipped code. It built its own tree (16 binaries), drove the ACCEPT side end to end -- recovering 0x0d (a value it wrote), 0x04 (CTRL_24H, set only by DEVINIT(rs5c313)) and 0x06 (the host clock's tm_year % 10, unforgeable by the probe) back through eight input clocks -- and then found that the shipped detector scored a SITE-1-ONLY brace slip 10/10 PASS. RPT drove [0x80, 0x80], a site-2 byte; nothing drove a site-1 offender twice.

It also measured the de-escalation clause's PREMISE rather than assuming it: the same guard growth applied to the PRE-FIX bodies ended the host, while post-fix the guest silently receives 0x50 where 0x0d was due. The tripwire this fix deletes was real and is now gone.

One of its predictions was wrong and it matters that it was built anyway: M15a (sci_cur_addr assigned before validation) was expected to escape row J and DIED at 6/9.

Named the sharpest mutant of either pass, and it is the natural typo: moving the `return` INSIDE the latch guard, since the braces are already open there. That declines the FIRST bad byte and lets every later one fall through, and a detector driving each offender once in a fresh emulator scores it perfect. Proposed a semantic-reason encoding (BAD_BIT7 / BAD_KIND_00 / BAD_KIND_11) rather than the raw byte, and warned that 0x00 cannot test site 1 because site 2 masks it -- recommending a bit-7-clear byte with a LEGAL transfer field instead.

The file:line verification seat. Confirmed against source that `address_transfer` is declared uninitialised at :641 and read at BOTH :659 and :680, which is what makes the early return mandatory rather than merely tidy, and that the function tail contains no further fatal() or exit(). Proposed two separate classes (SCIBIT7 at 1u<<0, SCIXFER keyed on the field) and warned that one shared class with 1u<<0 would let an S1 complaint swallow S2 -- the collision two pass-2 seats then built.

*** OPENED sh4_val_first() INSTEAD OF REASONING FROM THE PACKET, AND THAT IS THE FINDING THAT SAVED THE FIX. *** The helper computes `bits & ~reported` and returns `fresh != 0`, so a key of `cmd & 0x80` -- ZERO on the only path that reaches site 1 -- could NEVER report and the diagnostic would have shipped permanently silent. Nothing else in this round would have caught it. Also flagged that the function header calls bit 7 'Ignored (usually 1?)' while the code killed on it; that the shipped message says 'neither' for field 0x30, which is BOTH bits; and that moving `sci_bits_outputed = 0` into the callee below the returns jams the shifter at 8.

*** FOUND THE THIRD HOST DEATH. *** `(cmd & 0x30)` reaches the else arm for BOTH 0x00 and 0x30, so site 2 has two reachable faults where the witness had measured one; byte 0xb0 kills on the committed build exactly as 0x80 does. Also named the C2 OVERCLAIM precisely -- seven pulses versus eight proves the kill needs a WHOLE BYTE, not that it needs the clocking protocol, because the edge dance is baked identically into both -- which is why row C3 was added. Named the `(cmd & 0x20)` decode-loosening mutant that lets 0x30 slide into the address arm.

Asked for the two rows that turned out to matter most, from the design side: LOOP the offending byte rather than driving it once (otherwise an unlatched fatal() is indistinguishable from a latched one), and ASSERT POST-STATE rather than survival, because a fall-through with a default performs a real transfer while staying alive. Argued for a per-fault-site latch; its supporting premise -- that the offending byte is already in the diagnostic -- was MEASURED FALSE (neither live fatal() had a format specifier; the only %02x is on a commented-out line).

Converged on the discriminating-field key with the site folded in, bounded at three entries, and was the seat that called out the BRIEF's own overclaim: 'an unbounded key is a flood' is wrong, since a full-byte key is bounded at 256 -- the objection is bounded-but-excessive amplification, not unboundedness. Named the default-the-variable-and-fall-through mutant.

Gave no VERDICT line -- a FORMAT miss, recorded as such and not as a seat failure -- but was substantive. Argued the discriminating-field option is 'per-site wearing a hat'; the arithmetic refuted that (the field has two reachable values at site 2, so it is three lines against two), and its supporting premise about the byte being in the log was measured false alongside glm's. Requested the exit() count be grepped rather than trusted, which was done: exactly two, both the ones shown. Independently reached codex's point that 0x00 self-masks a missing site-1 return.

VERDICT: DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR, and correct. Found the cross-site latch collision as `1u << 0` at site 1 -- aliasing site 2's field-0x00 key -- and prescribed the row that catches it, [0x10, 0x80, 0xb0]. That prescription mattered: deepseek found the SAME class with a DIFFERENT bit (1u<<3), so the two-byte row then in place caught one variant and missed the other. Also found a real reporting defect: row O's boolean used the saved `landed` correctly, but its failure MESSAGE read `xf` after row J had overwritten it. And four comment claims that outran the measurements, all corrected.

VERDICT: SOUND. Worked the enum arithmetic out explicitly (SCICMD=9, NCLASS=10, val_reported[10][8], bounds check accepts 0..9) and proved the three live keys 0x80/0x01/0x08 pairwise disjoint. Predicted that M15a -- sci_cur_addr assigned before validation -- would ESCAPE via row J; it was built and DIED at 6/9, because the moved assignment also fires on the data byte and sends A2's write to 0xc. A prediction measured wrong, which is worth as much as one measured right.

VERDICT: SOUND, and then named a MEASURED SURVIVOR: site 2 falling through with `address_transfer = 1` rather than 0. M3 used 0, which reaches the write arm and fires the transfer oracle; 1 only re-latches sci_cur_addr and prints nothing at all. It passed 12/12 and forced row N2. Its other candidate -- widening the start-bit guard to `!(cmd & 0xa0)` -- was built too and DIED, because row N (added an hour earlier for a different finding) already covered it; grok was reviewing the nine-row draft.

VERDICT: DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR, and it stated the ROOT CAUSE in one sentence where others found instances: *'the corpus drives exactly one bit-7-clear byte, 0x10, once, in a fresh session -- every repeat and cross row exercises site 2 only.'* From that it derived two escapes, the site-1-only flood (which makes the word '(once)' in that message false while the gate stays green) and the site-1 key collision, and gave the two rows that close them. It also reconstructed why G1 kills R3, which is not obvious: the widened guard routes both 0x80 and 0xb0 to site 1, where one latch swallows the second.

VERDICT: SOUND. Packet-fed and explicit about it. Confirmed the fix shape against the #443 family and raised no new mutant; its pass-1 asks (loop the byte, assert post-state) had both been built into the detector by then, which is the honest reason it had less to add on the diff than on the design.

VERDICT: SOUND on the fix, and it produced the FIRST measured escape of pass 2: keying site 1 as `1u << 3`, which collides with site 2's field-0x30 key. It reasoned the gap correctly -- no row drove a site-1 fault and a site-2 0x30 fault in the same session -- and the mutant passed 9/9 when built. Row X exists because of this, and was then WIDENED to three bytes because codex's variant of the same class used a different bit.

VERDICT: SOUND, and the other MEASURED SURVIVOR of pass 2: widening the site-2 key mask from 0x30 to 0xf0 -- one character -- so the shift is no longer bounded. Bytes 0x80 and 0xc0 are the SAME fault category and the fix draws one line for the pair; the mutant keys them apart and draws two, silently breaking the ceiling the enum comment states. It passed 12/12 and forced row CEIL. The same seat caught the comment claiming the two `address_transfer` defaults are 'the same invention with tidier syntax' -- measured, 0 is loud and 1 is silent, which is exactly why 1 survived.

THE MEASURE SEAT, and the only one that acted on the SHIPPED file rather than the brief. It built 16 binaries in its own tree and found that a brace slip confined to SITE 1 scored the detector 10/10 PASS -- because RPT drove [0x80, 0x80], a site-2 byte. It also named the structural blindness behind row N: 0x20 is declined but its field selects the ADDRESS arm, which performs no memory_rw and prints no line, so `transfers == []` reads clean while the address latch is corrupt.

It drove the ACCEPT side END TO END, recovering three device signatures back through eight input clocks: 0x0d (a value it had written), 0x04 (CTRL_24H, set only by DEVINIT(rs5c313)) and 0x06 (the host clock's tm_year % 10, which the probe cannot forge).

*** AND IT MEASURED THE DE-ESCALATION CLAUSE'S PREMISE INSTEAD OF ASSUMING IT: *** the same guard growth applied to the PRE-FIX bodies ENDED THE HOST, while post-fix the guest silently receives 0x50 where 0x0d was due. The tripwire this round deletes was real, and its deletion is now a measurement rather than an argument. Its refinement to ACCEPT-ROW FAILABILITY is the first queue question in `hold`.

CLOSE (assess and review), both questions answered.

*** Q1 (joint vs guard-only): NEITHER a fixed recipe nor an exception. *** Restate the rule by its DISCRIMINATOR: the accept row must redden under the LEAST-OBSERVABLE growth form that is measured NON-EQUIVALENT at that site, found by the reading the rule already mandates. Where the latch operand can mask the guard (#449), guard-only is equivalent and JOINT is the least-observable non-equivalent form. Where the latch operand is a compile-time constant the guard cannot feed (#451), guard-only is non-equivalent AND quieter than joint -- the harder form, so the one to build. 'Build the form the latch operand does not mask' is the correct generalisation, and it is NOT a rule change: it is the rule's own reason made explicit, of which JOINT was the first measured instance. Cost stays one mutant per predicate; where the reading is uncertain, build both -- a spare build is cheaper than a wrong reading.

*** Q2 (ask again once the table is clean): ADOPT, capped at ONE ask-again per detector per round. *** It is not the #392 chain: #392 was unbounded fix-of-fix passes with no stop condition; this is a single extra adversarial query against a CLEAN table with a measured stop. The yield is measured -- 2 of the 5 rows #451 added came only from the fifteenth-mutant ask -- and the mechanism is real: a clean table redirects seats away from the shapes the author already covered. THE CAP IS THE ANTI-#392 CLAUSE: a second ask-again after an empty first is where the chain starts, and anything found past the cap is FILED.

rows.title: sh4pclock  One guest TCR store ends the host on THREE machine types (hpcsh, baresh, testsh) -- the sh4 device is added by the CPU, but only 2 of 5 arch-4 SH machines set pclock
rows.witness: probe:regress/sh_pclock_probe.py (rung 3, 16 rows, SHIPPED). MEASURED 6/16 on the true pre-fix build and 16/16 post-fix, SAME SCRIPT BOTH SIDES. The pre-fix build was made from `git show HEAD:src/devices/dev_sh4.c` into a private clone and grep-confirmed to still contain `INTERNAL ERROR: pclock`, NOT from build/ -- a seat measured build/gxemul's mtime moving underneath it mid-review, so a run it believed was pre-fix was post-fix and nothing in the output distinguished them. Controls: LIVENESS (guest store then guest load of an asymmetric 0x12345678) and DEVICE SIGNATURE (IPRD reset value 0xda74, which RAM cannot produce and an unmapped address answers with `non-existant paddr`), both green on both sides and both in their OWN sessions so neither touches TCR.

closure.note:
*** THE DEFECT IS A CLASS, AND THE FIX IS AT THE GUARD FOR THAT REASON. *** cpu_sh.c:233-234 adds the sh4 device from `arch == 4`, so THE CPU BRINGS THE TMU AND THE BOARD BRINGS THE CLOCK, and nothing checked that the two agree. Five registered SH machine types name an arch-4 CPU; only machine_dreamcast.c:51 and machine_landisk.c:81 assign pclock. Fixing the three machine files would leave every FUTURE arch-4 machine inheriting the same host kill.
THE ROW'S TITLE SAID 'hpcsh AND testsh' AND THAT UNDERCOUNTS. Two pass-1 seats independently found that machine_test.c:535 is MACHINE_DEFAULT_CPU(baresh) and :541 is MACHINE_DEFAULT_CPU(testsh) -- two separately registered machines in one file -- so `baresh` was never named by the brief or the filing. Measured: it dies identically. THREE machine types, not two. A seat also measured -e jornada690 reproducing (the subtype is never read; same code path) and confirmed all five machines carry the device.
THE FIX follows #447's precedent twenty lines below in the same arm, and its stated reason: 'substituting a prescaler for a clock source we cannot provide would be inventing a rate'. Once-only diagnostic, break, no state touched, using the ELEVENTH SH4_VAL_* latch class -- free, because the tenth-class enum conversion was already discharged. The guard STAYS ABOVE the prescaler switch: run it lower and timer_hz is already set from `idata & 3`, so with pclock == 0 the debug() line announces 'clock set to 0.000000 Hz'. `m_below` measures exactly that and is caught by `unlatch` alone.
DE-ESCALATION CLAUSE DISCHARGED BY MEASURED KILL. The predicate that gated death is exactly one, and a seat established it was THE LAST GUEST-REACHABLE exit( IN THE DEVICE (one wrapped in #ifdef SH4_DEBUG, three on interrupt_handler_lookup construction failures; LINE NUMBERS OMITTED DELIBERATELY -- an earlier draft cited four and the paragraph correcting the false panel claim shifted every one of them, which is the finding: a comment citing line numbers in its own file invalidates them when edited). Four accept rows across TWO machines and TWO channels each -- a single row pinned at landisk's 33.33 MHz is passed by a mutant that HARDCODES 33333333, and dreamcast's 50 MHz is the discriminator. They redden under a guard-only growth mutant `|| (pclock % 256) != 0`; guard-only is the correct form by the #451 discriminator because THE LATCH OPERAND IS THE CONSTANT 1, which the guard cannot feed.
THE HONEST COST HAS TWO HALVES, and the round demoted the first too far before two seats corrected it. (a) The STALL remains the primary behavioural cost, and for automation it turns an immediate nonzero exit into a possible timeout. (b) ADDITIONALLY the diagnostic degrades from unmissable to once-per-timer. (b) does not replace (a). What narrows (a)'s practical reach today: hpcsh's MACHINE_SETUP has its hpc_bootinfo half commented out at :48-64 -- the live body still registers RAM mirrors and a framebuffer -- so with no console wiring, no bootinfo and no disk NO OS BOOTS THERE. Note the stall is only hypothetical ON HPCSH: baresh and testsh run hand-written test programs, and a program that programs TCR and polls TCNT IS the hang. This detector plants exactly such a program; what actually degrades is the diagnostic, from unmissable to once-per-timer-for-the-device-lifetime.
*** THE ROUND SHIPPED A FALSE CLAIM ABOUT ITS OWN PANEL AND THE MISCOUNTED SEAT CAUGHT IT. *** An early draft of the shipped comment said 'a panel of nine seats reached this 8-1'; it was written WHILE THE NINTH SEAT WAS STILL RUNNING and that seat then did not vote B. Corrected in place. Accurate: all nine answered, ALL NINE AGREE THE DECLINE IS MANDATORY, seven say it is the whole fix, two would additionally give the SYNTHETIC machines a defined pclock -- filed as sh4testclock, not merged, per the round-scope rule.
CORRECTED AFTER THE CODE COMMIT, by pass 2: the guard-placement claim cited #447's silent-wrong-rate hazard, which CANNOT OCCUR AT THIS PREDICATE -- pclock == 0 makes every prescaler case 0.0 and timer_hz[] is already 0.0 from the DEVINIT memset. The placement is still right, for diagnostic consistency (the debug() line is unlatched and would print per-STORE). And `m_below` was misattributed to that claim: it is the missing-`break` mutant caught by `unlatch`, and NOTHING in the kill table measures the guard's position. Also: the read-back channel is itself a FABRICATION -- real SH-4 always latches TCR, so a guest doing read-modify-write silently loses its update, and `unlatch` pins that as correct. It is the lesser of two fabrications, not an architectural channel, and the record now says so.

entries.note:
FOUND BY CHECKING A SITE THAT READS AS UNREACHABLE, at the owner's explicit request. 'INTERNAL ERROR ... Aborting' is construction-fault wording, which is why four rounds of SH-4 exit(1) work passed over it.

The chain has four links and all four were checked rather than assumed: the device is added from cpu_sh.c:200 by the CPU (so every arch-4 CPU has the TCR handler, whatever the machine); only machine_dreamcast.c:51 and machine_landisk.c:81 assign pclock; machine_hpcsh.c:89 names SH7750, which is arch 4; and one guest store then ends the host on -e jornada680.

entries.note: The interim state sqreadtype deliberately ships, stated out loud so the next round is motivated by a named gap rather than rediscovered. Codex's dissent that C1 is an 'unshippable intermediate state' is recorded rather than resolved -- the round-scope rule decided it, not a majority. Smallest implementation and the licensing witness are both recorded in the bug file so the next round does not re-derive them.

*** THIS ROW'S TITLE WAS A WRONG RECORD AND THE ROUND'S OWN DETECTOR DISPROVED IT. Corrected in place. *** It read '...after sqreadtype an SQ page raises no MMU fault of any kind', which `sq miss evt` refutes by observing a read-type TLB miss (0x040) on the FIXED build -- and which is false under the charitable reading too, since user-mode PR=00/01 still takes a read-type protection violation. The claim was corrected in memory_sh.c:296-303 DURING #454 and survived in two more places, including this title, which flows into matrix.html twice. Mechanical rule 2's corrected-in-one-place-survived-in-two, inside the round that celebrated a seven-site sibling sweep -- the sweep covered the OLD claim's sites and nobody grepped the round's own NEW claim. RANKING NOTE from the same seat, and it raises this row's priority: #454 did not merely inherit a pre-existing conformance gap. Before it, the misplaced write-judgment at PREF was a FUNCTIONING, wrongly-placed tripwire -- a guest flushing onto a clean page got IPW (0x080), onto a PR=00 page got 0x0c0. #454 correctly deletes that, and the manual-correct enforcement point (the store half) does not exist, so a D-bit-tracking or write-protection-relying guest is observably WORSE OFF. That is the de-escalation clause's exact hazard shape, and it means this row carries de-escalation weight rather than footnote weight.

rows.state_note:
*** SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-27: THE DEFECT IS THE **WRITE HALF ONLY**, and saying the window 'bypasses the MMU ENTIRELY' reintroduces wording this row's title was already corrected away from. ***

**Why the unqualified form is wrong:** the round's own `sq miss evt` detector observes a **read-type TLB miss (`0x040`)** on the fixed build, so the read side is NOT unrouted. `memory_sh.c:290-301` carries the corrected scope.

> **THE CORRECT STATEMENT: no initial-page-write exception and no write-side protection check on stores into the SQ window.** The read/prefetch path translates; the store path does not. That asymmetry IS the defect, and it is narrower and more defensible than 'bypasses the MMU'.

**AND THE SECTION CITATIONS ARE BOTH RIGHT, FOR DIFFERENT THINGS -- reconciled here so the next reader does not have to choose:**
  * **section 3.6.7** *defines* the Initial Page Write exception and its code: *"occurs when the D bit is 0 even though a UTLB entry contains address translation information matching the virtual address to which a data access (write) is made... Sets exception code H'080 in EXPEVT."* (`sh7750_hardware.txt:9918-9928`)
  * **section 4.7.4, 'SQ Protection'** *applies* it to the store queues: *"Write type exception judgment is performed for writes to the SQs... a TLB miss exception, protection violation exception, or initial page write exception is generated."* (`:11742-11748`)
**The code cites 4.7.4; I cited 3.6.7. Cite BOTH -- 4.7.4 is the one that makes it apply to this window, and 3.6.7 is the one that says what the exception is.**

**Ranking, from today's adjudication: 7th of 8.** Latent -- no known guest depends on SQ write-protection. *It is a fidelity gap, not a live corruption, and my earlier 'most severe row in the batch' was severity within that batch, not across the queue.*

*** INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-27, and the step that could have KILLED it -- whether SH-4 exempts the store queue from translation -- goes the OTHER WAY. The manual refutes the exemption. (Already documented in-source and filed; today's work is re-verification.) ***

**THE BYPASS IS UNCONDITIONAL.** `memory_sh.c:353-357`:
```c
/*  Store queue region:  */
if (vaddr >= 0xe0000000 && vaddr < 0xe4000000) {
        /*  Note/TODO: Take SH4_MMUCR_SQMD into account.  */
        *return_paddr = vaddr;
        return 2;
}
```
**No `MMUCR.AT` test, no UTLB walk, no PR/D check**, and it returns 2 (read/write). `cpu_sh.c:106` is the only assignment of `translate_v2p`, and the sole SH consumer of `0xe0000000` in `src/cpus/` is `pref_rn` -- **no store instruction special-cases the window**, so every `mov.l Rm,@Rn` into it takes this branch. The preceding arm (`:339-350`) matches neither, so the path is identical with AT=1 and AT=0.

*** THE MANUAL SETTLES IT AGAINST THE EXEMPTION, from three directions: ***
  * **section 4.7.4, SQ Protection** (`sh7750_hardware.txt:11742-11748`): *"When MMU is on -- Operation is in accordance with the address translation information recorded in the UTLB, and MMUCR.SQMD. **Write type exception judgment is performed for writes to the SQs** ... a TLB miss exception, protection violation exception, or **initial page write exception** is generated."*
  * **section 4.7.3** (`:11691-11696`): *"the ASID, V, SZ, SH, PR, and D bits have the same meaning as for normal address translation."*
  * **QACR is explicitly the MMU-OFF-only mechanism** (`:11719-11723`, `:10473`), so it is NOT an alternative translation path under AT=1.

**AND PRIVILEGE DOES NOT RESCUE IT.** The Data TLB Protection Violation table (`:12632-12640`) gives `PR=00` as **"Only read access possible"** in PRIVILEGED mode, with EXPEVT `0x0A0` read / `0x0C0` write at `:12650`.

*** THE ASYMMETRY IS THE CLEANEST STATEMENT OF THE DEFECT: THE READ SIDE IS TRANSLATED AND THE WRITE SIDE IS NOT. *** The flush path at `cpu_sh_instr.c:3706-3765` explicitly checks `SH4_MMUCR_AT` and calls `sh_translate_sq_v2p()` -> `translate_via_mmu()`. The store path does none of it.

**WHY THE SHIPPED DETECTOR CANNOT SEE THIS, and it is not a detector defect:** `regress/sh_halt_probe.py:590-599` pins `sq pr00 evt` and `sq d0 evt` to **NOEXC deliberately** -- those rows exercise the read-type PREF path, where no protection or dirty case exists. **No row exercises the STORE side at all**, so the detector is silent here rather than contradicting the finding.

**ADJACENT, DISTINCT, ALREADY FILED:** the `SQMD` TODO on that same branch is a SECOND gap -- section 4.7.4 requires an ADDRESS ERROR for a user-mode SQ access when `MMUCR.SQMD = 1` even when translation succeeds, and the store path checks neither. `pref_rn` does check it (`cpu_sh_instr.c:3709-3715`) but raises `EXPEVT_RES_INST` instead -- filed as `sh4sqexpevt`.

*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE and GUEST-REACHABLE. A store into the store-queue window BYPASSES THE MMU, so page protection is not enforced on it. The most severe row in this batch. ***

**The mechanism:** the SQ write path does not go through `sh_translate_v2p()` / `translate_via_mmu()` (`memory_sh.c:353-357`, `:203-241`, with the source's own commentary at `:289-303`), so a store into the SQ window lands directly in the device's `sq` array.

**Guest access sequence, fully specified by the seat:**
  1. guest kernel enables paging (`MMUCR.AT = 1`);
  2. guest maps the SQ virtual page `0xe0000000` in the UTLB **valid** (`V=1`) and either **clean** (`D=0`) or **read-only** (`PR=00`);
  3. guest issues `mov.l r0, @r1` with `r1 = 0xe0000000`.

**Expected on hardware (SH7750 sections 4.7.4 / 3.6.7):** an **Initial Page Write** exception (`EXPEVT = 0x080`) on `D=0`, or a **Data Write Protection** exception on a read-only page.
**Actual here:** the store simply succeeds.

> **So a guest that maps a page read-only, or clean-for-dirty-tracking, and then stores through the SQ window gets a write that hardware would have faulted.** That is protection and dirty-bit tracking silently not enforced -- not a fidelity nit.

**Observable:** the guest `EXPEVT` register after the store -- `0x080` (or the write-protect code) when correct, unchanged when broken. Readable by an ordinary guest load, so no new probe capability is needed.

**CHECKABLE AGAINST A PRIMARY SOURCE WE HAVE:** the seat cites SH7750 sections 4.7.4 and 3.6.7, and `_scratchpad/sh7750_hardware.txt` is present and greppable. **Confirm the two sections before the round** -- and read the PROSE, not a figure, per the extraction rule.



*** PROMOTED BY THE CODEX RATING PASS, 2026-09-07, ON A ROW IT WAS NOT ASKED ABOUT -- and the
promotion is the answer to the brief's Q3, *what does my reading order miss?* ***

*"Promote `sh4sqwrite` ahead of the latent ASIC proposals.  Its title sounds like missing tests,
but `memory_sh.c` (anchor `Store queue region:`) grants read/write access directly, and `dev_sh4.c`
(anchor `DEVICE_ACCESS(sh4_sq)`) accepts the writes into queue storage.  Hardware requires
write-type exception checks on stores into those queues."*  (Renesas SH7750 manual, S4.7.4.)

> **THAT IS A GUEST-REACHABLE MISSING PROTECTION CHECK, not a coverage gap** -- and it was invisible
> to my keyword scan because the TITLE reads like harness debt.  *"No known guest depends on it"
> does not establish unreachability.*

**And the row's existing witness cannot carry it:** `sq pr00 evt` and `sq d0 evt` in
`regress/sh_halt_probe.py` exercise **PREF's READ-type judgement**, so they cannot witness a missing
STORE-side check.  A witness for this row has to drive a store.

*Filed as the strongest single finding of that pass; it needs a `sev` and a round of its own.*

rows.title: sh4itlbpr  ITLB data array 1 is one bit too wide, and SIX shipped rows now REQUIRE the extra bit
rows.witness: none -- ASSESSED 2026-08-27 and NOT CHANGED. A rung-3 probe is designable (privileged store/load at 0xf3000000, key on r2 & 0x20) but is deliberately not built: the oracle-correction rule requires re-pinning six SHIPPED rows and measuring the committed build RED *before* any edit, which needs a build the machine embargo forbids.

entries.note: dev_sh4.c:1020-1021 (cited as :999-1001 when written; the file has since moved and that range is now translation-cache invalidation -- re-derived 2026-08-23 by a changed-file sweep, and the real site is the mask expression in DEVICE_ACCESS(sh4_itlb_da1) at :1017) reuses the UTLB's two-bit SH4_PTEL_PR_MASK (0x60) where the ITLB has PR on bit [6] alone (3.7.2 at :10035, 3.4.2 at :9402). Correct mask 0x1ffffdda, model uses 0x1ffffdfa. SEVERITY LOWER THAN THE SWEEP RANKED IT: itlb_lo is live for instruction accesses (memory_sh.c:113-122) but the arm tests only (pr & 2) = bit 6, and data accesses never scan the ITLB. So the live cost is #452's six EQUALITY rows pinning a bit the hardware leaves undefined -- the SECOND detector in this family pinning the model rather than the architecture.

rows.state_note:
*** FIRST EVIDENCE 2026-08-27, from a farmed codex job. The mask arithmetic is CONFIRMED exactly; the SEVERITY is lower than the seat implied, and the reason is a phrase in the manual the seat did not weigh. ***

**CONFIRMED, and recomputed here from the header's own constants rather than transcribed:** `dev_sh4.c:1020-1021` builds the ITLB data-array-1 mask with `SH4_PTEL_PR_MASK` = **0x60, a TWO-bit field**, giving 0x1ffffdfa. Narrowing PR to the ITLB's own `SH4_ITLB_DA1_PR` = 0x40 gives 0x1ffffdda. Both values match the seat digit for digit. **The extra bit is 0x20.**

**THE PRIMARY SOURCE AGREES, and it was read as PROSE, not off a figure** (`sh7750_hardware.txt:10035-10036`, section 3.7.2):
  *"In the data field, PPN is indicated by bits [28:10], V by bit [8], SZ by bits [7] and [4], PR by bit [6], C by bit [3], and SH by bit [1]."*
**Bit [6], singular** -- so for the ITLB, bit 5 is not part of PR. The sibling `sh4_utlb_da1` at `:1220-1224` keeps the two-bit mask and is CORRECT: the UTLB's PR really is [6:5].

*** BUT THE SAME FIGURE'S LEGEND (`:10062`) SAYS RESERVED BITS ARE "0 write value, UNDEFINED READ VALUE" -- SO RETURNING 0x20 IS ARCHITECTURALLY PERMITTED, NOT WRONG. *** That single clause is what moves this from 'defect' to 'fidelity nit', and no seat quoted it.

**THE SEAT'S LOAD-BEARING PREMISE -- 'no translation decision uses that bit' -- IS TRUE, BUT ONLY VIA A TWO-STEP CHAIN IT DID NOT GIVE, AND I FIRST SCORED IT FALSE.** The single consumer is `memory_sh.c:163`, `pr = (lo & SH4_PTEL_PR_MASK) >> SH4_PTEL_PR_SHIFT` -- a TWO-bit read, and `lo` **can** be `itlb_lo` (`:120-122`). That looks like the bit reaching a decision. It does not, because:
  1. `:114-117` -- ITLB entries are walked **only** when `FLAG_INSTR` is set;
  2. `:195-200` -- the instruction arm tests **only** `if (!(pr & 2))`, i.e. `pr` bit 1, which is `lo` bit 6, the REAL PR bit.
Bit 5 becomes `pr` bit 0, which that arm never reads. The data-side `switch (pr)` at `:206`/`:219` DOES separate 0/1/2/3 -- but the ITLB never reaches it.

> **THE LATENT COUPLING, which is the part actually worth carrying:** the bit is inert because of ONE arm's specific test, not because of any structural guarantee. An edit making instruction protection 'more complete' -- replacing `if (!(pr & 2))` with a `switch (pr)` mirroring the data path -- would make a guest-stored reserved bit LIVE, flipping pr=2 into pr=3. Narrowing the store mask would make the inertness structural. *That is the real argument for the change, and it is a defence-in-depth argument, not a correctness one.*

**NOT CHANGED, and the cost is why.** Six SHIPPED rows in `#452`'s detector pin the current mask -- R3 and A4i in `sh4_tlbda2_probe.py` (`:37`, `:251`), C1 in `sh4_tlbda2_witness.py` (`:126`) -- all keyed off `ITLB_MASK = ... | _PR | ...  # 0x1ffffdfa` (`probe:71`, `witness:53`), which the probe uses as a **per-device signature** (`:68`) to tell ITLB from UTLB. The ADDITION LICENCE wants a measured delta or a transferred warrant; the manual supplies neither, since it makes the present read value legal. And the ORACLE-CORRECTION RULE requires re-pinning those rows FIRST and measuring the committed build RED under the new expectations **before** touching code -- which needs a build. **Correctly queued behind the machine embargo, not skipped.** (The signature property would survive a narrowing: 0x1ffffdda vs the UTLB's 0x1ffffdff still differ.)

*Apparatus note, against my own checking rather than the seat's: my first grep for the header constants used `[ 	]` in ERE, which is the set {space, backslash, t} and does NOT match a tab -- so it returned NOTHING and I nearly scored the seat unverifiable. Second instance of the same class today, after the `0x3e0` literal-vs-symbol miss on `sh4pcic15`.*

rows.title: shprotld  Every SH TLB row runs privileged, so the READ-side protection code is unreachable and corrupting it is invisible to all 31 rows

entries.note: From #454's ask-again, after the kill table was clean. FILED rather than fixed under the floor rules: the mutation is in the general TLB table not at #454's call site, and #454's detector is already above the vacuity floor with (a)(b)(c) green, so this is coverage DEBT. One user-mode row would close this AND a second escape named independently at pass 1 ('return 2 on any UTLB hit'), which is invisible for the same reason -- the caller treats 1 and 2 alike.

*** A THIRD FAMILY MEMBER, found by attacking #454's detector after its kill table was clean, and it is coverage debt rather than a reopening. *** Delete the early `return` at cpu_sh_instr.c:3761 -- call KEPT, abort REMOVED, which is vacuity-floor clause (d)'s own shape. It raises the fault and then completes the flush anyway, and it passes all 34 rows: on the miss rows `paddr` is an UNINITIALISED LOCAL, because the tlb_miss path never writes *return_paddr, so the payload lands at unpinnable stack garbage; and the deterministic protection path is privileged-unreachable post-fix. IT CLOSES WITH THE ROW THIS ROW ALREADY OWES: the same user-mode PR=00 row that closes shprotld's two existing escapes closes this one too -- PROVIDED that row pins BOTH observables, EXPEVT = 0x0a0 AND the destination untouched. It must pin both anyway for the return-2-on-any-hit escape, so the marginal cost of the third member is zero. Note the shape: an uninitialised local is what makes the escape invisible, so a row that checks only the EXCEPTION and not the DESTINATION cannot see it -- which is the one-observable-channel hazard the oracle-correction rule already names.

rows.state_note:
*** A FARMED grok JOB CONFIRMED THIS ROW 2026-08-26 AND ADDED A COMPANION GAP THE ROW DID NOT NAME. ***

**CONFIRMED, by enumeration rather than impression:** the `EXPEVT_TLB_PROT_LD` arm is privileged-unreachable on every SH TLB row in the tree. The seat read every SH TLB probe end-to-end and listed each row's SR/MD rather than inferring privilege from comments.

**ONE PREMISE OF MY BRIEF CORRECTED:** the read-side check is `translate_via_mmu()` in `src/cpus/memory_sh.c`, **not** a separate helper in `cpu_sh.c` -- `cpu_sh.c` only CONSUMES the code after it is chosen. Two callers: the P0/P3 arm of `sh_translate_v2p()` (ordinary load/store/fetch) and `sh_translate_sq_v2p()` from `X(pref_rn)` with `flags=0`.

**THE COMPANION GAP, and it is the useful addition: PRIVILEGED `PROT_ST` IS ALSO UNTESTED.** No row issues a write-type translation against a read-only page; PREF passes `flags=0`. So the row's read-side framing is right but narrow -- the store side has the same hole, and a round that builds a user-mode read row should cover both while the apparatus is out.

*** AND A SEAT-FAILURE MODE I HAVE NOT SEEN BEFORE TODAY: THE SEAT REFUTED A SENTENCE THAT DOES NOT EXIST. *** It reported an *'attack on the filed 0x180 sentence'*, arguing that a user P1 fetch is `0x040` and that `0x180` is `EXPEVT_RES_INST`. **The arithmetic is CORRECT -- verified, `sh4_exception.h:71` defines `EXPEVT_RES_INST 0x180` -- and the TARGET IS IMAGINARY.** Searched `OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md`, `ledger.json`, `CHANGELOG.md` and every `regress/*.py` with a word-boundary pattern: the only `0x180` in the tree is an unrelated code offset in a gdrom probe. No record makes the claim.

**That is the MIRROR of the `gdromdmawidth` farm result the same hour**, where agy re-derived a finding the tree already held and reached a WORSE conclusion because the constraints lived in a comment it had not been given. Same underlying cost, opposite direction: **a seat briefed without the existing record spends its effort on the wrong target** -- either re-deriving what is known, or refuting what was never claimed.

*The seat was scrupulous about its own limits and that is why this is cheap to correct: it labelled the 31/31 figure READ FROM THE FILING rather than re-measured, and said plainly it did not re-run the mutant because it had no build.*

**STILL NEEDS A BUILD** -- a user-mode read row plus (now) a privileged write-type row. Queued behind the machine embargo with the analysis done.
