rows.title: sh4pcic15  PCIC interrupt line 15 can never be delivered -- it lands on 0x3e0, one slot past the priority loop's bound, and the obvious fix is a NO-OP
rows.witness: none -- LATENT, and established as such by READING 2026-08-27: no modelled device connects to PCIC line 15, PCIC MMIO never raises an interrupt, and the only prospective PCI device on landisk is compile-disabled and would use line 5. No guest access sequence exists in the shipped tree.

entries.note: [filed by the MAIN LOOP wearing the fable5 model -- seat and adjudicator are distinct hats; the seats that found it are named in the text] dev_sh4.c:73 sets N_PCIC_IRQS 16 and :2822-2836 wires every one as SH4_INTEVT_IRQ0 + 0x20*i, so line 15 lands on 0x3e0 (SH4_INTEVT_IRQ15, sh4_exception.h:157). The priority loop at cpu_sh.c:352 stops at SH4_INTEVT_IRQ14 (0x3c0), so that slot keeps priority 0 for the machine's life. *** EXTENDING THE BOUND FIXES NOTHING: the loop body is `15 - ((i - SH4_INTEVT_IRQ0) / 0x20)`, which yields priority 0 for IRQ15 -- exactly the state it is already in. The bound is not an off-by-one; it is where this formula runs out of nonzero priorities, so a round must decide what IRQ15's priority OUGHT to be. *** #455 also changed the symptom class: before it, an assert on a priority-0 line ran fatal() then exit(1), so this was a guest-reachable host kill; after it the interrupt is SILENTLY DROPPED. That is the de-escalation clause's own hazard arriving on schedule. HONEST LIMIT: header-and-loop-bound arithmetic across three files, NOT witnessed -- no probe has driven a PCIC line 15 assert.

*** THE ROW SAYS 'NOT WITNESSED', AND A WITNESS IS BOTH CONSTRUCTIBLE AND ADMISSIBLE. *** The carrier's own rule is that 'no witness of either kind' is a CHECKABLE claim and must be checked rather than asserted -- dfreq's was measured false by building one in a single session -- so this is that check, done by READING (flagged as a reading, not a measurement; the tree was busy with #461's pre-fix run and a probe would have contended with it). THE OBSERVABLE ALREADY EXISTS: cpu_sh.c:168-173 registers `iprio_%x` as a readable setting for EVERY 0x20 slot in 0..0xfff, which includes `iprio_3e0` (IRQ15). The hardwired priority loop at cpu_sh.c:390 is `for (i = SH4_INTEVT_IRQ0; i <= SH4_INTEVT_IRQ14; i += 0x20)`, so slot 0x3e0 is never written and keeps 0 while 0x3c0 (IRQ14) gets 1. Two `print` commands on an unmodified machine separate the two. AND RUNG 2 IS THE RIGHT RUNG FOR IT, not a concession: the ladder licenses machine construction as a reproduction for 'defects in code construction itself executes (init-time)', naming the macppc heap OOB #23 as the exemplar. This IS init-time -- the loop populates the priority table at CPU init and the defect is a slot it never reaches. The ladder's warning about rung 2 is that registration proves presence not reachability, for ACCESS-PATH defects; this is not one. WHAT A RUNG-2 WITNESS WOULD NOT SETTLE, said plainly: it observes the priority TABLE, not delivery. It cannot show that an asserted line 15 is dropped -- for that the carrier's free-running shape is required (sr=0x40000000, vbr into RAM, `bra .` after the trigger, breakpoint at VBR+0x600), and driving a PCIC line needs a PCI device landing on line 15, since dev_sh4.c:2951-2967 registers the 16 lines as `<path>.pcic.<i>` for bus_pci_init's pciirq rather than as anything a guest store reaches directly. So the honest split is: the priority-0 STATE is witnessable at rung 2 today; the DROPPED-DELIVERY symptom is not, and the round should not claim it is. STALE CITATION CORRECTED: the row cites dev_sh4.c:2822-2836 for the wiring; that range is now the default arm's fatal()/exit block. The wiring is at :2951-2967.

rows.state_note:
*** FIRST EVIDENCE 2026-08-27. The row was a BARE TITLE with an empty note; a farmed codex job established it and every load-bearing claim was re-verified here by reading. ***

**THE CLAIM IS TRUE.** `dev_sh4.c` registers SIXTEEN PCIC interrupts (the *'Register 16 PCIC interrupts'* loop over `N_PCIC_IRQS`), and `SH4_INTEVT_IRQ15` is `0x3e0` (`sh4_exception.h:157`). But priority initialisation in `cpu_sh.c` runs

    for (i = SH4_INTEVT_IRQ0; i <= SH4_INTEVT_IRQ14; i += 0x20)

**-- it stops at IRQ14.** Line 15 therefore keeps priority 0, and an assertion at priority 0 returns without scheduling delivery. **A line the device registers can never be delivered.**

**IT IS LATENT, and the seat established that rather than asserting it:** PCIC MMIO never generates an interrupt; no modelled device connects to `.pcic.15`; landisk's only prospective PCI device is compile-disabled AND would use line 5 anyway. **There is no guest access sequence in the shipped tree**, so this ranks below anything guest-reachable.

**THE OBSERVABLE a detector would key on:** guest interrupt-vector entry with `SH4_INTEVT == 0x3e0` -- delivery sets INTEVT and transfers to `VBR+0x600`; the broken code never reaches that handler. That is one channel, not a design.

*The seat labelled its own work honestly: 'MEASURED -- Not run; no build is needed to settle these source facts.' Correct, and it is why this row could be settled under the machine embargo.*

*** ONE VERIFICATION NOTE, because it cuts against my own checking rather than the seat's: my grep for the literal `0x3e0` in the device file returned NOTHING and I nearly scored the citation as wrong. The file uses the SYMBOL `SH4_INTEVT_IRQ15`. The seat cited the right site; my pattern could not see it. Same shape as the other apparatus misses today -- searching for a value where the code names a constant.***

NOT FIXED: extending the loop to IRQ15 is a one-token change, but it is an EDIT TO INTERRUPT PRIORITY INITIALISATION and the addition licence wants a measured delta. With no device on line 15 there is nothing to measure today -- which is precisely why the row is latent, and why the fix should ride with the round that first connects a device there.

entries.note: PREDICTED, NOT MEASURED -- the seat said so itself. Mutant: guard #458's new rescan as `if (cpu->cd.sh.int_to_assert == 0) sh_recalc_int_to_assert(cpu);`. It escapes because `raise` asserts at priority 0 so the guard still fires; `lower` writes both IPR values BEFORE asserting, so nothing is standing during either store; and `deassert` uses the other path entirely. Guest-visible miss: assert SCIF at 15, then IPRC[7:4] := 1 with IMASK=1 -- hardware must drop it, the mutant keeps a stale level 15. THE KILL ROW IS ONE LINE: `run_deliver(0x00f0, 1, raise_iprc(0x0010))` wanting `refused`. NOTE this is a DETECTOR gap, not a code defect: the shipped code calls the rescan unconditionally and handles standing-lower correctly.

rows.state_note:
**TRUE as PREDICTED coverage debt -- and the label matters.**  `regress/sh_iprbcd_probe.py:264`:
`lower` changes priority BEFORE assertion, `raise` begins with no selected request, `deassert`
removes the request.  **None tests lowering the priority of an ALREADY-SELECTED request while it
remains asserted**, which is guest-reachable through SCIF and IPR writes.

**The product handles the case correctly today:** `cpu_sh.c:519` calls `sh_recalc_int_to_assert(cpu)`
unconditionally and the helper resets and recomputes the selection.  *So the escape stays labelled
PREDICTED, never measured* -- the distinction this project's mutant-that-will-not-die rule exists to

rows.title: sh4cpudevscope  the SH-4 on-chip block is added PER-CPU but is machine-scoped, and sh4pclock is one symptom of three
rows.witness: none

entries.note: *** THE CLASS #459 IS AN INSTANCE OF. *** cpu_sh.c:233-234 does device_add(machine, "sh4") from inside the CPU constructor, so a machine-scoped device is created once per CPU. Three measured symptoms: (1) sh4pclock -- the CPU brings the TMU and the board brings the clock, with nothing checking they agree, CLOSED in #459 at the guard; (2) `-n 2 -E landisk` REFUSES TO CONSTRUCT with `ERROR! "sh4" collides with device 11 ("sh4")`, so SMP is impossible on every SH machine and the reason is this line; (3) dev_sh4.c (near the end of devinit) hardcodes `machine[0].cpu[0].irq[...]` for the TMU interrupt lookup, which is only correct because (2) makes a second CPU impossible. Fixing (2) without (3) would produce a device on CPU 1 whose timer interrupts route to CPU 0.

rows.state_note:
**TRUE -- a product OWNERSHIP defect, and the reachability axis is what holds it at `low`.**
`cpu_sh.c:232` (anchor `device_add(machine, "sh4")`) sits inside each SH-4 CPU constructor, while
`dev_sh4.c:2844` (`DEVINIT(sh4)`) registers FIXED windows in SHARED machine memory.  A second SH-4
CPU therefore hits the overlapping-device construction check **before guest execution** --
**so guest software cannot create this topology**, which is why it is not higher.

**And removing the registration collision alone would not fix it:** the three TMU lookups still
contain `machine[0].cpu[0].irq`, so ownership would remain wrong.  *The missing-clock host
termination was separately fixed by `#459` and is not this row.*

rows.title: sh4frqcr  FRQCR is a bare latch with no reset value, so a guest reads back 0x0000 -- not a legal value for the register hardware derives pclock FROM
rows.witness: harness:READ from the shipped source and `_scratchpad/sh7750_hardware.txt` (SH7750 Hardware Manual Rev.7.00), 2026-08-30.  `dev_sh4.c` declares `uint16_t cpg_frqcr;` and touches it in exactly two places -- the write arm stores `idata`, the read arm returns it -- with NO initialiser anywhere, so it is zero from the `memset` at device construction.

entries.note: dev_sh4.c's `case SH4_CPG_FRQCR` models FRQCR as a plain store/load with no initialisation, so a guest reads 0x0000. SH7750 Hardware Manual Rev.7.00 Table 10.3 gives the legal initial values as H'0E1A / H'0E23 / H'0E13 / H'0E0A depending on clock mode. THIS IS THE HONEST LONG-RUN ANSWER TO sh4pclock: real hardware derives the peripheral clock from FRQCR and the mode pins, and a seat measured that the CPU:peripheral ratio in that table is only ever 4 or 6 -- calibrated against dreamcast, whose 200 MHz / 50 MHz = 4 is a legal mode this tree independently knows. A round here could make pclock DERIVED rather than assigned. Note the bound is not enough on its own: machine_hpcsh.c sets no emulated_hz at all, so the tree does not even claim a Jornada CPU clock to divide.

*** WITNESS CONSTRUCTIBLE AT RUNG 3, and the MANUAL confirms the value is wrong. *** dev_sh4.c:2715-2720 is a bare latch -- `odata = d->cpg_frqcr` with no reset value written at init, so a guest reads back whatever DEVINIT's memset left, i.e. 0x0000. THE MANUAL, READ LOCALLY rather than taken from a search summary: _scratchpad/sh7750_hardware.txt:18607-18608 reads 'FRQCR is initialized only by a power-on reset via the RESET pin. The initial value of each bit is determined by the clock operating mode', and the bit table immediately below at :18610-18614 gives initial values CKOEN=1 (bit 11), PLL1EN=1 (bit 10), PLL2EN=1 (bit 9) with bits 15-12 = 0. So the reset value carries at least 0x0E00 and is NEVER 0x0000. The register table at :18476 marks the reset column 'Undefined*'; :18607 is the footnote that explains the asterisk, so 'undefined' means MODE-DEPENDENT, not zero -- a distinction that would have been easy to read the wrong way from the table alone. A guest reading FRQCR therefore sees both PLLs disabled and clock output disabled, the opposite of the reset state. WITNESS: one 16-bit guest load from 0xffc00000 on an unmodified SH-4 machine. HONEST LIMIT, the same shape as sh4pcic15's: the model has no clock-operating-mode concept, so a round must DECIDE what to present rather than read one value off the manual. The three bits above are mode-INDEPENDENT and settle the floor; IFC2 and the divider bits are not.

rows.note: *** THIS ROW WAS A 4-CHARACTER STUB.  Filled 2026-08-30 from the manual, which CONFIRMS the claim and SHARPENS it: the defect is not merely 'no reset value', it is that THREE BITS ARE ARCHITECTURALLY 1 AT RESET AND THE MODEL READS THEM BACK 0. ***  **THE MANUAL, section 10.4.1, quoted from PROSE rather than a figure** (the extracted tables in this file stagger names against values; the prose does not):  *"FRQCR is initialized only by a power-on reset via the RESET pin.  The initial value of each bit is determined by the clock operating mode."*  So there is no single constant -- **but the bit table is unambiguous about which bits do NOT depend on the mode**, and it is aligned rather than staggered (eight initial values against eight bit positions):  bits 15-12 are Reserved, initial 0, *"always read as 0"*; **bit 11 CKOEN = 1, bit 10 PLL1EN = 1, bit 9 PLL2EN = 1**; bit 8 IFC2 and bits 7-0 (IFC1/IFC0, BFC2-0, PFC2-0) are mode-dependent and printed as `--`.  **SO THE MINIMUM ARCHITECTURAL RESET VALUE IS 0x0E00** (0x800 | 0x400 | 0x200), and the model returns 0x0000 -- which tells a guest that **clock output is disabled and BOTH PLL circuits are off**, a state the hardware cannot be in after a power-on reset.  **THE FIX IS ONE INITIALISER**, and its only design question is what to do with the mode-dependent low bits: either pick the divider ratios matching the clock mode GXemul models and say which, or set 0x0E00 and state in a comment that bits 8-0 are left zero because the emulator models no CKIO mode.  *The second is honest and cheap; the first needs a mode decision this row should not make silently.*  **SEVERITY, stated rather than assumed: UNKNOWN GUEST IMPACT.**  No rig here is known to read FRQCR, so this is a correctness defect with no measured symptom -- it belongs BELOW the host-kill rows and above cosmetic work.  A guest computing peripheral clock rates from these dividers would divide by zero-derived ratios, which is the shape worth watching for, but nothing in this tree has been observed doing it.
rows.state_note: **SEVERITY SET LOW, 2026-09-07, by the MAIN LOOP** (not a flagship adjudication -- opus5/fable5 are reserved for the 09-09 adjudication, and a rating is exactly the kind of judgment call that seat exists for; overturn it freely).  REASON: ASSESSED and not changed -- a bare latch with no reset value; the readback is 0x0000 and no consumer has been shown to care.

entries.note: doc/TODO.html:322-323 lists 'SH3-specific devices: Pretty much everything!' immediately followed by 'NetBSD/evbsh3, hpcsh!', grouping hpcsh with an SH3 target; machine_hpcsh.c:89 names SH7750, which is arch 4. TWO SEATS INDEPENDENTLY REFUSED TO SETTLE THIS FROM MEMORY, which is the #357/#362/#365 citation failure NOT repeating -- there is no SH-3 manual in _scratchpad, hpcsh's platid/bootinfo block is entirely commented out, HISTORY never mentions hpcsh, and vripreg.h (included by machine_hpcsh.c) is NEC VR41xx MIPS, a copy-paste leftover from hpcmips. IF IT IS SETTLED as SH-3, note what changes: arch-3 removes the WHOLE dev_sh4 block (CCN/MMU, INTC, TMU, RTC, BSC, DMAC, SCIF, TLB arrays, PCIC), both SH-3 interrupt handlers are /* TODO */ stubs (cpu_sh.c:527-533) that silently drop asserts, and cpu_sh.c:224 uses a leftover UTLB loop counter as templ.line -- latent today only because that handler is a stub. Obtain a source first; the SH7750 precedent shows that costs one download.

rows.title: sh4pclockquiet  five measured mutants of #459's pclock guard all score 16/16, because the declining-write value set is exactly {0x0000, 0x0001}
rows.witness: none

entries.note: COVERAGE DEBT filed after #459's capped ask-again. A measuring seat built six mutants and FIVE scored 16/16: m_unie (`&& !(idata & TCR_UNIE)`) which lands a TCR with timer_hz == 0 for EXACTLY the value a guest must write to use a TMU at all, while going QUIETER than the fix; m_below_switch (guard moved below the debug line) giving 4 unlatched `clock set to 0.000000 Hz` announcements for 4 stores; m_valkey (key `idata ? idata : 1u`) giving 3 lines for 4 values; m_tmr2 (`&& timer_nr != 2`); and m_wrongnr (every line says 'timer 0'). Only m_valnarrow died, 15/16, killed by `unlatch`. *** THE ROOT CAUSE IS ONE SENTENCE: the declining-write value set is exactly {0x0000, 0x0001} -- the three kill rows and says/once/pertmr all write 0x0000 and unlatch writes TCR_TPSC_P16, so ANY narrowing predicate that admits both escapes. *** m_valnarrow's death shows the remedy: a second distinct value. FOUR of the five closing rows cost ZERO extra sessions; only unlatch2 at TCR_UNIE|TCR_TPSC_P4 needs a new one, and it kills m_unie and the whole narrowing family.

rows.state_note:

rows.title: sh4gdromexit  GDROM_DATA had NO LEGAL FIRST TOUCH -- four exit(1) in one register's arm, every access width and both directions fatal on a fresh device
rows.witness: probe:regress/gdrom_data_probe.py (rung 3, 23 rows, SHIPPED). MEASURED 5/23 pre-fix and 23/23 post-fix, SAME SCRIPT, with the pre-fix build rebuilt from `git show HEAD:` into a private clone and grep-confirmed to still contain the old fatal text -- NOT from build/, which a seat had measured moving underneath it mid-review the previous round. All 17 pre-fix FAILs read `died`; none failed by a wrong value. Controls: LIVENESS (guest store then guest load), SH4 DEVICE SIGNATURE (IPRD reset 0xda74), and a GDROM-SPECIFIC mapping proof (a served GDROM_BUSY read rather than a paddr fault) -- all three green on both sides and each in its OWN session, so no control touches GDROM_DATA.

closure.note:
*** THE DETECTOR WAS INVERTED AND A SEAT CAUGHT IT BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN. *** Its rows asserted the OLD fatal text must be ABSENT, but the agreed #447/#459 shape KEEPS the diagnostic and drops only exit(1) -- so DELETING THE WHOLE REGISTER ARM scored 13/13 while the intended fix scored 8/13. Re-pinned in oracle-correction order: expectations first, committed build measured RED, then the code. The discriminating shape is driving the SAME site twice in one session -- pre-fix dies, the fix says it exactly once, a deleted arm says it zero times. A survival-only oracle cannot separate the last two.
THREE MORE DETECTOR DEFECTS, each found only by measuring: all four 'same site twice' rows were running ONE access (pc set to the second site, step 1), so they read 1 whether the latch worked or not; a rebuild lost the width rows' LOAD variants, and restoring exit(1) on WRONG-WIDTH READ ONLY then scored a clean 14/14 while one guest MOV.B still ended the host; and the accept row was survival-only, never touching GDROM_DATA, so a mutant stripping the whole success path scored full marks.
*** THE FOURTH DE-ESCALATED PREDICATE HAD NO ACCEPT ROW AND ITS MUTANT SCORED 22/22 WITH A BYTE-IDENTICAL VECTOR. *** Four host-fatal predicates were removed; three gained rows and `len` gained none. The mutant -- log, then decline instead of continue -- is the round's OWN CENTRAL CLAIM sitting unobservable, and it is the likeliest future edit here, since it is what the other three sites in the same arm do and what dev_wdc.c:155-167 does for its own bad-length case. Fixed in-round under L3 and DISCHARGED BY MEASURED KILL: m_widthdecline scores 22/23, red on `accept w8` alone.
THE FIX IS DELIBERATELY NOT UNIFORM. Three sites decline; the width guard LOGS AND CONTINUES, on dev_pvr.c:1577-1581 (#187)'s stated warrant that removing it changes no bound. Two pass-1 seats voted to EMULATE narrow access instead, and a build measured that ACTIVELY HARMFUL -- cmd_count stepping by 1 makes eleven byte writes plus one word write go 11->13, skipping the ==12 equality, reaching a site this round had assessed unreachable, and writing cmd[12] one past the array.
CORRECTED BEFORE SHIP: 'six byte stores dispatch exactly as six word stores do' is measured TRUE FOR THE TOC PACKET 0x14 ONLY, whose odd bytes are already zero -- idata>>8 forges every odd command byte to zero. A RELOCATION, not a regression, but it means 'changes no bound' is the memory-safety argument and not the whole safety story. Also, the per-site latch decision is this round's own measured warrant and is NOT inherited from dev_wdc.c, which SHARES one flag between its two sites.
:334 JOINED, AND THE JOIN FAILED A TEST IT COULD HAVE BEEN RECORDED AS PASSING. It and the COND_DATA_AVAIL site are one predicate family, and shipping three of four would leave a device where a declined read is safe in one state and lethal in another. But the reopening rule prices 'no new oracle', and reaching :334 needed a new opcode, a new loop shape and a new state manipulation. Recorded as DELIBERATELY OVERRIDDEN rather than met.

entries.note: CENSUS taken after #459 closed the last guest-reachable exit( in dev_sh4.c, counting CODE only -- `grep -c 'exit(1)'` is measurably wrong in this tree because the hardened comments DISCUSS exit(1) constantly, so dev_sh4.c scores 21 by that method and 0 by a real one. Live (non-#ifdef, non-construction) exits remaining on the SH surface: dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c 14, dev_dreamcast_g2.c 6, dev_dreamcast_maple.c 3, dev_dreamcast_asic.c 1, cpu_sh_instr.c 2, cpu_sh.c 1 (sh_exception). THE GDROM ONES ARE THE MOST GUEST-REACHABLE: handle_command() switches on d->cmd[0], a byte the guest writes, and its arms exit(1) on an unimplemented command, on a Read-TOC length that is not 408, and on a data format that is not 0x20 -- each an ordinary guest-supplied value. WITNESS SHAPE IS ALREADY PROVEN: a rung-3 cold-debugger probe on `-E dreamcast -x` (the -x is required; two console inputs make construction fatal without it, console.c:994-1007). NOT YET WITNESSED -- no dreamcast image exists in _images/, so the probe must drive the GDROM registers by planted guest stores rather than by booting.

TWO ROUNDS RUNNING THE HIGHEST-VALUE SEAT, AND BOTH TIMES BECAUSE IT BUILT THINGS. At pass 1 it ran the probe against six builds of its own and found THE DETECTOR WAS INVERTED -- deleting the register arm scored 13/13 while the intended fix scored 8/13 -- before a line of code was written. It also measured the brief's Option C ACTIVELY HARMFUL, settled the decline-vs-continue split by measuring that `len` appears exactly once in the arm, and corrected the census to EIGHT single-access-fatal sites. At pass 2 it built eight more binaries and found the round's undischarged de-escalation obligation: the width predicate had no accept row and its mutant scored 22/22 with a byte-identical vector. It also measured that log-and-continue is NOT width-transparent, correcting a claim that was about to ship.

Caught that the pass-1 brief said THREE exit sites when the arm has FIVE -- my quote elided two behind ellipses, and the de-escalation clause enumerates every predicate that gated death, so a wrong count made that enumeration incomplete BY CONSTRUCTION. Also caught my overclaim that 'a driver probing the device cannot avoid this': drivers probe STAT/BUSY/COND, and NetBSD's gdrom.c writes COND=0xa0 before ever touching DATA, so its first touch is legal by construction. At pass 2 it ruled on the re-pointed-regex question -- a pre-fix RED is NOT sufficient, because pre-fix reddens by PROCESS DEATH before any count is taken, so what defends a re-point is the surviving-but-wrong control. Its :334 FILE ruling was overturned by measurement and it was asked to defend that; it agreed on the merits while correctly noting the 'no new oracle' test was failed, which is now recorded as an override.

Named the escape that mattered most at pass 2: restoring exit(1) on WRONG-WIDTH READ ONLY passed all 14 rows, because the rebuild had wrapped the width rows around stores. Also caught that :334 was shipped-but-undriven ('not both-neither'), that the accept row never read the register, and that no row pinned the declined VALUE. Four findings, four rows added.
OPTION A at pass 1, SHIP at pass 2. Argued the latch must be per-site and that dev_wdc.c is the right precedent rather than sh4_val_first().
OPTION A. Substantive on the latch-scope question.

Voted OPTION B, three separate latch classes. Not taken: three classes with identical payload is registry bloat, and the duplicate-ID hazard grows with class count for zero added discrimination. The PER-SITE half of its position was taken.
Voted OPTION C -- emulate narrow access. MEASURED ACTIVELY HARMFUL: it re-opens the 'Too much GDROM_DATA' exit and writes cmd[12], one past the array.

Voted OPTION C on the argument that a byte access to a 16-bit port is a legal BUS operation rather than a guest fault. THE CLASS ARGUMENT WAS RIGHT and is why the width guard logs-and-continues instead of declining -- but its REMEDY (emulate) was measured harmful, and its supporting claim about what hardware does on a width violation is unsourceable in this tree.

SHIP, with a correct trace of every read and write path for len in {1,2,4,8}. NOTE ON EXTRACTION, NOT ON THE SEAT: it wrote `VERDICT: **SHIP**`, and BOTH my ad-hoc grep and the committed seat_verdicts.py regex require a letter immediately after the colon -- so a correct answer would have been filed as a FORMAT MISS. Filed as verdictbold.

rows.title: verdictbold  seat_verdicts.py cannot read a VERDICT line wrapped in markdown emphasis, so a correct answer is filed as a format miss
rows.witness: probe:tools/pipeline/seat_verdicts.py --selftest

closure.note: *** THIS CLOSURE NOTE WAS ITSELF A WRONG RECORD AND A REGRESS SEAT REOPENED THE ROW FOR IT. Corrected in place. *** It said 'closed with 17 selftest rows and 8 mutants', credited commits 3ad72e0 and e9f8c0c only, and repeated a dead-class claim that had gone false. All three are fixed here: the row closes at 3ad72e0 e9f8c0c 8eeeea2 with **24 rows and 13 mutants, every mutant red**. Crediting the 17/8 state was the worst of the three, because 8eeeea2's own commit message measured that state a NET REGRESSION (silently-wrong 57 -> 79 across 406 modern seat answers) -- the closure credited the version its own round had condemned. AUTHOR SELF-REVIEW DISCLOSED (badge A) on the fix; every escape was found by an independent seat and then measured. WHAT THE TOOL DOES: it decides whether a panel is recorded as split or unanimous, so its failures propagate into every round record. It shipped for its whole life with no test. Defects found and fixed: markdown emphasis unreadable (a LIVE seat's correct verdict filed as a format miss); a single-word capture that collapsed SHIP WITH CHANGES to SHIP and every OPTION A/B/C to OPTION, so EVERY SPLIT PANEL THIS PROJECT RAN WAS RECORDED AS UNANIMOUS; `VERDICT: Ship with changes` returning the single letter 'S' -- not None, an actual token that would have been reported as the verdict; mid-sentence prose swallowing a real answer via first-line-wins; and a line-start-only anchor that rejected 52 of grok's 58 answers, blanking a seat by the tool rather than by the seat. The general fix is REPORTING disagreement rather than resolving it -- last-wins was measured no better, and on this round's own pass 2 it reports codex as DO NOT SHIP by reading an illustrative example.

entries.note: MEASURED on the #460 pass-2 panel: minimax answered `VERDICT: **SHIP**` and the committed extractor's VERDICT_RE = r'VERDICT\s*:\s*([A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]*)' requires a LETTER immediately after the colon, so the `*` defeats it. The seat would have been recorded under 'answered, NO VERDICT LINE (format miss)'. *** THIS IS THE MIRROR IMAGE OF THE FAILURE THAT FILE EXISTS TO PREVENT: it was built so a DEAD seat is never counted as agreement, and here a LIVE seat with a correct verdict is downgraded to a formatting failure. *** grok's verdict on the same panel was also emphasis-wrapped (`VERDICT: SHIP WITH CHANGES**`). The fix is one character class -- allow leading `*`/`_`/backtick -- but it must PRESERVE the findall-count discriminator that stops the brief's own menu line matching, which is the guard that makes the extractor safe. Also fix the ad-hoc greps in the loop's own habit, which have the same blind spot.

Measured every claimed form against the live extractor rather than reasoning about the regex: 12 of 12 forms correct after the fix, all four guards still rejecting (brief menu, wrapped menu, instruction, silent seat).

*** MEASURED THE FIX A NET REGRESSION, over 953 real seat files in 144 panel dirs. *** Scored committed against mine on the 406 modern answers: silently-wrong rose 57 -> 79. The loosening genuinely fixed its two target shapes and CONVERTED LOUD FAILURES INTO QUIET ONES -- a mangled token or a bare None is something a human sees and checks; a plausible verdict lifted from the wrong line is not. Named the exact live instance (panel_20260823_085034/kimi.txt:4, a bullet re-rendering the brief's menu, which defeats all three guards and reported SHIP for a seat that wrote SHIP WITH CHANGES three times). *** AND MEASURED THAT LAST-WINS IS NOT THE FIX *** -- on this round's own pass 2 codex quotes a DO NOT SHIP inside an illustrative example below its real answer, so last-wins reports codex as DO NOT SHIP; it declined to claim its own 94%-vs-91% edge, saying the proxy was itself wrong on an inspected case. Recommended REPORTING the disagreement instead, which is this file's own doctrine applied to itself and needs no guess about which line is the answer. Adopted. Also: the check_score_claims pin count was a DISPLAY not an assertion, and the whole check can be disarmed for a probe with no behaviour change at all by quoting the pin literal, since regress/lib.sh:82 compares as a string either way. Also found a live duplicate-stem collision (`idle` pinned 9 in gate_arm.sh and 3 in gate_m88k_rounding.sh, last-write-wins by sorted filename).

Found the false positive that mattered most and it was still live after the first round of fixes: `My verdict: the code is fine and the records are honest.` -> `THE CODE IS FINE`. Case-insensitive matching made every mid-sentence 'verdict:' a candidate, and first-line-wins means one sentence of preamble outranks the seat's real answer -- *** AND THIS ROUND'S OWN BRIEFS ARE ABOUT THE VERDICT EXTRACTOR, so the very next panel would have hit it. *** Prescribed the line-start anchor and checked it against every row first. Also caught that all five case-insensitivity rows tested the ACCEPT side only, so the selftest was green while the extractor turned prose into a verdict -- a row set that only proves what SHOULD match is half a detector.

[panel_20260823_173510]  SHIP WITH CHANGES. Named the same-line-prose case (`VERDICT: SHIP I think this is ready.` -> `SHIP I THINK THIS`), conflicting verdicts, and fenced-code quoting as missing rows -- the first two measured true and are FILED as verdictprose; the split reporting makes them loud rather than silent. Its structural ask is the sharpest: provenance for a score claim should come from SYNTAX, not numerical proximity -- an explicit docstring marker rather than a distance heuristic. That is what the '<N>-row' era escape now does, arrived at independently. Asked that section U not be blocking until parsing is fail-closed and the checker has tests; the checker now has both a pinned coverage floor and negative controls, so the substance is met even though the check stays hard.

Also asked the docstring state the date false-positive class explicitly so a future operator does not chase a date mismatch.

*** REOPEN, on two MEASURED wrong records -- and the first is the sharpest finding of the round because it shows an absence record expiring. *** (1) THE M6 'DEAD CLASS' RECORD WENT FALSE WITHIN ONE COMMIT. At e9f8c0c a mutant aimed at a leading emphasis class could not be made to fail, because re.search was UNANCHORED -- true, measured, and correctly recorded as an absence. Then 8eeeea2 ANCHORED the label and introduced a NEW leading class in the anchor branch, broader than the one that died (it also admits `-`, `>`, `#`), and nothing re-ran the death measurement. The seat checked out e9f8c0c to verify the original warrant, then measured HEAD: dropping the new class REDDENS `label emphasis`. The class was alive, load-bearing, and covered by NO mutant -- one of only four rows the entire shipped table could not redden, the other three being deliberate controls. Re-verified independently before acting; M6 reinstated against the class that actually exists, comment rewritten as death-then-resurrection. (2) This closure note credited the 17/8 state that 8eeeea2 had measured a net regression, and omitted 8eeeea2 from the commit list. Corrected above. ALSO NAMED AND FIXED: the sentence-boundary branch had no mutant, so the grok row's only provable failure ran through M2's multiword capture -- attributable to the WRONG feature. M13 added; it also documents the 52-of-58 seat-blanking as a single-edit restoration. ON THE RULE QUESTION -- ADOPT, and it is not a generalisation from two cases: a mutant that will not die has exactly three explanations (mis-built mutant, dead target, mis-cut row), this round measured which one all three times and got three DIFFERENT dispositions, and the carrier already treats non-dying mutants as results twice (#449 measured EQUIVALENT, #451 the opposite). MULTI-PART AS DEFAULT: NO -- default stays smallest-single-edit, with multi-part licensed in exactly two shapes: verbatim reinstatement of what shipped (floor clause (b) applied to a harness tool), and reach-the-guard composites where EVERY added edit is first measured GREEN ALONE. That second condition answers the unfalsifiability objection: an unconstrained composite can be steered until it fails for an unrelated reason; a composite whose parts are proven inert can only fail through the interaction being claimed. ON verdictstate: FILING WAS CORRECT, not a floor breach -- the floor grades the detector shipped WITH THE FIX, and the fix is verdict_of. It attacked the state machine anyway across all 981 corpus files: ALL 78 WALLED CLASSIFICATIONS ARE GENUINE, ZERO FALSE WALLS, so no measured false pass exists to license L2. It did find one live mis-bucket on 9 real files (a 429 routed to 'transport error' when it is wall-shaped, and the remedies differ), filed into verdictstate with 78/9/0 as the golden baseline.

rows.title: gdromdefault  both `default:` arms of dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c ran exit(1) -- roughly 248 of 256 control offsets and 27 of 32 DMA offsets were host-fatal to a read OR a write at any width
rows.witness: probe:regress/gdrom_default_probe.py

closure.note: AUTHOR SELF-REVIEW DISCLOSED (badge A) on the fix; every escape was found by an independent seat and then MEASURED. Three panels ran (pass 1, pass 2, pass 3) plus two flagship reviews. 9/32 pre-fix, 32/32 post-fix, both measured AT 32 rows (pre461f.out); gate 10 PASS at 190 checks run alone (gate461f.log), 179 before this round. *** THE HOLD IS THE STORY OF THIS ROUND. *** The owner chose to hold it uncommitted for the Fable seat across two usage-limit failures, and that decision paid for itself four times: codex's pass-2 DO-NOT-SHIP on a write alias the fix would have CREATED; opus5's four mutants at a full 27/27; kimi's per-direction diagnostic finding; and fable5's undischarged L3 obligation, which no other seat named across two full panels. THE DEFECT: both `default:` arms ran exit(1) -- 21 control offsets sampled, 19 killed the host. Fixed with #443's latched-bitmap idiom plus a decline. THE FIX ALMOST SHIPPED A WORSE DEFECT THAN IT CURED: the DMA tail stores through TRUNCATING division, so a declined byte write at +0x05 landed in dma_reg[1] (the DMA destination), with the same alias reaching length and count. `case 0x18` reads count and enable to arm, then destination and length -- so a guest could arm and AIM a transfer entirely through declined offsets. PRE-FIX those accesses exited, so the fix would have created the capability, and the round's own comment claimed the opposite. Closed by an alignment guard whose soundness is an INJECTIVITY PROOF (on multiples of 4, off -> off/4 is injective, so an aligned offset reaching the arm cannot share an index with any implemented case), independently re-derived by a seat before it was believed. FOUR MUTANTS SCORED A FULL 27/27 at pass 2 and are now dead. The one that mattered: `& 3` -> `& 1`, one character, re-opening the alias -- and `dma alias`, the row written to pin that very repair, was STRUCTURALLY BLIND to it because it uses an odd address both guard forms drop. That measurement is what the owner adopted as vacuity-floor clause (d) NULL-REPAIR RED. FILED, NOT FIXED: gdromdmawidth (an ALIGNED narrow write to an IMPLEMENTED offset clobbers all 32 bits -- same family, and this round's new alignment rule explicitly does NOT cover it, so a future reader applying that rule would conclude the site is safe) and gdromcondlies. Eight exit(1) sites remain live in the file and are named individually, because half a census reads as a whole one.

entries.note: MEASURED pre-fix: 21 control offsets sampled, 19 killed the host; a 32-bit read scan of the DMA window died on committed HEAD. Fixed by a per-word/per-direction latch bitmap (#443's idiom) plus decline. *** THE PASS-2 PANEL FOUND THE FIX ITSELF INTRODUCED A WRITE ALIAS AND RETURNED DO NOT SHIP. *** The DMA tail indexes with truncating division, so a declined byte write at +0x05 landed in dma_reg[1] (destination); +0x09/+0x0d reach length and count. Pre-fix those exited, so the fix would have CREATED the capability. Repaired by returning before both tails on any unaligned access. Detector gdrom_default_probe.py, 31 rows, gate 10. HELD UNCOMMITTED pending the Fable seat.

PASS-2 KILL TABLE AT THE 31-ROW PIN, measured in a private clone restored cmp-clean afterwards: fix 31/31; pre-fix HEAD 8/31 (23 rows red -- the round's headline number, MEASURED at the shipped row count rather than carried over from a smaller detector); m_dmarevert (verbatim reinstatement at the DMA site) 22/31, so floor clause (b) is satisfied at BOTH fixed sites; m_oob 23/27 with scan uniq = 15. *** THE FOUR ESCAPES THIS SEAT FOUND AT 27/27 ARE NOW ALL KILLED: *** m_align1 29/31 (dma align16, dma rdleak), m_rdleak 30/31 (dma rdleak SOLE killer), m_wrongarr 30/31 (both windows SOLE killer), m_ctlwrongarr 28/31. m_align1 is the one that matters -- a ONE-CHARACTER edit, & 3 -> & 1, re-opened the alias the round had just closed, and `dma alias` (the row written to pin that very repair) was STRUCTURALLY BLIND to it because it uses an odd address that both guard forms drop. That measurement is what the owner adopted as vacuity-floor clause (d) NULL-REPAIR RED.

SEAT FAILURE, recorded by name and NOT counted as agreement. Fired twice on 2026-08-23; both returned 'You've reached your Fable 5 limit' -- the second deliberately, per the re-fire-a-walled-seat-once rule. The round is HELD UNCOMMITTED for this seat by owner decision. A third firing was launched after the owner ran /login, because this project has measured that an ACCOUNT-STATE CHANGE (not a calendar date) is what revived this seat once before.

*** DO NOT SHIP, AND IT WAS RIGHT -- the highest-value finding of the round. *** The DMA tail stores with TRUNCATING division, dma_reg[relative_addr / sizeof(uint32_t)], so a declined byte write at +0x05 misses the exact-value `case 0x04`, reaches the default arm, and is then stored into dma_reg[1]. Enumerated the full alias set: +0x05, +0x09..0x0b, +0x0d..0x0f, +0x15..0x17. Its exact words: 'Pre-fix, these accesses exited before the tail store. The fix therefore turns formerly fatal unimplemented accesses into unchecked mutations of implemented state.' Verified by reading case 0x18: it consults dma_reg[3] (count) and [5] (enable) to arm, then [1] (destination) and [2] (length) -- so a guest could arm and AIM a transfer through declined offsets alone. THE ROUND'S OWN COMMENT CLAIMED THE OPPOSITE ('No declined offset can reach a load-bearing one'). Fixed by returning before both tails on any unaligned access. Also corrected the direction-split cost: 12 bytes across both windows, not 8 as the brief said.

GO-WITH-CHANGES. Verified the two BADVAL sites and the gate/manifest wiring by citation. REQUIRED CHANGE: add DMA-window trigger coverage to the probe -- at that point every one of the 21 rows drove the control window, so the round claimed to fix two arms while covering one. Ten DMA rows now ship.

Named the must-change list and every item was actionable: write the four DMA rows the gate already listed and make the probe's count agree; correct or remove the 'inert / no declined offset reaches a load-bearing index' sentence (which codex independently proved false -- TWO seats reached the same defect from different directions); and PICK AN UNALIGNED-STORE BEHAVIOUR AND PIN IT, which is exactly the fix that was adopted. Also caught that the gate and probe comments still asserted raw-address indexing scores `scan uniq` 56/56 -- 'that was the analysis WITHOUT the guard'. Measured 15. Explicitly listed what was fine so it would not be re-argued.

Ship with two comment edits, both correct. (1) *** THE DIAGNOSTIC SAYS '(once per offset)' BUT THE LATCH IS KEYED BY OFFSET AND DIRECTION *** -- so a read and a write to the same offset each print, and the text understates the volume by 2x while misdescribing the key. That key is the thing the round spent a measurement defending (it overturned a 3-1 panel vote), so the user-visible message contradicting it is a wrong record in the one place a user looks. (2) The 'five words past ... dma_reg[]' magnitude claim should be replaced by the provable sentence. Also noted gdrom_unimpl_first takes uint32_t off while callers pass uint64_t relative_addr -- implicit narrowing, safe today because dispatch bounds it, and doubly safe behind the guard; assessed not worth churn. Verified the GDROM_REGX..GDROM_COND define move is a pure reorder with no value changed.

PACKET-FED. Named a mutant that passed all 21 rows: collapse bits[k >> 5] to bits[0] in both the test and the set. All 21 offsets then map to word 0 and, since 21 < 32, no two keys collide -- so every row still passes. Its reasoning is the general one and it is right: 'the detector's coverage is too shallow to ever reach word 1'. The `scan` row (all 64 word offsets) reaches word 1 and kills it; that row already existed, so this is a coverage observation rather than an escape. Honest about its own scope: also noted the DMA accept side was unpinned, which agy and grok independently required.

PACKET-FED. Three findings. (1) NREGS_GDROM_DMA is 0x100/4 = 64 against a 0x80 registered window -- the two constants must be reconciled. ASSESSED AND KEPT with a comment: harmless, since memory_rw gates on the registered range so the largest reachable index is 31, and shrinking it is a behaviour change with no witness. (2) A DMA row is REQUIRED -- the new default arm is uncovered. Agreed, ten now ship. (3) Ask-again mutant: delete the bounds check, which passes every control row because control offsets are all < 0x100 against 64 keys, so the guard is dead for control and only matters for DMA.

PACKET-FED. Ship, with two comment improvements. Assessed all four challenge areas and its per-item verdicts were sound: the direction split is justified by idata capture but the comment overstates it; the bounds guard is live only against the OOB mutant and dead on the happy path; and the decline semantics were 'pinned by INSPECTION, which is incomplete -- add a line-number citation or one detector row'. That is the same gap agy, grok, glm and deepseek each reached by a different route, and it is the gap the round's ten DMA rows close. Named GDROM_NKEYS = 0x100 (dropping the /sizeof) as a mutant invisible to all 21 rows.

*** SEAT ALIVE -- REVIVED BY THE OWNER'S /login, NOT BY THE CALENDAR, WHICH IS THE THIRD TIME THIS PROJECT HAS MEASURED THAT PATTERN. *** Two firings earlier the same day returned the usage limit; the owner ran /login and the next firing returned BOTH liveness tokens (prompt nonce and a verbatim CHECKPOINT.md quote), so prompt delivery AND file access are proven rather than assumed. VERDICT: SHIP WITH CHANGES. Q1 -- INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED the alignment rule's injectivity proof and verified it against the real case labels in BOTH switches, including the load-bearing set that case 0x18 reads and the 8-byte-access path; also checked the CONTROL window needs no such rule because its default arm has no store tail. Q2 -- `both windows` is an acceptable sole carrier (measured sole kill, not a vacuous one), but it drove READS ONLY, so a DIRECTION-ASYMMETRIC cross-wiring would pass all 31 rows; upgraded in-round under L1 to four accesses expecting 2/2, at zero new-session cost. Q3 -- SEVEN WRONG RECORDS, every one confirmed by grep or by reading before it was acted on. The sharpest: the gate comment's boast that its numbers were 'MEASURED at the final row count, not carried over' was ITSELF carried over and false three ways (final count is 32 not 27; no 7/27 measurement ever existed; the honest pre-fix number is 8 because dma seed passes pre-fix) -- the third generation of the frozen-number defect, inside the sentence memorialising the first two. Also: the refuted 'two fields that authorise a transfer' claim stood verbatim in THREE files because mechanical rule 2 (grep for siblings) was not run; the 'neither subsumes the other' heading survived in two places after its own body called it false; 'accept8 ... one session' is refuted by the loop eight lines below it; 'nine rows use pair()' when there are fifteen call sites; a gate claim that a host kill is 'otherwise unreachable' when it is reachable through the front door via two implemented cases; and the detector heading wrong in every field, with 'gate 10 PASS' never true at any pin at or above 25. Q4 -- FOUND THE ROUND'S UNDISCHARGED DE-ESCALATION OBLIGATION (L3): accept8 exists for the control window because three narrowing mutants scored full marks, and the DMA window got the same fatal->survive fix with NO accept row. Traced it: delete `case 0x18:` and the DMA trigger silently dies forever, where before this round that deletion was a loud exit on first touch. `dma accept` added. Also caught the gate's named-row list at 27 entries against 32 rows, missing exactly the five highest-value rows -- every one added BECAUSE a mutant escaped. And that the exit census names 4 of 8 survivors, which reads as a whole census.

[panel_20260823_213058] PASS 3. Asked that an explicit write-direction condition be added around the DMA arming at `case 0x18`, and said the '+0x18 semantic gap should be closed before treating gate 10 as a shipping record'. *** CHECKED IN TWO MINUTES RATHER THAN JUDGED, AND IT IS ALREADY SATISFIED. *** The arm tests `idata != 0` with no direction test of its own -- so the concern is well-aimed -- but `idata` is declared `= 0` and assigned ONLY under `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE)` 140 lines above, so on a read it keeps its initialiser and the arm cannot fire. A real, local guarantee, not an accident of memory_rw memsetting the caller's buffer. NO CODE CHANGE; the probe comment now names the actual property, because a guard 140 lines from what it protects is correct and hard to see, and a careful seat did not see it. Its other calls were right: the store asymmetry is NOT a defect (control has no shadow-register convention, DMA does, so each matches its own window), and the bitmap arithmetic is correct in the final state -- while noting `sizeof(arr) * 8` is brittle under a future element-type change, which is exactly the mutant the measuring seat was asked to build.

[panel_20260823_213058] PASS 3, GO. Verified the whole final state by citation rather than assertion: the unaligned guard at dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:878-882 quoted verbatim, the bitmap arithmetic (`1u << (k & 31)`, word `k >> 5`, bound via `sizeof(arr) * 8`), all 32 rows enumerated in the gate, and -- the one worth having -- it independently re-derived that the nine pre-fix survivors all touch IMPLEMENTED offsets, which is the round's own explanation for why 9 and not 8.

[panel_20260823_213058] PASS 3, ship. *** THE ONLY SEAT ASKED FOR A NEW 32/32 MUTANT THAT SAID PLAINLY IT COULD NOT FIND ONE, and enumerated what it had eliminated: *** `& 3`->`& 1` caught by `dma align16`, the write-restricted guard caught, cross-keyed arms caught, and `break` instead of `return 1` re-opens the alias and is caught. An honest empty result with its search space named is worth more than a speculative find, and it is the packet-fed seat that gave it. Also reached the correct read-safety answer for +0x18 independently ('guarded on idata/write direction').

[panel_20260823_213058] PASS 3. *** FOUND THE MACRO'S REAL CONSTRAINT, and it is the worst kind of brittleness because the obvious sanity check passes: *** `sizeof(arr) * 8` is element-type-AGNOSTIC and computes a correct BIT COUNT for any array, but gdrom_unimpl_first takes `uint32_t *bits` and indexes `bits[k >> 5]` with `1u << (k & 31)`. A uint8_t[] would give the right count and the wrong indexing. Now stated in the source (codex flagged the same brittleness independently; C11 _Static_assert is unavailable in this C99 tree). Also asked for a `relative_addr & 3` guard on the CONTROL arm as insurance -- DECLINED WITH A REASON rather than overlooked: that arm has no store tail, so the guard would be DEAD CODE, and this round already rejected one dead bounds check for exactly that reason. The invariant it depends on is now written down instead, with the instruction that adding a tail requires re-deriving the injectivity argument there.

[panel_20260823_213058] PASS 3, ship. Reached the control-window invariant independently of glm and asked for the same thing -- that the assertion be COMMENTED, both to document the current invariant and to flag that the injectivity argument needs re-deriving if a store tail is ever added. Done, in those words. Also asked that the injectivity reasoning sit next to the bitmap helper for a maintainer who adds an implemented DMA offset or resizes the bitmap; it is at the DMA arm, which is where the truncation it defends against lives.

[panel_20260823_213058] PASS 3. Did not assert a verdict it had not earned -- it named FOUR measurements (M1-M4) whose outcomes would decide between SHIP and an escape, and said so explicitly. *** M4 CHECKED IMMEDIATELY AND CONFIRMED: *** it asked for one-line confirmation that the DMA `odata` preload and the tail store index the SAME slot -- :749 is `odata = d->dma_reg[relative_addr / sizeof(uint32_t)]` and :889 is `d->dma_reg[relative_addr / sizeof(uint32_t)] = idata`, character-identical index expressions, so `return 1 -> break` has no silent read-path variant. Its M2 (whether `dma accept` and `dma seed` jointly assert quiescence AND write/readback at all five implemented offsets) is the sharpest residual and is the same gap a flagship seat raised about read-only accept rows.

[panel_20260823_213058] PASS 3 -- IN FLIGHT at the time this was recorded, not absent. Its file showed the opening plan and the first four tool steps: reading both switch tails, the remaining exit(1) sites, `relative_addr`'s type, how memory_rw treats unaligned 32-bit accesses, and whether the DMA accept path can arm on a read. That last question is the one codex raised and it was settled independently while grok was still working. Recorded as MID-ANSWER rather than as a seat failure, which is the distinction this project has mis-made before: a short file is not a dead seat.

closure.note: Verbatim reinstatement at the DMA site (m_dmarevert) measured 22/31, killing NINE rows (an earlier draft said five, which was the 27-row-era count from a different table -- two eras fused in one sentence) -- vacuity-floor clause (b) satisfied at BOTH fixed sites, which is what licenses closing this as part of #461.  COMMITS SET 2026-08-25 from a substance read of git. This row was raised by a seat ENUMERATING the file and joined #461/#462 on a MEASUREMENT; the fix and its detector shipped at `7c9dd9e`, which touches `src/devices/dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` and adds `regress/gdrom_default_probe.py` -- the probe this row's `witness` field already names. rows.title: gdromdmawidth  the DMA tail store ignores `len`: an ALIGNED byte or 16-bit write to an implemented offset clobbers all 32 bits of the shadow register
rows.witness: none committed -- MEASURED 2026-08-23 at rung 3 via a scratchpad probe (reported, not pinned): the row is DELIBERATELY not shipped, because pinning 0x000000ff would enshrine this model's own behaviour as an oracle

entries.note: Pre-existing upstream, untouched by #461, found by the pass-2 measuring seat while building mutants against the alias fix. NOT joined: #461's semantic class is 'unimplemented offset'; this is 'implemented offset, wrong width' -- a different fix design (read-modify-write honouring len, which raises an endianness question the default arm never has to answer) and a different oracle, so the round-scope rule makes it a separate round. *** IT IS THE SAME FAMILY AS THE ALIAS #461 DID FIX, AND #461's NEW RULE DOES NOT COVER IT: *** 'alignment alone separates unimplemented word from misaligned access to an implemented one' is true and says nothing about an ALIGNED NARROW write to an implemented offset. A future reader applying that rule here would conclude it is safe. Related to [hlen], but the OPPOSITE direction: hlen is a wide access spanning registers, this is a narrow access clobbering one. `dma seed` is one store away from being a witness.

*** WITNESS CONSTRUCTIBLE AT RUNG 3, contrary to `witness: none`. Verified by READING the arm; flagged as a reading, since a probe run would have contended with a live gate. *** The carrier's rule is that 'no witness of either kind' is a CHECKABLE claim and must be checked rather than asserted. Checked: `len` appears exactly THREE times in DEVICE_ACCESS(dreamcast_gdrom_dma), and all three are byte marshalling -- memory_readmax64(cpu, data, len) on the way in and two memory_writemax64(..., len, ...) on the way out. The store itself, at dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:889 (re-derived 2026-08-23), is `d->dma_reg[relative_addr / sizeof(uint32_t)] = idata;` -- a full 32-bit assignment with no width discrimination anywhere. THE WITNESS IS `dma seed` PLUS ONE STORE, exactly as the filing predicted: 32-bit store 0x11223344 at DMA+0x04, then a BYTE store of 0xff at DMA+0x04 (ALIGNED, so it matches `case 0x04` and is NOT the #461 alias), then read +0x04 back. Real hardware leaves the upper 24 bits; this model yields 0x000000ff. Ordinary guest instructions through real address decode on a committed machine -- rung 3, no new device and no machine edit, so no laundering. NO BUILD NEEDED EITHER: the defect is pre-existing upstream and untouched by #461, so it is in the current binary.

[panel_20260823_215652] *** FOUND THE DECISIVE PRECEDENT, AND IT IS IN THIS VERY FILE FROM THE PREVIOUS ROUND. *** dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:515-522, written by #460: 'DO NOT "EMULATE" NARROW ACCESS INSTEAD. A pass-1 panel split on that, and it was MEASURED ACTIVELY HARMFUL: letting cmd_count step by 1 makes eleven byte writes plus one word write go 11 -> 13, SKIPPING the == 12 equality, so busy&0x08 never clears and the next write reaches the "Too much GDROM_DATA" exit -- otherwise unreachable. It also writes cmd[12], one past the array.' VERIFIED BY READING. Option A is exactly that shape, ruled out by the file's own measured history one round ago. Its reachability line is the right distinction too: 'Reachable as a guest instruction; unobserved as a driver path. That is not Option C.' -- rung-3 reachability is established, driver reachability is not, and the ladder says a witness makes an item ELIGIBLE while severity orders it.

[panel_20260823_215652] Found the OTHER in-tree precedent, independently: sh4_bsc16_report() at dev_sh4.c:1646, the tree's existing handling for a narrow access to a wide register. Its conclusion: 'in-tree precedent unequivocally supports Option B (decline partial/narrow writes with a latched warn-once diagnostic)'. Two seats finding two different precedents that agree is the strongest form this panel produces -- the answer was already in the tree twice and the brief invented a three-way choice that the tree had effectively made.

[panel_20260823_215652] Supplied the discriminating row and the comment amendment, both adopted. The row -- W32 +0x04 = 0x11223344, then W8 +0x04 = 0xff, then R32 +0x04 -- separates all three options: A gives 0x112233ff little-endian (0xff223344 big-endian), B gives 0x11223344 preserved, C gives 0x000000ff. Its amendment text is the one to use: it SEPARATES ADDRESS DECODING FROM WIDTH VALIDATION, so #461's alignment rule cannot be misread as proof that implemented cases are width-safe.

[panel_20260823_215652] Reached codex's discriminating row independently, with the same three expected values including the endianness split on Option A. Its amendment wording is the crisper of the two: 'An aligned offset reaching the default arm is genuinely an unimplemented word. This does not imply that an aligned narrow access to an IMPLEMENTED offset is safe; narrow accesses to implemented registers are a separate width question and are currently not width-discriminated.'

[panel_20260823_215652] Option B with the clearest cost/benefit statement: one branch on `len != 4` before the tail store; consistent with #461's decline-rather-than-corrupt philosophy; establishes the missing in-tree precedent for the WIDTH axis without committing to Option A's endianness-dependent merge; and it 'turns an unreachable silent-clobber into an unreachable LOUD no-op'. Explicitly ranked B over C: 'B is C plus a guard for the same engineering cost.'

[panel_20260823_215652] *** THE ONLY SEAT THAT REFUSED TO PRETEND THE REACHABILITY QUESTION WAS SETTLED, and it is right. *** 'Probably not in well-behaved guest code, but the brief does not let us prove a negative.' It also caught a trap in the brief's own framing: adding the witness row makes the defect reachable IN CI, which 'is not the same as reachable' by a guest driver -- a distinction this project's witness ladder makes and the brief blurred. Its answer is correctly CONDITIONAL rather than confident.

[panel_20260823_215652] Went furthest on the endianness question the brief called the real technical risk, working out what memory_readmax64 does to a narrow value and where a byte write at +0x04 lands in dma_reg[1]. Its answer is the reason Option A is unsafe to implement from the brief alone: the fact is derivable but was NOT established in the tree, and SH-4 runs either endianness.

*** VERDICT: OPTION C, OVERTURNING A UNANIMOUS 7-OF-7 PANEL FROM SOURCE. *** The panel converged on Option B (decline narrow writes). This seat fetched mainline Linux drivers/cdrom/gdrom.c and read it line by line: :622 `__raw_writeb(1, GDROM_DMA_STATUS_REG)` is the DMA TRIGGER -- a BYTE WRITE to this window's +0x18 on every transfer -- and :618 byte-READS the same offset to poll for completion, while the four value registers at :585-589 are always __raw_writel. *** SO OPTION B WOULD BREAK A BOOTING LINUX, *** and the width-blind code delivers exactly the semantics the one real narrow user needs. The defect's actual content -- clobbering a value register's upper bits -- sits in cells no known guest reaches. It also checked NetBSD (never touches the DMA window) and promemul/dreamcast.c (zero references), and was explicit that KallistiOS widths are BELIEVED only. *** AND IT REFUTED OPTION A ON A DIFFERENT AXIS THAN THE BRIEF EXPECTED. *** The brief called endianness the real technical risk; the seat showed it is DERIVABLE (cpu_sh.c:96 sets EMUL_LITTLE_ENDIAN UNCONDITIONALLY, so there is no big-endian SH in this tree and the merge is always the low lane -- the brief's 'SH-4 can run either endianness' is true of silicon and FALSE of this tree, verified independently). The real objection is an ABSENT ORACLE: 0x005f74xx is Sega's Holly ASIC, outside the SH7750 manual, and this project holds NO documentation for it -- so the filing's own 'real hardware leaves the upper 24 bits' was an UNSOURCED CLAIM, the #357/#362 shape. A would ship an invented behaviour and pin the invention with a detector row. ON PRECEDENT it corrected the panel again: the BSC16 idiom (dev_sh4.c:1620-1680) is the direct shape-match, but *** IT TRANSFERS BY ITS WARRANT, NOT ITS SHAPE *** -- its warrant is 'a real OpenBSD/landisk boot makes ZERO non-16-bit BSC accesses (measured), so the latch costs a correct guest nothing', and that warrant FAILS here. Decided design recorded as B': decline at the four VALUE registers only, keep +0x18 byte-capable. It also flagged that the row pinning the REAL contract is currently UNBUILDABLE -- any nonzero store at +0x18 hits one of sh4gdromexit's filed exit(1) kills -- so this item is gated behind that round by probe-buildability rather than by ranking.

rows.state_note:
*** A FARMED agy JOB RE-DERIVED THIS ROW INDEPENDENTLY 2026-08-26, AND ITS RECOMMENDATION WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A DEFECT. Recorded because the failure mode is instructive, not because the seat was careless. ***

**What it got RIGHT, and it is a clean confirmation:** the tail store is `d->dma_reg[relative_addr / sizeof(uint32_t)] = idata;` with **no `len`**, `idata` arrives zero-extended from `memory_readmax64(cpu, data, len)`, an aligned narrow write to an IMPLEMENTED offset therefore widens to 32 bits, and it is directly guest-reachable. It gave a correct three-way oracle table (defect `0x000000ff` / merged `0x112233ff` / declined `0x11223344`) and named both controls.

**What it MISSED is what the source already says at the store itself, and it is decisive:**
  1. **THE ORACLE IS ABSENT.** `0x005f74xx` is Sega's Holly ASIC, outside the SH7750 manual, and this project holds NO documentation for it. *'Real hardware preserves the upper bits'* would be an ORACLE FROM PLAUSIBILITY -- the `#357`/`#362` shape this tree has already been burned by once.
  2. *** MAINLINE LINUX CONSTRAINS ANY FIX, and the comment records that this is the finding which KILLED THE PANEL'S UNANIMOUS ANSWER. *** `drivers/cdrom/gdrom.c` BYTE-WRITES `+0x18` to trigger every DMA transfer and BYTE-READS it to poll for completion. **So the width-blind code delivers exactly what the one real narrow user needs, and a blanket 'decline narrow writes' would BREAK A BOOTING LINUX.** The agy answer cited that same driver as EVIDENCE FOR the defect while missing that it is the CONSTRAINT AGAINST the obvious fix.
  3. **The detector has a trap already named:** the discriminating row must NOT ship pinning `0x000000ff`, because that would enshrine this model's own behaviour as an oracle.

*** AND THE PROVENANCE CLAIM WAS WRONG IN A WAY WORTH RECORDING: the seat labelled its oracle table MEASURED. *** Its numbers -- `0x000000ff`, liveness `0x12345678` -- are the EXACT values recorded in the source comment, which documents a real earlier measurement. **The numbers are true; the seat did not produce them.** That is the reading-vs-measurement distinction this project draws, and it matters because a seat quoting the tree's own measurement back looks exactly like independent confirmation.

**DISPOSITION UNCHANGED: assessed-not-changed.** The decided design, if a fix is ever warranted, is already written at the store: decline with a latched diagnostic at the four VALUE registers ONLY, keeping `+0x18` byte-capable. The farmed job confirmed the reading and did not advance the row.

*Worth carrying about the farm generally: a seat given a row whose analysis is already COMPLETE IN THE SOURCE will re-derive it and can reach a WORSE conclusion, because the constraints live in the comment rather than in the code it reads. rows.note: *** WITNESS BUILT AND MEASURED 2026-08-30, BEFORE ANY EDIT.  Both kills reproduce on the committed build. ***  One guest `mov.w` per site, planted in RAM and executed through real decode and real `memory_rw` on an unmodified `-E dreamcast`.  Exact observable: `waitpid` reports `WIFEXITED`, status 1 -- the `exit(1)` at `:1094` and `:1154`; the debugger prompt never returns.  Built from `git archive` into `/tmp`, so nothing was written to the repo and NO `.MUTANT` was owed; two-part clearance RUN, not asserted.  *** THE DEVICE-SIGNATURE CONTROL IS THE STRONG FORM, and it is worth copying: a TRANSFORMATION ONLY THE DEVICE PERFORMS. ***  The write arm masks to a byte, so storing `0x1234` to `CNTLO` reads back `0x34`.  RAM would return `0x1234` verbatim, so this discriminates against a RAM-BACKED WINDOW as well as against a dead one -- and it sits in the same register file as both kills.  A value-only control cannot do that; this project's footbridge probe once returned 0x0 everywhere with its RAM control green.  *** AND IT CARRIES ACCEPT ROWS THE LADDER DOES NOT REQUIRE BUT THIS RESULT NEEDS: `0xb` survives at site A, `0xa0` and `0xef` at site B. ***  Without them the measurement is equally consistent with the offset being UNSERVICEABLE -- which is the already-fixed `#461` default-arm defect, a different bug.  **The accept rows are what pin it to the VALUE**, and therefore what make this BADVAL (`#443`) rather than an unimplemented-offset kill.  ATTRIBUTION CONTROL, also unrequested: each kill row is paired with that site's own diagnostic, and site B's checks the echoed byte TRACKS the guest datum (`0x55`->`55`, `0x01`->`01`).  That proves the guest's value reached the predicate rather than merely that something died -- and it makes the patterns failable in both directions, since the same pattern reads 1 on a kill session and 0 on an accept one.  *** CLOSED 2026-08-30.  THE FIX HAD ALREADY SHIPPED AND THIS ROW NAMED NO COMMIT -- IT STOOD AT sev=high, state=`in work`, `commits` EMPTY, SO THE QUEUE ADVERTISED AN UNFIXED CRITICAL BUG THAT NO LONGER EXISTED. ***  `c516a9c` is titled *"#496 GD-ROM: two guest-reachable host kills de-fatalised"* and its body names EXACTLY this row's pair -- `GDROM_UNKNOWN_0x88` (write of any value but 0x0b) and `GDROM_COND` (write of anything outside {0xa0, 0xef}) -- calling them *"the #443 BADVAL class"*, which is the class this row's own title scopes itself to ("BADVAL PAIR ONLY").  Follow-ups `439dfd0` and `105c15c` close two measured escapes and land the detector's first clean baselines.  **AND THE FIX WAS LARGER THAN DE-FATALISATION, which is why closing it on the exit() count alone would have been wrong:** `d->cond = idata;` ran UNCONDITIONALLY above the dispatch, and COND_DATA_AVAIL is a bit of that byte gating the whole GDROM_DATA read path -- so deleting the `exit(1)` alone would have handed every unmodelled value a direct write to the readiness flag the guest polls.  Silent, and worse than the kill it replaced.  The store now lives inside the two accepted arms.  **THE WITNESS STAYS AND IS THE ROW'S BEST ARTIFACT** -- rung 3, 15/15 pre-fix, built BEFORE any edit, both kills reproduced on the committed build via one guest `mov.w` each through real decode on an unmodified `-E dreamcast`.  Test-first, done in the right order.  *** BUT ITS LINE CITATIONS HAVE GONE STALE, WHICH IS HOW THIS WAS FOUND. ***  The witness names the kills at `:1094` and `:1154`; today those lines are the `#460` and `#496` COMMENTS that replaced them, and the file's only live `exit(1)` is at `:1108` -- a different defect entirely (`cmd_count >= 12`, a COUNT rather than a VALUE, and outside this row's scope).  **A reader checking the row by opening its cited lines would have found comments where kills were claimed and drawn the opposite conclusion.**  That is the `citestale` class exactly -- a same-file citation invalidated by the round's own later edits -- and it is why the citation-form rule prefers grep anchors to line numbers.  *Found by reading the file rather than the row: the queue said HIGH and unfixed, the source said otherwise, and the commit log settled it.*

rows.hold_question: I closed this row from OUTSIDE the round that fixed it -- by reading `c516a9c`'s commit message and the source, days later -- so the closure rests on my inference rather than on the shipping round's own record.  That is the closure most worth a second reading.  **Q1: does #496 actually cover this row's WHOLE scope?**  The title scopes it to the "BADVAL PAIR ONLY" and explicitly hands a second defect to `gdromcondavail` -- so a closure that is right about the pair could still be wrong if #496 touched shared code in a way that changes the other row's status, in either direction.  **Q2: is `gdromcondavail` still live and still correctly scoped after #496?**  It says COND_DATA_AVAIL permanently lies after an overread; #496 MOVED the `d->cond = idata;` store inside the two accepted arms, and COND_DATA_AVAIL is a bit of that same byte.  A relocation of the store is exactly the kind of edit that can fix or worsen a neighbouring row silently.  **Q3: the witness's line citations are STALE** (`:1094`/`:1154` are now the comments that replaced the kills, and the file's only live `exit(1)` is `:1108`, a different defect).  Should the witness field be re-pointed at grep anchors, or is a stale citation on a CLOSED row acceptable because the artifact itself is preserved?

SCOPED THIS ROW AND SEPARATED IT FROM #462, by reading only. *** THE HOST-HANG CLASS IS EMPTY OF PLAUSIBLE MEMBERS AT THIS SITE. *** It grepped the whole DEVICE_ACCESS(dreamcast_gdrom_dma) body for while/for/do/goto and found that THE ONLY `while` IN THE CASE-0x18 REGION IS INSIDE A COMMENT -- the quoted NetBSD `while ((GDROM_BUSY & 0x88) != 0x08) ;` exhibit. The code is straight-line: cases, breaks, one bounded memory_rw of d->data_len. A mutant that hangs the HOST must invent a loop from nothing, which fails the round's own plausibility test for (d) mutants. The nearest adversarial candidate -- swapping d->data_len for the guest-controlled `length` -- gives a huge-but-BOUNDED copy, i.e. a segfault, i.e. TERMINATION, which these rows do catch. The GUEST-VISIBLE hang (busy-forever) is reachable by exactly one plausible edit and is ALREADY COVERED NON-LETHALLY AND MEASURED: M1 reddened arm idle/arm halfarm/arm twice/arm bytetrig at 0x1 vs 0x0, M3 the nodata side. *THE DETECTOR'S DIVISION OF LABOUR IS CORRECT -- survival rows pin non-termination, idle rows pin the shadow state a hang would corrupt -- it was simply never written down as a contract.* SO: a real PROBE-HARNESS defect, NOT a #462 detector gap, and the two are recorded separately. Ruled NOT an L2 floor breach: clause (a) is satisfied for the RIGHT reason, because pre-fix the store hits exit(1), the process terminates, and got reads `died`. *** FIX DIRECTION AND WITNESS, both supplied: *** a THREE-STATE predicate (terminated / responsive / unresponsive) via a session-tail sentinel echo, which converts hang to red for all nine rows WITHOUT touching any gate name; and a witness that needs NO DEVICE MUTANT AT ALL -- **SIGSTOP the emulator mid-session and show the row stays GREEN while the process is frozen.** That is a direct, cheap demonstration of the predicate defect. One reading offered as a reading and not a coverage claim: printed() returns `absent` when a readback is missing (:181-183), so even a host hang would turn arm idle/nodata idle/stale idle red as `absent` != `0x0` -- but no absent-red appeared anywhere in the preserved kill map AT THE TIME OF WRITING, so it earned a sentence and not a claim. *** SUPERSEDED WITHIN THE HOUR BY TABLE 3's M11 RUN, which produced exactly such an absent-red on `stale idle` -- so the path is now measured to FIRE, while its CAUSE stays unattributed (a hang and a session outrunning its spin budget are both consistent with it). Detection proven; diagnosis not claimed.*** Corrected here rather than left standing: a true-when-written claim that nothing revisits is how this project's records go false, and the round block beside it carries four separate memorials to that shape.
