RANKED FIVE CHANGES, and the ordering is careful in two places worth keeping: (1) replace `alive` with POSITIVE command-completion detection plus bounded child cleanup -- the positive-signal fix, not a longer timeout; (2) make `gate_hygiene.sh` ENUMERATE THE PTY-PROBE FILE DENOMINATOR FIRST and then reject every file lacking an approved predicate -- which is the closed-world fix: the ratchet currently counts occurrences across a concatenated stream, so a file with ZERO contributes to no counter; (5) rename the misleading `survive`/`live` rows **AFTER their hard-coded gate list is updated**, which respects the rename hazard rather than tripping it. It also warns that prompt detection `cannot be added without re-measuring the detector` because it changes inter-command scheduling and which output belongs to which command -- a cost the brief did not state. Endorsed the do-not-edit-while-measurement-is-in-flight ordering, and flagged one scope premise as stale (detail to extract on the next read).

ADJUDICATION of the nine-seat panel. It read the actual loop and one fact decided three of four decisions: *** `rd(t)` IS A FIXED-DURATION DRAIN. It waits the full `t` EVERY TIME and returns early only on EOF or OSError; it never returns early on `command done`, and the inter-command wait is a hardcoded `rd(0.35)`. *** **D2 -- AND THIS IS THE RULING THAT PREVENTS REAL DAMAGE:** codex's gate_hygiene fix is THIS ROUND (a gate change, re-measures nothing) **but it must be ENUMERATE-FIRST + RATCHET, not `reject every file lacking an approved predicate`** -- because EVERY CURRENT PROBE IS PROMPTLESS, so a hard reject-all reds the whole battery PERMANENTLY, which is the permanent-red hazard the carrier warns about. Grandfather the existing promptless probes on an explicit list; fail any NEW one. That still gives the closed-world denominator -- you know exactly which files are PTY probes and the set only shrinks -- without retro-failing the archive. *I was about to endorse the reject-all form.* **D3:** the re-measurement cost is REAL and DISQUALIFIES codex's (1) from any `cheap improvement` framing -- every command's output accumulates into one `buf` that the row regexes scan whole, so changing when the next command fires changes WHICH WINDOW a line lands in: a count that read 1 could read 2, an `absent` could resolve. **D1:** the conclusion survives, the premise is false, adopt deepseek's `non-exit predicate` framing WITH A TIGHTENING -- it is False on process exit **or pty error**, so precisely *the child neither exited nor errored the pty during the sampled windows*. **That tightening is not pedantry: it means a red `alive=died` CANNOT TELL A CLEAN EXIT FROM A PTY ERROR** -- the same cause-attribution gap that bit M11's `absent` firing last round. **D4 -- THE CHEAP FIX EXISTS AND IT IS NOT codex's (1):** append ONE sentinel command before `quit`, whose unique output matches no scored row's regex. alive False -> TERMINATED; alive True + sentinel present -> RESPONSIVE; alive True + sentinel absent -> UNRESPONSIVE. **Because it is APPENDED, every existing row's window and buf content is unchanged, so it RE-MEASURES NOTHING** -- where codex's (1) re-times every command. Honest limits stated: `unresponsive` still conflates hung with slow (the same ambiguity already on record for the `absent` path, but strictly better than a binary that reads a hang as alive), and it adds one rd() window per session, ~a minute across 39 sessions -- additive and bounded, not a re-measurement. Items (3), (4) and (5) FILED, with (5) -- the rename -- to its own dedicated commit with the diff-every-list check, never bundled, because it touches the hardcoded gate name-list.

PANEL panel_20260825_000248 -- IT MEASURED, and the result overturns a ruling I had recorded as settled. *** THE PREDICATE IS WORSE THAN HANG-BLIND: `alive == True` FOR A PROCESS THAT HAS ALREADY BEEN SIGKILLED. *** `rd()`'s loop is `while time.time() < end:`, so a death landing AFTER the last budget check is never read. `alive` does not mean `hung but not exited` -- **it does not even mean `not exited`.** Four measured branches on a rig built from the SHIPPED session()/rd() (slice sha256 recorded), with controls in both directions: untouched -> alive True, row ok; SIGKILL at t+2 -> alive False, row FAIL (so the rig CAN go red -- not a stuck-green artefact); guest `bra .` with NO SIGNALS AT ALL -> alive True, row GREEN; SIGSTOP -> alive True, row GREEN. *** AND THE #462 CARVE-OUT'S WARRANT IS MEASURABLY FALSE, WITH A SHIPPED INSTANCE. *** The ruling was that three rows are correctly covered because their predicate `computes nothing but liveness, making a non-lethal kill impossible`. It computes `no EOF/OSError was observed inside a budget window`. The instance is THIS ROUND'S OWN M11: table2 records `nodata stale died`, table3 records `survived`, SAME session, SAME command list. It re-synced a scratch tree byte-identical to SEC, rebuilt, reproduced the baseline green, applied the one-line edit and ran that session FIVE TIMES: **5/5 deterministic SIGSEGV**, preceded by `Transfering 408 bytes to 0x00000000 (guest asked for 0)`. **So the shipped table3 M11 entry records `survived` for a session that did not reach `print r2`** -- and the probe's own contract lists TWO candidate causes for that `absent` firing, omitting the one a clean rebuild reproduces: A HOST DEATH THE PREDICATE MISSED. *Honest limit it stated itself: table2's tree is not recorded in the artifacts, so it cannot assert both shipped runs used identical binaries.* **BOUNDING IT, because the gap is narrower than `the detector is hang-blind`: 45 of 58 rows carry a positive oracle a silent session breaks (42 redden, 3 RAISE). The detector is hang-MISATTRIBUTING, plus two genuinely blind rows.**

rows.state_note:
*** THE FILED COUNT OF `FIVE ROWS` IS WRONG: IT IS NINE OF 57, AND SIX OF THE NINE PREDATE #462. Measured 2026-08-24 from the archived log `_scratchpad/kill462/probe_M2.raw`. *** The nine whose got-column is the pure-liveness form (`'survived' if alive else 'died'`, want `survived`) are: rd lo, wr lo, rd hi, rd w16, scan, dma rd, arm survive, nodata live, nodata stale. **So the reframing is NOT confined to the three #462 rows the vacuity-floor carve-out blessed** -- six ordinary read rows in the pre-existing detector assert nothing except that the process did not exit, and under this row's finding that predicate is TRUE OF A HUNG EMULATOR. *** THE DERIVATION IS RECORDED BECAUSE I GOT IT WRONG TWICE FIRST, in both of the directions the carrier warns about. *** (1) Counting `row()` CALL SITES through `ast` gave `6 of 52` -- but CALL SITES ARE NOT ROWS: the probe emits 58 from 52 literal-label sites because three sites sit inside loops, and the site at :263 has a COMPUTED label, which is exactly why four of the nine (rd lo, wr lo, rd hi, rd w16) cannot be found by grepping for `row("name"`. (2) Anchoring the got-column at offset 14 instead of 15 -- the `%-14s` field is followed by a separator space -- returned `0 of 57`, a clean, confident PHANTOM ABSENCE that would have been read as `no row uses this form`. Both were caught only by carrying the DENOMINATOR: `0 of 57` and `0 of 0` are different claims and only one is evidence.  *** AND THE SECOND HALF OF THIS ROW'S CLAIM MEASURES AS SEVEN, NOT SIX, of 33. *** The filing says `six pty probes have NO prompt detection at all`. Counted 2026-08-24 with one pass -- `grep -l pty.fork *.py` then `xargs grep -L 'endswith('` -- **33 pty-forking probes, 7 with zero occurrences**: drive_guest.py, gdrom_data_probe.py, gdrom_default_probe.py, sh_intprio_probe.py, sh_iprbcd_probe.py, sh_pclock_probe.py, sh_tlbmulti_probe.py. The CLOSED-WORLD mechanism is confirmed by reading `gate_hygiene.sh:97-99`: `py_code()` pipes every file through `xargs -0 grep -h "endswith("`, so a file containing ZERO occurrences contributes to no counter and the ratchet passes. **A probe with no prompt detection is invisible to the ratchet built to catch probes with BAD prompt detection.**  *** AND THE `absent` PATH WENT FROM READING TO MEASUREMENT WITHIN THE HOUR, IN THIS ROUND'S OWN THIRD TABLE. *** The adjudicating seat wrote that printed() returning `absent` would redden the idle rows under a hang, but offered it as `a reading, not a measurement -- no absent-red appears anywhere in the preserved kill map`. Verified: 0 of the 14 table-2 logs contain one. **Table 3's M11 run contains one.** The comparison, same mutant, two runs: TABLE 2 -- `nodata stale` reads `died`, host TERMINATED, M11 scores 54/57 with three reds. TABLE 3 -- **all NINE liveness rows read `survived`**, so the host never terminated, and M11 scores 56/58 with two reds: `stale says` at `0` against a wanted `1`, and `stale idle` at **`absent`** against `0x0`. *** SO M11'S OBSERVABLE FAILURE IS NOT STABLE ACROSS RUNS -- a NULL-pointer read of 408 bytes faults on one run and does not on another -- AND ON THE RUN WHERE IT DID NOT FAULT, NOT ONE LIVENESS ROW REDDENED. *** Had `stale says` and `stale idle` not existed, M11 would have scored 58/58 and ESCAPED. That is a direct, measured demonstration of why the not-EOF predicate's blind spot matters, and it arrived inside the very round that was arguing about it. **HONEST LIMIT: `absent` with the process alive is CONSISTENT WITH a hang, and that reading is not yet established** -- it is equally consistent with the session simply outrunning its spin budget. Distinguishing them is exactly what the proposed three-state predicate (terminated / responsive / unresponsive) would do, and it is now the strongest argument for building it. *This also strengthens the case that the DETECTOR is sound while the PREDICATE is not: the value rows caught what the liveness rows could not see.*  *** THE `absent` CENSUS, WITH DENOMINATORS, AND A CONTROL THAT RULES OUT A FLAKY RIG. *** Across every preserved log: table 1 **0 of 10**, table 2 **0 of 14**, table 3 **1 of 4 completed runs** -- so one firing in 28 mutant runs, and it is M11. *** THE CONTROL IS M10, MEASURED IN THE SAME TWO TABLES: its reds are BYTE-IDENTICAL across them -- `arm count2` and `arm enable2` both times, 55/57 then 56/58. *** So the instability is specific to M11's NULL-source `memory_rw` fault path and is NOT a general property of the rig, the probe, or the host under load. **That distinction is the whole value of the measurement**: without it, `M11's mode changed` is indistinguishable from `this rig is flaky`, and the second reading would discredit every score in all three tables rather than one cell in one of them.  *** THE STALL DIAGNOSIS WAS CONFIRMED BY INTERVENTION, NOT INFERRED FROM A CONTRAST -- 125 BYTES -> 24,211 BYTES, SAME SEAT, SAME PANEL, SAME EVENING, ONE VARIABLE. *** minimax stalled at 125 bytes on a brief with ZERO inlined code that said `Read gdrom_default_probe.py's session()/rd()`. The brief was corrected -- `rd()` and the command loop inlined verbatim -- and the same seat was re-fired into the same panel: **24,211 bytes, a 194x difference.** The carrier's inline-every-fact rule has been stated for months from anecdote; this is the controlled version, and the counterfactual is measured rather than argued. *** AND THE SEAT THAT `STALLED` IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED THIS ROW'S CENTRAL CLAIM. *** This row rests on `rd() returns False ONLY on EOF`. minimax, as soon as it could SEE the code: `this is NOT just EOF -- it could be EIO, EBADF, etc.` The `except OSError` arm catches considerably more than end-of-file, so `alive == False` means `the read raised OSError or returned empty`, not `the process exited`. **That sharpens the row rather than refuting it** -- the hang-blindness stands, since none of those conditions fires for a wedged-but-open pty -- but the premise as written is imprecise and a detector built on the literal wording would mis-describe what it observes. *The seat was never unable to contribute; it was unable to SEE.*  *** THE PANEL CONVERGED ON THE PREMISE, NOT THE CONCLUSION: THREE SEATS INDEPENDENTLY ISOLATED `rd() RETURNS FALSE ONLY ON EOF` AS THE SINGLE LOAD-BEARING AND UNVERIFIED CLAIM -- and one of them showed it is WRONG AS WRITTEN. *** minimax: `rd() claim is wrong` (`except OSError` catches EIO, EBADF). kimi: real `only if` that claim holds. glm: `rests on a single unverified load-bearing premise`. **That is a panel doing the job a panel is for -- not voting on the conclusion, but finding the one sentence everything else hangs from.** deepseek then gave the corrected form its sharpest statement: **`alive` is a NON-EXIT predicate, not a liveness predicate** -- which says what it DOES observe, where the row's own wording said only what it fails to observe. The conclusion survives (a wedged-but-open pty raises no OSError and returns no EOF, so the hang-blindness stands) but the row must be restated in deepseek's terms before it is acted on.  *** THE ROUND'S SHAPE IS NOW ADJUDICATED: the cheap fix is a SESSION-TAIL SENTINEL, not a per-command change, and the reason is the corrected premise. *** Because `alive` is a NON-EXIT predicate, the cheapest way to add a liveness reading is ONE EXTRA NON-EXIT CHECK AT THE END -- not re-timing the reads that already work. Appending it leaves every scored row's window untouched, so it re-measures nothing; codex's positive-completion detection is the eventual full conversion and carries a fresh matrix. **D1 explains the SHAPE of D4, and D2/D3 keep the expensive forms out of this round.**  *** THE CENSUS NUMERATOR WAS RIGHT AND MY DERIVATION OF IT WAS WRONG IN BOTH HALVES -- corrected 2026-08-25 after a measuring seat re-derived it and I re-checked with `ast`. *** I wrote that the count is `9 of 57` because `three sites sit inside loops, and one site at :263 has a COMPUTED label`. Strictly better than blind, and the cost is DIAGNOSIS, not detection: a hang regression reddens the battery but the signature points at values. *** AND THE TWO SUPPOSEDLY-BLIND ROWS ARE IN DIFFERENT STATES, which the verify-across-all-tables caveat caught before the record could call both `genuinely blind`: *** `accept8` has NO recorded kill anywhere -- genuinely unproven coverage. `dma accept` **HAS a measured kill on record** -- `m_deldma18`, 31/32, reddening that row alone -- but it is a **#461** mutant, so it is absent from all three #462 tables (verified: 0 red across 40 mutant runs) **and its per-row log is in the `killartifacts` gap**, making it verifiable from PROSE ONLY. *That is this session's own archive defect blocking the verification of a claim, in the round that filed it and wrote the durability rule against it.* FILED as coverage debt, not owed: a row with no kill is UNPROVEN coverage, not a demonstrated false pass, so the stopping rule files it.  *** PARTIAL SHIP at `abf665c`, and the row STAYS OPEN: that commit corrected the probe's own CONTRACT (a wrong record about what `alive` observes) but did NOT fix the predicate. *** The distinction matters for anyone reading the row later: what shipped is the honest description -- `alive` means no EOF and no OSError were seen inside the sampled windows, it is True for a hung, a frozen AND an already-killed process, and a red `alive == died` cannot tell a clean exit from a pty error. rows.title: makercfalse  a build that FAILED reported MAKE_RC=0 -- cause NOT established
rows.witness: *** CORRECTED 2026-08-29 (L4).  THIS FIELD SAID: "harness:READ 2026-08-27. The row had an EMPTY note; this is the first evidence on it. `regress/build_asan.sh` reports `make rc=$?` inside an `echo` and never asserts on it; its pass/fail decision is `" -- and it is wrong in FOUR ways, each verified by opening the file. ***  (1) build_asan.sh is invoked as a FILE, so the wsl -c dollar-stripping cannot reach it at all.  (2) its rc sits BEFORE the find substitution in the same word, and expansion is left-to-right, so the rc printed IS make's (measured both orderings: before gives 1, after gives 0).  (3) the existence check is SOUND because build_one() wipes the directory first AND the gxemul link is the last action of `make all`, so existence is equivalent to make succeeding.  (4) 'Called by gate_asan_sweep.sh' is FALSE: that gate references it three times -- one gate_skip guard, two comments -- and no committed caller invokes it.  **AND THE POLARITY IS BACKWARDS: on 2026-08-28 the existence check this field condemns is what CAUGHT failed builds while MAKE_RC read 0.**  harness:regress/artifacts/makercfalse/wsl_dollar_20260829.out -- sections A-F, controls in both directions, ending MAKERC_SECTION_F_DONE.  Honest residual: the printed rc is informational and nothing asserts on it, which costs nothing with the directory wiped first.

entries.note: The compile errors were in the log ('GDROM_NDIR' undeclared, four of them, then make: *** Error 2) and the wrapper printed zero. Failing form: `cd ... && rm ... && make > log 2>&1; echo MAKE_RC=$?`. Correct form: `make > log 2>&1` then `rc=$?` on its own line. *** I CANNOT EXPLAIN THE DIFFERENCE AND WILL NOT INVENT ONE *** -- the honest record is that one form was observed lying once and the other was not. MITIGATION SHIPPED, and it is independent of the cause: `[ build/gxemul -nt src/.../file.c ]` cannot be fooled by a status-propagation subtlety and answers the question the round actually cares about, did my edit get compiled into the thing I am about to measure. This is worth more than the incident: every round this session claimed 'build clean, MAKE_RC=0' in its commit message.

VERDICT: **CAUSE ESTABLISHED** -- and it had been established TWICE IN THIS REPO
BEFORE THIS ROW WAS FILED.  Artifact: regress/artifacts/makercfalse/wsl_dollar_20260829.out
(sections A-E, each stating its WANT, ending MAKERC_SECTION_E_DONE).

*** THE MECHANISM, MEASURED WITH CONTROLS: `$?` AND `$VARS` DO NOT REACH THE INNER
SHELL THROUGH `wsl -d Gentoo -- bash -c`, **EVEN INSIDE SINGLE QUOTES**. ***

    bash -c 'false; echo $?'                        -> 1     (ordinary, local)
    wsl -- bash -c 'false; echo $?'                 -> 0     <- the defect
    wsl -- bash -c 'X=hello; echo [$X]'             -> []    <- same, on a var
    wsl -- bash -c 'echo "a  b"'                    -> a  b  (quoting DOES survive)

The third line is what makes it not a naive re-split, and the second is what makes it
dangerous: a variable SET AND USED IN THE SAME COMMAND comes back empty.  A mutant that
is never applied then scores the BASE binary and reports a clean table.

TWO WORKING FORMS, both measured green in the same artifact:
  * **backslash-escape the dollar** -- `echo \$?` -> 1, `echo [\$X]` -> [hello];
  * **a SCRIPT FILE** (the carrier's mandated `wsl -d Gentoo -- bash /mnt/c/...`) -> rc=1.

*** IT WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN, TWICE, AND THIS IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF THE
UNREAD-REVIEW CLASS -- the most expensive shape this project has. ***

  * `tools/nightly_battery.sh`, committed **581b8f3, 2026-08-17** -- SIX DAYS before this
    row was filed -- says in its own header, naming the exact symptom:
        "Written to a FILE deliberately: $VARS and $? do NOT survive
         `wsl -- bash -c '...'` -- git-bash expands first, which once made a
         REGRESS_FAIL run read as exit 0."
  * `regress/pass2_ledger.tsv`, receipt for **af4884c, 2026-08-20** -- THREE DAYS before --
    measured it independently: "THE FIRST KILL TEST WAS A VOID CONTROL THAT SCORED ITSELF
    GREEN: run through wsl -- bash -c from git-bash, the shell ate $M, no mutant was ever
    applied, and both rows printed ok on unmodified source."

The 2026-08-23 seat entry answered honestly from what it had (*'I CANNOT EXPLAIN THE
DIFFERENCE AND WILL NOT INVENT ONE'*) and that was the right answer to give.  The failure
is not the seat's: **the answer was in two committed artifacts and nothing pointed at
them.**  Note the shape -- one of the two records is a SCRIPT HEADER, which is exactly
where the carrier's own witness-ladder correction found the `harness:` term hiding.
*A tool's own header is a primary source, and this project has now been caught twice not
reading one.*

*** AND THE RECORDED **REASON** IS PROBABLY WRONG WHILE ITS **ADVICE** IS RIGHT -- which
is this file's most-repeated pattern, so it is flagged rather than propagated. ***
`nightly_battery.sh` says *git-bash expands first*.  If that were the whole story, SINGLE
QUOTES WOULD PROTECT -- and section A measures that they do, locally.  Through wsl they do
not.  So some layer past git-bash's own word-splitting is expanding.  **I have NOT
established which layer and am not guessing**; what is established is the observable and
the two working forms.  Anyone citing the reason should cite the measurement instead.

*** build_asan.sh IS NOT DEFECTIVE.  The witness field on this row mischaracterises it,
and that correction is owed in place. ***
It is invoked as a FILE, never via `bash -c`, so the mechanism above cannot reach it.
The witness's two specific charges were checked and both fail:
  (1) *'reports make rc=$? inside an echo'* -- the `$(find ...)` sits AFTER the `$?` in
      the same word, and expansion is left-to-right, so the rc is make's.  Measured both
      orderings: `$?` before `$()` gives rc=1; after gives rc=0.  The file has the sound one.
  (2) *'its pass/fail decision is an EXISTENCE check'* -- true, and SOUND HERE, because
      `build_one()` does `rm -rf "$dir"` first.  A stale binary cannot survive into the
      decision, so no-gxemul is exactly make-failed.
HONEST RESIDUAL, kept because it is real in the abstract: :42's rc is informational and
nothing asserts on it.  With the directory wiped first that costs nothing today.

PROPOSED DISPOSITION -- **CLOSE as diagnosed**, witness `harness:` (the subject IS the test
apparatus, and the proof is the differential above with its working control).  NOT CLOSED
HERE: this stage has one seat, and a stage refused for thin seat coverage four times today
was refused correctly every time.  Held with the question below.

entries.note:
VERDICT: **CLOSE as `harness:`-witnessed -- BUT NOT YET: one seat is not the mandated
roster, and the seat said so itself.  PROVISIONAL on 1 of 9.**  Every claim below was
re-verified by me against the files before being written down.

*** MY 'ESTABLISHED TWICE' WAS AN UNDERCOUNT.  IT IS THE FIFTH OCCURRENCE AGAINST FOUR
PRIOR WRITE-UPS. ***  Two more, both verified by opening them:
  * `CHANGELOG.md` (#477-era) -- the identical differential, X=hello then echo of [$X]
    printing empty brackets, and it **cost the Opus seat TWO wrong measurements that both
    looked like results**.
  * `OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md` (`asanbaselinedrift`, 2026-08-28) -- *"make reported MAKE_RC=0
    on every one of the failed builds.  It was caught only because the check was
    [ -x gxemul ] rather than the exit status."*

**Five occurrences, four records, zero prevention.**  That is the structure-first rule's
conversion condition met with room to spare -- prose is MEASURED ineffective for this class.

*** WHY THIS CLASS IS GENUINELY UNLIKE THE TWO CHECKERS THIS PROJECT REJECTED ON
MEASUREMENT (counts, citation-form), and the distinction is not special pleading. ***
Those rejections turned on: nothing consumes the value functionally, and a drifted value
SELF-REFUTES at the point of use.  **Invert every clause here.**  The corrupted value IS the
functional observable (an rc, a mutant variable).  It SELF-CONFIRMS -- 0 is exactly what a
green build prints, and an emptied loop variable prints a reassuring '(no binary)'.  And the
pre-specified escalation trigger those classes are still waiting on -- *the first MEASURED
decision consumed* -- **has already fired here, twice**: a REGRESS_FAIL run read as exit 0,
and a kill-table control that scored itself green on unmodified source.

*** BUT THE OBVIOUS CHECK HAS ZERO RECALL, MEASURED, AND THAT IS THE USEFUL PART. ***
A census of the committed tree finds the wsl-bash-c form **exactly four times, and all four
are QUOTATIONS OF THE DEFECT** (two records, the nightly_battery header, the carrier's nohup
incident).  **Zero live committed instances.**  All five occurrences were interactive,
ad-hoc invocations.  So a precommit grep scores zero on the entire recorded history -- the
same profile that killed the citation checker -- and its false positives would be honest
correction-records, which is the quoted-marker-re-arms-the-tool trap.

SO THE STRUCTURE GOES AT THE TYPING SURFACE, NOT THE COMMIT SURFACE:
  * **FILED, not done: a PreToolUse hook** warning when a wsl invocation's -c string carries
    an unescaped dollar.  The hook layer is this project's standing precedent for 'does not
    depend on remembering'.  Two negative controls owed: it must FIRE on the bare form, and
    stay SILENT on the script-file and backslash-escaped forms.
  * **A zero-population ratchet** over tracked scripts -- grandfathers nothing (population
    measured zero), fails on the first violation.  Its header must state its recall honestly.

**And the primary defence already exists and already fires**: the binary-newer-than-source
check, the object-count assertion, and inside-computed sentinels caught all five occurrences
after the fact.  The hook would catch them before.

*** (2) THE WITNESS-FIELD CORRECTION IS RIGHT, AND THE FIELD IS WRONG IN A FOURTH WAY I DID
NOT CLAIM. ***  All three of my claims verified against the file, plus: **'Called by
gate_asan_sweep.sh' is FALSE.**  That gate REFERENCES it three times -- one gate_skip guard
and two comments -- and never calls it; no committed caller invokes it at all.

**AND THE POLARITY IS BACKWARDS, which is the sharpest correction here.**  The field
condemns the existence check as weak.  On 2026-08-28 that exact check is what **CAUGHT** the
failed builds while MAKE_RC read 0.  *The record condemns the guard that is on record
catching the defect.*

Claim (c) is also STRONGER than I put it: the gxemul link is the LAST action of `make all`,
so in a freshly wiped directory there is no post-link failure window -- existence is
EQUIVALENT to make having succeeded, not merely correlated with it.

*** (3) CORRECT THE HEADER'S REASON, DO NOT DROP IT -- AND MY OWN ARTIFACT PROVES MORE THAN
I CLAIMED. ***  I wrote that the expanding layer is 'NOT established and not guessed'.
Section D licenses more than that: I typed the backslash-escaped dollar inside SINGLE quotes,
so git-bash passed it through literally -- and had the inner bash received it verbatim it
would have printed the two characters, not 1.  **The measured 1 proves something between
git-bash and the inner shell consumed the escape and left the dollar live.**  With a bare
dollar-query expanding to 0 and quoted whitespace surviving, that layer exhibits POSIX
double-quote semantics.  That much is ENTAILED BY THE ARTIFACT.  Only the component's
identity stays open.

Two 2-second discriminators, NOT run (a measurement holds the machine): echo of a
single-quoted dollar-zero through wsl (a relaying shell prints its own name), and the same
rc test via `wsl -e bash -c` (predicted 1 if the relay is the expander).

*** ALSO FOUND, VERIFIED, AND FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: `build_asan.sh` ALWAYS EXITS 0. ***
The trailing BUILD_ASAN_DONE echo launders build_one's `return 1`, and the catch-all arm
discards the head build's rc entirely.  **Latent, not live** -- no caller consumes its exit
status -- so the stopping rule says FILE.  It is the carrier's own failure-laundered-into-a-
clean-completion shape, one scripted && away from mattering.

*Fairness, since I asked for it: the seat found the sharpest fact cuts AGAINST my framing.
af4884c's receipt says 're-run from a script file on disk, PER THE DOCUMENTED FIX' -- so the
08-20 seat HAD read the first write-up and the class still bit first.  That indicts
memory-as-trigger, not any seat.*

**THE SURVIVING CAPTURES ARE MOSTLY SOUND, which narrows it usefully:**

Its own header says why: *'make then exits rc=2 having built nothing -- which looks like "0 errors" if you only grep for the word error. The object COUNT is the real check, which is why it is asserted rather than reported.'*

*** `regress/build_asan.sh` HAS NEITHER GUARD, AND IT HAS A LIVE CALLER. ***

I have not reproduced the original incident, and `build-asan/` does not currently build (a pre-existing June-27 tree with eight diverged headers), so the exposure may be dormant. What is certain is that the guard the rest of the tree uses is ABSENT here.*

`codex  909882  95%  SHIP-WITH  answered`. Codex had issued no verdict line at all -- `grep -n '^VERDICT' codex.txt` returns NOTHING -- and it was **still running**, its file growing from 909,882 to 965,763 bytes during the check with its tail mid-grep.

The panel would have been reported complete with its most substantial seat still thinking, and nobody reading the record could tell.

Codex, agy and grok stream their SEARCH RESULTS into the same file as their answer -- so the richer the seat's investigation, the more other people's verdicts it quotes, and the more likely a position-blind matcher latches onto one.

rows.title: gdromexitsix  the DMA+0x18 pair ends the host from a protocol-correct guest, and the four command-layer exits split out

entries.note: *** FOUND BY FOLLOWING A FLAGSHIP SEAT'S POINTER AND CHECKING IT. *** The gdromdmawidth adjudication said to let `sh4gdromexit` take this file's next round, describing it as OPEN. It is CLOSED (98a3408 16f06a0) and its scope is specifically #460's GDROM_DATA arm -- it was never an umbrella for the file. #461's own CHANGELOG says twice that the remaining eight exit(1) sites are 'filed under the sh4gdromexit umbrella'. CHECKED: of the eight, `gdromcondlies` covers exactly TWO (:639 GDROM_UNKNOWN_0x88 and :699 GDROM_COND, the BADVAL pair). *** THE OTHER SIX HAD NO OPEN CARRIER AT ALL, *** so a census that read as 'filed' was really six live guest-reachable host-kill sites sitting in nobody's queue -- the 'half a census reads as a whole one' hazard one level up, where the census is complete and the QUEUE is not. THE SIX, with line numbers re-derived 2026-08-23 after the last edit to the file: :294 'GDROM Read TOC not 408 bytes?'; :346 'unimplemented data format 0x%02x'; :424 handle_command default, 'unimplemented command 0x%02x'; :600 'Too much GDROM_DATA?'; :804 'DMA transfer but d->data is NULL'; :820 the DMA arming-mismatch report. The first four are command-layer, reachable through GDROM_DATA packets; the last two are the DMA+0x18 pair. RANKING NOTE: the DMA pair is the interesting half, because #461 made the surrounding window survivable, so a guest can now reach +0x18 without dying on the way -- and one nonzero store there still ends the host. It is also the blocker gdromdmawidth is gated behind: the row that would pin that item's real contract cannot be built until these two exits go.

*** WITNESSED AT RUNG 3 BY ONE GUEST STORE, MEASURED RATHER THAN PREDICTED. *** The filing said a witness was 'likely cheap' now that #461 made the window survivable; the carrier's rule is that such a claim is CHECKABLE, so it was checked. On the committed build ba30e64, `r7 = 0xa05f7418; r8 = 1; mov.l r8,@r7` ENDS THE HOST PROCESS, with its own diagnostic ('Unimplemented GDROM DMA start? TODO') observed first -- site :820, the arming-mismatch report, reached because count (+0x0c) and enable (+0x14) are both 0 on a fresh device so the `dma_reg[3] == 1 && dma_reg[5] == 1` test fails. DEVICE-SIGNATURE CONTROL IN THE SAME RUN: the IDENTICAL store to +0x04, an implemented offset, leaves the host alive. Without that control 'died' could have been anything, which is the footbridge lesson -- its first draft returned 0x0 everywhere with its RAM control green, so one control is not enough and this run carries the discriminating one. Real guest instruction, real address decode, unmodified in-tree machine description, no device added: rung 3, and the clause (iii) laundering test is passed because nothing was introduced in order to reach the site. THE WITNESS IS ALSO THE DE-ESCALATION CLAUSE READ FORWARDS: before #461 a guest scanning this window died on the first unimplemented offset, so it never got here. Removing one host-fatal class made the next one EASIER TO REACH -- which is a cost of that round showing up on schedule, not a defect it introduced. *** RE-MEASURED ON THE CURRENT REVISION 2026-08-23 after codex pointed out, correctly, that the first run was taken on ba30e64 and the line mapping to HEAD 'is credible because of the unique diagnostic, but is not itself a current-revision execution measurement'. Same result: host dies, own diagnostic seen, control at implemented +0x04 survives. The objection was precise and the re-run cost one minute -- a witness is cheap to re-take and a stale one is exactly the frozen-number defect wearing different clothes.

[panel_20260823_222813] *** THE ONLY DISSENT: DO NOT SHIP, and its three points are all substantive. *** (1) `:804` MUST BE SPLIT from the other sites, because de-fatalising it into a decline is unsafe: the smallest detector-surviving break is DELETING THE COMPLETION/STATUS-CLEAR from the recovery branch -- diagnostic remains, host stays alive, a liveness-only row passes, AND LINUX POLLS FOREVER. Its required postconditions: +0x18 reaches its completed/idle value, the completion event occurs, no destination bytes are copied, and repeated triggering yields one diagnostic. Its line lands: 'thirty-two unrelated rows do not close this mutation gap.' (2) CORRECTED THE BRIEF'S FRAMING: 'the other five decline unsupported requests' is inaccurate -- :294, :600 and :820 are INVARIANT/STATE failures, so each needs an explicit recovery postcondition rather than a decline. (3) CORRECTED MY WITNESS CLAIM, precisely: the rung-3 measurement was taken on ba30e64, and the line mapping to the current revision 'is credible because of the unique diagnostic, but is not itself a current-revision execution measurement'. Re-measured on the current build in response.

[panel_20260823_222813] Reached codex's central point independently and stated the consequence in one line: 'applying a pure decline at :804 actively harms the guest by causing a hang. The fix for :804 must be latched-diagnostic-plus-COMPLETION, not latched-diagnostic-plus-decline.' Also flagged the brief's framing as flawed for implying the three-round idiom transfers to :804 -- it does not.

[panel_20260823_222813] *** DISSENTS FROM glm AND codex ON THE DECISIVE POINT, and the split is the round's real question. *** It wants `:804` to latch, keep the diagnostic, and `break` -- 'never reach memory_rw / DMA IRQ / idata=0'. That is the opposite of firing completion. The disagreement is empirical (does Linux's poll loop time out, or spin forever?) and this project settles those by measurement, never by vote -- the flagship seat is the one reading the actual driver. Its scope call is the strictest and the best-argued: take the DMA pair only, file :294/:346/:424 as the next round RANKED BY LINUX COMMAND 0x13, leave :600 dead with its existing warrant, leave :639/:699 in gdromcondlies -- 'one device, one register, one fix design, one detector, no new invented DMA behaviour'. It also wants the new rows keyed off their OWN log variable rather than folded into gdrom_default_probe.py's.

[panel_20260823_222813] *** NAMED THE RISK IN THE ROUND'S OWN JUSTIFICATION, which no other seat did. *** The brief sells this round partly as unblocking gdromdmawidth. minimax: 'if the gdromdmawidth row turns out to need a DIFFERENT +0x18 behavior than the one this round lands, the round does not unblock what it claims to unblock.' That is exactly the failure mode of scheduling-justified work, and it means the +0x18 semantics chosen here must be checked against gdromdmawidth's reserved Linux byte-contract BEFORE they ship, not after.
[panel_20260823_222813] SHIP WITH CHANGES; verified the six sites and the witness framing by citation.
[panel_20260823_222813] SHIP WITH CHANGES; converged on the completion-postcondition requirement for :804 rather than a bare decline.
[panel_20260823_222813] SHIP WITH CHANGES, 49 KB. Longest analysis of the seven; converges on the scope split and the :804 postcondition question.

*** SETTLED THE codex/grok SPLIT EMPIRICALLY, AND BOTH SIDES WERE PARTLY WRONG. *** It re-fetched mainline drivers/cdrom/gdrom.c: the post-trigger wait is wait_event_interruptible_timeout(..., GDROM_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT) = HZ*7, and the pre-trigger poll is guarded by time_before(jiffies, timeout) with HZ/2. EVERY WAIT IN THE DMA PATH IS TIME-BOUNDED, so a decline lands on a 7-second timeout -> BLK_STS_IOERR -> EIO. Degraded and bounded, NOT a hang: codex's and glm's central fear does not materialise. *** BUT IT FOUND THE MECHANISM NEITHER SIDE NAMED, AND THE FOUR-ROUND IDIOM WALKS STRAIGHT INTO IT. *** The DMA window's tail store runs after every aligned break. The SUCCESS arm sets `idata = 0` before breaking -- which is why a completed transfer polls idle -- and both exits die BEFORE the tail. So 'keep the diagnostic, drop exit(1)', the shape #447/#459/#460/#461 all used, lets the guest's trigger value 1 flow into dma_reg[6] and *** +0x18 READS BUSY FOREVER. *** For Linux that is a bounded HZ/2 tax per transfer; for a guest that waits the NetBSD way -- its own control-window waits are unbounded spins, fetched verbatim -- it is a real hang. Fix is one line per declined arm: `idata = 0` before break, mirroring the success arm. *** AND FIRING THE COMPLETION EVENT IS THE ACTIVELY HARMFUL OPTION, the opposite of what the brief asked about. *** gdrom_dma_interrupt clears gd.transfer UNCONDITIONALLY and checks no error bit anywhere, so firing SYSASIC_EVENT_GDROM_DMA on an empty transfer exits the wait with BLK_STS_OK -- the block layer is told the read succeeded when zero bytes moved, and the guest consumes whatever was in the destination page AS DISK DATA. That is #460's invented-behaviour class reproduced at the block layer. The driver has exactly one error channel, the timeout, so 7-second EIO is not a compromise but the only honest signal available. IT ALSO STRENGTHENED THE ROUND'S WARRANT: :804 is a COMPLIANT-GUEST path today. gdrom_readdisk_dma writes the four DMA registers before sending packet 0x30; if diskimage_access fails on a short image, or OB-20's sector clamp rejects the request, handle_command leaves d->data == NULL and Linux -- told nothing it checks -- byte-writes 1 to +0x18. On committed HEAD that is host death from a protocol-correct guest with an imperfect disk image, i.e. two shipped defensive declines currently feed a host kill. CORRECTED THE WITNESS CLAIM, precisely: only :820 had been measured; :804 needs three stores and 'test-first is not satisfied by a sibling's witness'. Measured in response -- arming with no staged data kills the host, own diagnostic seen, control with trigger=0 survives. CORRECTED THE SCOPE AND THE TITLE: :600 is NOT guest-reachable (busy&0x08 is set only by COND=0xa0 which zeroes cmd_count; increments are +2; at exactly 12 the flag clears), so 'six guest-reachable' was false for it -- AND it should stay fatal because it has MEASURED value as an invariant tripwire: #460's rejected Option C was caught precisely because it made :600 reachable. De-fatalising it would delete the one accidental detector of the cmd_count invariant. The census is also EIGHT sites, not six; :639/:699 are carried by gdromcondlies, so the arithmetic was defensible but the brief never stated the exclusion and the seat had to consult the ledger to avoid re-filing them. L4 NIT FOR THE ROUND: the transfer diagnostic prints `length` (the guest's +0x08 value) while the code transfers d->data_len -- so it lies in exactly the sessions where the discrepancy matters. One word, inside the hunk being edited.

:804 WITNESSED on the current revision, closing the gap the flagship seat named. Three stores to IMPLEMENTED offsets -- +0x0c=1, +0x14=1, +0x18=1 -- satisfy the arming condition, enter the transfer branch, and die on `d->data == NULL`. Host dies, its own diagnostic is seen, and the DEVICE-SIGNATURE CONTROL in the same run -- the identical three stores with the trigger left at 0 -- leaves the host alive, which isolates the trigger as the cause rather than the arming. Rung 3, unmodified machine, nothing added to reach the site. Both halves of the pair are now measured, each with its own control.

[panel_20260823_230930] *** DO NOT SHIP -- the lone dissent, and it found the one hole that mattered. Its verdict is explicitly about the DETECTOR: 'The C hunk does not need a redesign.' *** The finding: firing SYSASIC_TRIGGER_EVENT on a declined path PASSES EVERY ROW, because nothing reads the pending register. That is exactly the mutant the flagship seat identified as ACTIVELY HARMFUL -- worse than the defect this round fixes, since gdrom_dma_interrupt() clears gd.transfer unconditionally with no error check, so a completion signalled on an empty transfer returns BLK_STS_OK and the guest consumes the destination page as disk data. A host death is loud; that is silent. The flagship seat had SPECIFIED that row in its design and the round did not build it -- grok caught the omission by measuring rather than by re-reading the design. It also named the observable precisely (SYSASIC_BASE 0x5f6900, pending_irq[0] at offset 0, bit 14 = 0x4000, guest-readable), which is why the row could be written immediately. TWO records defects in its list were live: check_probe_wiring still said '32 rows', and a constant insertion had stranded DMA's comment on GDROM_DATAP so a CONTROL-window address was labelled 'the DMA window, SEPARATELY registered'. Both fixed.

[panel_20260823_230930] Found the missing `nodata idle` row -- the structural twin of `arm idle` -- and stated the consequence exactly: 'without it, the :804 idata = 0 is unpinned, and the smallest possible regression (deleting one line) passes green'. The sibling site had its row from the start and this one did not, which is an asymmetry a reader of the fix would never notice. Honest about its own limit too: it called the completion-event row 'ideal but maybe harder to implement in a register-probe harness' -- it was not, because the pending register is guest-readable, but flagging the uncertainty was right.

[panel_20260823_230930] Reached the same missing `nodata idle` independently and gave the crispest summary: 'Only the missing nodata idle detector row; the code itself is shippable.' Also checked the accept rows against the brief's question and confirmed they pin BOTH removed predicates, with the reasoning per row.

[panel_20260823_230930] SHIP WITH CHANGES. Found real UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR in the new hunk: the diagnostic uses %08x and %x with (int) arguments, and those conversions require unsigned int -- benign on common ABIs but UB by the C format rules. Fixed; the %i arguments correctly stay int. Reached the warn-bit widening independently and stated the mechanism the same way ('the compound assignment truncates it, causing the warning to repeat indefinitely').

[panel_20260823_230930] SHIP WITH CHANGES, 54 KB -- the longest of the seven. Its verdict line was split across two accepted lines, which the extractor now REPORTS as a split rather than silently resolving, so the round record shows both.
[panel_20260823_230930] SHIP WITH CHANGES.

*** SEAT DIED ON AN API 529 (server-side overload) MID-RUN -- recorded as a SEAT FAILURE, never as agreement, and re-fired once because a 529 is TRANSPORT and not a wall. *** But it got its decisive measurement out first, and it is the one that settles the round's detector question. IT CONFIRMED THE COMPLETION EVENT IS OBSERVABLE BY AN ORDINARY GUEST LOAD at 0xa05f6900 (ASIC pending_irq[0], bit 14 = 0x4000), and measured both harmful mutants individually:                     fix      m_event_null   m_event_else fresh               0x0      0x0            0x0 nodata decline      0x0      0x4000         0x0 arm decline         0x0      0x0            0x4000 accept              0x4000   0x4000         0x4000 *** THE LAST ROW IS THE FINDING: `accept` reads 0x4000 under ALL THREE BUILDS, so an accept-only row could NEVER have caught either mutant. *** It takes the DECLINE rows reading 0x0 -- which is exactly the pair added on grok's finding (`nodata quiet` and `accept event`). So the measurement says both are load-bearing and neither is redundant: grok predicted the gap by reading, this seat measured both halves of it, and the two mutants are separable rather than one defect seen twice.

SECOND CONSECUTIVE SEAT FAILURE, same cause: API 529, service-side overload. Recorded by name and never as agreement. *** A 529 IS TRANSPORT, NOT A WALL, and the carrier draws that distinction for a reason: a wall is the seat refusing and you wait it out; a transport failure is the connection being absent. *** Two in a row is a pattern rather than a blip, so the retry was held rather than hammered and the decision was put to the owner, who chose to HOLD THE ROUND. entries.ev: direct reading of all six arms, alloc_data(), the struct and the common tail
entries.note:
*** THE SIX SITES ARE NOT ONE EDIT.  THEY ARE THREE CLASSES, AND TWO OF THEM CORRUPT IF
THE exit(1) IS SIMPLY DELETED. ***  This is the round's design finding and it is the
carrier's own 'dropping exit(1) alone would have...' trap, live at two sites.

CLASS B -- BARE REMOVAL CORRUPTS.  An explicit decline is MANDATORY, not stylistic:

  :662  guard `if (d->cmd_count >= 12)`, and the struct declares `uint8_t cmd[12]`.
        Deleting the exit runs `d->cmd[d->cmd_count++] = idata;` TWICE with
        cmd_count >= 12 -- an out-of-bounds WRITE past a 12-byte array inside the
        device struct.  The kill is currently the only thing preventing it.
  :357  guard `if (d->cnt != 408)`, and the next statement is `alloc_data(d)`, which
        does `d->data_len = d->cnt; malloc(d->data_len); memset(...)`.  Deleting the
        exit allocates `cnt` bytes where the TOC writer below expects 408 -- a heap
        UNDER-allocation for any cnt < 408, and malloc(0) at cnt == 0.

CLASS A -- BARE REMOVAL IS SAFE, because the enclosing control flow already does the
right thing:

  :486  `default:` in handle_command().  Falling through reaches the common tail, and
        the tail is CORRECT for an unhandled command: d->data is NULL, so it takes the
        else branch, sets d->cnt = 0, clears COND_DATA_AVAIL, and fires
        SYSASIC_TRIGGER_EVENT.  That is precisely 'the command did nothing' reported
        properly.
        *** AND AN EARLY `return` HERE WOULD SKIP SYSASIC_TRIGGER_EVENT AND LEAVE THE
        GUEST WAITING FOREVER.  The sketch rule's exact failure mode, live at this
        site. ***  Any proposed edit must be run against the real tail.
  :761  falls to a `break`.  Clean decline, no state mutation.
  :701  falls to a `break`.  Clean.

CLASS C -- THE FILE ALREADY DECIDED, ONE LINE UP:

  :409  the arm immediately above is `if (d->cmd[1] == 0x24) fatal("... Continuing
        anyway")` -- no exit.  So an unimplemented data format ALREADY continues for
        one value and dies for every other.  The precedent for surviving is in the
        same `if`/`else if`.
  :701  the same shape INSIDE ONE CASE: the READ arm's exit is already commented out
        (`// exit(1);`), only the WRITE arm still dies.

  *That asymmetry is a sibling-parity finding the round must put to the panel rather
  than resolve by tidying: somebody already judged that continuing is acceptable here,
  and the question is whether that judgement generalises or was specific to 0x24.*

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROUND: the de-fatalisation option set must be chosen PER SITE, and
the two Class-B sites need the accept-side reasoning that clause (d) demands -- their
guards are load-bearing bounds checks wearing diagnostic clothing, so a mutant that
weakens `>= 12` or `!= 408` is squarely inside the DEPENDS-ON bound.

entries.ev: direct reading of the TOC arm, alloc_data(), free_data() and handle_command()'s head
entries.note:
*** TWO PREMISES I HAD ASSERTED WITHOUT CHECKING, BOTH CHALLENGED BY PACKET-FED SEATS THAT
COULD NOT SETTLE THEM FROM THE PACKET, NOW SETTLED BY READING.  ONE IS CONFIRMED AND IS
WORSE THAN I WROTE IT; THE OTHER'S DOUBT IS ANSWERED. ***

`:357` IS A GUEST-CONTROLLED HEAP OVERFLOW, not an under-allocation question.

  `alloc_data()` mallocs `d->cnt` bytes.  glm and deepseek both asked, independently and
  correctly, whether the TOC writer then writes `d->data_len` bytes (safe under any cnt) or
  a fixed 408 (unsafe below it).  Neither, and the answer is the bad one:

    memset(d->data, 0xff, d->cnt);        <- uses cnt, safe
    d->data[0*4] = ...  d->data[1*4] = ...  d->data[99*4] = ...
    d->data[100*4] = ...  d->data[101*4+3] = ...   <- HARDCODED indices

  Derived mechanically rather than by eye:
    grep -oE 'd->data\[[0-9]+\*4(\+[0-9])?\]' src/devices/dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c
      -> highest byte index 407, so the writer needs 408 bytes REGARDLESS of cnt.

  `cnt` is guest-supplied.  So deleting the exit(1) yields `malloc(cnt)` followed by writes
  up to index 407 -- **an overflow of up to 408 bytes whose size the guest chooses**, and
  the exit(1) is currently the only thing preventing it.  `cnt == 0` gives malloc(0) plus
  the full 408.

  CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROUND: `:357` and `:662` are not merely 'bare removal corrupts'.  Both
  guards are load-bearing BOUNDS CHECKS on guest-controlled quantities, and both fixes must
  decline BEFORE the guarded statement rather than after it.  That is a different fix design
  from the four unimplemented-command arms, which strengthens the case for Class B being its
  own round.

`:486`'s Class-A claim HOLDS, and deepseek's doubt is answered.  It asked whether `d->data`
is reliably NULL on entry to `default:`, since a stale non-NULL would make the common tail
set COND_DATA_AVAIL wrongly.  It is: `handle_command()` calls `free_data(d)` at `:343`
(tagged #465) before the switch, and free_data() sets `d->data = NULL` and `data_len = 0`.

AND A CLASSIFICATION ERROR OF MINE, found by glm: **`:701` appears in BOTH Class A and Class
C.**  It genuinely has both properties -- its WRITE arm falls to a `break`, and its READ
arm's exit(1) is already commented out -- but listing it twice without saying so may mean
the class boundary is drawn on the wrong axis.  Put to the adjudicator explicitly.

*Both settled premises came from seats that CANNOT READ FILES refusing to certify what a
brief asserted.  That is the packet-fed seats doing exactly what they are for, and it is the
second round running in which their refusal-to-ratify found a real hole.*

entries.outcome_note: Its :662 refutation is CONFIRMED by reading, and it reverses a claim I made three times in committed records.  Its :357 refinement is sharper than my own and its round-scope proposal is better than mine.
entries.note:
VERDICT: DO NOT SHIP THIS AS SIX SITES / THREE CLASSES.  It refuted my taxonomy, my
reachability census, and my scope proposal -- and the refutations are in the tree.

*** :662 IS NOT GUEST-REACHABLE, AND MY RE-CENSUS SAID IT WAS.  I CONFIRMED THE REFUTATION
BY READING BEFORE RECORDING IT. ***

  `busy |= 0x08` has EXACTLY ONE WRITER (`:753`) and the very next line is
  `d->cmd_count = 0`.  Stores increment by TWO (`:665`, `:666`), and at `cmd_count == 12`
  the gate CLEARS (`:668`).  So the arm cannot be ENTERED with cmd_count >= 12: what
  prevents the overflow is the busy&0x08 gate plus the +2 stride landing exactly on 12 --
  **not the exit(1)**.

  *** AND THE RECORD WAS IN THE PRODUCT FILE ALL ALONG, TWENTY LINES ABOVE A SITE I WAS
  CENSUSING. ***  #460's own comment reads: 'the next write reaches the "Too much
  GDROM_DATA" exit -- OTHERWISE UNREACHABLE', and records that a proposed fix was REJECTED
  because it would have re-opened it ('A fix that re-opens a dead site is worse than the
  defect').  The 2026-08-26 witness design on this same row had already concluded 'NO
  TRIGGER ROUTE -> :662 -> document the invariant instead.'

  **MY 2026-08-27 RE-CENSUS CONFLATED 'the exit(1) is still in the file' WITH
  'guest-reachable'.**  Those are different questions and I asked only the first.  I then
  wrote 'the kill is currently the only thing preventing it' into three committed records.
  That is the unread-review class turned on a product comment: the answer was in the file
  I was censusing.

  DISPOSITION: **KEEP :662 FATAL.**  It is the measured tripwire for the cmd_count
  invariant, de-fatalising it buys no guest-facing safety, and it is the detector that
  caught #460's Option C.

:357 -- CLASS B HOLDS AND IS SHARPER THAN I PUT IT.  The memory-safety bound is
`cnt < 408`, NOT `cnt != 408`: cnt > 408 is a host-SAFE over-allocation, 1..407 is the
heap OOB, and cnt == 0 is malloc(0) then OOB **or** CHECK_ALLOCATION -> FAILURE() ->
another exit(1).  So the live guard is the stricter PROTOCOL check and the fix must decline
BEFORE alloc_data(), then `break` into the common tail -- never `return`.

:409 -- NOT A SAFETY CLASS AT ALL.  Deleting the exit does NOT OOB; it falls into the
2048-byte sector path and returns disk data AS IF the format were 0x20.  **Invented
success, not host corruption.**  And the 0x24 arm is a SPECIFIC exception -- if it
generalised, the `else if` would not exist.  Keep 0x24 continuing; latched `break` for every
other format.  It could not settle 0x24's hardware meaning from this tree and said so
rather than inventing one.

:486 -- fall-through is safe (free_data() at entry), the early-`return` warning is right,
but BARE DELETION leaves an UNLATCHED fatal() with no -q early-out: floodclass, in a
function a guest can call in a loop.  *** AND ITS SHARPEST POINT: Linux's GET SENSE is
packet 0x13, so `default:` is hit by a COMPLIANT DRIVER, not by junk opcodes. ***

:701 / :761 -- **already designed in `gdromcondlies`**, a different row, and Class A is
FALSE for :761.  Pulling them here duplicates that row's work.

SCOPE, and it is better than mine: **take the three handle_command exits as ONE round** --
one semantic class, one fix design (decline + latched announce, break to the common tail),
one detector.  Leave :662 fatal.  Leave :701/:761 to gdromcondlies.

It also names a FIFTH option member my set lacked: **keep the kill** -- which is exactly
the right disposition for :662 and which a four-member set cannot express.

VERDICT: THREE implementation rounds among the FIVE reachable sites -- and it reached
`:662`'s exclusion INDEPENDENTLY of grok.

  1. `:357` ALONE -- malformed fixed-size TOC transfer, bounds-dominating decline.
  2. `:409` + `:486` TOGETHER -- unsupported packet selector/opcode, same common-tail
     decline and the same detector oracle.
  3. `:701` + `:761` TOGETHER -- already the `gdromcondlies` round.
  `:662` gets DOCUMENTATION or a separate internal-invariant hardening filing, **not
  de-fatalisation.**

'If gdromexitsix excludes the two sites already owned by gdromcondlies, then that carrier
becomes exactly two rounds: site 1, then sites 2+3.'

*** SO CODEX AND GROK AGREE ON EXCLUSIONS AND SPLIT ON GROUPING: grok says the three
handle_command exits are ONE round, codex says TWO (`:357` alone, then `:409`+`:486`). ***
That is a real disagreement about round scope and it goes to the adjudicator.  The
substance behind codex's split is that `:357`'s decline is BOUNDS-dominating while
`:409`/`:486` are protocol declines sharing one oracle -- which is the same distinction I
drew as Class B vs Class A, arriving at a different grouping.

AND IT KILLED ONE OF MY PROPOSED CHEAPER DISCRIMINATORS for the closure gate: **'A
distinguishable nonzero emulator exit code is not acceptable -- it merely reintroduces a
host kill under a different number.'**  Its alternative is oracle STRENGTHENING rather than
expectation correction: assert the failure, show the correct probe green, flip `cmd[0]` and
`cmd[1]` independently in probe mutants and show those red, then de-fatalise and show the
same mutants still red.  It notes this is why requiring the unmodified product to go RED
would be inappropriate here -- the oracle-correction order does not apply to strengthening.

VERDICT: GO-WITH-CHANGES.  Line-by-line verification against the tree confirms all six
sites exist verbatim and that the Class B memory-safety claims for `:357` and `:662` are
correct AS WRITTEN -- but see grok and codex on whether `:662`'s arm can be ENTERED, which
is a different question from whether the OOB would occur if it were.

THREE findings: **a critical implementation blocker -- `warned` latch BIT EXHAUSTION** (the
device's latch field cannot carry another flag, so a round adding latched declines at three
sites must widen it or reuse); an inaccurate control-flow claim about Site 6's state
mutation; and a scope bundling that violates the round-scope rule in CLAUDE.md.

*The latch-exhaustion finding is the one nobody else raised and it is an implementation
blocker rather than a design objection -- the house idiom is one latch per site per
instance, and this device may not have room for three more.*

VERDICT: the split is sound in derivation but has an OVERLAPPING CLASSIFICATION and rests
on an uncheckable premise.

* **`:701` is listed in BOTH Class A and Class C** -- correct, and I had not noticed.  It

* The option set is complete and no site qualifies for member 4 (accept).

VERDICT: the split is correct for `:662` and `:701`/`:761`, but `:357` and `:486` rest on

*Its answer is largely a careful re-derivation of the brief's own structure rather than an

Its reasoning on `:357` is the sharpest of the packet-fed seats: it noted that the guard's

*Recorded by TRANSPORT: the kimi CLI is 403-walled on its WEEKLY limit; this is the

*** (d) THE WITNESS ARTIFACTS ARE GONE, AND I VERIFIED IT BEFORE RECORDING: a `find` over

rows.title: gdromwarnbits  six of eight warn bits are used and they are hand-assigned hex masks; the ninth overflows a uint8_t SILENTLY and floods

entries.note: Raised by the main loop while writing #462's pass-2 brief, then checked against the tree. `d->warned` is a uint8_t and GDROM_W_LEN/NODATA/NOTWAIT/OVERREAD/DMANODATA/DMAARM are hand-assigned 0x01..0x20 -- SIX of eight, and #462 is what took it from four to six. *** THE FAILURE MODE AT NINE IS SILENT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH FILING RATHER THAN NOTING. *** `warned |= (1u << 8)` truncates to 0 in a uint8_t, so the latch never sets, `!(warned & BIT)` stays true forever, and the diagnostic FLOODS -- the exact behaviour every one of these latches exists to prevent, arriving with no compile error and no runtime complaint. A duplicate hand-assigned mask fails the same way for a different reason: two sites share one bit and the second is silenced by the first. *** THE ZERO-COST STRUCTURAL FIX HAS IN-TREE PRECEDENT AND THE CARRIER RECORDS IT. *** dev_sh4.c:124-263 converted its SH4_VAL_* defines to a C99 enum ending in SH4_VAL_NCLASS, 'correct by construction instead of by maintenance'. The shapes differ -- those are ARRAY INDICES, these are BIT MASKS -- so the analogue is an enum of bit POSITIONS ending in GDROM_W_NBITS, with each mask defined as `1u << GDROM_W_x_B`. Duplicates become impossible, and NBITS gives a checkable bound against the width of `warned`. *** NOT FIXED NOW, AND FILED WITH A PRE-SET TRIGGER, WHICH IS HOW THE SH4 ONE GOT DONE ON TIME. *** That conversion carried the trigger 'when a tenth class arrives'; SH4_VAL_SCICMD was the tenth and the work happened. #462's semantic class is de-fatalising the DMA pair -- converting the latch representation is a different change, and the stopping rule reserves in-round work for a measured false pass or a wrong record. THE TRIGGER HERE: **the seventh warn bit**. At seven, widen `warned` and convert to the enum form in the same edit; there is no reason to wait for the overflow.

*** THE PRE-SET TRIGGER FIRED EXACTLY AS WRITTEN, AND THAT IS THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING
AS MUCH AS THE CONVERSION. ***  It was set as 'at the SEVENTH bit'.  `gdromexitsix` Round
1 adds THREE latches to the six in use, so the NINTH would be `1u << 8` -- truncating to
zero in a uint8_t, never setting, and letting the diagnostic it guards FLOOD, with no
compile error and no runtime complaint.

TWO SEATS REACHED IT INDEPENDENTLY on that round's pass 1: the adjudicator named it as an
obligation the brief had missed entirely, and agy called it a critical implementation
blocker.  Neither was told about the trigger; both derived the budget from the code.

CONVERSION: six `#define`d masks -> an enum of bit POSITIONS ending in GDROM_W_NBITS, with
each mask `(1u << ..._B)`, and `warned` widened uint8_t -> uint32_t.  GDROM_W_NBITS is now
correct BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by maintenance, and a duplicate mask is impossible to
write -- which was the file's other stated hazard ('the second site is silenced by the
first').

BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVATION MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED: a compiled check confirms all six masks are
BIT-IDENTICAL to the hand-assigned originals (0x01/0x02/0x04/0x08/0x10/0x20) and reports
GDROM_W_NBITS == 6 with 26 bits free.  The device object compiles.  Propagated identical
to est/, build/ and build-asan/.

*Precedent transferred rather than invented: dev_sh4.c did the equivalent conversion for
its value-class keys on its own pre-set trigger ('when a tenth class arrives'), and the
carrier records that one as discharged.  A trigger set in advance, fired by an unrelated
round, and discharged without a fresh design argument is the cheapest thing in this
project -- and it only worked because the condition was written down as a CONDITION rather
than as a note saying 'watch out for this'.*

  executes the settled form without re-opening pass-1 design, and the brief cites the
  trigger VERBATIM as a settled premise.  **It buys nothing at REVIEW**: the executed diff
  is panelled like any diff -- riding in the firing round's pass 2, or on its own full
  stage whose brief inlines the whole diff -- and the row closes only on full stages.

  trigger's text and the executed diff, so seats review the choices actually made instead
  of re-litigating the settled form.

against the settled FORM itself (enum-ness, count suffix, mask shape) is a LATE DESIGN

entries.note: MEASURED while running #462's detector. The probe was comfortable at 32 rows and at 41; at 44 it overruns 1800s, because the four ACCEPT rows each drive a full TOC staging sequence (several emulator sessions apiece) rather than the one or two a value row needs. *** THE COST IS NOT THE RUNTIME, IT IS THAT AN OVERRUN LOOKS LIKE NOTHING. *** The wrapper captured output with `out=$(timeout 1800 ...)` and grepped for specific patterns, so a kill mid-run yielded an EMPTY log and exit 0 -- indistinguishable from a run still in progress. Compounded by stdout buffering, which the carrier already records: under a timeout nothing flushes, so even a traceback vanished. Two diagnostic attempts returned no output at all before the cause was found. MITIGATION APPLIED, and it is the general fix rather than a bigger number: run the probe with `python3 -u` and STREAM to a file instead of capturing at the end, so a partial run is visible and row-by-row progress can be watched. The budget was raised to 5400s too, but the streaming is what turns a silent failure into a legible one. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OWED: gate 10 runs this probe, so the gate's own budget inherits the overrun. Either the accept rows share ONE staging session -- they currently stage independently, which was never necessary -- or the gate's timeout rises with the probe's. The first is better: four stagings for three observations is the real waste, and sharing them would also make the rows measure the SAME transfer rather than three similar ones.

PARTLY ADDRESSED BY #462, and the honest state is worth separating from the fix. *** WHAT IS DONE: *** the four accept rows now share ONE staging session instead of four, which was this row's recommended repair and was applied in-round on the owner's decision (L1, pre-ship construction). Three of the four TOC stagings are gone. Verified: one staging occurrence where there were two in the source, one session driving all four rows, row count unchanged at 44, and the detector measures 44/44 with the four accept rows reading coherently -- yes / 0x0 / set / 0. *** WHAT IS NOT MEASURED: whether the probe now fits the original 1800s budget. *** The run that produced 44/44 was given 5400s and completed, which proves it fits 5400 and says nothing about 1800. So the row stays OPEN on exactly that question, because gate 10 runs this probe and the gate's own budget is what actually matters -- and 'it feels faster' is not a measurement. The next run should be timed. *** AND THE ROW'S OTHER HALF -- THE ONE THAT MATTERED MORE -- IS FULLY ADDRESSED. *** The original finding was not that the probe was slow but that AN OVERRUN LOOKED LIKE NOTHING: output captured with `out=$(timeout ...)` and grepped for patterns, so a mid-run kill yielded an empty log at exit 0, indistinguishable from a run still in progress. Every measurement since streams `python3 -u` to a file, and that change earned itself twice within the hour -- once on a plain-`&` launch that killed its own child, and once on a NameError at row 41 whose failing line was visible instead of silent.

rows.state_note: *** AND THE FEATURE'S VALUE WAS DEMONSTRATED THE SAME HOUR, BY A SEAT THAT BUILT ONE. *** While measuring Round 2's mutants the opus seat wrote its own probe WITH session selection (`tprobe2.py 'S1 badfmt,S4 acceptA'`) and used it immediately: for the Site A fallthrough mutant it ran TWO sessions instead of eight, because only those two can distinguish a decline from an accept. **That is the argument for the feature and, read carefully, also the argument for why it is a separate round.** Selection is CHEAP in a purpose-built probe where it is designed in; the cost measured here is RETROFITTING it to a 1200-line probe whose 36 sessions run at module level. The two facts are not in tension -- they are the same fact seen from each end, and a future round should read them together rather than citing one. *** A FOURTH COST FACT, MEASURED 2026-08-28, AND IT IS ABOUT THE FIX RATHER THAN THE COST: A ROW FILTER IS NOT A SMALL CHANGE TO THIS PROBE. *** Round 2 was going to fold one in -- the owner approved it on a cost I stated -- and the estimate was wrong by roughly 10x. Measured before building: session() calls at MODULE level (column 0) 36 session() calls inside a block 3 -- 39 **Skipping a row therefore means skipping TOP-LEVEL STATEMENTS.** A filter in `row()` alone changes what is SCORED and saves NOTHING, because the expensive part -- the session -- has already run by the time row() is called. Real per-row selection needs either a label threaded through all 36 call sites with an early-return in session(), or the probe restructured into per-row functions. **WITHDRAWN FROM ROUND 2 BY OWNER DECISION** so the strengthening diff stays about the replacement channel, which is what its pass 2 reviews. It ships as its own round with its own panel and its own negative controls -- a filter that silently selects nothing is this project's most-recorded failure class, and it must not ride in on a diff reviewed for something else. WHEN IT IS BUILT, the guards are already specified: print a DENOMINATOR (`selected N of 58`) beside every result; HARD-FAIL on zero matches; HARD-FAIL on a selector naming a row that does not exist (so a renamed row cannot silently stop being tested); and unset MUST be byte-identical to today, which is the negative control the gate itself provides. Name derived from the tree rather than invented: `GDROM_DEF_ROWS` -- the house idiom is `os.environ.get("_")` (SELFMUTANT_RUN_TIMEOUT and friends) and this probe already owns the GDROM_DEF_ namespace via GDROM_DEF_RESULT= / GDROM_DEF_VECTOR=. *** AND THE GATE PINS THE DENOMINATOR AT 58: *** gate_sh_rounding.sh names rows in a `for v in ...` list and checks the ratio, so any filter must leave the unset-path denominator untouched. *** A THIRD COST VARIABLE, MEASURED 2026-08-27: COMMANDS PER SESSION. *** This row's headline is *"cost is SESSIONS, not rows"*, and that was derived from probes whose rows each run one short session. **A row added to `asic_badaddr_probe.py` today is ONE session -- cheap by this row's own measure -- and took roughly SIX MINUTES.** ``` the other 13 rows ~15 s each one session, a handful of debugger commands `sweep 256` ~6 min one session, 768 debugger commands ``` It walks all 256 offsets of the SYSASIC window with `r1=; pc=; step 1` per offset. Each of those is a pty round-trip, and the round-trips dominate: the emulator work itself is 256 byte loads. **SO THE RULE NEEDS A SECOND TERM.** A probe's wall clock is roughly `sessions x boot_cost + total_debugger_commands x round_trip`, and the two terms are traded against each other by DESIGN CHOICES that look unrelated: folding N rows into one session removes N boots and keeps every command. **THE CHEAPER SHAPE, not built:** drive the walk from GUEST CODE -- a loop, or an unrolled block written once with `put h` -- so one `step N` replaces hundreds of round-trips. Not done today because hand-assembling SH is this project's documented encoding trap, and a wrong encoding yields a probe that measures the wrong thing while looking green. *Recorded rather than acted on: the six minutes buys a row that defends 256 offsets where nine were defended before, and the alternative risks a silently-wrong instrument.*

The killing set is four contiguous byte ranges per 16-byte group (0x0c-0x0f, 0x1c-0x1f, ... 0xfc-0xff); the sixteen first cited are the word-aligned quarter. Detector consequence: a word-aligned walk covers a QUARTER of the defect while reporting full coverage; it must walk bytes, and in both directions, since `r == 3 && writeflag == MEM_WRITE` is invisible to a loads-only probe. Same seat: delete fatal() with exit(1) -- not because fatal() kills (it does not) but because 64 unlatched guest-drivable addresses are a flood.

The round chose between keeping it UNLATCHED and deleting it, when this fork's own `memory_rw.c:495-523` already ships the third option -- a BOUNDED diagnostic (`static int n_trunc_msgs`, 8 emissions) whose comment reasons that 'probing at the end of a device's mapped range is common and benign'. **The same phenomenon, in the file that DISPATCHES to this device, and #463 reached the opposite conclusion without citing it.** It proposed candidate-1-plus-latch WITH the `memory_writemax64` call -- independently finding and fixing the read-path defect that the other three dissenters' bare `return` would have introduced. VERDICT: the characterisation HOLDS -- 64 is right, 'one guest load' is the right minimum trigger, host-kill was the right primary severity. *** BUT IT ADDED A CLASS THE ROUND HAD ONLY AS AN EXAMPLE: TRANSACTION CLOSURE. *** Bases OUTSIDE the 64 die when a non-base LANE lands inside. **VERIFIED HERE INDEPENDENTLY: 16 eight-byte bases (0x08, 0x18, 0x28 ... ) whose own offset is safe die on their high word, and ALL 8 aligned 32-byte store-queue bases span exactly TWO killing words (base 0x0 hits 0xc and 0x1c) -- dying MID-BURST, after earlier words have already committed.** The round's own `fmov.d` at +0x18 IS this instance; it was found as an illustration and never counted as a class. RESEARCH STAGE, filled last (the row's codex research entry had been a HELD MARKER, not an answer -- counted as one by a name-count, which is the gap-closes-itself shape). VERDICT: the DECLINE is the better trade; **the LATCH is not**. FOUR facts no other seat had. (1) *** `mask_13[4] IS mask_11[1]` IS AN OBSERVED ABI/LAYOUT CONSEQUENCE, NOT VALID C -- the subscript is UB regardless of member adjacency.*** Every other seat, the adjudicator and I treated it as a well-defined layout fact. **That makes an EXECUTABLE bound more valuable, not less.** (2) *** FIRST HARDWARE ORACLE IN THE ENTIRE ROUND. *** The project holds no Holly ASIC documentation and the ledger records that absence; codex cited external sources -- Linux's mach-dreamcast IRQ code documents three status words and three per mask group, and KallistiOS exposes exactly +0/+4/+8. **The three-word bound is a HARDWARE fact, not an implementation choice**, which independently condemns `[4]`. (3) *** THE ARGUMENT AGAINST THE LATCH, AND IT IS GROUNDED IN THIS ROUND'S OWN ASSESS FINDING: a latched warning would fire on legitimate traffic -- *** WITHDRAWN 2026-08-25: this was measured too broad. The handler receives `len`, so a byte at +0x0d or an unaligned call IS distinguishable from any lane of a legal 8-byte access; the predicate is empty only for an ALIGNED 32-BIT access at +0x0c. Silence remains defensible as POLICY, not as forced ***. *** The old alarm fired on reserved lanes INCLUDING the second half of a legitimate split access -- and kimi's transaction-closure finding proves those are normal: every 8-byte access based at one of the FOUR word-2 registers (+0x08/+0x18/+0x28/+0x38 -- an earlier version of this sentence omitted +0x38 and said 'an implemented register', which reads as all twelve; word-0 bases do not die and word-1 offsets are not 8-byte aligned at all) touches a reserved lane by construction. Also notes `return;` bare is invalid, DEVICE_ACCESS expanding to an int function. It agrees the shipped fix introduced no PRESENT silent OOB (all twelve cases yield r <= 2; the default path is old, only the pairing is new) and that the weakness is PROSPECTIVE.

The FIX is unchanged and the fmov.d ROW is FILED, but the round may NOT ship the old framing. *** The honest statement is **`a documented register accessed at the wrong SZ ends the host`**, not `a guest probes reserved space`. The split is witnessable and severity-bearing; the permutation is structurally invisible to readback and is clause-(e) non-coverage. **Keep them distinct in the record so neither is read as covering the other.**  *** AND THE INVARIANT CLAIM IS SCOPED, NOT GLOBAL: *** the structural-invariant comment this round leaves in `dev_dreamcast_asic.c` governs THAT FILE ONLY. A second route to `r == 3` exists via `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR` whenever `(e>>5) & 3 == 3` -- `[96,127]`, `[224,255]`, `[352,383]` -- **not for 'any event >= 96', which is false because `[128,159]` maps to `+0x10` (r = 0); see the correction on `asiceventaddr`** -- and the edit that reaches it adds a `#define` to a header with no change to the device file -- filed as `asiceventaddr`. **The round may not claim the invariant is fully protected.**  *** THE WITNESS IS NO LONGER A DESIGN -- IT RAN ON THE COMMITTED BUILD AND REPRODUCED THE DEFECT: 5/9, with EXACTLY the four intended reds and nothing else (`regress/artifacts/asic463/witness_prefix_HEAD.raw`). *** All three controls green: `live` returns 0x5eed through RAM, `devsig` returns the SH4 IPRD reset value 0xda74 proving dispatch, and `asic ok` stores-and-reads-back 0x5a on mask_13[0] -- which RAM cannot fake and a deleted case cannot satisfy. That pass is where the round's worst record was made: **the brief stated SIXTEEN killing offsets and the true number is SIXTY-FOUR**, because `relative_addr` need not be word-aligned. Four seats corrected it, one SILENTLY NARROWED the claim to 'sixteen word-aligned' (repairing the sentence while hiding the defect), and four did not engage with alignment at all. `kill byte` (+0x0d) is the row that pins the correction. TWO REPORTING IMPRECISIONS IN `panel.sh`'s OWN SEAT CHECK, recorded because they mislead a later reader: it printed `*** RATE-LIMITED (HTTP 429)` for what is actually a **403 quota/billing** failure -- the disposition is right (an operational failure, never agreement) but the label names the wrong status; and it tallied `6/7 scriptable` while `ollama_kimi.txt` (17.4 KB) sat answered in the same directory, because the check does not count the substitute transport. entries.note: There is NO copy of Linux's drivers/cdrom/gdrom.c or NetBSD's sys/arch/dreamcast/dev/gdrom.c anywhere in this tree, yet #462's design rested on three claims about them. *** ONE WAS REFUTED FROM ITS OWN QUOTED LINE. *** Four records cited `while ((GDROM_BUSY & 0x88) != 0x08) ;` as an unbounded NetBSD poll of +0x18. That loop exits only when bit 3 is SET and bit 7 CLEAR; +0x18's domain is {0 idle, 1 busy} and neither ANDs to 0x08 -- IT WOULD HANG ON CORRECT HARDWARE. Independently, dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:722-737 -- code this round never touched -- documents that same wait as NetBSD's COMMAND-START handshake on the CONTROL window's BUSY register and sets d->busy |= 0x08 in reply. The exhibit was lifted from that comment and re-pointed at a register it says nothing about. The conclusion survives on Linux; the reason does not, and a wrong reason gets reused -- this project already has the fatal()-is-byte-for-byte-debug() case on record. All four corrected IN PLACE. This is the #357/#362/#365 shape: citations from panel output rather than a local source. Obtaining the SH manual refuted a wrong finding the same session it was raised; obtaining these two drivers is the same cheap move.

rows.title: gdrompionull  the PIO data read dereferences d->data with no NULL test, reachable with LEGAL values only and with no diagnostic at all

entries.note: Found while answering a pass-1 question about gdromcondlies, a DIFFERENT defect. Three facts, each verified by opening the file: COND_DATA_AVAIL is 0x08 and 0xef & 0x08 == 0x08, so the LEGAL value 0xef sets the emulator's data-available flag; handle_command frees d->data and NULLs it but NEVER resets d->data_len (the only writer is alloc_data); and the PIO read guards ONLY `cur_data_offset < data_len` before dereferencing d->data[...] -- there is no NULL test. The DMA arm received one in #462; ITS PIO TWIN DID NOT, because it relies on cond & COND_DATA_AVAIL, a flag the guest can set back. Sequence, legal values throughout: stage TOC (data_len=408) -> stage Mount 0x70 (frees data, data_len STAYS 408, bit 3 cleared) -> write COND=0xef (bit 3 back on) -> read +0x80 -> d->data[0] on NULL. OB-20's two breaks reach the same data==NULL/data_len>0 state without needing 0x70. *** AND IT CONSTRAINS gdromcondlies: the naive Site B fix (decline but keep d->cond = idata) turns this from ONE legal value into EVERY unmodelled value with bit 3 set -- that round would be the one that WIDENED a NULL-deref primitive. Leave d->cond UNCHANGED on decline; cond bit 3 is INTERPRETED as a readiness flag gating a pointer path, so storing an arbitrary guest byte hands the guest a direct write to internal readiness state.

*** RECORDED RETROSPECTIVELY, same audit as the sibling entries. *** This seat answered at the REVIEW stage; its earlier entry on this row is filed under ASSESS, so the review stage read 8/9 with the flagship measuring seat apparently absent. PASS 1: all four premises HOLD, and the item is STRONGER than recorded. P1 has a third answer -- `d->cond = idata` sits OUTSIDE both arms, so 0xef both stores and fires, and 0xef is the UNIQUE surviving guest-settable bit-3 value at HEAD. P3 was UNDERSTATED: there is a ONE-COMMAND route needing no disk image and no prior staging, because diskimage_access returns 0 NON-fatally with no IDE disk attached and the gdrom code frees d->data AFTER alloc_data has set data_len. Recommended fix: `d->data_len = 0;` beside `d->cnt = 0;` in handle_command's tail -- one line, zero blast radius, and ZERO warn bits, which matters because a dedicated arm would be the SEVENTH bit and would fire the gdromwarnbits trigger in THIS round rather than in gdromcondlies. Rejected refusing 0xef -> COND_DATA_AVAIL: it makes memory safety downstream of an undocumented register-modelling choice. Also corrected two of my records, including 'four stores and a load' (it is 18 accesses, or 9 by the cheap route) which was load-bearing in the queue ranking. [panel_20260824_100322]
