rows.title: asiceventaddr  SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR is correct only for e in [0,95]: high events decode to DROPPED fourth-word offsets OR to LEGAL mask-register cases that clobber guest state, and no r-guard can see the second kind
rows.witness: none -- LATENT, and provably so: the highest defined event is 67 < 96
rows.state_note:
*** #466's PASS 2 OVERTURNED THE ADJUDICATION THAT SHIPPED IT. TWO SEATS INDEPENDENTLY REFUTED THE 'NO BUILD-TIME CHECK IS POSSIBLE' RULING, AND ONE OF THEM BUILT ALL FOUR VARIANTS. #468 ships the guard. ***

The adjudicator rejected a compile-time check on SHAPE: *an assert can only reference NAMED terms, so a future `#define SYSASIC_EVENT_FOO 96` adds a name it does not mention and compiles clean.* **That is true of a STANDALONE assert and false of a check INSIDE THE MACRO**, which fires at the RAISE and therefore cannot be bypassed by adding a name.

MEASURED by the opus5 seat, four variants under the real build compiler:

    V0 shipped macro           feared edit compiles CLEAN   <- the defect
    V1 standalone assert       CLEAN   <- adjudicator's objection CONFIRMED
    V2 check inside the macro  ERROR: negative array size
    V3 bitfield width          ERROR: negative width in bit-field

**V3 is preferred over V2 and the reason is measured:** with a runtime-variable `e`, V2 silently degrades to a VLA and compiles; V3 hard-errors because a bitfield width must be an integer constant. **Both need only C89** -- clean under `-std=c89 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra` -- so *the C11 leg of the rationale ruled out one SPELLING, not compile-time checking.* And the kimi substitute reached the same conclusion independently, by reasoning rather than building: *'a name-insensitive construction that catches the feared mutant exists, is build-time, and touches neither product code nor the vendored header.'*

**SO THE OPTION SET HAD THREE MEMBERS AND THE ADJUDICATION NAMED TWO** -- comment / standalone assert / **assert inside the macro**. Exactly the three-membered-option-set rule, biting the ruling that invoked it.

*** THE ADDITION LICENCE NOW CLEARS ON A MEASURED DELTA, which it did not before: *** V0 compiles the feared edit, V3 refuses it, and **all 21 real events keep BYTE-IDENTICAL addresses**. That is the A-vs-B measurement the licence asks for, and it is why this ships rather than staying a comment.

INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED HERE before landing: the feared edit is refused **and fails for OUR reason** (a bitfield diagnostic, not an incidental one); the boundary is exact (`e=95` compiles, `e=96` does not); the header still preprocesses `rc=0` and still holds its 21 numeric event defines, unchanged from before `#466`.

**THE COMMENT'S BAND TABLE WAS ALSO WRONG AND IS CORRECTED.** It omitted the ENTIRE `mask_9` group and understated the clobber domain **5.5x** -- the true domain is `e in [128,479]`, 352 values across NINE mask words, of which the comment named 64. It also mispaired `96..127 -> +0x0c, +0x1c`, which is the same band-to-address error the device file had already corrected an earlier draft for. Restated STRUCTURALLY: the macro treats the event's high bits as a word index into the whole 64-word register file, when only words 0-2 are the `pending_irq` group.

*And a clobber is worse than the comment implied: the mask cases carry no hack-bit discrimination and the store is a wholesale replacement with the tick called immediately, so the raise both FAILS and DESTROYS the guest's programmed IRQ mask.*

*** THREE APPARATUS FAILURES OF MINE ON THE WAY, ALL DOCUMENTED CLASSES, RECORDED BECAUSE THE THIRD IS NEW: ***
  1. my verification harness redefined `SYSASIC_BASE`, which the header owns -- every leg died of `redefined` and the feared-edit leg's 'pass' was a **FALSE PASS**, failing for the wrong reason. Rule 4 caught it: *did it fail for the reason under test?*
  2. I wrote the guard with a Python string instead of `chr(92)` and put a **literal `
` into product code** where a line continuation belongs -- the documented Bash->heredoc->Python trap, propagated to all four trees before I caught it.
  3. **NEW, AND WORTH THE SPACE: my own comment's worked example -- `#define SYSASIC_EVENT_FOO 96` -- POISONED THE CENSUS that greps the header for event defines.** The harness read the DOCUMENTATION as SOURCE and built a program out of the very construct the comment forbids. **A comment containing an example of a forbidden construct breaks any census that greps for that construct.** Same shape as the grep that matched a comment and was read as code earlier the same day.

*** ADJUDICATED 2026-08-26. MY DISSOLUTION READING HELD -- AND MY FOLD WAS HALF WRONG, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. ***

**THE DISSOLUTION CONFIRMED, MEASURED:** every event raise is a `memory_rw` write through the device decode. `SYSASIC_TRIGGER_EVENT` computes the address and issues the write; `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR` has exactly TWO occurrences in `src/` -- its definition and that one use -- and every in-tree raiser goes through the macro. The arrays are declared file-locally in the `.c`, so no other unit can index them. **There is no bypass, so the vendored-header LICENCE QUESTION IS MOOT** -- the guard need never live in the header.

*** BUT THE HEADER DEFECT IS BROADER THAN THE r==3 INVARIANT, AND THE EXCESS IS EXACTLY WHAT AN r-GUARD CANNOT SEE. Verified here by arithmetic and by reading the case: ***

    e=96..127   -> +0x0c   r=3   default: -- DROPPED (an r-guard covers this)
    e=128..159  -> +0x10   r=0   *** case 0x10: `d->mask_13[r] = idata` -- LEGAL WRITE ***
    e=256..287  -> +0x20   r=0   *** case 0x20: another legal mask case ***
    e>=2048     -> +0x100+       OUTSIDE the device window entirely

**A raise in [128,159] is decoded as a perfectly legal mask write and CLOBBERS a mask register the guest programmed.** Memory-safe, guest-visible, and invisible to any guard on `r` -- because r is 0, not 3. So the row FOLDS ONLY HALFWAY: the fourth-word half is covered by `asicindexcase`'s already-adjudicated #463b decline at zero added cost; **this row survives as DOCUMENT-ONLY for the mask-clobber bands and the window escape.**

**THE TRUE STATEMENT OF THE DEFECT: `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR` is correct only for e in [0,95].** The old title said it 'routes any event >= 96 to relative 0x0c' -- FALSE, true only of [96,127] -- and it contradicted this row's own tail correction AND the shipped comment in the device file, which already says *'an earlier draft said any event >= 96, which is false'*. **The queue's most-read field carried a falsehood its own body had corrected.** Title rewritten.

*** AND I REPEATED THAT SAME FALSE UNIVERSAL TO THE ADJUDICATOR while asking the question -- 'Every event >= 96 gives (e)>>5 == 3' -- when the correction already existed in TWO of my own shipped records. *** A brief built on my own uncorrected summary rather than on my own corrected record: the dropped-qualifier class, aimed at the seat I was asking for help.

**THE COMPILE-TIME ASSERT IS REJECTED ON SHAPE, NOT ON LICENCE, and the reason is this project's own named class.** An assert can only reference NAMED terms, so it pins today's max (`67>>5 == 2`, already true) while a future `#define SYSASIC_EVENT_FOO 96` -- **the exact feared edit** -- adds a name the assert does not mention and compiles clean. **A check that cannot fail on its own target mutant.** The `SH4_VAL` enum idiom does not transfer either: sparse hardware numbers need explicit `= n` per member and a terminal count sees only members above it. **The house precedent points the other way and is in this very device family**: `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` chose *'Stated rather than asserted: `_Static_assert` is C11 and this tree is C99'*. Follow it -- STATE the domain restriction.

CLOSING ARTIFACT: a 2-5 line comment in the header beside the macro -- the one place a future event-adder's eyes are guaranteed to be -- pointing at the device file's existing #463 invariant comment, which already points back. A comment adds no product code, so the addition licence is not even triggered. Tag it `/* #NNN: */` per house ethos. Must land byte-identical in `est/`.

*Premises the adjudicator discharged: the two-commit thirdparty figure CONFIRMED -- and sharper than I had it, since `8dd86b5` touched four thirdparty headers but NOT this one, so **this fork has never edited it**; the `[3]` arrays CONFIRMED; and 'a device-file comment cannot govern a header #define' is TRUE of the comment and HALF-TRUE of the guard, which is exactly why the row folds halfway.*

*** THE THREE ASIC ROWS REST ON ONE INVARIANT, AND TWO OF THEM MAY BE ONE FIX. Scoped 2026-08-26 by reading, no run. ***

**THE SHARED INVARIANT: `r == 3` is unreachable by any implemented case.** VERIFIED by reading the switch labels -- they are three CONSECUTIVE words at group bases `0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30`, so `r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3` yields 0, 1, 2 and never 3. All three rows are that one invariant, differing only in **which edit would break it**:

    asiceventaddr    a #define in the vendored HEADER (event >= 96 -> offset 0x0c)
    asicindexcase    an indexing `case` added at an r==3 offset in the DEVICE FILE
    asicoffsetkill   an adversarial MUTANT at an r==3 offset no detector row touches

**THE THIRD IS DIFFERENT IN KIND and should not be folded with the other two:** it is a DETECTOR-COVERAGE question, not a product invariant. `kill far` (+0xfc) was added to defeat a GROUP-NARROWING mutant and cannot defeat a SINGLE-OFFSET one; the seat that raised it said plainly it did not build it.

*** THE FINDING THAT MAY FOLD THE OTHER TWO, and it contradicts `asiceventaddr`'s own stated reason for being a separate row: *** that row argues a device-file comment "cannot govern a `#define` added to a header". **True of a COMMENT. Not true of a GUARD.** An event `>= 96` does not stay in the header -- it becomes an ADDRESS the driver accesses, arriving at the device as `relative_addr == 0x0c` and decoding to `r == 3`. **So a guard on `r` in the device file would catch the header entry point too**, because the header case MANIFESTS as a device-file access.

If that holds, one guard covers both rows and the vendored-header edit -- the expensive part, on a file this fork has touched once -- may be unnecessary. **Stated as a question rather than a conclusion because I have not built it**, and the adjudicator was asked the licence question on the header assumption; this finding is being sent to it as a correction rather than acted on unilaterally.

STOP CONDITION: if the guard-covers-both reading holds, fold `asiceventaddr` into `asicindexcase` as one fix with two entry points and close it as a duplicate; if it does not, the rows stay separate and the header licence question stands.

*** SCOPED 2026-08-26 WITHOUT A RUN -- the row is read-only by construction, and the scoping found a CONSTRAINT that changes the fix's cost. ***

**THE FIX SITE IS A VENDORED THIRDPARTY HEADER.** The macro is at `src/include/thirdparty/dreamcast_sysasicvar.h`, which carries BOTH a GXemul `$Id$` and an upstream **`$NetBSD: sysasicvar.h,v 1.5`** line. **MEASURED: `git log --all -- 'src/include/thirdparty/*'` returns TWO commits -- the 0.7.0 import, and the single ~119-correction hardening commit.** So this fork has edited thirdparty exactly ONCE.

*The precedent is not absent, and it cuts both ways: the header's own banner says it was "Extended with useful macros and also some more event definitions described in KOS comments", so GXemul UPSTREAM already extends this vendored file. Editing it is precedented -- it is just rare, and rarity is the cost.*

**WHY THAT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TRIVIA:** the row's whole reason for existing separately is that *the edit which reaches this defect adds a `#define` to a header, with no device-file change at all* -- so a structural-invariant comment in `dev_dreamcast_asic.c` cannot govern it. **The only place a guard can sit is the same rarely-touched header**, which means the fix's licence question is sharper than for an in-file addition.

**THE CANDIDATE FIX, stated so it can be adjudicated rather than argued:** a compile-time assertion beside the macro, so that adding an event `>= 96` fails the BUILD rather than silently routing to relative `0x0c` and indexing three-element arrays at 3. It is self-verifying by construction -- a negative control is one test `#define` -- and it costs nothing at runtime.

**BUT IT IS AN ADDITION TO PRODUCT CODE, so the ADDITION LICENCE governs: a MEASURED DELTA or a TRANSFERRED WARRANT, never 'it cannot hurt'.** The delta cannot be measured without a build, and the machine is reserved (owner directive 2026-08-26: hold off on anything needing an idle machine). **`asicbadaddr` is the natural warrant donor** -- same device, same `r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3` decode, same three-element arrays -- and whether that transfers to a THIRDPARTY header edit is exactly the judgement an adjudicator owes rather than me.

*** WHAT IS NOT IN DOUBT AND NEEDED NO RUN: the arithmetic. *** `(e)>>5 == 3` for every `e >= 96`; the highest defined event is 67; therefore latent today, and reachable by a one-line header addition by anyone adding a high event number. Two seats confirmed both numbers from source on 2026-08-24 and I re-derived the macro form here.

NEXT ACTION: adjudicate the licence and the thirdparty-edit question. NOT shipped unilaterally -- a rarely-touched vendored header is precisely where 'it cannot hurt' does the most damage.

RAISED BY THE opus5 SEAT on the asicbadaddr pass-1 panel (panel_20260824_231824), ADJUDICATED 2026-08-24. `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR(e)` is `SYSASIC_BASE + 4*((e)>>5)`, so ANY event number >= 96 gives `(e)>>5 == 3` and a relative offset of 0x0c -- which `dev_dreamcast_asic.c`'s `r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3` maps to index 3 of three-element arrays. **LATENT AND PROVABLY SO: the highest defined event is 67 (MATOUTOFMEM), and both the 67 and the 96 threshold were confirmed from source by two seats.** *** WHY IT IS A SEPARATE ROW RATHER THAN PART OF asicbadaddr: THE EDIT THAT REACHES IT ADDS A #define TO A HEADER, WITH NO CHANGE TO THE DEVICE FILE AT ALL -- so the structural-invariant comment asicbadaddr plans to leave in `dev_dreamcast_asic.c` CANNOT GOVERN IT. *** Post-fix the failure mode also changes rather than disappearing: an event >= 96 would write to 0x0c, fall to `default:`, and the pending bit would be SILENTLY LOST where pre-fix it was `exit(1)`. Neither is correct; neither is reachable today. *** DISPOSITION: NO RUNTIME GUARD *** -- a guard that cannot fire is the insurance-that-isn't this tree already rejects. The carrier is a one-line comment at the event-define block IN THE HEADER. **FILED RATHER THAN SHIPPED THIS ROUND, and the reason is the file class:** the header lives under `src/include/thirdparty/`, which this fork HAS edited (the 8dd86b5 hardening commit) but where NO file carries the `/* #NNN: */ ` correction tag the ethos otherwise requires -- so the convention for editing it is unsettled, and settling it is not this round's job. *** THE MANDATORY HALF IS THE RECORD, NOT THE COMMENT: `asicbadaddr` must SCOPE its invariant claim to `dev_dreamcast_asic.c` and name this header path as a separate latent item, rather than claiming the invariant is fully protected. ***  *** CORRECTED 2026-08-25 BY THE #463 RECORDS AUDIT (`_scratchpad/panel_20260825_024101_audit`, grok seat), and the correction makes this row STRONGER. *** Every earlier statement of this row said the macro reaches `0x0c` for "any event >= 96". **That is false**: `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR(e) = SYSASIC_BASE + 4*((e)>>5)` (`dreamcast_sysasicvar.h:74`) sends `e` in `[128,159]` to `+0x10`, which is r = 0 and perfectly legal. The true predicate is `(e>>5) & 3 == 3` -- `[96,127]` -> `+0x0c`, `[224,255]` -> `+0x1c`, `[352,383]` -> `+0x2c`, `[480,511]` -> `+0x3c`. So the violator is not a single range above a threshold but a REPEATING FAMILY that lands on the fourth word of every 16-byte group -- the same structural shape as `asicbadaddr` itself, one level up in the header. Verified by enumerating `4*(e>>5)` over `e>>5` in `[0,15]`. The LATENCY argument is unchanged and still holds: max over all 21 `SYSASIC_EVENT_*` defines is 67 (`:72`), and `67>>5 == 2` lands at `+0x08`.

*** CLOSURE PROPOSED, NOT MADE.  Verified by me against the source; held for the 2026-09-09
adjudication because a row closed on one seat's reading plus my own agreement is exactly the
self-review the conflict-of-interest badge exists to disclose. ***
**codex (rating pass, 2026-09-07): `low -- the named domain hazard is ALREADY GUARDED`.**  *"the
header now embeds `((e) >= 0 && (e) < 96) ? 1 : -1` in `SYSASIC_EVENT_RANGE_OK(e)`, which
`SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR(e)` invokes."*

**VERIFIED BY READING:** `dreamcast_sysasicvar.h:135` defines `SYSASIC_EVENT_RANGE_OK` and `:140`
is `(SYSASIC_BASE + 4*((e)>>5) + SYSASIC_EVENT_RANGE_OK(e))` -- the guard is inside the macro, so an
out-of-domain event cannot produce an address at all.  Added by `#467`/`#468` (`29b450c`), whose
title says *"the ASIC domain is now ENFORCED"*.

**The row's own witness text is now STALE**: it reads *"LATENT, and provably so: the highest defined
event is 67 < 96"*, which was the pre-fix warrant for it being latent.  The current warrant is
stronger and different -- the macro rejects the domain structurally -- and that is what the closure
should record.

rows.title: probeabsentraise  three rows guard a THREE-state value with a TWO-state test and raise ValueError on `absent`, taking the whole probe down with no verdict line -- and the correct guard is already used by two other rows in the same file
rows.witness: MEASURED by the opus5 seat against a real wedged transcript: printed(t,'r2') == 'absent' -> ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 16
rows.state_note: `printed()` returns THREE values -- `died`, `absent`, or a `0x...` string. Three rows test only `!= "died"` before calling `int(_, 16)`: `gdrom_default_probe.py:878` (`_p`), `:962` (`_a`), `:1184` (`_q`). A wedged session in any of those three makes `printed()` return `absent`, and the probe dies with a traceback and **NO `GDROM_DEF_RESULT` LINE AT ALL**. *** THE FIX IS NOT AN INVENTION: TWO OTHER ROWS IN THE SAME FILE ALREADY USE THE CORRECT GUARD. *** `devsig` (:324) and `data 0xffff` (:554) both write `if g.startswith("0x")`, which is a THREE-state-safe prefix test. So the repair is to apply the pattern the file already contains, three times -- not to design one. *That two rows got it right and three got it wrong in one file is the more useful observation than the crash itself: the correct form was available and not reached for.* **FILED, NOT FIXED IN-ROUND**, and the stopping rule is why: this is neither a measured false pass nor a wrong record. It fails in the SAFE direction -- a traceback yields no verdict line, so the gate's `rows run` check reads 0 against a wanted 58 and FAILS LOUDLY rather than passing something wrong. It is a robustness gap, ranked below live defects. **It is also cheap and natural to fix alongside `probetimebased`'s three-state predicate**, which is the round that makes `absent` a first-class state rather than an accident.

rows.title: asicpermute  `(relative_addr / 4) % 3` permutes the ASIC register index bijectively and NO round-trip row can see it
rows.witness: none -- LATENT; needs a free-running assertion probe, which no SH probe here has
rows.state_note: OUTSIDE the #463 detector's contract, and the contract says so rather than claiming completeness. `% 3` maps each group bijectively -- {4,5,6} -> {1,2,0} -- so every write and its readback round-trip through the SAME permuted cell and AGREE. Batching does not help: batching catches ALIASING (two offsets colliding on one cell) and a permutation collides nothing. Yet the tick's `pending_irq[i] & mask_13[i]` then pairs the wrong words, so the OBSERVABLE is interrupt assertion, which no row here reaches. **A single-stepping probe cannot observe interrupt DELIVERY** (`cpu_dyntrans.c:204-206`), so closing this needs the free-running shape. `% 3` is the most plausible naive 'repair' anyone writes at this site -- it is what you reach for when worried about an index out of range -- so this is the highest-probability future edit in the file.

rows.title: asicindexcase  the deleted guard was ALSO a bounds check, so an INDEXING case added at an r==3 offset is now a SILENT out-of-bounds access
rows.hold: #463b FINAL FORM, ADJUDICATED AT 9/9 WITH NO MARKERS. Ships a SILENT FALL-THROUGH decline. The LATCH is REFUTED, not deferred. Budget: the guarded arm, the r==3 row value upgrade, one contract sentence. Not run.
rows.witness: none -- LATENT; the invariant is verified TODAY (max r = 2 over 12 labels)
rows.state_note:
*** THE THREE ASIC ROWS REST ON ONE INVARIANT, AND TWO OF THEM MAY BE ONE FIX. Scoped 2026-08-26 by reading, no run. ***

**THE SHARED INVARIANT: `r == 3` is unreachable by any implemented case.** VERIFIED by reading the switch labels -- they are three CONSECUTIVE words at group bases `0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30`, so `r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3` yields 0, 1, 2 and never 3. All three rows are that one invariant, differing only in **which edit would break it**:

    asiceventaddr    a #define in the vendored HEADER (event >= 96 -> offset 0x0c)
    asicindexcase    an indexing `case` added at an r==3 offset in the DEVICE FILE
    asicoffsetkill   an adversarial MUTANT at an r==3 offset no detector row touches

**THE THIRD IS DIFFERENT IN KIND and should not be folded with the other two:** it is a DETECTOR-COVERAGE question, not a product invariant. `kill far` (+0xfc) was added to defeat a GROUP-NARROWING mutant and cannot defeat a SINGLE-OFFSET one; the seat that raised it said plainly it did not build it.

*** THE FINDING THAT MAY FOLD THE OTHER TWO, and it contradicts `asiceventaddr`'s own stated reason for being a separate row: *** that row argues a device-file comment "cannot govern a `#define` added to a header". **True of a COMMENT. Not true of a GUARD.** An event `>= 96` does not stay in the header -- it becomes an ADDRESS the driver accesses, arriving at the device as `relative_addr == 0x0c` and decoding to `r == 3`. **So a guard on `r` in the device file would catch the header entry point too**, because the header case MANIFESTS as a device-file access.

If that holds, one guard covers both rows and the vendored-header edit -- the expensive part, on a file this fork has touched once -- may be unnecessary. **Stated as a question rather than a conclusion because I have not built it**, and the adjudicator was asked the licence question on the header assumption; this finding is being sent to it as a correction rather than acted on unilaterally.

STOP CONDITION: if the guard-covers-both reading holds, fold `asiceventaddr` into `asicindexcase` as one fix with two entry points and close it as a duplicate; if it does not, the rows stay separate and the header licence question stands.

NAMED BY THE FABLE ADJUDICATION AND BY minimax, INDEPENDENTLY (_scratchpad/panel_20260825_020219). `r == 3` is out of range for `uint32_t[3]`, so `if (r == 3) exit(1)` was doing TWO jobs and #463 reasoned about only one. Before #463 the switch had NEVER ONCE executed with r == 3. It is safe today only because r == 3 lands on `default:`, whose body indexes nothing -- ENUMERATED, not asserted: all twelve labels give max r = 2. **But #463 also deleted the tripwire that made this self-announcing**, so a future edit adding an indexing case at a +0x0c-class offset is a silent OOB that no detector row sees. Deliberately NOT fixed in-round: it is outside the DEPENDS-ON enumeration (it adds a predicate rather than weakening one the fix depends on), so fixing it in-round would be the runaway chain. Closing options: extend the arrays to [4] (see `asicarray4`), or ship `if (r == 3) return;` as a bounds-safe decline.  *** ENRICHED 2026-08-25 FROM #463'S RESEARCH STAGE, which was fired to close a panel gap AFTER the round had committed -- the owner was offered an exemption and DECLINED it. *** (a) THE SURVIVING ARGUMENT, credited to the kimi seat and the only one that survives contact with the file: the fix insured brand-new state with a COMMENT where one line would insure it with CONTROL FLOW. It is an ADDITION, not a reversal -- 'keep the deletion; add the line'. (b) THE CORRECTED FORM, and it matters because the obvious form is WRONG: a bare `if (r == 3) return;` SKIPS the function's common tail (`if (writeflag == MEM_READ) memory_writemax64(cpu, data, len, odata); return 1;`), handing a guest read an untouched buffer. **FOUR readers independently proposed that broken line -- deepseek, minimax, kimi AND THE ADJUDICATOR ITSELF** -- from packets that showed the guard and the switch but not the tail. The correct form declines while leaving `odata` at 0 and reaching the common tail. (c) IN-TREE PRECEDENT nobody had cited: `memory_rw.c:495-523`, in the file that DISPATCHES to this device, bounds a guest-drivable diagnostic to 8 emissions (`n_trunc_msgs`) because 'probing at the end of a device's mapped range is common and benign'. The fork's own answer to this phenomenon is BOUND THE COUNT, KEEP THE MESSAGE -- so a latched variant has precedent the round never weighed. (d) THE ANCHOR PROPERTY, verified arithmetically: an explicit decline pins the DECLINE COLUMN at `(addr & 0x0c) == 0x0c`, so a translation MOVES it onto a probed offset -- `+1` reddens `safe 8`, `+2` reddens `safe 4` (the residual that escapes even `mask9 rt`), `-1` reddens `asic ok`. The whole translation class would close with one line and rows already shipped. (e) PRECONDITION for shipping it: a 13-mutant x 13-row table re-measured byte-identical with the line in, and `mask9 rt` KEPT -- it is the only anchor surviving if the line is later deleted, and the two catch the class through different channels. *** AND A CORRECTION TO THE ADJUDICATION THAT ORDERED THIS ENRICHMENT. *** It counted five layers protecting this hazard, one being 'four measured kill rows asserting survive-plus-DECLINE-VALUE at r==3 offsets', concluding a future `case 0x0c:` assigning visible data would redden the detector. **MEASURED FALSE BY READING THE PROBE**: `kill word`, `kill byte`, `kill store` and `kill far` all compare `'survived' if alive else 'died'` against `'survived'` -- SURVIVE-ONLY, no value check. Such a case would keep them GREEN. That layer does not exist; the other four (verified enumeration, the in-code comment, this filed item, the contract's disclosure) stand. The adjudicator wrote 'the dissent read the diff, it did not read the detector' in the same answer -- it had descriptions rather than the source, and the opus5 seat, which DID read it, had already reported the rows as survive-only. **This is `asickillsurvive`, and it has now caused a wrong claim by an adjudicator, which is a sharper argument for fixing it than the original filing made.**  *** #463b FULLY SPECIFIED 2026-08-25 BY ADJUDICATION. Ships decline+latch, not a bare decline. *** THE FORM: `if (r == 3)` declines with a ONE-SHOT LATCHED `fatal()` and an explicit `memory_writemax64` so the read path writes the defined 0 -- early-return, which makes a future `+0x0c`-class label DEAD CODE BY CONSTRUCTION and CLOSES THIS ROW. Per-instance struct field, not a `static`, because the device is multi-instance. WHY LATCHED RATHER THAN BARE: the loss is MEASURED, not aesthetic -- #463's finding 5 established the deleted `fatal()` printed unconditionally while the surviving `debug()` is silenced by `-q` and by free-running at verbose 0. **Code that does not make the trade beats prose confessing it.** And the latch rebuilds exactly the property the de-escalation clause mourned: under a future `+1`-style decode defect every legal `+0x?8` access lands in the decline column, and the first 8 announce -- field-time announcement complementing the gate-time detector, with no host kill and no flood. THE ROW BUDGET, and it is bounded ON PRINCIPLE rather than by restraint: (1) **UPGRADE the four r==3 rows' oracle** to assert the returned value is the defined 0. They are survive-only today; they already READ, so this only adds the assertion. This discharges an adjudicator condition open since the FIRST adjudication ('confirm the kill rows check the decline VALUE, not survival alone'), never discharged, and now load-bearing because the candidates differ exactly in decline-column semantics. (2) **ONE BOUND ROW**: the fix now ADDS a predicate (`n < 8`), so clause (d) / accept-failability owes a row that reddens when the bound is REMOVED -- count <= 8 occurrences across the probe's 64 r==3 accesses. **Pin the COUNT, not the message text.** (3) One contract sentence. EXPECTED EQUIVALENCE, recorded in advance so it is not mistaken for an escape: the decline-nulled mutant (`if (r == 3)` kept, fall-through restored) will likely measure EQUIVALENT at base, because `default:` declines identically -- the #449 pattern, an equivalence RESULT and not a failure. MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE: base is an INVARIANCE CONTROL, never a discriminator -- all candidates are guest-identical at base and a detector should pin CONTRACT, not implementation. The evidence is entirely in the mutant deltas, and the translation mutants must go STRICTLY REDDER (`+1` -> safe 8, `+2` -> safe 4, `-1` -> asic ok; arithmetic verified). **Base must be RE-RUN on the latched build, not inherited** -- 8 new `fatal()` lines enter the pty logs, and `gate_hygiene` GRADES pty logs, which is a known trap class here: a new diagnostic entering graded logs must be shown green, not assumed. CLOSE-OUT: full 13-mutant table on the latched build, pass 2 on the real diff, targeted gate, one commit, and then #463 and #463b are OVER -- the next dissent on this device buys a new round or a filed row, never a reopening.  *** FINAL FORM 2026-08-25: A SILENT FALL-THROUGH DECLINE. THE LATCH IS DEAD. *** `if (r == 3) { /* comment */ } else switch (...)` -- a guarded arm joining the EXISTING epilogue, NOT an early return. That form uses the tail's own `memory_writemax64` so nothing is duplicated, and it does not lean on the dispatcher pre-zeroing read buffers (`memory_rw.c:485`) -- codex's objection answered STRUCTURALLY rather than by trusting a non-local guarantee. *** WHY THE LATCH DIED, on two independent closures either of which is fatal. *** (1) THE PREDICATE IS EMPTY WHERE IT MATTERS: implemented registers occupy words 0-2 of all four groups (documentarily grounded -- Linux mach-dreamcast and KallistiOS both show three words per group, no fourth), so every r==3 lane in modelled space sits directly above an implemented word-2 register and IS the second lane of a legal 8-byte access. 'Latch only on offsets that are not a lane of a legal multi-word access' selects the EMPTY SET -- a dead guard, and this round has refused three of those already. (2) THE INFORMATION IS ABSENT, NOT MERELY AWKWARD: the decoder issues two independent 32-bit accesses, so at the handler **the second half of a legal fmov.d and a direct probe of a reserved word are BYTE-IDENTICAL CALLS.** No predicate written inside this function separates them at any complexity. A dispatcher-layer latch, where transaction context exists, is a different change to a different file -- out of scope. *** AND IT REWRITES THIS ROUND'S FINDING 5: the deleted `fatal()` did not merely print unconditionally, it printed ON LEGAL TRAFFIC -- the second half of every 8-byte access to an implemented register. The 'self-announcing property' the latch was meant to restore was PARTLY A FALSE-ALARM PROPERTY ALL ALONG, so the trade the deletion made was SMALLER than finding 5 claimed and smaller than the latch ruling claimed on top of it. *** THE COMMENT MUST CARRY THE INOCULATION, one line: *silent by design -- r==3 lanes occur inside legitimate split accesses (fmov.d, SQ), so any diagnostic here false-alarms.* That sentence is what stops the next reader re-deriving the latch. WARRANT, THREE INDEPENDENT LEGS: the measured anchor (`+1`->safe 8, `+2`->safe 4 closing the one mutant that escaped everything, `-1`->asic ok); enforcement by control flow instead of enumeration; and the UB upgrade -- a broken invariant buys UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR a compiler may exploit, not a defined overlap, which makes the decline the only C-meaningful statement of the bound in executable form. DETECTOR DELTA: **the bound-count row DIES WITH THE LATCH** -- it was the latch's own accept-failability obligation, and no predicate means no row. The r==3 value upgrade stays.

rows.title: asicoffsetkill  a per-offset kill at an offset no detector row touches -- `if (relative_addr == 0x1c) exit(1)` scores clean
rows.witness: harness: the subject is DETECTOR COVERAGE, so the ladder's `harness:` term applies and the proof is a mutation. MEASURED both directions with one script: regress/artifacts/asicoffsetkill/sweep_20260827/ (BASELINE_RUN.txt 14/14 green, MUTANT_RUN.txt sweep RED and all nine pre-existing rows green).
rows.state_note:
*** CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-08-27, AND THE MUTANT WAS THE ONE THIS ROW PREDICTED. ***

The row said `if (relative_addr == 0x1c) exit(1)` scores clean against every existing row.
Built exactly that and ran it:

```
  kill word    survived  survived  ok     <- all NINE pre-existing rows stay GREEN
  kill byte    survived  survived  ok
  kill store   survived  survived  ok
  kill far     survived  survived  ok
  safe 4       survived  survived  ok
  live         0x5eed    0x5eed    ok     <- controls prove the fixture works
  devsig       0xda74    0xda74    ok
  sweep 256    died      0x5eed    FAIL   <- ONLY the new row catches it
```

Baseline on the clean build: **14/14, sweep green**.  Same script both directions.

**THE ROW: one session that byte-loads every offset in the SYSASIC window** (SYSASIC_SIZE
is 0x100, verified), then reads back a liveness marker -- so reaching the marker proves the
session survived all 256 accesses rather than that the pty merely stayed open.  A kill
planted at ANY offset kills that session.

**ALL 256, not the 16 word-aligned r==3 offsets**, because the carrier records a census
that was wrong by 4x for exactly this reason: `relative_addr` need not be word-aligned, so
the killing set is 64 byte addresses and not 16.  Sweeping the whole window costs the same
one session and is immune to that arithmetic being re-derived wrongly again.

**HONEST LIMIT: it is SURVIVE-ONLY and does NOT close `asickillsurvive`.**  It proves no
offset terminates the host; it says nothing about what a declined offset RETURNS.

**COST, and it is a finding in itself: ~6 MINUTES for one row.**  768 debugger round-trips
dominate; the emulator work is 256 byte loads.  Recorded against `probeslow`, whose
headline -- *cost is SESSIONS, not rows* -- needs a second term.
RAISED BY THE grok SEAT on the #463 pass-2 panel (_scratchpad/panel_20260825_020219), which stated plainly that it did NOT build it. The detector's rows touch +0x04, +0x08, +0x0c, +0x0d, +0x10, +0x14, +0x18, +0x24 and +0xfc. A kill planted at any OTHER r==3 offset -- 0x1c, 0x2c, 0x3c ... 0xec -- re-opens a host kill and every row stays green. `kill far` (+0xfc) was added precisely to defeat a GROUP-NARROWING mutant, but it cannot defeat a SINGLE-OFFSET one. Outside the DEPENDS-ON enumeration (adds a predicate), so FILED not fixed. Note the honest bound: this is coverage debt against a detector that is above the vacuity floor, not a floor breach.

**SEVERITY SET MED, 2026-09-07, by the MAIN LOOP** (not a flagship adjudication -- opus5/fable5 are reserved for the 09-09 adjudication, and a rating is exactly the kind of judgment call that seat exists for; overturn it freely).  REASON: a per-offset host kill at an offset NO detector row touches -- a live kill plus a coverage hole in one row.

rows.title: asickillsurvive  #463's four kill rows are SURVIVE-ONLY, so an OOB read returning garbage would score green
rows.witness: none -- the rows exist and pass; this is about what they OBSERVE
rows.state_note: RAISED BY THE FABLE ADJUDICATION (_scratchpad/panel_20260825_020219). `kill word`, `kill byte`, `kill store` and `kill far` compare 'survived' against 'survived' -- they prove LIVENESS but do not check the value returned. A mutant that made an r==3 read return garbage WITHOUT crashing would keep them green. **A disagreement worth recording rather than silently resolving:** the seat called this a witness-ladder violation. The ladder's clause (ii) says *the witness* must carry a liveness control AND a device-signature control, and it does -- `live` and `asic ok` are separate rows doing exactly that. So this is coverage debt, not a ladder breach, and it is filed on that reading. Cheap to close: the rows already issue `print r2`, so the value is captured and unused -- the oracle can become 'survived 0x0' at the cost of re-measuring the table.  *** PROMOTED 2026-08-25: this is not a bare residual, it is WHY A FULL RESEARCH PANEL COULD NOT BE REPLACED BY RE-RUNNING THE GATE. *** The opus5 research seat established the consequence: all four rows touching r==3 offsets (`kill word` +0x0c, `kill byte` +0x0d, `kill store`, `kill far` +0xfc) are SURVIVE-ONLY, and every value-checking row touches only r in {0,1,2}. **Therefore the 13-row detector cannot distinguish the shipped fix from a bare decline, from a decline-plus-latch, or from a latched diagnostic -- all four leave it 13/13.** So 'the detector is green' was NO EVIDENCE AT ALL for the disposition the research stage was asked to review. The detector pins the kill's absence and register distinctness; it pins nothing whatever about reserved-space semantics.

rows.title: asicarray4  sizing the ASIC's four register arrays [4] instead of [3] would de-fang the whole out-of-bounds class
rows.witness: none -- design proposal, not a defect
rows.state_note: RAISED BY THE kimi SEAT on the #463 pass-2 panel (_scratchpad/panel_20260825_020219), via `kimi-k3:cloud` because the kimi CLI is quota-walled -- a DIFFERENT TRANSPORT, recorded as a substitute. The struct declares `pending_irq[3]`, `mask_13[3]`, `mask_11[3]`, `mask_9[3]` consecutively, so `mask_13[4]` IS `mask_11[1]` and any mask widening corrupts a neighbour silently. Padding each to [4] converts that class from CORRUPTION back to mere silent wrongness at a cost of 16 bytes. **The seat was explicit that this is a TRADE, not a fix**, and that framing is the reason to keep it: it does not make a wrong index right, it only stops it reaching another array. Weigh against `asicindexcase`, which it would also partly de-fang.  *** MEASURED AND PARTLY REFUTED 2026-08-25 by the opus5 research seat, which had first FAVOURED this option and then argued against it. *** Sizing the arrays [4] makes the `+1` translation mutant **ESCAPE** `mask9 rt`. The row's kill mechanism is that DEVICE_TICK ERASES `asserted_13` (`d->asserted_13 = ... = 0`, loop bound i<3) and the mask_9 write arm calls the tick immediately -- so at [3] the stored 0xb2 lands on asserted_13, is wiped, and the readback reddens the row. **At [4], index 3 is a real slot the tick never touches, the value survives, and the mutant escapes**: N=3 readback 0x0 (RED, killed) vs N=4 readback 0xb2 (GREEN, ESCAPES). So this option **costs a mutant kill and needs a replacement row before it can ship** -- the original filing ("de-fangs the whole OOB class for 16 bytes") understated its cost and is corrected here. Filing it rather than shipping it was right for a reason the filing did not know.  *** DEAD BY THREE INDEPENDENT ROUTES, which is the strongest refutation this round produced for any alternative. *** (i) agy's phantom-state argument -- it invents hardware that does not exist and leaves the tick loop ignoring the fourth word; (ii) opus5's MEASUREMENT -- it makes the `+1` mutant ESCAPE `mask9 rt`, because that row's kill works by the tick erasing the cell and [4] gives index 3 a real slot the tick never touches; (iii) codex's HARDWARE ORACLE -- Linux's mach-dreamcast IRQ code documents three status words and three per mask group, and KallistiOS exposes exactly +0/+4/+8 with no fourth. **The three-word bound is a HARDWARE FACT, not an implementation choice.** Three seats, three methods, one conclusion -- and note this round holds NO Holly ASIC documentation of its own, so route (iii) is the first external oracle it ever obtained.

rows.title: panelseatlabel  panel.sh reports a 403 quota wall as 'RATE-LIMITED (HTTP 429)' and its tally omits the substitute transport

closure.note: both defects verified discharged against LIVE panel output, not by reading the code

rows.witness: none needed -- both are visible in _scratchpad/panel_20260824_231824/SEATS.txt
rows.state_note:
*** BOTH DEFECTS WERE ALREADY FIXED BY `faffad7` AND THIS ROW SAT OPEN. Verified 2026-08-26 AGAINST LIVE OUTPUT, not by reading the source. *** Today's panel printed:

    *** WALLED / RATE-LIMITED / MISCONFIGURED -- NOT a considered non-answer: kimi
    *** read each seat file for the ACTUAL status; do not assume 429.
    ... the kimi CLI is walled but kimi-k3:cloud ANSWERED -- that seat
        is COVERED by its substitute transport, not lost.

**(1) is discharged**: the label no longer names a status code the script did not observe, and `panel.sh:554-560` carries a comment stating the exact defect this row filed -- a 403 billing-cycle wall printed as `HTTP 429`. **(2) is discharged**: `:565-566` reports a CLI wall with a live substitute as ONE SEAT ANSWERED rather than one lost, which is what the row asked for.

*** THIS IS THE SECOND FIXED-DEFECT-RECORDED-AS-OPEN FOUND TODAY, after `sh4dmacie` (fixed by `f532bb6`, recorded `held` with no commit). *** The cost is not cosmetic: an open row is an offer of work to a fresh session, so a stale one spends a round rediscovering that there is nothing to do -- and it inflates the queue that everything else is prioritised against.

**The check that found it was cheap and is worth repeating: for a tooling row, run the tool and read what it prints.** Reading the source would have worked here too, but running it is faster and cannot be fooled by a fix that was written and never wired -- which is exactly the failure `#465` shipped with its detector.

MEASURED on `_scratchpad/panel_20260824_231824`. Two separate reporting defects in the seat check, neither of which changes a disposition but both of which mislead a later reader. (1) The kimi CLI failed with `provider.auth_error: 403 ... usage limit for this billing cycle` and SEATS.txt printed `*** RATE-LIMITED (HTTP 429)`. The carrier draws a sharp line between failure classes -- a WALL you wait out versus a REFUSED CONNECTION one command fixes -- and a status code named wrongly is how that line gets blurred. (2) It printed `SEATS: 6/7 scriptable` while `ollama_kimi.txt` (17,382 bytes) sat answered in the same directory: the check counts the CLI seat only, so a seat that is walled on one transport and LIVE on another is tallied purely as a loss. That undercounts the panel exactly when the substitution is working. Note the related counting trap the carrier already records: the two Agent seats leave NO FILE, so any file-based count under-reports by two more.  *** THE THREE CLI SEATS HAVE DIFFERENT WRITE BEHAVIOURS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM MAKES A SIZE CHECK MEANINGFUL MID-RUN. Measured 2026-08-25 on the #463 records audit. *** `codex` STREAMS its reasoning, so its file grows continuously and was 311 KB while still working. `grok` streams slowly -- 229 then 357 bytes, each sample a partial sentence. **`agy` writes NOTHING until it finishes**: its file sat at EXACTLY 0 bytes for minutes with a live `agy.exe` (pid 23548), then lands in one shot -- 8,044 bytes on the pass-2 panel. So for agy, and ONLY for agy, a zero-byte file is the normal mid-run state, and it is indistinguishable BY SIZE from the plain-`&` failure the carrier records (where a killed child leaves a zero-byte log). **The discriminator is the PROCESS, not the file**: `tasklist | grep agy` settles it in one command. Note the related trap already recorded -- check `tasklist` WITHOUT `/v`, because `/v` changes the column layout and a follow-up check using it once reported no processes when three were alive, nearly destroying a true positive.  *** AND THE THIRD DEFECT IS IN THE FIX: A WALL-KEYWORD CHECK PRODUCES A FALSE POSITIVE ON ANY SEAT THAT READS THIS LEDGER. Measured 2026-08-25. *** After widening the seat check to catch the quota/403/429/stalled family, it scored a LIVE codex seat as WALLED. The seat was mid-answer at 225 KB and still running; what the check matched was **this project's own prose about walls** -- the rows describing a 403 mislabelled as 429, and the empty-response class -- echoed back by a seat that had been asked to read the ledger. **A keyword detector applied to a document ABOUT that keyword cannot work**, and the tasks most likely to trip it are exactly the records and matrix audits this project now runs routinely. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS POSITION AND TERMINATION, not presence -- which is what the carrier already says (`verify the CONTENT, never the size`) applied one level down: a walled seat's notice is the LAST thing in the file with nothing substantive after it, and the answer either ends mid-sentence or is the echoed brief. A live seat mentions a wall in the middle of a large body of its own reasoning and keeps going. `seat_verdicts.py` already uses a POSITION discriminator for exactly this reason; the seat check should borrow it rather than grep the whole tail. Cheapest interim guard, and it costs one line: **if the process is still alive, it is not walled** -- `tasklist` settles it, and this project has now used that test twice in one session (once to prove a 0-byte agy file was buffering rather than dead).  *** SECOND MEASURED INSTANCE 2026-08-25 (`panel_20260825_112845`), AND THE SECOND DEFECT IS WORSE THAN THIS ROW SAYS -- IT IS NOT A TALLY PROBLEM, IT IS A LOST SEAT. *** Defect (1) reproduced exactly: the kimi CLI returned `provider.auth_error: 403 You've reached your usage limit for this billing cycle` and SEATS.txt printed `*** RATE-LIMITED (HTTP 429)`. Same wrong status code, same blurring of the wall-versus-transport line the carrier draws. *** BUT DEFECT (2) IS NOT MERELY AN UNDERCOUNT. *** This row records that the tally omits a substitute transport that ANSWERED. Measured today: `panel.sh` **never fires the substitute at all**. It launches exactly one kimi seat -- the CLI, at `:222` -- and its three Ollama seats are hardcoded to `$OLLAMA1/2/3` (glm, deepseek, minimax) at `:270/:274/:278`. Meanwhile `curl -s localhost:11434/api/tags` lists **`kimi-k3:cloud` as LIVE**, and three earlier panels (`panel_20260824_191634`, `panel_20260824_231824`, `panel_20260825_000248`) each hold an `ollama_kimi.txt`, so the seat was being fired BY HAND and then stopped being. *** SO THE HONEST STATUS OF THIS SEAT IS NOT "DOWN". *** kimi's CLI transport is walled; kimi itself is reachable and idle. Every panel since the CLI wall has silently run one seat short while a working transport sat unused -- which is the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape with an extra step, because here the roster does not even record a failure to investigate. RECOVERED IMMEDIATELY: the seat was fired by hand onto the live `wdcflood` pass-1 panel dir as `ollama_kimi.txt`. FIX OWED IN panel.sh, deliberately NOT APPLIED YET because panel.sh was RUNNING when this was found and bash reads a script incrementally -- editing a running script is its own defect class. The fix: fire `kimi-k3:cloud` as a fourth Ollama seat, and have the seat check report the CLI wall and the substitute SEPARATELY so a walled transport with a live substitute reads as one seat answered, not as a loss. Also correct `429` to the actual status text rather than a hardcoded code. *** AND THE GENERAL RULE THIS EARNS: WHEN A SEAT WALLS, ASK WHETHER THE MODEL IS REACHABLE BY ANOTHER TRANSPORT BEFORE RECORDING IT DOWN. *** The carrier already separates a wall from a refused connection; this is the third class -- **one transport walled, another live** -- and it is the only one where the seat is available the whole time and nobody asks.

rows.title: seatthinkburn  a FIFTH seat-failure class: an empty response wrapped in 260 KB of thinking, which every size check scores as the panel's best answer
rows.witness: measured -- _scratchpad/panel_20260825_024101_audit/consistency_deepseek-v4-pro_cloud.txt
rows.state_note:
*** TWO MORE INSTANCES 2026-08-26, BACK TO BACK, AND THEY CARRY A CORRELATION THIS ROW DID NOT HAVE: THE BURN TRACKS BRIEF COMPLEXITY, NOT THE SEAT. ***

    panel_20260826_090604    4,032 b   normal answer
    panel_20260826_190055    2,845 b   normal answer
    panel_20260826_222557  142,525 b   BURNED  done_reason=length  eval_count=65536
    panel_20260826_230207  222,981 b   BURNED  done_reason=length  eval_count=65536

**The two burns are on the day's two most COMPLEX briefs** -- one asking it to verify band arithmetic across three separate claims, one asking five questions spanning two rounds. The two clean runs were simpler briefs to the same seat, same transport, same day.

*** THAT REFRAMES THE CLASS. *** The row recorded it as a SEAT property -- something to detect and work around. Today's evidence says it is at least partly a BRIEF property, which is actionable in a way a seat outage is not: **I can shorten the brief.** That matches the carrier's oldest lesson about packet-fed seats -- their behaviour is governed by the brief, and this project once spent DAYS misdiagnosing a brief defect as a seat outage.

**AND THE SECOND BURN SHOWS WHAT IS BEING LOST, which the first instance could not.** Its output ends mid-sentence: *'So verdict likely NOT RATIFY due to #467. But maybe the question is from a panel'* -- **it had REACHED a verdict and was second-guessing itself when the budget ran out.** That is a substantive dissent destroyed by a token limit, not a seat with nothing to say. On that same panel the other dissenting seat found a LIVE DEFECT, so a lost dissent here is not hypothetical cost.

**DETECTION IS ALREADY SOLVED AND SHOULD NOT BE RE-ARGUED:** `seat_verdicts.py` reports these as `SEAT DOWN -- spent its whole budget on hidden reasoning (length, N tokens)`, by reading `done_reason` rather than size. Both of today's burns were caught and named correctly.

**WHAT IS STILL OWED is the MITIGATION, and it is now cheap to state:** keep a packet-fed brief to ONE question with the facts inlined, rather than a multi-part audit. Splitting a complex brief across two firings costs one extra invocation and preserves the answer.

MEASURED 2026-08-25 on the #463 consistency audit. `deepseek-v4-pro:cloud` returned **`"response": ""` -- completely empty -- inside a 265,845-byte JSON object whose `thinking` field is 260,678 bytes, with `done_reason: 'length'` and `eval_count: 65536`. It spent its ENTIRE output budget on hidden reasoning and never emitted an answer. *** IT IS DISTINCT FROM ALL FOUR RECORDED CLASSES. *** Not a WALL (no quota text, no 403/429). Not the ECHO-ONLY shape (it echoes nothing). Not a REFUSED CONNECTION (the daemon served it fine, for 267 seconds). Not the shared-transport outage (the other three cloud seats answered normally in the same firing). *** AND IT DEFEATS EVERY SIZE-BASED CHECK IN THE WORST DIRECTION: at 265 KB it is the LARGEST file in its panel and would be scored the best answer. *** The carrier already warns 'verify the CONTENT, never the size; the failure mode is a big file' -- this is that lesson in a new variant, where the bulk is not an echoed brief but the model's own reasoning. **It was diagnosable only by accident**: `panel_ollama.py` does `body = resp.get('response') or json.dumps(resp)`, so an empty response falls back to dumping the raw JSON. Had it written the empty string, the file would have been 0 bytes and indistinguishable from a transport failure. That fallback should be made deliberate, and documented as the thing that preserves the diagnosis. THE FIX, and it is cheap: the seat check must parse any Ollama output that starts with `{`, and report SEAT DOWN when `response` is empty -- naming `done_reason` and `eval_count`, because `length` says 'budget exhausted' while `stop` would say something else entirely. A working checker exists (used to produce this row) and needs wiring into `panel.sh` and `seat_verdicts.py`. CONTRIBUTING CAUSE worth recording separately: the brief was the ENTIRE 18 KB round-block draft. The carrier's rule is to INLINE every fact for packet-fed seats, and that rule is sound -- but inlining an 18 KB artifact and asking for exhaustive cross-checking gives a thinking model enough to reason itself past its own budget. **Inline the facts; do not inline an entire document and ask for an audit of it.**  *** AND A SIXTH CLASS, MEASURED THE SAME SESSION on the matrix-review panel: THE SEAT'S OWN TRANSPORT DIED MID-ANSWER. *** `agy` returned 293 bytes reading `I have launched the topic cluster analysis script ... Waiting for background script completion.` followed by `Error: the connection to the agent was interrupted before the response finished: subscriber fell behind updates, stalled for 6s`. It is none of the five: no quota text (not a wall), it connected and worked for minutes (not a refused connection), it echoed nothing, it emitted a real partial answer rather than an empty response inside vast thinking, and the other seats on the same panel were unaffected (not the shared-Agent-tool outage). **The distinguishing shape: the seat DELEGATED to a background script and its own streaming connection dropped while it waited.** Two consequences. (1) The keyword set every seat check in this project uses -- quota / rate limit / balance / 403 / 429 / refused -- does NOT contain `interrupted`, `stalled`, or `subscriber fell behind`, so this scored as `answered`. Widened. (2) **It is worth RE-FIRING, unlike a wall**: a wall is the provider refusing and you wait it out; this is a dropped connection and the work simply did not survive. The re-fire rule the carrier already states for walled seats applies here with better odds.  *** THE CONTRIBUTING CAUSE THIS ROW FILED WAS MEASURED FALSE THE SAME SESSION. *** It said the trigger was inlining an entire 18 KB document and asking for an exhaustive audit of it, and prescribed 'inline the facts; do not inline a document'. **A SECOND burn then happened on a brief a fraction of that size** -- 11 ledger rows, truncated narratives, ~10 KB -- with the identical signature: `response: ""`, `done_reason: 'length'`, `eval_count: 65536`, and 275,778 bytes of `thinking`. Larger thinking than the first burn, on a much smaller brief. **So SIZE IS NOT THE CAUSE**, and the prescription derived from it was wrong. What the two share is the TASK SHAPE, not the input size: both asked for an EXHAUSTIVE PER-ITEM AUDIT with several independent sub-questions per item (four categories over a document; four questions over each of eleven rows). The seat answered a 6.5 KB pass-2 REVIEW brief normally in the same session -- one subject, one set of questions. **The working hypothesis is now COMBINATORIAL: N items x M orthogonal questions, where the seat appears to explore the cross-product before emitting anything.** That is a hypothesis, not a measurement, and it is recorded as such -- the honest state is that the cause is NOT ESTABLISHED and the first stated cause is REFUTED. OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, which does not depend on the cause: **deepseek is unreliable for per-item audit tasks and reliable for single-subject review**, so route it accordingly rather than by brief size. And the detection rule is unchanged and now doubly warranted: parse the JSON, report SEAT DOWN on an empty `response`, and never score by file size -- both burns produced the LARGEST file in their panel.  *** AND THE TEST THAT LOOKED LIKE A CONFIRMATION IS CONFOUNDED -- CORRECTED IMMEDIATELY RATHER THAN LEFT STANDING. *** deepseek ANSWERED a #463 research-stage brief cleanly (1,724 bytes, a real dissent) after burning on two audits, and that was momentarily reported as confirming the task-shape hypothesis over the size hypothesis. **It confirms nothing.** The brief was 3,614 bytes -- SMALLER than both that burned it (19,395 and 10,408) -- so it varies BOTH suspected causes at once and cannot discriminate between them. The honest state of the evidence: burns at 19,395 (per-item audit) and 10,408 (per-item audit); clean answers at 8,583 (single-subject review) and 3,614 (single-subject research). **Size and shape are perfectly correlated across all four data points**, so nothing here separates them. A discriminating test exists and is cheap -- a LARGE single-subject brief, or a SMALL per-item one -- and until someone runs it the cause remains NOT ESTABLISHED. *Recorded because the first stated cause was already refuted once; a second unearned cause would be the same defect with better manners.*

**RESIDUAL-REMAINS.**  `a4d054d` recorded occurrences and brief mitigation, and recognition of the
empty-response signature already existed before it.  **Exhausting the reasoning budget remains an
operational failure; shortening briefs is mitigation with no demonstrated general prevention.**

rows.title: scoreclaimhex  check_score_claims reads a slash-separated HEX LIST as a score claim, and reports a stale score that was never written

closure.note: author self-review disclosed; negative-controlled both directions and coverage verified not to shrink

rows.witness: measured -- _scratchpad/precommit_463.log, section U, three FAIL lines
rows.state_note:
*** THE FIX IS IN THIS COMMIT; THE ROW CLOSES IN THE NEXT ONE WITH THE REAL HASH. *** Section L correctly refused a `PENDING` placeholder -- a closed row must name a hash, and the hash does not exist until the commit lands. That is the documented two-step, not a defect.

*** FIXED 2026-08-26: one character, `x` added to the negative lookbehind. *** `check_score_claims.py` now reads `(?<![\dx/])(\d+)\s*/\s*(\d+)(?![\d/%])`. The `00` in `0x00/0x10` is preceded by `x`, which the old `(?<![\d/])` allowed, so a slash-separated HEX LIST parsed as a score claim.

**NEGATIVE-CONTROLLED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS BEFORE LANDING, which is the whole discipline for a regex change:** five real score claims (13/13, 26/26, 8/32, "52 / 52", 16/16) all still match; two hex lists no longer do; zero regressions.

**AND MEASURED ON THE FILE THAT PRODUCED THE ORIGINAL FALSE FAIL** rather than on synthetic strings: over the whole of `asic_badaddr_probe.py` the old regex found 11 matches and the new one finds 7. **The four killed are `04/4`, `08/4`, `10/4`, `18/4` -- every one a fragment of a hex offset. The kept are `12/12` and `12/13` -- every real claim, intact.**

*** COVERAGE VERIFIED NOT TO HAVE SHRUNK, because 'the false positive is gone' and 'the checker stopped looking' produce the same output: *** the gate still carries 12 rows naming the probe, the checker still reports SCORE_CLAIMS_PASS over 19 pinned probes, and the docstring still yields its 5 genuine `12/13` claims under BOTH regexes. A fix that silently drops a probe from coverage would have read as success.

*The row's own diagnosis was correct and complete; nothing in it needed revising. Worth noting because most rows worked today needed their evidence corrected -- this one was filed right the first time.*

MEASURED 2026-08-25 during #463's pre-commit. Section U reported THREE stale score claims in `asic_badaddr_probe.py`'s docstring -- `claims 00/0`, `10/0`, `20/0`, pin is 12. **None of them was ever written.** All three come from ONE line of ordinary prose: `bases 0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30`, a slash-separated list of hex group bases. The pattern `(?<![\d/])(\d+)\s*/\s*(\d+)(?![\d/%])` sees `0x00/0x10` and takes `00` / `0`. *** IT IS A FALSE FAIL, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE FAILURE FROM THE ONE SECTION U EXISTS TO CATCH, AND IS STILL EXPENSIVE. *** A gate that reddens on prose trains its reader to explain away red rows, which is exactly how a REAL stale score would then get waved through. And this project writes `0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30` constantly -- the fourth-word invariant is naturally expressed that way -- so it will recur in any file section U checks. WORKED AROUND, NOT FIXED, and deliberately: #463 reworded its own docstring to use commas, because the round's material is unshipped (L1) while `check_score_claims.py` is a shared gate and editing it is a different scope. **The workaround is also the weaker fix** -- it relies on every future author avoiding a natural notation. THE REAL FIX is one lookbehind: reject a match whose left digit run is preceded by `0x` or `0X`, i.e. require the numerator not be part of a hex literal. Note the existing escape hatch (`write '<N>-row' on the same line`) does NOT help here, because the denominator the checker invented is 0 and nobody would write `0-row`.

rows.state_note:
*** DO NOT CLOSE THIS ROW ON THE EXISTENCE OF `state_semantics`.  I ALMOST DID, 2026-08-29. ***

The block is written, all five observed states are documented (`closed`/`held`/`open`/
`in work`/`dropped` -- census run 2026-08-29, 270 rows, none undocumented), and `_ADOPTED`
says the owner ratified it on 2026-08-25 with both amendments.  **That is the SEMANTICS half
and it IS discharged.**  It is also the visible half, which is why it reads like the whole row.

**The row's own `hold` names the other half: ~50 mis-stated instances across five classes,
and it is ITS OWN RECORDS-CORRECTION ROUND** -- which additionally owes the standing second
review pass, because corrections repeat the errors they correct.  None of that is done.

So the state is right and the row is easy to misread as finished.  Recorded here because the
cheapest defence against a wrong closure is a sentence at the place the closure gets made.

PASS-1 PANEL: `_scratchpad/panel_20260825_030653_matrix`. SIX SEATS FIRED, FIVE ANSWERED, ONE DOWN. grok, codex, minimax-m3, kimi-k3:cloud and glm-5.2 answered; **agy FAILED on a SIXTH seat-failure class -- its own streaming transport dropped mid-answer** (`connection to the agent was interrupted ... subscriber fell behind updates, stalled for 6s`) -- and was re-fired, since a dropped connection is worth retrying where a wall is not. *** grok's verdict is the headline: DO NOT TRUST STATES. *** THE FINDINGS, by class. (1) STATE CONTRADICTS SUBSTANCE: `pitlatch` and `pitclobber` sit `in work` while every closure note says CLOSE and the residual their hold names is already discharged by a CLOSED carrier; `hpcshcpu` is `open` while its own note says DROP FROM THE ACTIONABLE QUEUE; `m8invpred` is `held` behind a codex wall discharged 2026-08-20; `reprowitness` is `in work` although the witness ladder it produced has been in the carrier since 2026-08-19; `gdromdmawidth` is `open` while admitting shipped code carries a comment under its name. (2) *** THE BURIAL SHAPE, TEXTBOOK FORM: `b115` and `b126` EACH CARRY TWO INDEPENDENT DEFECTS UNDER ONE ID. *** Closing either on one defect buries the other -- the exact hazard the carrier records. This is the highest-severity finding here. (3) STALE BLOCKERS: `gdromdmawidth` waits on `sh4gdromexit`, a carrier that will never do the work attributed to it. (4) UNEVIDENCED CLOSES: `rtcdet`, `gdromdmadefault`, `witnessinvisible` close asserting shipped substance with no commits; `b75` is a contested close with no recorded adjudication; `fbwitness` closes with an absent witness while its title claims a probe. (5) A CORRECTION THAT DID NOT PROPAGATE: a measured 4x inflation was corrected in `arcbiosubsan` and never in `sgiarcbiosoob`, which still asserts it -- mechanical rule 2 (grep for a claim's SIBLINGS before calling it fixed) failing in the ledger itself. *** AND A WARNING FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS ROUND, because the round that filed it got this wrong THREE TIMES: THE LEDGER HAS MULTIPLE SCHEMA ERAS AND A CHECKER THAT KNOWS ONE ERA INVENTS ANOMALIES. *** (a) Narrative lives in `entries` on 198 older rows and `state_note` on 19 newer ones; counting only the latter reported 191 rows with no narrative when the true number is ZERO. (b) `witness` is FORWARD-ONLY from 2026-08-19 (`CLAUDE.md:1191`), so of 16 closed-without-witness rows FOURTEEN are compliant and only `rtcdet` and `fbwitness` are owed. (c) `closure.by` postdates part of the ledger. (d) 'open/held WITH commits' looked like 16 anomalies and is ZERO -- all sixteen carry a HOLD marker, which is the normal batching state by design. **Establish the validity rule for each class BEFORE touching a cell, and print a denominator beside every count.**  *** THE SCOPE WAS MEASURED AND IT IS 12 ROWS, NOT ~50. The ~50 figure this row was FILED with was my own, and it was wrong for the FIFTH time in one session, by the same mechanism every previous time. *** Establishing each class's validity rule BEFORE counting -- which is what the adjudication demanded -- collapses the raw counts hard: A closed-without-witness 16 raw -> **2** (14 predate the 2026-08-19 forward-only cutoff and are COMPLIANT); B closed-without-commits 6 raw -> **3** (three are withdrawn / not-a-bug / documented-only); C open-or-held-with-commits 17 raw -> **1** (fifteen carry a HOLD, the normal batching state, and one was `asicbadaddr` itself, closed when #463 committed); D closed-without-closure.by 2 raw -> **2**; E state-contradicts-closure 30 raw -> **5**. *** RULE 5, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT COST THE MOST: `closure.note` MAY DISPOSE OF A STAGE, NOT THE ROW. *** The ledger defines four `phase_labels` -- assess, research, review, regress -- so `CLOSE (assess)` closes the ASSESS STAGE and the row legitimately stays `held`. TWENTY-FIVE of class E's thirty are that shape; `exitsweep`'s own hold says so out loud (*"CLOSURE REVERTED ... the fable5 batch answered this row's held stage"*). Reading a stage-scoped disposition as a row-scoped one manufactured 25 false defects. THE TWELVE THAT SURVIVE: rtcdet, fbwitness, gdromdmadefault, witnessinvisible, gdromdmawidth, gate3scope, m437ord, m8invpred, ledgerwitness, cmtattr, hpcshcpu -- plus this row. Note the convergence worth trusting: `fbwitness`, `rtcdet`, `gdromdmadefault` and `witnessinvisible` were named INDEPENDENTLY by the reading seats AND fall out of the mechanical census, which is the only kind of agreement that counts here.  RECONCILIATION, demanded by the adjudicator before either number may be quoted: the class column sums to **13 instances** and the repair set is **11 rows**. 13 - 1 dedup (`fbwitness` is in BOTH closed-no-witness and closed-no-commits) - 1 self (`ledgerstatelies` is this tracking row) = 11. Both numbers are correct; the arithmetic was simply never shown, which made the correction READ as contradicting its own column -- **a sixth counting defect sitting inside the correction that reports the fifth.**  *** THE ROUND'S CENTRAL FINDING, MEASURED, AND IT IS NOT WHAT EITHER SEAT CLAIMED: `state` IS NOT DERIVABLE FROM THE RECORD. *** Two file-reading seats disagreed on `fbwitness` -- one said `CLOSE (assess)` disposes of a STAGE so the row must be `held`, the other said it retires the assessment so `closed` is fine. Settled empirically rather than by vote, and BOTH inferences are unsupported: **23 rows carry the IDENTICAL `closure.note` of `CLOSE (assess)` and they are spread across THREE states -- 12 `held`, 7 `in work`, 4 `closed`** (the closed four being ns16550, fablequeue, carrier, fbwitness). The obvious second hypothesis was tested and also fails: the number of STAGES with recorded entries is statistically identical across the three groups (mean 1.8 / 1.8 / 1.9, same min and max), so stage coverage does not explain the split either. **`state` and `closure.note` are independent fields with no enforced relationship**, so a reader cannot derive one from the other and neither can a checker. That is why 'DO NOT TRUST STATES' is the correct verdict, and it reframes this round: **the repair cannot be a mechanical rewrite of 11 cells, because there is no rule to rewrite them TO.** The round must first establish what `state` MEANS -- most plausibly 'is there work outstanding on this row', which is a different question from 'has any stage been adjudicated' -- and only then repair. ALSO REFUTED HERE, and worth keeping because it was checkable in two minutes: the claim that `fbwitness` is ALONE among its 2026-08-20 cohort in being closed. That cohort is 84 rows -- 17 closed, 43 held, 11 dropped, 13 in work -- and four of the closed share `fbwitness`'s exact closure string. A seat's argument from 'this row is the only one' is worth checking every time; this one was wrong.  *** FIVE SEATS, ELEVEN ROWS, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS THE EVIDENCE RATHER THAN THE NOISE. *** agy, kimi-k3, glm-5.2, minimax-m3 and grok each assigned a correct state to all eleven rows, reading the same ledger under the same four validity rules stated in the brief. **They agree on only 4 of 11.** `hpcshcpu` drew THREE different answers (closed / dropped / held); six more drew two. This is what a field with no derivable meaning looks like from the outside: competent independent readers do not converge, because there is nothing to converge ON. *** IT ALSO PARTITIONS THE ROUND CLEANLY, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART. *** **UNANIMOUS (4) -- and all four are ALREADY IN THE RIGHT STATE**: `gdromdmadefault` and `witnessinvisible` (closed, missing `commits`), `m437ord` (closed, missing `closure.by`), `cmtattr` (held, correct as-is). What these need is FIELDS, not state changes, and a field that is absent is absent under any definition of `state` -- so they are repairable NOW, independently of the rule question. **SPLIT (7)**: rtcdet, fbwitness, gdromdmawidth, gate3scope, m8invpred, ledgerwitness, hpcshcpu. Every one of these turns on what `state` MEANS, and none can be repaired until that is settled -- editing them now would be manufacturing the appearance of correctness by picking whichever seat I found most persuasive. **THE SPLIT IS ALSO A CHECK ON THE 23-ROW FINDING**, arrived at from the opposite direction: that one measured one closure string against three states; this one measures five readers against one row set. Both say the same thing and neither depends on the other's method.  *** ADJUDICATED 2026-08-25, AND IT REFRAMED THE ROUND WHILE CONVICTING ME OF ONE OVERREACH. *** The ruling: `state` and `closure.note` are different TENSES. The note is a PAST-TENSE event log of what happened to a STAGE; `state` is a PRESENT-TENSE assertion of what the ROW still OWES. **Under that reading the multi-state spread of one closure string is the ledger WORKING AS DESIGNED, not the defect** -- rows that experienced the same stage event legitimately differ in what else they owe -- and the stage-coverage test failing is CORROBORATION rather than a second mystery, because state depends on what REMAINS, not on how much happened. **SO THE THING TO FILE IS THE MISSING SCHEMA SEMANTICS, NOT THE SPREAD.** That single absence is the cause behind six mis-counts in one session, two seats inferring opposite conventions from one string, and five seats agreeing on only 4 of 11 rows. The fix is written: a `state_semantics` block now sits in the ledger's own schema, PENDING OWNER RATIFICATION, forward-only in the same way `witness` was. *** MY OVERREACH, RETRACTED IN PLACE: I wrote that 'for most of the 11 there is no fact of the matter to restore -- only a decision'. THAT IS FALSE AND IT WAS CONVENIENT FOR ME*** -- it converts eleven tedious substance reads into one interesting rule question. What died was a repair METHOD (derive state from the note), not the fact of the matter, which is read from commits, gates, holds and filed questions -- exactly how `asicbadaddr` was closed, with no note convention needed. **The seminar is over in one paragraph; the eleven reads remain owed.** *** AND NO NUMBER IN THIS ROW MAY BE QUOTED AS A PREMISE UNTIL A SECOND PARTY CHECKS IT. *** I have mis-counted this ledger six times in one session. Every ruling above depends on the EXISTENCE of the spread, not its size -- ONE held row and ONE closed row sharing a closure string already prove non-derivability -- so the whole second-party check is two greps. The figures 23, 84 and the 1.8/1.8/1.9 stage means are UNVERIFIED SUPPORTING COLOUR, labelled as such, and are leads rather than premises.  *** A SEVENTH COUNTING HAZARD, FOUND BY MAKING IT: SEAT NAMES ARE NOT SEAT ANSWERS. *** While closing #463's stages I reported research at 9/9; it was 8/9. The `codex` entry on that stage is a **`[HELD AWAITING SEAT:` MARKER** -- a record that the seat is OUTSTANDING -- and I counted it because I counted seat NAMES. `check_stage_panels.py` excludes marker entries deliberately, and its own comment says exactly why: *'otherwise marking a gap would close it.'* **Writing down that a seat is missing would, under a name-count, make the stage look complete** -- the seat-failure-as-agreement shape in its purest mechanical form. **THE LEDGER CARRIES 44 SUCH MARKER ENTRIES**, each one a seat that has NOT answered. Any future census of panel coverage that counts names rather than answers over-reports by up to that much. Three marker tokens exist and all three must be excluded: `[HELD AWAITING SEAT:`, `[NOT A PANEL STAGE: SINGLE-SEAT RE-READ]`, and `[RUN UNDER THE PRE-2026-08-16 POLICY]`. *This belongs with the schema-semantics finding rather than beside it: `entries` is not a list of answers, it is a list of EVENTS, and some events record an absence. That is the same present-tense/past-tense confusion that `state` and `closure.note` embody, one level down.*  *** A NEW INSTANCE OF THIS ROW'S OWN DEFECT, FOUND 2026-08-25 BY THE ADJUDICATOR TRIPPING OVER IT WHILE ADJUDICATING THIS VERY BLOCK. *** Asked to rule on the queue, the fable5 seat reported that `idesync` "is already closed as document-do-not-fix". The ledger says `state = "in work"` with `commits` EMPTY. Both readings are half right, and the shape is new: *** THE DISPOSITION IS SETTLED BUT THE DOCUMENT HAS NOT SHIPPED. *** The row carries an opus5 REVIEW verdict (2026-08-20) of DOCUMENT-DO-NOT-FIX on a deciding fact nobody else raised -- the drive never advertises FLUSH CACHE, so the highest IDENTIFY word written never sets it -- plus a closed assess stage (`closure.by = fable5`, `CLOSE (assess)`). A SUBSTANCE reader therefore sees a finished decision and says "closed"; a STATE reader sees no commits and says "unfinished". Under the semantics now written, `closed` means discharged BY WORK, and a documenting commit IS work that has not happened -- so the state field is RIGHT and the adjudicator was WRONG, while the adjudicator was right about the only thing anyone would act on. *** THE LESSON IS THAT `document-do-not-fix` NEEDS ITS OWN DISCHARGE, AND NOTHING TRACKS IT. *** A row in this state is invisible to both readings: it looks decided to anyone reading the verdict and claimed to anyone reading the state, so nobody ships the document. That is an UNDISCHARGED OBLIGATION with no carrier -- the class section I of precommit exists for, one field over. Candidate fix, NOT applied pending ratification: `closed` requires either a commit or an explicit `documented-only` closure badge, so an assessed-not-changed record cannot close without the record existing. The project's ethos already demands honest 'assessed, not changed' records; what is missing is anything that NOTICES when one was promised and never written.
