entries.note:
VERDICT: **(1) OPTION C WAS NOT WRONGLY DISMISSED, AND MY QUESTION WAS MIS-POSED.
(2) OPTION F STAYS FILED, with two named promotion triggers.  (3) NO rung-3 ask was
made or recorded -- a one-line records debt.**  Evidence basis: 7 of 9 mandated seats;
opus5 still owed, so this ruling is PROVISIONAL on its face.

*** FOUR ERRORS FOUND IN MY OWN FRAMING, and the third is a live records defect. ***

**(i) THE (1) PREMISE IS FALSE.**  I wrote that #477's read-arm repair 'did a phase-scoped
version of exactly' option C.  It did the OPPOSITE.  C truncates the flag's LIFETIME; the
repair phase-scopes ONE READER and deliberately leaves the stale state in place.  Different
state object (the len/received pair, not the flag), opposite mechanism.  The shipped code's
own comment says so: *"that leaves this window untouched (the flag is legitimately 1 here)"*.
C is orthogonal to the window this row reproduces -- the defect fires MID-DATAIN, before any
completion event, so no clear-at-completion rule can reach it.  C also breaks the ATAPI
handshake at four verified register-read sites.  **The tree converged on the ANTI-C, twice.**

**(ii) 'THREE GUARDS' IS AN UNDERCOUNT -- IT IS FIVE, AND THE TWO I MISSED ARE THE STRONGEST
EVIDENCE FOR MY OWN ARGUMENT.**  Four dispatch conjuncts plus the read-arm scope.  Four of the
five exist to compensate for shared-ring aliasing, and two have measured catastrophic
weakenings (M_phaseonly swept 52 rows and destroyed a sector; M7_ge12 is a heap overflow
invisible to 44 rows).  So the structural argument has measured teeth -- but a GUARD CENSUS IS
NOT A MEASURED DELTA, which is why F is round-eligible and still correctly ranked below live
defects.

**(iii) 'A SEAT MEASURED F's MIGRATION COST' IS AN UNARTIFACTED OVERCLAIM, AND IT WAS
ECHOING.**  No build, no table, no log anywhere.  It was a READ.  Worse, it originated in
OUTSTANDING_BUGS, I inlined it into two briefs, and codex quoted the diff back -- so five
artifacts now carry the word 'measured' and a future grep reads independent confirmation.
**CORRECTED IN PLACE the same hour** (OUTSTANDING_BUGS, the `wdccdbaccum` residual), including
the content: the accept side ports nearly as-is, and the reject rows go TARGET-DEAD owing
case-2 absence records rather than 'stopping working'.  Migration and target-death are
different dispositions.  The real cost is a re-cut plus a full re-table -- a STRONGER argument
for filing than the wrong one was.

**(iv) THIS ROW HAS A SECOND HOLD AND I DID NOT SEE IT.**  Beyond the research stage, a
regress-phase hold carries its own unanswered rule question -- *which panel discharges a row:
its own stage, or the fixing round's?* -- and that was NOT among today's three adjudications.
**Even at 9/9 research this row stays held until that is ruled.**

THE TWO PROMOTION TRIGGERS FOR F, both mechanical so no future round re-argues this:
  * **(a) THE SIXTH-GUARD TRIGGER** -- the first time a MEASURED LIVE defect's fix would add
    another dispatch predicate or another phase-scoped consumer guard, ship F instead.  At that
    point the accumulated deltas ARE the measured warrant.
  * **(b) THE DATAOUT TRIGGER** -- when DATAOUT payload support lands, F ships as its enabling
    structure.  Implementing DATAOUT into the shared ring would create the aliasing a THIRD time.

F's contract, if it ever ships: three classes become unrepresentable -- the `==12` occupancy
collision, the `>= 12` heap overflow, and wdcringnoflush's CDB-drop consequence.  An F round

the pipeline**: it gets no seat coverage tracking, no stage panel, no dashboard line, and
section H never asks whether it ran a panel.  *A row that exists only in prose is filed in
the sense that a reader could find it and unfiled in every sense a tool cares about.*

exists to act on records cannot see it.

row-id tokens (the backticked ``id`` convention already used), and fail when one names
no ledger row.  **Dated-cutoff and forward-only**, like `check_bugfile_sync.py` itself: a
rule that retro-fails the whole file blocks the next commit on reconstruction nobody
scheduled, and a rule that does that gets switched off.

rows.state_note:
*** DID `#476` CLOSE THE CLASS OR ONE INSTANCE?  ENUMERATED 2026-08-27, and the answer is
THE CLASS -- but the enumeration is the point, not the answer. ***

`#475` taught that repairing a counter can WAKE DEAD CODE, so fixing one dereference proves
nothing about the others.  All nine derefs of `atapi_st` in the file, with their protection:

```
  :812  atapi_received < atapi_st->data_in_len   <- the #476 site, NOW GUARDED
  :877  atapi_len = atapi_st->data_in_len - ..   <- nested inside :812's true arm
  :884  wdc_addtoinbuf(.. atapi_st->data_in[..]) <- same block
  :1033 atapi_st->cmd = scsi_cmd                 <- immediately after the alloc
  :1034 atapi_st->cmd_len = 12                       at :1023
  :1039 atapi_st->cmd_len = 10
  :1072 if (atapi_st->data_in != NULL)
  :1082 atapi_len = atapi_st->data_in_len
  :1087 wdc_addtoinbuf(.. atapi_st->data_in[j])
```

**The first three are the reachable family and all three are inside the arm `#476` guards**
-- `:812` runs only when `atapi_len == 0 && atapi_st != NULL`, and `:877`/`:884` are nested
within its true branch.

**The remaining six sit after `scsi_transfer_alloc()`, WHICH CANNOT RETURN NULL** -- verified
by opening it: on malloc failure it prints and `exit(1)`s.  (That exit is a separate,
pre-existing, OOM-only concern and is not guest-reachable.)

*Worth noting for anyone reasoning about the free: `scsi_transfer_alloc` runs a FREELIST, so
a fresh alloc typically REUSES the just-freed chunk.  That is why a pointer-identity oracle
reads a false negative on a plain build and only separates under a sanitiser's quarantine --
a seat measured exactly that.*

**So no second host kill of this family is in the tree.**  Recorded as an enumeration a
reader can re-derive rather than as an assurance.

*** A REGRESSION I SHIPPED, FOUND BY THE MEASURING SEAT ONE COMMIT LATER, FIXED THE SAME
HOUR.  2026-08-27. ***

```
  d894e35 (before #475)   a DATA read with no transfer survives   exit 0
  d64a1fc (with #475)     a DATA read with no transfer survives   host killed, signal 11
```

**THE MECHANISM IS ENTIRELY #475's.**  Before it, a data-port read with `atapi_len` already
0 drove the counter NEGATIVE, so `if (atapi_len == 0)` never fired again and the
`d->atapi_st->data_in_len` deref on the next line was **dead code**.  The clamp makes
`atapi_len` STAY 0.  The test fires.  `atapi_st` is NULL.

> **A FIX THAT STOPS A COUNTER GOING NEGATIVE CAN MAKE A PREVIOUSLY-UNREACHABLE BRANCH
> REACHABLE.**  The clamp was right; the branch it woke was never NULL-safe.  *Repairing a
> counter can enable code that was only ever protected by the broken value* -- and nothing
> in `#475`'s own kill table could see it, because every mutant there attacked the clamp
> rather than what the clamp let through.

MEASURED `SIGSEGV at address 0x48` = `offsetof(struct scsi_transfer, data_in_len)`.  Two
guest register accesses from a fresh device: write ATAPI_PKT_CMD to COMMAND, then read
DATA.  The seat's control -- the same command with NO data read -- survives on both blobs,
so it is the READ.

**THE BISECT IS UNAMBIGUOUS AND PLEASINGLY SYMMETRIC:** on the same pair of builds, the row
for the defect `#475` FIXED goes one way and the row for the defect it CREATED goes the
other.

**FIXED** by declining with the file's own latch idiom -- a device that cannot service an
access must not take the emulator with it, which is the `#337`/`#184`/`#186`/`#315`/`#316`/
`#326` class this fork has spent many rounds closing and which I had just reopened.

*The row FORKS: the defect is a SIGNAL, and an in-process oracle would take the differential
down with it and report nothing at all.*

rows.title: wdccdbaccum  give the ATAPI CDB its own accumulator, as dev_mb89352.c does, instead of trigger-matching on a SHARED ring occupancy
rows.witness: none -- structural, filed from two seats' reading of the in-tree precedent.
rows.state_note:
Filed by `#477`, which shipped the point-fix (phase-guard the dispatch) rather than this.

**THE ALIASING IS THE ROOT.**  `inbuf_len == 12` is a SHARED-RING trigger: it cannot tell CDB
bytes from DATA-IN payload from disk-write payload.  Every candidate fix considered in that
round -- guard the push, guard the dispatch, clear the flag, guard the free -- is a patch over
that ambiguity.

**THE IN-TREE ANSWER, verified by opening it:** `dev_mb89352.c` switches on `d->phase` to
SELECT A DESTINATION BUFFER (`PH_DATAOUT` -> `data_out`, `PH_CMD` -> `cmd`) with a declining
`default:`, and its dispatch trigger is **`transfer_bufpos >= len`** -- *this phase's own
buffer is full* -- never a shared count.

So: `unsigned char cdb[12]; int cdb_pos;` filled only in `PHASE_CMDOUT`, dispatching on
`cdb_pos == 12`.

**COST, MEASURED BY A SEAT RATHER THAN GUESSED:** with the fix in place it still reds two
existing rows, because they hand-fill the ring with `wdc_addtoinbuf()` to fake a CDB.  **It
relocates where a CDB lives, so every probe that fakes one stops working.**  That is the
migration cost, and it is why the round shipped B.

*One caution against copying `dev_mb89352` wholesale: its `default:` arms set
`cpu->running = 0`.  Transfer the SHAPE, never the halt -- removing exactly that from this
file is what `#337` was for.*

rows.title: wdcaltfixture  every alt-ctrl row runs in a state NO REAL DRIVER IS EVER IN, so eleven single-field qualifications escape the whole file
rows.witness: none -- filed from a MEASURED escape set, no fix work done yet.
rows.state_note:
*** FILED BY `#483` FROM ELEVEN MEASURED ESCAPES, AND AS **ONE** ITEM WITH A ONE-ROW
REMEDY -- NOT AS ELEVEN ROWS. ***

`altctl_fresh()` memsets the device struct, so EVERY predicate that is true at zero
escapes every altctl row in `diff_wdc_identify.c`.  `&& !d->lba` is the exemplar the
seats measured; it is NOT the item.  Eleven single-field qualifications were built and
all eleven swept the file clean.

**THE HONEST BOUND, and it is what stops this becoming `#392`:** a guard can be added on
any of ~40 struct fields, so the enumeration is unbounded and chasing members is the
wrong shape.  The principled scope is THE FIELDS A REAL DRIVER SETS IN ORDINARY
OPERATION -- and the finding is that today every altctl row runs in a state no real
driver is ever in, which is a property of the FIXTURE, not of any one guard.

Remedy shape: one row that drives the device through a realistic prologue (a command
issued, LBA/head/sector registers written as a driver writes them) before the control
write, so a qualification on any driver-set field reddens.  Cost is one row and no new
oracle; it needs no `scsi_transfer_alloc()`, which is the boundary that would have made
it expensive.

rows.title: wdcaltwidth  the alt-ctrl register's ACCESS WIDTH is unpinned: every row uses len == 1 while the region is registered TWO bytes wide
rows.witness: none -- filed from a reading of the registration, no measurement yet.
rows.state_note:
*** FILED BY `#483`. ***  `wdc_altstatus` is registered with LENGTH 2 (pristine
upstream), and its handler consults NEITHER `relative_addr` NOR `len`.  Every one of the
103 rows in `diff_wdc_identify.c` calls it with `len == 1` at offset 0.

So two decode questions are unpinned by construction: what a 2-byte store does, and what
a store at `+1` does.  Both are inside the region the model claims.

Sibling of `wdcwidthmatrix`, which records the same gap for the DATA port -- the two
MAY be one round under the round-scope rule (same device, same semantic class, same
detector, no new oracle), but that is a claim to CHECK before acting, not an assumption:
they are different registers with different handlers, and `wdcwidthmatrix` already has
measured coverage at widths 4 and 2 while this has none at all.

entries.ev: direct reading of wdc_flood_probe.py and dev_wdc.c
entries.note:
*** THE 'SPEED NOT CORRECTNESS' CLAIM BELOW NEEDS A QUALIFIER AND IS CORRECTED HERE (L4, same day, by the adjudicating seat). ***  It is TRUE for seeing the synchronous assert, and FALSE AT THE MUTANT LEVEL: under stepping `debug()` PRINTS, so a `fatal(` -> `debug(` downgrade at the producer stays INVISIBLE to a stepped row -- the contract's own documented escape, guarded today only by a gate floor on the fatal( count, which a compensating addition elsewhere would net out.  A free-running row at verbose 0 REDS on that downgrade, because debug()'s early-out goes quiet while fatal() does not.  **So free-running buys a per-site DETECTION CAPABILITY, not only wall-clock**, and the choice is not purely economic.  Shipped in 6f39c95 without the qualifier.

THREE OF THE PANEL'S FOUR NOT-SETTLED ITEMS SETTLED BY READING, while the timing seat runs.

P4 -- CAN THE TWO REGEXES BOTH MATCH ONE LINE?  NO.  `P_OVERRUN` matches
`wdc_addtoinbuf(): WARNING! wdc inbuf overrun`; `P_DATA` matches `wdc: write to DATA, but
not`.  Two distinct fatal() calls in the device, two distinct texts, no shared substring
either pattern would match.  The #464 unexpected-write latch cannot pollute the overrun
count.

P5 -- DOES ADDING A runloop VARIANT BREAK ANOTHER ROW?  NO.  `runloop` has EXACTLY ONE call
site in the whole probe, and it is the `overrun x2` row itself.  Converting it in place is
therefore as safe as adding a variant, and cheaper.

*** Q3 -- AND THIS ONE DE-RISKS THE ROUND. ***  The overrun `fatal()` lives INSIDE
`wdc_addtoinbuf`, reached SYNCHRONOUSLY from the data-port write handler inside the guest's
own store instruction.  Nothing this row depends on comes from a host timer.  By the
carrier's own refined rule -- a step-based probe sees an assert that is SYNCHRONOUS, and
misses only what a host-timer callback produces -- A STEPPED PROBE CAN SEE THIS.

  **So free-running is a SPEED choice, not a CORRECTNESS one.**  That matters for the
  disposition: if the timing run says `step 394202` is tolerable, the re-aim needs no
  free-running conversion at all and the round shrinks to a count change plus the header
  correction.  The substitute seat raised exactly this possibility -- 'possibly a full
  re-evaluation of whether free-running is even needed' -- and it was right to.

STILL NOT SETTLED, and it needs a run rather than a reading: the wall-clock of the re-aimed
row.  A seat is measuring it.

*** AND A UNIT ERROR IN MY OWN BRIEF, CAUGHT INDEPENDENTLY BY TWO SEATS. ***  I wrote '~145
refused pushes' and named no unit.  It is 145 refused BYTES, which is about 73 refused
STORES, because each two-byte store pushes twice.  minimax: 'internally consistent once you
pick a unit; the brief should pick one and say so.'  kimi-k3: 'settled here: ~73, not ~145'.
That is this project's own rule -- a count that names neither unit cannot be checked -- and
I broke it in a brief that quotes the rule elsewhere.

IT IS NONE OF THE RECORDED CLASSES.  No quota text, so not a WALL.  98% novel, so not the

*** AND seat_verdicts.py FILED IT AS 'answered, NO VERDICT LINE (format miss)'. ***  That is
the daemon case's conflation again: a seat that produced NO ANSWER recorded as a seat with
bad FORMATTING.  Scoring it 'answered' credits a verdict that does not exist, and this panel

A CHECKABLE SIGNATURE EXISTS AND IS CHEAP: does the answer END INSIDE A QUOTED FILE OR CODE
BLOCK rather than with a sentence?  A finished answer ends in prose.  This one ends in `}`.
That is a different question from 'is there a verdict line', which is a FORMAT question --
and the two are being answered by one check.

NOT GENERALISED FROM ONE INSTANCE, deliberately: the same seat produced a real verdict with a
real finding on #484's pass 2 (566 KB) and a substantive answer on #485 (2.2 MB, the landisk
unmapped-write finding at its tail).  So this is not 'codex is broken'.  It is one firing

It is 145 refused BYTES, about 73 refused STORES, because each two-byte store pushes twice. ***  That is this project's own rule -- a count that names neither unit cannot be checked -- broken in a brief that cites the rule elsewhere.

Also put the unit error precisely -- 'internally consistent once you pick a unit; the brief should pick one and say so' -- and listed four facts it could not check from the packet, each with the single fact that would settle it.

Its framing is the durable part: the deciding variable is not 'same file' (my argument) but 'SAME LANDING DATE', which is conditional on checks the packet had not run.  It also independently corrected the unit error (~73, not ~145) and raised the possibility I had not -- that free-running may not be needed at all, which I then settled by reading: the overrun fatal() is SYNCHRONOUS inside the data-port write handler, so a stepped probe CAN see it and free-running is a SPEED choice, not a correctness one.

VERDICT: RE-AIM.  Free-running preferred, STEPPED LICENSED; RETIRE only if BOTH probe shapes
fail a measured wall-clock test.  Header correction INSEPARABLE from the re-aim -- one round.
Order unchanged: #486 still leads by deadline, and the deadline got closer.

*** THE OPTION SET I POSED WAS INCOMPLETE BY THREE MEMBERS, and one of them is aimed
directly at me. ***

  M4  RE-PIN THE WANT TO 0 AND KEEP THE DEAD STIMULUS.  One character; the gate goes green.
      REJECTED as the oracle-correction rule's laundering case with no architecture warrant,
      AND as a check that cannot fail: with the dead stimulus, shipped bytes read 0, the
      unlatched mutant reads 0, the silenced mutant reads 0.  It cannot red under ANY
      mutation of the producer.  *** Named because it is the cheapest path to a green
      battery and someone under Sunday pressure will think of it. ***
  M5  REVIVE THE STIMULUS BY PRODUCT EDIT (make the command reset conditional).  REJECTED:
      that reset closed three measured state-leak defects, and a HARNESS round does not edit
      product code to keep a test alive.
  M6  RE-AIM **AND** add a redundant clause-(b) carrier in the offline differential, so the
      producer's coverage stops being route-dependent.  FILES as its own item -- it is a
      second detector with its own oracle, so the round-scope rule excludes it.

RETIRE-WITHOUT-REBUILD IS NOT A MEMBER AT ALL: it re-opens the exact L2 state the probe's own
header records a seat catching.  LEAVE loses always -- a known-red scored row in the weekly
battery is a standing mis-attribution engine, which is what this round exists to prevent.

TWO MUTATIONS OWED, and the second is the anti-fake control:
  M_relatch  remove the latch guard and flag-set, keep the fatal() and the refusal return.
             Every refused byte then announces -- expect the count >> 1 against want 1, RED.
  M_silent   DELETE the producer's fatal(), keep the guard and the refusal.  The row must
             read 0, RED.  *** THIS IS WHAT PROVES THE COUNTED 1 COMES FROM THE PRODUCER'S
             ANNOUNCE and not from a widened regex: the smallest fake is a one-token widening
             of P_OVERRUN so the datawr line feeds it, and M_silent is the only row-level
             check that catches it -- a polluted row reads 1 and stays green. ***

FOUR FACTS BEYOND THE BRIEF:
  1. P4 is disjoint BY DESIGN, not by luck.  #484's bulk-arm message deliberately names
     wdc__read() instead of the producer, with an in-source comment saying the shared latch
     removed the only other way to tell the sites apart.  P_OVERRUN anchors on
     `wdc_addtoinbuf():`, so the ONLY line in the device that can feed the count is the
     producer's own announce.  The regex-to-site mapping is pinned in product prose.
  2. *** A len=4 ROUTE HALVES THE COST AND ALREADY EXISTS IN THE ROW SET. ***  The write
     arm's `case 4` pushes four bytes per store, WD_DATA is 4-byte aligned, and `datawr x2`
     already drives MOV_L green there.  65,700 stores is about 197,102 steps against the
     brief's 394,202 -- one constant swap, same margin, same site coverage.
  3. THE STEPPED FORM IS A LOAD-SENSITIVE ORACLE IN ITS WORST SHAPE.  The announce fires at
     ~99.9% through the run and session() reads for a FIXED spin with no completion
     detection -- so a load-starved spin truncates the transcript BEFORE the announce and the
     row reads 0.  That is the gate_ab false-FAIL class, sitting in the weekly battery whose
     rules exist because of it.
  4. *** MY OWN FRAMING NEEDS A QUALIFIER -- see the L4 correction on the entry below. ***

P3 REMAINS NOT SETTLED and the seat declined to transfer the 171k/s figure, saying it could
not locate the number's provenance.  Neither could I.  That is the right refusal.

VERIFIED THE ADJUDICATOR'S COST-HALVING CLAIM RATHER THAN TAKING IT.  `datawr x2` already
drives MOV_L_R8_AT_R7 (opcode 0x2782, a FOUR-BYTE store) at WD_DATA, and it is a SHIPPED
GREEN ROW.  So the len=4 route is proven working on this machine, not hypothesised, and the
write arm's `case 4` pushes four bytes per store.

ARITHMETIC, derived rather than transcribed (WDC_INBUF_SIZE = 262656, capacity 262655):

    byte store   262655 to fill   262695 with margin   ~788087 single-steps
    half store   131328 to fill   131368 with margin   ~394106 single-steps
    LONG store    65664 to fill    65704 with margin   ~197114 single-steps

So the long form is HALF the brief's cost, for one constant swap and no new mechanism.  The
seat quoted 65,700 / 197,102; the small difference is the margin choice, not a disagreement.

IT DOES NOT MAKE THE TIMING MEASUREMENT UNNECESSARY -- 197k single-steps is still large, and
the load-sensitivity hazard the seat named is unchanged in kind: the announce still fires at
~99.9% through the run, and session() still reads for a FIXED spin with no completion
detection, so a load-starved spin truncates before the announce and the row reads 0.  Halving

*** AND ITS FIRST RUN PAID FOR IT THE SAME HOUR. ***

#489's bare-deletion mutant under the shipped 19-row detector: **7 x heap-buffer-overflow, every one a WRITE**, five `0 bytes after 407-byte region` and two `0 bytes after 1-byte region`.  The stack runs from `main` through `sh_run_instr` and a guest `mov.w` store into `handle_command`, onto a buffer from `alloc_data`'s `malloc(guest cnt)`.  `regress/artifacts/gdromexitsix/asan_m0_20260828/`.

*The FIRST attempt reported `6/19, zero reports` -- noise, not a negative.  LeakSanitizer fires at exit on every session and ASan's default exit code is 1, so every survival row read as a death while the genuine reports went to a pty the probe does not retain.  The tell was `ok surv` reading exit1 on the LEGAL length, which the mutant cannot affect.*

*** FIXED 2026-08-28.  THE TREE BUILDS, RUNS, AND HAS ASAN LINKED. ***

Four build attempts, each peeling one layer, every layer INVISIBLE to the propagation gate:
  1. stale HEADERS   -- diskimage.c vs a diskimage.h missing nr_of_tracks, DISKIMAGE_MAX_SPT,
                        struct diskimage_track.  Fixed by back-filling 474 .c/.h from SEC.
  2. stale GENERATORS -- new sources against an OLD makeautodev.sh emitted
                        `int devinit_Makefile.skel(...)`, a glob expansion the script's own
                        comment warns about.  Fixed by syncing 16 scripts/.index/Makefile.skel.
  3. stale GENERATED MAKEFILE -- OBJS predating dev_ne2000.c (a SEC-only file), giving
                        `undefined reference to devinit_ne2000`.  Fixed by re-running
                        ./configure with CFLAGS='-fsanitize=address,undefined
                        -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g'; COPTIM verified to still carry the
                        sanitizer afterwards, and the 15 prior Makefiles were backed up first.
  4. none -- it built.

*** MAKE_RC REPORTED 0 ON EVERY FAILED BUILD. ***  Caught only because the check was
`[ -x gxemul ]`.  The carrier already says the exit status lies here; this is three more
instances in one session.

**THE CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL AND OUTLIVES THIS TREE: AN INCREMENTAL PROPAGATION CHECK CANNOT
SEE A STALE BASELINE.**  precommit_check.sh enforces propagation for `$CHANGED` -- the files
THIS commit touches -- which is deliberate and right (*a gate that hard-fails on a tree
someone chose not to build is a gate that gets switched off*).  But the tree was ALREADY
stale when the 2026-08-27 ruling landed, and nothing back-fills.  diskimage.h and
makeautodev.sh are touched by no recent round, so no gate ever required them.

**The tree passed every commit's check while compiling nothing at all** -- worse than the
gate comment's own fear of *a detector that has silently stopped detecting, worse than no
detector because it reassures*.

*** OWNER DECISION 2026-08-28: a SOFT-WARNING full `diff -rq` of the .c/.h set, SKIPPED
ENTIRELY when the tree is absent. ***  Warning rather than hard-fail, and absent-is-skipped,
so the absence-is-not-a-failure rule that keeps the gate switched on is preserved.  Filed as
`asanbaselinedrift` to ship as its own harness round with its two negative controls.

NOW UNBLOCKED: #489's headline claim.  Its bare-deletion mutant scored 12/19 with the host
SURVIVING a 408-byte write past a malloc(0) -- which shows the write does not FAULT, not
that it is ABSENT.  An ASAN run settles that, and the tree to run it on now exists.

*A check of mine scored the finished binary as having no ASan: `nm | grep -c __asan` = 0.
Wrong test -- the sanitizer symbols are in the SHARED LIBRARY.  `ldd | grep libasan` is the
test, and the build I nearly discarded was already correct.*

*** DIAGNOSED AND FIXED 2026-08-28, AND THE CAUSE IS A GAP IN THE HARNESS RATHER THAN A
STALE FILE. ***

MEASURED FIRST: `make -j8` in build-asan/ reported **MAKE_RC=0 AND PRODUCED NO BINARY** --
the documented trap, caught only because the check was `[ -x gxemul ]` rather than the exit
status.  The real errors were in diskimage.c: `struct diskimage has no member named
nr_of_tracks`, `DISKIMAGE_MAX_SPT undeclared`, `invalid use of undefined type struct
diskimage_track` -- a current .c against a STALE .h.

*** THE CAUSE: THE PROPAGATION RULE IS INCREMENTAL AND THE TREE NEEDED A BASELINE. ***
The owner ruled on 2026-08-27 that build-asan/ joins the propagation set, and
precommit_check.sh implements that for `$CHANGED` -- the files THIS commit touches.  That
is deliberate and well-reasoned (its own comment: *a gate that hard-fails on a tree someone
chose not to build is a gate that gets switched off*).  **But the tree was already stale
when the ruling landed, and nothing back-fills.**  `diskimage.h` is touched by no recent
round, so no gate ever required it -- and it is what broke the build.

**So the tree could pass every commit's check and still not compile.**  That is worse than
the gate comment's own fear -- it says a stale ASAN tree is *a detector that has silently
stopped detecting, worse than no detector because it reassures*.  This one did not build at
all, so it detected nothing, while every commit touching it reported green.

MEASURED DIVERGENCE at diagnosis: **111 differing .c/.h files, 1 present only in SEC**
(360 paths total, the rest .o and generated Makefiles).  No divergence is permitted for
shared files -- unlike est/, build-asan has no allowlist -- so all 111 were staleness.

FIXED by back-filling every .c/.h from GXEMUL-SEC/src (474 files copied, source divergence
measured 0 afterwards), under a `.MUTANT` sentinel so an interrupted sync could not be
mistaken for a clean tree.  Rebuilt with `rm src/cpus/*.o` first.

*** WHAT REMAINS OPEN IS THE HARNESS GAP, NOT THIS TREE: an incremental propagation check
cannot detect a stale BASELINE, and there is no periodic full comparison.  The next
baseline drift will be just as invisible. ***  A full `diff -rq` of the .c/.h set is cheap
and would have caught this in one command; whether it belongs in the gate (and at what
cadence, given the absence-is-not-a-failure rule) is an owner decision, not a round's.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: `#489`'s strongest single result is the bare-deletion
mutant scoring 12/19 with the host SURVIVING a 408-byte write past a `malloc(0)`.  The
measuring seat stated its own limit -- that shows the write does not FAULT, not that it is
ABSENT.  An ASAN run is exactly what closes that gap.

*** `build-asan/` DOES NOT BUILD AND HAS NO BINARY. Found 2026-08-27 while propagating
#484, and it PREDATES that round -- `dev_wdc` appears ZERO times in the failure log. ***

    make        103 errors, and it reported EXIT 0 -- the documented false-zero, again
    build-asan/gxemul   DOES NOT EXIST
    stale objects       222 .o files with no binary to link them into

ROOT CAUSE, verified rather than guessed: `build-asan/src/disk/diskimage.c` is IN SYNC
with SEC while `build-asan/src/include/diskimage.h` is NOT.  The new .c uses members the
old .h does not declare -- `nr_of_tracks`, `total_disc_sectors`, `first_data_track_lba`,
`DISKIMAGE_MAX_SPT`, `struct diskimage_track` -- each present in SEC's header and absent
from this one.  **A .c was propagated without its header**, which is the no-VPATH rule
obeyed halfway.

AND IT IS NOT ONE FILE: **363 files under `build-asan/src` differ from SEC.**  This tree
is broadly abandoned, not narrowly stale.

*** THE CONSEQUENCE IS SILENT COVERAGE LOSS, THE SAME CLASS AS A GATE THAT SKIPS. ***
`gate_asan_sweep.sh` exists to run the machine-construction sweep under ASAN.  With no
binary it cannot do that -- and this project has already been bitten once by a gate
skipping on a missing binary and scoring the skip as a pass.

NOT FIXED IN #484, and deliberately: the stopping rule fixes a finding in-round only if it
is a MEASURED FALSE PASS of this round or a WRONG RECORD.  This is neither -- it is a
pre-existing tree defect in a tree #484 does not measure against.  Folding a 363-file
resync into a ring-buffer round is exactly how rounds stop converging.

REMEDY when it is worked: re-derive the tree from SEC rather than patching the header.
A tree 363 files out of date has no property worth preserving, and a header-only fix
would leave the other 362 to be discovered one build at a time.

rows.title: landiskaux  DEVINIT has no MACHINE_LANDISK case, so twelve measured Device Control writes land on unmapped memory -- one line, and now UNBLOCKED

entries.ev: direct reading of DEVINIT(wdc) and machine_landisk.c
entries.note:
A STRUCTURAL OBSERVATION, AND THE PART OF IT I NEARLY OVERCLAIMED.

*** THE ALT-STATUS ADDRESS IS COMPUTED FROM AN UNSCALED BYTE OFFSET, WHILE THE MAIN REGISTER
BLOCK IS SCALED BY addr_mult. ***  All four rules -- the default +0x206, MACPPC's +0x160,
HPCMIPS' hardcode and IQ80321's +0x402 -- consult `devinit->addr` and never
`devinit->addr_mult`, while the main registration uses `DEV_WDC_LENGTH * devinit->addr_mult`.

AND LANDISK IS THE ONLY IN-TREE wdc WITH addr_mult != 1 (it passes addr_mult=2; every other
instantiation omits it and gets 1).  So it is the only machine where the two conventions can
disagree -- which looked like a complete explanation for why it is the only machine whose
device-control writes land nowhere.

*** IT IS NOT THE EXPLANATION, AND I CHECKED BEFORE WRITING IT DOWN AS ONE. ***  Scaling does
not produce the measured address: 0x206 * 2 = 0x40c, and the driver writes +0x2c.  Neither
the raw ISA offset nor any scaling of it predicts 0x2c, so landisk's aux block genuinely
sits somewhere machine-specific.  A `case MACHINE_LANDISK:` is therefore the RIGHT SHAPE,
matching MACPPC and IQ80321 -- not a paper-over of a scaling bug.

WHAT SURVIVES IS A LATENT HAZARD WORTH RECORDING AND NOT FIXING: the offsets are unscaled,
so a FUTURE machine with addr_mult != 1 that falls through to the default rule would get a
wrong alt-status address for exactly the reason landisk does not.  Landisk escapes it only
by getting an explicit case.  Filed as an observation on this row rather than as its own
item, because no such machine exists today and inventing a guard for one would be the
'it cannot hurt' addition this fork refuses.
entries.outcome_note: [SELF-GRADED -- the main loop this session IS Opus 5, so grader and seat are the same family.  Disclosed rather than excluded, and this seat's 100% rate should not be read as accuracy.]  It confirmed the lost seat's figures across four runs AND captured what no previous report had -- the other six values, one of which carries WDCTL_RST.  Its discriminating control (does the command block succeed?) came back decisively and settles which of two diagnoses is right.  Its MEMORY_RW_ONE_PAGE relative-offset trap is a real instrument finding that plausibly explains the earlier report.

entries.ev: direct reading of DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc_altstatus) and machine_landisk.c
entries.note:
TWO OF THE PANEL'S OPEN QUESTIONS SETTLED BY READING, while the third is measured.

Q3 -- WHAT DOES A MAPPED WRITE ACTUALLY DO?  The entire write arm, comments stripped, is:

        if (idata & WDCTL_RST) {
                d->cur_command = COMMAND_RESET;
                wdc_new_command_reset(d);
        }

Nothing else.  Two effects -- latch the ATAPI signature, and reset the ring/tenant state --
and BOTH are gated on 0x04.  A read returns status_byte() and has no side effect.  So the
'untraced code path' the steelman worries about is four lines long.

P5 -- COLLISION?  NO.  landisk registers exactly one wdc block, 0x14000000-0x1400000f, and
+0x2c lies outside it.  Nothing else in the machine claims that address.

*** AND THAT SHARPENS THE ONE QUESTION THAT IS STILL OPEN INTO SOMETHING WORTH MEASURING:
IF ANY OF THE TWELVE WRITES CARRIES WDCTL_RST (0x04), THEN MAPPING THE REGISTER STARTS
PERFORMING REAL RESETS ON A MACHINE THAT HAS NEVER HAD ONE. ***  The prior report said six
of twelve are 0x08 and did not record the other six.  0x08 is inert post-#481; 0x04 is not.

PANEL DISPOSITION, adopted: SHIP, BUT NOT ON THIS PACKET.  The twelve-write measurement
comes from a LOST LOG -- the third artifact lost from the same seat's scratch directory --
so every number in the round's warrant is a seat's report rather than a citation.  A re-take
is in flight, and it carries the control that discriminates the two diagnoses: if the
command-block accesses at +0x00..0x0f SUCCEED, the defect is a missing offset case; if they
do NOT, the defect is a wrong devinit->addr and the one-line fix would paper over it.

AND A DISPOSITION THE PANEL WAS RIGHT TO STATE PLAINLY: do NOT fold this into wdcnoirq as a
rider.  nIEN stays dead either way, and the two rounds answer different questions.

Disclosed rather than excluded, and this seat's 100% rate should not be read as accuracy.]  It confirmed the lost seat's figures across four runs AND captured what no previous report had -- the other six values, one of which carries WDCTL_RST.  Its discriminating control (does the command block succeed?) came back decisively and settles which of two diagnoses is right.  Its MEMORY_RW_ONE_PAGE relative-offset trap is a real instrument finding that plausibly explains the earlier report.

entries.note:
VERDICT: CONFIRMED -- the lost seat's numbers were right, AND THE RE-TAKE FOUND WHAT THE
ORIGINAL NEVER RECORDED.  The panel's gate is discharged: the warrant no longer rests on
an unpreserved artifact.

Q1 -- twelve writes to 0x1400002c, six of value 0x08?  **YES TO BOTH.**  Reproduced on
four runs (three pristine boots plus the instrumented build): 12 writes, 0 reads, all
len=1, all from pc=0x8c15f6e8 <obio_iomem_write_1+0x8>, all real guest stores
(no_exceptions=0).

*** Q2 -- THE VALUES, WHICH NO PREVIOUS REPORT CAPTURED, AND ONE OF THEM CARRIES
WDCTL_RST. ***

     1   0x0c   WDCTL_4BIT | WDCTL_RST      <-- SRST ASSERTED
     2   0x08   WDCTL_4BIT                  <-- SRST released
  3..12   0x02 / 0x08 alternating (IDS / 4BIT, five pairs)
  histogram: 0x0c x1, 0x08 x6, 0x02 x5

So the FIRST write is a real ATA soft-reset assert/release pair at the head of the channel
probe, silently discarded today.  Bit names taken from the tree's own
src/include/thirdparty/wdcreg.h, not from memory.  Confirmed independently ON THE
UNMODIFIED BINARY by the tree's committed write-watchpoint (#250): same paddr, 0x0c first,
same value set.  It saw 9 of 12 because the watchpoint self-suppresses while
about_to_enter_single_step is set -- **a lower bound BY CONSTRUCTION**, so it corroborates
the VALUES and not the count, and the seat said so rather than reporting 9 as a discrepancy.

  CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX, and it is the question this round has been holding for: mapping
  the register makes that first write REACH `wdc_new_command_reset()` -- clearing
  atapi_cmd_in_progress, atapi_phase and write_in_progress, and purging the inbuf ring.
  On a fresh channel probe those are already zero, so the effect is probably nil HERE; but
  it is a real state change and the round must say so rather than describe the arm as inert.
  The 0x08/0x02 writes hit no WDCTL_RST branch.  COMMAND_RESET's only two consumers (the
  cyl_lo/cyl_hi read arms) are both diskimage_is_a_cdrom()-gated and do not fire on this
  IDE-disk rig.  **The fix-side measurement was deliberately NOT taken.**

*** Q3 -- THE DISCRIMINATING CONTROL, AND IT DECIDES BETWEEN THE TWO DIAGNOSES: THE
COMMAND BLOCK SUCCEEDS. ***  12,718 accesses across all eight registers (2560 DATA reads,
10,033 status polls, 33 sdh writes, 14 commands), and wd0 ATTACHES: 131 cyl / 16 head /
63 sec / 132048 sectors -- a device signature RAM cannot produce.  Cross-checked against
the pristine build's own -v output, which counts 2560 `wdc: read from DATA`, matching the
hook exactly.

  So the defect is a MISSING OFFSET CASE, not a wrong devinit->addr, and the one-line fix
  is aimed correctly.  Had it come back the other way, the one-liner would have papered
  over a misplaced device.

Q4 -- anything else claiming 0x1400002c?  NO, and confirmed on the CONSTRUCTED machine via
`device list` rather than by grep alone.  And the registered wdc_altstatus at 0x14000206
receives ZERO accesses for the entire boot -- the handler that exists is never reached.

*** THE INSTRUMENT TRAP, WHICH IS THE PART THAT OUTLIVES THIS ROW. ***  The seat's FIRST
census hook reported 12 unmapped writes and ZERO command-block accesses -- clean,
confident, and half wrong.  The device arm of MEMORY_RW_ONE_PAGE does
`paddr -= mem->devices[i].baseaddr` BEFORE calling the handler, so device accesses reach
do_return_ok carrying the RELATIVE offset.  **A window predicate on `paddr` is therefore
blind to exactly the mapped half -- the half that answers Q3.**

  That is plausibly how the earlier lost report came back with the writes and no control:
  not a lost log so much as an instrument that could only see one side.  It is the
  phantom-absence class with a subtraction in it, and the fix was an entry-paddr latch
  plus PROVING THE INSTRUMENT SEES THE POSITIVE CASE BEFORE BELIEVING ITS NEGATIVES.

NOT SETTLED, recorded as such: whether delivering the reset changes the boot outcome
(fix-side, deliberately untaken); CD-ROM rig behaviour; anything past the installer

rows.title: asanbaselinedrift  the propagation check is INCREMENTAL, so a stale BASELINE is invisible -- build-asan/ drifted until it would not compile while passing every commit
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-08-28 BY OWNER DECISION, from the round that fixed `asanunbuildable`.

**THE GAP:** `precommit_check.sh` enforces build-asan propagation for `$CHANGED` -- the files
THIS commit touches.  That bound is deliberate and correct; its own comment says *a gate that
hard-fails on a tree someone chose not to build is a gate that gets switched off*.  **But a
file no round happens to touch is never checked**, so a tree that was already stale when the
2026-08-27 ruling landed stays stale forever.  Measured: 111 divergent .c/.h files, of which
`diskimage.h` and `makeautodev.sh` broke the build -- neither touched by a recent round.

**THE SHAPE, worth stating because it generalises past this tree: an INCREMENTAL sync check
cannot detect a stale BASELINE.**  The tree passed every commit while compiling nothing.

*** THE DECISION: a SOFT-WARNING full `diff -rq` over the .c/.h set, SKIPPED ENTIRELY when the
tree is absent. ***  Warn, do not hard-fail -- and skip on absence -- so the
absence-is-not-a-failure property that keeps this gate switched on is preserved.  Chosen over
a hard fail (which is the exact shape the gate's author warned gets disabled) and over doing
nothing (which leaves the next drift to be found the way this one was: by someone trying to
use the tree).

**TWO NEGATIVE CONTROLS ARE OWED, as for any gate change:** (1) with a source file deliberately
reverted in build-asan/, the check WARNS and names it; (2) with the tree absent entirely, the
check is SILENT and the gate stays green.  Ships as its own small harness round -- a gate edit
must not ride in on a diff reviewed for something else.

SCOPE NOTE: `Makefile`s legitimately differ (they carry the ASan COPTIM) and must be excluded;
the measured expectation after a correct sync is **14 differing files, all Makefiles, zero
others**.  `est/` is NOT in scope -- it has a declared divergence allowlist
(`tools/est_divergence.txt`); build-asan has none, which is why any .c/.h divergence there is
staleness by definition.

**SEVERITY SET MED, 2026-09-07, by the MAIN LOOP** (not a flagship adjudication -- opus5/fable5 are reserved for the 09-09 adjudication, and a rating is exactly the kind of judgment call that seat exists for; overturn it freely).  REASON: same family: the propagation check is INCREMENTAL, so a stale BASELINE is invisible and the tool reports green over it.

entries.ev: direct reading of gate_build.sh's list_diffs() and precommit_check.sh's section A
entries.note:
*** THE FIX THIS ROW FILED WOULD HAVE REPRODUCED THE DEFECT IT FIXES.  Found by reading,
before any code was written. ***

The row said: make `gate_build.sh` READ `est_divergence.txt`, as `precommit_check.sh`
already does, and cited the two lists disagreeing by `devices/.index` as evidence of drift.
**The disagreement is CORRECT, because the two consumers cover DIFFERENT POPULATIONS.**

  gate_build.sh   compares the whole trees via `list_diffs()`, which is
                  `find . \( -name '*.c' -o -name '*.h' -o -name '*.cc' -o -name
                  '*.skel' \)`.  **`.index` matches none of those, so list_diffs can
                  NEVER produce it.**  The gate then checks for STALE entries -- listed
                  as divergent but not actually divergent.
  precommit_check iterates `$CHANGED` from git, filtered to `src/*`, and uses the list to
                  SKIP known-divergent files.  Any path can appear there, `.index`
                  included, because the population comes from git rather than from a
                  find with extension filters.

*** SO IF gate_build READ THE FILE VERBATIM, `.index` WOULD ENTER ITS EXPECTED SET, WHERE
`list_diffs` CANNOT PRODUCE IT -- AND ITS OWN STALE-ENTRY CHECK WOULD FLAG IT STALE ON
EVERY RUN.  Permanently red.  That is exactly the failure that cost five days and a
skipped gate, reintroduced by the repair for it. ***

THE ROW'S CORE FINDING SURVIVES AND IS UNCHANGED: gate_build pins its own list, that pinned
copy DID go stale, and the staleness cost a red battery plus `gate_mips`.  What is refuted
is only the proposed remedy and the `.index` evidence for it.

TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, neither taken here, both now stated with the constraint they must
satisfy:
  (a) gate_build reads the file but FILTERS to the extensions list_diffs covers, so the
      expected set and the actual set are drawn from the same population;
  (b) leave them separate and add a check that gate_build's list is exactly the
      extension-filtered SUBSET of the file's -- which catches drift without coupling two
      checks that legitimately differ.

*This is the addition licence doing its job before an edit rather than after: the proposed
change had no measured delta and no transferred warrant, only 'the two lists disagree, so
unify them'.  Reading what each list is FOR took minutes and refuted it.*

E2 is 'assignment where or-assignment was meant' at a single site -- is there a form that makes it unrepresentable or loud?  If not, E2's row needs a shape this file has none of: stage one site's latch, decline at the OTHER, re-trigger the first.  E3's coverage rests on a row ORDER nobody chose deliberately -- should the two-site rows run BOTH orders, and does that cost a row or just a session?
rows.state_note:
*** TWO MEASURED 20/20 ESCAPES FROM #490's CAPPED ASK-AGAIN, FILED 2026-08-29 BECAUSE
CONTRACT-DISCLOSED IS NOT FILED.  A supplementary pass-2 seat found them ranked nowhere --
zero hits in OUTSTANDING_BUGS, one ledger mention buried inside the ask-again note. ***

Both were BUILT and SCORED against the shipped 20-row detector, each mutant's whole row
block BYTE-IDENTICAL to base -- total escapes, not ties.  Artifacts:
`regress/artifacts/gdromexitsix/p2askagain_20260829/`.

**E2 -- `d->warned |= GDROM_W_FMT;` becomes `d->warned = GDROM_W_FMT;`  (ONE CHARACTER)**

Ranked FIRST and it is the worst of the three.  Site A still announces exactly once, so
every Site-A row stays green -- **but the assignment CLEARS THE OTHER EIGHT LATCHES.**  A
guest alternating a short TOC with a bad data format then re-announces #489's diagnostic
**WITHOUT BOUND**, and `fatal()` cannot be silenced by `-q`, so it reaches the host log
every time.  That is the guest-drivable flood this whole campaign exists to remove,
reintroduced by one character and invisible to the detector that was written for it.

**THE STRUCTURAL GAP, which is the part worth fixing rather than the instance:** every
latch row checks its OWN bit.  **No row observes any latch ACROSS a decline at the other
site.**  Closing E2 by rows needs an oracle that stages one site's latch, declines at the
OTHER site, and then re-triggers the first -- a shape no row in this file has.

`wdcsectorreset` is its recorded structural twin, and that row's own note says the first
job is to build the mutant and score it.  **Here the mutant arrives already measured.**

**E3 -- `if (!(d->warned & GDROM_W_FMT))` becomes `& (GDROM_W_FMT | GDROM_W_CMD)`**

Invisible ONLY because of row ORDER: both two-site rows run Site A before Site B, so
widening Site A's test is unobservable -- **the same edit at Site B WOULD be caught**
(`1,0`).  And pass 1's `S3 both` session ran the OPPOSITE order; the shipped rows inverted
it and nothing recorded the change.  *So the coverage depends on an ordering nobody chose
deliberately and nothing pins.*

**WHY THESE ARE DEBT AND NOT A FLOOR BREACH**, stated so nobody re-argues it: all four
floor clauses measure clean -- (a) PREFIX 8/20 CONTROL=OK, (b) 13/20 at BOTH sites,
(c) NULLMEDIUM 4/20 CONTROL=DEAD, (d) three forms.  These are hypothetical future edits in
uncovered cells, which is exactly #447's grading and #464's precedent.

**THEIR SIBLING E1 IS CLOSED AND THAT IS THE RANKING ARGUMENT.**  E1 was the same class --
a latch bit aliased onto an existing one -- and it was closed not by rows but by a
COMPILE-TIME assert, measured in five states plus a multi-bit-literal delta.  **Ask of E2
and E3 first whether a constructional bound exists**, before spending rows: E2 in
particular is 'assignment where or-assignment was meant', which may be reachable by
construction rather than by an oracle.

entries.note: *** THIS ITEM NOW ARRIVES WITH ITS ROWS ALREADY BUILT AND MEASURED, which changes it from a hunt into an implementation. ***  E2 (`|=` -> `=` on a latch) and E3 (widened guard) are STATEMENT defects, not constant-expression ones -- so unlike E1 they cannot be closed by a declaration, and the seat gave the reason: no constant expression can observe a statement, so the by-construction route is exhausted at E1.  A latch HELPER MACRO does not close E2 either: a macro-level `=` still escapes all 20 rows, because every row exercises one latch in isolation.  MEASURED against the ask-again's surviving binaries, one frozen instrument: base 22/22 (negative control -- neither row manufactures a failure), `E2_assignA` 21/22 with `latch keep` moving (got 2, want 1), `E3_widenA` 21/22 with the two-site row moving (got 0,1 want 1,1).  Both had previously escaped at 20/20, and the two are ORTHOGONAL -- each is green under the other's mutant.  `latch keep` = TOC_SHORT + BAD_FMT + TOC_SHORT, counting the #489 TOC diagnostic; its channel is a latch OTHER THAN the one Site A owns, which is exactly why all 20 shipped rows were blind.  The two-site row = BAD_CMD + BAD_FMT: both existing two-site rows fix FMT-then-CMD, where `warned` is 0 at Site A, so a widened guard is indistinguishable -- ONE REVERSED SESSION covers the whole order-asymmetry class.  *** RENAME BEFORE SHIPPING: the seat's own name `both sites rev` is exactly 14 chars = the gate's column width, so it renders with a trailing space and the gate anchor would miss it.  Use `rev sites`.  The seat found this by noticing its own summary table printed blank for that row while the FAIL list caught it. ***  NOT added to #490: E2/E3 were adjudicated coverage debt rather than floor breaches, and 20 -> 22 rows moves every score in a 13-build table.  More witnesses create more candidate ROUNDS, never bigger rounds.

rows.title: The wsl-dollar hook's 18 controls are run by nothing
rows.witness: harness:the suite now runs from precommit when the hook or the suite changes -- 18 of 18, 0 wrong, preserved at regress/artifacts/makercfalse/hook_controls_20260829/CONTROL_hookctl_20260830.out; a bogus GXHOOK path makes it REFUSE rather than report 18 of 18 against a missing file
rows.note: `artifacts/makercfalse/hook_controls_20260829/hookctl.py` is an 18-row control suite (9 must FIRE, 9 must stay SILENT) for the PreToolUse wsl-dollar guard.  It is classified CLASS_RESEARCH -- evidence -- because no emulator gate can run it: it tests a Claude-Code hook, not the emulator.  **So the guard that fires on every Bash call has no regression test that anything executes.**  *** THE CASE FOR GATING IT IS MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: the hook shipped 2026-08-29 with FOUR defects and nobody noticed for hours. *** Two false negatives (a multi-line `bash -c` block whose dollar sits below the -c -- the shape that actually bites, and which cost two confident wrong readings the same day) and two false positives that line-scoping was adopted to fix AND NEVER FIXED: a control of the very shape the hook's own comment cited as its motivating case still fired.  It scored 14/18; the rescoped form scores 18/18.  AGAINST gating: an emulator gate running a harness-tool control suite is a category mixture, and the suite depends on a file OUTSIDE the git root's normal scope.  A `tools/`-level check is likelier right than a `regress/` gate.  Cost is small (the suite runs in about a second) and it owes the usual two negative controls -- prove it reds on a broken hook, prove it greens on the shipped one.  *** CLOSED 2026-08-30.  The 18 controls are run by something now: a conditional section in `precommit_check.sh`. ***  CONDITIONAL on purpose -- the suite takes ~28 s, which is too slow for every commit and is exactly how a gate earns being switched off.  It fires when the hook, or the suite itself, is in the changed set, which is when it can regress.  Not a regress gate: it tests a Claude-Code hook rather than the emulator, so no battery gate can host it.  **NO SENTINEL IS NOT A PASS.**  The section fails when `HOOKCTL_DONE` is absent, because the suite REFUSES outright if the hook is missing and that refusal must read as a failure rather than a skip.  *** AND RUNNING IT SURFACED A DEFECT IN THE SUITE ITSELF: `HOOK` WAS ONE MACHINE'S HARDCODED ABSOLUTE PATH, IN A TRACKED FILE. ***  That is the defect the whole harness migration fixed on 2026-08-17 -- *scripts DERIVE the project root from their own location; they used to hardcode one machine's absolute path, which is only half-tracked* -- and this suite was written twelve days later carrying it.  Now derived from `__file__` with a `GXHOOK` override, and it REFUSES if the target is absent instead of reporting a clean sweep against nothing.  Controlled both ways.  It still points at the `.claude/` path rather than the tracked file, deliberately: that is what Claude Code actually invokes, so testing it exercises the shim AND the hook behind it.  Pointing at the tracked file would stop testing the delegation, which is the part that can silently break.

rows.title: round_reminder.sh is untracked -- lost on a fresh clone
rows.witness: harness:the shim was driven on BOTH arms and both emit valid hook JSON; negative control with the tracked target hidden returns rc=0 and ZERO bytes, so a fresh clone degrades to 'no reminder' rather than 'no session'
rows.note: `.claude/` sits at the PROJECT ROOT, one level ABOVE the git root (`GXEMUL-SEC/`), so anything written there is outside version control.  `tools/install_hooks.sh` states the identical problem for git hooks in its own header -- *'Git hooks live in .git/hooks, which is NOT tracked, so the hook cannot simply be committed'* -- and solves it by tracking an INSTALLER.  The wsl-dollar guard was fixed on 2026-08-29 by a different and better route: **the settings point at a TRACKED path and `.claude/` holds only a delegating shim, so there is exactly ONE copy and divergence is structurally impossible rather than policed by a gate.**  That avoids the carrier's stated antipattern (*'a copy nothing checks'*) without owing a section-J-style byte-divergence check.  **`round_reminder.sh` -- the SessionStart and TaskCompleted hook, which is what makes the panel directive and the end-of-round triage fire -- still lives only at the untracked path.**  It is arguably the most load-bearing hook in the harness and a fresh clone gets none of it.  Same one-file remedy; the only reason it was not done in the same pass is that changing the hook that injects the round directive mid-session is its own hazard, and editing a running shell script is a documented defect class here.  *** CLOSED 2026-08-30 BY THE SAME ROUTE THE wsl-dollar GUARD USED, and the row itself named that remedy. ***  `tools/hooks/round_reminder.sh` is now TRACKED and `.claude/hooks/round_reminder.sh` is a delegating shim.  **There is no copy**, so divergence is structurally impossible rather than policed -- which is what lets this close without owing a section-J byte-divergence gate, exactly as the row argued.  FAIL-SAFE, for the measured reason a broken hook can wedge every tool call: if the tracked target is absent the shim exits 0 and emits nothing.  Controlled by hiding the target: rc=0, 0 bytes.  *** AND COPYING IT SURFACED A DEFECT WORTH MORE THAN THE DURABILITY FIX: THE HOOK'S TEXT WAS STALE IN THREE WAYS, AND IT FIRES INTO EVERY SESSION START. ***  It announced an **EIGHT**-seat panel (it is nine), said `./panel.sh` **fires six** (it fires seven scriptable transports and omitted Grok entirely), and named **glm-5.2:cloud**, migrated to glm-5.3 on 2026-08-29.  So the mechanism that exists to make the panel directive fire had been announcing the wrong roster to every session, and nothing re-reads a hook.  Corrected, plus two additions the hook never carried: invoke panel.sh by ABSOLUTE path and never `./panel.sh` (the cwd drifts and a relative launch is a silent zero-seat failure that looks like a completed run), and VERIFY EACH SEAT BY CONTENT RATHER THAN SIZE -- a thinking burn returns an empty response inside 100+ KB of hidden reasoning, which a size check scores as the panel's best answer.  That last one happened in THIS round, to the glm seat, hours before the hook was read.  *The stale word lived in BOTH the session and task arms and the first fix caught only one; the grep-for-siblings rule is what found the second.*

rows.title: The battery's pre-flight git status is a multi-minute BLIND WINDOW
rows.witness: none
rows.note: *** MEASURED, NOT REASONED: `ps` showed `git -C ... status --porcelain` at 2:03 elapsed with NO verdict file and NO battery log on disk -- and the FULL span was ~15 MINUTES, not two: the task fired at 16:06:12 and the verdict's own START line reads 16:21:09. ***  (I filed 'over two minutes' from the single sample I had; the run's own record settled it afterwards. A number written from one observation is a lower bound, not a measurement.)  `nightly_battery.sh` computes `HEADSHA` and `DIRTY` BEFORE it opens either output: the verdict block ends `} > "$SUM"` and the run line is `./run.sh > "$LOG" 2>&1`, and a shell creates a redirect target only when it reaches that redirect.  So for the whole of the git call there is nothing to observe.  **THIS IS EXACTLY THE AMBIGUITY THE CARRIER'S OWN REDIRECT-TARGET RULE EXISTS TO RESOLVE, arriving inside the battery's own pre-flight.**  That rule says: log MISSING -> the command NEVER STARTED; log 0 bytes -> started.  Here the log is missing and the command HAS started, so the discriminator gives the wrong answer -- and it gives it during the exact window when an operator is most likely to be checking.  It compounds a hazard the script's own header already records: a battery launched from a Claude Code shell is ORPHANED, and *'the only tell was a log mtime 4.4 h stale'*.  During the blind window there is no mtime to read, so a genuinely orphaned start and a healthy one are INDISTINGUISHABLE by every documented check.  The only thing that separated them today was `ps -eo pid,ppid,etime,args`, which named the git child.  **REMEDY IS ONE LINE AND COSTS NOTHING: write a STARTING stamp to `$SUM` (or touch `$LOG`) BEFORE the git calls**, so the redirect-target rule works on this script.  The stamp is overwritten by the real verdict block moments later, so nothing is lost.  *Not fixed in the same pass because the battery was RUNNING and editing a shell script mid-execution is a documented defect class here -- bash reads incrementally by byte offset, and the failure looks like a syntax error in a file that parses clean afterwards.*  SECOND, SMALLER FINDING: the git call itself is slow because the repo is Windows-owned and WSL reaches it over /mnt/c.  Whether it should be narrowed (`git status --porcelain -- src/ tools/ regress/`) or simply stamped is a design question, not a defect -- **the blind window is the defect, and it exists at any duration.**  *** THE WINDOW'S DURATION IS TREE-STATE-DEPENDENT, measured the same evening on a SECOND run.  The defect is real and the ~15-minute figure is NOT its general size. ***  The 16:06 run took ~15 minutes to reach `START` because the pre-flight is `git status --porcelain` over `/mnt/c` on a DIRTY tree carrying a whole round's uncommitted work.  The 22:39 run reached `run.sh` in about SEVENTEEN SECONDS -- same machine, same command, same script -- because the tree was CLEAN.  **So the blind window is near-instant when it does not matter and long exactly when a round is mid-flight**, which is when someone is most likely to be watching it and most likely to misread the absence.  That makes it worse than a fixed-cost gap, not better: the failure mode is correlated with the moment of highest attention.  The remedy is unchanged and now has a second reason: a STARTING stamp written before the git calls costs nothing and removes a window whose length nobody can predict from the outside.

rows.title: #472's clamp introduced two -Wsign-compare warnings that cost a GATE
rows.witness: detector:regress/artifacts/diskimagesign/cascade_20260829
rows.note: *** NOT A COSMETIC WARNING -- IT WAS COSTING AN ENTIRE GATE'S COVERAGE, and that was found only by re-running a battery that had been RED AND UNREAD FOR FIVE DAYS. ***  `#472` replaced `len > OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE? OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE : len` with `len > remain? remain : len`, where `len` is `size_t` (parameter) and `remain` is `off_t`.  gcc warns twice at diskimage.c:1382 under the tree's own CWARNINGS.  **THE CASCADE:** `gate_build` wants ZERO warnings, so it FAILED; it withdraws `$RIG/gxsec-gxemul` at start and republishes only on success; `gate_mips` then `need_exec`s that binary and reported *'SKIP -- missing or non-executable binary'*.  **A whole gate lost, scored as SKIP rather than FAIL** -- byte-identical in shape to what one stale allowlist line cost on 2026-08-23, which is the defect `gatebuildallow` records.  **IT IS NOT A LIVE BUG AND THE ROUND SAYS SO:** `inblock = curofs & (OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE-1)` gives [0,511], so `remain` is in [1,512] and positive by construction; the conversion is value-preserving at every reachable value.  Both casts are therefore provable, not plausible.  MEASURED, control first: the reconstructed pre-fix line compiles rc=0/44072 b with **2** sign-compare warnings; the shipped source compiles rc=0/44112 b with **0**.  *** MY FIRST VERIFICATION WAS VACUOUS AND ITS OWN CONTROL CAUGHT IT: *** it reported 0 warnings for the PRE-FIX form, which must be 2.  The compile was failing on a missing include and the script read its empty output as a result -- the phantom-absence class, in a script written to prove a fix.  Take 2 reports compile rc and object size BEFORE the warning count and refuses to read the count without them.  EXPOSURE, stated honestly: warnings need a BUILD, builds are too slow for precommit, so warnings are checked only by the weekly battery -- a warning-introducing commit is invisible for up to seven days, and only if someone reads the result.  *** THE ROW NAMED NO COMMIT WHILE THE FIX HAD SHIPPED.  Found 2026-08-30 by reading `src/disk/diskimage.c`: the clamp now reads `lentoread = len > (size_t) remain? remain : (off_t) len;` with a `#491` comment proving both casts safe -- `inblock` is `curofs` masked to [0, OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE-1], so `remain` is in [1, 512] and can never be negative. ***  `git log -S` puts it in **18893de**, now recorded.  **This is the same shape a gate caught on `holdmarkermulti` in the same session -- work shipped, row names no commit -- and it did NOT trip here only because the state is `in work` rather than `open`.**  `check_row_states` scopes its shipped-work test to open rows, so an `in work` row can carry shipped code indefinitely without any gate objecting.  *Recorded as an observation about the checker's scope, not filed as a defect: widening it to `in work` would fire on every round that is genuinely mid-flight, which is what `in work` means.  The honest fix is the habit of filling `commits` at ship time, not a wider gate.*  The row's own EXPOSURE note stands unchanged and is the important part: warnings need a BUILD, builds are too slow for precommit, so a warning-introducing commit is invisible for up to seven days -- and only then if someone reads the battery result.
rows.state_note:
**CLOSEABLE.**  `18893de` fixed both signedness conversions; the casts remain and the bounded
remainder makes them value-preserving (`src/disk/diskimage.c`).

Carrier: `gate_build.sh`'s **`arc: warnings`**, which requires ZERO -- and the archived `#491`
verification records the pre-fix two-warning control against the repaired zero-warning build, so the
carrier is discriminating rather than merely present.

*Closure PROPOSED, not made; ratification is queued for the 2026-09-09
adjudication.  Evidence: codex closure pass 2026-09-07, regress/artifacts/queueunrated/codex_closeable_20260907.txt.*

rows.title: The propagate script prints 'propagated' after a FAILED cp
rows.witness: harness:regress/artifacts/makercfalse/propagate_controls_20260830/ -- SIX checks in BOTH directions, sentinel CPGUARD_PASS.  The old idiom is reproduced and shown to announce success on a missing source; the shipped idiom is shown to report the failure AND to catch a case cp's exit status cannot see.
rows.note: Measured 2026-08-29 on my own tooling.  The build-tree propagate script does `cp "$SEC/$F" "$D/$F"` and then unconditionally `echo "  propagated"`.  When the path was wrong the log read:  *cp: cannot stat '...': No such file or directory*  immediately followed by  *propagated*.  **That is a CLAIM OF ACTION printed at the exact moment of the failure**, the same shape as `panel.sh` printing *'re-firing once'* while re-firing nothing -- which this carrier already names as worse than a stale citation, because it reassures the one person who could still fix it.  **THE SENTINEL DISCIPLINE CONTAINED IT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.**  The two-part clearance reported `part 1 source cmps clean: NO` and KEPT the sentinel, so the tree was marked untrustworthy rather than silently wrong.  The false line cost confusion, not a wrong measurement.  FIXED in the rewritten script (`cp ... || { echo 'cp FAILED'; continue; }`), but the ORIGINAL at the #490 script still carries it, and any future copy inherits it.  *Root cause worth naming: the bad script was GENERATED FROM ANOTHER SCRIPT BY CHAINED `sed`, which produced `src/devices/disk/diskimage.c` from `src/devices/dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c`.  Generating a script by regex is the same class as substituting a grep for a parser -- it produces something that runs and is wrong.*

entries.note: The script the row named was a scratch tool and no longer exists, so closing on its absence would have been closing on a technicality.  **The CLASS is what mattered, and the current instance was checked instead** -- `propagate494.sh`, written today and run twice, which verifies the copy with `cmp` against the intended source rather than announcing unconditionally.  *** THE CONTROL FOUND SOMETHING THE OBVIOUS FIX WOULD HAVE MISSED. ***  The natural repair is `cp ... || { echo failed; exit; }`.  That guards the case where cp FAILS -- and the control's third block shows **a cp of the WRONG file exits 0**, so an exit-status guard passes while the destination holds content that was never intended.  Only a comparison against the INTENDED source catches it, which is what the shipped form does.  So the fix is not merely present, it is stronger than the one the row asked for.  **Controlled in both directions**, because a check that only ever passes is the exact shape this row is about: the OLD idiom is reproduced and measured announcing `propagated` on a missing source, and the NEW one is measured failing there and passing on a real copy with the destination verified to have actually changed.  Kept from the original finding because it is the part that generalises: the sentinel discipline CONTAINED the failure -- the two-part clearance reported part 1 red and KEPT the sentinel, so the tree was marked untrustworthy rather than silently wrong.  **The false line cost confusion, not a wrong measurement.**  Same family as `panelrefire` (still open), where a script prints `re-firing once` and re-fires nothing.

rows.title: diag_div_sweep.py reports line numbers that are systematically too small
rows.witness: harness:regress/artifacts/makercfalse/divsweep_controls_20260830/ -- BEFORE.txt and AFTER.txt from the same tool at the same HEAD, with the row COUNT pinned at 27 in both so the fix is shown to move WHERE sites are reported without changing WHICH are found.
rows.note: *** EVERY LINE NUMBER `diag_div_sweep.py` PRINTS IS TOO SMALL, AND `gate_hygiene.sh`'s OWN COMMENT CITES TWO OF THEM. *** MEASURED 2026-08-29: the sweep reports `dev_ns16550.c:79` for `115200 / d->divisor`, whose call really begins at **:180**; and `diskimage.c:543` for `bytes_left % ct->sector_size`, whose call really begins at **:976**.  *** THIS ROW FIRST SAID 181 AND 983.  THOSE ARE THE DIVISION LINES, NOT THE CALL-START LINES, and the sweep correctly reports the latter -- a call may span lines and the start is the sensible anchor.  Corrected after the scratch proof reported 180/976 and I checked WHICH SIDE was wrong instead of assuming the tool was. ***  It also reports `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:211 fatal`, where line 211 is PROSE inside a comment block. MECHANISM, read from the source rather than guessed: `strip_lits()` does NOT preserve offsets -- a string literal of any length becomes a single space, and a `/* ... */` block becomes a single space WITH ALL ITS NEWLINES DESTROYED.  The scan then runs over the stripped text while the line number is computed as `raw[:m.start()].count(chr(10))` -- an offset into the STRIPPED string indexed against the RAW one.  Since stripping only ever shortens, every reported line is too small, and the error grows with the size of the comment blocks above the site.  `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` carries 40-line comment blocks, which is why its site lands 400+ lines early, inside prose. *** THE COUNTS ARE UNAFFECTED AND THE RATCHET IS SOUND. ***  Match counting does not depend on line numbering, so `DIAG_DIV_TOTAL=21` and `DIAG_DIV_NONCONST=2` are correct, and both non-constant sites are correctly IDENTIFIED by file and expression.  Only their CITATIONS are false.  This is a records defect, not a coverage one. **WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY:** the wrong numbers did not stay in the tool. They were transcribed into `gate_hygiene.sh`'s rationale comment, where a future round reads them as the authoritative location of the two sites the ratchet exists to protect -- and this project's citation-form rule exists precisely because a drifted number is consumed by a reader who then opens the wrong place. FOUND BY CHASING A REFUTED SEAT CLAIM: agy attributed the 24->21 drop to '#490 consolidating 4 fatal() calls into 1 at dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:211'.  Checking it showed #490 removed ZERO fatal lines containing a division and that :211 is a comment -- so the claim was false, but the line number it rested on was the tool's, not the seat's.  *A seat's wrong answer led straight to a real defect in the tool that supplied its premise.* REMEDY: make `strip_lits` length-preserving -- replace each removed character with a space and each removed newline with a newline -- so stripped offsets index the raw text correctly.  That is the standard fix and it makes the two texts positionally identical.  Then re-derive the two citations in gate_hygiene.sh's comment.  Owes a control: the known sites must report 181 and 983.  *** REMEDY PROVEN IN SCRATCH, 2026-08-29, before any tree was touched. ***  A length-preserving `strip_lits` (one space per consumed character, newlines preserved) moves the two citations from 79 -> 180 and 543 -> 976, the true call-start lines, while DIAG_DIV_TOTAL stays 21 and DIAG_DIV_NONCONST stays 2 -- so it is a pure CITATION repair with no behavioural change, which is the property that makes it safe.  The proof harness itself failed twice first and both failures were apparatus: the scratch copy resolves ROOT from its own location and scanned an empty directory (reporting 0 sites -- the phantom-absence shape), and a `re.sub` replacement ate the backslashes in the override path.  Both were caught because the control demanded specific numbers rather than merely 'different'.  *** AND THE SURROUNDING STORY WAS WRONG TOO, MEASURED BY THE fable5 SEAT. ***  I recorded the class ratchet's 24 -> 21 as 'three sites legitimately REMOVED'.  It is a CONSOLIDATION: the pre-#462 tree carried FOUR one-division `fatal("  %08x", (int) d->dma_reg[N / sizeof(uint32_t)])` calls, and HEAD carries the SAME FOUR DIVISIONS as arguments of ONE fatal().  **No instance of the class was removed at all** -- `DIAG_DIV_TOTAL` counts CALLS carrying at least one division, so merging four calls into one moves the total while the division census is unchanged.  A round acting on my version would have gone looking for three removals that never happened.  ATTRIBUTION SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY VOTE: the two Agent seats DISAGREED -- opus5 said `fb0cc78` (#490), fable5 said `7c9dd9e` (#462).  `git show <sha> -- src/devices/dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c | grep -c dma_reg` gives **9 for 7c9dd9e and 0 for fb0cc78**, so fable5 is right.  One command, no tally.

entries.note: *** REFUTED THE ONE THING I TOLD THE PANEL I COULD NOT FIND. ***  My Q3b said there was no mechanical discriminator between 'drives a pty' and 'simulates a stream'.  It is `pty.fork`, TWELVE LINES ABOVE in the same gate, already the census basis at `:162`.  MEASURED: scoping `probe_code()` to files containing it takes `whole_full` 4 -> 2 with `conv_anchor`/`conv_echo`/`conv_mark` all UNCHANGED at 23 -- **row 3 goes green with no pin moved, no allowlist widened and no filename exemption**, and it subsumes the existing `readiness_predicate_test.py` exemption automatically.  It also showed my proposed exclusion is the shape the gate itself REJECTS: `:92-95` and `:347-348` require an exemption to travel WITH a content pin on the excluded file -- *'an allowlist entry that checks what it exempts'* -- and I proposed it bare.  *** AND IT MEASURED MY ROW-5 FLOOR VACUOUS. ***  A kill table: under `>= 12`, deleting ONE latch's two-line guard pair PASSES (raw 13), restoring the exact unbounded flood #464 fixed; and gutting a guard while naming the latch twice in a COMMENT also passes (raw 15).  Six per-latch `>= 2` rows are ALSO inadequate -- satisfied by two reads and no set, while the row's label claims 'one set + one read each'.  Its shape: TWO rows over comment-stripped code, `SET_OK == 6` and `READ_OK == 6`, measured 6/6 at HEAD, killing both mutants and scoring 0/6 on a null medium (floor clause (c)).  *** THREE FINDINGS LARGER THAN THE FIVE REDS. ***  (F1) the sweep's line bug -- which I had found independently the same hour, and its measured fix agrees with mine EXACTLY: 79 -> 180, 543 -> 976, counts unchanged. The score was the tell: a true pair deletion reads 5/5, and the table shows 5/6.'  Both M1 and M2 were MISLABELLED -- my vac() guard caught only TOTAL no-ops, so a partially-applied mutant scored as the thing it was not. *** THE DEFECT HAD TWO HALVES AND FIXING EITHER ALONE LOOKS LIKE A PARTIAL IMPROVEMENT RATHER THAN A REMAINING BUG -- which is what makes the shape worth recording. ***  **(1)** `strip_lits()` collapsed a whole `/* ... */` block to a SINGLE SPACE, destroying every newline inside it, so each comment shifted every later line number down.  **(2)** the line number was then counted in `raw` using an offset from `src` -- `m` matches the STRIPPED text, so `m.start()` is a src offset, and indexing raw with it mixes two coordinate systems.  Fixing only (1) moved a measured case from `:79` to `:80` when the truth was `:180`.  **A one-line improvement that still reads as broken is easy to mistake for the fix not working, rather than for a second cause.**  MEASURED, same tool, same HEAD, before and after:  `dev_ns16550.c` 79 -> **180** (the call the division sits in starts at 180; the division itself is at 181, and the sweep correctly anchors on the call start).  `diskimage.c` 543 -> **976** (division at 983).  `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` 211 -> **1383**: 211 was PROSE INSIDE A COMMENT BLOCK -- the drift was large enough to land the anchor inside the very construct being stripped -- and 1383 is a real `fatal("[ dreamcast_gdrom_dma: DMA start with dst"`.  **DENOMINATOR, because a spot-check of three proves nothing about 27:** all 21 parseable rows now point at code and **ZERO land inside a comment**. Both fixes now say so in their own comments.  `gate_hygiene.sh`'s comment cites two of the OLD numbers and is now stale; left for a round that touches that file, since editing a gate is not a records change.
