rows.note: *** FILED BECAUSE `gate_hygiene.sh` SAYS IT IS FILED.  A comment reading 'FILED, not taken here' with no row behind it is the gap-closes-itself shape, and fable5 caught exactly that on pass 2. ***  `DIAG_DIV_TOTAL` is pinned by EQUALITY.  A seat argued for a FLOOR: an equality breaks on every legitimate de-fatalisation, and de-fatalisation is this fork's whole queue.  The re-pin round declined to convert it, because that changes what the check PROVES and must not ride inside a re-pin.  *** THE ADJUDICATOR THEN REFUTED BOTH SIMPLE DIRECTIONS, which is why this is a design question and not a deferred chore. ***  A CEILING lets the sweep rot silently -- a total drifting DOWN to 0 would pass, the vacuous-green shape this denominator exists to catch.  A FLOOR >= 21 reds on every legitimate de-fatalisation exactly as the equality does, so it purchases nothing.  The equality's break on each de-fatalisation is a FORCED-ACKNOWLEDGMENT FEATURE, now priced correctly by the DOWN-direction instruction this round added: the NUMERATOR is the discriminator, and the site list is diffed at FILE granularity because the printed line numbers are wrong (see `divsweeplines`).  WHAT TO WEIGH WHEN IT IS TAKEN: a two-sided BAND, or equality-with-ritual. Both are semantic changes; neither may ride a re-pin.

rows.title: A round can ship without writing back, and no gate can see it
rows.witness: none
rows.note: *** MEASURED 2026-08-29: a complete pass-1 brief was written and NINE SEATS FIRED to redo work that had shipped two days earlier as #479/#480/#481/#482. ***  Three dev_wdc.c rows carried a full 9/9 RESEARCH stage; the work shipped under four commit numbers; ZERO entries landed back on the rows; the ledger froze at 'in work'; and the main loop, correctly treating the ledger as the queue, drafted a fresh brief.  The brief's own 'mandatory' mutant was already in the preserved kill table, KILLED.  **The CHANGELOG knew -- its Round 479 block names all three row ids -- and the ledger did not.**  *** THE EXISTING GATES ARE BLIND TO THIS BY CONSTRUCTION. ***  precommit section H reads LEDGER ENTRIES and SKIPS STAGES THAT NEVER STARTED; the implement and review stages never started on those rows.  So a round that ships without writing back cannot be seen by the check built to notice missing panel coverage.  This is the unread-review class one step worse: an unrecorded ROUND.  TAKEN ALREADY (2026-08-29): a §C0 block in BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md -- two commands, `git log -1 -- <file>` and `grep <rowid> CHANGELOG.md`, pasted into the brief's settled premises.  It lives in the TEMPLATE because the carrier's own finding is that the one piece of prose which demonstrably fires is the one in the artifact present at the moment of decision.  FILED HERE, NOT BUILT: a checker warning when a row id named in a CHANGELOG round block is still 'in work' with no post-ship entry.  Existence-only, forward-only from a cutoff, owing two negative controls (a staged unrecorded round must warn; a properly-closed row must not).  **It changes what every commit must pass, so it is an owner decision rather than a round's** -- and this project has measured that a checker policing a minority of a class while alarming on prose gets switched off, so the population it would fire on should be counted before it is written.

entries.note: *** CONFIRMED THE GHOST ROUND AND THEN FOUND A LIVE HIGH-SEVERITY DEFECT THE PANEL WAS NOT CONVENED FOR. ***  Settled the premise by `git log -S'wdc_new_command_reset'`, quoted the shipped helper verbatim, and named both preserved kill tables (13/13 and 10/10).  Then MEASURED nine mutants in a scratch tree at 128 rows baseline: SEVEN KILLED including the per-SITE partial resets (`MdAltRingOnly`, `MdAltWipOnly`, `MdAltNoRing` -- the ALT-CTRL site resetting a strict subset) and `MdNoFlag`, which drops `atapi_cmd_in_progress`, **a fourth tenant NEITHER shipped table enumerates**, and still dies 6 red.  TWO ESCAPED AND IT PROVED THEM EQUIVALENT RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT: a positional differential showed `MdRingDrain`/`MdRingRewind` leave head/tail at 777 vs 0 while occupancy, capacity and readback are byte-identical -- the inbuf is a correct circular buffer, so position is unobservable.  **It then drew the consequence against the anchor rule: clause (f)'s reviewer check answers NONE for the ring and that is CORRECT here, because nothing in the device can observe the shift; an anchored ring row would be the addition licence's 'it cannot hurt'.**  THE FINDING THAT BECAME A ROW: `#481` widened offset-1 aliasing from a harmless signature latch into a FULL SOFT RESET.  `DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc_altstatus)` reads `relative_addr` ZERO times over a TWO-BYTE region, so a guest write to `0x3f7` -- the READ-ONLY Drive Address Register -- aborts a live ATA write and purges 40 queued bytes.  **#481's OWN committed artifact already measured it at rung 3** and no row carried it.  Filed as `wdcaltoffset`, sev=high.  Also: the kill drivers score a CRASH as a result -- `build_run` checks the COMPILE status, then runs the mutant and greps FAIL lines without reading the run's exit status or the `WDC_IDENTIFY_PASS` sentinel, so a mutant that dies partway is scored by how far it got.  Not hypothetical here: `write_in_progress` and `write_count` are set together and CLEARED AT DIFFERENT SITES, and the drain guard divides by `512 * d->write_count` -- an operand swap leaving the flag while zeroing the count is a SIGFPE.  **It disclosed its own violation**: wrote one file into the tree against instruction, removed it, and verified `git status` and the `dev_wdc.c` md5 afterwards.

*** RULED THE ROUND ALREADY RAN, AND RULED AGAINST ITS OWN RECOMMENDATION IN THE SAME ANSWER. ***  Reconstructed the chronology from the repo: the 10:36 matrix, then `#479` at 12:18 shipping F-narrow, `#480`'s L2 call-site fix, `#481` closing the ALT-CTRL gap, `#482` splitting the joint row into four one-tenant rows.  A3: **the standing RED row it had itself recommended is DEAD** -- '`a permanently red row is the dual of this project's check-that-cannot-fail -- a check that cannot PASS`', and it violates the blanks rule since a deliberate red and a regression red render identically.  `#481` closed the gap instead, which is better.  It gave the disclosure ladder in order: close the gap; else an accept/tripwire row pinning today's behaviour GREEN; else prose plus a FILED item.  A2: **corrected MY premise** -- `#492` did NOT touch `dev_wdc.c` (`git show d9efd33 -- src/devices/dev_wdc.c` is empty); it touched a checker.  It then checked the interaction precisely and found the two detectors cover DISJOINT mutant classes, so both are needed.  A5: the witness string is defective THREE ways -- a stale count, `probe:` where `detector:` was adopted for exactly this shape (the mis-scoring `check_witness.py`'s own header calls laundering), and the rung-3 accept probe owed its own clause.  It required PER-ROW CARRIER NAMING or three closures are mutually indistinguishable, which is the overtaken-row rule's condition 2 unmet.  It named the structural remedy that was adopted: a BRIEF_TEMPLATE settled-premise line, because the carrier's own finding is that the prose which fires is the prose in the artifact present at the moment of decision.

Caught it independently while grepping the ledger, and surfaced `wdcaltwidth` -- an OPEN row with ZERO entries about the alt-ctrl register's access width -- which is what made me check whether the 'ALT-CTRL gap' was already filed under another name.  That check is what kept the round from filing one defect twice.  Its wall grep flagged it as walled and it was a FALSE POSITIVE: every match was codex QUOTING ledger rows whose notes record old seat-wall history.

Caught it, and corrected a SECOND premise of mine in the same breath: **'Two rounds have shipped since' is false as a bound** -- after the matrix came #479, #480, #481, #482 and more.  It opened by pinning session start to HEAD `d9efd33` before answering anything.

Caught it, and its reasoning is visible in the transcript as it happens: 'the fix `wdc_new_command_reset()` is ALREADY IN THE TREE -- this is #479/#480/#481 ... So the tree ALREADY contains the fix?  That would mean this round's work is already done.'
Caught it, treating F-narrow as 'the historical Pass 1 context (#479)' rather than as a live proposal.

*** COULD NOT CATCH THE GHOST ROUND, AND THAT IS NOT A SEAT FAILURE. ***  A ghost round is a REPO FACT, and a packet-fed seat can only know what the brief inlines -- the brief asserted 'PASS 1, before any edit' and it could not check that.  Recording this as a failure would be exactly the conflation the pipeline doctrine forbids.
As glm: structurally unable to settle a repo fact from a packet.  Its answer is about the design as briefed, and is sound on that scope.

As glm and deepseek.  **The three packet-fed seats failing to catch this, while all four file-reading seats caught it, is the FILE-READING vs PACKET-FED distinction confirmed by measurement rather than asserted** -- and it is the clearest instance this project has recorded.

rows.title: wdc alt-ctrl: a guest write to the READ-ONLY Drive Address Register aborts a live transfer and purges the ring
rows.witness: probe:regress/artifacts/wdcaltoffset/witness_20260829/ -- RUNG 3 on unmodified `evbmips -e malta`, reached through the machine's own committed piix4_ide path with no device_add, free-running, with BOTH controls (RAM liveness through identical instruction shapes, and a device signature: two reads of one address returning push order, which a memory cell cannot do).  Sentinel ALTOFF_DONE.  The SHIPPED fix was then re-measured against it at 18 rows, both legs, 36 of 36 predictions -- killtable_20260830/RESULTS_detector18.txt, sentinel ALTOFF_DET_DONE.  (RESULTS_shipped.txt is the 15-row witness at 30/30 and must not be cited for 36/36; a seat caught that citation error from the log itself.)
rows.note: *** LIVE IN THE SHIPPED TREE, MEASURED AT RUNG 3, AND ITS WITNESS WAS ALREADY COMMITTED -- by `#481`, the round that made it worse. ***  Found by the opus5 seat on a panel convened for an unrelated (and already shipped) round; every element re-verified before filing.  `DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc_altstatus)` **never reads `relative_addr`** -- measured, ZERO uses in the handler -- while the region is registered TWO BYTES WIDE.  Offset 0 is Device Control (`0x3f6`).  **Offset 1 is the Drive Address Register (`0x3f7`), which is READ-ONLY on real ATA hardware** and on many platforms is shared with the floppy controller.  So the handler cannot distinguish a write to a writable control register from a write to a read-only one, and treats both identically.  *** `#481` WIDENED THE CONSEQUENCE FROM HARMLESS TO DESTRUCTIVE. ***  Before it, the arm tested `WDCTL_4BIT`, so a `0x06` write did nothing at either offset -- the aliasing existed but was a harmless signature latch.  `#481` corrected the bit to `WDCTL_RST` and wired in `wdc_new_command_reset()`, which was RIGHT for offset 0 and turned offset 1 into a full soft reset.  Measured, same scenario on both builds (a live `WDCC_WRITE` with 40 bytes queued, then a one-byte `0x06` write):  pre-#481 (`867c697^`) offset 1 -> `cur_command 0x30  wip 0x30  occ 40` (untouched); HEAD offset 1 -> `cur_command 0x100  wip 0x0  occ 0` -- **the live ATA write is aborted and 40 queued guest bytes are purged**.  AND THE RUNG-3 WITNESS IS ALREADY IN THE TREE, committed by #481 itself at `.../rung3_witness/rung3_offset.txt`: a guest writing 0x06 to `0x180003f7` leaves `cyl=0x6655` unchanged pre-fix and `cyl=0xeb14` after.  *** SO A MEASUREMENT EXISTS, IS PRESERVED AT A DURABLE PATH, AND NO ROW CARRIED IT -- the unread-review class one level down, on a LIVE defect. ***  `wdcaltwidth` CANNOT ABSORB THIS and must not be used to: it is about access WIDTH (`len == 1` rows against a 2-byte region) and carries witness `none -- filed from a reading of the registration, no measurement yet`.  **Width and offset DECODE are different claims**, and merging them would be the queue-id-covering-two-defects shape that closing one buries the other.  SEVERITY: `high` and set deliberately -- this is guest-reachable, needs no harness, destroys queued guest data, and the register it fires on is one a correct guest may legitimately WRITE to expecting nothing to happen.  Note the fix is NOT to revert `#481`, which corrected a real bit error; it is to make the handler decode its offset.  *** CORRECTION 2026-08-30 (L4), AGAINST THIS NOTE'S OWN WORDS, BY THE opus5 SEAT'S PREMISE AUDIT. ***  The sentence above calls the pre-`#481` aliasing `a harmless signature latch`.  **That is true of the witness's value and false as a characterisation.**  Pre-`#481` the arm was `if (idata & WDCTL_4BIT) d->cur_command = COMMAND_RESET;` -- and `WDCTL_4BIT` (0x08) is libata's STEADY-STATE `ap->ctl`, as `#481`'s own comment records.  So a store to offset 1 carrying the common case already clobbered `cur_command` and latched a bogus ATAPI signature.  The witness value 0x06 is `WDCTL_RST|WDCTL_IDS` and has bit 3 CLEAR, so for 0x06 specifically the claim holds -- **which is exactly the dropped-qualifier class: a property measured on one value, restated as a property of the arm.**  What `#481` changed is WHICH bit triggers it and it ADDED the ring purge; severity rose, but `harmless` never obtained.  Note this is the same channel m3 escapes on, which is why a signature row could measure it at all.

entries.note: *** RUNG-3 WITNESS BUILT, DURABLE AND RE-RUNNABLE -- the first this defect has ever had. ***  Its two prior measurements could not be re-run: `#481` preserved 201 bytes of OUTPUT with no driver, and a later HEAD measurement lived in a /tmp tree its own script deleted.  **VERDICT: `On the COMMITTED build phase 1 and phase 2 are BYTE-IDENTICAL`** -- a guest store to `0x3f6` (Device Control) and to `0x3f7` (Drive Address Register, READ-ONLY on real ATA hardware) produce identical results.  On the fix leg they separate.  30 of 30 row predictions; encodings 122/122 and 122/122; both legs parked.  BOTH LADDER CONTROLS, several times over and green on BOTH legs: LIVENESS -- a RAM round-trip (0x55) and a cyl readback (0x6655, reusing #481's own idiom), plus a DRQ-armed check per phase; DEVICE-SIGNATURE -- the data port reading as a FIFO (0x5a then 0xa5, so not a memory cell) and a status byte the DEVICE computes (0x51).  RAM would answer differently to every one.  **EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: the READ path is untouched, so the ONLY variable between the two legs is the aliased STORE.**  *** THE FIX LEG IS LABELLED `WITNESS FIX LEG ONLY -- NOT a proposed shipped fix`, and that distinction is kept. ***  It exists to prove the witness DISCRIMINATES, not to pre-decide the design; what the shipped fix should be is the panel's question.  The leg declines the store at offset 1 with a diagnostic and leaves the read path alone.

*** FOUND THE FACT THAT REFUTED THE ADJUDICATOR, and found it from the other side of the collision. ***  Read `wdcreg.h` and saw that `wd_digin` sits inside `#if 0 /* NOT MAPPED; fd uses this register on PCs */` -- so the header defines ONE aux register, not two. rows.title: Kill drivers score a CRASHED mutant as a table result
rows.witness: harness:read from the drivers' own source
rows.note: Found by the opus5 seat while measuring an unrelated round.  `kill479.sh`'s `build_run` checks the COMPILE exit status, then runs the mutant binary and pipes straight to `grep -c '^  FAIL'` -- **it never reads the RUN's exit status, nor the `WDC_IDENTIFY_PASS` sentinel the detector already emits.**  A mutant that dies partway through is therefore scored `KILLED (n red)` or `*ESCAPED* (clean sweep)` purely by HOW FAR IT GOT.  *** NOT HYPOTHETICAL FOR THIS DEVICE, and the shape is one edit away. ***  `write_in_progress` and `write_count` are set together in `wdc__write()` but CLEARED AT DIFFERENT SITES -- the reset helper clears the flag, only a completed drain clears the count -- and the drain guard divides: `inbuf_len % (512 * d->write_count) == 0`.  A clause-(d) operand swap that leaves the flag standing while zeroing the count is a MODULO BY ZERO.  Today the `&&` short-circuit saves it; a driver blind to exit status would report the SIGFPE as a table result.  CENSUS, with its limitation stated because it is the same defect one level up: 16 kill/measure drivers examined; **7 mention no sentinel at all**, and all seven are the 2026-08-27 wdc-family drivers (`killalt.sh`, `kill482`, `kill480`, `kill480b`, `kill477b`, `kill479`, `kill478`).  Every GD-ROM driver from 08-28 onward does check one, so the practice improved and the older drivers were never retrofitted.  *** THE CENSUS COUNTS MENTIONS, NOT CHECKS, AND IS THEREFORE A CANDIDATE LIST RATHER THAN A COUNT. ***  A driver that merely ECHOES a sentinel at the end scores as having one -- my own `killrow5c.sh` does exactly that.  Emitting a sentinel is not reading one.  Confirming each of the seven needs the driver opened.  *This is the round's own recurring defect -- counting a textual form where a property was meant -- committed inside the census that reports it.*  REMEDY: two columns, EXIT and SENT, in each driver's row output.  The opus5 seat already ran its own table that way and every mutant came back clean, so nothing measured today was mis-scored -- but the drivers cannot tell.  Cheap, and the rule already exists: *a preserved log is verified by its COMPLETION SENTINEL, not by its existence.*  *** CONFIRMED BY READING ONE OF EACH, rather than by the mention-count. ***  `kill479.sh`'s run path is three lines: `if [ $? -ne 0 ]` (the COMPILE), then `"$O/$2" > "$O/$2.out" 2>&1` (runs the mutant), then `grep -c '^  FAIL'` -- **the run's status is never captured between those two lines.**  By contrast `kill489d.sh` (GD-ROM, 08-28) extracts STRUCTURED RESULT TOKENS with `grep -o 'TOCLEN_RESULT=[0-9]*/[0-9]*' | tail -1`, so a truncated run yields a MISSING token rather than a plausible score.  **That is the difference worth copying: not 'check the exit code' but 'score from a token the run only emits when it finishes'** -- the same discriminator the completion-sentinel rule already states, applied to the scorer instead of to the log reader.  *** ONE DRIVER FIXED 2026-08-30, AND IT WAS THE ONE WRITTEN AFTER THIS ROW WAS FILED. ***  `killtable_20260830/killswap.sh` -- authored during `wdcatapistswap`, hours after this row named the class -- read NEITHER the run exit status NOR the completion sentinel.  It was PARTLY protected by accident: a missing prediction count already refused.  But the probe prints that count BEFORE its differential section and its sentinel, **so a crash in the gap scored normally** -- narrower window, same class.  It now refuses any run that did not reach `ADDTOINBUF_RUNG3_DONE`.  NEGATIVE CONTROL, and it is the one that matters for a tightening: all THIRTEEN preserved kill logs from that round carry the sentinel -- **including M7, whose guest deliberately never parks** -- so the new check rejects nothing that legitimately scored.  A gate that refuses valid runs is worse than no gate.  *The row STAYS OPEN*: the census names seven drivers with no sentinel check at all and this fixes one of them, in a file that did not exist when the census ran.  **The instructive part is that the class was FILED and the very next driver written in this project reproduced it** -- the carrier's own trigger-versus-memory finding, with a four-hour gap between the writing-down and the repetition.  *** A NEW MEMBER, ADDED 2026-08-31 BY CHECKING RATHER THAN BY WAITING FOR IT TO BITE: `#499`'s `table499.sh` HAS THE DEFECT, AND ITS TABLE IS NEVERTHELESS VERIFIED CLEAN. ***  Both halves matter and they are different claims.  **The DRIVER has it.**  `table499.sh` checks three things and none of them is the run: variant-generation rc (`VARIANT GEN FAILED ... ABORT`), binary existence (`NO BINARY -- ABORT`), and build freshness (`build: STALE -- ABORT`, the two-part clearance).  It then runs the detector and scores the output **without reading the run's exit status or the `DETECTOR_DONE` sentinel the detector already emits**.  A mutant that died partway would be scored by how far it got -- `KILLED` or `ESCAPED` depending on where it stopped.  *Note the driver is careful about the BUILD and blind to the RUN; that is the class's signature, and it is why an otherwise disciplined driver has it.*  **The TABLE is unaffected, and that was MEASURED, not assumed.**  Counting sentinels against score lines in the three committed logs: `table499.out` 6 `DETECTOR_DONE` / 6 `SCORE`; `extra_rows.out` 4 `EXTRA_DONE` / 4 `XSCORE`; `m5.out` 1 / 1.  **Every variant that produced a score also produced its completion sentinel**, so no row in `#499` rests on a truncated run.  *This is the cheap form of the repair available to any round TODAY, without touching a driver: the sentinel count and the score count must be equal, and that is one `grep -c` each.  The driver-side fix -- abort on a missing sentinel -- remains this row's work.*  **Census update: the candidate list is no longer only the 2026-08-27 wdc family.**  The practice was recorded as improving from 08-28 onward, and a driver written on 08-31 by the seat that FOUND this defect still has it -- which says the lesson lives in the finder's head rather than in a template.  That is this project's structure-versus-prose finding again, and it argues for a shared driver preamble rather than another round of care.

rows.title: wdc alt-ctrl: a READ of the Drive Address register returns the alt-status byte, which matches no hardware on any layout
rows.witness: none -- but the DEFECT is witnessed and the fix is not.  A seat measured the wrong value at rung 3; what is missing is an ORACLE for the right one.
rows.note: Split from `wdcaltoffset` (#494) DELIBERATELY, and the split is the record that matters: #494 fixed the STORE half only, because its witness holds the read path byte-identical so the aliased store is the only variable.  Shipping a read fix under that number would have claimed coverage the witness was designed not to provide.  *** THE DEFECT IS WITNESSED AND CHEAPLY SO -- WHICH REFUTES THE RULING THAT IT HAS NO ORACLE. ***  Two adjudications held the read half unfixable for want of a bit layout (bit 7 high-impedance, write-gate representation, active-low drive/head select).  The opus5 seat refuted that by measuring, and the reason is that **the test is an INVARIANCE, not a value**: `status_byte()` never reads `d->head`, and a Drive Address register is by definition a function of head select.  On the committed build, reading 0x3f7 gives 51 at head=0 AND 51 at head=15 -- invariant -- while the SDH readback of 0xaf proves the head write landed and 0x3f6 is unchanged by it, so the invariance is not `nothing moved`.  That refutes every candidate model of 0x3f7 without naming a single expected bit.  *** WHAT IS STILL MISSING IS THE FIX'S ORACLE, NOT THE DEFECT'S. ***  An invariance proves today's value WRONG without saying what is RIGHT, and none of the fifteen PDFs under `_scratchpad/` is an ATA or ISA document -- `ls _scratchpad/*.pdf` is the authority, not this note.  Pinning digin's bits from model memory is exactly the #357/#362/#365 failure this project already paid for.  AND THE OWNERSHIP QUESTION MAY DISSOLVE IT: on a PC the byte belongs to the FLOPPY controller (see `wdcaltownership`), in which case the right answer is not a wdc value at all.  Settle ownership first.  SCOPE NOTE: the model does hold the raw material -- `case wd_sdh` latches `d->sectorsize`, `d->lba`, `d->drive` and `d->head` from the stored byte -- so ACCEPT is structurally available here in a way it was NOT for the store half, where there is no discarded right answer.  ARTIFACT, added on the fable5 seat's requirement that these numbers name their log: `regress/artifacts/wdcaltoffset/mutants_20260830/TABLE_B.txt` (sentinel `TABLE_B_DONE`).  It also records a SECOND refutation the summary above omits -- a read of 0x3f7 returns 58 with DRQ raised, and **a real Drive Address register never carries DRQ**, so the read is tracking the status register on a channel independent of the head-invariance argument.

rows.title: 0x3f6/0x3f7 are contested between wdc and the floppy controller, and the tree documents the collision from BOTH sides while resolving it from neither
rows.witness: none -- a device-topology design question, not a bounds defect.  No measurement is owed until a disposition is chosen.
rows.note: Filed by #494, which REJECTED narrowing the alt region and owes the reader the reason rather than a silence.  **The tree says twice that these bytes are contested, and the two statements do not agree with each other.**  `src/include/thirdparty/wdcreg.h` compiles the aux-region offset-1 define out entirely, under `#if 0` with the annotation *NOT MAPPED; fd uses this register on PCs* -- i.e. the wdc does not own it.  `src/devices/dev_fdc.c` carries `#define DEV_FDC_LENGTH 6` with the comment *TODO 8, but collision with wdc*, registered at `isa_portbase + 0x3f0` -- i.e. the FLOPPY is the one being truncated.  *** THE ARITHMETIC IS WHY NARROWING WAS REJECTED, and it is the whole finding: fdc's stated end-state of 8 ports is 0x3f0..0x3f7 and the alt region is 0x3f6..0x3f7, so the OVERLAP IS TWO BYTES, not one. ***  Narrowing wdc to 1 byte frees 0x3f7 and still blocks fdc at 0x3f6, which wdc must keep.  So the end-state is a two-device ARBITRATION design, not a width flip -- narrowing as proposed would have fixed half a collision and called it done.  Derived by the fable5 adjudicator on re-ruling; arithmetic re-checked before filing.  A second reason narrowing is not free, MEASURED by the opus5 seat: an unmapped access faults nothing and the guest parks normally, but it emits one `non-existant paddr` warning PER ACCESS with no latch and no counter (the floodclass shape, guest-drivable at default verbosity), a read then returns 0x00 silently, and under `-T` it sets `running = 0` on EVERY cpu.  HONEST BOUND, because the disposition is not obvious: generic ATA DOES define a read-only Drive Address register at that port, so the `#if 0` annotation is a PC-MAPPING decision by its own wording and is unsettled on the three non-PC layouts this device also serves (macppc +0x160, hpcmips 0x14000386, iq80321 +0x402).  Whatever is decided must claim only what it covers.  Blocks `wdcaltdigin`: if the byte is the floppy's, the right read value is not a wdc value at all.

rows.title: the no-VPATH rule has FOUR build trees and precommit section B enforces only three -- the WSL arc tree is invisible to it
rows.witness: harness:three-state negative control on the SHIPPED lines -- green in sync, RED on a one-line divergence, SKIP when absent; preserved at regress/artifacts/wdcatapistswap/killtable_20260830/CONTROL_novpadfourth.out
rows.note: **Found by a measuring seat, not by a check, and that is the whole finding.**  `precommit_check.sh` section B compares `build/` and `build-asan/` against SEC because they sit under the Windows project root and it can walk them.  **`/tmp/gxsec-build` lives in the WSL filesystem and the Windows-side checker never sees it.**  So the carrier's own no-VPATH rule -- *propagate every edit into them or you measure a stale binary* -- names four trees while the gate enforces three.  **Why it is worse than an unchecked tree**: scratch clones are made FROM these trees.  A clone of a stale donor `cmp`s CLEAN against its donor and carries no sentinel, so the two-part clearance passes on it -- the stale-binary trap reached from a direction the sentinel discipline cannot cover, exactly as the carrier already records for a different route.  Here it would have measured `#494`-less code in the file `#494` edited.  REMEDY, and it is not obviously a checker: section B would have to reach across the WSL boundary, which is a different kind of check from every other one it does.  The cheaper form may be a `wslpropagate.sh` invocation in the round-boundary step beside the existing two-part clearance -- structure where the decision happens, rather than a checker that cannot see the thing it checks.  A script exists (`regress/artifacts/wdcaltoffset/killtable_20260830/wslpropagate.sh`) and ran clean; what is missing is the obligation to run it.  *** CLOSED 2026-08-30.  THE OBSTACLE THIS ROW RESTED ON DOES NOT EXIST, AND ONE COMMAND SETTLED IT. ***  The row stayed open on the assumption that a WSL tree is unreachable from the Windows-side gate.  **It is reachable**: `//wsl.localhost/Gentoo/tmp/gxsec-build` reads fine from git-bash, and a `cmp` across that boundary completes in **83 ms**.  The check was never written; nothing was ever preventing it.  `precommit_check.sh` now carries a fourth section mirroring the build-asan one: `.MUTANT` sentinel row, then a `cmp` per changed `src/` file, keyed on `${GXWSLTREE}` so it is testable without touching the real tree.  **ABSENCE SKIPS FOR TWO REASONS RATHER THAN ONE**, and the second is new: the tree may never have been built, OR the distro may simply not be running, in which case the UNC path is unreadable and nothing is wrong.  A gate that hard-fails because a VM is asleep is a gate that gets switched off.  CONTROLLED IN THREE STATES, on the SHIPPED LINES rather than a retyped copy -- the control extracts the block from `precommit_check.sh` by grep anchor and drives it with a synthetic file list, because this round edits no `src/` file and the real list would leave the loop empty:  (1) real tree in sync -> GREEN;  (2) a copy whose `dev_wdc.c` differs by ONE LINE -> **RED**, which is the control that matters because without it the section is a claim rather than a check;  (3) absent tree -> SKIP, not fail.  *** AND THE CONTROL'S OWN FIRST DRAFT FAILED IN THE CLASS THIS PROJECT KEEPS RECORDING. ***  Its awk range ended on the block's last MESSAGE (`rows skipped, not failed`) and stopped ONE LINE SHORT of the closing `fi`, so `eval` died with 'unexpected end of file'.  Re-anchored on `^fi$`.  **A range that ends on prose ends wherever the prose happens to sit** -- and the extraction prints its own line count, so a range that selects almost nothing is refused rather than run.

rows.title: the #495 guard's flag operand can be swapped for `atapi_st != NULL` and the detector cannot see it -- measured to refuse every ordinary data-port write for the life of the device
rows.witness: harness:BOTH HALVES MEASURED IN THIS ROUND, not transcribed -- the COMMITTED probe cannot see the swap (LEG 0: 22/22 ESCAPED) and the EXTENDED probe kills it (E2: 26/30, 4 red).  Logs at regress/artifacts/wdcatapistswap/killtable_20260830/ (TABLE.txt, kill_L0_committed_probe.out, kill_E2.out).  *** REPLACED, not appended: the previous field read 'probe:measured by the pass-2 measuring seat --...' -- a `probe:` prefix that check_witness.py scores as RUNG 3, which that file's own header calls laundering for a round whose subject is the test apparatus; and its 20/20 figure disagreed with its own note ("all 22 rows") while the artifact it cited no longer existed.  Named by the fable5 seat.
rows.note: *** AN OPERAND SWAP THAT ESCAPES ALL 22 ROWS, AND THE SEAT MEASURED THE DAMAGE RATHER THAN REASONING IT. ***  Replace `d->atapi_cmd_in_progress` in `#495`'s guard with `d->atapi_st != NULL`.  Pre-packet push/pop pair reads `5a,a5` on both legs; **post-packet it reads `5a,a5` shipped versus `ff,ff` under the swap** -- refused, empty-ring over-read.  **THE MECHANISM, READ FROM SOURCE: `atapi_st` is allocated at the first dispatch and NEVER set back to NULL.**  `wdc_new_command_reset()` zeroes the flag, the phase, `write_in_progress` and the ring pointers, and does not touch it.  So after ONE ATAPI command the swapped guard refuses every ordinary data-port write for the life of the device.  **NOT a clause-(d) breach by the letter of the DEPENDS-ON bound** -- `atapi_st` is not read by the guarded body, so the operand-swap enumeration does not reach it -- which is why this files rather than being repaired in-round.  What it shows is that the detector's ACCEPT side is unpinned for ordinary non-ATAPI writes: no row asserts that a plain data-port write still lands after a packet command has completed.  **IT IS NOT A CONTRIVED MUTANT.**  `dev_wdc.c`'s own comment files exactly this refactor, recording that `atapi_cmd_in_progress` *conflates two roles* -- so a future round separating them could write this swap believing it a simplification.  REMEDY: one accept row -- an ordinary data-port write after a completed packet command, asserted to land.  *** CORRECTED IN PLACE 2026-08-30, PASS 1 OF THE ROUND THAT CLOSES THIS ROW. THE STATE THIS NOTE NAMES CANNOT EXIST. ***  The note says the differential runs *post-packet*, reading `5a,a5` shipped versus `ff,ff` swapped, with no command in between.  A packet-fed seat challenged that from the inlined facts alone and it is right: `atapi_cmd_in_progress` has exactly TWO write sites -- cleared in `wdc_new_command_reset()`, set at the packet dispatch -- and **no completion path clears it** (the completion arm sets `PHASE_COMPLETED` and leaves the flag; the only `memset(d, 0, ...)` is devinit).  So immediately after a transfer the flag is still 1, **the SHIPPED guard refuses too**, both legs read `ff`, and the differential as described would show no difference at all.  **THE MEASUREMENT IS NOT DISPUTED -- the recorded STATE is.**  The seat's run almost certainly carried an intervening command that this summary dropped; that is being put to the seat directly rather than assumed.  *** THE CORRECTION STRENGTHENS THE REMEDY RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT. ***  The states where the two builds differ are exactly `flag == 0 && atapi_st != NULL`, and ONLY a command can produce them, because the reset is the sole writer of `flag = 0` while `atapi_st` has one write site and no clear site.  So the accept row's clearing command is LOAD-BEARING, not scene-setting -- the naive post-packet form of this row would have been VACUOUS, green on both legs, and would have shipped looking like coverage.  *** CLOSED 2026-08-30 in `e61ccd8`.  WHAT ARRIVED AS 'one accept row' LEFT AS TWO VEHICLES, THREE ACCESS WIDTHS AND A REPAIRED FLOOR -- every step forced by a seat rather than chosen. ***  THE ARMS: M (after `WDCC_RECAL`) and N (after `ATAPI_SOFT_RESET`), two rows each.  The second vehicle exists because with one, `&& d->cur_command != WDCC_RECAL` re-opens the hole and sweeps every row -- one conjunct cannot exempt two opcodes.  MEASURED: E3 reds the N rows and leaves the M rows green.  TWELVE LEGS, 15 rows / 30 predictions, every score generated from TABLE.txt rather than transcribed.  **Both halves of the harness proof are results of THIS round**: the COMMITTED probe cannot see the swap (LEG 0, 22/22 ESCAPED) and the EXTENDED one kills it (E2, 26/30, 4 red).  The inherited escape figure was re-measured because its artifact had vanished and the row disagreed with itself.  TWELVE OF TWELVE PREDICTIONS, written before the table ran, confirmed -- one after being corrected: M7 was predicted green on the accept rows, and a seat refuted it before any build because M7's guard fires at the DATA-IN injection and the guest never parks.  **The arms are UNREACHED, not inert**; measured 15/30.  A prediction about a row's VALUE presumes the row RUNS.  *** AND THE ROUND'S LAST PREDICTION BECAME A MEASUREMENT: E6. ***  The claim that the SECOND row of each pair is not redundant rested on an unbuilt mutant that -- unlike E2 and E5 -- sits INSIDE clause (d)'s enumeration.  Built and run alone: 26/30, 4 red, and exactly the predicted asymmetry.  The FIRST row of each pair stays GREEN (the ring genuinely is empty at that push) and only the SECOND reds.  A CLAUSE-(d) FLOOR BREACH WAS FOUND AND REPAIRED HERE: `&& len != 4` swept the whole detector while restoring the defect.  One instruction, no new row -- a 4-byte `sw` -- kills E4, M3 and M6 together, and the probe turned out to have NO 4-byte emitter at all, so the device's `case 4:` WRITE arm had never executed on any leg of any run.  Filed as `wdcwidth4`, now closed.  PASS 2 FOUND FOUR WRONG RECORDS IN WHAT THIS ROUND HAD ALREADY WRITTEN, all mine: a FALSE evidence table (the `a5/5a/00` bytes came from a probe whose injection had been widened, not from E4 against this instrument -- found by opening the log); the probe calling a repaired escape 'Filed' with the repair in the same diff; clause (e) breached because the contract was written at the 13-row stage and the round grew past it; and a phase-write census of FIVE where there are SEVEN, because the grep could not match two assignments SPLIT ACROSS LINES.  *** AND THE ROUND COMMITTED ITS OWN CONCURRENCY DEFECT: two kill-table runs alive together, both writing one scratch tree, the second's `rm -rf` wiping the first's. ***  The twelve-leg table survived only because the output filename had been parameterised an hour earlier.  That is now STRUCTURAL -- a subset run with no TABLETAG is REFUSED rather than trusted to remember.  *** af62a06 NAMED AFTER THE FACT, AND THE GATE IS WHAT NOTICED. ***  The row closed naming only `e61ccd8`, but the regress-review commit also edits this row's code -- the probe's LEG-1 banner, and `killswap.sh`'s untagged copy-back and missing sentinel check.  A closed row must name every commit that touches its code, and the check refused the NEXT commit until it did.  *That is the second time today this rule fired, after `census`/`e3cf79f`.  It is a good rule precisely because follow-up commits to a just-closed row are the easiest attribution to lose: the round feels finished.*

entries.ev: [panel_20260830_124335]  wdcatapistswap pass 1 on the design brief, READ seat
entries.note: *** RAN THE WHOLE TABLE ON REAL BINARIES: nine mutants, scratch clones only, base-leg apparatus check on all fourteen runs. ***  Confirmed ALL EIGHT of the brief's predictions, M7 in its grok-corrected form, with red-counts matching the PRETABLE's arithmetic at every mutant.  *** THEN FOUND E4 -- `&& len != 4` -- SWEEPING 30/30 WHILE RESTORING THE DEFECT BYTE-FOR-BYTE. ***  Rows G/H/I return the injected a5/5a/00, identical to the PRE-FIX build, against the fix's real disk content c2/c3/c4: the guest is handed its own bytes AS DISK DATA and the detector scores clean.  **It DISSENTED on disposition and the dissent is correct**: `if (X)` -> `if (X && Y)` on the predicate #495 ADDED, which DOMINATES the edited lines, is clause (d)'s canonical form, and #488's adjudication names that exact shape a floor breach.  Filed as coverage debt by an earlier seat; RE-DISPOSITIONED to L2 and repaired in-round.  It derived the CLOSURE CONDITION rather than guessing: `&& P(len)` escapes iff P is true on every INJECTED width and false on some IMPLEMENTED width, so only {1,2,4} closes the family.  Repair is ONE instruction and NO new row -- a 4-byte `sw` -- and it kills E4, M3 and M6 together.  *** AND THE PROBE HAD NO 4-BYTE EMITTER AT ALL: the device's `case 4:` arm and its whole `consumed` accounting had never executed on any leg of any run this detector ever made. ***  Not an uncovered mutant -- an uncovered ARM.  E5 (`cur_command == ATAPI_PKT_CMD`) also sweeps 30/30 and the N arm does NOT defeat it: it REPLACES the flag operand rather than exempting an opcode, so both vehicles leave it green.  Filed as `wdcflagswap2`, ranked below E4 because its harm is over-refusal and transient.  It also narrowed what the arm buys: rows B and M differ in ONE readable dimension, so E2 is their only UNIQUE kill and *'the accept side is pinned' is measurably false*.  Confirmed the `WORDS_OK` dead check independently, caught a wrong record in kill495_M7.sh, and flagged this loop's own killswap.sh appearing while its table built.

entries.ev: [panel_20260830_124335]  wdcatapistswap pass 1 on the design brief, READ seat
entries.note: Went clause by clause and ruled the arm's channel VALID, `harness:` the right witness term, and the design sound -- then named what was still owed.  **Its headline is an evidence hole the round was about to build on: the E2 escape figure's cited artifact (`opus495/wave2/run_q3.out`) NO LONGER EXISTS**, and the row disagrees with itself -- witness field `20/20`, note `all 22 rows`.  A number that disagrees with itself and whose evidence is gone is a transcription, not a measurement.  **The table now re-measures it as LEG 0** (22/22 ESCAPED on the committed probe), so the escape is a result of this round.  It also caught: clause (a) CANNOT govern an accept row (green on both legs by definition) -- the governing rule is ACCEPT-ROW FAILABILITY, discharged by a MEASURED kill, and claiming clause (a) would have been an unfalsifiable L2 claim; the probe's clause-(e) CONTRACT did not name this family; the header sentence *'THE PROGRAM AND THE ROWS BELOW ARE UNTOUCHED ... measured 20 of 20'* was ALREADY FALSE when committed, because #495 added the J/K/L arm in the same round; the wrong post-packet narrative had an uncorrected SIBLING in OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md whose REMEDY line prescribed the VACUOUS form of this very row; `kill495.sh`'s `WORDS_OK` is computed and referenced nowhere while the script claims the encodings agree; and PRETABLE item (ii) as first worded LICENSED EDITING #495's true records.  It derived two escapes (`wdcwidth4`, `wdcringresetblind`) and named a per-row kill the block had missed: an empty-ring gate passes the FIRST accept row and fails only the SECOND, so the two are not redundant.  It advised splitting the unrelated gate_hygiene edit into its own commit -- done, `e3cf79f`.

entries.ev: [panel_20260830_124335]  wdcatapistswap pass 1 on the design brief, READ seat
entries.note: Started from the repo rather than the brief.  **Refuted one of the eight predictions before the table ran, which is exactly what writing them down is for**: M7 replaces the refusal body with `return 0;`, and the guard FIRES at row E during DATA-IN, so the mutant guest takes EXCEPTION_DBE and never parks -- *the accept arms are UNREACHED, not inert*.  Predicted 15/30 with every register `??`; measured 15/30, 15 red.  A prediction about a row's VALUE presumes the row RUNS.  **And it found the one-conjunct exemption that produced the N arm**: with a single vehicle, `&& d->cur_command != WDCC_RECAL` re-opens the hole and sweeps every row, because after RECAL `cur_command` is 0x10 while during DATA-IN it is still ATAPI_PKT_CMD.  Its remedy -- issue TWO different no-fill commands, since one conjunct cannot exempt two opcodes -- is the M5/M6 lesson on a new axis (WHICH no-fill opcode cleared the flag) and was adopted in-round as the SOFT_RESET arm.  It also caught that REGS was not updated, and that recasting `/22` to `/26` is not a licence to skip the table because the instruction stream and CONTROL 0 counts change.  Looked like a stall at 616 bytes across two samples; the PROCESS was alive and it finished at 11 KB.

entries.ev: [panel_20260830_124335]  wdcatapistswap pass 1 on the design brief, PACKET seat
entries.note: *** REFUTED THE BRIEF'S OWN MECHANISM FROM THE INLINED FACTS ALONE, and it is the finding that saved the row from being vacuous. ***  The brief said the measured hole is a post-packet push/pop with NO COMMAND IN BETWEEN.  It objected that this requires some completion path to clear `atapi_cmd_in_progress`, and named the absence of one as a hole in the narrative.  Checked against the tree and it is right: the flag has exactly TWO write sites and no completion path clears it, so post-transfer the SHIPPED guard refuses too, both legs read ff, and the naive form of this row would have been GREEN ON BOTH LEGS -- shipping as coverage while pinning nothing.  **The clearing command is load-bearing, not scene-setting.**  It also refused to let a register question pass: the draft arm wrote `t3` three times while the brief listed `t3` as live, and it could not tell from a packet whether `t3` is read back.  It is not in REGS, so the draft was safe -- and the sidestep (do the stores through the arm's own output registers) costs the same eight instructions.  Adopted.  **A false concrete claim with a correct recommendation, and the brief's sloppy word `live` is what produced it.**

entries.ev: [panel_20260830_124335]  wdcatapistswap pass 1 on the design brief, PACKET seat
entries.note: **Challenged the brief for inlining the switch without the rest of `wdc_command()`, and was right.**  The function has TWO early returns BEFORE its switch -- a no-disk-image ABRT and a CDROM+WDCC_IDENTIFY ABRT.  This probe attaches a CD image, so IDENTIFY -- the natural choice of clearing command -- would never have reached its case.  RECAL is unaffected and both returns sit AFTER the reset so the flag clears on every path, but the brief had inlined an incomplete function, which is the failure the full-enclosing-function rule names.  Its reasoning is now the recorded warrant for the vehicle choice. rows.title: every wdc rung-3 probe has only a LITTLE-ENDIAN leg, so the big-endian half of each guard is unpinned by construction

A mutant that applies the `#495` guard on the LE path and omits it on the BE path escapes all 22 rows -- measured, 22/22 -- because no row ever executes the other branch.  **The same hole exists for every guard in that switch**, not just this round's: the BE arm is a mirror of the LE arm and nothing walks it.  COVERAGE DEBT, filed rather than fixed: closing it needs a big-endian rig for this device, which is a rig question rather than a row question, and no round has yet needed one. rows.note: *** THE CARRIED NUMBER WAS RIGHT.  MY RECOUNT WAS THE ERROR, AND THE GATE PRINTED THE ANSWER MINUTES AFTER I FILED THE CONTRADICTION. ***  A checkpoint line read *'10 closed rows carry panel entries with no seat outcome'*.  I re-derived it, got **1993 entries across 83 closed rows**, filed this row saying the carried figure was wrong by two orders of magnitude -- and then `precommit_check.sh` said: **`closed rows with panel entries but NO seat outcomes: 10 total`**, followed by *`(51 more are GRANDFATHERED pre-2026-08-23 and not counted above)`*.  **THE TWO NUMBERS COUNT DIFFERENT THINGS AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS THE CLAIM.**  The checker counts CLOSED ROWS, restricted to rows carrying PANEL entries, excluding a grandfather cutoff it applies deliberately.  I counted RAW EMPTY FIELDS over every entry of every closed row, grandfathered and non-panel entries included.  My denominator was never the claim's denominator.  *** THIS IS THE SESSION'S OWN RECURRING DEFECT, COMMITTED INSIDE A ROW ABOUT COUNTING: A TEXTUAL FORM COUNTED WHERE A PROPERTY WAS MEANT. ***  `outcome` being an empty string is a textual form; *'a closed row whose panel work is ungraded'* is the property, and the checker already encodes it -- cutoff and all.  **A count that names neither its unit nor its method cannot be checked, and I wrote one while correcting one.**  *** AND THE CHEAPEST CHECK WAS THE ONE I SKIPPED: ASK WHETHER A TOOL ALREADY COUNTS THIS. ***  `check_bugfile_sync.py`/`seat_scorecard.py` had the definition, the cutoff and the population the whole time.  Re-deriving a number by hand when a checker already derives it does not verify the checker -- it produces a second, unrelated number and an argument.  THE LIVE WORK, which is small and was correctly stated from the start: **ten rows** -- `exitsweep`, `xfamscope`, `m8sarseq`, `wdcnoirq`, `verdictbold`, `gdromdefault`, `asicbadaddr`, `lethalonly` and two more the gate truncates -- need an `outcome` plus `outcome_note` per `seat_scorecard.py`. An unrun check and a completed one must not render the same.  It is the only undated entry in the ledger, and that finding is independent of the miscount.

rows.title: an INEQUALITY width qualifier swept the whole detector -- CLOSED by injecting a third access width, so the width family is closed on both sides
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED both ways -- swept 30/30 before the repair; after it, E4 scores 29/30 with the kill on row L (want 50 got 58, the 4-byte store admitted).  Log: regress/artifacts/wdcatapistswap/killtable_20260830/kill_E4.out
rows.note: *** THE PROBE'S OWN COMMENT CLAIMS THIS FAMILY IS CLOSED, AND IT IS CLOSED ONLY ON ONE SIDE. ***  The K arm says *'No single width qualifier can refuse both'*, having made one injection 2-byte and the other 1-byte so that neither `len == 1` nor `len == 2` can refuse the pair.  **That is true of EQUALITY qualifiers and false of the inequality.**  Append `&& len <= 2` -- equivalently `&& len != 4` -- to the shipped guard and it still refuses BOTH committed injections, so every defect row stays green; row M stays green because the flag is 0 after RECAL; and **4-byte stores to the data port land in the ring during DATA-IN**, which is the defect #495 removed.  The write arm implements `case 4:` explicitly, so this is a width the device supports and no row exercises.  ABOVE-FLOOR COVERAGE DEBT, filed rather than fixed: the shipped detector sits above the vacuity floor and this is a hypothetical edit in an uncovered cell, not a live defect.  REMEDY: a 4-byte injection variant, the natural sibling of `wdcrearmwalk`.  Derived by the fable5 seat on the `wdcatapistswap` pass 1, from the probe's own closure claim -- it asked what the claim was quantified over and found the quantifier was narrower than the sentence.  *** RE-DISPOSITIONED THE SAME DAY: THIS IS A CLAUSE-(d) FLOOR BREACH, L2, REPAIRED IN-ROUND -- NOT THE COVERAGE DEBT IT WAS FIRST FILED AS. ***  Filed on the fable5 seat's derivation; the opus5 seat then MEASURED it and dissented on disposition, and the dissent is correct.  `if (X)` -> `if (X && Y)` on the predicate `#495` ADDED, which DOMINATES the edited lines, is clause (d)'s canonical form -- and `#488`'s adjudication says so in terms: *'E1 was `if (X)` -> `if (X && Y)` on the DOMINATING predicate -- the canonical clause-(d) form, i.e. a floor breach.'*  `#495` is closed, so the LATE-DISSENT rule applies: disposition 2, a MEASURED FALSE PASS against a shipped detector's floor, repaired in a follow-up commit.  `wdcatapistswap` IS that commit and was already rewriting the row list, so the repair cost nothing extra.  *** THE MEASUREMENT, and it is worse than the filing said. ***  Under E4 the guest is handed its own injected bytes AS DISK DATA and the detector scores a clean sweep -- not a hypothetical edit in an uncovered cell, but the exact defect `#495` removed, restored, invisible.  THE CLOSURE CONDITION, derived by the seat: `&& P(len)` escapes iff P is TRUE on every width the probe injects and FALSE on some width the device IMPLEMENTS.  {1,2} leaves `!= 4`; {2,4} leaves `!= 1`; {1,4} leaves `!= 2`.  **Only {1,2,4} closes the family** -- the 3- and 8-byte cases push nothing and are inert as escape routes.  REPAIRED WITH ONE INSTRUCTION and NO new row: a 4-byte `sw` beside the existing 1-byte K injection.  On the fixed leg it is refused like its neighbours so row L still reads ST_IDLE; on the base leg it lands like them so row L still reads ST_DATAIN.  It kills E4, M3 and M6 together.  *** AND THE PROBE HAD NO 4-BYTE EMITTER AT ALL -- no `sw`, no `lw` -- so the device's `case 4:` arm and its whole `consumed` accounting had never been executed on any leg of any run this detector ever made. ***  That is the real finding: not an uncovered mutant, an uncovered ARM.  *** CLOSED 2026-08-30, IN THE ROUND THAT FOUND IT.  The state and the substance had disagreed: this row shipped `in work` with a present-tense title -- *sweeps all 26 ... no row injects at len == 4* -- for a defect the same diff repaired. ***  A future reader who trusts states reads that as live, which is false; the es438 shape, named by the fable5 seat on pass 2.  CLOSED BY: a 4-byte `sw` in the probe's K2 arm, one instruction, no new row.  The probe now injects widths {1,2,4}, and the closure condition -- `&& P(len)` escapes iff P is TRUE on every INJECTED width and FALSE on some IMPLEMENTED width -- has no remaining solution, because the device implements exactly {1,2,4} and the 3- and 8-byte cases push nothing.  *** AND THE EVIDENCE MUST BE CITED PRECISELY, WHICH IT WAS NOT AT FIRST. ***  The `a5/5a/00` readback this finding is usually quoted with came from a probe whose DATA-IN injection had been WIDENED to four bytes to demonstrate the hazard -- not from E4 against the shipped instrument.  Against the repaired probe E4 leaves G/H/I GREEN and dies on ROW L.  Same conclusion, different row; the grok seat caught the misattribution by opening `kill_E4.out` rather than reading the claim.

rows.title: the rung-3 wdc probe cannot see #479's ring-reset half: deleting the ring reset from wdc_new_command_reset() escapes all 26 rows
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED at the CURRENT 15-row instrument -- deleting the ring reset scores 30/30 ESCAPED.  Log: regress/artifacts/wdcatapistswap/killtable_20260830/kill_X4.out (sentinel present), table TABLE_X4.txt
rows.note: `wdc_new_command_reset()` does three things -- clears the ATAPI flag and phase, clears `write_in_progress`, and empties the ring (`inbuf_head = inbuf_tail = 0`).  **Delete the ring-emptying line and the probe scores a clean sweep**, because on the fixed leg the #495 guard already keeps the ring empty at every command boundary this probe crosses, so there is nothing left for the reset to discard.  The instrument is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to that half of #479.  Note this is a property of the probe, not of the fix: the ring reset is live and load-bearing on paths the probe does not walk.  LOW because the blind spot needs a deliberate deletion to expose and the offline detector covers ring occupancy from the other side -- the two instruments are complementary and this is one of the seams between them.  Recorded in the probe's BLIND-TO list in the same round, because a contract that does not name its blind spots is the overclaim clause (e) exists to prevent.  Derived by the fable5 seat on `wdcatapistswap` pass 1.  *** RE-MEASURED 2026-08-30 AT THE CURRENT INSTRUMENT: 30/30 ESCAPED.  The old figure said 'escapes all 26', which was the 13-row instrument this round then grew past -- a figure the round's OWN repair invalidated and nobody re-ran until a seat said so. ***  *** AND THE MEASUREMENT SETTLED A DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO SEATS, IN FAVOUR OF THE ONE THAT REASONED ABOUT WHICH TREE THE MUTANT LANDS ON. ***  The opus5 seat predicted **29/30** -- that on the BASE leg the K and K2 injections land, so the ring holds bytes at the RECAL boundary and row M/t7 would pop a stale `0xa5` where it wants `0x5a`.  The kimi seat predicted a **clean escape**, and gave the reason: the mutant is applied to the **FIX** tree, the base leg is UNMUTATED, and on the fix leg the intact guard refuses every injection -- so the ring is empty at every command boundary this probe crosses and **the reset is dead code there**.  Measured 30/30.  **Kimi is right.**  *Both seats reasoned carefully and one of them tracked which leg the mutation reaches.  That is the whole difference, and it is not a difference of care.*  SO THE BLIND SPOT IS REAL AND CONFIRMED AT THE SHIPPED INSTRUMENT: this probe structurally cannot see `#479`'s ring-reset half, because the `#495` guard it exists to pin makes that half unreachable on the only leg a mutant can alter.  **Two fixes of one round can be mutually masking**, and no row count closes that -- it needs a leg where the guard does NOT hold.  RANKED LOW and left open: closing it needs an instrument whose fix leg admits ring content at a command boundary, which is a probe-shape question rather than a row question.

rows.title: a SECOND flag-operand replacement -- `cur_command == ATAPI_PKT_CMD` -- sweeps the 15-row probe 30/30, and the two-vehicle accept arm does not defeat it
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED by the opus5 seat at 30/30 ESCAPED on the extended probe; its guest-visible divergence is DERIVED, not measured
rows.note: Replace `d->atapi_cmd_in_progress` in the `#495` guard with `d->cur_command == ATAPI_PKT_CMD`.  **30/30, clean sweep.**  *** THIS IS NOT THE ESCAPE THE N ARM WAS BUILT FOR, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE ROW. ***  `E3` is `&& cur_command != WDCC_RECAL` -- an EXEMPTION of one opcode, which the second vehicle (ATAPI_SOFT_RESET) defeats because one conjunct cannot exempt two opcodes.  **E5 is a REPLACEMENT of the flag operand -- E2's own family -- and the two-vehicle argument does not touch it**: after BOTH RECAL (0x10) and SOFT_RESET (0x08), `cur_command != 0xa0`, so the guard is false and BOTH accept arms stay green.  DIVERGENCE, derived rather than measured: `wdc_command()`'s no-disk-image early return sits AFTER `wdc_new_command_reset()`, so selecting a nonexistent drive and then writing ATAPI_PKT_CMD leaves `cur_command == 0xa0` with the flag CLEAR -- shipped accepts there, E5 refuses.  Two stores, and probing a nonexistent slave is what a bus scan does.  RANKED BELOW `wdcwidth4` and FILED rather than fixed: its harm class is OVER-REFUSAL (M1's class) and TRANSIENT, where E2's is permanent for the life of the device, and the divergence is reasoned rather than run.  **The honest statement of what the accept arm buys, from the same seat: rows B and M differ in exactly ONE dimension a mutant can read -- whether a packet command has ever run.  E2 is the arm's only UNIQUE kill, because at row B `atapi_st` is NULL so E2's guard is false and B stays green.  'The accept side is pinned' is measurably false.**  *** RE-ANCHORED 2026-08-30: this row said *Ranked below `wdcwidth4`*, and `wdcwidth4` has since been DISCHARGED. ***  A ranking against a closed row conveys nothing.  The standing comparison is to the swap `wdcatapistswap` closed: **that one is PERMANENT** -- once a packet command runs, every ordinary data-port write is refused for the life of the device -- while this one is **TRANSIENT over-refusal**, cleared by the next command write, and its divergence is derived rather than measured.  That is why it files.  *** TWO SEATS DISAGREED ABOUT WHETHER THIS IS CATCHABLE AT ALL, AND READING THE FUNCTION SETTLED IT IN FOUR LINES.  2026-08-30, pass 2. ***  The kimi seat derived, at length and honestly, that the swap is **UN-CATCHABLE by any accept row** because `flag == 1` and `cur_command == ATAPI_PKT_CMD` are EQUIVALENT device-wide -- which would make filing the only possible disposition forever.  The opus5 seat derived the opposite: the distinguishing state exists via the no-disk-image early return.  **THE ORDER INSIDE `wdc_command()` DECIDES IT, and opus5 is right:** `cur_command = idata` runs FIRST, then `wdc_new_command_reset()` clears the flag, then the no-disk-image early RETURN fires -- and the flag is set again only inside the ATAPI_PKT_CMD case, which sits AFTER that return.  So writing 0xa0 to a driveless slot leaves **`cur_command == 0xa0` with `flag == 0`**: the equivalence fails and the swap is distinguishable.  **KIMI'S PROPOSED ALTERNATIVE VEHICLE IS SEPARATELY REFUTED.**  It reasoned that a control-port SRST might clear the flag while leaving `cur_command` stale at 0xa0, which would kill this swap AND the whole opcode-exemption family at once.  It does not: the SRST arm writes `cur_command = COMMAND_RESET` before calling the reset helper, so nothing is left stale.  A good idea, refuted by one line.  *** THE SEAT BEHAVIOUR IS WORTH RECORDING SEPARATELY FROM THE ANSWER. ***  Kimi marked its own claim as unsettled -- *'MUST verify from source ... pending reading the actual code around 730-745, 822-870, 945-960'* -- and named the exact line ranges that would decide it.  Those are the lines that decided it.  **A seat that cannot check a premise and says which check would settle it is more useful than one that guesses**, even when its conclusion is wrong.  CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW: it stays FILED, but the disposition is now stronger.  It is not un-catchable; it is catchable by an ARM, not a vehicle -- a data-port write after `ATAPI_PKT_CMD` is issued to a slot with no image.  That is a design a future round can start from rather than a hunt.

So **every commit after 2026-09-20 is blocked** until all eight are wired or the dates are moved.  The checker is right to do this -- a dated exemption that never comes due is not an exemption -- but eight coming due together is a scheduling hazard rather than a deadline.  *** AND THE POPULATION IS TWICE WHAT THE REGRESS REVIEW NAMED. ***  That review found *'FOUR wdc probes share the single-leg-mode debt and the same 2026-09-20 expiry'* and recommended ONE design round covering four instruments.  Correct about the wdc cluster; the expiry itself is shared by EIGHT probes with FOUR DISTINCT remedies:  **(1) single-leg mode, 4 probes** -- `wdc_altoffset_probe.py`, `_sig_`, `_4bit_`, `wdc_addtoinbuf_probe.py`.  Two-leg differentials; a gate has only one binary.  Two of them additionally need a CD-ROM rig (`ciR:`) and one needs a POISONED image the battery does not build.  This is the one-design-round cluster.  **(2) `hpcmips_ctor_probe.py`** -- rung 2, ~8 s, no rig image; wants a CONSTRUCTION gate.  Different mechanism entirely.  **(3) `sh4_bsc_width_probe.py` -> gate 10; `pit8253_latch_probe.py` -> gate 14.**  Each names the gate it belongs in; these are wiring, not design.  **(4) `fbpending_drain_probe.py`** -- REPORT-ONLY until `EXPECT_CAP` is set, so wiring it without setting that ships a row that cannot fail.  *** THE POINT IS THE SHAPE, NOT THE COUNT: four of the eight are CHEAP (two are plain gate wiring, one is a one-variable decision), and only the wdc four need a design round. ***  Doing the cheap four first shrinks the cliff from eight to four before it arrives, and each is independently shippable.  *Advisory, from the same run: the checker also notes two SELFLABEL discrepancies (`pit8253_latch_probe.py` and `wdc_addtoinbuf_probe.py` -- manifest says detector, the probe's own summary line says witness).  It flags these as advisory precisely because self-labels are measurably unreliable in both directions.*  *** ONE OF THE EIGHT WAS ABOUT TO BE GATE-WIRED WITH NO WAY TO DETECT A TRUNCATION.  FIXED PRE-EMPTIVELY 2026-08-30. ***  `pit8253_latch_probe.py`'s last output was a bare `PASS`/`FAIL` -- a word that occurs in dozens of contexts and is not uniquely greppable.  Its only SCREAMING_TOKEN was `print("MEASURED")`, a **mid-run section header** that a truncated log still contains.  So a gate row written against it could not have distinguished a completed run from a killed one, which is exactly the `killdrivercrash` class arriving in new work rather than old.  Now emits `PIT8253_LATCH_DONE`, on both the pass and fail paths -- a completed FAILURE is not a truncation.  *Doing this BEFORE the wiring means the gate row can be written correctly the first time.  `sh4_bsc_width_probe.py`, the other plain-wiring member, already carries a proper `SH4_BSC_WIDTH_PASS`/`_FAIL` pair and needs nothing.*  *** AND A METHODOLOGICAL CORRECTION WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX, because it nearly became a filed defect count. ***  A sweep for probes lacking a `_DONE`/`_PASS` token returned **34 of 46**.  That number is MEANINGLESS: gate 10 verifies `sh_rounding_probe.py` by grepping `SH_ROUND_RESULT=`, which is a perfectly good completion marker in a different shape.  The convention is per-probe and per-gate, so **there is no 34-probe defect and the question is not sweepable** -- it is 'does this probe's CONSUMER verify completion, and by what?', one probe at a time.  An earlier version of the same sweep put `sh4_bsc_width_probe.py` in the missing list, which is how the pattern was caught: it flagged a probe I had confirmed compliant ten minutes earlier.  **A pattern that selects the wrong set produces a clean, confident, wrong population**, and this is the third instance today.  *** THE CHEAP FOUR, INVESTIGATED READ-ONLY 2026-08-30 SO A ROUND CAN START WITHOUT RE-DERIVING ANY OF IT.  Ranked by what each actually needs. ***  **(a) `pit8253_latch_probe.py` -> gate 14.**  ALREADY UNBLOCKED: it lacked any completion marker and now emits `PIT8253_LATCH_DONE`.  Machine `-E cats`, 10 rows.  Gate 14 is `gate_arm.sh`, which already runs `-E cats`.  Remaining work is the exec line plus row checks.  **(b) `sh4_bsc_width_probe.py` -> gate 10.**  Machine `-E landisk`; already emits `SH4_BSC_WIDTH_PASS`/`_FAIL`.  **Gate 10 (`gate_sh_rounding.sh`) already execs three probes in exactly the needed idiom** -- `python3 <probe>.py "$PMAX" "$KERNEL" > "$LOG" 2>&1 || true`, then `check` rows against the log.  Copying that idiom is the whole change.  **(c) `hpcmips_ctor_probe.py` -> a construction gate.**  Rung 2, ~8 s, NO RIG IMAGE, takes no positional argv, accepts `--binary PATH` (default `$GXROOT/build/gxemul`), emits `HPCMIPS_CTOR_PASS`/`_FAIL`, and already runs its subprocess with a timeout.  `gate_asan_sweep.sh` is the construction gate and sweeps 41 machine types.  ONE MISMATCH TO RESOLVE, named rather than discovered later: that gate drives an ASAN binary while this probe defaults to `build/gxemul` -- `--binary` makes it parameterisable, so the decision is which binary the row should assert against.  **(d) `fbpending_drain_probe.py` -- ONE VARIABLE, BUT NOT A FREE ONE.**  It is REPORT-ONLY until `--expect-cap N` is set (`EXPECT_CAP = -1` means report only), and **wiring it without choosing N ships a row that cannot fail** -- the check-that-cannot-fail shape.  Choosing N needs a measurement, and the probe carries a **31.51 s wall-clock floor by construction**, so it is timing-sensitive and must be measured on a quiet machine.  Cheapest in code, most expensive in care.  *Ordering follows from that: (a) and (b) are mechanical, (c) needs one decision, (d) needs a measurement.  Three of the four can ship before the wdc design round even starts.*  *** `8404520` NAMED: that commit shipped this row's FIRST piece of code -- the `PIT8253_LATCH_DONE` sentinel -- and the attribution check refused the NEXT commit until the row said so.  Third time today this rule has fired (after `census` and `wdcatapistswap`), and every one was a real gap rather than a nuisance. ***  The row stays OPEN: one of eight probes is unblocked, seven remain, and the cliff is unmoved until they are wired.
