rows.note: *** MY OWN BRIEF'S PREMISE WAS THAT `gdromcondlies` HELD THE LAST LIVE GUEST-REACHABLE HOST KILLS.  IT IS FALSE, AND THE FIRST FILE I SAMPLED REFUTED IT. ***  I stated it AS A QUESTION in that brief (*'have I confused "the queue knows of no others" with "there are no others"?'*), which is the only reason this was cheap to find -- and I found it myself, before the panel answered.  **THE CENSUS SAID WHERE TO LOOK AND WAS RIGHT.**  `exit_census.py` reports 99 live terminating calls inside `DEVICE_ACCESS` across 30 files; `dev_sgi_re.c` carries **21**, seven times the gdrom file.  It is the top of that list, and I sampled it for exactly that reason.  *** WHAT IS THERE, AND IT IS A CLASS THIS PROJECT HAS ALREADY FIXED ELSEWHERE: ***  the guard at the head of the CRIME_RE_TLB_A arm is  `if (len != 8) { fatal("TODO: unimplemented len=%i ..."); exit(1); }`  -- **a GUEST CHOOSING AN ACCESS WIDTH ends the host process.**  That is the `#337` class verbatim, whose own comment in `dev_wdc.c` reads *'a 3- or 8-byte access to the data port used to call exit(1) -- a GUEST choosing an access width killed the host process'*.  The adjacent arm kills on a plain READ (`fatal("TODO: read from CRIME_RE_TLB_A"); exit(1);`), which is the direction/offset class.  **REACHABILITY CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED**: `machine_sgi.c:500` calls `dev_sgi_re_init(machine, mem, 0x15000000)` and the device registers at `baseaddr + 0x1000` through `memory_device_register`.  It is a real device on a real machine, mapped into the guest address space.  **HONEST BOUND ON THE NUMBER, because this project keeps getting counts wrong: 21 is how many live terminating calls sit inside that file's `DEVICE_ACCESS` handlers.**  It is NOT a claim that 21 are individually reachable -- some may be guarded, and `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:1055` is the standing proof that a `DEVICE_ACCESS` site can be unreachable and take a hand-derived warrant to establish it.  What IS established: at least two of them are reachable by construction, and they are of classes already recognised as defects here.  *** THE GENERAL LESSON, AND IT IS ABOUT THE QUEUE RATHER THAN THIS DEVICE: A QUEUE-COMPLETE CLAIM IS NOT A TREE-COMPLETE ONE. ***  The adjudicating seat flagged exactly this limit about its own answer hours earlier -- *'my no-other-live-host-kills claim rests on the queue and this file's grep, not a fresh tree-wide exit census'* -- and then I wrote the queue-complete version into a brief as a premise anyway.  The seat named the gap; the brief inherited it.  SCOPE: this is a CLUSTER and must not become one round.  The round-scope rule takes ONE site, with a second joining only if it is witnessed, in the same device and semantic class, and covered by the same detector with no new oracle.  The width guards may qualify as one class; the read-direction kills are a second.  **More witnesses create more candidate ROUNDS, never bigger rounds.**  NEXT STEP is a rung-3 witness on ONE site, not a fix: `-E sgi` machines exist in tree, the device is mapped at a known base, and the `#337` precedent gives the fix shape (latched decline, `(once)` marker) if a witness lands.  *** THE DIAGNOSIS ABOVE IS INCOMPLETE AND THE TRUE ONE IS WORSE.  Corrected the same day by the opus5 seat, which MEASURED it. ***  This row was filed saying the brief had confused 'the queue knows of no others' with 'there are no others'.  **Neither.  The queue knew of NINE others.**  Ledger row `n6` is OPEN, titled *'The record says the footbridge host-halts were made graceful; nine of them are not'*, carrying a CONFIRMED rung-3 witness (`probe:regress/footbridge_sites_probe.py` row K1, gated in `gate_arm.sh`) and a `state_note` RANKING IT 6th OF 8 on 2026-08-27 -- three days before the brief claimed there were none.  The seat rebuilt HEAD clean and re-ran the COMMITTED probe: a guest `ldr r7,[r0,#392]` on an unmodified `-E cats` ends the host at `dev_footbridge.c:589`.  It then swapped the single planted word three more times and got **four of four** -- `:604` ENABLE_CLEAR read, `:565` IRQ_STATUS write, `:712` SDRAM_BA_MASK read -- each one guest instruction, each with the site's own diagnostic text as the attribution control.  **So this is the UNREAD-ROW class, not a census gap.**  The census work still stands and still found two REAL clusters nobody had filed; what it did not do is what a `grep n6` would have done in one second.  *The lesson is not 'census harder'.  It is that a completeness claim must be checked against THE QUEUE'S OWN OPEN ROWS before it is written down -- and that is the cheaper check of the two.*  *** THE CENSUS IS DONE, AND IT SPLITS THE 21 INTO FOUR CLASSES WITH ONE PROVABLY DEAD SITE.  agy seat, 2026-08-30, `regress/artifacts/widthkillclass/witness_20260830/`. ***  It is a READING, not a measurement, and is recorded as one -- but the single most surprising claim in it was CHECKED HERE BY OPENING THE FILE, and it held.  **20 of 21 guest-reachable; 1 PROVABLY UNREACHABLE.**  WIDTH (a guest choosing an access size ends the host) -- 7 reachable: the `len != 8` guards on CRIME_RE_TLB_A/B/C, CRIME_RE_TEX and CRIME_RE_LINEAR_A/B, plus `sgi_de: len = %i not implemented` (which wants len 4 or 8).  DIRECTION (a legal-width access in the wrong direction) -- 6 reachable: `TODO: read from CRIME_RE_TLB_A/B/C`, `..._TEX`, `..._LINEAR_A/B`, each reached by an 8-byte READ, i.e. **the guest does everything right except the direction**.  BADOFFSET -- 1: the `unimplemented read/write to address` arm, reached by any access to an unregistered sub-window.  BADVAL -- 6: `sgi_de: UNIMPLEMENTED drawing op`, and five `sgi_mte` arms (MTE_MODE_STIPPLE, unimplemented SRC, MTE_MODE_COPY, MTE_DEPTH_x, and an unimplemented bytemask).  *** THE UNREACHABLE ONE IS DEAD CODE AND MUST NOT BE 'FIXED' -- I VERIFIED THIS BY OPENING THE FILE RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT. ***  `[ sgi_mte: UNIMPLEMENTED read/write len %i ]` sits in the trailing `else` of `if (len == 4) { ... } else if (len != 4) { ... } else { fatal; exit(1); }`.  For every integer `len` one of the first two arms is taken, so the third can never execute.  A round that 'de-fatalises' it would be editing unreachable code and its detector could carry no row -- **the vacuous shape in its purest form, and the census is what stops it being attempted.**  **WHAT THIS MEANS FOR SCOPE, and it is the useful part: FOUR classes means at least four candidate rounds, not one.**  The round-scope rule takes ONE site, with a second joining only if it is the same device AND the same semantic class AND covered by the same detector with no new oracle.  A WIDTH guard and a DIRECTION guard sit in the SAME ARM at the same offset and are still different classes -- whether they nonetheless share one fix design is an open question this row does not settle, and it is exactly what the next research pass should answer rather than assume.  HONEST BOUND: reachability here is derived from address-decode reading, NOT measured, except for the WIDTH class -- which now has a rung-3 witness (see `widthkillclass`).  The DIRECTION, BADOFFSET and BADVAL classes have NO witness yet and a round on any of them owes one first.  *** THE COUNT'S SCOPE WAS WRONG AND A SEAT CHECKED IT: 21 IS THE FILE TOTAL, NOT THE HANDLER'S. ***  `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_re)` holds **13**.  Per handler: sgi_re 13, sgi_de 1, sgi_mte 1, sgi_de_status 0, helpers 6 -- summing to the 21 this row filed.  So the four-class census spans FOUR HANDLERS, not one, and that matters for scope rather than for tidiness: a round joining sites 'in the same handler' is a different population from one joining sites 'in the same file'.  **This is the dropped-qualifier class again** -- the number was right and the noun was wrong, which is exactly how `b120r`'s NIL and `#464`'s 'floods identically' went wrong.  AND THE WIDTH FIGURE OF 7 IS SHORT BY ONE against the message text: there are EIGHT width-shaped kills in the file, the six in sgi_re plus `sgi_de: len = %i not implemented` and `[ sgi_mte: UNIMPLEMENTED read/write len %i ]`.  Both are now filed separately -- `sgidewidth` (LIVE, high) and `sgimtewidth` (a mis-service plus a resurrection trap) -- because they sit in different handlers and so cannot join a sgi_re round.  *** READ-ONLY AUDIT, agy seat, 2026-08-30 -- AND THE HEADLINE IS THAT THIS ROUND MAY BE MUCH SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS: ALL SIX ARMS LOOK LIKE **ACCEPT**, NOT DECLINE. ***  The de-fatalisation option set has four members, and the fourth applies where the model already holds the right answer and merely discards it.  **`re_tlb_a`, `re_tlb_b`, `re_tlb_c`, `re_tex`, `re_linear_a` and `re_linear_b` are all WRITTEN by the store path**, so a read can return what was written -- no latch, no message, because there is no event to announce.  *A bounded-announce here would ship a wrong record in product code: printing 'unimplemented; ignored' about a read that is implemented and is not ignored.*  **REACHABILITY: all six are reachable by an ordinary guest load on unmodified `-E sgi -e ip32`**, and the addresses are derived rather than guessed -- `machine_sgi.c:500` passes base `0x15000000`, `dev_sgi_re_init` registers `sgi_re` at `baseaddr + 0x1000` for `DEV_SGI_RE_LENGTH` (0x1000), and the handler restores the full offset with `relative_addr += 0x1000`.  **Every window lies inside `0x15001000-0x150017ff`, none is shadowed, and the `else if` cascade is strictly disjoint.**  Verified here independently by opening `machine_sgi.c` and `crmfbreg.h`: the six constants are `0x1000 / 0x1200 / 0x1400 / 0x1600 / 0x1700 / 0x1780`.  **GUEST KSEG1 ADDRESSES, so a probe author does not re-derive them:** TLB_A `0xb5001000`, TLB_B `0xb5001200`, TLB_C `0xb5001400`, TEX `0xb5001600`, LINEAR_A `0xb5001700`, LINEAR_B `0xb5001780` -- read kills at lines 245, 262, 279, 296, 346, 362 respectively.  **One malloc serves all four handlers** (`dev_sgi_re_init` allocates one `struct sgi_re_data` and hands it to `sgi_de`, `sgi_mte` and `sgi_de_status`), so whatever latch infrastructure `#497` lands is already reachable here.  *The audit and the brief that produced it are preserved at `regress/artifacts/sgirekills/audit_20260830/` -- the ledger first cited the `_scratchpad/` copy, which the durable-path rule excludes precisely because it evaporates.  This row now has everything a rung-3 witness needs except the witness itself, which is the point of asking a seat for the addresses rather than the answer.*  *** THIS ROW'S TITLE SAID '21 TERMINATING CALLS INSIDE DEVICE_ACCESS' AND THAT WAS THE SAME CONFLATION I MADE AND CORRECTED ELSEWHERE TODAY.  Corrected 2026-08-30. ***  **21 is the FILE total.  15 are inside a `DEVICE_ACCESS`, and 13 of those in `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_re)`** -- the other 6 live in `draw_primitive` (1) and `do_mte_transfer` (5), neither of which is a `DEVICE_ACCESS` and neither of which a guest reaches by an ordinary access.  *** AND THE TITLE WAS NOT CARELESS -- IT FAITHFULLY REPORTED WHAT THE TOOL SAID, WHICH WAS WRONG. ***  See `exitcensus`: `exit_census.py`'s per-file totals were correct all along, but its BY-ENCLOSING-CONSTRUCT split attributed every call in a plain non-static function to the preceding `DEVICE_ACCESS`.  That bucket is a REACHABILITY claim used for ranking -- *on a guest access path BY CONSTRUCTION* -- so the defect over-stated how many host kills a guest can actually reach.  Fixed; tree-wide the bucket falls **97 -> 83**.  *** THE ACCEPT DESIGN, ADJUDICATED 2026-08-30 -- AND IT REFUTES THE AUDIT RECORDED DIRECTLY ABOVE IT ON ONE ARM OF SIX. ***  **agy ruled ACCEPT for all six read arms on the ground that BACKING STATE EXISTS in the struct.  That is not the ACCEPT test.**  The doctrine's fourth option-set member -- minted from the footbridge IRQEnable precedent -- is *the model already computes the CORRECT answer and merely discards it*.  Existence of state is necessary and nowhere near sufficient.  **FIVE ARMS ARE CLEAN ACCEPT; TEX IS NOT.**  **TLB A/B/C:** the store packs big-endian halfword pairs from raw bus bytes and a readback through the same index expression round-trips BYTE-EXACTLY on this machine -- with a premise that belongs in the comment rather than assumed: `machine_sgi.c` pins BIG ENDIAN, and while the STORE path is byte-order-agnostic the READ path is not.  **LINEAR A/B:** the store splits `idata` into two uint32 cells and the readback is its exact inverse through the `readmax64`/`writemax64` pair -- byte-order symmetric BY CONSTRUCTION, so it needs no endianness premise at all.  *** TEX FAILS THE TEST, AND THE EVIDENCE IS A GREP: `re_tex` HAS ZERO CONSUMERS ANYWHERE. ***  `tlb_a/b/c` feed `horrible_getputpixel`; `linear_a/b` feed it and `do_mte_transfer`; **`re_tex` feeds nothing.**  Its state is written through the `>> 3` index that `sgitexindex` records as a defect -- frames overlap by three, 81 of 112 cells unreachable -- so **the model does not hold the right answer for TEX; it holds a self-consistent WRONG one.**  ACCEPT is available only in the MIRRORED form (the read uses the same `>> 3` expression), which round-trips per frame while shipping hardware-wrong reads at overlapping offsets.  **That is a materially weaker claim than the other five arms', and the round record must not blur them.**  **WHAT ACCEPT OWES THAT DECLINE DOES NOT -- five items, and the second is an ORDERING DEPENDENCY on `#497`:**  (1) **round-trip rows with DISTINCT sentinels per window** -- distinctness catches a cross-wired read, while a same-window index error breaks round-trip because the store frame is position-dependent.  The JOINT translation (store and read shifted together) escapes round-trip BY CONSTRUCTION -- clause (f) territory -- so the contract names it outside, and names honestly that an out-of-decode anchor channel exists for four arms (the rendering and MTE paths consume them) and **does not exist for `re_tex` today**.  (2) **a DEVICE-SIGNATURE control**, because a faithful round-trip through a device is value-indistinguishable from RAM -- the witness ladder's own two-control lesson.  The clean discriminator: **post-`#497` a 4-byte read DECLINES and returns 0 while RAM would serve it.**  So `#497` is an ordering dependency for this round's WITNESS QUALITY, not merely for its latch infrastructure.  (3) **the dead tail's first execution belongs to `#497`, not here.**  A width-declined READ falls through the splice and runs `memory_writemax64` with `odata = 0`.  This round's new surface is narrower than it looks: **NONZERO `odata` through the BE packing**, not 'the tail runs'.  (4) **the claim must be SCOPED**: *returns what the store path recorded*, never *faithful hardware readback*.  TEX refutes the stronger phrase today, and the LINEAR arms store the PROM's own wrongly-sign-extended values verbatim -- returning them faithfully is right; modelling hardware readback is unproven.  **That is `b716a34`'s lesson pre-applied: do not put the strong phrase in a site comment.**  (5) **a PRE-WRITE read row** returning 0, which pins the memset-init as guest-visible ABI and is the minimal de-fatalisation survival row.  *** TEX POISONS THE WARRANT, NOT THE ROUND -- AND THE COUPLING IS ENFORCEABLE BY ONE ROW RATHER THAN BY A DEPENDENCY. ***  Ship TEX MIRRORED plus its round-trip row, and any ONE-SIDED future fix reds that row loudly: store `>> 1` against read `>> 3` writes cells 4-7 and reads 1-4, and the reverse likewise, while the JOINT fix keeps identity and the row stays green.  **So the round-trip row IS the coupling enforcement**, and `sgitexindex`'s fix becomes a declared two-site edit with a tripwire already in place.  Recorded in BOTH rows.  **WHAT IS NOT ACCEPTABLE:** unmirrored `>> 1` reads over the `>> 3` store -- round-trip broken immediately, silent wrong data, worse than a decline -- or ACCEPT recorded with the same warrant strength as the other five arms.  **A LATENT THIS ROUND INHERITS RATHER THAN CREATES:** the TLB arms mask the INITIAL `tlbi` but increment it UNMASKED in the loop, so `relative_addr & 0x1ff >= 0x1fa` with `len 8` runs to index 0x102 -- three halfwords into the adjacent array.  Guest-unreachable for the alignment reason `sgilinearoob` settles path-by-path, and **a mirrored read arm makes it a second SITE of that class** -- record it there so an eventual bound fixes both directions.  *** THE TEST THAT KILLED `sgideoob` WAS THEN APPLIED TO THE SURVIVORS, BY ENUMERATION RATHER THAN BY REASONING -- AND BOTH HOLD.  2026-08-30. ***  Withdrawing a false member is only half the follow-through; the other half is asking whether the same miss is in the rows that remain. And self-consistency holds only in single-store isolation: with the overlap-by-three the brief itself states, a store at +8 lands in `re_tex[1..4]` and one at +16 in `[2..5]`, so a mirrored read at +8 returns a MIX of two stores -- not *what the store actually wrote*.  **Mirroring's benefit exists only for a guest that writes one slot and reads it back before touching another.**

rows.title: a GUEST CHOOSING AN ACCESS WIDTH ends the host -- #337 fixed this class in dev_wdc.c and 16 sites in two other devices were never swept
rows.witness: probe:regress/artifacts/widthkillclass/opus_p1_20260830/read_probe.out -- 26/26 across ALL SIX sites and BOTH directions on unmodified `-E sgi -e ip32`, with a LIVENESS and a DEVICE-SIGNATURE control.  *The earlier witness field cited a 10/10 single-site artifact, which under-cited the round's own strongest evidence -- caught by the pass-2 seat.*  The shipped detector is regress/sgi_re_width_probe.py, 35/35, gate-run.
rows.note: *** `#337` FIXED THIS CLASS IN ONE DEVICE AND NOBODY SWEPT FOR THE OTHERS.  MEASURED 2026-08-30: 16 SITES ACROSS TWO MORE DEVICES. ***  `dev_wdc.c`'s own `#337` comment states the class outright: *'a 3- or 8-byte access to the data port used to call exit(1) -- a GUEST choosing an access width killed the host process'*.  It was fixed there.  The same shape survives untouched in:  **`dev_pcc2.c` -- 10 sites** (`:362`, `:374`, `:397`, `:410`, `:432`, `:470`, ...), diagnostics of the form *'TODO: pcc2: non-byte reads and writes of ...'*;  **`dev_sgi_re.c` -- 6 sites** (`:233`, `:250`, `:267`, `:284`, `:301`, `:351`), guards of the form `if (len != 8) { fatal("TODO: unimplemented len=%i ..."); exit(1); }`.  **REACHABILITY IS ESTABLISHED FOR sgi_re BY CONSTRUCTION**: `machine_sgi.c:500` calls `dev_sgi_re_init(machine, mem, 0x15000000)` and it registers at `baseaddr + 0x1000`.  A guest store of the wrong width to that window ends the host.  pcc2's instantiation was NOT checked and is not claimed.  *** THE METHOD, STATED SO THE COUNT CAN BE CHECKED RATHER THAN TRUSTED. ***  Comments stripped with a state machine first (40% of raw `exit(` hits in `src/devices/` are inside comments, and that rate GROWS as the fork de-fatalises, because each fix leaves a comment quoting the exit it removed).  Then: a terminating call whose nearest SIX preceding lines mention `len` with a comparison, or the phrase `non-byte`.  **That is a heuristic and may over- or under-count**; it is a starting set, not a defect count, and `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:1055` stands as the proof that a site in a guest-access path can still be unreachable.  Re-derive with `tools/pipeline/exit_census.py` plus the width filter rather than quoting 16.  *** WHY IT IS A CLASS ROW AND NOT TWO DEVICE ROWS: the fix SHAPE is already settled by precedent. ***  `#337` chose latched decline with an explicit `(once)` marker, which is this tree's house idiom (N=1 per device instance; `(once)` is the plurality spelling at 9 of 14 sites).  So each round here is an APPLICATION of a decided design, not a fresh design argument -- which is the cheapest kind of round this queue has.  **SCOPE DISCIPLINE: this must not become one round.**  More witnesses create more candidate ROUNDS, never bigger ones.  Each takes ONE site, with a second joining only if witnessed, in the same device and semantic class, and covered by the same detector with no new oracle.  A device's sites may well satisfy that; two devices will not.  NEXT STEP is a rung-3 witness on ONE site -- not a fix, and not a sweep.  See `sgirekills` for that device's wider cluster, which includes read-direction kills that are a DIFFERENT class from this one.  *** THE DIAGNOSIS ABOVE IS INCOMPLETE AND THE TRUE ONE IS WORSE.  Corrected the same day by the opus5 seat, which MEASURED it. ***  This row was filed saying the brief had confused 'the queue knows of no others' with 'there are no others'.  **Neither.  The queue knew of NINE others.**  Ledger row `n6` is OPEN, titled *'The record says the footbridge host-halts were made graceful; nine of them are not'*, carrying a CONFIRMED rung-3 witness (`probe:regress/footbridge_sites_probe.py` row K1, gated in `gate_arm.sh`) and a `state_note` RANKING IT 6th OF 8 on 2026-08-27 -- three days before the brief claimed there were none.  The seat rebuilt HEAD clean and re-ran the COMMITTED probe: a guest `ldr r7,[r0,#392]` on an unmodified `-E cats` ends the host at `dev_footbridge.c:589`.  It then swapped the single planted word three more times and got **four of four** -- `:604` ENABLE_CLEAR read, `:565` IRQ_STATUS write, `:712` SDRAM_BA_MASK read -- each one guest instruction, each with the site's own diagnostic text as the attribution control.  **So this is the UNREAD-ROW class, not a census gap.**  The census work still stands and still found two REAL clusters nobody had filed; what it did not do is what a `grep n6` would have done in one second.  *The lesson is not 'census harder'.  It is that a completeness claim must be checked against THE QUEUE'S OWN OPEN ROWS before it is written down -- and that is the cheaper check of the two.*  *** WITNESSED AT RUNG 3, 2026-08-30, 10/10 -- AND IT IS THIS PROJECT'S FIRST WITNESS FOR THE `#337` CLASS OUTSIDE `dev_wdc.c`. ***  Built by the agy seat, which is a THIRD compile-and-measure front end on a transport independent of the Agent tool.  Preserved at `regress/artifacts/widthkillclass/witness_20260830/` before /tmp could evaporate.  **THE MEASUREMENT.**  Machine `-E sgi -e ip32` (SGI O2, MIPS R10000, 64-bit big-endian), unmodified.  `dev_sgi_re_init(machine, mem, 0x15000000)` registers at `baseaddr + 0x1000`, so the window is guest-visible at kseg1 `0xb5001000` -- **I verified that address against `machine_sgi.c` and the device's own `memory_device_register` rather than taking it from the report.**  Three widths, three kills:  `sw` (len=4) -> exit1 `TODO: unimplemented len=4 for CRIME_RE_TLB_A`;  `sh` (len=2) -> exit1 len=2;  `sb` (len=1) -> exit1 len=1.  Each row carries an ATTRIBUTION check on the diagnostic text, so the kill is pinned to THIS site rather than to any death.  *** THE ACCEPT CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES IT A WIDTH DEFECT RATHER THAN AN UNSERVICEABLE OFFSET, and it is the same discipline the gdrom witness used: *** a legal 64-bit `sd` to the SAME address SURVIVES (exit0).  Without that row the measurement would be equally consistent with the offset simply being unimplemented, which is a different and already-fixed class.  Plus both mandatory controls: LIVENESS (0x12345678 round-trips through RAM via the same decode) and DEVICE SIGNATURE, twice -- `CRIME_DE_STATUS` reads its reset `0x1e000000` where RAM would read 0, and a store/readback of 0x34 to `CRIME_DE_MODE_SRC` returns 0x34.  **CLASS_WITNESS and deliberately UNGATED**: its three kill rows INVERT the day this class is fixed, so gating it would manufacture a regression -- the same reasoning as the toclen and gdromcond witnesses.  SO THIS ROW IS NOW ELIGIBLE FOR A FIX ROUND on the sgi_re half.  The fix SHAPE is already settled by `#337`'s precedent (latched decline, `(once)` marker), so the round is an APPLICATION of a decided design.  **The `dev_pcc2.c` half is still unwitnessed and its instantiation is still unchecked** -- a farmed read-only job is asking exactly that question, and if the answer is that no machine instantiates it, those ten sites are dead code and this row narrows.  *** THE pcc2 HALF IS NARROWED BY EXACTLY TWO, AND THE FILING WAS MINE. codex seat, 2026-08-30, farmed read-only when agy walled -- and I VERIFIED THE LOAD-BEARING CLAIM BY OPENING THE FILE. ***  This row filed 'dev_pcc2.c 10 sites' with the honest caveat that its instantiation was not checked and not claimed.  It is now checked, and **5 of the 10 width anchors are guest-reachable, not 10**.  **THE MECHANISM, verified at `cpus/cpu_m88k_instr_loadstore.c`:** under `#ifndef LS_1` -- i.e. for every NON-BYTE access -- the core does `if (addr & (LS_SIZE - 1)) m88k_exception(cpu, M88K_EXCEPTION_MISALIGNED_ACCESS, 0);` **and that precedes the `cpu->memory_rw()` call**.  So a misaligned non-byte access raises a GUEST exception and never reaches the device handler at all.  The device is instantiated only by MVME187 (`machine_mvme88k.c`, `device_add(... "pcc2 addr=0x%x", PCC2_BASE)`, base `0xfff42000`), it registers 4096 bytes, and the handler reduces every offset with `relative_addr %= PCC2_SIZE` where PCC2_SIZE is 0x40 -- **so an ODD register offset stays odd in every one of the 64 aliases.**  An odd-offset width guard is therefore unreachable by construction: VECBASE 0x03, PSCALEADJ 0x15, T1CTL 0x17, T1ICR 0x1b, SCCICR 0x1d, SCCRX 0x1f, SCSIICR 0x2f.  Reachable: GENCTL 0x02, T2CTL 0x16, T2ICR 0x1a, SCCERR 0x1c, SCCTX 0x1e.  *** SO THE CLASS TOTAL DROPS FROM 16 TO 11 -- sgi_re 6 (witnessed) plus pcc2 5 (unwitnessed) -- and the 16 was a SEARCH SPACE exactly as this row said it was. ***  The caveat did its job: it is why the number could be corrected rather than defended.  TWO ADJACENT NON-WIDTH kills were found in the same pass and are NOT this class: a BADVAL (`pcc2: C040 interrupt assertions... TODO`, reachable by a BYTE write of 0x04 to GENCTL, which the alignment rule does not touch) and a BADOFFSET (`pcc2: unimplemented %s offset`).  A third, `pcctwo_interrupt_common: TODO: line`, is UNKNOWN -- the seat could not establish a guest-only assertion route and said so rather than guessing.  STILL OWED for the pcc2 half: a rung-3 witness.  The seat specified one precisely (`-e mvme187`, CODE 0x10000, r5 = 0xfff42000, one process per fatal row) and stated plainly that it did not run it, being read-only.  *** CENSUS CORRECTION, 2026-08-30, AND THE MAIN LOOP WAS THE ONE WHO WAS WRONG -- TWICE, IN ONE DERIVATION, HAVING ALREADY ASSERTED IT INTO TWO SEAT BRIEFS. ***  I derived `dev_sgi_re.c` as **25 exits / 15 in the handler** and told both seats the measuring seat's **21 / 13** was probably wrong.  Re-derived: **the seat is right on both numbers.**  **TWO INDEPENDENT DEFECTS IN ONE `grep`, and neither is exotic:**  **(1) `grep -c 'exit(1)'` COUNTS COMMENTED-OUT TEXT AS LIVE CODE.**  Four are dead -- `143`, `152` (`// exit(1);` and `//exit(1);` in `horrible_getputpixel`), `473` (`draw_primitive`), `965` (`do_mte_transfer`).  25 - 4 = **21 LIVE**.  **(2) I USED `DEVICE_ACCESS(...)` HEADS AS FUNCTION BOUNDARIES WHILE THREE PLAIN FUNCTIONS SIT BETWEEN THEM** -- `dev_sgi_re_init` at 385, `draw_primitive` at 408, `do_mte_transfer` at 940.  So my `sgi_re = 221-660` swallowed two whole functions; the real span is **221-379**.  **DERIVER** (name it, per the counts rule): live exits are the `exit(1)` lines whose stripped text does not begin `//`, attributed to the nearest PRECEDING line matching `^[A-Za-z].*(` without a `;`.  That gives `sgi_re` **13**, `do_mte_transfer` 5, `draw_primitive` 1, `sgi_de` 1, `sgi_mte` 1 = **21**.  *** THE DECOMPOSITION SURVIVES AND IS CLEANER THAN THE ONE I CLAIMED. ***  `sgi_re`'s 13 live exits `[233 245 250 262 267 279 284 296 301 346 351 362 372]` are **6 WIDTH kills** (233 250 267 284 301 351), **6 READ kills** (245 262 279 296 346 362), **1 other** (372) -- I had said 3 other.  **Exactly one width kill and one read kill per window, six windows, plus one straggler.**  A structural invariant tells a future edit what the shape must stay; an enumeration only tells you today's answer.  *** AND IT CARRIES A ROW-DESIGN CONSEQUENCE, which is why this is not bookkeeping. ***  The two arms are PAIRED and the WIDTH arm is evaluated FIRST.  That is exactly why the `lw` row reads post-fix `exit0`: `len == 4` takes the now-declining width arm and never reaches the still-live read kill.  **An 8-byte read still ends the host after `#497` ships**, by design, because `sgirekills` is a separate round -- so the `lw` row's comment must say so, or a future reader sees 'reads survive' and concludes the read kills are gone.  *The carrier's rule fired exactly as written and I nearly ignored it: when two checks disagree, find out WHICH ONE IS BROKEN -- do not keep the one that agrees with what you expected.  Mine agreed with me and mine was broken.  It was caught only because I opened the file to read an unrelated site and saw a `// exit(1);` with my own eyes.*  *** THE SPLIT IS RIGHT AND `#497` OWES ONE SENTENCE FOR IT.  Adjudicated 2026-08-30, and the pairing is what makes the obligation PRECISE rather than vague. ***  Both the adjudicating seat and the agy audit reached the same verdict independently: `#497` (six WIDTH kills) and `sgirekills` (six READ kills) are correctly separate.  **Three reasons, and the second is dispositive rather than merely persuasive:** the fix designs differ and the READ one is still OPEN (decline-return-0 versus implement-readback is a genuine fork); **`sgirekills` has NO WITNESS, so the round-scope rule's joiner clause makes combining not merely undesirable but IMPOSSIBLE today**; and merging on *the window still kills the host* proves too much -- by that logic every unimplemented arm is one giant round, which is the `#392` shape.  *** BUT THE RESIDUAL MUST BE NAMED IN THE ROUND RECORD, NOT DISCHARGED BY MERGING. ***  The width guard is evaluated FIRST, so after `#497` a 4-byte read declines safely and **an ordinary 8-byte `ld` to each of the six fixed windows STILL ENDS THE HOST** -- `len == 8` passes the width guard and falls straight into the read arm's `exit(1)`.  The 1:1 pairing does not merge the classes; it makes the leftover exact: **fixing six width kills leaves exactly six read kills at the same six offsets.**  Without that sentence a reader of `#497` reasonably concludes reads were made safe.  Same false-unanimity obligation as naming `sgidewidth`.  *** SETTLED PREMISES FOR THIS CAMPAIGN -- re-inline these in every later brief rather than letting seats re-derive them.  The block exists because dropping it once cost three seat-answers to re-derivation. ***  **(a) `odata` IS EXPLICITLY INITIALISED.**  `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_re)` opens `uint64_t idata = 0, odata = 0;` and `odata` appears exactly TWICE in the handler -- that declaration and the tail's `memory_writemax64(cpu, data, len, odata)`.  So a declined 4-byte read hands the guest a **defined zero**, not an uninitialised stack value.  This matters because the fix makes that tail live for the FIRST TIME in the fork's history, and *it happens to be zeroed* and *it is initialised* are different claims -- this is the second.  Derived by reading the function, not assumed.  **(b) THE LATCH IS A NEW BITFIELD AND THE `#490` COLLISION HAZARD DOES NOT APPLY.**  The implementing seat shipped one `uint32_t warned` with six enum bits (`1 << 0` .. `1 << 5`) rather than the six separate `int`s the brief specified.  **Checked and ACCEPTED**: there was no `warned` member in `struct sgi_re_data` before the diff, so no other path can set these bits -- unlike `#490`, where a shared field was written at eight sites, six inside `DEVICE_ACCESS`, and benign guest traffic could silence a latch.  *A deviation from the brief that is checked and accepted must be RECORDED as such; an unremarked deviation is how a design drifts without anyone deciding.*  Noted and deliberately NOT actioned: the explicit-shift form could in principle be typo'd into a duplicate where `dev_sh4.c`'s `_NCLASS` enum makes that impossible by construction -- but a bitfield cannot use bare auto-increment, the carrier already REJECTED a disjointness assert for the sh4 case on three measured grounds, and six consecutive visible lines is low risk.  **Recorded so the round can say the question was asked and answered rather than not asked.**  **(c) THE SPLICE SHAPE IS VERIFIED AT ONE SITE BY THE MAIN LOOP, not delegated wholesale**: `if (len != 8) { latch } else if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE) { ... } else { read arm }` -- no `return`, no `break`, control reaches the common tail, `(once)` marker present.  **(d) STILL OPEN, and it is the one that could make this round UNDERSTATED rather than overstated:** can a guest reach this handler with `len == 8` and a NON-8-byte-aligned `relative_addr` -- via `ldl`/`ldr`/`sdl`/`sdr`, another CPU family sharing the device, DMA, or the debugger?  The LINEAR comments make alignment load-bearing for the OOB argument, and that is a CROSS-FILE claim about `cpu_mips_instr_loadstore.c`, not a fact about `dev_sgi_re.c`.  **If alignment is not guaranteed, the OOB is reachable TODAY.**  *** (d) IS NOW SETTLED, PATH BY PATH, AND THE ANSWER IS THE SAFE ONE WITH EXACTLY ONE EXCEPTION.  Read-only review, agy seat; both load-bearing claims re-verified here by opening the files. ***  **ALIGNMENT IS GUARANTEED ON EVERY GUEST PATH:** `ld`/`sd` test `addr & (LS_SIZE-1)` and raise ADES/ADEL **without calling `memory_rw` at all**; the unaligned variants `ldl`/`ldr`/`sdl`/`sdr` compute `aligned_addr = addr & ~(wlen-1)` and pass THAT to all three of their `memory_rw` calls, so they cannot deliver an unaligned 8-byte access either -- verified at `cpu_mips_instr_unaligned.c:52` and its three call sites; narrower accesses carry `len != 8` and are declined by the fix; the device is registered only for SGI/MIPS so no other CPU family reaches it; and the MTE reads `re_linear_[ab]` through a bounded `for (i = 0; i < 32; ++i)` and never writes RE registers by DMA.  *** THE ONE EXCEPTION IS THE HOST DEBUGGER, AND IT IS NOT A GUEST VECTOR. ***  `put d` prints `WARNING: address isn't aligned` **and then proceeds**, handing the unaligned address straight to `store_64bit_word` and into `memory_rw` -- confirmed by opening `debugger_cmds.c`.  **TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the second is a trap for a future round:** the OOB is NOT guest-reachable today, so `#497` is correctly scoped and `sgilinearoob` stays filed; and **`sgilinearoob`'s 'unreachable' must be read as NOT-GUEST-REACHABLE**, because a probe driving `put d` at an unaligned address could reach it.  That is not a witness route -- the ladder's rung 3 wants a real guest instruction through real decode, and `put d` bypasses the guest instruction path entirely, so building a witness that way would be laundering rather than witnessing.  *** THE ROUND'S MOST IMPORTANT MEASUREMENT: `d_returnzero` SCORED 35/35 -- A COMPLETE ESCAPE OF EVERY ROW -- AND THE SEAT PREDICTED IT IN WRITING BEFORE MEASURING. ***  The mutant makes the declined path `return 0` instead of falling to the common tail.  **All 35 rows stayed green**, which confirms the v1 read rows were **SURVIVAL-ONLY ORACLES AT A REFUSAL-EFFECT SITE**: `return 0` raises a guest Data Bus Error, and a guest bus error leaves the HOST alive, so an oracle that asks only *did the host survive?* cannot see it.  That is vacuous BY CONSTRUCTION against this class, and it is the exact shape the pre-table CHANNEL check names -- *a survival oracle at a REFUSAL-EFFECT site: guarded and unguarded code both survive*.  **IT IS A CLAUSE-(d) NULL-REPAIR -- the guard kept, the reach-the-tail repair nulled -- so it is L2 and repaired IN-ROUND**, however late it was found.  Table 2's sentinel-preset rows are that repair.  *** WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING BEYOND THE FIX: THE PREDICTION WAS FILED FIRST. ***  `PREDICTIONS.out` carries the instrument's md5 and states plainly that *where measurement disagrees, THE TABLE WINS and the disagreement is the interesting part*.  This seat wrote down that `d_returnzero` would escape ENTIRELY, and then measured exactly that.  A prediction recorded after the result is not a prediction; its own mtime is the order proof, the same discriminator the oracle-correction rule uses.  **Every one of the table's predictions has matched measurement so far** -- FIX 35/35, floor (a) 15/35, floor (c) CONTROL=DEAD, `b_all` 15/35, the five per-site `b_*` at 30/35 each, `d_andwrite` 29/35, `d_growth` 29/35 (which discharges the accept-row FAILABILITY obligation by measured kill rather than by existing), `d_ifnotelse` 29/35.  *A table that matches a filed prediction on thirteen consecutive mutants is evidence about the INSTRUMENT, not just about the fix.*  *** AND `d_sharedbit` SETTLED THE ROUND'S ORIGINAL SCOPE DISAGREEMENT BY MEASUREMENT, WHICH IS THIS PROJECT'S RULE FOR SPLITS. ***  On pass 1 `codex` ruled SIX rounds and `fable5` ruled ONE; `opus5` made it moot by discharging the witness at all six sites.  **The table has now supplied the empirical argument neither side had.**  `d_sharedbit` -- the blunt latch-collision form, every site sharing one bit -- scored **33/35, reddening PRECISELY the two cross-site rows** and leaving every per-site row green.  That is not a near miss: **each per-site row runs in its own session, forked with `d->warned` at zero, so it is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to a collision** -- the shape can never be seen from inside one site.  **SO SIX SINGLE-SITE ROUNDS WOULD HAVE MADE THE SEAM ROW CONTINGENT RATHER THAN STRUCTURAL** -- and the stronger phrasing I first used, *guaranteed the blind spot by construction*, is WRONG and was caught before it entered any durable record, each shipping only per-site rows and each passing while the collision sat undetected across them.  The one-round form is what makes a cross-site row possible at all, and the cross-site row's existence is now justified by a measured kill rather than by taste.  *The prediction was filed before the run: PRETABLE's CHANNEL section named this exact blindness as the reason the row exists.  Sixteen consecutive mutants have now matched their filed predictions.*  *** AN L4 IN MY OWN SETTLED-PREMISES BLOCK: I RECORDED THE HANDLER AS SPANNING 221-384. IT ENDS AT 379. ***  Verified by the mechanical test -- the first `^}` at or after line 221 is line **379**, and `return 1;` sits on 377.  Corrected here and in the pass-2 brief.  *The figure was harmless in effect -- 380-384 are blank lines and a comment, so no exit call was mis-attributed and every derived number stands -- but it was propagated into a brief as a SETTLED premise, which is exactly the field seats are told not to re-derive.  A wrong number in a settled-premises block is worse than a wrong number anywhere else, because the block's whole purpose is to stop it being checked.*  *** THE ROUND IS MEASURED.  TWO 35-ROW TABLES, 22 MUTANTS, BOTH RESTORES VERIFIED, BOTH LOGS CARRYING THEIR COMPLETION SENTINELS. ***  **THE ESCAPE AND ITS REPAIR, both measured on the same instrument pair:** `d_returnzero` escaped **ALL 35 v1 rows (35/35)** and is **KILLED at 29/35 in v2**.  The evidence is one line and it is the clearest statement of the whole channel problem this round found:      `tlb_a lw surv    got exit0/0xdeadbeef    want exit0/0x0`  **The EXIT STATUS is identical on both sides.**  Only the untouched `0xdeadbeef` sentinel shows the guest load never completed.  A survival-only oracle at a refusal-effect site is vacuous BY CONSTRUCTION, and the repair was to make the row read a VALUE.  **AND IT WAS DISCLOSED AS AN EXPLICIT NO-ROW IN `PRETABLE.out` BEFORE TABLE 1 RAN, AND PREDICTED IN ADVANCE.**  That is the CHANNEL line's claim -- that a row's channel-under-its-mutant is knowable at WRITING time -- holding on its first mandated application.  **`d_lessthan` scored 35/35 and is a RESULT, NOT AN ESCAPE:** measured EQUIVALENT by construction over the reachable domain `len in {1,2,4,8}`.  The carrier's rule is exact here -- *a mutant that will not die has exactly three explanations, and silently re-aiming it picks one without measuring which*.  This one is case 2, the target is dead, and it is recorded as such.  **FLOOR (a)-(f) ALL DISCHARGED BY MEASUREMENT**, not by assertion: (a) 15/35 pre-fix, (b) verbatim reinstatement 15/35 and six per-site forms at 30/35 each, (c) null medium **strengthened from 12/35 to 6/35** as a side effect of the v2 rows demanding a value, (d) six clause-(d) mutants including the one that escaped and was repaired, (e) the contract in the probe header, (f) `e_swapsite` isolating the anchor.  **MY LEFTOVER SENTENCE WAS PROMOTED TO SIX ROWS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED:** an 8-byte `ld` still ends the host at every one of the six fixed windows (lines 245, 262, 279, 296, 346, 362), each `exit1+txt`.  I had asked for a sentence; the round shipped rows.  **ROW ASYMMETRY: NO, and the reason is the right one** -- every enumerated mutant reopening the LINEAR over-run is already killed by a symmetric row, and the `& 0x1f` mask is outside the clause-(d) closure.  Recorded in CHANNEL rather than as rows, which is the addition licence working: no row was added because a site felt riskier.  **PREDICTION ACCURACY: 20 of 22 EXACT.**  Both misses under-counted the cross-site blast radius while getting the mechanism right -- a more useful failure than a lucky hit, and the seat says so itself.  *** THE PRETABLE ARTIFACT WAS AUDITED END TO END, WHICH THE CARRIER EXPLICITLY OWED, AND THE OWED SENTENCE IS: THE CHANNEL LINE HELD ON ITS FIRST MANDATED APPLICATION. ***  Every channel named at WRITING time was confirmed across 41 measured runs over two tables, with **37 of 41 exact-score predictions**; the four deviations were one pre-declared two-candidate uncertainty and two blast-radius under-counts, **all on aggregate rows and all in the SAFE direction -- more rows red than predicted**.  **IT DID REAL WRITE-TIME WORK TWICE**, which is the difference between a rule holding and a rule being obeyed: it drove the bit-3 accept-offset design that `d_growth` later reddened, and it caught `xsite order` as VACUOUS-BY-CONSTRUCTION before any table ran, prescribing `e_swapsite` -- which table 2 then confirmed as the exact discriminator (`6msg` GREEN, `order` RED).  **AND ITS ONE MEASURED LIMIT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE RATIFICATION: it validates the channel a row NAMES, not whether that observable matches the CLAIM the row carries.**  That gap was disclosed pre-table, measured as `d_returnzero`'s 35/35 escape on v1, and repaired and re-proven on v2.  *The seat's own phrase -- 'it half-worked' -- is the honest form and is kept rather than smoothed.*  **THE `#490` FAILURE MODE DID NOT RECUR.**  Section 5 prescribes 30 rows and addendum A1 diffs its own rewrite explicitly (REMOVED `ld readkill`, ADDED six `ld kill`, NET 35).  **Both instrument generations were diffed against the prescription** and both implement exactly the 35 prescribed rows under the prescribed names.  That is the row-list-diff obligation discharged rather than assumed.  **ONE N/A WAS AN UNRUN CHECK IN DISGUISE, AND THE BLOCK REFUTED ITS OWN REASON.**  Claim C2's DBE-half no-row was justified as *would test a fix nobody proposed* -- **wrong: that edit is squarely inside the clause-(d) DEPENDS-ON closure.**  The block's own mutant enumeration then built `d_returnzero` anyway, measured the escape and repaired it under L2.  *The apparatus caught its own bad reason inside the same round, and the sequence disclose -> predict -> measure -> repair is log-attested rather than claimed.*  **A DOCUMENTED RESIDUAL, correctly NOT converted into row debt:** the seven contract rows are never reddened by a product-shaped mutant in either table.  The null medium reds them (29 FAILs), proving non-tautology but not sensitivity to a silent read-kill removal specifically.  **Under the row-demand bound no mutant is owed**, so this is a residual and not debt -- the distinction the addition licence exists to hold.  *** TWO RECORD DEFECTS THE AUDIT FOUND, ONE OF THEM TIME-SENSITIVE -- AND THE RECOVERY ATTEMPT FAILED SAFELY, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. ***  **(F1) AN ORDER CLAIM CONTRADICTED BY ITS OWN LOG.**  Addendum 1 stamps itself *added 19:22 ... BEFORE the definitive 35-row table*, and *what runs after it: everything* -- while its own preserved log stamps `=== b_all 19:21:21 ===`, and the three pre-loop probes put the run's start at about 19:14-19:16.  **The load-bearing order survives on harder evidence** (the 35-row instrument frozen at 19:16, its md5 echoed at the head of the master log), but the NARRATIVE claim is refuted by the log -- in the one file whose whole value is its order property.  *And the standing phrase 'its own mtime is the order proof' stops being literally true the moment addenda are appended in place.*  **(F2) THE v1 INSTRUMENT IS GONE, AND I ALMOST PRESERVED THE WRONG FILE AS v1.**  The table-1 probe was overwritten in place and is cited by md5 `d04d6bc4...` in three records.  `/tmp/gx497_probe_frozen.py` still existed -- **and its md5 is `7b74ee69...`, which is the v2 hash.  The frozen path was REUSED.**  So v1 is genuinely unrecoverable.  *** THE md5 CHECK IS WHAT MADE THAT FAILURE SAFE.  Without it I would have copied v2 into `table1/` under a v1 filename, in a directory three records cite BY MD5 -- a mislabelled artifact is far worse than a missing one, because a missing artifact announces itself and a mislabelled one does not. ***  Nothing is unverifiable: the v1-to-v2 delta is re-derivable from the preserved want-columns.  **The lesson is the frozen-copy rule's missing half: a frozen path must be STAMPED, not reused** -- `probe.v1.py` and `probe.v2.py`, never one `frozen.py` overwritten per generation.  *** THE SCOPE WARRANT WAS OVERCLAIMED AND THE SEAT THAT MADE THE RULING IS THE ONE THAT CORRECTED IT.  2026-08-30. ***  I wrote that six single-site rounds *would have guaranteed this blind spot by construction*.  **`d_sharedbit` proves something narrower:** the only channel observing latch sharing is a multi-site session -- two rows of 35 -- so each single-site round's OWN DETECTOR is blind.  It does **not** follow that the SEQUENCE is: the mandatory pre-table GUARD-FIELD check carries `#490`'s bitfield question, and a compliant round 2 would have owed the cross-site row the moment a second bit entered a shared field.  **The honest form: the joint round made the seam row STRUCTURAL in one act; the partitioned sequence would have made it CONTINGENT on five future acts of compliance.**  Weaker claim, same conclusion.  *** AND A CIRCULARITY I OWE PLAINLY: the shared-bitfield hazard exists BECAUSE the one-round fix chose six bits in one `uint32_t`. ***  Six independent rounds would most naturally have added six independent `int`s, under which sharing is impossible and there is no blind spot to guard.  So the cross-site rows partly defend a hazard the joint design introduced.  **The non-circular licence for one round was never the table -- it is the REOPENING RULE**, whose every clause is satisfied: witnessed 26/26, same device, same semantic class, one detector, no new oracle.  `d_sharedbit` is corroboration of the detector's SHAPE, not the round-count's warrant.  *** THE CAPPED ASK-AGAIN IS NOW SPENT, AND IT RETURNED TWO ESCAPE CANDIDATES -- BOTH READINGS, BOTH OWED ONE MEASURING PASS BEFORE DISPOSITION IS FINAL. ***  **F1 -- `d->warned |= BIT` becomes `d->warned = BIT`, one character.**  Traced to pass all 35 rows: same-site `lat1` still counts 1 because the second decline sees its own bit, and `xsite 6msg` visits each site ONCE in ascending order, so the clearing of earlier sites' bits is never observed.  Property broken: a guest ALTERNATING narrow accesses between two windows re-announces on every alternation -- an unbounded guest-drivable `fatal()` flood, the exact `floodclass` the latch exists to shut, while the `(once)` claim stays green.  **ROOT CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL: every multi-site session uses ONE traffic pattern -- each site once, ascending.**  One row kills the whole family: extend the existing xsite session with a REVISIT of site 1 and pin its count at 1.  No new session, no new oracle.  *And a note for the pre-table check's future: `#490`'s bitfield question was asked in its SET direction only. THE IMPLEMENTER SHOULD READ THIS BEFORE THE BRIEF -- the brief has three known defects the panel repaired. ***  **1. `break` IS NOT LEGAL C AT THESE SITES, and EIGHT OF EIGHT ANSWERING SEATS SAID SO.**  The guards sit in `if`/`else if` arms, not a `switch`, so `break` exits the nearest enclosing loop or switch -- there is none.  The correct edit is an `else if` SPLICE: the decline arm ends and control falls to the common tail.  One structural token changes per site (`if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE)` becomes `} else if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE) {`).  *Unanimity on a defect in the brief is the premise-audit instruction working: the seats were told not to ratify, and none did.*  **2. `return 1`, NOT `return 0` -- and two seats CHECKED it rather than reasoning.**  `memory_rw.c` coerces a 0 return to -1 and the `res <= 0 && !no_exceptions` arm raises `mips_cpu_exception(..., EXCEPTION_DBE, ...)`. THE COMMON TAIL IS DEAD CODE TODAY AND THIS FIX MAKES IT LIVE. rows.title: a probe row whose oracle is 'the store had no effect' PASSES when the store never executed -- seven of #496's twenty-two rows, and the class is tree-wide
rows.witness: harness: derived row-by-row against regress/gdrom_cond_probe.py by the fable5 seat in #496's adjudication pass; NOT yet exhibited by a run, which is why it files rather than reopening #496
rows.note: *** THE SEED SENTINEL PROTECTS LOADS.  STORES HAVE NO EXECUTION WITNESS, AND SEVEN OF `gdrom_cond_probe.py`'s TWENTY-TWO ROWS PASS IF THEIR CRITICAL STORE NEVER RUNS. ***  Named by the fable5 seat in `#496`'s ADJUDICATION pass, as a REFINE on the round's own F11.  **THE SHAPE.**  `#496` added `SEED = 0xdead` so an unexecuted LOAD is distinguishable from a load that genuinely read zero -- and `bit()` returns `SEED-NEVER-RAN` so the sentinel cannot itself be misread as a set bit.  Both are right and both are about the READ side.  A row whose oracle is the CONSEQUENCE OF A STORE has no equivalent: if the store silently fails to execute, the device stays in its fresh state -- **and for these rows the fresh state IS the want.**  The seven, with why each is green on a dead store: `R5b cond 00` (cond stays 0x0 = want); `R7 no event` (event stays clear = want); `R7b cond st` (before == after trivially); `R10 a88 nop` (0x0|0x0|0 = want); `R3 a88 x3` and `R4 cond x3` (one live store plus two dead ones still yields count == 1 = want); `R5c cond a0`.  **R1, R2, R5, R6, R8, R9 FAIL SAFE** -- their wants are values only a live store produces.  *** WHY THE CONTROLS DO NOT COVER IT, which is the whole reason this is a class and not a note. ***  The four control rows catch a WHOLE-RUN-DEAD rig, and they are per-run.  The contention actually measured on `#496` was PER-SESSION INTERMITTENT -- the probe forks one gxemul per row, so a single row's session can die while every other row and all four controls run fine.  A per-run control cannot see a per-session failure.  **NOT A FLOOR BREACH, and the reasoning matters because it is what keeps this from being an in-round fix.**  Every enumerated mutant still reds WHEN THE APPARATUS RUNS, and no run has yet exhibited the false pass.  It is a latent apparatus risk, not a measured escape -- so it FILES under the stopping rule rather than reopening `#496`.  *** THE SKETCH, from the seat, and it costs nothing for five of the seven: assert the decline announce -- already in the transcript, count == 1 -- inside the SAME row's got string. ***  That announce is the store's own execution proof: it cannot appear unless the guest store reached the device handler.  `R10` needs a trailing canary decline instead (it has no announce of its own, by construction -- silence IS its oracle).  **`R3` and `R4` are the hard pair and no cheap form is known**: a MID-SEQUENCE store death leaves count == 1, which is exactly the want, so the announce trick is circular there.  Those two need a distinguishable per-store marker or a different oracle shape, and that is the part worth a round rather than a rider.  GENERALITY: this is not specific to gdrom.  **Any pty-driven probe in this tree whose oracle is 'the device state did NOT change' has the same hole**, because not-changing is what a dead session produces.  A sweep is NOT proposed here -- the population is unmeasured and a sweep would be `#392`'s shape.  What is proposed is the write-time question: *for each row, what does a dead session score?*  If the answer is the want, the row needs an execution witness.  *** THE COUNT WAS WRONG AND IS AT LEAST NINE, NOT SEVEN.  codex seat, same day, under the standing license while adjudicating something else. ***  **`R12` is an eighth**: its oracle is the presence of the no-data diagnostic after a declined COND write, and a FRESH device has `cond == 0` -- so if the declining store never executes, the subsequent DATA read produces exactly the wanted diagnostic anyway.  **`R13` is a ninth**, and it is the worst of them because it drives NINE stores: if the second `0xa0` or any of the first six DATA words is missed, the mutant never reaches the kill guard and the oracle still reads `0|exit0`.  *A row that drives a longer sequence has MORE ways to die silently, not fewer* -- which inverts the intuition that a richer row is a stronger row.  **THE SKETCHES ARE PER-ROW AND CHEAP FOR BOTH.**  `R12`: additionally require its own COND-decline announcement, which no dead store can produce.  `R13`: prove the BUSY TRANSITIONS rather than the absence of a kill -- set after the first `0xa0`, clear after six words, set again after the second `0xa0` -- so a missing store reds on a transition that did not happen instead of passing on a kill that did not happen.  Both are execution witnesses in the row's own channel, which is the shape the original sketch already proposed for the other five.
rows.state_note:
*** A codex CENSUS WAS FIRED 2026-09-08 AND CUT SHORT BEFORE DELIVERING THE COUNTS -- BY MY OWN
REPEAT OF A SCOPE ERROR I HAD RECORDED ONE BRIEF EARLIER.  Its partial findings are below and three
of them are new. ***

**THE MEMBERSHIP DEFINITION IT GAVE IS THE BEST STATEMENT OF THIS CLASS YET, and it is the property
rather than any correlate:**

> *"A row belongs in this census if its own oracle can pass when the tested action is OMITTED; it is
> already paired only if another check ON THAT SAME ACCESS requires positive evidence AFTER the
> action."*

It said so explicitly of the trap: *"a label such as `survives' or `unchanged' does not decide
membership"*, and *"some negative assertions include a required readback in the same predicate,
while others rely on a separate row or only on process status."*

*** A FOURTH GUISE I HAD NOT NAMED, and it is subtler than the three in this row: ***

> **"exactly one message across two or more accesses."  The FIRST access can supply the one message
> even if a LATER access never runs.**

The row looks positive -- it asserts a message is PRESENT, not absent -- and is still satisfied by a
skipped action, because the evidence was produced before the skip. *That defeats the obvious repair
for this whole class, which is "pair the negative oracle with a positive one": a positive oracle
sited BEFORE the action under test is no better than a negative one.*

*** TWO CONCRETE SITES NAMED, both of which a text search would miss: ***
* **the CMMU probe prints a row labelled "VALUE" whose return path grades only SURVIVAL** -- the
  label claims more than the oracle delivers;
* **some ARM flag rows reduce the untouched-output sentinel to a SINGLE BIT that matches the
  expected answer**, so the sentinel cannot distinguish untouched from correct.

Both are unverified here and are recorded as LEADS, not findings.

*** AND IT NOTICED ME EDITING A PROBE WHILE IT WAS READING IT. ***  Its words: *"I detected a change
to `lca_confbus_probe.py` while reading it.  I'm taking an in-memory snapshot of the permitted probes
so the final row names, counts, and line references all describe one consistent version.  No probes
have been run or files changed."*  **This project records the edit-a-running-script hazard for
SHELL and for a multi-run PYTHON driver; this is the same hazard from the READER's side**, and the
seat handled it correctly and said so. *A seat that had silently continued would have produced line
references spanning two versions of one file.*

*** WHY IT WAS CUT SHORT, AND IT IS THE SAME DEFECT AS THE `exit0oracle' FIRING ONE BRIEF EARLIER. ***
I wrote the scope as `regress/*.py -- the probe files only`, which is not a bound at all: it is the
whole directory. The stream reached **2.4 MB** and stopped at the snapshot step without ever
producing the per-file table.

**I had recorded the fix in [[exit0oracle]] within the hour** -- *"A READING-SCOPE BOUND MUST BE
EXTENSIONAL.  Name the files."* -- and then wrote the next brief with a glob. That is this project's
own finding about itself, exactly: knowing a rule and having it fire on the object in front of you
are different problems, and only the second is solved by writing the rule down.

**RE-FIRE OWED**, with the file list stated extensionally and the membership definition above given
as settled so the budget goes to the census rather than to re-deriving it.

rows.title: panel.sh WARNS that a brief exceeds the argv cap and then fires the two argv seats anyway -- measured, two seats lost on a 38 KB brief
rows.witness: harness:regress/artifacts/panelargvcap/controls_20260830/ -- the same control script scores 6/6 rc=0 on the fixed panel.sh and EXTRACT FAILED rc=9 on the pre-fix form preserved beside it.
rows.note: *** MEASURED 2026-08-30: A 38 KB BRIEF LOST TWO SEATS, AND `panel.sh` PRINTED A WARNING AND FIRED THEM ANYWAY. ***  `WARNING: brief is 38983 bytes (>30KB). Codex/Kimi take it on argv and may fail with 'Argument list too long'. Trim, or point those seats at the file path instead of piping its contents.`  Then it launched all seven, and:      codex.txt  ->  `.../codex: Argument list too long`   (123 bytes)      kimi.txt   ->  `.../kimi: Argument list too long`    (97 bytes)  **grok survived because it uses `--prompt-file`**, which the carrier already names as the one CLI seat immune to this; the three Ollama seats POST and have no argv at all.  So the loss is exactly the two seats that take the brief on the command line.  *** THE DEFECT IS THAT THE WARNING IS ADVISORY. ***  It correctly diagnoses the problem, correctly names the remedy, and then does the thing it just warned about.  That is one step milder than the check-that-cannot-fail this project names first -- it INFORMS and does not ACT -- and the operator it informs is the same party who just wrote the brief and is about to walk away while nine seats run.  **The failure surfaces minutes later as two ~100-byte seat files, which the seat check reports as a seat failure rather than as a launcher failure.**  **THE REMEDY IS ALREADY IN THE WARNING'S OWN TEXT and costs nothing at run time: when the brief exceeds the cap, pass codex and kimi a SHORT PROMPT NAMING THE FILE PATH instead of the contents.**  Both accept it -- recovered by hand in this incident, in one command each, and both then answered.  The file-reading seats can read the brief; only the packet-fed ones need it inlined, and those are the ones with no argv limit.  *** NOT FIXED IN THE MOMENT, DELIBERATELY: a panel was running, and editing a running shell script corrupts it mid-execution -- bash reads incrementally by byte offset. ***  That is a documented defect class here and the reason this is a filed row rather than an in-passing edit.  **WHAT THE FIX OWES, since it changes the script every panel runs:** two negative controls, in the shape this project already requires -- prove an oversized brief now reaches both seats and they ANSWER, and prove a normal-sized brief still goes on argv unchanged (so the switch does not silently become the default and change what every seat receives).  *Note the cap is not exactly 32 KB and the warning threshold is 30 KB; the measured failure was at 38,983 bytes and no bisection was done, so the true boundary is not established and this row does not claim one.*  *** FIXED 2026-08-30.  `panel.sh` WARNED ABOUT THE ARGV CAP AND THEN LAUNCHED ANYWAY -- the remedy its own message recommended was one the script could simply TAKE. ***  A 38 KB brief killed BOTH argv-fed seats with `Argument list too long`; codex and kimi had to be recovered BY HAND, while this block printed advice sixty lines above the launch that ignored it.  **IT IS THE CHECK-THAT-CANNOT-FAIL FAMILY'S SIBLING: a message reporting an ACTION the code does not take.**  The re-firing message (`re-firing once (a wall can be minutes long) ...` followed by a `return 2` every caller discards) is the same defect, and its recorded lesson applies unchanged -- telling the operator it was handled is WORSE than silence, because the one person who could fix it by hand is told not to.  **THE FIX IS THAT BOTH SEATS ALREADY READ FILES.**  Grok has been immune all along (`--prompt-file`), agy too (`--add-dir` plus a pointer prompt); codex and kimi were the only two still fed the brief on argv.  Above the cap they now get `PTR_PROMPT` -- read `$BRIEF_ABS` and review it as its own Questions section directs -- and below it the inline form is byte-unchanged.  **CONTROLLED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the control READS THE REAL FILE rather than a re-typed copy** -- `sed` extracts the decision block and the prompt-build out of `panel.sh` and `eval`s them, because a verification that shares the defect of the thing it verifies always passes, which this project has measured.  POST-FIX **6/6, rc=0**, including both boundary rows (exactly 30000 -> inline, 30001 -> pointer) and a both-seats-agree column.  PRE-FIX the same script reports **EXTRACT FAILED, rc=9** -- *the old form has no cap branch at all* -- which is the failability proof: the test can fail, and it fails on the code this fix replaces.  `PANEL_ARGV_CAP` exists ONLY so the branch is testable without keeping a 38 KB fixture, and the comment says so; it is not a tuning knob.  *** AND THE GATE CAUGHT A RECORD DEFECT I MADE WHILE CLOSING THIS ROW: I wrote the fix up as a ledger ENTRY with `seat: mainloop`. ***  There is no such seat -- the declared vocabulary is the nine, and `mainloop` appeared exactly ONCE in 2,278 entries, mine.  **A seat entry is what sections G and H COUNT for panel coverage, so inventing one inflates the roster with a seat that never answered** -- the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape reached from the other side, by manufacture rather than by omission.  Main-loop work belongs in the row's note, which is where this sentence is.  *Caught by `precommit_check.sh` naming the declared list back at me, not by review.*

rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c's CRIME_RE_TEX index uses >> 3 where its three sibling arms use >> 1 -- consecutive writes overlap by three entries and 81 of 112 are unreachable
rows.witness: harness:ENUMERATED against the shipped source, 2026-08-30.  Walked every 8-byte access in [0x1600,0x16e0): shipped base indices run 0..27, reaching 31 of 112 cells, leaving 81 unreachable, with a 3-entry overlap between consecutive accesses.  Both figures in the row reproduce EXACTLY.
rows.note:
*** A GUEST WRITING THE TEXTURE ARRAY SEQUENTIALLY CORRUPTS ENTRIES IT HAS ALREADY WRITTEN, AND 81 OF 112 ENTRIES CANNOT BE REACHED AT ALL.  Found by the codex seat under the STANDING LICENSE while answering a scope question about a different defect in the same file. ***  **THE EVIDENCE IS THE SIBLING COMPARISON, and it is as strong as this kind of finding gets: three arms of the same handler do it one way and the fourth does it another.**  `CRIME_RE_TLB_A`, `_TLB_B` and `_TLB_C` each compute their index as  `int tlbi = ((relative_addr & 0x1ff) >> 1) & 0xff;`  -- a BYTE offset shifted right by 1 to give a HALFWORD index.  `CRIME_RE_TEX` computes  `int tlbi = ((relative_addr & 0xff) >> 3) & 0xff;`  on an array of the same kind, `uint16_t re_tex[112]`.  **THE ARITHMETIC, and it is decidable from the declaration alone.**  The window is `relative_addr >= CRIME_RE_TEX && < CRIME_RE_TEX + 0xe0` -- 224 bytes -- and 112 halfwords is exactly 224 bytes, so window and array correspond one-to-one.  The write loop steps `tlbi++` once per halfword, so an 8-byte `sd` writes FOUR entries.  But `>> 3` advances the STARTING index by only ONE per 8-byte step:      offset 0x00 -> tlbi 0, writes 0,1,2,3      offset 0x08 -> tlbi 1, writes 1,2,3,4   <- OVERLAPS THREE      offset 0x10 -> tlbi 2, writes 2,3,4,5   <- OVERLAPS THREE  So consecutive aligned writes overwrite three quarters of their predecessor.  And the top of the window, `0xdf >> 3` = 27, reaches index 30 at most: **entries 31..111 are unreachable by any access.**  **`>> 1` gives exactly the right answer at both ends**, which is what makes this a typo rather than a design: `0x00 >> 1` = 0, and `0xdf >> 1` = 111 -- precisely the last valid index.  The three siblings already use it.  *** THIS IS NOT THE WIDTH-KILL CLASS AND MUST NOT BE FOLDED INTO IT. ***  `widthkillclass` is a guest ENDING THE HOST by choosing an access size; this is SILENT DATA CORRUPTION inside a legal, correctly-sized access.  Different class, different fix, different detector -- and the round-scope rule's same-semantic-class arm fails, so it files rather than joining `#497`.  **Arguably worse in one respect and better in another:** it is silent, so nothing announces it and a guest gets wrong texture data rather than a dead emulator; but it corrupts only emulated device state, where a host kill ends the process.  Ranked med on that trade, not high.  *** WHAT A ROUND HERE OWES, and one of them is a trap: ***  a rung-3 witness (the machine and window are already established -- `-E sgi -e ip32`, `dev_sgi_re_init(machine, mem, 0x15000000)`, so TEX is at guest `0xb5001600`); and **an ADJACENT-OFFSET oracle, because a naive 'the sd changed something' accept row STAYS GREEN under this defect** -- the write does land, just in the wrong cells and on top of its neighbour.  The row has to write two adjacent 8-byte groups and read back the FIRST, which is the only shape that sees an overlap.  SOURCE-DERIVED, NOT MEASURED.  The seat said so explicitly and this row repeats it: no probe has been run against TEX.  The arithmetic is checkable from the declaration and was re-verified here against the three sibling arms, but the behaviour has not been observed on a running guest.  *** THE COUPLING TO `sgirekills` IS ENFORCEABLE BY ONE ROW, SO THIS IS NOT A HARD PREREQUISITE.  Adjudicated 2026-08-30, recorded in both rows. ***  If `sgirekills` ships TEX's read arm MIRRORED -- using the same `>> 3` expression as the store -- then a ONE-SIDED fix of this row reds its round-trip row loudly: store `>> 1` against read `>> 3` writes cells 4-7 and reads 1-4, and the reverse likewise, while the JOINT fix keeps identity and the row stays green.  **So this row's fix becomes a DECLARED TWO-SITE EDIT with a tripwire already in place**, rather than a change that could silently half-land.  **AND THE ORDER IS GENUINELY FREE, with a real trade either way**: this row first makes TEX's ACCEPT identical in kind to the TLB arms, and its own red-first witness needs no readback at all because the store loop's `debug("d->re_tex[%i] = ...")` lines already show the index.  `sgirekills` first is licensed by severity -- host kills outrank silent corruption -- and hands this row a strictly stronger witness afterwards, since a write-write-read overlap can then be observed through real readback.  *** RE-DERIVED BY ENUMERATION 2026-08-30, after a sibling row in this family was WITHDRAWN as a false out-of-bounds. ***  All three of this row's figures were walked rather than reasoned: every `relative_addr` in `0x1600-0x16df` mapped through `((ra & 0xff) >> 3) & 0xff` with four writes per access.  **Maximum index 30 -- so this row is NOT an OOB and does not claim to be**; `re_tex[112]` has ample headroom.  **81 cells unreachable** and **3 entries of overlap** between consecutive 8-byte writes, both matching the filed claim exactly.  *The withdrawn sibling was filed source-derived and never range-checked; this one now has been.*  *** CONFIRMED BY ENUMERATION AND RE-DIAGNOSED: IT IS A UNIT MISMATCH, NOT A WRONG SHIFT. ***  The codex seat derived the TEX geometry from the CRIME spec -- 28 entries of 64 bits at 0x1600 + 8n -- and my walk of the shipped code found base indices running exactly 0..27.  **Independent agreement on 28, one from the specification and one from the source.**  28 x 8 = 224 = 0xe0 (the window bound) and 28 x 4 = 112 (the array), so `re_tex` is 28 entries of FOUR HALFWORDS each.  **`>> 3` therefore selects the ENTRY correctly.  The array is indexed in HALFWORDS, and entry n begins at halfword 4n -- so the code writes [n],[n+1],[n+2],[n+3] where it must write [4n]..[4n+3].**  Verified over all 28 entry starts that `(addr & 0xff) >> 1` is identically `4 * ((addr & 0xff) >> 3)`, so the three siblings' `>> 1` IS the correct expression.  **NOT A MEMORY-SAFETY DEFECT** -- max index 30 against a [112] array.  Model correctness only: the guest's texture data lands in the wrong cells and clobbers its own previous write.  *The fix comment matters more than the edit here: `>> 1 because re_tex is halfword-indexed and each 64-bit entry spans four halfwords` survives a future reader, while `>> 1 to match the siblings` invites someone to "fix" the siblings instead.*  *** THE NATURAL OBJECTION TO THE PROPOSED `>> 3` -> `>> 1` FIX IS THAT IT COULD RUN OFF THE END OF A [112] ARRAY.  CHECKED 2026-08-31: IT CANNOT, AND THE MARGIN IS EXACTLY ZERO. ***  Recorded because an unanswered overflow objection is what stalls a one-token fix at review, and because "exactly zero margin" is a fact the fixing round must know rather than rediscover.  With `>> 1` the index is the halfword offset: window `[0x00, 0xe0)`, so `tlbi` spans 0..111 and the array is `uint16_t re_tex[112]` -- one-to-one, as the sibling comparison predicts.  The write loop steps `tlbi++` per halfword, so an 8-byte `sd` writes FOUR entries.  **The worst case is the last legal 8-byte slot.**  8-byte accesses are 8-ALIGNED (the guest path cannot deliver an unaligned `len == 8` -- ordinary `ld`/`sd` raise ADEL/ADES without calling `memory_rw`, and the `ldl/ldr/sdl/sdr` helper masks the address itself), so the reachable offsets are `0x00, 0x08, ... 0xd8`.  At `0xd8`: `tlbi = 0xd8 >> 1 = 108`, writing **108, 109, 110, 111** -- the last four entries, and `0xd8 + 8 = 0xe0` is exactly the window bound.  **Fits with nothing to spare.**  *The zero margin is why this is worth writing down rather than waving through: `0xdc` would give `tlbi = 110` and write 110..113, two entries past the array -- so the fix's safety rests ENTIRELY on the 8-byte alignment invariant, exactly as the LINEAR arms' own `#497` comment says theirs does.*  A round shipping this owes the same alignment note the LINEAR arms already carry, and its detector owes an accept row at the LAST slot (`0xd8`) -- which is the window's far bound, and per the 2026-08-31 correction to the accept-row rule, a SECOND row or an ANCHORED oracle for the near bound.  *** PASS-1 PACKET-FED PANEL, 2026-08-31 (`_scratchpad/panel_20260831_045142`): THE CORE CLAIM IS UPHELD BY THREE INDEPENDENT DERIVATIONS, AND THE ZERO MARGIN IS CONFIRMED TWICE. ***  Reachability: **31 of 112 entries, 81 unreachable** -- glm and deepseek both derived 31 independently and it matches this row's original figure; minimax wrote 30/82 and is off by one (`[0,30]` is 31 entries).  **glm named a premise the brief never stated and I had assumed**: the whole `& 0xff` analysis needs `CRIME_RE_TEX` to be 256-aligned.  Checked: `0x1600`, so it holds, and every sibling window's mask matches its own base as well.  **minimax supplied a better warrant than the one I led with**: `112 x 2 = 224 = 0xe0` is an INTRINSIC identity between array size and window size, where the sibling comparison is merely comparative and can be answered with *maybe TEX is different on purpose*.  **The fixing round should lead with the size identity.**  **deepseek answered the detector-design question**: no index-only mutant survives a detector that writes and reads back EVERY halfword, so full distinctness closes the clause-(f) hole here.  **MY BRIEF CARRIED A COUNT DEFECT, caught by two seats independently**: it said *four* windows compute an index and then inlined *six*.  Immaterial to the arithmetic and it is precisely the class the brief's own opener warns about -- recorded rather than quietly fixed.  *** STILL UNSETTLED, AND THE SEATS WERE RIGHT NOT TO SETTLE IT: whether hardware might legitimately space texture registers every 8 bytes.  There is no datasheet for this device in `_scratchpad/`.  That question decides FIX vs DOCUMENT and is the one thing a file-reading seat or a manual could still change.***  *** THE PANEL'S ONE OPEN QUESTION IS NOW CLOSED WITHOUT A DATASHEET, AND THE DISPOSITION IS FIX RATHER THAN DOCUMENT.  Derived 2026-08-31. ***  All three seats correctly declined to settle *whether hardware might legitimately space texture registers every 8 bytes*, and `ls _scratchpad/*.pdf` confirms there is **no SGI, CRIME, IP32 or O2 document** among the fifteen present.  **But the question turns out not to gate the fix, because BOTH candidate readings give the SAME index expression.**  *(a)* the struct's own declaration -- `uint16_t re_tex[112]`, indexed by halfword -> `offset >> 1`.  *(b)* the rival reading the missing spec would license -- **28 x 64-bit entries, one per 8-byte store**.  The write loop emits FOUR halfwords per store, so entry `k` must START at halfword `4k`, i.e. the correct index is `(offset >> 3) * 4`.  **For 8-ALIGNED offsets `(offset >> 3) * 4` IS `offset >> 1`** -- checked across the window (0x00->0, 0x08->4, 0x10->8, 0x40->32, 0xd0->104, 0xd8->108, identical both ways).  *** SO `>> 1` IS CORRECT UNDER BOTH HYPOTHESES AND `>> 3` IS WRONG UNDER BOTH -- under (b) it is short by exactly the factor of 4 that the loop consumes. ***  **This also strengthens minimax's intrinsic-identity warrant rather than replacing it.**  That argument (`112 x 2 = 224 = 0xe0`) depends on the `uint16_t` CHOICE being right, and the header does not confirm it: `crmfbreg.h` carries an explicit `/* 32bit entries ... */` comment for **LINEAR_A/B and not for TEX**, so the element size there is GXemul's own reading.  *The both-hypotheses derivation is the stronger form precisely because it does not need the element size to be settled at all.*  **And the window bound is confirmed from the header rather than from the guard**: the next register is `CRIME_RE_CLIP_IDS = 0x16e0`, so `[0x1600, 0x16e0)` really is 224 bytes and the guard's `+ 0xe0` is not an invention.  *What is still genuinely unknown, and is now a DOCUMENTATION question rather than a blocker: how many entries the real device has and how wide they are.  The fix is right either way; the array's declared type is a separate, smaller question that no evidence in this tree settles.*  *** THE `sgirekills` / `sgitexindex` COUPLING, ESTABLISHED 2026-08-31 AND RECORDED ON BOTH ROWS SO NEITHER CAN BE CLOSED IN IGNORANCE OF THE OTHER. ***  **The fact, which is settled:** `sgitexindex`'s `>> 1` is correct under BOTH candidate readings of a TEX entry -- 112 halfwords indexed `offset >> 1`, or 28 64-bit entries where entry `k` starts at halfword `4k`, since `(offset >> 3) * 4 == offset >> 1` for 8-aligned offsets.  **So the store's shift is wrong INDEPENDENTLY of the missing datasheet**, and there is no SGI document in `_scratchpad/`.  **Consequence for `sgirekills`:** its TEX read arm can only ACCEPT in the MIRRORED form -- reusing the store's `>> 3` -- because only that round-trips what the store wrote.  Mirroring therefore enshrines a KNOWN-WRONG index in a second place, and gives it a green round-trip row.  *When someone later corrects the shift, that row goes RED because of their correct fix.*  **Consequence for `sgitexindex`, in the other direction:** the TEX read arm is TODAY a live host kill, so **no guest can read back what those writes stored** and the aliasing is currently unobservable from inside the guest.  Fixing `sgirekills` is what would expose it.  That bears on severity and on ORDER, and neither row had recorded it.  *Neither consequence decides the disposition -- that is the question `sgirekills` is held for and a panel is answering it.  What is recorded here is the COUPLING, which is a fact either way.*

*** MAIN-LOOP MEASUREMENT 2026-08-31 (not a seat answer; recorded here rather than in `entries` so it cannot be counted toward the panel). ***  evidence: grep -rn re_tex src/ (3 occurrences, all dev_sgi_re.c)

MEASURED BY GREP, 2026-08-31, settling hold_question (1) and reframing (3): `re_tex' occurs EXACTLY THREE TIMES in the whole tree, all in dev_sgi_re.c -- the declaration, ONE write site, and a debug() on the very next line echoing what was just stored.  Nothing else in src/ mentions it.  *** SO THE `>> 3' ARM IS THE SOLE WRITER (question 1: YES, the fix's assumption holds and changing it repairs rather than splits the mapping) AND THE ARRAY HAS NO CONSUMER ANYWHERE IN THE MODEL. ***  That is stronger than the row's own framing, which says only that no GUEST can read it back because the READ arm is fatal+exit: even with that arm de-fatalised there is nothing else that consumes the array, so the aliasing's only channel today is the debug() text.  Consequence: it lowers this row (no consumer, no observable corruption) and couples it to `sgirekills', whose mirrored-TEX-read fix would create the array's FIRST consumer.
