rows.note: *** THE HARNESS PUNISHES PROGRESS, AND TWO REPAIRS HAVE NOW MOVED THE PUNISHMENT WITHOUT REMOVING IT. ***  The selftest first broke when `pit8253_latch_probe.py` was wired and its exemption deleted; `_pick_exempt_detector()` fixed that by DERIVING the exemplar.  It broke again when `sh4_bsc_width_probe.py` was discharged; deriving M5c-M5e and M12 fixed that.  **Both repairs kept the same shape -- pick a live exemption and take something away from it -- so the tripwire moved from the FIRST discharge to the LAST one.**  **THE ROOT CAUSE, named by the seat in one sentence: the selftest MUTATES LIVE INPUT DATA IT DOES NOT NEED.**  A mutant that must find a real exemption to delete is coupled to a table designed to empty; a mutant that INSERTS its own fixture is not.  M9's machinery already does exactly this for the gate list, so the pattern is in-tree rather than invented.  *** THE END STATE IS REACHABLE AND IT IS WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH A ROUND: *** six exemptions remain, all dated 2026-09-20.  When the last is discharged -- which is the point of the table -- `precommit_check.sh` prints THE PROBE-WIRING CHECKER CAN NO LONGER BE SHOWN TO FAIL and blocks the commit that did the right thing.  *** SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-30 BY THE ADJUDICATING SEAT, AND THE CORRECTION IS MEASURED: AS FIRST FILED THIS ROW SHIPPED AN INCOMPLETE FIX. ***  **NINE mutants depend on the live table, not seven: M1, M2, M2b, M3, M5c, M5d, M5e, M5f, M12.**  I had excluded `M5f` on the ground that it *"uses a COMPUTED date rather than a live table entry, so it is addition-shaped already"*.  **That is false and the code says so in one line:** `_st_apply(chk, _exline(EX), '    "%s":   ("%s", "x"),' % (EX, _yest, ...))` computes the DATE and takes the ENTRY from `_exline(EX)` -- a LIVE PICK, exactly like the seven I did scope.  On an empty table `EX is None` and M5f falls into the byte-identical `results.append(False)` arm that **M12 has, which I DID scope.**  *I excluded one twin and scoped the other.*  **AND THE EXEMPLAR WAS WRONG IN THE SAME BREATH.**  The row held M5f up as *"the pattern the other seven should follow"*.  The genuinely addition-shaped exemplar is **`M3x`** -- the seat's insert-a-fixture-for-`arm_flags_probe.py` STALE EXEMPTION mutant, which scored `ok` on a FULLY EMPTY table.  A future implementer reading the old text would have converted seven, skipped M5f for the reason I wrote, copied the wrong exemplar, and **the selftest would still fail on an empty table** -- the exact failure this row exists to prevent, shipped inside the row that prevents it.  **SCOPE: convert the NINE table-dependent mutants from SUBTRACTION to ADDITION, using `M3x` as the pattern.**  Each owes two negative controls (it must still red on the rule it tests, and it must NOT red on a clean tree), which is why this is its own harness round and not a rider: it is fourteen controls, and a botched one silently weakens the check that guards every probe in the tree.  *Filed rather than fixed under the stopping rule: the shipped selftest is above the vacuity floor today (22/22, and the frozen-clock control proves it can fail), so this is COVERAGE DEBT with a known trigger date, not a false pass.*  *Found by the adjudicating seat when asked the load-bearing question -- WHICH of my accepted dispositions is wrong, with the count named.  It found four of six.  A round that accepts everything has either had a very good panel or has stopped arguing, and only a seat can tell you which; this one had stopped arguing.*  *** AND THE CORRECTION ABOVE WAS ITSELF WRONG, TWICE, IN THE TWO WAYS THIS PROJECT NAMES MOST OFTEN.  Both found by the adjudicating seat, one of them against its own earlier answer. ***  **(a) THE CORRECTION LEFT ITS REFUTED CONCLUSION STANDING IN THE SAME NOTE.**  A diff of this note between `43106c2` and `9ccb47b` shows the correction block INSERTED and the scope sentence rewritten -- and the region after it UNCHANGED, so the note read: scope is NINE including M5f ... then, in the closing position of authority, *'M5f is deliberately NOT in scope ... the pattern the other seven should follow'*.  Not a quotation; the original text, live.  **A future implementer reading to the END does exactly what the correction says reproduces the failure.**  That is the carrier's superseded-conclusion rule and mechanical rule 2 (grep for siblings) failing together, with the sibling 200 characters away in the same field.  Deleted, not demoted.  **(b) NINE WAS AN UNDERCOUNT.  THE SET IS TEN, AND THIS ROW'S OWN WITNESS FIELD HELD THE REFUTATION ALL ALONG.**  `M5b` mutates nothing but runs the checker with `--today 2026-09-21` wanting rc=1 and `EXPIRED EXEMPTION`; on an empty table there is nothing to expire, the checker prints `PROBEWIRING_PASS` rc=0, and M5b FAILS.  **The arithmetic proves it without running anything: the witness records `SELFTEST_FAIL 12/22`, which is TEN failures, and 22 - 9 = 13.**  A recorded count that contradicts the measurement recorded beside it -- the carried-number shape, in the row written to fix a counting defect.  **AND THE CORRECTION REPEATED THE ERROR'S SHAPE:** M5f was excluded on a FALSE ground (*addition-shaped already*); M5b was then excluded on a TRUE-BUT-IRRELEVANT one (it is not subtraction-shaped) -- when the failure class is *the table emptying breaks the selftest*, and M5b is squarely in it.  Its repair is the same insert-a-fixture pattern.  *** (c) AN ELEVENTH, OF A WORSE KIND: `M5a` GOES VACUOUS-GREEN. ***  It wants `PROBEWIRING_PASS` with `--today 2026-09-19`; on an empty table it gets PASS while testing nothing.  It does not fail, so no count reveals it -- **the check-that-cannot-fail shape, arriving inside the fix for a different defect.**  **SCOPE, RESTATED: TEN failing mutants (M1, M2, M2b, M3, M5b, M5c, M5d, M5e, M5f, M12) plus M5a's vacuity, all converted to fixtures, with `M3x` as the pattern.**  The control count is deliberately NOT restated as a literal here -- the previous figure, 'fourteen controls', was 7 rules x 2 and went stale the moment the rule count moved.  Derive it when the round is scoped, and name its unit.

rows.title: exit_census.py's BY-ENCLOSING-CONSTRUCT split attributed every call in a plain non-static function to the preceding DEVICE_ACCESS -- inflating the bucket used to rank reachability
rows.witness: harness:the pre-existing tools/pipeline/exit_census.py reports dev_sgi_re.c = 21 LIVE, which is the correct answer I spent an hour deriving by hand after a grep gave 25
rows.note: *** THIS ROW WAS FILED CLAIMING I BUILT A TOOL.  I DID NOT.  I OVERWROTE ONE THAT WAS ALREADY THERE, ALREADY CORRECT, AND ALREADY IN THE SAME DIRECTORY AS THE LEDGER I HAD BEEN EDITING ALL EVENING.  Caught by a `git diff --cached --stat` line reading `416 insertions(+), 126 deletions(-)` on a file I believed I had just created. ***  **THE `Write` TOOL SAID 'has been updated successfully', NOT 'created', AND I DID NOT READ IT.**  The standing rule is *before deleting or overwriting, look at the target*, and I did not look.  Restored from HEAD; `git status` on the path is clean, so nothing was lost.  *** WHAT THE EXISTING TOOL ALREADY DID, ALL OF WHICH I RE-DERIVED FROM SCRATCH: ***  it strips C comments with a state machine that respects string literals; it reports the denominator beside the numerator so a pattern selecting nothing is visible; it tags each site by enclosing construct (`DEVICE_ACCESS` / `DEVINIT` / `DEVICE_TICK` / `static`) so guest-reachable sites are separable from construction-time ones; and **its docstring already carries the exact lesson I thought I had found** -- *a naive grep gets steadily MORE wrong as this fork gets more honest, because every de-fatalisation leaves a comment QUOTING the exit(1) it removed.*  It even records the same false positive shape, from a different file.  **IT REPORTS `dev_sgi_re.c = 21`, WHICH IS THE ANSWER I SPENT AN HOUR REACHING BY HAND** -- after asserting 25 into two seat briefs and telling a seat its 21 was probably wrong.  One command would have settled it at the start.  *** THE REAL LESSON, and it is a generalisation of one this project already has: BEFORE WRITING A TOOL, CHECK WHETHER IT IS THERE. ***  The carrier already says a hand-maintained inventory of FILES is a wrong record waiting for someone to add a file, and mandates `ls _scratchpad/*.pdf` over trusting the list.  **The same applies to `tools/pipeline/` -- `ls` it before building anything.**  This is the third instance today of the same shape: an absent-source note that was wrong (the footbridge datasheet, twelve days), a census asserted rather than derived, and now a tool re-implemented because nobody looked.  **PER-FUNCTION ATTRIBUTION WAS THE ONE THING MY VERSION ADDED, AND IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT BEING ADDED.**  The existing tool counts per FILE and tags by construct, and its own design note says why: *UNIT is SITES, not defects* and *DEVICE_ACCESS means WHERE TO LOOK; reachability stays a per-site question*.  A per-function count invites exactly the false precision it warns against, and the addition licence requires a MEASURED DELTA or a TRANSFERRED WARRANT -- 'it would have caught my brief typo' is neither.  **My 13-in-sgi_re figure was a detail in a brief, not a decision input; the file-level 21 was the number that mattered and the tool had it.**  Closed as a RECORDS row: no code shipped, and the correct code was already in the tree.  *** AND THE TOOL DID HAVE THE BOUNDARY DEFECT AFTER ALL.  I SAID IT DID NOT, AN HOUR AGO, IN THIS ROW.  Measured 2026-08-30. ***  I closed this row concluding the existing tool *counts per FILE and tags by construct, so it never had defect 2* -- and its per-file totals ARE right, which is what I checked.  **Its CONSTRUCT split is not.**  `MARK` is `^(DEVICE_ACCESS|DEVINIT|DEVICE_TICK|static\s)`, and a **plain NON-STATIC function definition is not a boundary** -- `void draw_primitive(...)`, `void do_mte_transfer(...)` -- so every terminating call inside one was attributed to the preceding `DEVICE_ACCESS`.  **WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDY: that bucket is a REACHABILITY CLAIM used to rank defects** -- the tool literally tags it *on a guest access path BY CONSTRUCTION*.  Over-counting it over-states how many host kills a guest can reach, and at least one ledger row (`sgirekills`) took its title from the wrong figure.  **MEASURED DELTA, tree-wide over `src/devices` (118 files, 172 live calls): DEVICE_ACCESS 97 -> 83**, a 14-call / 14.4% over-count.  `static` also fell 51 -> 13, which is the same defect from the other side: a plain function FOLLOWING a static one was inheriting `static`.  **CONTROLLED against a hand-derived fixture** -- `dev_sgi_re.c`, whose true split was derived by hand and independently reproduced by two seats: `DEVICE_ACCESS` **15** (sgi_re 13 + sgi_de 1 + sgi_mte 1) and plain functions **6** (draw_primitive 1 + do_mte_transfer 5).  Before the fix the tool put all 21 in `DEVICE_ACCESS`; after it, 15/6 exactly.  **AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE FIX HAD A DEFECT OF ITS OWN, caught before shipping:** the new pattern also matched `DEVICE_ACCESS(foo)` lines, yielding two marks at one offset -- 4 duplicates in that file alone.  Harmless *today*, because at equal offset the `DEVICE_ACCESS` label sorts last and wins, **but that is a silent dependence on sort order inside a tool whose output ranks defects.**  Excluded the four MARK forms from the new pattern; duplicates now 0 across five spot-checked files.  *The honest shape of today: I diagnosed this defect correctly by hand, then wrongly concluded the shipped tool did not have it, because I checked the number people quote (per-file) rather than the number that ranks (per-construct).*

rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c's unmatched-address else arm ends the host on ANY width in EITHER direction across 2080 bytes of its own registered window -- one guest `lb` at 0xb5001800 -- and NEITHER #497 nor sgirekills-as-scoped touches it
rows.witness: probe:regress/sgi_re_unmapped_probe.py -- 28 rows, gate-run by gate_arm.sh.  Test-first evidence in regress/artifacts/sgireunmapped/killtable_20260831/: 18/28 on the pre-fix build and 28/28 on the fix, plus the ORDER PROOF for the re-pinned sibling probe (34/35 RED on the committed build under the new oracle, 35/35 after), all sentinel-verified and re-run by the coordinator rather than inherited.
rows.note: *** THE WIDEST DOOR IN THIS DEVICE, AND NO LEDGER ROW COVERED IT.  Found by the adjudicating seat while ranking the OTHER four sgi_re rows; verified here by opening the file and deriving the gap arithmetic. ***  **THE SITE** is the final `else` of the window cascade in `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_re)` -- a `fatal()` for each direction and then a bare `exit(1)`, with **NO WIDTH PREDICATE AT ALL**.  Every other kill in this handler is reached only by choosing an unusual access WIDTH (the six `len != 8` arms) or a DIRECTION (the six read arms).  This one needs neither: any width, either direction, any unmatched address.  **THE DOOR, derived rather than asserted.**  `memory_device_register` covers `baseaddr + 0x1000` for `DEV_SGI_RE_LENGTH` = `0x1000`, and the handler restores the full offset with `relative_addr += 0x1000`, so the dispatched range is `0x1000-0x1fff`.  The six windows occupy `0x1000-0x17ff` with one internal gap:      TLB_A 0x1000-0x11ff   TLB_B 0x1200-0x13ff   TLB_C 0x1400-0x15ff      TEX   0x1600-0x16df   LINEAR_A 0x1700-0x177f  LINEAR_B 0x1780-0x17ff  leaving **`0x16e0-0x16ff` (32 bytes) plus `0x1800-0x1fff` (2048 bytes) = 2080 bytes** that fall through to the kill.  Guest KSEG1: a single `lb` at `0xb5001800` ends the host process.  *** IT SURVIVES BOTH ROUNDS THAT LOOK LIKE THEY WOULD FIX IT, WHICH IS WHY IT MUST BE FILED BEFORE THE NEXT COMPLETENESS SENTENCE SHIPS. ***  `#497` repairs the six WIDTH guards and never reaches this arm.  `sgirekills` as scoped repairs the six READ arms inside the windows and never reaches it either.  A reader of either round record could reasonably conclude the device no longer kills on a stray access.  It does.  **AND ITS FIX CANNOT BE ACCEPT**, which is what keeps it out of `sgirekills`' round rather than a scheduling preference: nothing backs an unmapped address, so there is no stored value to return.  It is DECLINE + a latched `(once)` announce -- a different fix design, so the round-scope rule's same-fix-design arm fails.  *The agy audit listed this arm as '1 unhandled offset fallback' and never asked whether it was reachable.  A census that enumerates a site without ranking it is how the widest door stays open.*  *** DESIGN SETTLED 2026-08-30 BY ADJUDICATION, BEFORE EITHER ROUND STARTS, SO NEITHER BURNS ITS PANEL ARGUING SCOPE. ***  **TWO ROUNDS, and both separate from `#497` -- all THREE round-scope conjuncts fail, worked through rather than asserted.**  SAME DEVICE fails: `sgi_de` and `sgi_re` are separate `memory_device_register` registrations at `baseaddr+0x2000` and `+0x1000`.  SAME SEMANTIC CLASS fails: `sgidewidth` is the WIDTH class with a real accept set `{4,8}` a decline must PRESERVE, while `sgireunmapped` is the BADOFFSET class where nothing legal reaches the arm at all.  **SAME DETECTOR / NO NEW ORACLE fails, and this is the one that decides it:** `sgi_de`'s registers are READABLE so its rows read back through `odata` -- a real device-signature channel -- while `sgi_re`'s else arm has NO BACKING STORE and its rows can only observe the diagnostic and the guest-gets-zero channel.  *Those are different oracles in kind, and the tempting collapse -- 'both are a refused access ending the host' -- is exactly what the no-new-oracle clause exists to refuse.*  *** THE CHANNEL FINDING, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS BLOCK. ***  `#497`'s `d_returnzero` escaped 35/35 and the reason generalises to BOTH these rounds: **the `(once)` announce prints IDENTICALLY for a correct decline and for a `return 0`**, because the announce happens before the return statement.  So the DIAGNOSTIC channel does not kill it either -- and neither does host survival, since a guest bus error leaves the host alive.  **The only discriminator is what the GUEST RECEIVED.**  Every round in this family owes a SENTINEL-SEEDED READ ROW: seed the destination register, perform the declined read, and assert it reads back 0 -- a correct decline delivers zero, `return 0` faults and the register keeps its seed.  *That is the row `#497` was missing, and the measuring seat reached the same repair independently while this adjudication was being written.*  **TWO LATCH BITS, NOT ONE, and the precedent is MEASURED rather than stylistic.**  The arm prints two distinct messages -- `unimplemented write to address` and `unimplemented read from address`.  `#490` built the one-bit form as `M3shared` and **it ESCAPED**: a session declining at both sites sees the second fall silent because the first already latched.  `#279` states the rule outright -- *one flag per DISTINCT MESSAGE and never one shared flag*.  A single bit here means the first stray READ silences the first stray WRITE's message forever, and vice versa.  **THE DE-ESCALATION ACCEPT CLAUSE IS N/A, WITH ITS REASON RECORDED -- not unrun.**  The clause enumerates predicates that used to gate death and pins each accept side.  This arm **has no predicate**: it is the fall-through when none of the six window conditions match, so there is no adjacent modelled value because **nothing legal reaches it**.  The enumeration is the empty set.  *Adding a row to test the WINDOW predicates instead would be the addition licence's 'cannot hurt' wearing detector clothes -- and it is unnecessary, because `#497`'s own accept rows already prove those addresses reach their own arms rather than this one.  That is inherited coverage, not an uncovered hole.*  **WHAT IT OWES INSTEAD IS A CONTRACT SENTENCE (clause (e)):** this fix makes every unmatched address a silent zero-decline, so a future window-boundary regression that drops a legal address here no longer announces -- and that class is pinned by `#497`'s window accept rows, not by this arm.  *** AND A CONTRACT LIMIT WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ROWS ARE WRITTEN: the WRITE arm's `return 0` mutant is NOT distinguishable by a value-only cold-debugger probe. ***  A declined write and a faulting write both leave no readback.  The READ arm is killable by the seeded-read row; the write arm needs exception-state observation, which is a heavier probe shape than `#497` used.  **State it as a limit rather than shipping a completeness claim the rows cannot support.**  *** THE 32-BYTE GAP IS NOT DEAD SPACE.  IT IS `CRIME_RE_CLIP_IDS`, A SEVENTH REAL HARDWARE WINDOW. ***  `crmfbreg.h` defines `CRIME_RE_CLIP_IDS 0x16e0` between `CRIME_RE_TEX 0x1600` and `CRIME_RE_LINEAR_A 0x1700`, and `struct sgi_re_data` carries `// todo: clip_ids registers.` exactly where they would go.  The codex seat reached the same conclusion from the CRIME spec and put it best: **"six real windows" should read "six MODELED windows"** -- CLIP_IDS is real hardware with no dispatch and no state.  **The 2080-address count is UNCHANGED** (CLIP_IDS still falls to the kill) **but the characterisation splits, and the decline message must follow it:** 32 bytes are a documented, unmodelled register block; 2048 are genuinely unmapped.  A single "unimplemented address" diagnostic is accurate for the 2048 and WRONG for the 32.  *The brief asked whether `CRIME_RE_TEX + 0xe0` was a bug or the gap was real; both options were wrong, and a seat answering as posed would have had to pick the wrong one of two.  Three local facts agree the bound is deliberate: the next defined constant, the struct's own todo comment, and `re_tex[112]` x 2 bytes = 0xe0 exactly.*  *** THE fable5 SEAT'S EQUIVALENCE CLAIM IS REFUTED, AND THE REFUTATION CHANGES A DISPOSITION RATHER THAN SCORING A POINT. ***  It reported that an early `return 1` after the announce is OBSERVATIONALLY EQUIVALENT because *"`memory_rw.c`'s #95 block memsets `data` to 0 on EVERY device read before the handler runs"*, and advised disposing of that mutant as EQUIVALENT rather than chasing it.  **Checked both halves and both are false.**  The device handler is called at `memory_rw.c` `res = mem->devices[i].f(cpu, mem, paddr, data, len, ...)` and NOTHING zeroes `data` before it -- the three `memset(data, 0, len)` sites in that file are all on NON-DEVICE paths (the MIPS Sprite area, the beyond-physical_max arm, and the `memblock == NULL` unmapped-RAM arm), each followed by a `goto do_return_ok`.  And the MIPS caller's buffer is `uint8_t data[LS_SIZE];`, an **UNINITIALISED STACK ARRAY** with no memset anywhere in that file.  **SO THE MUTANT IS NOT EQUIVALENT -- BUT THE CORRECT DISPOSITION IS NOT 'DETECTABLE' EITHER, AND THAT NUANCE IS THE POINT.**  Skipping the tail leaves the guest whatever was on the stack, which is neither 0 nor any fixed value: the observable is REAL but NONDETERMINISTIC.  A row asserting a specific sentinel would be FLAKY, not sound.  *Filing it as EQUIVALENT would have retired a live mutant on a false mechanism; filing it as ordinary coverage debt would invite a flaky row.  It is neither, and the round must say so.*  **The seat's own remedy for the sibling `return 0` case is the one that works here too: seed the destination register with a sentinel and prove execution continued past the load** -- which pins the mutant without depending on stack contents.  *Everything else in that answer verified: `dev_unreadable.c` IS `return 0;` and `machine_sgi.c` installs it TEN times, so the FAULT member is real and in use on this machine.*  *** THE PASS-1 PANEL RESOLVED THE ROUND'S ONLY DISAGREEMENT BY WARRANT, NOT BY VOTE. ***  grok said ONE latch bit, deepseek said TWO.  I grepped first and found ZERO device files in the tree splitting a latch by direction -- which looked like precedent for grok.  **fable5 showed the framing was wrong: the house latch is per-MESSAGE-SITE, and this arm has TWO message texts (the write arm prints the data value, the read arm does not).  So two bits is not a new rule, it is the existing rule counted correctly** -- and my grep found nothing because I searched for the wrong property.  Two further warrants: a declined READ fabricates data the guest acts on while a declined write is a no-op, and one shared bit order-couples the two message rows so 'read message exactly once' becomes unpinnable.  *** WITNESSED AT RUNG 3, 32/32.  The row's witness field said `none`. ***  **AND ONE ROW FAILED FOR A REASON WORTH KEEPING: `lw` from 0x16ff SURVIVED** -- the log shows `exception ADEL`, because an unaligned load is refused by the CPU before `memory_rw` is reached.  Re-cut to 0x16fc it kills.  *The row was wrong, not the code, and the seat said so rather than adjusting the claim to fit.*  **THE ESCAPES, ranked by how little they cost:**  (1) *** A WINDOW-BOUND SHRINK (`+ 0x80` -> `+ 0x40`) SCORED A TOTAL ESCAPE, 9/9, AGAINST THE FIRST DETECTOR -- because the accept row wrote to the window's BASE, where a move of the FAR bound is invisible by construction. ***  That is clause (f)'s anchor rule arriving on the accept side, and the repair is one word: **an accept row must use the window's LAST slot.**  (2) a latch-bit collision reusing `SGIRE_W_TEX_LEN` scores 13/14, caught only by a row that touches another latch site first.  (3) `return 0` escapes both "host survives" and "message once" -- and the seat measured the discriminator side by side: with `v0` pre-set to **0** the row PASSES the mutant; pre-set to **0xa5a5a5a5** it FAILS, because a DBE leaves the register untouched.  The log is decisive (`reading from device 'sgi_re' ... failed` / `exception DBE`).  **So the brief's stated pin "the declined read returns 0" is MEASURED VACUOUS unless the sentinel is non-zero.**  **A REFINEMENT TO THE SIX-MEMBER OPTION SET, and it is not a quibble:** the set collapses THREE DISTINCT ANNOUNCE DISCIPLINES living in this one file -- unbounded-and-always-visible (`fatal()`, in sgi_de and sgi_mte), **unbounded but VERBOSITY-GATED (`debug()`, in sgi_de_status, invisible at default verbosity)**, and latched-once.  Folding the second into "already declines" hides exactly the flood question the round has to answer.  *** ROW COVERAGE, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: ONLY 10 OF 14 ROWS EVER FIRED, AND THREE OF THE FOUR SILENT ONES ARE AN UNDISCHARGED OBLIGATION. ***  `accept tlba`, `accept tlbb` and `accept tlbc` never fired because **no shrink mutant was built for the three TLB windows**.  By the accept-row failability rule an accept row is discharged by a MEASURED KILL, not by existing -- so these three are NOT discharged, and the round owes three more mutants (about 1.5 s per build).  **AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME MUTANT SHAPE AS THE FOUR ALREADY BUILT.**  TLB_A and TLB_B are bounded by *the next window's constant* while the other four use *base + size*, so shrinking a TLB bound perturbs TWO arms at once -- it moves a boundary two windows share, rather than opening a gap.  A mutant written on the base+size pattern would not exercise them.  The fourth silent row, `read0 VACUOUS`, is **deliberately** never red: it is the control that DEMONSTRATES the brief's stated pin is vacuous.  Same load, `v0` pre-set to 0 instead of 0xa5a5a5a5, and it PASSES on the mutant where the real row fails.  *A row that never fires because it is a negative control and a row that never fires because nobody built its mutant must not be counted alike, which is why they are separated here.*  **DISPOSITION: this is L3, an undischarged obligation, not coverage debt** -- the three rows are the sole carriers of the de-escalation accept side for their windows, and the round's claim to have shipped accept rows is false about them until the mutants exist.  It is owed BEFORE the fix ships, not filed after.  *** RETRACTED.  MY REFUTATION OF fable5's EQUIVALENCE CLAIM WAS WRONG, AND I READ THE PRISTINE 2021 UPSTREAM COPY OF `memory_rw.c` TO PRODUCE IT.  fable5 WAS RIGHT. ***  I wrote that *"nothing zeroes `data` before the handler call -- the three `memset(data, 0, len)` sites are all on NON-DEVICE paths"*, and shipped it in `a115a4a`.  **The fork's `src/cpus/memory_rw.c` has SIX such sites, and one of them is exactly what fable5 described**, inside the device-found branch, before `paddr -= baseaddr` and before the dispatch:  `/*  #95: zero the caller's buffer up front on a read so a device handler that fills only part of it ... can never hand back uninitialised host memory to the guest.  */  if (writeflag == MEM_READ) memset(data, 0, len);`  *** HOW IT HAPPENED, AND IT IS THE HAZARD THIS PROJECT DOCUMENTS IN CAPITALS FOR SEATS -- IT CAUGHT THE MAIN LOOP INSTEAD. ***  There are two `memory_rw.c` under the project root: the fork at **794 lines** (`GXEMUL-SEC`, `est`, `build`, `build-asan`, md5 3d47dd66) and a PRISTINE 2021 UPSTREAM copy at **530 lines** (`./src/cpus/`, md5 75fbe149, plus two archive copies).  My grep ran as `src/cpus/memory_rw.c` while the cwd had drifted to the PROJECT ROOT, so it resolved to the upstream file.  **Every line number I reported -- 161, 222, 425, 437, 486 -- is below 530, and the fork's are 215/267/492/671/683/732.  The numbers themselves were the tell and I did not read them as one.**  **THE CONSEQUENTIAL ERROR, not the embarrassing one:** I dispositioned the early-`return 1` mutant as *"REAL but NONDETERMINISTIC -- a row asserting a sentinel would be FLAKY"*.  With #95 in place the guest gets a DETERMINISTIC ZERO, so on the value channel that mutant is **EQUIVALENT**, and a sentinel row is not flaky -- it is simply BLIND to it.  The opus5 seat measured this with two builds differing only in #95's fill byte: filling 0x00 gives `lbu = 0x0`, filling 0xa5 gives `lbu = 0xa5`, tracking byte-for-byte.  *So the disposition inverts: not coverage debt on a flaky channel, but an EQUIVALENT mutant that the mutant-that-will-not-die rule says to dispose of as a RESULT.  In `sgi_de` it is not equivalent overall, because that tail also DRAWS and `dec_switch` separates them -- but in `sgi_re`, whose tail is bare, opus5 expects true equivalence.*  **AND I TOLD THE OWNER I HAD REFUTED A SEAT.**  The correction is recorded here, in the carrier, and reported back -- because a wrong refutation that stands is worse than the original error: it teaches the next round to distrust the seat that was right.  *** L4 -- THE REASON THIS ROW GIVES FOR ITS OWN GAP IS WRONG FOR ONE OF ITS THREE MEMBERS, found 2026-08-31 by #499's PRE-TABLE block (sibling parity) before any mutant was built. ***  The note explains all three missing kills with *the TLB windows are bounded by the NEXT window's constant, not base+size*.  Re-derived from the file: that is TRUE of TLB_A (`< CRIME_RE_TLB_B`) and TLB_B (`< CRIME_RE_TLB_C`) and **FALSE of TLB_C, which is `< CRIME_RE_TLB_C + 0x200` -- structurally IDENTICAL to TEX, LIN_A and LIN_B, all three of which got a shrink mutant and all three of which FIRED.**  So `accept tlbc` was never blocked by window shape; it was simply not built.  **The asymmetry is TWO arms, not three, and a third of the filed obligation is the same edit that already worked three times.**  Recorded because a wrong reason gets reused: a future round reading this note would have gone looking for a special mutant shape for a window that needs the ordinary one.  Durable anchor: `grep -nE 'relative_addr < CRIME_RE' src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c` prints all six far bounds in one screen, which is what made the asymmetry visible at all.  *** #499's MUTANT TABLE (regress/artifacts/sgireunmapped/killtable_20260831/): THE THREE ACCEPT ROWS ARE DISCHARGED, AND THE SEAT OVERTURNED MY FRAMING TWICE. ***  **MY PREMISE WAS FALSE AND I GAVE IT TO THE SEAT AS SETTLED.**  I briefed that the `exit(1)` "was replaced by a latched refusal", reading the row's `commits: a643e18` as the fix.  **At HEAD the catch-all is STILL `exit(1)`** -- `grep -n 'unimplemented read from address' src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c`, with the kill two lines below.  `a643e18` shipped the WITNESS and the analysis; **#499 is the round that ships the fix**, not one auditing a shipped one.  *A premise-audit opener would have caught this and my brief did not carry one -- I wrote the settled-premises block and then stated a premise in it that was wrong.*  The seat also corrected my expected-results line: I asked for a baseline that is all-green, and **base is 10/14 BY DESIGN** -- that is test-first, and the all-green control is the FIX.  **THE TABLE.  base 10/14, fix 14/14, and each shrink reddens EXACTLY its own row:** `M1 tlba_shrink` 13/14 (`accept tlba`), `M2 tlbb_shrink` 13/14 (`accept tlbb`), `M3 tlbc_shrink` 13/14 (`accept tlbc`).  **No shrink perturbs a neighbour**, which also refutes this row's own "a shrink to a next-constant bound moves a boundary two windows share" -- editing the `<` EXPRESSION opens a gap and does not touch the sibling arm; only editing `CRIME_RE_TLB_B` in `crmfbreg.h` would.  **So all three accept rows now carry measured kills and the L3 is dischargeable.**  **M4 bitcollide ESCAPED at 14/14, exactly as the PRE-TABLE block predicted** -- and the prediction was measured rather than trusted.  The seat then BUILT the killing row: **one emulator, two NARROW (`len != 8`) accesses, one in TLB_A and one in TLB_B**, oracle `count("CRIME_RE_TLB_B -- declined") == 1`.  The session shape is the whole point -- the accept rows do ONE 8-byte store in a fresh emu, so they never enter a width guard and never set a latch bit, making the collision unobservable to them BY CONSTRUCTION.  Generalised for one session's cost: six narrow accesses, one per window, asserting all six decline texts appear, which pins every pairwise collision among the six bits.  *** AND A DEFECT NEITHER OF US HAD ENUMERATED: `#498` SILENTLY BROKE THIS ROW'S WITNESS GENERATOR. ***  `opus_witness_20260830/mkvariant.py` inserts `SGIRE_W_UNMAP_WR = 1 << 6`; `#498`/`cb28a6f` added `SGIRE_W_DE_LEN = 1 << 6` to the same enum.  **A duplicate enumerator is legal C and silent**, and `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_de)` casts the same `struct sgi_re_data *`, so `d->warned` is shared across both devices.  Measured as `fix6`: **14/14, total escape**, with a transcript showing one guest `sb` to sgi_de permanently silencing sgi_re's catch-all diagnostic.  The replacement `mkvariant499.py` uses `1<<7`/`1<<8` and hard-fails on duplicates.  *A cross-round interaction: one round's enum addition invalidated another round's generator, with no gate able to see it.*  *** M5 -- THE ACCEPT SUITE TESTS THE FAR BOUND AND NEVER THE NEAR BOUND, AND THIS FALSIFIES A CARRIER RULE MINTED FROM THIS VERY ROW EARLIER THE SAME DAY.  Ranked a FLOOR BREACH (clause (d), L2) by the measuring seat. ***  The carrier said: *an accept row written at a window's BASE tests the near bound twice and the far bound never -- put it at the LAST legal slot, **where both bounds are load-bearing***.  The first half is right and is why these rows were moved to the top slot. **The second half is measured FALSE.**  `M5`: `>= CRIME_RE_LINEAR_A` -> `>= CRIME_RE_LINEAR_A + 0x40`, **one token**, scores a **14/14 CLEAN SWEEP** -- while a control row storing at the window BASE reds on M5 and is serviced normally on the fix.  **Moving the rows from base to top SWAPPED the blindness rather than removing it.**  **The reason is structural, not a detail of this device:** an accept row's oracle is *this access was serviced*, which is a single bit, and ONE bound can explain that bit on its own.  So there is no slot from which both bounds are observable, and a single accept row pins exactly the bound it is near.  **THE REPAIR COSTS NO EXTRA SESSIONS AND IS STRICTLY BETTER THAN TWO ROWS:** the store's own `debug()` already prints the destination -- `[ d->re_linear_b[30] = 0x... ]`.  Assert **the array NAME and the INDEX** rather than merely that the catch-all was missed.  That converts each relative row into an ANCHORED row in clause (f)'s sense, pins BOTH bounds from one access, and additionally catches TRANSLATIONS -- which no base-or-top accept row can see at all.  Two rows (base AND top) is the fallback where no such channel exists, and it is weaker: it pins two bounds and still cannot see a re-map that keeps both.  **Because M5 weakens a predicate the fix DEPENDS ON and dominates the edited catch-all, it is clause (d) and therefore L2 -- repaired IN-ROUND, not filed as coverage debt.**  The carrier has been corrected in place; the detector repair ships with the fix.  *This is the freshly-minted-exemplar rule firing on itself: a rule minted from ONE instance carried that instance's shape as if it were the class, and the first round to APPLY it measured the general claim false within hours.  The instruction survived; the universal clause did not.*  *** LATCH-BIT DECONFLICTION BETWEEN TWO ROUNDS IN FLIGHT, caught 2026-08-31 BEFORE either shipped rather than measured afterwards. ***  `dev_sgi_re.c`'s `SGIRE_W_*` enum uses bits **0-6** today (`TLBA/TLBB/TLBC/TEX/LINA/LINB` 0-5, `DE_LEN` 6).  **`#499` takes `1 << 7` (`SGIRE_W_UNMAP_WR`) and `1 << 8` (`SGIRE_W_UNMAP_RD`)**, per its measured `mkvariant499.py` fix.  **`#500` was designed for `SGIRE_W_PRIMOP = 1 << 7` and MUST TAKE `1 << 9` instead.**  *A duplicate enumerator is legal C and silent, and both devices cast the same `struct sgi_re_data *`, so a collision makes one arm's decline permanently suppressible by unrelated traffic to the other -- measured as a 14/14 total escape when it happened between `#498` and `#499`'s generator.*  *** THE PORT SHIPPED AND IT CAUGHT THREE MUTANTS THE ARTIFACT DETECTOR LET THROUGH -- which is the L2 repair working, measured on the artifact that will actually run rather than inherited from the one that will not.  `regress/sgi_re_unmapped_probe.py`, 28 rows, self-contained, artifacts under killtable_20260831/port/. ***  **Re-measured on the SHIPPED probe:** `m4_bitcollide` **14/14 ESCAPED -> 27/28 KILLED**; `m5_lina_near` **14/14 -> 25/28** (three rows); the duplicate-1<<6 variant **14/14 -> 27/28**.  Base 10/14 -> **18/28**, fix 14/14 -> **28/28**.  Five further mutants built and killed: `mret0` 26/28, `m6_idxshift` 26/28, `m7_wintrans` 24/28, `mnolatch` 26/28, `mbothsame` 27/28, `mrdcollide` 27/28.  *** THE TRANSLATION CLAIM WAS MEASURED AND CAME BACK NARROWER THAN I STATED IT, which is why it was asked for as a measurement. ***  I recorded that the anchored-oracle repair *should also catch translations*.  Measured: **anchoring ALONE does not catch a translation; anchoring PLUS a base-slot row does.**  Under `m7_wintrans` the TOP-slot row `tlba acc hi` stayed **GREEN** -- a row inside the moved window cannot see that the window moved -- while `tlba acc lo` reddened by falling out, and `tlbb acc lo` reddened on the MIS-ATTRIBUTION channel (the transcript says `d->re_tlb_a[0]` where the row wants `d->re_tlb_b[0]`), which no unanchored oracle can see at all.  An index re-map (`m6_idxshift`) IS caught outright, both rows.  **So the true claim is: anchored + BOTH bounds catches index re-maps outright and catches window translations at the base row.**  *** AND THE SEAT CHECKED WHAT ALREADY EXISTED BEFORE BUILDING WHAT I ASKED FOR. ***  I proposed generalising the latch-collision row to all six windows.  `sgi_re_width_probe.py`'s `xsite 6msg` **already ships that exact generalisation, is gate-wired, and measured 32/35 against m4** -- so a duplicate would have been a row that can never fail alone.  It re-aimed the idea at THIS round's own two bits instead (`xwin wr`/`xwin rd` walk all six #497 latches plus #498's sgi_de bit, since the four handlers share one malloc'd struct), with `xwin7 pre` as the partner control.  **ONE ROW DELIBERATELY DROPPED and one row's base value deliberately CHANGED, both disclosed rather than buried:** `read0 VACUOUS` was a pedagogical control that cannot fail under the mutant it names, so it is gone and its lesson survives as the reason `rd sent` presets a sentinel; and `latch fresh` (green on base, because base ALSO prints its text before dying) became `xwin wr`, which counts the `-- declined.` literal and is RED on base.  *A port that silently changes a score is the failure mode here, so both are named.*  **COVERAGE DEBT, stated rather than glossed: 8 of 28 rows never failed on any of 14 variants.**  Two are the witness ladder's clause-(ii) controls (`live`, `devsig`) and fire only if the harness or machine breaks.  The other six are per-window accept replicas of shapes discharged elsewhere, filed WITH the mutants that would discharge them (near-grow at TLB_C, far-shrink at TEX/LIN_B, near-grow at LIN_B).  **The seat stopped rather than chase per-row, which is the `#392` shape** -- the right call.  *One caveat it raised against its own work: `xwin7 pre` is a control that a product defect can redden (m4, m5, m7).  That is a valid kill, but the round must not cite it as the PRIMARY m4 detector -- `xsite 6msg` names that properly.*  *** INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF THE RE-PIN, 2026-08-31: DO NOT SHIP IT AS WRITTEN.  It repairs `otherkilldeath` and walks STRAIGHT INTO `exit0oracle`. ***  The proposed oracle is `exit0 + text`.  **Mutant: keep the fix's latch and message and add `exit(0);` after the if/else at the catch-all.**  The message prints (text True), the process exits 0 (`how == "exit0"`), `got == want` -> **GREEN, total escape** -- and `other kill` is the ONLY row in that 35-row probe that touches `OUTSIDE` (verified: two hits in the file, the definition and one use), so nothing else catches it.  *** AND THE KNOWLEDGE WAS ALREADY IN THE GATE, ADDRESSED TO THIS EXACT CLASS, WRITTEN THE SAME DAY. ***  `regress/gate_arm.sh` carries the flagship seat's note against re-pinning `tail_acc_x` onto `exit0` -- *exit status cannot vary between 'declined and then quit' and 'died with status 0'* -- together with the repair.  **The `#499` re-pin was written without it.**  That is this project's unread-review shape: the answer sat in a file the round had itself just edited.  **REPAIR, using material already in the probe:** assert a DEVICE SIGNATURE through the existing `DE_STATUS`/`DE_STAT_VAL` constants (the `devsig stat` idiom), giving survival AND identity in one channel; or the `lw surv` sentinel-preset idiom, which distinguishes *the tail ran and wrote odata 0* from *the load never completed*.  **Minimum:** `session()` already returns `alive` and the proposal throws it away.  **So the round owes a FOURTH mutant of its own -- `exit(0)` at the sgi_re catch-all -- and the order measurement must be RE-RUN with whichever oracle actually ships.**  Worth knowing: the NEW 28-row probe would survive that mutant; the escape is confined to the re-pinned shipped row, so this is a floor question about the RE-PIN, not about the new detector.  *** THE ORDER CLAIM OVERCLAIMS BY ONE WORD, AND A STRONGER WARRANT WAS ALREADY IN HAND. ***  `REPIN_REQUIRED.md` is headed *"ORDER DISCIPLINE -- measured, not asserted"*.  **The RED is measured; the ORDER is not** -- every artifact carries the same copy-time mtime, so nothing shows the oracle was written before the fix was built.  **But the oracle was PRE-REGISTERED in a committed artifact by a prior round**: `git log -S "death is the shared answer"` gives `112867a` (#497, 2026-08-30 22:41), the commit that filed `otherkilldeath` and prescribed this repair -- **six hours before** this round's baseline `3ded1e8` (2026-08-31 04:34).  *That is checkable by `git show` rather than by trusting a timestamp, and it is what should carry the not-laundering claim.*  L4: correct the heading.  *** THE PORTED DETECTOR IS INDEPENDENTLY VALIDATED BY THE COORDINATOR, NOT ONLY BY THE SEAT THAT WROTE IT.  2026-08-31, log preserved at `regress/artifacts/sgireunmapped/killtable_20260831/port/coordinator_validate.out`. ***  Run against the COMMITTED tree at `fe5e2c1` with `build/gxemul`, from the gate's own working directory: **`PROBE_RC=0`, `OPUS499T_CONTROL=OK`, `OPUS499T_RESULT=18/28`, `OPUS499T_DONE` present.**  18 ok + 10 FAIL = 28, so the tally is internally consistent and no row was lost.  **AND THE TEN RED ROWS ARE EXACTLY THE ONES THE FIX ADDRESSES**, which is the test-first evidence rather than a bare number:  `wr surv`, `rd surv` (the host dies today), `wr kill`, `rd kill` (the kill text is present today), `wr decl`, `rd decl` (the decline text is absent today), `rd sent` (the sentinel survives an unanswered read), `wr rd 2msg` (no per-direction messages exist yet), and `xwin wr`/`xwin rd` (the new latch bits do not exist yet).  **Every accept row and both witness-ladder controls stay GREEN**, so the detector is not simply red about everything.  *Three things this checks that a seat's summary cannot: that the probe RUNS from the gate's cwd rather than only the seat's, that it emits its completion sentinel so a score is a measurement rather than a truncation, and that the reddening rows are the RIGHT ones.  The figure matches the seat's report exactly, which is what makes it a confirmation rather than a second opinion.*  *** CLOSED 2026-08-31 at `9f666a8`. ***  The catch-all is a per-direction latched decline falling through to the common tail; live `exit(1)` in `dev_sgi_re.c` 14 -> 13.  Two bits (`1 << 7`, `1 << 8`) placed AFTER `SGIRE_W_DE_LEN` in numeric order, because an earlier draft left the enum ending at `1 << 6` and a maintainer scanning to the last enumerator would have taken an already-used bit.  **The re-pin that shipped is NOT the one proposed**: `exit0+txt` was measured to ESCAPE an `exit(0)` mutant, and the measuring seat's own first-choice replacement escaped two more, so the sentinel-preset read of the unmapped address itself is what shipped. What it does not support is the stronger *three distinct values* framing used to dismiss the one-channel-wearing-three-hats objection.  *Caught by a packet-fed seat reading the parenthetical `(died / 0xdeadbeef / died)` against the claim it was offered to support -- i.e. by checking a claim against its OWN cited evidence, which is the cheapest audit there is and which neither I nor the seat that wrote it performed.*  **AND IT IS DIRECT EVIDENCE ON THE QUESTION OF WHETHER A LATE PASS 2 IS WORTH RUNNING**: this round shipped without one, the gate refused the next commit for it, and the pass run afterwards found a wrong record in the round's own justification within minutes.  *** codex's SEMANTIC CORRECTION, recorded because the records use the wrong word: THIS IS NOT A DECLINE AT THE CALLBACK BOUNDARY. ***  The handler returns **1** for an unmatched access exactly as for a serviced one, so `memory_rw` sees a handled access either way.  What the fix changes is that the host survives and a latched message is printed -- the access is still ACCEPTED at the boundary and answered with a defined 0 on the read side.  **The six-member option set distinguishes DECLINE from ACCEPT by precisely this boundary**, so calling it a decline blurs the distinction the set exists to draw.  *The behaviour is right and the word is wrong; a future round reading `sgireunmapped` as a DECLINE precedent would be citing something that returns success.*  *** L2 FLOOR BREACH, MEASURED BY THE PASS-2 SEAT: TWO MUTANTS SWEEP ALL 28 ROWS CLEAN, AND ONE RESTORES THIS ROUND'S OWN CITED WITNESS VERBATIM.  Repair is owed IN-ROUND however late. ***  **`W` -- re-add the pre-`#499` `len != 8` kill at the top of the catch-all, lifted verbatim from `9f666a8^`.  28/28, zero red -- and `sb` AND `lb` at `0xb5001800` die, printing the pre-fix kill text.**  That is floor clause (b): a verbatim reinstatement of the removed defect passes the detector.  **`T` -- `relative_addr < CRIME_RE_TEX + 0xe0` -> `+ 0x100`, ONE HEX DIGIT.  28/28, zero red -- and `ld` at `0xb50016e0` dies with `TODO: read from CRIME_RE_TEX`**, handing 32 bytes back to `exit(1)`.  Clause (d): a bound relaxed on a predicate dominating the edited lines.  *** THE TWO REASONS ARE STRUCTURAL, NOT LUCKY, AND I VERIFIED BOTH. ***  **(1) EVERY catch-all row uses len 8 and nothing else.**  `store()` defaults to `OP_SD_T0_A3` and `load()` to `OP_LD_V0_AT`; `OP_SB_T0_A3` exists but is aimed at the six mapped windows.  **So the detector pins the DIRECTION axis -- which the contract argues at length -- and never the WIDTH axis at the catch-all, while the round's HEADLINE is *no width predicate at all* and its WITNESS is a `lb`.**  **(2) All four catch-all offsets (`0x800/0x8c0/0x900/0x9c0`) land in the SECOND component.**  The round's own CHANGELOG names two: `0x16e0-0x16ff` (32 bytes) and `0x1800-0x1fff` (2048).  **The 32-byte component has ZERO rows.**  *This is `#498`'s `len == 2` hole one round later, in the same file: a detector that exercises one axis exhaustively and the other not at all.*  **AND THE PRETABLE MANDATE WAS ONLY PARTLY DISCHARGED, which is why the CHANNEL check did not catch it.**  The block's own header names baseline `e898c84`, the ARTIFACT detector, and the subject *discharge accept tlba/tlbb/tlbc*. rows.title: WITHDRAWN -- a FALSE out-of-bounds: de_reg/mte_reg are sized to the FULL window while the START strip HALVES the index range, so regnr+1 has 512 slots of headroom
rows.witness: none, and the absence of one is the point -- this row was filed 'source-derived' and the index-range measurement that would have refuted it was never run.
rows.note: *** THE THIRD MEMBER OF A FAMILY THIS FILE KEEPS PRODUCING: a fixed-arity store that writes `[i]` AND `[i+1]` while the index reaches the array's last slot. ***  Surfaced by the adjudicating seat while designing `sgidewidth`, and explicitly kept OUT of that round -- `sgidewidth`'s decline does not touch the `len==8` arm, so folding it in would be scope creep rather than adjacency.  `de_reg` is declared `uint32_t de_reg[DEV_SGI_DE_LENGTH / sizeof(uint32_t)]`, and the `len==8` arm writes both `de_reg[regnr]` and `de_reg[regnr+1]`.  At the top of the window `regnr+1` indexes one past the end.  **SAME SHIELD AND SAME TRAP AS `sgilinearoob`:** guest paths cannot reach it because an 8-byte access must be 8-aligned while the top offset is only 4-aligned -- but the debugger's `put d` prints a warning and PROCEEDS.  **That does not give this row a witness; it takes one away.**  A `put d` reproduction bypasses the guest instruction path entirely and would be laundering rather than witnessing.  **The pattern is now worth naming as a class rather than a coincidence:** `sgilinearoob` (`re_linear_[ab][tlbi+1]` into a `[32]`), the TLB arms' unmasked loop increment, and now `de_reg[regnr+1]`.  Three sites, one shape -- *a store whose arity is fixed by the ACCESS WIDTH while its index is bounded only by the OFFSET MASK*.  A future round should consider whether the bound belongs at the index computation rather than at each store.  *** WITHDRAWN 2026-08-30, HOURS AFTER IT WAS FILED.  IT IS A FALSE FINDING AND THE ARITHMETIC THAT REFUTES IT IS ONE LINE THE ANALYSIS SKIPPED. ***  Found by the mandated second review pass on the same session's records corrections; re-verified here by opening the file rather than taking the refutation on trust.  **THE MISSING LINE.**  `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_de)` reads  `int startFlag = relative_addr & CRIME_DE_START;` then **`relative_addr &= ~CRIME_DE_START;`** and only THEN `regnr = relative_addr / sizeof(uint32_t);`.  `CRIME_DE_START` is `0x0800`.  So `relative_addr` starts in `[0, 0xfff]`, is capped at `0x7ff` by the strip, and **`regnr` <= 511 while `de_reg` is `[DEV_SGI_DE_LENGTH / sizeof(uint32_t)]` = `[1024]`.  `regnr+1` <= 512: IN BOUNDS, with 512 slots of headroom.**  The `mte_reg` twin is identical -- same strip, same `[1024]`.  **HOW I GOT IT WRONG:** I reasoned *top of window / 4 = 1023, +1 = 1024 = one past the end* and simply did not see the strip on the line above the index.  *** AND THE PROCESS TELL IS SHARPER THAN THE ARITHMETIC. ***  `sgilinearoob`'s overclaim was caught because a seat ran `offsetof` instead of trusting source-derived arithmetic.  **This row's witness field says `source-derived`, and the equivalent measurement -- what is the actual RANGE of this index? -- was never applied to it.**  The same defect class, in the same file, on the same evening, caught the first time and not the second.  **THE REAL CLASS IS NARROWER AND BETTER STATED, which is what this withdrawal buys.**  I wrote *three sites, one shape: a store whose ARITY is fixed by the access width while its INDEX is bounded only by the offset mask*.  The true discriminator is **whether the array is sized to the INDEX RANGE or to the FULL WINDOW**:    * `re_linear_a[32]` is sized EXACTLY to `tlbi`'s `& 0x1f` range -> `tlbi+1` overflows.  **REAL** (`sgilinearoob`).    * `re_tlb_x[256]` with `tlbi` capped at 255 and a loop adding +3 -> overflows.  **REAL** (recorded on `sgirekills`).    * `de_reg[1024]` / `mte_reg[1024]` with the index range HALVED to 511 by the strip -> **the over-sizing is what prevents it.  FALSE.**  *** WITHDRAWING COSTS LESS THAN LEAVING IT: a false OOB row sends a future round chasing a hole the array sizing already closes, and it would have done so carrying my name and a confident derivation. ***  Withdrawn the way `sh4aaalias` was -- state `dropped`, the reasoning kept in place rather than deleted, so the next person who spots the same arithmetic finds the refutation instead of re-filing it.

rows.title: dev_footbridge.c answers FIQEnable reads with a silent constant 0 while its IRQ twin kills the host -- the whole FIQ column is softer than the IRQ column
rows.witness: harness:READ from the shipped source and the datasheet, 2026-08-30, both sides side by side.  `case FIQ_ENABLE_SET:` is `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE) d->fiq_enable |= idata; break;` -- a READ falls through with `odata` untouched, so the tail returns 0.  Its twin `case IRQ_ENABLE_SET:` does `odata = d->irq_enable;` and then `fatal(); exit(1);`.  Same architectural register (188h/288h, IRQEnable/FIQEnable), opposite failures.
rows.note: *** THE SIBLING-PARITY CHECK FIRING AT DESIGN TIME, WHICH IS WHERE IT IS SUPPOSED TO FIRE.  Found while adjudicating n6's ordering, 2026-08-30. ***  `n6` is about to ACCEPT the `+0x188` IRQEnable read on the warrant that the DC21285 prose makes it a documented read-only register.  **That same prose covers `188h` and `288h` JOINTLY** -- and `FIQ_ENABLE_SET` at `+0x288` has **no read arm at all**, so the model answers it with a silent constant 0.  A guest that sets FIQ bits and reads them back gets zero: **wrong value, no kill, no announce.**  **IT IS NOT IN THE EIGHT-KILL CENSUS AND THAT IS THE POINT** -- it is the same semantic class with the same one-line fix shape and the same row shape, differing only in that the IRQ column kills where the FIQ column lies quietly.  *Shipping the IRQ accept while leaving its FIQ twin silently wrong and unnamed is exactly the asymmetry the sibling-parity line exists to catch.*  **AND IT IS A COLUMN, NOT A SITE:** `FIQ_ENABLE_CLEAR`'s read side at `+0x28c` is also a silent constant 0 while its IRQ twin kills.  Worth ONE sentence in the decline round's `PRETABLE.out` rather than five separate discoveries later.  Under the reopening rule this becomes a candidate JOINER for a footbridge round once a row witnesses it, and a filed row otherwise.  *** THE DATASHEET SPLITS WHAT THIS ROW TREATS AS ONE CLASS.  Derived 2026-08-30 from `_scratchpad/dc21285.txt`, cross-confirmed in THREE independent places so no extraction stagger is possible: the register summary (`IRQEnable/IRQEnableSet 188h`, `IRQEnableClear 18Ch`), the offset table (`188h  IRQEnable  IRQEnableSet` / `18Ch  --  IRQEnableClear`), and the section heading `7.3.32 IRQEnableSet/FIQEnableSet Register--Offset 188h/288h`. ***  Constants confirmed in `src/include/thirdparty/dc21285reg.h`.  **(a) READ of 0x188 -> ACCEPT.**  *"IRQEnable/FIQEnable Register--Offset 188h/288h.  This read-only register is used to mask the interrupt input sources... The value of this register can only be changed by writing to the EnableSet and EnableClear registers.  Reset value: 0."*  The emulator ALREADY does `odata = d->irq_enable;` -- the documented value -- and then calls `exit(1)` on it.  Delete the kill, KEEP THE VALUE, **no latch**: there is no event to announce, because the read is implemented and is not ignored.  A bounded announce here would ship a wrong record in product code.  **(b) READ of 0x18c -> DECLINE.**  The offset table gives `--` for its read function: there is NO defined read.  The emulator returns `d->irq_enable`, which is a GUESS, then exits.  **Different disposition from its immediate neighbour, and the code treats them identically.**  **(c) WRITE to FIQ_STATUS (0x280) -> DECLINE.**  *"The Status and RawStatus are read-only."*  *** WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TRIVIA: a single splice across all three would ACCEPT an undefined read at 0x18c and DECLINE a documented one at 0x188 -- getting both neighbours wrong, in OPPOSITE directions. ***  This is the option-set rule paying out again, with the ACCEPT member in play -- and that member is visible only from the datasheet, never from the source.  **AND IT SHARPENS THIS ROW SPECIFICALLY:** the IRQ/FIQ asymmetry recorded here is not merely an inconsistency to be normalised in either direction -- **the datasheet adjudicates which side is right.**  0x188/0x288 is IRQEnable/FIQEnable, a documented read-only register with reset value 0, so answering a FIQEnable read with a constant is closer to correct than killing the host on the IRQ side.  The fix direction is therefore ACCEPT on both, not decline on both.  *** THE TWO-LINE FIX, DATASHEET-BACKED, AND IT REPAIRS A HOST KILL AND A WRONG VALUE AT ONCE. ***  The datasheet says 188h/288h read back IRQEnable/FIQEnable -- the live enable mask, reset value 0.  So:  **IRQ side:** delete the kill and KEEP the value the model already computed (`odata = d->irq_enable`).  **FIQ side:** serve the read too -- `odata = d->fiq_enable` -- instead of falling through with `odata` at 0.  **The FIQ side is not merely 'silent', it is WRONG whenever `fiq_enable != 0`:** a guest that enables FIQ sources and reads the register back is told nothing is enabled.  That is the more insidious half, because unlike its twin it never announces anything.  *Both are member 4, ACCEPT -- no latch, because there is no event to announce: after the fix the reads ARE implemented and are NOT ignored.  A bounded announce would ship a wrong record in product code, which is exactly how the ACCEPT member was discovered.*  **RANKS AS AN EASY RESOLVABLE: two lines, three independent datasheet confirmations, no new latch bit, no struct change, and the accept rows read back through `odata` rather than through debug lines.**  Its only design question is whether 0x18c (IRQEnableClear, which the offset table gives NO read function) joins the same round -- it does not: different disposition, DECLINE not ACCEPT, per the split recorded above.

rows.title: 13 witnesses are ungated BY DESIGN, so a witness whose arms rot is indistinguishable from one that works -- and n6 is about to rot one
rows.witness: none -- a proposal about test apparatus.  Its motivating instance is measured: fbpending_witness.py scores a row on a death at the site n6 removes, and NO GATE RUNS IT, so nothing will report the breakage.
rows.note: *** THE THIRD TIER OF `n6`'s BLAST RADIUS, GENERALISED -- THE QUIETEST FAILURE THIS HARNESS CAN HAVE. ***  `check_probe_wiring.py` reports **13 witnesses correctly ungated**, and *correctly* is the right word: gating a witness would MANUFACTURE a regression, because a witness is built to INVERT after its fix (`#496`'s reads 15/15 pre-fix and 11/15 post-fix, and its record says so).  **But ungated means unrun, and unrun means a witness whose arms rot is indistinguishable from one that works.**  `n6` supplies the concrete instance: `fbpending_witness.py` scores a row on a death at the very site `n6`'s ACCEPT round removes, and no gate runs it -- so when that round ships, the witness breaks on disk and nothing anywhere says so.  **THE REMEDY IS NOT AN INVENTION -- THE IDIOM IS ALREADY IN THIS TREE.**  `fbpending_drain_probe.py` carries `EXPECT_CAP` defaulting to `-1 = report only`, with its scoring gated on `EXPECT_CAP >= 0`.  Run-but-do-not-score exists, is understood, and supplies the TRANSFERRED WARRANT the addition licence requires -- that plus a measured instance, never *it cannot hurt*.  *** AND IT IS HARDER THAN IT LOOKS, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN BUILT. ***  A witness is SUPPOSED to change score after its fix lands, so report-only output is **noisy by construction**: a flipped row is the expected inversion, or a real break, and the raw output cannot tell them apart.  Making it useful means each witness recording its **EXPECTED post-fix score**, so the report can say *expected 11/15, got 11/15* rather than *something changed*.  That changes what every witness in the tree must carry -- an owner decision rather than a round's, the same boundary that kept the per-row `kills:` comment filed rather than adopted.  **Ranked LOW deliberately:** apparatus about apparatus, competing with four open HIGH rows that are live host kills.  Filed so the `n6` round can NAME it rather than discover it, and so the next person who finds a rotted witness lands here instead of re-deriving it.

rows.title: the owner's agy-reserved-for-measurement ruling lives in the carrier as PROSE and panel.sh knows nothing about it -- so agy was fired in the very next panel
rows.witness: harness:panel_20260830_214609/ -- agy.txt exists in a routine panel fired AFTER the ruling; `grep -ci 'reserved' panel.sh` returns 0, and the launch at panel.sh's AGY block is unconditional.
rows.note: *** THIS IS THE CARRIER'S OWN STRUCTURE-FIRST FAILURE, MEASURED AGAINST ITSELF WITHIN TWO HOURS OF THE RULING BEING RECORDED. ***  The owner ruled 2026-08-30 that **agy is RESERVED FOR MEASUREMENT and held out of routine panels**, on the warrant that it is the only compile-and-measure seat NOT behind the Agent-tool transport -- the roster's insurance against the outage that once cost a round all its measuring capacity at once.  **The ruling was written into the carrier.  `panel.sh` was not touched.**  `grep -ci 'reserved for measurement' panel.sh` returns **0**, its AGY block is unconditional, and `panel_20260830_214609/` -- a routine panel fired after the ruling -- contains an `agy.txt`.  *The carrier's own diagnosis applies verbatim: knowing a rule and having it fire on the right object are different problems, and only the second is solved by writing more.  A rule that earns its second instance while sitting in that file has thereby proven it was mis-filed as prose.  This one earned its FIRST instance in under two hours.*  **THE FIX FOLLOWS THE `OLLAMA4` PRECEDENT EXACTLY, AND THE PRECEDENT'S WARNING IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART:** a variable, plus a conditional BANNER, LAUNCH, SEAT CHECK and VERDICT ROSTER.  The carrier records why all four: *blanking the variable alone would have left `panel_ollama.py` running with an empty model name, writing an error file, and producing a PHANTOM SEAT that answers the seat check.*  The agy shape is different but the hazard is identical -- a blank binary path would fail loudly rather than phantom, but the SEAT CHECK would then report a seat FAILURE where the truth is a deliberate omission.  *** AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE RULING'S COST CLAUSE: a seat DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED is a different thing from a seat FAILURE and a different thing again from AGREEMENT.  Conflating them is what the seat ledger exists to refuse. ***  So the seat check must print DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED by name, every panel, rather than silently omitting agy or reporting it down.  **DEFERRED, NOT FORGOTTEN, AND THE REASON IS A RULE THIS PROJECT HAS ALREADY PAID FOR:** a panel was RUNNING when this was found, and **bash reads a script incrementally by byte offset**, so editing `panel.sh` mid-run corrupts that run -- the failure signature being a syntax error in a file that parses clean afterwards.  The edit waits for the panel to finish.  *The urge to edit arrives exactly when you are watching the script run, which is why the rule exists.*

rows.title: gate_arm.sh has become the tree's device-probe gate by accretion, and #497 is the FIRST probe in it on a foreign machine AND CPU family
rows.witness: harness:gate_arm.sh runs footbridge, PIT and now an SGI/MIPS probe.  The first two at least share this gate's own -E cats machine; the third does not.
rows.note: *** FILED BECAUSE A COMMENT ALREADY CLAIMED IT WAS.  The #497 gate comment ended 'the right answer is a gate_devices.sh split ... Filed, not done' -- and it was NOT filed: no ledger row, no queue entry, under any phrasing.  Caught by the pass-2 seat while the comment was STAGED. ***  *That is the gap-closes-itself shape: a claim that a process step is complete, shipping in the same commit as the thing it excuses.  A future reader greps for the row, finds nothing, and cannot tell whether the split was considered and rejected or simply forgotten.*  **AND THE PRECEDENT CLAIM WAS ONE STEP SHORT, which the same seat measured.**  I wrote that `gate_arm.sh` already runs footbridge and PIT probes, 'neither an ARM instruction test'.  True -- **but both run `-E cats`, this gate's OWN ARM machine, and the PIT wiring comment says it was placed there BECAUSE 'this is the only gate whose machine it shares'.**  So `#497`'s probe is not the third instance of an existing accretion; it is **the FIRST probe in this gate on a foreign machine AND CPU family**.  My words were true and my implication was generous to my own decision.  **THE FORCING CRITERION, so this row cannot sit forever:** *the NEXT device probe wired into `gate_arm.sh` converts this from FILED to OWED.*  The accretion story guarantees each addition makes the next cheaper, which is exactly how a least-bad accommodation becomes permanent.  **THE OPERATIONAL COST, named rather than left to be discovered:** a red row in `gate_arm` can now mean an SGI/MIPS device regression.  That is an attribution trap for whoever reads the battery output at 3am.  *** OWED AS OF 2026-08-31, BY ITS OWN FORCING CRITERION, AND RAISED low -> med. ***  The #497 gate block filed this row with the criterion written into the gate itself: *"the NEXT device probe wired into this gate converts it from filed to OWED."*  #498's `sgi_de_width_probe.py` is that probe, wired in the same commit that records this.  **A pre-specified trigger that fires and is ignored is worse than one never written, because the next reader trusts it.**  `gate_arm.sh` now runs THREE device detectors that have nothing to do with ARM -- the pit8253 block, #497's sgi_re and #498's sgi_de -- purely because it is the only gate with probe infrastructure and a machine they share.  *The split was not done in this round on purpose: it is a harness round owing its own negative controls, and holding a HIGH device fix hostage to a gate refactor would be the tail wagging the dog.  What was not acceptable was compounding it silently.*

rows.title: sgi_re_width_probe.py's `other kill` row is a DEATH-ONLY oracle -- a one-character change to the text it claims to pin scores 35/35, MEASURED
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED by the #497 pass-2 seat in its own clone, with the prediction filed BEFORE building.  base 35/35 CONTROL=OK; x_othertext (catch-all message text altered, exit(1) untouched) 35/35 with ZERO red rows; x_readtext (one read arm's text altered) 34/35, reddening `tlb_a ld kill got=exit1-txt want=exit1+txt`.  The matched pair is the point: it proves the six siblings ARE failable and this one is not.
rows.note: *** THE ROUND APPLIED THE DEATH-AND-TEXT DISCIPLINE TO SIX ROWS AND MISSED THE SEVENTH. ***  `sgi_re_width_probe.py`'s catch-all row captures the transcript and **throws it away** -- `row("other kill", how, "exit1", ...)` uses only the how-it-died value -- while its six `ld kill` siblings twelve lines above compute an `ok_txt` membership test and report `exit1+txt`.  **So the row's own note claims IDENTITY -- *the catch-all is untouched* -- on an oracle that observes only DEATH.**  Any edit that keeps the arm fatal while changing what it is passes.  *** IT IS THE `d_returnzero` LESSON MIRRORED ONTO THE DEATH SIDE. ***  That one was a survival-only oracle at a site where SURVIVAL is the shared answer; this is a death-only oracle at a site where DEATH is the shared answer.  Same shape, opposite polarity, and the round fixed the first while shipping the second.  **AND FINDING IT DISCHARGED AN OBLIGATION THE TWO SHIPPED TABLES NEVER DID.**  Across all 41 preserved probe outputs, **SEVEN rows were red under NO mutant in either table** -- the six `ld kill` and `other kill`.  `PRETABLE.out` names their channel as *a round that silently removed the READ kills*, **but no such mutant was ever built**, so for those seven the CHANNEL line was satisfied ON PAPER.  The pass-2 pair now measures six of the seven failable.  **One remains measurably blind, and it is this row.**  **DISPOSITION: COVERAGE DEBT, NOT A FLOOR BREACH -- and the reasoning is the seat's, recorded so nobody re-argues it.**  Clauses (a), (b) and (c) pass, and the row DOES red against a null medium.  The catch-all is not a predicate the fix DEPENDS ON, so the bounded (d) closure does not reach it.  And clause (e)'s contract says *silent REMOVAL*, which this mutant is not -- **the contract is precise even though the row's inline note overclaims.**  **THE FIX IS ONE LINE:** make `other kill` symmetric with its six siblings by adding the text membership test.  It is deliberately NOT done in-round -- editing a shipped detector row means re-measuring, and the round's stopping rule fixes only measured FALSE PASSES and WRONG RECORDS.  *This is neither: it is a row that is weaker than its note claims, which the note has now been corrected to say.*  *** RECORDS DEBT, NAMED BY THE fable5 SEAT AND CONFIRMED BY LOOKING: THE 35/35 AND 34/35 RUNS ARE CITED IN TWO COMMIT MESSAGES, THIS ROW, THE BUG FILE AND A PROBE COMMENT -- AND THEIR LOGS ARE NOT PRESERVED ANYWHERE DURABLE. ***  `34/35` appears under `regress/artifacts/widthkillclass/opus_impl_20260830/` only in `PREDICTIONS.out` and `PRETABLE.out`, which are PREDICTIONS written BEFORE the run -- not the measurement.  The measuring seat built `x_othertext` and `x_readtext` in its own scratch directory and reported the scores; **the Agent seats leave no file in the panel dir**, so even the report is in volatile temp.  **This is the volatile-path rule breached from a direction it does not cover: the rule says copy the log before the record cites it, and here the record cites a log THAT WAS NEVER MINE TO COPY.**  A measuring seat's scratch evaporates with its session, and nothing in the harness asks it to hand the log back.  **DISPOSITION: the numbers are NOT retracted -- they are a seat's measured report with its method stated and a matched control, which is the ordinary evidentiary basis here -- but they are re-graded from CONFIRMED to MANUAL, because no artifact backs them.**  Re-deriving costs two mutant builds and one probe run each.  *The general fix is a brief line, not a rule: when a measuring seat reports a score, ask it to write the log to `regress/artifacts/<row>/` -- it has the file access, and the ask costs one sentence in the invocation.*  *** IT IS A CLASS WITH TWO MEMBERS, NOT ONE ROW -- censused 2026-08-31, and BOTH were shipped by the same session two days apart, which makes it a habit rather than two accidents. ***  `grep -rn 'row(".*", *how, *"exit1")' regress/*.py` returns exactly two rows whose ENTIRE oracle is *the host died*:  **`sgi_re_width_probe.py` `other kill`** (this row) and **`sgi_de_width_probe.py` `tail_acc_x`**.  Every other death assertion in the tree carries a text companion.  **The shared defect: at a site where death is the SHARED answer, a death-only oracle cannot see the message change** -- an edit that reworks the diagnostic while leaving `exit(1)` standing passes, measured 35/35 for `other kill` against a matched control at 34/35.  **The two are NOT equally exposed and the difference is worth stating rather than folding in.**  `tail_acc_x` has a sibling (`tail_acc`) that counts the message text, so the PAIR pins identity even though the row does not; `other kill` explicitly discards the transcript its six `ld kill` siblings test for membership, so nothing pins it.  *So this row is the live one and `tail_acc_x` is the latent one* -- and `tail_acc_x` additionally carries a documented expiry, since the round that fixes `sgideprimop` reds it by succeeding.  **One fix shape covers both: the `ok_txt` companion the siblings already carry.**  Doing them together is the class fix and costs one round instead of two.  *Filed, not fixed in-round: this is coverage debt against SHIPPED detectors sitting above the vacuity floor, which the stopping rule files rather than chases.*  *METHOD NOTE, because the check nearly lied to me: the census `grep -rhc ... | paste -sd+ | bc` printed **0** while the listing showed two -- `grep -c` emits nothing for non-matching files, so the sum was taken over an empty set.  The count cited here is from the LISTING, not from that arithmetic.  A denominator that disagrees with a listing you can see is the cheapest signal there is.*

rows.title: gen_codex_wall.py's marker regex matches ONE seat name, so a stage held awaiting SEVEN seats is invisible to section I -- the biggest holds are the ones that escape
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED against HEAD and working ledgers.  `MARKER = re.compile(r'\(HELD-AWAITING-SEAT/defanged:\s*([a-z0-9_]+)\s*\]')` -- the class has no comma, so `(HELD-AWAITING-SEAT/defanged: opus5, codex, grok, kimi, glm, deepseek, minimax)` does not match.  Enumerated: 2 multi-seat markers present, of which `sgirekills` is a genuine live hold owing all seven scriptable seats and is counted NOWHERE.  CLOSED by 9abd175: a strict token grammar plus seat-id validation against the ledger's own roster, controlled in both directions -- real ids render clean with empty stderr, an unknown id renders `?token` and names row, phase and token, and the real ledger is unchanged at 8 held rows with no warnings.  Controls preserved at regress/artifacts/holdmarkermulti/controls_20260830/controls.out.
rows.note: *** A CHECK THAT CANNOT FIRE ON ITS LARGEST CASES. ***  `gen_codex_wall.py` exists because section I of `precommit_check.sh` requires that every `(HELD-AWAITING-SEAT/defanged: ...)` marker is ALSO NAMED IN THE QUEUE -- its own docstring: *holding a stage and queueing it are ONE action, not two*.  **Its regex accepts a single `[a-z0-9_]+` seat name.**  A marker naming two or more seats contains commas, fails the match, and is therefore neither counted as a held stage nor required to appear in the queue.  **So the enforcement is strongest on the SMALLEST holds and absent on the biggest.**  A stage awaiting one seat is policed; a stage awaiting all seven is not -- and a seven-seat hold is, by construction, the one carrying the most owed work.  *** MEASURED, not argued: `sgirekills` is held awaiting `opus5, codex, grok, kimi, glm, deepseek, minimax` and `gen_codex_wall.py` reports it in no count. ***  **THE FIX IS THE CHARACTER CLASS** -- admit `[a-z0-9_,\s]+` and split on commas.  Note the class must stay RESTRICTED: `ledgerstatelies` QUOTES the literal inside prose containing `*` and `-`, and a permissive `[^\]]+` would match that quotation and manufacture a phantom hold -- **the quoted-marker hazard the carrier already records, arriving from the other direction.**  That prose is the built-in negative control.  **OWED CONTROLS (a tooling change owes them both ways):** (1) POSITIVE -- `sgirekills` appears as held after the widening; (2) NEGATIVE -- `ledgerstatelies`' quoted prose still does NOT; (3) NEGATIVE -- a defanged marker still does not.  *Found while defanging stale markers: the count did not move for the multi-seat ones, and a count that does not move is not thereby correct -- which is the same tell the carrier records from the stuck 27.*  *** AND I QUOTED THE LITERAL IN THIS VERY ROW WHILE DOCUMENTING THE HAZARD OF QUOTING IT -- two live copies, in `witness` and `note`, defanged the same day. ***  They were harmless TODAY because `held_rows()` reads only `entries[].note`; they would fire the moment any tool widens its scan.  *The carrier's rule is: before quoting a string a tool matches on, ask what that tool will do with your copy.  I wrote the row that says so and then did not ask.*  **A SECOND, SMALLER FINDING FROM THE SAME COUNT:** `gen_codex_wall.py` prints `N held stages` and `held_rows()` returns ONE TUPLE PER ROW, phases joined -- so the number is ROWS, not stages.  Today that is 8 rows carrying 9 (row, phase) stages, because `wdccdbmidxfer` is held at both `research` and `regress`.  **STAGES AND ROWS ARE DIFFERENT UNITS**, which this project has already paid for once when four counting methods gave four answers to one question.  The label is wrong, not the tool.  *** TWO CLAIMS IN THIS ROW WERE REFUTED BY THE PANEL AND ARE CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN SILENTLY SUPERSEDED. ***  (1) It prescribed admitting `[a-z0-9_,\s]` -- MEASURED to span NEWLINES and replaced by a strict token grammar `[a-z0-9_]+(?:[ 	]*,[ 	]*[a-z0-9_]+)*`, which also kills the `split(", ")` separator mutant a seat found surviving the character class.  (2) It called the `ledgerstatelies` quotation a 'built-in negative control'.  It is VACUOUS: that row has ZERO entries and its quotation sits in a row-level field `held_rows()` never reads, so the permissive class this row forbade passes every control and renders byte-identically.  Both found pre-ship (L1).  *A row filed to document a check-that-cannot-fail shipped with a check that could not fail.*

entries.note: *** FILE-READING, not packet-fed -- the CLI is the kimi seat again since 2026-08-29, and my first entry for this seat both mislabelled its transport AND said only 'recorded as answered'.  That is the unread-review shape written into the ledger by the person who fired the panel. ***  213 KB.  **Its distinctive finding is a phantom the character class could not stop:** `(HELD-AWAITING-SEAT/defanged: codex and opus5)` -- the word `and` instead of a comma -- matches the loose class and yields ONE garbage seat token `codex and opus5`.  Verified here: the loose v2 class matches it, the strict token grammar adopted from opus5 rejects it.  *** AND IT NAMED THE DURABLE CLOSE, WHICH IS BETTER THAN EITHER REGEX: validate split tokens against `ledger["seats"]` ids and flag unknowns, rather than tuning the class. ***  Adopted in this commit -- the roster is DERIVED from the ledger, an unknown token renders `?token` and warns on stderr rather than being dropped, and it is controlled both ways.  *Tuning a character class is an arms race against prose; an id that is not a seat is wrong whatever shape it arrived in.*  It also reached the manufactured-answer mechanism independently of fable5 -- removing the literal from a `seat=fable5, phase=regress` entry drops it into the content-keyed seat tally as a regress ANSWER -- and confirmed the say/echo analysis.  *** AND QUOTING THAT EXAMPLE ARMED A DIFFERENT TOOL.  `check_stage_panels.py` keys on the RAW literal and has no seat-id validation, so it read this note's quotation as a live marker and reported `holdmarkermulti review 8/9 awaiting: codex and opus5` -- a stage held for a seat that does not exist.  The gate caught it and refused the commit. ***  **That is the third instance in one session, and this one is inside the note documenting the hazard.**  The carrier's rule is *before quoting any string a tool matches on, ask what THAT tool will do with your copy* -- and the answer differs per tool: `gen_codex_wall.py` now validates against the seat roster and would have rendered `?codex and opus5` with a warning; `check_stage_panels.py` does not, and simply believed it.  *Recorded rather than quietly fixed, because the seat-id validation adopted in this same commit demonstrably does NOT generalise to the other two readers of this literal -- which is a real limit of the fix, found by breaking it.*
