rows.title: the hold-marker discriminator was implemented with `>=` where the carrier says LATER, and six holds were cleared by SAME-DATE siblings written by the batch that created the marker
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED by the codex and opus5 seats on the #497b pass-2 panel, independently, and confirmed here row by row before reverting.  SIX markers were wrongly cleared, ALL of them phase=regress / seat=fable5: ns16550, carrier, es438, sh4sci, wdcdataoutdrain, and wdccdbmidxfer entry [26].  *** THIS FIELD PREVIOUSLY NAMED THE SIXTH AS 'research/opus5, answered at review'.  THAT IS THE MARKER THE COMMIT **KEPT** -- disposition (b) -- NOT the one it cleared.  Caught by the fable5 seat; I had copied the framing from another seat's table without checking which entry it pointed at. ***  widthkillclass was the one CORRECT clearance: held at review, all seven named seats answered at review.  A strictly-later + same-stage test keeps all six and clears that one.
rows.hold_question: The DATE bug is settled and reverted -- strictly-later keeps all six, measured.  The open question is narrower: should the rule ALSO require a SAME-PHASE answer?  It affects none of these six, so it is not urgent; but `regress` is fable-only by standing directive, which makes a regress-phase hold a specific obligation that another phase's answer from the same seat arguably cannot discharge.  Does that reasoning extend to assess/research/review, where any seat can answer?
rows.note: *** THE FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND IS KEPT HERE BECAUSE THE CORRECTION IS THE USEFUL PART. ***  I recorded this as the carrier's rule being too loose (phase-agnostic).  **Measured: the rule is right as stated and my implementation was wrong.**  The carrier says the seat must have *a LATER entry on the same row*; my code compared `>=`.  **All six cleared markers have NO strictly-later answer of any kind** -- they were discharged by same-date siblings written by the very batch that created the marker to record the stage as NOT done.  A strictly-later test keeps all six.  **MEASURED COST BEFORE THE REVERT: 9 held rows -> 3, with `es438` and `ns16550` leaving `fable_queue.md` entirely** -- and their regress stage carries no non-marker seats, so it was invisible to section H as well.  The owed work was recorded nowhere mechanical.  **IN FAIRNESS, AND IT MATTERS FOR RANKING: NO GATE CHANGED COLOUR.**  `check_fable_queue.py` passes against both ledgers.  The loss was to the human-readable derived record, which is what this machinery exists to produce -- so it is real, and it is not a broken gate.  *Found by codex as a cross-phase pattern, by opus5 as the date bug underneath it, and confirmed here row by row.  Two seats, two different framings, one cause.*

rows.title: gxprobe cached the pc across `step`, so a driver that stepped without _exec_at() had its next pc assignment silently skipped -- a detector row that could not fail
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED by the #497-family measuring seat and re-verified here.  `gxprobe.py` skips a redundant register assignment when `cache_regs` is on; `_exec_at()` pops the cached pc after stepping, but a driver calling `send("step")` DIRECTLY did not -- so its next `set_reg("pc", a)` was dropped as redundant.  The transcript is unambiguous: the first access carries a `pc=` line, the second and third do not, and they execute `nop`.
rows.note: *** THE CHECK-THAT-CANNOT-FAIL CLASS, IN A PROBE RATHER THAN IN PROSE, AND IT WAS INVISIBLE TO EVERY SCORE. ***  A clause-(d) latch mutant swept **14/14** against the very row written to catch it.  The seat checked all three explanations the mutant-that-will-not-die rule requires rather than picking one: MIS-BUILT? no -- the diff removes exactly the two `d->warned |=` lines and all nine variant binaries have distinct md5s.  TARGET DEAD? no -- measured directly, three unmapped writes give `fix` 1 message and the mutant **3**.  ROW MIS-CUT? **yes**, and the cause was in the instrument.  **IT BIT ONLY ROWS REUSING ONE INSTRUCTION WORD.**  A driver alternating two different words gets a cache MISS on pc and works by accident -- which is why eight of nine variants scored plausibly and nothing looked wrong.  *** BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED AND SMALL, AND MY FIRST MEASUREMENT OF IT WAS WRONG. ***  I grepped for probes calling `send("step")` and found FOURTEEN -- then checked whether they use gxprobe at all, and **none of them does**; every one rolls its own pty plumbing.  The genuinely exposed population is the seat's own new witness and detector.  *A grep for the symptom found the wrong population; the discriminator was whether the file imports the harness.*  **FIXED AT SOURCE RATHER THAN DOCUMENTED.**  The seat proposed a rule -- *any driver stepping without `_exec_at()` must pop the pc cache itself*.  Removing the footgun is better: the invalidation now lives in `send()`, so any command that ADVANCES the guest (`step`, `continue`, `c`, `s`) invalidates pc wherever it is sent from.  Controlled: those four fire it; `print pc`, `reg`, `put w` and the empty string do not.  *** AND A SEPARATE FINDING FELL OUT: `gxprobe.py` IS NOT IN VERSION CONTROL. ***  `git ls-files` matches zero; it lives only in `_scratchpad/`.  The carrier tells every round to use it rather than hand-rolling pty plumbing, so the tree's recommended instrument is untracked, unreviewed by any gate, and one accident away from being lost -- and this defect would have been invisible to `git log` forever.

rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c draw_primitive(): a guest-written drawing op ends the host -- 254 of 256 top-byte values reach `default: fatal(); exit(1);`
rows.witness: probe:regress/sgi_de_primop_probe.py -- 35 rows, gate-run by gate_arm.sh (gate 14 ARM: PASS 546 checks, 0 FAIL; primop 35 emitted / 35 green / 0 red).  Test-first evidence in regress/artifacts/sgideprimop/killtable_20260901_table3_SHIPPED/: PREFIX 10/35 against the NAMED commit 840f3d0^ (never HEAD, which moved under an earlier control and gave a clean sweep that read like a vacuous detector), BASE 35/35.  22 mutants, 22 predictions written into the driver BEFORE each run so the order is provable by mtime, ZERO surprises.
rows.note: *** A GUEST-CONTROLLED VALUE ENDS THE HOST PROCESS.  Same shape as `gdromcondlies` -- the #443 BADVAL class, a known register rejecting a VALUE by killing -- and that one was rated HIGH. ***  **THE ARITHMETIC, ENUMERATED RATHER THAN ARGUED:** the switch discriminates on the TOP BYTE only, so the domain is 256 values; two are implemented; **254 of 256 kill.**  **THE PATH IS TWO ORDINARY STORES.**  (1) write the op into `CRIME_DE_PRIMITIVE` -- the store lands in `de_reg[]` through the handler's generic width arms, and the `case CRIME_DE_PRIMITIVE:` in the switch below only *debug()*s it, so nothing filters the value; (2) write any DE register with bit 0x800 set, which makes the handler's tail `if (startFlag) draw_primitive(cpu, d);`.  Neither store is unusual.  *** WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY COVERED: `sgirekills` scopes itself to "15 [terminating calls] inside a DEVICE_ACCESS", and this one is in `draw_primitive` -- a PLAIN FUNCTION.  It sits in the census's other bucket and no row names it. ***  **IT ALSO SETTLES A DETECTOR DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO SEATS ON `sgidewidth`.**  fable5 held that a survival oracle cannot see a spurious `draw_primitive` because the host stays alive; kimi held that against a PRISTINE register file the spurious draw dies in `default:` and so IS catchable by survival.  **Both are right, conditioned on register state**: with `de_reg[PRIMITIVE]` at its reset value the top byte is 0x00, which is neither implemented case, so the draw kills -- and a startFlagged survival row catches it.  With a LINE or RECTANGLE op already programmed, the draw succeeds silently and survival sees nothing.  *A detector must therefore pin the register state it relies on, or the row's channel varies with what the guest did before it.*  **AND IT RAISES THE STAKES ON `sgidewidth`'s FIX SHAPE:** the whole reason that round must NOT copy #497's splice is that the tail draws.  Now we know the thing it would draw with is itself lethal on 254 of 256 ops -- so a naive splice does not merely cause a spurious primitive, it hands a declined access a 99%% chance of killing the host.  *Found by reading the kimi seat's 133 KB answer.  Its verdict line was the literal words "verdict line first." -- a FORMAT MISS that `seat_verdicts.py` would file as "answered, no verdict line", and which I nearly recorded as a non-answer.  The carrier's rule that an unread review is neither a seat failure nor agreement, paying out on the third instance this session.*  *** AND IT IS NOT 254 GARBAGE VALUES: TWO OF THE FOUR DOCUMENTED PRIMITIVE TYPES ARE LETHAL.  `crmfbreg.h` defines FOUR: ***  `DE_PRIM_POINT 0x00000000`, `DE_PRIM_LINE 0x01000000`, `DE_PRIM_TRIANGLE 0x02000000`, `DE_PRIM_RECTANGLE 0x03000000`.  The switch implements LINE and RECTANGLE.  **So a CORRECT driver drawing a POINT or a TRIANGLE -- using documented hardware features, with a well-formed value -- ends the host process.**  That is a different and worse claim than "a guest can pass a bad value": it needs no malformed input at all.  **AND POINT IS 0x00000000, WHICH IS ALSO THE RESET VALUE** (`memset(d, 0, sizeof(struct sgi_re_data))` at device construction).  So the register's power-on state names a documented primitive the model kills on -- which is exactly why kimi's pristine-register-file conditioning holds: at reset the top byte is 0x00 = POINT, not an implemented case, so a spurious `draw_primitive` dies and a startFlagged survival row catches it.  *The reset-value coincidence is doing double duty here: it makes the detector row possible AND it means the very first legitimate draw a driver attempts, before programming any op, lands on the killing arm.*  *** WITNESSED 2026-08-31, AND CHEAPER THAN THIS ROW CLAIMED.  The row said "no rung-3 witness yet: the reachability is READ, not booted" -- it was measured within the hour, for free, by the neighbouring round's seat. ***  **The row also over-stated the cost: I wrote "two ordinary stores".  At RESET it takes ONE.**  `dev_sgi_re_init` memsets the shared struct, so `op == 0 == DE_PRIM_POINT` already -- no need to program the op register at all.  A single store with bit 0x800 set ends the host.  *** AND THE SCOPE IS FAR WIDER THAN 'A GUEST DRAWS A POINT'.  MEASURED: **EVERY access to offsets 0x800-0xfff, AT ANY WIDTH, INCLUDING ACCEPTED WIDTHS, ALREADY ENDS THE HOST TODAY.** ***  That is half the DE window -- 3072 of the 6144 reachable declined pairs, plus every accepted-width access up there too.  A reader of `sgidewidth` alone would conclude the window is safe once the width guard is fixed; half of it is not, and the second kill is not that row's to fix.  **It also confirms the fable5/kimi detector dispute exactly as this row adjudicated it:** a startFlagged survival row at reset state DOES catch a spurious draw.  The seat's `tail_acc` row is that row, working.  *** RIDER FOR THIS ROW'S OWN BRIEF, PUT HERE BECAUSE THE ROUND THAT FIXES THIS WILL READ THIS NOTE AND NOT SOMEONE ELSE'S PROBE HEADER. ***  Closing this row REDS **two** rows in `regress/sgi_de_width_probe.py`: `tail_acc_x` (wants `exit1` -- the death this row removes) and `tail_acc` (counts the `UNIMPLEMENTED drawing op` message TEXT, which a de-fatalisation will latch or reword).  **Both are in the blast radius, not just the obvious one.**  Oracle-correction ordering applies: re-pin the rows FIRST, measure the committed build RED under the new expectations, THEN edit -- otherwise the re-pin is observationally identical to fitting the test to the binary.  *The expiry was recorded only in that probe's header until a pass-2 seat pointed out that the round meeting the red gate would have no idea why: the note existed where the decision was MADE rather than where it will be USED.*  *** SHARPENED 2026-08-31, AND THE FILED DESCRIPTION UNDERSTATES IT IN THE WAY THAT MATTERS.  This row is carried as "254 of 256 op values kill the host", which is true and reads as a claim about UNDEFINED encodings.  The fork's OWN header defines FOUR drawing primitives and TWO OF THEM ARE IN THE KILLING SET. ***  `src/include/thirdparty/crmfbreg.h` (grep `DE_PRIM_POINT`) gives `DE_PRIM_POINT 0x00000000`, `DE_PRIM_LINE 0x01000000`, `DE_PRIM_TRIANGLE 0x02000000`, `DE_PRIM_RECTANGLE 0x03000000`.  `draw_primitive()` switches on `op & 0xff000000` and implements exactly `case DE_PRIM_LINE` and `case DE_PRIM_RECTANGLE`; **POINT and TRIANGLE fall to the `default:` arm, which ends in `exit(1)`.**  So this is not a defect a guest reaches only by writing a nonsense opcode -- **a correct driver drawing a point or a triangle ends the emulator**, and POINT is the all-zeroes encoding, which is also what an uninitialised or partially-written op register produces.  Durable anchors: `grep -n 'switch (op & 0xff000000)' src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c` and `grep -n 'UNIMPLEMENTED drawing op' src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c`.  *Stated as a finding rather than folded into the count because the two framings license different urgencies: "undefined encodings kill" is a robustness gap, "two of the four documented primitives kill" is a live functional defect for any guest that draws.*  *** PASS-1 PACKET-FED PANEL, 2026-08-31 (`_scratchpad/panel_20260831_033247`): THE SHARPENING ABOVE IS A **PARTITION** OF THE 254/256 CLAIM, NOT A CORRECTION OF IT, AND RECORDING ONLY THE SHARPER HALF WOULD BE THE EXACT FAILURE THE BRIEF WARNED AGAINST. *** The glm seat put it plainly: *"If the row's history now records only '2 of 4', that is exactly the locally-true restatement the brief warns repairs a sentence and hides the defect. Record both."*  **Both are true and both are recorded: of the 256 masked top-byte values, 2 are DOCUMENTED primitives (POINT, TRIANGLE) and 252 are undefined encodings; all 254 reach `exit(1)`.**  *That is the agy-shaped failure -- a locally-true qualifier that hides the size of the set -- caught by a seat, against me, one paragraph after I quoted the rule at the panel.*  **AND A THIRD MEMBER NOBODY HAD NAMED, from glm's one checkable caveat: THE MASK IS FOUR TIMES WIDER THAN THE FIELD.**  It asked whether bits [31:26] are live.  Checked in `src/include/thirdparty/crmfbreg.h` by listing every `DE_PRIM_` constant: the primitive type occupies **bits [25:24]** only (POINT/LINE/TRIANGLE/RECTANGLE = 0x00/0x01/0x02/0x03 << 24), the other flags live at bits 18/17/16 and [15:0] (`LINE_SKIP_END`, `RL`, `TB`, `LINE_WIDTH_MASK`), and **NO constant defines any bit above 25**.  The code switches on `op & 0xff000000` -- eight bits.  **So a LEGAL `LINE` or `RECTANGLE` carrying any stray bit in [31:26] fails both `case` labels and ends the host**, and that is a fourth reachable shape distinct from the documented-primitive and undefined-encoding sets.  Whether a guest ever sets those bits is NOT established and must not be assumed either way; what is established is that the decode is wider than the field it decodes.  **deepseek supplied the clause-(d) mutant and the row that kills it, before the fix exists:** drop the `!` from the proposed guard (`if ((d->warned & SGIRE_W_PRIMOP))`) -- the latch never sets, the announce never fires, and any detector testing only for the bit's presence and `exit(1)`'s absence passes.  **The killing row is a session that triggers TWO distinct unimplemented primitives and expects EXACTLY ONE message.**  **All three seats REFUSED to ratify the no-common-tail premise**, correctly -- it is not settleable from a packet, and it is the premise that broke four readers on a sibling round.  Also unsettled and owed to the file-reading seats: whether `op`'s backing field resets to zero (which is what would make POINT the uninitialised-register encoding -- *all-zeroes is a fact about the CONSTANT, not the REGISTER*, as glm noted), the guest store path to `op`, and whether `tail_acc`/`tail_acc_x` are the complete blast radius.  *deepseek's precision note, kept because the row's own wording invites the error: 254/256 counts MASKED TOP-BYTE CLASSES, not full 32-bit register values.*  *** TWO OF THE THREE UNSETTLED PREMISES ARE NOW DISCHARGED BY READING, AND THE BLAST RADIUS IS SMALLER THAN I RECORDED YESTERDAY -- an L4 against my own note. ***  **(1) NO COMMON TAIL, confirmed.**  In `draw_primitive()` the `exit(1)` is followed by a one-tab `}` closing the switch, a column-0 `}` closing the function, a blank line, and then `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_de)`.  Nothing between.  So in THIS function a `break` in the `default:` arm is equivalent to falling off the end, and the early-`return`-skips-the-tail hazard that broke four readers on the sibling round **does not exist here**.  *All three packet-fed seats correctly refused to take this from the packet, and minimax answered conditionally on both branches -- which is why the refusal cost nothing.*  **(2) THE BLAST RADIUS IS ONE CERTAIN ROW AND ONE CONDITIONAL ROW, NOT TWO CERTAIN ONES.**  Four rows in `regress/sgi_de_width_probe.py` touch this channel and their expectations differ:  `hi_draw` and `hi_rd_draw` both assert `count(DRAW) == 0` and a declined width still draws nothing, so **both stay GREEN**;  `tail_acc_x` asserts `how == "exit1"` and **reds with certainty** the moment the host survives;  `tail_acc` asserts `count(DRAW) == 1` where `DRAW` is the substring `sgi_de: UNIMPLEMENTED drawing op` -- so **if the fix KEEPS that substring and merely latches it, the first occurrence still prints and `tail_acc` stays GREEN.**  It reds only if the fix rewords the message.  *My #498 note said "Both are in the blast radius, not just the obvious one", which overstates it: one is unconditional and one is a consequence of a WORDING choice the fixing round has not made yet.*  **The practical consequence is a design constraint worth having before the fix is written: keeping the existing message text and adding `(once)` costs ONE oracle re-pin instead of two.**  **(3) STILL OWED to a file-reading seat: whether `op`'s backing field resets to zero** -- the claim that POINT is the uninitialised-register encoding rests on it, and all-zeroes is a fact about the CONSTANT, not the REGISTER.  *** THE THIRD PREMISE IS NOW SETTLED TOO, AND IT MAKES THE DEFECT WORSE RATHER THAN SMALLER -- WHICH IS WHY THE SEAT WAS RIGHT TO REFUSE IT. ***  glm declined to grant that POINT is the uninitialised-register encoding, on the correct ground that *all-zeroes is a fact about the CONSTANT, not the REGISTER*, and named the settling fact: the backing field's initializer.  Traced: `op` is `d->de_reg[(CRIME_DE_PRIMITIVE - 0x2000) / sizeof(uint32_t)]`, and `dev_sgi_re_init()` does `memset(d, 0, sizeof(struct sgi_re_data))` immediately after its `CHECK_ALLOCATION` (anchors: `grep -n 'uint32_t op = d->de_reg' src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c` and `grep -n 'memset(d, 0, sizeof(struct sgi_re_data))' src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c`).  **So `de_reg[]` really is zero before the guest touches it, `op` reads 0, `op & 0xff000000` is 0, that IS `DE_PRIM_POINT`, and it falls to the `default:` arm.**  *** THE REACHABILITY STATEMENT IS THEREFORE MUCH STRONGER THAN "A GUEST THAT DRAWS A POINT": ANY GUEST THAT STARTS A DRAWING COMMAND BEFORE WRITING `CRIME_DE_PRIMITIVE` ENDS THE HOST -- INCLUDING ON ITS VERY FIRST DRAW. ***  No unusual width, no unusual direction, no undefined encoding, and no need for the guest to want a point at all: the killing value is the RESET value.  **This is the premise-audit discipline paying its clearest dividend on record.**  I asserted the uninitialised-register claim in the brief; a packet-fed seat refused it and named the one fact that would settle it; settling it turned a plausible aside into the strongest reachability claim this row has.  *Had the seat ratified me, the claim would have shipped as an unchecked aside carrying far less weight than it deserves.*  *** THE TWO FILE-READING SEATS APPEAR TO DISAGREE ON Q4 AND DO NOT; THEY ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS, AND BOTH ANSWERS ARE NEEDED. ***  codex: `hi_draw`/`hi_rd_draw` **remain green** after a reword, because their declined-width paths bypass `draw_primitive()` anyway.  grok: a reword **BLINDS** them, because they assert `count(DRAW) == 0` and after a reword that string exists nowhere.  **Both are true: they do not RED, and they become UNFAILABLE.**  codex is answering *which rows change colour*; grok is answering *which rows still mean anything*.  Recorded together because taking either alone loses half the constraint -- and the vacuity half is the one no gate can report.  *** MY OWN PARTIALLY-WRITTEN-REGISTER CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN, refuted by codex against `#498`'s own width guard. ***  The reachability statement stands on the RESET value alone, which is proven and is sufficient: any accepted-width START access at reset draws with the zeroed POINT selector, with no store to `CRIME_DE_PRIMITIVE` needed at all.  *** F1 CREDIT CORRECTED: `#498`'s PROBE HEADER ALREADY KNEW THIS. ***  The adjudicating seat found the reset-value fact stated in `regress/sgi_de_width_probe.py`'s own DOES-NOT-CATCH section -- *"254 of 256 drawing ops are unimplemented and the reset value is one of them"*.  **So this round did not discover it; it PROMOTED it to the headline and VERIFIED it** (the `memset`, and the trace showing no store to `CRIME_DE_PRIMITIVE` is needed), which a packet-fed seat's refusal to grant the premise is what forced.  Recorded this way because booking a fresh discovery over a fact the tree already carried is the unread-review shape wearing a discovery's clothes -- *this project has three recorded instances of a finding sitting unread in a file it had written itself*.  *** LATCH-BIT DECONFLICTION BETWEEN TWO ROUNDS IN FLIGHT, caught 2026-08-31 BEFORE either shipped rather than measured afterwards. ***  `dev_sgi_re.c`'s `SGIRE_W_*` enum uses bits **0-6** today (`TLBA/TLBB/TLBC/TEX/LINA/LINB` 0-5, `DE_LEN` 6).  **`#499` takes `1 << 7` (`SGIRE_W_UNMAP_WR`) and `1 << 8` (`SGIRE_W_UNMAP_RD`)**, per its measured `mkvariant499.py` fix.  **`#500` was designed for `SGIRE_W_PRIMOP = 1 << 7` and MUST TAKE `1 << 9` instead.**  *A duplicate enumerator is legal C and silent, and both devices cast the same `struct sgi_re_data *`, so a collision makes one arm's decline permanently suppressible by unrelated traffic to the other -- measured as a 14/14 total escape when it happened between `#498` and `#499`'s generator.*  *** THE NINTH SEAT'S STATIC-LATCH CENSUS WAS SHORT, AND THE CORRECTION STRENGTHENS ITS ADVICE RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT. ***  It reported the four `draw_primitive()` sites as *"the tree's only such sites"*.  Re-derived with a wider pattern: **10 sites across 3 files** -- `dev_jazz.c` 2, `dev_pcc2.c` 4, `dev_sgi_re.c` 4 -- because `#119` and `#179` spell the latch `static int w = 0`, which its grep could not see.  **Its instruction is unchanged and now better supported: copy the shape, not the scope.**  The class is filed as `staticlatchscope`; this round still uses `d->warned` and is unaffected.  *** WITNESSED 2026-08-31 ON THE COMMITTED BUILD, WITH A CONTROL -- and the FIRST attempt was CONFOUNDED in a way the exit status could not show. ***  **The confound:** a START-aliased WRITE also writes the register, so the trigger value BECOMES `op`.  My first attempt appeared to test the reset value and actually tested `op = 1` (top byte 0, so POINT -- right death, wrong reason), and its TRIANGLE case programmed `0x02000000` and then **clobbered it** with the trigger write, producing output identical to the first case.  **Both died, both reported exit status 1, and a probe checking only *did the host die* would have scored it a clean success.**  The transcript is what disagreed: `drawing op = 0x00000001` where I expected `0x00000000`.  **Corrected, with the encoding in the TRIGGER write:**  `0x02000000` (TRIANGLE) -> KILL, op echoed correctly;  `0x00000000` (POINT) -> KILL, op echoed correctly;  **`0x03000000` (RECTANGLE) -> SURVIVES, zero kill messages.**  *The RECTANGLE control is the load-bearing row: without it, `unimplemented ops kill the host` is unfalsifiable, since everything else tested dies.*  *** AND ONE RESULT IS INCONCLUSIVE FOR APPARATUS REASONS, RECORDED AS SUCH RATHER THAN AS A FINDING. ***  I tested the reset-value claim with a START-aliased READ using the debugger's `x` command.  It returned exit 0 with no message -- and **`x` IS NOT A DEBUGGER COMMAND**: the table holds 27 and `x` is not among them (`dump` is the read command).  So that null is an apparatus artifact, and I nearly recorded *a START-aliased read does not draw*, which would have contradicted a seat's reading of `if (startFlag)` being unconditioned on `MEM_WRITE`.  **The reset-value and read-direction claims remain UNWITNESSED** and need a guest LOAD instruction, since `dump` may be bypassed for a `DM_DEFAULT` device exactly as `put b` was measured to be on `pcc2`.

entries.note: FILE-READING.  **CORRECTED HALF OF MY OWN HEADLINE CLAIM.**  I recorded POINT as what *an uninitialised OR PARTIALLY-WRITTEN op register* produces.  The reset half is proven (`memset(d, 0, sizeof(struct sgi_re_data))` zeroes `de_reg[]`); **the partially-written half is FALSE** -- `#498`'s width guard declines byte and halfword accesses BEFORE `de_reg[]` is updated, so accepted 32/64-bit writes always store complete words.  *One of this round's own fixes closed the door I was citing.*  **DID THE OPTION-SET PRECEDENT GREP the three-membered-set rule demands**, and the tree answers clearly: `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` declines an unimplemented command with a per-instance `(once)` diagnostic and completes normally, `dev_m8820x.c` ignores one; `dev_asc.c` raises a guest interrupt ONLY because it has an explicitly modelled illegal-command channel, which this site does not.  That is why FAULT is wrong here -- an in-tree warrant, not an argument.  *** TWO MORE ONE-CHARACTER MUTANT CLASSES, ONE OF WHICH IS NEW TO THIS PROJECT. ***  (a) `1 << 7` -> `1 << 6` aliases an existing bit -- the `#498` collision class, killed by pre-arming all seven existing latch bits in one session before triggering.  (b) **`d->warned |= SGIRE_W_PRIMOP` -> `d->warned = SGIRE_W_PRIMOP`, one character, which CLEARS EVERY EARLIER LATCH** -- killed by an A -> primitive -> A session requiring A's message exactly once.  It proposes combining them: fire all seven latch sites, trigger POINT, revisit the sites, and require every message exactly once.  *** AND A VACUITY FINDING AGAINST SHIPPED MATERIAL: `exit0` IS NOT A SAFE SURVIVAL ORACLE. ***  *"A wrong `exit(0)` still kills the emulator and satisfies that oracle."*  `#498`'s `hi_alive`/`lo_alive`/`lo_alive2` rows all pin `how == "exit0"`.  Assert the `alive` value captured BEFORE the harness sends `quit`, ideally with a post-trigger command.  Filed as its own row -- it is coverage debt against a shipped detector above the floor, not an L2.  **GUEST-CONTROL TRACE, concrete:** RE base `0x15000000`, DE mapping `0x15002000`, `CRIME_DE_PRIMITIVE` offset `0x60`, START alias `0x60 | 0x800 = 0x860`, so a guest `sw` to **`0xffffffffb5002860`** with `t0 = 0` draws a POINT.  `startFlag` captures bit `0x800` and is cleared; `regnr = 0x60/4`.  **And `if (startFlag)` is NOT conditioned on `MEM_WRITE`, so a START-aliased READ also invokes drawing** -- worth a row of its own. It killed the other three members on facts: ACCEPT needs a computed-then-discarded value and nothing computes a POINT or TRIANGLE; FAULT is an ADDRESS-SPACE disposition and this is a command-register VALUE, with no space to leave unmapped; BACKED ACCEPT fabricates storage where there is no register.  *** Q2 -- A FIFTH MUTANT, AND IT IS A FLOOR OBLIGATION RATHER THAN COVERAGE DEBT. ***  **`M5 primdrop`: delete the `case DE_PRIM_RECTANGLE:` LABEL** so RECTANGLE falls into the de-fatalised `default:`. Caveat that decides the session shape: `rop_used` is function-static, so the anchor fires once per PROCESS.  *** AND A HAZARD IN THE VERY PRECEDENT THAT LICENSES THE FIX: COPY THE SHAPE, NOT THE SCOPE. ***  `static char rop_used[256]` and `static int first` are FUNCTION-STATIC -- process-global, shared by every device instance, the `n_trunc_msgs` anti-pattern.  Census: **4 lines, ALL in this file, ALL inside `draw_primitive()`** -- the tree's only such sites.  `d->warned` + `(once)` is the house form. entries.outcome_note:
*** ORDER PROOF FOR THE tail_acc_x RE-PIN -- the discriminator that separates a legitimate oracle correction from fitting the test to the binary. ***

#500 de-fatalises draw_primitive's default arm, which makes `tail_acc_x' in regress/sgi_de_width_probe.py CERTAIN red: that row pinned a host DEATH on purpose.  #499 had predicted this blast radius in three tiers and derived the design constraint -- KEEP THE MESSAGE TEXT AND ADD `(once)' -- which this fix obeys, so `tail_acc' stays green and `hi_draw'/`hi_rd_draw' are not silently blinded.

*** THE OBVIOUS RE-PIN IS A TRAP AND WAS NOT TAKEN. ***  `exit1' -> `exit0' would read GREEN under a future exit(0) reinstatement, because EXIT STATUS CANNOT VARY between `declined and then quit' and `died with status 0'.  A sibling round MEASURED that exact shape as a 48/48 clean sweep the same day.  So the re-pin is onto a POSITIVE POST-DRAW OBSERVABLE: the guest performs a further load after the drawing access and the row asserts the VALUE, so it reds on a death however the death is spelled.  The exit-status check is KEPT as a labelled second channel (`tail_acc_h'), because two channels that fail differently are worth more than one that fails twice.

MEASURED, one frozen instrument for both runs, on the COMMITTED pre-fix build:

    tail_acc     1      1       ok    (the message still prints pre-fix)
    tail_acc_x   died   0x0     FAIL  <- the order proof
    tail_acc_h   exit1  exit0   FAIL

28 ok / 2 FAIL.  Same script, opposite colour, and the red was measured BEFORE the code change was committed.  Rows 29 -> 30; gate row list and both denominators updated in the same edit.

INCIDENTAL BUT WORTH KEEPING: `tail_acc_x' read "died", not "absent" -- so the probe's liveness detection DID fire here.  That makes the still-unexplained E0 case, where three `sent' rows stayed green on a build whose catch-all called exit(0), MORE interesting rather than less: the mechanism demonstrably works in this configuration.

rows.title: dev_pcc2.c: TEN live width kills (of twelve guards -- #119 already fixed two in this same file, and its shape is the answer)
rows.witness: probe:regress/pcc2_width_witness.py -- rung 3, 4/10 on the committed build (three aligned accesses each exit1, four controls green); artifacts/pcc2widthkills/witness_20260903_PREFIX.out
rows.note: *** THE SAME CLASS #337 FIXED IN dev_wdc.c AND #497 FIXED IN dev_sgi_re.c, AT TWICE THE SITE COUNT, IN A FILE NOBODY HAS EXAMINED. ***  A guest choosing an access width is not an emulator error; here every register in the block insists on a byte and ends the host process otherwise.  **REACHABILITY IS STRONGER THAN `sgidewidth`'s, and this time I checked the domain before saying so.**  `sgidewidth`'s exotic widths turned out unreachable because the MIPS core raises ADEL/ADES first.  **No such filter helps here: the killing widths are 2, 4 and 8 -- all ORDINARY, all naturally alignable.**  A plain aligned 4-byte read of `PCCTWO_GENCTL` needs no misalignment, no truncation and no unusual instruction.  *** HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the method transfers and the finding is a symptom of it: *** all four HIGH rows tonight were in `dev_sgi_re.c`, which invited the question of whether that file is uniquely BAD or merely uniquely LOOKED AT.  Comparing live terminating-call density against ledger attention answers it:  `dev_sgi_re.c` 15 exits / 11 rows / 4 HIGH -- heavily examined.  **`dev_pcc2.c` 13 exits / 2 rows / 0 HIGH.  `dev_lca.c` 11 exits / 2 rows / 0 HIGH.**  The kill density is comparable and the attention is not.  **`dev_lca.c` IS THE OTHER ONE AND IT IS NOT EXAMINED HERE** -- filed as a companion question rather than swept in, because a second file's worth of claims made in the same breath is how a census gets over-claimed.  MACHINE: `machine_mvme88k.c` is the only consumer.  **There is no mvme88k rig in this tree**, which is why the file has escaped attention -- and is also why a witness will be harder here than for the sgi rows: gate 9 constructs machines, but a rung-3 access witness needs a guest that reaches these registers.  *That is a reason to rank the WITNESS work, not a reason to rank the DEFECT lower: reachability by construction is established, and no rig means no coverage rather than no bug.*  *** THE STATED BLOCKER -- "there is no rig" -- IS NOT A REASON A RUNG-3 WITNESS IS IMPOSSIBLE, AND THIS PROJECT'S OWN MOST RECENT WITNESS REFUTES IT.  Measured 2026-08-31. ***  `#498`'s rung-3 witness for `sgidewidth` execs `gxemul -V -x -E sgi -e ip32 -M 64 0x80001000:<DUMMY>` and **`DUMMY` falls back to `/dev/null`** when `regress/dummy_kernel.bin` is absent (anchor: `grep -n 'DUMMY = ' regress/sgi_de_width_probe.py`).  **No disk image, no kernel, no boot -- a cold-debugger probe needs a machine that CONSTRUCTS and an empty load file, and that is all.**  Verified by running all four candidates under WSL with `<addr>:/dev/null`: `-E sgi -e ip32`, `-E alpha -e alphabook1`, `-E mvme88k -e mvme187` and `-e mvme188` **all reach `machine:` and print a cpu line**.  *A rig is what a rung-4 BOOT needs.  Conflating the two is what left both of these rows ranked as witness-blocked when neither had been tried.*  **WHAT IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, and the attempt is exactly for this:** whether the debugger reaches these registers through the machine's real decode, and whether the observable differs pre- and post-fix.  Constructing is necessary, not sufficient.  *My first run of this test reported all three machines failing -- because I ran the WSL-built ELF from git-bash and got `cannot execute binary file`, while my own grep for `GXemul|machine:` matched the word `gxemul` INSIDE that error and scored it a healthy banner.  A broken apparatus plus a check that matched the error text nearly filed a confident "these machines do not construct".*  For this row the target is **`-E mvme88k -e mvme187`** specifically: `case MACHINE_MVME88K_187:` is the arm that adds `pcc2 addr=0x%x` at `PCC2_BASE`, and `mvme188`/`mvme197` do not.  *** PASS-1 PACKET-FED PANEL, 2026-08-31 (`_scratchpad/panel_20260831_054552`).  THE ROW OVERCOUNTS BY TWO, AND THE DISPOSITION WAS ALREADY SETTLED BY THIS PROJECT'S OWN `#119` IN THIS SAME FILE. ***  **THE COUNT.  Twelve `if (len != 1)` guards; TEN still `exit(1)`; TWO already carry a warn-once decline.**  Deriver rather than a literal:  `grep -c 'if (len != 1)' src/devices/dev_pcc2.c` = 12, and an `awk` window over each guard separates the arms ending in `exit(1);` from those carrying `static int w`.  The two already-fixed arms are `PCCTWO_IPL` and `PCCTWO_MASK`.  *** AND `#119`'s SHAPE IS THE ANSWER TO THE DISPOSITION QUESTION, WRITTEN IN THE FILE WITH ITS OWN ROUND NUMBER ON IT: ***  `static int w = 0;  /* #119: was exit(1) -> warn-once + continue */` followed by `if (!w) { fatal("[ pcc2: non-byte access to PCCTWO_IPL; ignored ]"); w = 1; }`.  So the member is **decline + latched announce**, the message says *ignored*, and a prior round already chose it here.  **This row's remaining work is to finish a job `#119` started and left two-twelfths done** -- which is a materially different framing from *twelve host kills nobody has looked at*.  *** BUT THE EXISTING PRECEDENT USES THE ANTI-PATTERN LATCH, AND THE NEW WORK MUST NOT COPY IT. ***  `static int w = 0` inside the arm is FUNCTION-STATIC -- process-global, shared by every device instance, so one guest's access silences the diagnostic for every other `pcc2` in the machine.  That is the `n_trunc_msgs` shape the `sgideprimop` seat censused hours earlier as the tree's one bad model.  The house form is a per-instance `d->warned` bit with `(once)` in the text.  **Copy `#119`'s DISPOSITION and TONE; do not copy its LATCH SCOPE** -- and the round should say whether it converts the two existing sites too, or leaves a file with two latch idioms in it.  **glm's premise audit was right about method and the conclusions split.**  *(a)* It refused my unshown claim that `fatal()` returns.  **Checked: it returns** -- `va_start / va_debug / va_end`, no exit -- so the in-file precedent really is announce-and-continue.  My premise was right and I should have inlined the evidence.  *(b)* It challenged `grep -c '^\s*exit(1);'` as blind to terminating calls spelled otherwise.  The count is unchanged at 13 -- **but the four extra `exit(` hits are `#119`'s own comments, which is how the fourfold precedent was found at all.**  A methodological objection that found a fact even though the number held.  *(c)* **It refuted my Q3 premise outright.**  I wrote that the read path for these arms assigns `odata`.  Measured: `odata` appears twice in the whole file and both are in a DIFFERENT access function; the twelve guarded arms handle `MEM_WRITE` and `break`.  So a declined *read* of these registers returns whatever the caller pre-set -- and `#95`'s pre-zero in `memory_rw.c` supplies 0.  **The ACCEPT option's premise -- that the model computes a value and discards it -- is false here.**  *** Q1 IS ANSWERED AND THE ROW IS A DEFECT, NOT DOCUMENTATION -- confirmed from the tree's own header, which documents the legality of exactly what these guards kill. ***  `mvme_pcctworeg.h:9-10` states the PCCchip2 CSRs *"can be accessed as bytes (8 bits), two-bytes (16 bits), or four-bytes (32 bits)"*, and the m88k load/store path is compiled for `LS_SIZE` 1/2/4/8 and passes that width to `memory_rw`.  **So the ten live `len != 1` kills fire on accesses this fork's own vendor header calls legal**, and the *byte-wide* framing describes the MODEL rather than the chip.  My premise that a wide access might be undeliverable is refuted, and the row's severity goes UP rather than down.  A rung-3 probe has a concrete target: debugger `put h`/`put w` at `0xfff42000 + off` under `-E mvme88k -e mvme187`.  *** THIS ROW NOW HAS A MEASURED RUNG-3 WITNESS, NOT AN ENUMERATED ONE.  The kimi seat stopped reading and built it; I reproduced it rather than recording its measurement as fact. ***  **A. REAL GUEST DECODE, reproduced:** four hand-assembled m88k words placed with `put w`, `pc=0x1000`, `step 4`.  The trace shows `or r2,r2,0x201c ; 0xfff4201c` then `st r1,r2,0x0 ; [0xfff4201c] = 0x00000042`, then `TODO: pcc2: non-byte reads and writes of PCCTWO_SCCERR`.  **A real store, through real address decode, on an unmodified in-tree machine description** -- which is the ladder's rung 3, not a debugger poke.  *** B. A PROBE-AUTHORSHIP TRAP THAT WOULD PRODUCE A CONFIDENTLY WRONG RESULT, and it is worth more than this row: `put b` NEVER REACHES THE DEVICE. ***  Measured: a byte `put` to a guarded register produces **0** device messages, while `put w` to the same register produces **1**. Use `put h`/`put w` or real guest instructions.  **C. I wrote the rule about GATES and then piped a WITNESS. ***

entries.note: FILE-READING, and it settled the question that decides whether this row is a defect or documentation -- **against me, and in the direction that makes the row WORSE**.  *** Q1: WIDE ACCESS IS REACHABLE.  My premise was that these are byte-wide control registers and the CPU or bus glue might be unable to deliver a 2- or 4-byte access at all.  Refuted twice over, both verified here. ***  **(a) The tree's OWN header documents the legality of what is being killed.**  `src/include/thirdparty/mvme_pcctworeg.h:9-10`: *"PCCchip2 control and status register can be accessed as bytes (8 bits), two-bytes (16 bits), or four-bytes (32 bits)."*  So **byte-wide is a property of this MODEL's `switch (relative_addr)`, not of the chip the header describes** -- the guards kill on accesses the hardware documentation in this very tree says are legal.  **(b) The CPU delivers them.**  `src/cpus/cpu_m88k_instr_loadstore.c` is compiled for `LS_SIZE` 1, 2, 4 and 8, declares `uint8_t data[LS_SIZE]` and passes that size to `cpu->memory_rw`, faulting on misalignment rather than narrowing the access. entries.ev: cpu_m88k_instr_loadstore.c (LS_SIZE 1/2/4/8; MISALIGNED_ACCESS guard; memory_rw with sizeof(data) == LS_SIZE); mvme_pcctworeg.h GENCTL 0x0002 / VECBASE 0x0003
entries.outcome_note:
*** THE ROW'S OWN HELD QUESTION Q1 -- `IS A WIDE ACCESS EVEN REACHABLE?  If it cannot be, ten guards are unreachable and this row is DOCUMENTATION' -- IS ANSWERED: YES, AND BY THE MOST ORDINARY ACCESS THERE IS.  Settled by reading, in about two minutes, per the rule that anything checkable in two minutes gets CHECKED rather than judged. ***

THE CHAIN, each link read rather than assumed:

1. `cpu_m88k_instr_loadstore.c` is generated for `LS_SIZE` of 1, 2, 4 AND 8 -- the m88k ISA has byte, halfword, word and doubleword load/store, so wide accesses exist at the CPU.
2. Alignment is enforced, and enforced as an EXCEPTION rather than a silent mask: `if (addr & (LS_SIZE - 1)) m88k_exception(cpu, M88K_EXCEPTION_MISALIGNED_ACCESS, 0);`.  So a MISALIGNED wide access never reaches memory_rw -- but an ALIGNED one is untouched by that guard.
3. The access is delivered AT FULL WIDTH IN ONE CALL, not split into bytes: the buffer is `uint8_t data[LS_SIZE]` and the call is `cpu->memory_rw(cpu, cpu->mem, addr, data, sizeof(data), MEM_READ, memory_rw_flags)`.  `sizeof(data)` IS `LS_SIZE`.  So a halfword load arrives at the device handler with `len == 2`.
4. The registers are CONSECUTIVE BYTES and the boundary is EVEN: `mvme_pcctworeg.h` gives `PCCTWO_GENCTL 0x0002` and `PCCTWO_VECBASE 0x0003` (also `PCCTWO_IPL 0x003e` / `PCCTWO_MASK 0x003f`).  **0x0002 is 2-ALIGNED.**

*** THEREFORE: a guest halfword load at offset 0x0002 spans GENCTL and VECBASE, takes no misalignment exception, reaches DEVICE_ACCESS(pcc2) with len == 2, hits `case PCCTWO_GENCTL:` and dies on `if (len != 1) { fatal(); exit(1); }`.  A SINGLE NATURALLY-ALIGNED HALFWORD LOAD ENDS THE HOST. ***

That is the same shape as `#499`'s finding -- an ordinary access, no unusual width choice needed in the sense of `unusual', because a halfword read of two adjacent byte registers is exactly what a driver does when it reads a register PAIR.  It is not an exotic probe.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROW: it is a LIVE DEFECT, not documentation, and its HIGH severity stands.  The disposition question (which of the six members) is unchanged and still open; what is settled is that the question is worth asking.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, stated so the next round does not over-read it: it establishes reachability for a LOAD spanning two byte registers.  Whether a real MVME driver actually issues one, and whether the WRITE direction is equally reachable, are separate questions -- the row's own Q1 flagged the read/write asymmetry and this note does not close that half.  A rung-3 witness already exists for this row; the natural next step is to extend it with an aligned halfword access at 0x0002 and record which direction it was taken in.

entries.outcome_note:
FOUND THE THING THAT RESCOPES THE ROW.  *** IT ASKED WHETHER THE TOP-OF-FUNCTION `memcpy' ALREADY MAKES WIDE READS SUCCEED, AND THAT QUESTION CORRECTS MY BRIEF. ***  dev_pcc2.c has, BEFORE the switch: `if (writeflag == MEM_READ) { if (relative_addr + len <= PCC2_SIZE) memcpy(data, d->pcctwo_reg + relative_addr, len); ... }'.  MAIN LOOP TRACED THE CONTROL FLOW: the memcpy fills `data' and then FALLS THROUGH to the switch, so a wide READ is SERVED CORRECTLY AND THEN THE HOST DIES OVER IT at `len != 1'.

**So the ACCEPT member is LIVE for the read direction, and my brief told the panel it was not.**  I wrote *'the ACCEPT premise appears false here'* and asked them to check rather than take it from me; they checked and I was wrong.  ACCEPT means *the model already computes the right value and then discards it* -- which is EXACTLY what the read path does.  That changes the fix design: the read direction may want the kill simply DELETED (the value is already correct and no event needs announcing), while the write direction still needs a disposition.

the reachability claim is ONE LEG SHORT -- and it was right.  *The CPU -> memory_rw leg is fully inlined, but the memory_rw -> device-accessor leg (that a wide access is not SPLIT into per-byte device calls) is ASSERTED, not evidenced, and that leg is the one that decides whether anything dies.*

**CORRECT, AND NOW EVIDENCED.**  memory_rw.c calls `mem->devices[i].f(cpu, mem, paddr, data, len, writeflag, extra)' ONCE, with `len' passed through.  There is no loop around it.  `len' is written in exactly two places: a PAGE-STRADDLING split path, and a clamp to the device's own end which prints a diagnostic.  An aligned halfword at 0x0002 neither straddles a page nor reaches the device end, so it arrives as ONE call with len == 2.  The leg holds -- but glm was right that I had asserted it, and this is the second time today a seat caught me presenting an untraced leg as settled.

entries.outcome_note: RULING -- Q1.1 DIRECTION SPLIT: **YES**, and the seat supplied a stronger warrant than my brief had.  Decisive fact, verified: wide reads spanning GENCTL/VECBASE are ALREADY ACCEPTED TODAY when the base offset lands on an unchecked arm -- a word read at 0x00 (CHIPID) returns those same bytes through the top-of-function memcpy with no kill.  The identical bytes flow or kill depending only on which case label the base hits, so the read-side kill defends nothing that is not already served one offset away.  And no arm computes a read value, and arms break to `return 1' with no common read tail, so an early decline cannot skip anything (the sketch-rule hazard does not apply).  Writes land ONLY inside arms, so a write decline is honest.  READS: delete the kill, keep the value, NO latch -- there is no event to announce.  WRITES: decline + latched announce.  *** AND THE FILE ALREADY HOLDS FOUR WIDTH DISPOSITIONS, NOT TWO: the timer block accepts wide writes by memcpy, SCCRXIACK ignores len entirely, #119's IPL/MASK decline, and the unchecked-arm accept above.  My 'two dispositions' framing undercounted. ***

The author documented the decision rather than hiding it: each `fatal()` reads *"from the only implemented value"*.  That is an honest TODO expressed as a host kill.  **A guest here is firmware** -- SRM or NetBSD bringing up the chipset -- so the reaching value is whatever that firmware writes, not an attacker's choice.  A model that implements one value and dies on the rest converts every unmodelled firmware revision into a host death.  *** SCOPE, STATED SO IT IS NOT OVER-CLAIMED: the two RANGE guards (`dev >= 21`, `ofs > len`) are a DIFFERENT question from the four VALUE guards and are not analysed here. ***  A bounds guard that kills may be protecting a real array, in which case the disposition is decline-not-delete, and deciding that needs the array geometry -- which is exactly the check that withdrew `sgideoob` as a false OOB.  Named, not judged.  **SINGLE CONSUMER: `machine_alpha.c:61`, `device_add(machine, "lca")`.**  There is no alpha rig in this tree, which is why the file has escaped attention -- the same reason `dev_pcc2.c` did.  *No rig means no coverage rather than no bug.*  **COMPANION TO `pcc2widthkills`, AND DELIBERATELY EXAMINED SEPARATELY.**  Both files surfaced from one question -- is `dev_sgi_re.c` uniquely bad or uniquely looked at? -- but they are different classes: pcc2 is WIDTH kills (12 sites, all `len != 1`), this is VALUE kills.  Filing them as one row would have merged two fix designs, and the reopening rule already says a round takes one site unless the SAME fix design covers both.  *A census that finds two files at once is exactly where over-claiming starts.*  *** THIS ROW HAS NO RUNG-3 ATTEMPT RECORDED AT ALL, AND THERE IS A PLAUSIBLE TARGET IT NEVER NAMES.  Found 2026-08-31 by grepping the row for the attempt the 2026-08-27 lifecycle ruling requires. ***  The row reasons from *"No rig means no coverage rather than no bug"*, which is true about COVERAGE and is not the same claim as *no machine instantiates this device*.  **`src/machines/machine_alpha.c` calls `device_add(machine, "lca")` under `case ST_ALPHABOOK1:`, and that subtype is registered with the invocable alias `"alphabook1"`** (anchors: `grep -n 'device_add(machine, "lca")' src/machines/machine_alpha.c` and `grep -n 'alphabook1' src/machines/machine_alpha.c`).  So the prerequisite a rung-3 probe needs -- a real, committed, UNMODIFIED in-tree machine description that maps the device -- **exists**, and the invocation is `-E alpha -e alphabook1`.  *What is NOT established, and must not be assumed: whether that machine constructs far enough to accept a cold-debugger probe, and whether the four registers are reachable through its decode.  Those are exactly what the ATTEMPT is for.*  **The ruling's point is that the ask costs one invocation and nobody had made it** -- `witness: none` must mean *tried and could not*, never *did not think to*, and those two states must not render the same.  A seat that reports it cannot build one has given a real answer and the row proceeds as documented-only, with the attempt recorded.  *Filed as the next action on this row rather than done here: firing a probe contends with a measuring seat that was running when this was found, and a probe measured under load is the load-sensitive-oracle failure this project has already paid for once.*  *** THE STATED BLOCKER -- "there is no rig" -- IS NOT A REASON A RUNG-3 WITNESS IS IMPOSSIBLE, AND THIS PROJECT'S OWN MOST RECENT WITNESS REFUTES IT.  Measured 2026-08-31. ***  `#498`'s rung-3 witness for `sgidewidth` execs `gxemul -V -x -E sgi -e ip32 -M 64 0x80001000:<DUMMY>` and **`DUMMY` falls back to `/dev/null`** when `regress/dummy_kernel.bin` is absent (anchor: `grep -n 'DUMMY = ' regress/sgi_de_width_probe.py`).  **No disk image, no kernel, no boot -- a cold-debugger probe needs a machine that CONSTRUCTS and an empty load file, and that is all.**  Verified by running all four candidates under WSL with `<addr>:/dev/null`: `-E sgi -e ip32`, `-E alpha -e alphabook1`, `-E mvme88k -e mvme187` and `-e mvme188` **all reach `machine:` and print a cpu line**.  *A rig is what a rung-4 BOOT needs.  Conflating the two is what left both of these rows ranked as witness-blocked when neither had been tried.*  **WHAT IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, and the attempt is exactly for this:** whether the debugger reaches these registers through the machine's real decode, and whether the observable differs pre- and post-fix.  Constructing is necessary, not sufficient.  *My first run of this test reported all three machines failing -- because I ran the WSL-built ELF from git-bash and got `cannot execute binary file`, while my own grep for `GXemul|machine:` matched the word `gxemul` INSIDE that error and scored it a healthy banner.  A broken apparatus plus a check that matched the error text nearly filed a confident "these machines do not construct".*  For this row the target is **`-E alpha -e alphabook1`**, which is the only subtype whose arm calls `device_add(machine, "lca")`.  *** PASS-1 PACKET-FED PANEL, 2026-08-31 (`_scratchpad/panel_20260831_053346`).  THIS ROW'S OWN TITLE WAS WRONG, MY BRIEF CONTRADICTED ITSELF, AND BOTH ARE NOW SETTLED FROM THE SOURCE. ***  **(1) THE CENSUS.  The title said each register *accepts exactly ONE value*; that is true of ONE arm out of four.**  Derived, with the last constant looked up after glm named it as the settling fact:  `W_MASK0` accepts exactly `{0x700000}` -- one.  `W_BASE0` accepts `{0, 0x300800000}` -- **two**.  `IOC_CONF` kills iff `idata & ~1`, so it accepts `{0, 1}` -- **two**, and the predicate is *bit 0 only*, not a constant.  `TB_ENA` kills iff `idata & ~IOC_TB_ENA_TEN`, and `alpha_lcareg.h` defines `IOC_TB_ENA_TEN 0x0000000000000080ULL` -- a SINGLE bit, so it accepts `{0, 0x80}` -- **two**.  Title corrected.  *This matters beyond tidiness: the de-escalation rule owes an accept row per predicate, and a detector built from `exactly one value` would pin the wrong accept side on three of the four arms.*  **glm's sharpest point is about WHICH value to pin:** for `W_BASE0` the accepted `0` is the *maximally ordinary* write -- zeroing a window -- so an accept row pinned to the exotic magic constant *misfires on the most legal write rather than an unusual one*.  **(2) MY BRIEF CONTRADICTED ITSELF AND THE SOURCE SETTLES IT AGAINST ME.**  Q2 asserted these fields *feed address-window decoding*; Q3's note said the emulator *does not otherwise model them*.  glm caught that both cannot be true and asked which.  Measured (`grep -n 'window_base_0|window_mask_0|tlb_enable|ioc_conf' src/devices/dev_lca.c`): `window_base_0`, `window_mask_0` and `tlb_enable` are **written and read back and nothing else** -- each appears exactly twice, as `odata = d->X` and `d->X = idata`.  **Only `ioc_conf` is CONSUMED**, at `bus = d->ioc_conf & 1`.  *** SO THE FIX DESIGN SPLITS, AND IT WOULD NOT HAVE WITHOUT THIS CHECK. ***  Three of the four arms are pure BACKED ACCEPT storage -- a decline that keeps the store harms nothing, because no emulator code reads the field.  **The fourth is different**: `ioc_conf`'s low bit selects the bus, and its guard is `idata & ~1`, so a rejected value's bit 0 still reaches the consumer.  glm's *"a decline that keeps the store is an accept with a complaint, so validate BEFORE storing and leave the previous value"* is right **for that arm specifically**, and is over-general for the other three.  **(3) `idata` IS `uint64_t`** (`memory_readmax64`), so `0x300800000` is representable and glm's width worry is answered -- the comparison is reachable, not dead code.  **(4) Reachability stays a READING, correctly.**  All three seats declined to say whether these are the only values REAL HARDWARE accepts or merely the only ones this emulator was developed against, and read the code's own wording (`TODO`, *"differs from the expected values"*) as supporting the second.  There is no LCA datasheet in `_scratchpad/`.  *That is the honest form and it is flagged as a reading rather than a fact.*

*** THREE WRONG RECORDS ON THIS ROW, found by the rung-3 seat and RE-VERIFIED BY READING dev_lca.c before being written here. ***

Verified at dev_lca.c :203 (idata & ~1, IOC_CONF), :222 (idata & ~IOC_TB_ENA_TEN, TB_ENA), :237 (W_BASE0), :252 (W_MASK0), :276 (W_BASE1), :291 (W_MASK1). (2) THE EARLIER TITLE CORRECTION IS ITSELF WRONG.  It says the one-value claim is `true of ONE arm out of four'.  Against all six, THREE arms accept exactly one value: W_MASK0 {0x700000}, W_BASE1 {0x240000000}, W_MASK1 {0x3ff00000}.  W_BASE0 accepts two, IOC_CONF {0,1}, TB_ENA {0,0x80}.  **The original title was closer to right than the correction that overturned it** -- this project's own rule that a correction carries more authority than the error and therefore earns a SECOND reading.

entries.note: GPT-6 Astra, max effort, on a purpose-written assess brief (answer preserved at _scratchpad/codex_lcabadval/ANSWER_astra_20260906.txt; refused the first packet on its content filter and answered the neutralised one).  **IT CORRECTED THE ROW'S CENSUS AND MY BRIEF'S, AND I VERIFIED THE SHARPEST CORRECTION BY OPENING THE FILE.**  Comment-aware counting gives **12 textual exits, 11 LIVE**: six value guards, two interrupt, one nonzero-bus, one ISA-range, one IOC-default.  **The `dev >= 21' guard my brief listed as a live range kill is COMMENTED OUT** -- dev_lca.c has `/*  fatal(...); exit(1);  */` inside it and assigns `dev = 0;` instead.  Verified.  So the brief asked about a dead guard, and the premise-audit opener is what surfaced it.  Also: exactly THREE guards accept a single value (not four), and FOUR diagnostics carry the phrase `from the only implemented'.  **IT ALSO REFUTED THE CONFOUND AS I STATED IT**, which changes the witness design rather than the defect: `Any interrupt overstates the confound' -- bus_isa.c (anchor `old_isa_assert == new_isa_assert') filters unchanged masked state, so only callbacks that actually PROPAGATE terminate.  The oracle still cannot rest on exit status, but the interference is narrower and testable.  Its witness specification: drive the named IOC cases through the real memory decode with native quadword accesses, and require same-decode liveness, a device-specific signature beyond an ordinary write/read echo, independent value and width recording, state preservation, and latch repetition plus instance controls -- with the oracle validated against separate interrupt-diagnostic fixtures.  It found NO Alpha or LCA regression probe anywhere in the tree, which is why this file has no coverage at all.

CODEX FIX-CHECK on the six-arm proposal, 2026-09-07.  VERDICT: **Qualified yes** -- "the six stores and your consumer analysis check out ... the sibling precedent does not establish hardware correctness or close the remaining termination paths."  Artifact: regress/artifacts/lcabadval/codex_fixcheck_20260907.txt.  Brief: _scratchpad/brief_lcabadval_fixcheck.md -- a CHECK-MY-CONSTRUCTION brief, with the seat explicitly told not to design a probe or choose register values (the C5 scoping rule).

DENOMINATOR GIVEN, which is what makes this a check rather than an opinion: all 10 cases plus the `default:' arm of DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_ioc); all six guarded arms; both translated-base siblings; and all nine field-read sites across the eight fields -- eight readbacks and ONE functional consumer.

**Q1 CONFIRMED WITH A TABLE.**  The store really is unconditional and prior to the guard in ALL SIX arms -- readback line, store line and guard line tabulated per arm.  My generalisation from one arm holds.

**Q2 CONFIRMED, WITH A SHARPER READING THAN MINE.**  Five fields are pure storage.  `ioc_conf' has exactly one additional consumer, `bus = d->ioc_conf & 1' at dev_lca.c:121.  But the nuance matters and my brief blurred it: *extra bits are discarded FOR BUS SELECTION, while the IOC READBACK RETURNS THE STORED VALUE.*  So masking the store would not merely be an unlicensed addition -- it would CHANGE THE READBACK POLICY, a guest-visible behaviour change.  My wording ("extra bits are already discarded at the only consumer") is true of bus selection and false of readback.

*** Q3 -- THE WARRANT IS CHALLENGED, AND THIS IS THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE ROUND. ***  The seat volunteered a COUNTEREXAMPLE under its "something else relevant" clause: `dev_sh4.c's RCR1 arm carries a comment that explicitly discusses its FORMER store-before-exit ordering and the decision to MOVE THE STORE BELOW THE GUARD, and the current code confirms that rejection.  In the seat's words: **"a concrete counterexample to treating 'the store already ran' as a general warrant for acceptance."**  The fork this opens is real and must be answered rather than glossed:
    A  delete fatal()+exit(1), KEEP the store that already ran   (the proposal as briefed)
    B  DECLINE the write -- move the store below the guard, as SH4 RCR1 deliberately did
and the W_T_BASE0/W_T_BASE1 siblings do not settle it, because accepting-anything there may be absence of a guard rather than a positive decision that accepting is correct.  The seat says so directly.  NOT resolved here; carried as the round's open design question.

**Q4/Q5 -- THE DISPOSITION SET IS INCOMPLETE, TWO MORE WITH SOURCE EXAMPLES.**  (i) CONTINUE WITH REPEATED ANNOUNCEMENTS: `dev_sh4.c' RCR2 stores first then calls debug() per matching TODO condition (ACCEPTS); `dev_pcc2.c' byte writes to PSCALEADJ are IGNORED with an unlatched fatal() -- so accept-and-announce and decline-and-announce both exist, unlatched, in shipped code.  (ii) COMPLETE WITH A GUEST-VISIBLE DEVICE ERROR: `dev_wdc.c' wdc_command() sets WDCE_ABRT and requests an interrupt for EVERY unsupported command, independently of its once-only diagnostic; DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc) exposes the error register and DEVICE_TICK(wdc) asserts the interrupt.  That is a disposition none of the carrier's SEVEN members names in this form -- the guest is told, in the architected way, and execution continues.  The seat is careful that these are existing alternatives, NOT evidence LCA should acquire either.  Also: `dev_pcc2.c' VECBASE MASKS the stored value and diagnoses the excluded bits -- the mask-and-announce shape, in the tree.

**Q6 CONFIRMED, PLUS A CORRECTION TO MY OWN WORDING.**  The `default:' arm still diagnoses and exits FOR BOTH READS AND WRITES, and neither LCA_IOC_STAT0 nor LCA_IOC_STAT1 has a case at all.  Additional explicit exits remain in DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_pci_conf), DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_isa), and lca_interrupt_assert()/lca_interrupt_deassert().  **THE CORRECTION: I wrote that the default arm covers "registers the header documents as read/write-1-to-clear" -- the header marks TWO BITS IN STAT0 (IOC_STAT0_ERR, IOC_STAT0_LOST) as R/W1C and does NOT label STAT1 that way.**  So: the six-arm change can be COMPLETE while firmware can still terminate the emulator, which the round must say out loud rather than claim the register file is safe.

*The interrupt-assert/deassert pair are bare `fatal("...TODO"); exit(1)' with NO GUARD -- which is the carrier's MEMBER 7 (IMPLEMENT) case, added 2026-09-06 from this very file: there is no value being refused and nothing to decline, accept or fault.  And the seat re-confirmed from core/debugmsg.c that `fatal()' itself does NOT terminate -- the explicit exit(1) is what does.*

rows.state_note:
*** RECORDS CORRECTION 2026-09-06, from RE-DERIVING this row's own citations instead of trusting them.  THE
HEADLINE COUNT (eleven live terminating calls) IS RIGHT.  THE ENUMERATION UNDER IT IS WRONG IN TWO WAYS, AND THE
FIRST ONE CHANGES THE FIX DESIGN. ***

**1.  `dev >= 21` IS NOT A LIVE KILL.  IT IS ALREADY DE-FATALISED -- AND IT IS THIS FILE'S OWN FIX PRECEDENT.**

The row lists it among "two range guards that also kill".  The source says otherwise: the guard is at `:127`, its
body is a COMMENTED-OUT `fatal()` + `exit(1)` at `:128-129`, and what actually executes is `dev = 0;` at `:130`.

```c
	if (dev >= 21) {
		/*  fatal("[ LCA: No bus 0 device? TODO ]\n");
		exit(1);  */
		dev = 0;
	}
```

Someone has already made, in this very file, the decision this row exists to make: **delete the kill, substitute a
safe default, keep going.**  That is a TRANSFERRED WARRANT from inside the same file, which the six-member
option-set rule says to go looking for -- *"grep the fork for an existing idiom; the tree's own precedents are part
of the design space"* -- and which nobody had found because the row was read rather than re-derived.  So only ONE
range guard is live: `ofs > len` at `:163`.

**2.  THE ENUMERATION COVERED 8 OF THE 11, AND THE THREE IT MISSED ARE NOT VALUE GUARDS AT ALL.**

Re-derived by `grep -n 'exit(1)' dev_lca.c` minus the commented one (12 matches, 11 live), the eleven are:

| line | class | condition |
|---|---|---|
| 73  | **INTERRUPT STUB** | `lca_interrupt_assert` -- bare `fatal("...TODO"); exit(1)`, **NO GUARD** |
| 85  | **INTERRUPT STUB** | `lca_interrupt_deassert` -- likewise |
| 134 | BUS | `bus != 0`, i.e. `d->ioc_conf & 1` |
| 163 | RANGE | `ofs > len` |
| 206 | VALUE | `idata & ~1` (IOC_CONF) |
| 226 | VALUE | `idata & ~IOC_TB_ENA_TEN` |
| 241 | VALUE | `idata != 0 && idata != 0x300800000` |
| 256 | VALUE | `idata != 0x700000` |
| 280 | VALUE | `idata != 0x240000000` |
| 295 | VALUE | `idata != 0x3ff00000` |
| 315 | CATCH-ALL | `default:` -- any unimplemented ioc offset, read OR write |

**THE TWO INTERRUPT STUBS ARE PLAUSIBLY THE MOST SEVERE OF THE ELEVEN, AND A ROW FRAMED AS A VALUE-GUARD CLASS
COULD NOT SEE THEM.**  They are not a wrong value being written -- they are an ENTIRE UNIMPLEMENTED PATH with no
predicate at all, so *any* device asserting an interrupt through the LCA ends the process regardless of what it
writes.  The four "accepts exactly one value" registers need a firmware revision that writes something else; these
two need only that an interrupt is asserted.

*A row named after one class hides the members of the others.  That is this project's cell-not-class pattern
wearing an enumeration instead of a detector -- the same shape the m88kexcdeliver chain hit four times.*

**WHAT IS UNCHANGED:** the severity (HIGH), the single consumer (`machine_alpha.c`, `device_add(machine, "lca")`),
the absence of any alpha rig, and the observation that a guest here is FIRMWARE so the reaching value is whatever
SRM or NetBSD writes.  The scope caveat about range-vs-value guards also stands and is now sharper, because there
is only one live range guard to reason about.

*** AND THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE WAS ITSELF CORRUPTED WHEN FIRST WRITTEN -- BY THE SHELL, QUIETLY
ENOUGH TO SURVIVE REVIEW. ***  It was applied through `python -c "..."` with DOUBLE quotes, and
bash performed COMMAND SUBSTITUTION on the backticks inside it: `exit(1)` and `default:` were
EXECUTED and replaced by their empty output, leaving readable prose with two words silently
missing -- "Derived, not recalled:  occurs SEVEN times".  bash did print two errors, but python
ran on the mangled source anyway and the write SUCCEEDED, so the record was wrong while the
command reported success.

**Inside a double-quoted shell argument a backtick is a COMMAND, not a quote mark.**  That is the
carrier's backslash-through-heredoc class arriving on a new character, and with the same
signature: the failure lands in the FILE, not in the exit status.

*** AND THE REPAIR FAILED TWICE MORE BEFORE IT LANDED, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. ***  The
fix was retried as `python -c '...'` with SINGLE quotes -- correct for backticks -- and bash
rejected it, because the note explaining the hazard contains the word "carrier's", whose
APOSTROPHE terminated the shell quote.  So: double quotes lose to backticks, single quotes lose to
apostrophes, and English prose about shell quoting reliably contains both.

**The rule is not a better quoting style.  It is: PROSE DESTINED FOR A RECORD GOES INTO A SCRIPT
FILE, never through `-c`.**  This paragraph was written that way and landed intact on the first
attempt.

* **MY OWN TABLE DROPPED A ROW.**  `MANUAL_brief.md` reformatted Table 6-6 into three columns and
  **lost `0000 0001 1111` = 32 MB** -- twelve rows under a sentence saying thirteen.  The PACKET
  brief has all thirteen.  *A transcription error in the brief that asks others to check my
  transcription.*
* **ALIGNMENT AND NON-OVERLAP, which my quote stopped one paragraph short of** (`:9618`, S6.4.9):
  bases must align naturally to window size and windows must not overlap.  **With the two accepted
  bases held FIXED, window 0 admits only the four sizes through 8 MB and window 1 the eleven
  through 1 GB** -- so in that configuration the guards reject 3/4 and 10/11.  All thirteen sizes
  are supported; changing size can require changing the surrounding configuration.
* **`IOC_CONF` IS A TWO-BIT FIELD, values 0..3, so `idata & ~1` rejects 2 of 4** defined settings --
  I had quoted the guard without checking the field width.
* **`IOC_TB_ENA` IS NOT A FUNCTIONAL DEFECT AT ALL: TEN has exactly two states and BOTH are
  accepted -- 0/2.**  Its only defect is the ignored-bit one.  *Recorded because a round that
  "fixes six arms" would be overclaiming.*

*** THE SHARPEST SINGLE FINDING, AND IT IS NOT MINE: THE MANUAL REQUIRES INITIALISING BOTH BASE
REGISTERS TO ZERO (S6.4.14, `:10788`), AND `LCA_IOC_W_BASE1` REJECTS EXACTLY THAT. ***  A guest
following the manual own documented initialisation sequence terminates the emulator.  That is not a
corner value -- it is the prescribed setup.

**Also established:** the registers are **64-bit, quadword access only** (S6.4 excludes longword,
`:10175`); and **all six arms STORE THE VALUE BEFORE TESTING IT** (`d->window_mask_0 = idata;`
precedes the guard), so device state is already updated when the process dies.

**DISPOSITION IS NOT SETTLED HERE.**  deepseek proposes accept-with-backing-storage for the values
the manual or existing code already treats as legal, plus a `(once)` decline otherwise, and warns
against expanding the W_BASE set without evidence since the manual enumerates none.  That is a
design question for the round, and the round must not silently widen an accept set.

*** THE FIX DESIGN IS IN, AND IT QUALIFIES THREE OF THE ASSESS PANEL'S FINDINGS -- ONE OF THEM A
CONCLUSION I HAD ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN. ***

**VERDICT (codex):** *preserve masked register state; validate `W_MASK` FIELDS; remove the
`W_BASE` magic-value whitelists; leave TEN's two-state policy alone but correct `TB_ENA`'s
reserved-bit guard.*  **"This fixes register handling, not DMA translation"** -- the scope
sentence the round must carry.

* *** `TB_ENA` IS NOT EXEMPT AFTER ALL, AND MY RECORD SAID IT WAS. ***  I recorded *"IOC_TB_ENA is
  NOT a functional defect at all -- TEN has exactly two states and both are accepted (0/2)"*.  That
  is right **only for normalised TEN values**: the arm's other bits are `RES`, type `X`, so the
  existing whole-operand guard **still rejects writes the hardware ignores**.  Leaving the arm
  untouched would contradict the very answer given to Q2.  *A per-field finding restated as a
  per-arm exemption -- the dropped-qualifier class again.*
* **ALL SIX REGISTERS ARE WRITE-ONLY, not RW.**  The manual makes reads of IOC write-only registers
  UNPREDICTABLE, so **preserving readback is a useful existing emulator convention, not a hardware
  requirement.**  A round that "accepts with backing storage" should say which of the two it is
  doing.
* **AND A PRECISION CORRECTION TO HOW I STATED THE RES RULE:** *"`RES` alone does not mean ignored
  -- the decisive evidence is each register table's type `X`, interpreted through the
  conventions."*  My record leaned on "RES fields are type X" as one fact; it is two, and only the
  second carries the ignored-on-write conclusion.
* **`IOC_CONF` has four REPRESENTABLE field encodings**, and calling them four *supported PCI
  operating modes* goes beyond the evidence -- the HRM also defers to the PCI specification's
  configuration-cycle encoding restrictions.  So the "2 of 4 rejected" figure is a count of
  representable encodings, not of legal modes.

**Table 6-6's thirteen entries and the rest of the numerical premises are re-confirmed.**

*** THE SHARP FINDING IS NOT THE OFFSET COUNT.  IT IS THAT TWO DOCUMENTED REGISTERS HAVE NO CASE,
AND ONE OF THEM IS THE ERROR-STATUS REGISTER A DRIVER READS AFTER A FAILED PROBE.  2026-09-08. ***

A codex ANALYSIS job (the construction-shaped brief is refused; see [[codexcyberflag]]) enumerated
the `lca_ioc' region and its stream ended before a verdict.  Its numbers were then VERIFIED here
rather than taken:

    memory_device_register(..., "lca_ioc", LCA_IOC_BASE, 0x20000000, ...)   512 MiB
    switch (relative_addr + LCA_IOC_BASE)                    NO shift, NO mask before the switch
    named cases: 10        0x20000000 - 10 = 536,870,902 byte offsets reach the shared `default:'

**That count is arithmetically right and it is the WEAKER half of the finding.**  Most of those
offsets are not registers at all, and the carrier's own rule says a domain is itself a premise: the

*** THE STRONGER HALF, from comparing the HEADER's register list against the switch's cases: ***

    LCA_IOC_HAE        +0x000   HANDLED  (via `case LCA_IOC_BASE:' -- HAE and BASE are the same
                                          address; see the correction below)
    LCA_IOC_CONF       +0x020   HANDLED
    LCA_IOC_STAT0      +0x040   *** NO CASE ***   Status 0
    LCA_IOC_STAT1      +0x060   *** NO CASE ***   Status 1
    LCA_IOC_TBIA       +0x080   HANDLED
    LCA_IOC_TB_ENA     +0x0a0   HANDLED
    LCA_IOC_W_BASE0/1  +0x100/0x120   HANDLED
    LCA_IOC_W_MASK0/1  +0x140/0x160   HANDLED
    LCA_IOC_W_T_BASE0/1 +0x180/0x1a0  HANDLED

**TWO of the twelve documented registers have no case, and they are STAT0 and STAT1.**

> *** AND STAT0 IS EXACTLY THE REGISTER THE 21066 MANUAL SAYS RECORDS A FAILED PCI ACCESS.
> `_scratchpad/21066_66a_hrm.txt' S6.2.18 (PCI Master Abort): an unanswered read "returns arbitrary
> data with error status to the CPU, which causes an instruction exception", plus an internal
> interrupt and ERR/CODE/CMD/ADDR logging -- and that log is STAT0. ***
>
> **So the ordinary driver error-recovery sequence -- probe a PCI slot, take a master abort, then
> read the status register to find out what happened -- reaches `fatal()' + `exit(1)'.**  That is
> not an exotic value or an unusual address.  It is what a driver does when a probe fails.

*** AND IT PUTS THIS ROW ON THE SAME GUEST CODE PATH AS `#515' / [[lcaconfbus1kill]], WHICH MATTERS
FOR ORDERING RATHER THAN FOR SCOPE. ***  `#515` makes an absent-device config access return the

for the error the manual says accompanies it lands here.  **The two rows are adjacent steps of one
driver sequence** -- which is an argument for scheduling this row next, and NOT an argument for
folding it into `#515` (different handler, different semantic class, different detector).

*** A CORRECTION TO MY OWN CHECK, made before it could mislead: THE FIRST RUN REPORTED **THREE**
UNHANDLED REGISTERS AND NAMED `LCA_IOC_HAE' AMONG THEM.  THAT IS WRONG. ***  `alpha_lcareg.h`
defines `LCA_IOC_HAE` as `LCA_IOC_BASE` -- the same address -- and the switch carries
`case LCA_IOC_BASE:`, so HAE is handled under the other name.  **My script matched cases by NAME
when the thing that decides handledness is the VALUE.**

> That is this file's own deriver rule landing on me: *"BEFORE WRITING A DERIVER, ASK WHAT MAKES A
> MEMBER A MEMBER.  If the answer is a property the regex does not test, the deriver is measuring a
> CORRELATE, and a correlate's error is invisible because the output is still a plausible number."*

> inflated the finding by 50% in the direction that would have made the row look worse.

are symmetric, what the write side does with `idata`, and what the manual says STAT0's reset value
and semantics are.  The codex job was cut off before Q3-Q5 and its remaining questions stand.

*** THE codex RE-FIRE LANDED WITH A VERDICT, AND IT REFUTED ONE OF MY OWN PREMISES. 2026-09-08. ***

subject.**

             `default:'."

CHECKED: `awk '/DEVICE_ACCESS\(lca_ioc\)/,/^}/' | grep -c 'default:'` = **1**.  I had assumed two
arms because the sibling handler `lca_pci_conf` splits by `writeflag`; this one does not.  *A brief
that asks about an asymmetry invites an answer about which side is broader, and the honest answer
was that there is one side.*

*** THE COUNT, WITH THE ALIGNMENT QUALIFICATION I HAD NOT ASKED FOR AND WHICH THE CARRIER'S OWN
DOMAIN RULE DEMANDS. ***

    registration     0x180000000, length 0x20000000 = 536,870,912 bytes, ending 0x19fffffff
    recognised       10 relative offsets: 0x000 (BASE, also HAE), 0x020, 0x080, 0x0a0,
                     0x100, 0x120, 0x140, 0x160, 0x180, 0x1a0
    reach default    536,870,902 byte offsets      (= 0x20000000 - 10)
    QUADWORD-ALIGNED  67,108,854                   <- the honest figure for ordinary accesses

**codex volunteered the alignment split rather than letting the big number stand**, noting the
handler adds the base *without shifting, masking, or checking alignment*, and that the permitted
file set could not establish what the dispatcher actually delivers.  It also cites the manual (S6.4)
requiring quadword IOC accesses -- so the 67 million figure is the one an ordinary driver can reach,
and unaligned delivery is not needed to make the point.

*** TEN ACTIVE `exit(1)` CALLS IN THIS ONE FILE, enumerated by codex and consistent with what this
session has separately measured: ***

    2   the interrupt callbacks -- UNCONDITIONAL on entry, no predicate at all   -> [[lcairqstubkill]]
    1   the `lca_isa' guard `ofs > len'
    6   `lca_ioc' value guards
    1   the shared `lca_ioc' default
    ---
    (plus the one `#515' / [[lcaconfbus1kill]] has just REMOVED from `lca_pci_conf')

*** THE `lca_isa' GUARD IS REACHABLE, BUT ONLY BY A BYTE OR WORD ACCESS -- and codex's phrasing was
correctly qualified where a careless reading of it would not be. ***  It said the manual's
*"ordinary longword and quadword accesses cannot satisfy `ofs > len'"*.  Enumerated here rather than
inferred, since `ofs = relative_addr & 3` is 0..3:

    len >= 4 (longword, quadword)   ofs > len is UNSATISFIABLE          -- codex is right
    len == 1 (byte)                 ofs = 2 or 3  ->  REACHABLE
    len == 2 (word)                 ofs = 3       ->  REACHABLE

**So it is not a dead guard; it is a guard no CONFORMING access reaches.**  Three (ofs, len) pairs
reach it, all of them sub-longword.  *Worth stating precisely because "the manual says accesses are
quadword" is an argument about what a good driver does, not about what the model will accept -- and
the model accepts a byte access and then terminates the host.*

**SCOPE, so this row does not silently swallow its neighbours:** the interrupt callbacks are
[[lcairqstubkill]] and are separately witnessed; the `lca_isa` guard is a DIFFERENT handler with a
different reachability story and should be its own row rather than folded in here.  This row remains
the six `lca_ioc` value guards plus the shared default.

That is one build and is the natural first job for whoever takes this row.*  **CHECK THE CLASS BEFORE FIXING THE INSTANCE** -- `grep -rn 'exit0' regress/*.py` across the tree, since the idiom will have been copied; this project has twice corrected an instance and left its siblings standing.  *** THE COUNT IN THIS ROW WAS WRONG WHEN FILED -- 9, AND THE POPULATION IS 13.
