rows.title: SGIRE_W_* spells its bits as literal `1 << N`, so a duplicate is legal C and silent
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED -- the #498/#499 collision scored 14/14, a total escape
rows.note:
*** THIS CLASS HAS THREE INSTANCES IN THREE DAYS AND THE STRUCTURAL FIX IS ALREADY BLESSED IN THIS PROJECT FOR THE SAME SHAPE. ***  **Instance 1, MEASURED:** `#498` added `SGIRE_W_DE_LEN = 1 << 6`; `#499`'s witness generator independently inserted `SGIRE_W_UNMAP_WR = 1 << 6`.  Legal C, silent, and because `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_de)` casts the same `struct sgi_re_data *`, `d->warned` is shared -- **14/14 total escape**, with a transcript showing one guest `sb` to `sgi_de` permanently silencing `sgi_re`'s catch-all diagnostic.  **Instance 2:** the codex seat independently proposed `1 << 7` -> `1 << 6` as the canonical clause-(d) mutant for the `#500` fix -- i.e. an adversary reaches for this collision unprompted.  **Instance 3, PREVENTED:** `#499` and `#500` were both designed for `1 << 7` while in flight together.  Caught by listing the enum before writing either fix; `#500` moves to `1 << 9`.  *Two of three instances were found by measurement AFTER the fact; the third by one `grep` BEFORE it, which is the cheap end of this.*  **THE FIX, and it is the idiom the carrier already records for `SH4_VAL_*`:** that enum was converted to a C99 enum ending in `_NCLASS` precisely so *duplicates are impossible by construction*, and the carrier marks that work DISCHARGED.  The same shape applies here with one extra step, because these are MASKS rather than ids -- enumerate the BIT POSITIONS and derive the masks:  `enum { SGIRE_WB_TLBA, SGIRE_WB_TLBB, ..., SGIRE_WB_NBITS };` then `#define SGIRE_W_TLBA_LEN (1 << SGIRE_WB_TLBA)`.  **The enumerator auto-increments, so two bits cannot collide however many rounds add one**, and `SGIRE_WB_NBITS` gives a compile-time check that the set still fits `uint32_t warned`.  **NOT a rider on either round in flight.**  It touches every latch site in the file (seven today, nine after `#499` and `#500`), it is a pure refactor with no behavioural delta, and under the ADDITION LICENCE a no-delta change needs a warrant -- which it has, in a MEASURED instance rather than in "cannot hurt".  It ships as its own round with the obvious control: the pre- and post-refactor binaries must be byte-identical, or the refactor was not one.

*** MAIN-LOOP MEASUREMENT 2026-09-01 (not a seat answer; recorded here rather than in `entries` so it cannot be counted toward the panel). ***

*** THE HAZARD STOPPED BEING HYPOTHETICAL TODAY: TWO ROUNDS IN ONE DAY WERE BOTH DESIGNED FOR `1 << 7', AND THE COLLISION WAS CAUGHT ONLY BY A HUMAN LISTING THE ENUM. ***

`#499` took 1 << 7 and 1 << 8; `#500` took 1 << 9.  Both were originally written against 1 << 7.  `#500`'s own PRETABLE.out records it: *"Both rounds were designed for 1<<7 and the collision was caught by listing the enum before writing either fix."*

**WHAT A COLLISION WOULD HAVE COST, measured rather than argued:** `#498` measured a reused bit at 23/25, and `#500`'s own kill table measured `M_BITALIAS` (SGIRE_W_PRIM_OP aliased onto `#498`'s 1 << 6) at 18/21 -- killed by ONE row, `xlatch decl`, which exists only because a seat pointed out every other row ran in a fresh session.  **Without that row the collision would have been INVISIBLE**, and a duplicate enumerator is legal C with no diagnostic.

**And it crosses DEVICES, not just windows:** the sgi_re / sgi_de / sgi_mte / sgi_de_status handlers all cast ONE malloc'd struct, so `d->warned` is shared.  A bit reused between two of them is silenced by the other's ordinary traffic.

**THE FIX IS STRUCTURAL AND COSTS NOTHING AT RUNTIME**, and the tree already has the precedent: `dev_sh4.c` converted `SH4_VAL_*` to a C99 enum ending in `_NCLASS`, where duplicates are impossible by construction.  For BIT FLAGS the analogue is an index enum plus a shift --
    enum { SGIRE_B_TLBA_LEN = 0, SGIRE_B_TLBB_LEN, ..., SGIRE_W_NBITS };
    #define SGIRE_W_TLBA_LEN (1 << SGIRE_B_TLBA_LEN)
-- because auto-incrementing enumerators cannot collide, whereas explicit `1 << N` values can and did nearly do so twice today.

**NOT DONE THIS SESSION, and the reason is the addition licence rather than effort:** it touches product code in a file two rounds have just edited, it owes its own pass 1, and `#500`'s repair chain is still open.  Filed with the near-miss recorded so the next round does not have to rediscover that the hazard is live.

rows.title: dev_*.c: warn-once latches that are FUNCTION-STATIC, so one guest access to one device instance permanently silences the diagnostic for every other instance -- count DERIVED BY SCOPE, never by variable name (three name-based censuses came back wrong; see the row's deriver)
rows.witness: harness:DERIVED from the shipped source, 2026-08-31, across all of src/devices/
rows.note: *** THREE SEPARATE ROUNDS INDEPENDENTLY REACHED FOR THE SAME IDEA AND ALL THREE USED PROCESS-GLOBAL STATE.  Found 2026-08-31 by re-deriving a census a seat had made with a narrower pattern. ***  **THE DERIVER, because two separate counts of this class have already been short:**  `grep -rn 'static int w = 0;|static int first = 1;|static char .*_used\[' src/devices/*.c`  ->  **10 sites across 3 files** on 2026-08-31:  `dev_jazz.c` 2 (from `#179`), `dev_pcc2.c` 4 (from `#119`), `dev_sgi_re.c` 4 (upstream `rop_used`).  **THE DEFECT.**  A `static` inside a function is process-global, not per-instance.  Every one of these is a *warn-once* latch on a GUEST-DRIVABLE diagnostic, so **one guest access to one device instance permanently silences that diagnostic for every other instance of the same device in the machine** -- and for every later machine in the same process.  The house form is a per-instance bit in the device's own struct (`d->warned` plus `(once)` in the message text), which `#337`, `#460`, `#461`, `#497` and `#498` all use.  **THE INTENT IS RIGHT EVERYWHERE AND ONLY THE SCOPE IS WRONG.**  `#179`'s comment says *"guest-reachable; ignore the write instead of fatal()-flooding host stdout"*; `#119`'s says *"was exit(1) -> warn-once + continue"*.  Both are correct de-fatalisations that this project would make again.  **This row is about SCOPE, not disposition, and must not be read as reopening either round.**  *** HOW IT WAS FOUND IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: TWO CENSUSES OF THIS CLASS WERE BOTH SHORT, IN OPPOSITE WAYS. ***  A measuring seat censused it while answering an unrelated question and reported *"4 lines, ALL in this file, ALL inside draw_primitive(), the tree's only such sites"* -- true of its pattern (`static int first`/`_used[`) and false of the class, because `#119` and `#179` spell their latch `static int w = 0`.  Then a packet-fed seat on a DIFFERENT row challenged an `exit(` regex of mine as too narrow; the count it challenged did not move, **but chasing the four extra hits surfaced `#119`'s comments and hence the second file**.  *Neither seat was looking for this class.  A pattern-based census is only ever a census of its pattern, and the way out was two independent narrow greps disagreeing.*  **SCOPE NOTE for whoever takes this:** `dev_jazz.c` is one of the six paths in `tools/est_divergence.txt`, so a change there is SEC-only and does not owe an `est/` counterpart -- unlike the other two files.  **CONTROL a fix owes:** a per-instance latch must be shown to announce ONCE PER INSTANCE and not once per process -- i.e. a machine with two instances of the device, expecting two messages where the current code emits one.  That is the measurement that distinguishes the repair from a no-op rename.  *** THIS ROW'S OWN COUNT WAS WRONG WHEN FILED -- 23 SITES ACROSS 7 FILES, NOT 10 ACROSS 3.  THAT IS THE THIRD MISCOUNT OF THIS CLASS, AND THIS ONE IS MINE, USING THE DERIVER I WROTE WHILE TELLING OTHERS NOT TO TRANSCRIBE NUMBERS. ***  **The wider deriver:** `grep -rnE 'static int (w|warned|first) *= *[01];|static char [a-z_]+\[' src/devices/*.c`  ->  **23 sites / 7 files**: `dev_osiop.c` **8**, `dev_pcc2.c` 5, `dev_sgi_re.c` 4, `dev_jazz.c` 2, `dev_pvr.c` 2, `dev_disk.c` 1, `dev_ps2_gs.c` 1.  **My deriver matched `static int w = 0` and `static int first = 1` and missed `static int warned = 0`, which is the DOMINANT spelling** -- it accounts for 16 of the 23.  `dev_osiop.c` alone has more sites than my entire filed count, and I never looked at that file.  *** THE LESSON IS ABOUT DERIVERS, NOT ABOUT THIS CLASS.  I filed this row saying "record the deriver rather than the number, because this class has already been miscounted twice" -- and the deriver I recorded was itself too narrow.  A deriver is only a census of its own pattern, exactly like the number it replaces; what it buys is that the NEXT reader can widen it, which is what happened here. ***  *Found because a `pcc2` seat's answer mentioned a `static int warned` site my census did not contain, and I re-ran the grep instead of assuming the seat meant one I already had.*  **`dev_osiop.c` should be looked at first by whoever takes this row**: 8 sites, several commented `#118/#119: was exit(1)`, so it is the same de-fatalisation campaign and the largest single population.

rows.title: a 64-bit guarded value printed through (int) in a KILL diagnostic, so the message can name a value that would NOT have killed -- and at one site names the value the code calls ACCEPTABLE.  A CLASS, censused; derive the population, do not quote it
rows.witness: probe:regress/lca_confwidth_probe.py -- RUNG 3, MEASURED 2026-09-07 on the COMMITTED build (a264a34), unmodified `-E alpha -e alphabook1'.  HEAD 4/6: `kill width' reads 0x0 where 0x100000000 is required, `kill notzero' reds because 0x0 is a value the guard ACCEPTS.  Four controls green.  Artifact: regress/artifacts/lcaconfwidth/probe_head_20260907.out
rows.note:
*** FILED AS ONE SITE IN dev_lca.c; CENSUSED THE SAME DAY AND IT IS A CLASS.  Widened low -> med. ***

THE DERIVERS -- run them, do not trust these numbers, and note they answer DIFFERENT questions:

    # (1) the whole cast population -- mostly HARMLESS and NOT the defect
    grep -rc '(int)idata\|(int) idata' src/devices/*.c | grep -v ':0$'

    # (2) the sharp sub-class: a cast inside a diagnostic at a site that then EXITS
    #     (a python window scan; see the round record for the exact form)

On 2026-08-31 (1) gave 309 casts across 70 device files and (2) gave 45 host-kill sites, about twenty of which carry an explicit full-width guard on idata.

*** MOST OF THE 309 ARE NOT DEFECTS, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT -- an 8- or 16-bit register loses nothing through (int). ***  The defect needs BOTH halves:
  * a guard that tests the FULL 64-bit value -- `idata & ~MASK' or `idata != CONST'; and
  * a diagnostic that prints the TRUNCATED one.
Then a guest write whose only distinguishing bits are above bit 31 dies, while the message reports a value that would have been accepted.

*** THE SHARPEST INSTANCE, VERIFIED BY COMPUTATION AND BY READING THE ARM: dev_pvr.c's `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE && idata != 0x0cff0000)' paired with `(int) idata'. ***  A guest writing 0x1_0cff0000 fails the 64-bit compare and the host dies -- and the message prints 0x0cff0000, **EXACTLY THE VALUE THE CODE SAYS IS ACCEPTABLE**.  So the diagnostic tells a maintainer the guest wrote the correct value and died for it, which sends the investigation in precisely the wrong direction.  dev_lca.c's `idata & ~1' is the same shape, milder: it prints 0x0 for a value whose low half is genuinely zero.

SEVERITY REASONING, stated rather than assumed: none of this changes WHETHER the host dies -- the guards are unchanged and the kills are the kills.  It changes only what the log says about WHY, at the one moment the log is all that survives.  That is why it is med and not high, and why it is a RECORDS-CORRECTNESS defect in product code rather than a control-flow one.

NOT A ONE-LINE SWEEP.  Each site needs its own read: the fix is the format specifier plus a (long long) cast, but which sites are genuinely reachable with a >32-bit datum depends on the register width and the guest paths that reach it, and a blanket edit to 45 diagnostics is exactly the unlicensed addition this project refuses.  The honest first round is the ~20 sites whose guard is demonstrably full-width, ordered by whether a guest can deliver a >32-bit write at all.

Found while checking whether the dev_lca.c site was a one-off, as parallel work during a gate run.
rows.state_note:
*** CODEX REFUSAL #7, 2026-09-07, ON THE `lcaconfwidth` CENSUS BRIEF -- AND MY OWN LAUNCHER
REPORTED IT AS A CLEAN RUN.  Two defects, both mine, both of the check-that-cannot-fail family. ***

    codex rc=1        stdout 0 bytes        stderr 768,161 bytes
    stderr tail:  ERROR: This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk.
    tokens used:  108,432

**The seat did 108k tokens of real work first** -- the stderr shows it reading `dev_osiop.c` and
enumerating diagnostic sites -- and the filter discarded the answer at the end.  So this is not a
seat that declined the task; it is a seat whose completed answer was destroyed on the way out.

**LAUNCHER DEFECT 1: the content check read the WRONG STREAM.**  It grepped the `.txt` for refusal
text.  A content-filter refusal writes NOTHING to stdout and puts the ERROR line on STDERR, so the
check printed `refusal hits: 0` **on a refusal**.  A check that looks in the wrong stream returns
the same answer whether or not the thing it tests is true -- which is the exact shape this project
named after `panel.sh`'s phantom re-fire.

**LAUNCHER DEFECT 2: the script exited 0 while holding `rc=1`.**  It captured codex's status into a
variable, printed it, and then ended on a successful command.  **The harness reported the task
COMPLETED.**  That is the failure-laundered-into-a-clean-completion class, and this project has
three prior instances (a `diff` under `set -e`, a Windows path to `wsl`, a truncated preserved log).

> **BOTH FIXED in `cxlaunch.sh`, which greps BOTH STREAMS and exits 7 on a refusal, 8 on a wall, 6
> on an empty answer with neither, and `rc` otherwise.**  A refused seat can no longer render as a
> completed one.

**THE TRIGGER, added to the recorded set.**  The brief asked, of a kill diagnostic, *"say whether a
64-bit value exists that trips the guard and prints as something the guard would accept -- give the
discriminating value where one exists."*  That is a diagnostic-correctness question, but its SHAPE
is *find the input that defeats the check*, and it sits beside an enumeration of `exit(1)` sites.
**Chain-shaped content, whatever the question form** -- the trigger this project already recorded,
met again.

**ROUTED TO GROK**, which the carrier records as the working path for a refused brief and which has
answered three of them, finding something material in each.

*** GROK CENSUS 2026-09-07 (`regress/artifacts/lcaconfwidth/grok_census_20260907.txt`), after
codex refused the brief.  IT CORRECTED MY COUNT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND NARROWED THE FIX TO TWO
LINES. ***

**MY CENSUS MISSED A SPELLING.**  I grepped `(int)idata`; the tree also writes **`(int) idata`**
with a space.  Real total **309 sites in 70 files**, not 226 -- and 309 itself includes
COMMENTED-OUT casts (`dev_clmpcc.c:125`, `dev_dc7085.c:236`, `dev_dec21143.c:914/1072`), so the live
figure is lower again.

**AND MY PROXIMITY SET WAS SHORT: 18 live sites within +/-3 of an `exit(1)`, not 15.**  The three I
missed are `g2` CHAN_ENABLE, `g2` XFER_ENABLE and the `osiop` default -- a blank line inside the
window is still inside the window.  grok also priced the string-vs-call distinction: a scanner that
counted comment text would report **30** (18 live + 2 commented-out `exit(1)` + 10 `dev_pvr.c`
*"don't exit(1)"* comments).

*** THE FINDING THAT SETS THE DISPOSITION, and it is the opposite of a tree-wide class: ***

    (uint64_t)idata  IS next to a live exit(1) FIVE times, ALL IN dev_lca.c
        225/226  TB_ENA      240/241  W_BASE0     255/256  W_MASK0
        279/280  W_BASE1     294/295  W_MASK1
    (uint32_t)idata  13 sites, NONE within +/-3 of a live exit(1)
    (long)idata       1 site, not near one
    (int32_t) / (unsigned int) idata   0

**Those five LCA guards already print the FULL 64-bit value.**  So `dev_lca.c` is mostly correct
already, and the narrowing print survives at exactly **two** sites in it -- `:205` (IOC_CONF, the
exemplar) and `:313`.  **The repair is two lines in one file, matching the idiom its own siblings
twelve lines away already use.**  That is a transferred warrant from inside the same function, which
is the strongest kind this project recognises, and it makes the sibling-disposition check answer FOR
a local fix here -- the opposite of how it answered for [[sgirebufshiftub]].

**Also found: the filed PVR 'sharpest instance' is ALREADY DE-FATALISED by `#166`** -- the fourth
already-fixed claim surfaced today.

> **ORDERING vs [[lcabadval]]:** that row's witness must match `fatal()` TEXT rather than exit status
> (because the interrupt stubs kill with the same status), and IOC_CONF is one of the arms it would
> read.  With the repair confined to two lines whose siblings already do it right, taking this first
> is cheap and removes the oracle's one unsound arm.

*** REACHABILITY ESTABLISHED BY READING, 2026-09-07 -- so a rung-3 witness is a construction
problem rather than an open question. ***

    alpha_lcareg.h      LCA_IOC_BASE 0x180000000 ; LCA_IOC_CONF = BASE + 0x020 = 0x180000020
    dev_lca.c :359-361  memory_device_register(..., "lca_ioc", LCA_IOC_BASE, 0x20000000,
                        dev_lca_ioc_access, ..., DM_DEFAULT, NULL)   <- NO length constraint
    dev_lca.c :188      idata = memory_readmax64(cpu, data, len)     <- takes the full width
    machine_alpha.c :61 device_add(machine, "lca") -- inside `case ST_ALPHABOOK1:` ONLY

**And the technique is already proven on that exact machine.**  `regress/alpha_harness_probe.py`
ran today on an unmodified `-E alpha -e alphabook1` at **7/9**, with `live`, `exec` and `palgate`
green; it builds K0SEG addresses as `0xfffffc0000000000 | x` and K0SEG translation is
`vaddr & 0x000003ffffffffff`, so `k0(0x180000020)` reaches the register with no page tables.

**The 64-bit question is answered too:** Alpha `STQ` is opcode `0x2d` with `loadstore_type = 3`
(quadword) -- established in the grok harness review against `cpu_alpha_instr.c` -- so a guest `stq`
delivers `len = 8` and `idata` holds bit 32.  **The discriminating store is therefore
`0x100000000` to `k0(0x180000020)`: the guard `idata & ~1` fires, and `(int)idata` prints `0x0` --
a value that same guard ACCEPTS.**

> **THE CONTROL THIS WITNESS OWES, and it is the device form of the trap that nearly voided the
> Alpha harness:** if `k0(0x180000020)` does NOT land on the LCA window, the store goes to unmapped
> space and **nothing happens at all** -- no message, no exit -- which is indistinguishable from
> *the guard did not fire*.  So the probe needs a positive control proving the store reached
> `dev_lca`: a legal `0x1` write that SURVIVES, and/or a read-back of `d->ioc_conf` through
> `LCA_IOC_CONF`.  **That question is out to the grok seat rather than settled here**, because
> whether either is sufficient alone is exactly the judgement this project keeps getting wrong.

*Design brief: `regress/artifacts/lcaconfwidth/WITNESS_brief.md`.  Sent to grok rather than codex --
codex refused the sibling census brief on its content filter, and the shape 'find the value that
defeats the check' is the recorded trigger even when the subject is a printf format specifier.*

*** GROK WITNESS DESIGN, 2026-09-07 (`grok_witness2_20260907.txt`).  VERDICT: CONSTRUCTIBLE as a
rung-3 witness on stock `alphabook1`.  It corrected FOUR of my premises, one of which was a wrong
record in this row's own OUTSTANDING_BUGS entry. ***

**1. THE RECOMMENDED FIX WAS WRONG, AND SO WAS ITS WARRANT.**  The entry said `0x%llx` with a
`(long long)` cast, *"the file's own idiom elsewhere"*.  `dev_lca.c` uses **`PRIx64` five times and
`%llx` never**, and the siblings **KEEP** the cast as `(uint64_t)idata`.  My design brief compounded
it by saying to DROP the cast -- a third wrong form.  Corrected in place.

**2. `load_const` CANNOT BUILD EITHER OPERAND.**  LDA/LDAH make 32-bit sign-extended constants; the
K0SEG address needs bits 63..42 and the test value needs bit 32.  **A probe using `load_const` for
either is not this witness.**  The working bootstrap is the one the Alpha harness already uses:
`put d` the 64-bit words into RAM below 64 MB, then guest `ldq` them while `ptbr` is still 0.

**3. THE MISS MODE IS NOT ONLY 'UNMAPPED -> NOTHING'.**  Offset 0 is `LCA_IOC_BASE` (HAE), which
`break`s with no kill -- so a store to `k0(0x180000000)` is **silent while INSIDE the LCA window**.
Unmapped and HAE both read back 0, which is why the control has to distinguish them.

**4. TWO ROUTES THAT LOOK LIKE CONTROLS AND ARE NOT:**
  * **debugger `dump` cannot read the register.**  `dump` calls `memory_rw` with `NO_EXCEPTIONS`, and
    LCA is `DM_DEFAULT` rather than `DM_READS_HAVE_NO_SIDE_EFFECTS`, so the handler is **SKIPPED** and
    the caller gets the pre-zeroed buffer -- *the unmapped signature, produced by a hit.*
  * **`put d` of the killing value is not rung-3.**  `store_64bit_word` goes through `memory_rw` with
    `CACHE_DATA` and no `NO_EXCEPTIONS`, so it DOES enter the handler and `exit(1)` from the
    debugger -- a real kill, by no guest instruction.

> **THE CONTROL THAT WORKS: a guest `stq` of `0x1` followed by a guest `ldq`, same decode, BEFORE
> the killing store.**  It is the analogue of the Alpha harness's `swpctx mapped` row.  Neither it
> nor the kill text is sufficient alone -- the round-trip proves the window is THIS arm and not HAE
> or unmapped; the text `IOC_CONF: 0x0` proves the arm fired and that a 32-bit zero store could not
> have produced that pair.

**Q3 CONFIRMED IN DETAIL, and it hardens S2:** `stq` is opcode `0x2d` -> `loadstore_type 3` -> `LS_Q`;
`host_store` is NULL for a device page, so it falls to `LS_GENERIC_N` and calls `memory_rw(..., 8,
MEM_WRITE)`; the memblock granule is 1 MB so `0x20+8` crosses nothing; Alpha is little-endian and
`memory_readmax64` rebuilds the value.  **And the guard's own arithmetic is load-bearing:** `~1` is a
signed `int` (-2) converting to `0xfffffffffffffffe`, **so it sees bit 32 -- `~1U` would NOT, and
that is a different mutant worth building.**  The same function already compares against
`0x300800000ULL`, so 64-bit values are this handler's native width.

**One honest weakening:** `(int)0x100000000 == 0` is IMPLEMENTATION-DEFINED, not guaranteed by C99.
GCC/Clang truncate, so the witness holds on this build -- but the row should not claim a language
guarantee.

*** AND THE 309 FIGURE WAS ALREADY IN THIS ROW'S OWN ENTRY, DATED 2026-08-31. ***  I ran a census
today, got 226, treated it as new, and was corrected to 309 by a seat -- while
`OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md` had recorded **"309 casts across 70 device files"** five days earlier, with
its deriver.  **The unread-review class, in the file I was writing about.**  (Its companion figure,
45 host-kill sites, is not in conflict with today's 18: the two used different window sizes, and
neither states one, which is the reason they cannot be reconciled.)

*** WITNESS BUILT AND RUN THE SAME HOUR THE DESIGN LANDED.  HEAD 4/6. ***

    live          alive   alive          ok    the control session survives the legal write
    ioc rt        0x1     0x1            ok    guest stq 0x1 then guest ldq, SAME decode
    kill fired    yes     yes            ok    the IOC_CONF arm announced -- not HAE, not unmapped
    kill width    0x0     0x100000000    FAIL  the message must name the value that ACTUALLY killed
    kill notzero  0x0     NOT 0x0        FAIL  0x0 is a value this guard ACCEPTS
    died          died    died           ok    exit(1) really ran

All four of grok's design corrections are implemented and each is a comment in the probe: the
64-bit operands are planted with `put d` and loaded with `ldq` (`load_const` cannot build them);
the read-back is a guest `ldq` (debugger `dump` would skip a `DM_DEFAULT` handler and hand back the
pre-zeroed buffer -- the unmapped signature from a hit); the killing store is a guest `stq` (a
`put d` would kill from the debugger and not be rung-3); and `ioc rt` distinguishes the real arm
from HAE at offset 0, which `break`s silently INSIDE the window.

*** AND MY FIRST DRAFT HAD THE ORACLE POLARITY BACKWARDS -- it scored 6/6 on the committed build. ***
It asserted the DEFECT as the passing state, so it read as success and would have gone RED the
moment the bug was fixed.  **The ladder requires a witness to show the symptom pre-fix and go green

*** PASS-1 AUDIT 2026-09-07 (codex, `regress/artifacts/pcc2c040kill/codex_pass1_20260907.txt`).
THE CENTRAL PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION MAKES THE DEFECT SIMPLER AND WORSE. ***

**VERDICT:** *"DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE for unsupported C040 delivery.  Survival is a nonvacuous
oracle here, but cannot establish interrupt correctness."*

*** THE CORRECTION: *"the GENCTL write itself immediately calls the terminating helper.  Arming and
termination occur within that access; subsequent SCC traffic is unnecessary."* ***

**Line 459 IS `reassert_interrupts()` inside the GENCTL byte-write arm.**  So the whole
`SCCRXIACK`-plus-OpenBSD-`cl.c` entry story -- which this row records as a NEW FACT improving
reachability, and which the brief built its S4 around -- is UNNECESSARY.  **A single legal byte write
of 0x04 to offset 0x02 terminates the emulator on the spot.**  No second access, no driver, no
interrupt.

*That does not make the earlier finding wrong -- SCCRXIACK really does run the helper with no
direction test, and that really is routine traffic.  It makes it SUPERFLUOUS: the row had found a
long road to a place reachable in one step, and nobody noticed the short one because the long one was
interesting.*

**CONFIRMED BY READING, beyond what the brief asserted:**
  * `pcctwo_reg[]` holds **`uint8_t`**; GENCTL rejects non-byte writes, but the accepted byte write
    **stores `idata` WITHOUT MASKING** and immediately calls the helper.  **No read-only treatment
    prevents the bit being stored**, and the header explicitly permits byte accesses.
  * The ten call sites are confirmed with their contexts -- 383 `pcctwo_interrupt_common()`, 400 the
    device TICK (unconditionally), 459 GENCTL write, 551 T1ICR/T2ICR, 574 SCCICR, 588 SCCTX,
    602 SCCRX, 609 SCCRXIACK (no direction test), 622 SCSIICR, 662 MASK -- all reaching **one shared
    terminating branch**.
  * **THE CONDITION IS NOT STICKY:** a GENCTL write CLEARING C040 stores the cleared value before
    calling the helper.  So the state is recoverable in principle -- and unrecoverable in practice,
    because the arming write has already terminated the process.
  * **`400` is the device TICK, called unconditionally.**  So even a guest that arms C040 and then
    does nothing at all is terminated at the next tick.  That is worth stating separately: it removes
    the last version of the story in which the guest must go on to do something.

**Q4 ANSWERED, and it is the opposite of the neighbouring rounds' problem:** *"Survival is a
nonvacuous oracle here."*  This project has measured that survival rows at REFUSAL-EFFECT sites are
vacuous by construction -- guarded and unguarded code both survive.  Here the pre-fix build genuinely
does NOT survive, so survival discriminates.  **But it cannot establish interrupt correctness**, which
is the second half of the disposition question and needs its own row.

**THE WITNESS IS NOW TRIVIALLY CHEAP.**  This row's `witness` field says a rung-3 attempt *"looks
cheap (one more session in `regress/pcc2_width_probe.py`, which already byte-writes this register on
this machine)"* -- and with arming-equals-termination it is cheaper still: **one byte write and
observe that the process is gone.**  The field's promise that it says `not yet done` rather than
`did not think to ask` is now cashable in a single session.

*And a note on the brief: it was written with C5 applied FROM THE START -- neutral register, scoped
reading, no chain -- on a subject (process termination) that is trigger 1's own vocabulary.  **It was
not refused.**  First time today I wrote one that way instead of learning it from a refusal.*

**READY TO CLAIM AS A ROUND, 2026-09-07.**  The stated blocker was *"next round after
pcc2widthkills closes"*; that row now carries `commits=b78bb0f`, so the width fix is IN THE TREE and
only its formal closure is outstanding.  Nothing about this defect depends on that closure.

**THE WITNESS IS ONE SESSION IN AN EXISTING PROBE.**  `regress/pcc2_width_probe.py` already drives
GENCTL byte writes on this machine and carries an authoring-time assertion, `c040ok()`, whose whole
job is to keep its lanes (`0xd9`/`0x40`) OFF this path.  **So the probe already proves the access
works and already knows the bit is dangerous** -- the witness is the same access with the bit set,
and the oracle is that the process is gone.

  *That assertion is worth keeping rather than deleting when the row is added: it protects the WIDTH
  rows from wandering onto this path, which is a different job from the new row deliberately
  stepping onto it.  A row that turns the guard off for the whole file would re-open exactly what
  `c040ok()` was written to prevent.*

**FIX SHAPE, from the audit:** DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE, with its own latch bit -- the same
per-instance reasoning as `dev_sgi_re`'s bits, since a shared latch is silenced by the other site's
ordinary traffic.  **The open design question is Q2, which the audit did not settle from the source:**
after declining, does the helper fall through to the normal level recalculation, or return having
asserted nothing?  Those differ in what the guest observes, and the answer decides whether the round
owes a second row on interrupt behaviour -- which the verdict's own second clause anticipates
(*"survival ... cannot establish interrupt correctness"*).

*** WITNESS DESIGN REVIEWED AND NOT RATIFIED.  grok,
`regress/artifacts/pcc2c040kill/grok_witness_20260907.txt`. ***

**VERDICT:** *"NOT RATIFY as proposed.  A guest `st.b` of 0x04 at GENCTL is a sound CORE of a rung-3
witness of this kill.  Survival-only, in `pcc2_width_probe.py`, with no same-decode preset and no
site-attribution, is not.  **That is the same class as the design you asked me to assume: the

the required attribution is specific:

*** THE TICK CLAIM IS VACUOUS, AND SO IS 'TEN CALL SITES' AS A STATEMENT OF HAZARD.  My record,

grok called S3's tick claim *"possibly sequencing-wrong"*.  Checked, and it is wrong:

  * `DEVICE_TICK(pcc2)` really does call `reassert_interrupts(d)` unconditionally -- that part of my

  * **but GENCTL is written in exactly ONE place** -- its own case arm -- and that arm calls

**So the process always terminates on the ARMING WRITE ITSELF, and the tick can never be the first
hit.**  *"Even a guest that arms C040 and then does nothing is terminated at the next tick"* describes
a state that cannot be reached: there is no interval during which C040 is set and the process is
alive.

*** AND THE SHARPER CORRECTION: 'TEN CALL SITES' IS TRUE AND MISLEADING. ***  All ten reach one
shared branch, which is what the audit established and which stands.  But **nine of them are
unreachable AS A FIRST HIT**, because the only way the guard's condition becomes true is a write that
immediately calls the helper itself.  **The defect has exactly ONE reachable entry.**

**WHAT THIS CHANGES:**
  * the WITNESS is simpler than the design assumed -- one session, one store; **no tick row is owed**,
    and a row waiting for a tick would wait forever;

    framing was inflated: ten sites reads as ten ways in, and there is one;
  * the FIX is unaffected -- de-fatalising the shared branch covers all ten regardless of which can
    reach it first, and that is the right place to repair it.

*This is the third over-broad claim of mine this session and the same shape as the others: a census I
ran correctly, restated as a claim about REACHABILITY that the census does not support.  The count of
call sites answers "how many places call this helper"; it does not answer "how many can arrive here
first", and I wrote the second while measuring the first.*

*** grok's CASE, and it is the better-evidenced of the two: ***
  * **C040 is R/W in the board manual.**  `OPER R/W` on that bit in VMESBCP2 -- the manual this
    project already has at `_scratchpad/vmesbcp2.pdf`.  It is **not an unlisted offset, not a
    read-only bit, and not a wide write with a lane hazard**.

    **None of those is a legal R/W bit at a listed offset.**

    announce); `#432` TIMER_EXTERNAL (a legal named encoding that hit `exit(1)`); and

    asserting INT is A WRONG RECORD IN PRODUCT CODE** -- the same shape the IRQEnable round refused,
    printing "unimplemented; ignored" about a path that is implemented and is not ignored.
  * **C040 selects which PINS carry a level this emulator does not model.  It does not change the
    level itself.**  So storing the bit and using the existing 88100 INT path is a no-op relative to
    every observable the emulator has -- which is ACCEPT, not a refusal.

  compute the level and assert on the existing path, and C040 does not change that level.  So the

asserting**, which is exactly the Q2 the audit left open.

hold-for-adjudication directive is what keeps it from being settled by whichever seat I asked
first. ***

**FOR THE ADJUDICATION:** the question is not "decline or accept" in the abstract.  It is whether a
LEGAL R/W BIT whose modelled effect is nil should be STORED (accept) or REFUSED (decline), and
whether an announce that describes an unmodelled PIN SELECTION while the INT path is used is a true
record or a false one.

*** THE RUNG-3 WITNESS IS BUILT AND MEASURED.  `regress/pcc2_c040_probe.py`, 3/4 on the committed
build, artifact `regress/artifacts/pcc2c040kill/witness_HEAD_20260907.raw`. ***

    c040 kill      died(exit1)  alive        THE DEFECT -- RED, as clause (i) requires

rows.note: *** THE ROW WAS FILED WITH AN EMPTY NOTE AND ZERO ENTRIES; the analysis below was written 2026-09-06 from the source and from the board manual that landed on disk the day before, NOT from the filing. ***  PATH, verified by reading: the write arm (anchor `case PCCTWO_GENCTL:') declines only WIDE writes -- that guard is #500's -- so a ONE-BYTE write passes it, is stored VERBATIM WITH NO MASK (`d->pcctwo_reg[relative_addr] = idata;`), and the arm then calls `reassert_interrupts(d)`, whose first statement is `if (d->pcctwo_reg[PCCTWO_GENCTL] & PCC2_C040) { fatal(...); exit(1); }`.  PCC2_C040 is 0x04 (mvme_pcctworeg.h).  GENCTL resets to 0x00, so the bit is clear until something writes it.  A single `st.b 0x04' to 0xfff42002 therefore ends the host process.  PRIMARY SOURCE, and it is new on disk (_scratchpad/vmesbcp2.txt, the MVME187 board manual, added 2026-09-05; anchor `General Control Register'): the register is at $FFF42002, 8 bits, layout DR0 / four READ-ONLY bits / C040 / MIEN / FAST -- so the model's constants agree with the manual -- and C040 is documented as *"CPU040.  This bit should be set when the MPU is from the M68000 family.  It should be cleared when the MPU is an MC88100.  When the bit is set, EIPL<2..0>* are driven as outputs which carry the priority encoded interrupt request from the PCCchip2 interrupt sources."*  The only machine that instantiates this device is MVME187, whose own comment in machine_mvme88k.c cites the installation guide for its `88100 MPU' -- so the manual says the bit SHOULD be clear here, which is what makes the TODO defensible as a TODO.  But NOTHING IN THE MANUAL GIVES THE CHIP A WAY TO REFUSE THE WRITE: setting C040 on an 88100 board is a misconfiguration that re-purposes three pins, not an access violation.  The model turns it into the death of the emulator.  REACH IS WIDER THAN THE WRITE ARM: `reassert_interrupts' has TEN call sites, and two are not guest accesses at all -- DEVICE_TICK(pcc2) calls it unconditionally every tick, and pcctwo_interrupt_common() calls it on every device interrupt assert/deassert.  There is no state in which C040 is set and the machine keeps running.  A SECOND, SMALLER FINDING IN THE SAME ARM: the manual marks bits 6..3 read-only and the model stores the whole byte unmasked, so a write of 0x78 sets four bits hardware would leave clear and a later read returns them.  The sibling arm one case below already carries the idiom (`case PCCTWO_VECBASE:` stores `idata & 0xf0` and announces the remainder).  Unmeasured either way -- no MVME187 boot runs in this harness.  OPTION SET, all six named before choosing (the carrier's rule): delete / decline silent / decline + latched announce (the file already has the machinery -- pcc2_width_decline() and the PCC2_W_* bit enum) / ACCEPT / fault / backed accept.  THE DECIDING QUESTION IS ACCEPT vs DECLINE: the model already computes the interrupt level and C040 only changes WHICH PINS carry it, and the model has no pins -- so if there is no observable difference inside this emulator between C040 set and clear, a decline would ship a wrong record in product code (announcing an ignore that did not happen) and ACCEPT is right.  Naming that observable is what the assess panel is for.  DE-ESCALATION COST, stated before the design is chosen: removing the host-fatal guard deletes the accidental tripwire, so the detector owes an ACCEPT-side row that REDDENS under the smallest realistic growth mutant -- a byte write of 0x04 serviced, the machine surviving, and a subsequent tick not killing.  Witness looks cheap at rung 3: regress/pcc2_width_probe.py already drives byte writes at this register on this machine, so it is one more session in an existing probe rather than new plumbing.  Assess brief written and panel-ready: _scratchpad/pcc2c040/brief_pcc2c040_assess.md (not yet fired -- a kill table held the machine).  A TRAP FOR A LATER ROUND, found while checking the constant against the manual and recorded so nobody re-derives it: mvme_pcctworeg.h defines the C040 bit TWICE, under two spellings with DIFFERENT values -- `PCC2_C040 0x04' (anchor `#define PCC2_C040') and `PCC2_GENCTL_C040 0x03' (anchor `#define PCC2_GENCTL_C040', in a second block at the end of the header alongside PCC2_GENCTL_FAST 0x01 and PCC2_GENCTL_IEN 0x02).  The manual's bit table settles it: C040 is 0x04 and the model uses the right one -- `PCC2_GENCTL_C040' has ZERO consumers in this tree (grep -rn PCC2_GENCTL_C040 src/ returns only its own definition).  It is a vendored third-party header, so this is upstream's inconsistency and not the fork's, and nothing is edited; but a future round reaching for the obvious-looking name would silently test FAST|MIEN instead of C040.

PASS 8: **NO-GO** -- three findings, and I VERIFIED ALL THREE FROM THE TREE AND THE MANUAL ON DISK before accepting any of them (the seat cited a web copy of the manual; the check used _scratchpad/mc88100.txt).  (1) FLOOR GAP, and it is the one that matters: **the repair varies PSR only on the NON-TRAP side.**  errind and errc both enter through `!is_trap', so a disjunct on the TRAP side -- `if (!is_trap || !(cr[PSR] & M88K_PSR_IND))' -- is predicted 46/46: every one of the eleven frozen-trap rows enters with PSR 0x8000000b, so the added disjunct is false for all of them, and errind cannot see it because `!is_trap' is already true there.  The same escape exists for C set, SFD1 clear, MODE clear and SER set.  STATIC PREDICTION, not measured by the seat, and it owes a build.  (2) **SER IS NOT AN 88110-ONLY BIT AND THE PROBE'S DISCLOSURE SAYS IT IS.**  VERIFIED against the primary source on disk: _scratchpad/mc88100.txt, anchor `SER - Serial Mode', says *"This bit is set by software as appropriate"* -- in the MC88100 manual.  The fork's vendored header carries `#define M88K_PSR_SER 0x20000000 /* 88110 serial mode */`, which is upstream's error and which my disclosure copied.  And m88k_stcr's PSR case stores `value' verbatim after the BO / MXM / MODE checks, so a guest CAN set SER.  Every current row has SER clear, so `if (!is_trap && !(cr[PSR] & M88K_PSR_SER))' is predicted 46/46 too.  (3) TWO WRONG RECORDS IN THE SHIPPED PROBE, both confirmed by reading: the contract's disclosure line still lists OVERFLOW x {C, IND} as uncovered when `ovfc' (C set) and `indclr' (IND clear) BOTH fault at the OVERFLOW arm (`add 0x7fffffff + 1' -> V_OVF) and are therefore exactly that cell; and the trailing comment the v12 edit claimed to remove from REFATAL_EXPECT IS STILL THERE -- v12 added a COPY above the EXPECT_VECTOR line and never deleted the original, so the file now carries it twice and the surviving one describes a boolean dict as if it held vectors.  DISPOSITION: pass 8 does NOT close the chain.  Passes 7 and 8 have now both found {re-route} x {PSR bit} cells, so by the class-closure amendment the next repair owes the FULL product -- {is_trap, non-trap} x {MODE, SFD1, IND, C, SER} x {both polarities} -- in ONE diff, with the two record errors fixed in the same pass. PASS 8: **ONE MORE REPAIR -- and it SETTLED THE PANEL'S DISAGREEMENT BY MEASUREMENT, which is the only way this project resolves one.**  codex and grok predicted a floor gap; kimi enumerated four families and reported ZERO survivors.  Opus BUILT the mutants: **THREE CLEAN SWEEPS AT 46/46 ON THE SHIPPED COMPOSITE**, row-for-row identical to BASE -- `case ILLEGAL_INTEGER_DIVIDE: implemented = (PSR & IND) != 0`, `case ERROR: implemented = !(PSR & C)`, and `case BOUNDS_CHECK_VIOLATION: implemented = (PSR & IND) != 0`.  So the class is at the SWITCH-1 ARMS, not only at the re-route where pass 7 repaired it.  Its polarity twins prove the mutants are not inert: CTL_DIV0INDINV 23/46, CTL_OVFNOC 45/46 (ovfc), CTL_DIV0SFD1 45/46 (trapfrozen8). rows.title: wdcbeoddtail  on a BIG-ENDIAN machine a 16-bit data-port read that pops the last valid byte plus the empty-ring sentinel folds the sentinel INTO the valid byte -- (v << 8) + 0xffff...ff = (v << 8) - 1, so the guest reads v-1 (0x00 becomes 0xff; a borrow can alter two valid bytes on a 4-byte read); the LE arm only pollutes the padding byte
rows.witness: none
rows.note: DEFECT, MEDIUM (re-rank HIGH if a real driver is measured popping the odd tail: the tell is the `[ wdc: WARNING! someone is reading too much from the wdc inbuf! ]' line in a `evbmips -e maltabe' boot log with an ATAPI image).  Site: dev_wdc.c `case wd_data:' BE assembly `odata = (odata << 8) + wdc_get_inbuf(d)' with `wdc_get_inbuf' returning (uint64_t) -1 on an empty ring; memory_writemax64 (BE) hands buf[0] bits 15:8.  Enumerated by Fable: 2-byte/1 valid -> [v-1, 0xff]; v = 0x00 -> [0xff, 0xff]; 4-byte with valid 0x12 0x00 -> [0x11, 0xff, 0xfe, 0xff].  Reachable: MALTA BE (machine_evbmips.c `MALTA (evbmips, big endian)') gets the wdc via bus_pci.c `PCIINIT(piix4_ide)'; odd lengths from `case SCSICMD_INQUIRY:' (retlen = cmd[4], min 36); the model reports the ODD byte count unpadded in wd_cyl_lo/hi, so whether a driver pops the tail is arch-specific (OpenBSD 2.2 isa/wdc.c uses bus_space_read_raw_multi_2 with the odd len).  WITNESS OWED AT RUNG 3 before any edit: `evbmips -e maltabe' + ATAPI image, INQUIRY-37 CDB via six 16-bit data-port stores then nineteen 16-bit loads -- pre-fix the 19th returns [v-1, 0xff], post-fix intact; LE control on `-e malta'; the over-read latch line is the device signature.  OPTION SET: (1) mask each pop `& 0xff' at the assembly (no other consumer changes); (2) return 0 on empty -- changes the LE pad 0xff -> 0x00 AND reds the shipped `overread -1' row (oracle-correction ORDER rule applies); (3) pad odd DATA-IN transfers to an even count and report it (BELIEVED: the ATAPI word-transfer rule; no standard on disk).  Detector: the differential's `row_odd_width' checks counters only and its memory_writemax64 stub always serialises LE -- both must change for an offline row; discharges part of wdcletwins and wdcprobeendian.  Provenance: retrospective re-check (owner directive 2026-09-04) batch 3a -- GPT-6 Astra (codex, max effort) read-only review, adjudicated by Fable 5.1; artifacts regress/artifacts/retro_20260905/batch3a_wdc/ (astra_batch3a.txt, fable_adj_batch3a.md). rows.title: wdcpktstatus  a REJECTED or CHECK-CONDITION ATAPI packet command completes with the ERR bit CLEAR (status 0x50): `atapi_st->status' is never consulted, `d->error' stays 0, and the #416 CHECK CONDITION repair never reached the IDE/ATAPI path -- an out-of-range READ(10) is delivered as zeros with success
rows.witness: none
rows.note: DEFECT, MEDIUM.  Read by Fable: `wdc_command' sets `d->error = 0'; the PACKET dispatch calls diskimage_scsicommand once; on res == 0 -> PHASE_COMPLETED + int_assert, on res == 1 it tests only data_in != NULL; no `atapi_st->status' read anywhere in dev_wdc.c; `status_byte' ORs WDCS_ERR only from d->error.  Backend (diskimage_scsicmd.c): return 0 only for structural errors; return 1 for everything else INCLUDING CHECK CONDITION (`SCSI READ: refusing oversized transfer', status[0] = 0x02) and the out-of-range READ (`diskimage__return_check_condition' after memset 0 -- the #416 repair whose own comment says it alone reports a successful read of zeros); an unknown opcode returns 1 with no data -> PHASE_COMPLETED, no ERR, no message.  Guest expectation CONFIRMED on disk: _guest-src-openbsd22 sys/dev/isa/wdc.c `case PHASE_COMPLETED:' reads wd_error only `if (st & WDCS_ERR)'; atapi/atapiconf.c `atapi_sense(acp, error >> 4, flags)' decodes the sense key from bits 7:4 -- with ERR clear the guest treats the command as SUCCESS.  WITNESS OWED AT RUNG 3: landisk wdc rig (wdc_flood_probe.py machinery) or maltabe, READ(10) beyond the image end or opcode 0xff; read wd_status/wd_error: pre-fix 0x50/0x58 and 0x00, post-fix ERR set + non-zero error register; controls: a valid INQUIRY shows DRQ with ERR clear; an out-of-range CHS READ on a plain disk shows ABRT.  OPTION SET: (1) d->error = WDCE_ABRT on res == 0 and on status[0] == 0x02; (2) mirror the backend's sense key into bits 7:4 ((key << 4) | WDCE_ABRT, ILLEGAL REQUEST -> 0x54) via a diskimage sense_key accessor -- the option under which the guest's NOT_READY/UNIT_ATTENTION/RETRY logic works; (3) on CHECK CONDITION with a zeroed data_in, complete with ERR and NO DATA-IN phase.  Register-layout conformance to the standard is BELIEVED (no ATA document on disk); the in-tree guest's expectation is CONFIRMED.  Provenance: retrospective re-check (owner directive 2026-09-04) batch 3a -- GPT-6 Astra (codex, max effort) read-only review, adjudicated by Fable 5.1; artifacts regress/artifacts/retro_20260905/batch3a_wdc/ (astra_batch3a.txt, fable_adj_batch3a.md). rows.title: m88kdslotshadow  cpu_m88k.c: for a precise fault in the delay slot of a taken br.n the else-arm sets SNIP = slot+4, SFIP = target (upstream's 'Perhaps something like this could work'); the MC88100 UM says the shadows copy NIP = target, FIP = target+4 -- rte then executes slot+4 (skipped by the branch) before the target, or the target twice when target == slot+4

rows.note: DEFECT by reading (Fable review seat, codex, grok on the #502 pass 2; kimi DISSENTS -- see below).  Pre-existing upstream; made reachable by ORDINARY compiled code by #502 (before it, every trap-like fault in a delay slot stopped the machine at the fallback; only a trap >= 128 in a slot reached the else-arm).  Manual: pointer definitions mc88100.txt:2097-2104 (FIP = XIP + d26 while the branch is in XIP; one stage later, while the SLOT executes, NIP = target, FIP = target+4), :4207-4208, :8898-8902, Table 6-3; X(rte) (anchor `The NIP instruction should first be executed') executes the SNIP instruction then jumps to SFIP when SFIP != SNIP+4.  The fork's own DATA_ACCESS delay-slot arm two lines up already has the manual's shape (SNIP = delay_target | V; SFIP = SNIP + 4) -- the in-tree precedent, exercised by OpenBSD on every page fault in a delay slot.  #502's detector row `dslot' PINS THE ARM AS IMPLEMENTED (labelled so in the probe: br.n +16 -> SNIP 0x1000e, SFIP 0x10016); when this round lands the row is RE-PINNED FIRST (oracle-correction rule: re-pin, measure HEAD red, then fix).  Rows for this round: dslot16 (fork today SNIP 0x1000e/SFIP 0x10016; manual 0x10016/0x1001a; a no-special-case arm 0x1000e/0x10012 -- three distinct pairs, one row discriminates all three) and dslotnt (a NOT-taken bcnd.n with a faulting slot: fork SFIP == SNIP; manual SFIP = SNIP+4), plus a handler-RETURN row (rte + counters at fallthrough/target/target+4 -- codex) that observes the execution sequence, not only the registers.  KIMI'S DISSENT, verbatim: The manual's SNIP/SFIP pipeline-shadow semantics at 6.4.3.1.2/.3 do support the code's else-arm: SNIP = shadow of NIP, SFIP = "the target of a jump or branch instruction."  The pre-existing DATA_ACCESS-in-delay-slot arm, SNIP = delay_target, is the odd one out against that reading.  The two readings predict DIFFERENT post-rte execution sequences, so the handler-return row settles it by measurement.  Severity MEDIUM by reasoning (no OpenBSD luna88k source on disk to show a guest path that depends on it).  Provenance: #502 pass 2 (fable_p2.md finding 1; codex pass-2 answer; grok verdict) and the #502 adjudication pass.

rows.title: mipstiny  cpu_mips_coproc.c fpu_subst_tiny(): does classifying tininess on the ENCODED destination word match the MIPS rule, or is after-rounding tininess judged with an UNRESTRICTED exponent range?  THE SOURCE ARGUES ONE WAY AND A REVIEWING SEAT THE OTHER -- unresolved, for the flagship seat
rows.witness: none -- READ only.  No emulator run was made by either side; the seat says so itself (`no emulator witness was run').
rows.hold_question: The fork's own comment and the reviewing seat give OPPOSITE readings of the same MIPS sentence, and both are reasoned.  Which is right: is IEEE/MIPS after-rounding tininess judged on the value rounded to the destination PRECISION with an UNBOUNDED exponent (the seat), or on the word as ENCODED in the destination format (the source)?  They differ exactly on the sliver where a value rounds UP into the normal range only because the subnormal encoding has fewer significand bits.  Second: if the seat is right, is the divergence reachable by any OS in the tree -- the seat found no setter for the flush control in the supplied sources and recommends documented-only pending an OS-use witness rather than claiming unreachability.
rows.note: RAISED by the retrospective batch-12 review and RE-FIRED as a standalone question to GPT-6 Astra at max effort on 2026-09-06; its answer is preserved at _scratchpad/codex_mipstiny/ANSWER_astra_20260906.txt.  *** FILED AS A DISAGREEMENT, NOT AS A DEFECT, BECAUSE THE SOURCE CARRIES A REASONED COUNTER-POSITION AND NOBODY HAS MEASURED EITHER. ***  THE SEAT'S POSITION: MIPS specifies after-rounding tininess with an UNRESTRICTED exponent range, and `fpu_subst_tiny` incorrectly equates that with the destination word coming out subnormal.  Discriminating input 0x1.fffffep-127 = (2^24 - 1) * 2^-150 through cvt.s.d under round-to-nearest with the flush control set and the underflow and inexact traps disabled: exactly 24 significant bits, so it is unchanged by rounding at unbounded exponent and is tiny; but the subnormal encoding at 2^-126 has fewer significand bits, so it rounds UP to FLT_MIN and encodes NORMAL -- and the fork therefore substitutes nothing where the seat says MIPS requires a substitution.  THE SOURCE'S POSITION, which the seat did not quote and which I read before filing (anchor `Classification is done on the ENCODED word'): *"Classification is done on the ENCODED word, not on the host double, so it is tininess AFTER rounding, which is what MIPS specifies: the exact upper midpoint 2^-126 - 2^-150 rounds to FLT_MIN under nearest and is then a NORMAL result that must not be substituted at all."*  So the fork made this choice DELIBERATELY and argues it IS the MIPS rule.  The two positions turn on one question -- whether the rounding that decides tininess is done at unbounded exponent or in the destination encoding -- and that question is settled by the manual, not by either party's confidence.  WHAT THE SEAT ALSO ESTABLISHED, and it is useful whichever way the main question goes: the guest write that enables the flush control is accepted (`case COPz_CTCz`); the operand is normal in double precision so the operand-denormal trap does not intercept it; the destination-register difference would be observable; and OpenBSD 2.2's arc/pmax `machdep.c` zeroes the whole control word at `setregs`, with NO setter for the flush bit found anywhere in the supplied sources.  Its own recommendation is documented-only pending an OS-use witness, on the ground that calling it unreachable would overstate the evidence -- which is the right shape.  AND IT REFUTED THE CHEAP CROSS-CHECK: the SuperH model's denormal-mode policy is NOT a parallel that can justify the MIPS one.  It cites sh7750_hardware.txt (anchor `6.7.1 Rounding Mode and Underflow Flag'), which discusses a result that IS normal after rounding while an underflow is still signalled -- different rules that happen to agree on the tested inputs.  OWED: the manual sentence itself, quoted with its anchor from mips-iv.txt / mips64_volII.txt / mips32_volII.txt, by a seat that has not already taken a side.  Ranked LOW until then -- if the seat is right this is a real conformance divergence on a sliver, and if the source is right the batch-12 record needs a line saying so, because an uncorrected claim gets reused.

entries.note: GPT-6 Astra, max effort, fired standalone after the batch-12 review raised it.  Traced the source and the manuals, gave the discriminating input and its exact rational arithmetic, established the control-bit reachability and the absence of any OS setter in the supplied sources, and refuted the SuperH cross-check with a specific anchor.  Honest about its limit: `no emulator witness was run'.  It did NOT quote the fork's own counter-argument in the same function's comment, which is why this row is filed as unresolved rather than as a defect.

rows.title: m88k SFRZ re-route, TRAP side: MODE and SFD1 do not vary across the fourteen trap rows, so a widened inner guard escapes the 57-row detector
rows.witness: detector:regress/m88k_exc_probe.py -- rows trapfrozenuser (MODE) and trapfrozensfd1 (SFD1)
rows.state_note:
FILED as clause-(e) DEBT on 2026-09-06 and ADJUDICATED TO FLOOR the same evening by the pass-11 panel; REPAIRED IN-ROUND as L2 (probe v19, 57 -> 59 rows).  The original filing text is preserved below the rule, because a filing that was overturned is part of the record and not an embarrassment to be tidied away.

*** WHY IT IS FLOOR AND NOT DEBT -- TWO INDEPENDENT PRECEDENTS, BOTH FROM THIS ROUND'S OWN RECORDS, BOTH VERIFIED BY OPENING THE ARTIFACT BEFORE ACTING. ***
  * grok: PRETABLE12 graded this EXACT inner `if' as L2 -- its disposition line reads "L2, in-round" -- when     `if (!is_trap || !(PSR & IND))' swept 46/46.  IND, C and SER at this site were then repaired in-round as     floor (trapfrozenind/c/ser).  Grading the remaining two bits at the SAME SITE as debt would be     inconsistent, and would retroactively un-grade three rows this campaign shipped as floor.
  * kimi: ITS VERDICT LINE SAID DEBT AND ITS BODY SAID FLOOR, reaching grok's conclusion by a different     route -- the pass-5 and pass-7 mutants `!is_trap || vector == <class>' condition on `vector', which the     guarded body does not test either, and those were repaired in-round (trapfrozen4/5/6/9, then     trapfrozen450/496).  So the PRACTISED rule already covers fields a mutant can condition on at this guard.
  * minimax voted DEBT and is outvoted BY ARGUMENT, not by count: neither precedent was contested by anyone,     and both are checkable in one grep.

My own reading -- the generating-set letter, `the partitions the guarded body itself tests' -- loses on its own terms, which kimi showed: it would ALSO have made the vector rows debt, and the round shipped those as floor.  The letter was written for idata bits of a device write; here PSR is the GUARD's operand and the value the body writes is `vector = ERROR'.

*** AND MY REACHABILITY ARGUMENT WAS WRONG IN ITS DETAIL, which grok corrected. ***  I claimed the cell is reachable by composing `errpriv' (a frozen handler dropping to user mode) with `trapfrozen128' (a frozen user trap).  `trapfrozen128' is a SUPERVISOR trap NAMING vector 128, MODE=1 -- not a user-mode trap -- and `errpriv''s handler does stcr then ldcr, which raises PRIVILEGE with is_trap == 0 and never reaches a trap at all.  The cell IS reachable, by a different construction: `[STCR_R5_CR1, TB1_0_R3_128]' with r5 = PSR_FRZUSER and **r3 = 0x11**, because bit 0 must be SET or the tb1 does not trap and the row is silently inert.

THE REPAIR: two rows in trapfrozenind's shape, so they inherit its frozen-shadow expectations and its no-refatal channel with no new machinery.  `trapfrozenuser' puts MODE clear at the trap side (a frozen handler drops to user mode, then traps at vector 128 -- >= USER_TRAPS_START so the fallback does not claim it, and X(tb1) checks privilege only for vector < 128).  `trapfrozensfd1' puts SFD1 clear (PSR_FRZSUP, then the same tb1 naming 7 as trapfrozenind).  CHANNEL: under the mutant a trap that WOULD be exempted is re-routed, so each row moves from DELIVER at its own vector to STOP at 0x50 AND the re-route diagnostic appears where REFATAL_EXPECT says it must not -- two observables, both already read.

*** THIS IS THE FOURTH TIME THIS CHAIN HAS CLOSED AN AXIS AT SOME CELLS AND CALLED THE REST SOMETHING ELSE, AND I DID IT INSIDE THE CENSUS WRITTEN TO END THAT PATTERN. ***  Passes 6, 7, 8 and 9 each found a repair that reproduced the defect it repaired; the cell census was built to make the whole space visible at once, and the filing written from it closed three cells at a site and filed the other two under a different heading.

--- THE ORIGINAL FILING, preserved ---
FILED 2026-09-06 from the #502 pass-10 cell census (regress/artifacts/m88kexcdeliver/derive_cells.py, output CELLCENSUS.out).  DERIVED, NOT MEASURED, and said so.

At the SFRZ re-route's TRAP side every one of the fourteen trap rows carries MODE=1 and SFD1=1.  A widened inner guard -- `if (!is_trap || !(PSR & M88K_PSR_MODE))' -- would therefore be invisible to the shipped instrument.  THE CELL IS REACHABLE, and both halves already exist in the probe separately: a frozen handler can drop to user mode (errpriv/errunimpl do exactly that, via PSR_FRZUSER) and a user trap at a vector >= 128 is a genuine trap (trapfrozen128).  No row combines them.  The SFD1 cell is the same shape via PSR_FRZSUP, which errdiv0 already builds.

DEBT, NOT A FLOOR BREACH, and the distinction is the carrier's own bound rather than a convenience: the floor asks for the partitions THE GUARDED BODY ITSELF TESTS.  That body tests `is_trap' and the outer `PSR & SFRZ', and both polarities of both are rowed.  MODE at the trap side is a single-axis marginal against an lvalue the body does not test there, which clause (e) discloses.

*** A FALSE L4 WAS NEARLY FILED BESIDE THIS AND WAS CHECKED FIRST. ***  The contract's sentence `every stcr-settable 88100 bit now varies there' reads like a per-branch claim and is measurably FALSE of the trap side alone.  It governs the OUTER guard, which sees both branches -- and over their union every bit does vary (MODE by errpriv, SER by errser/trapfrozenser, C by errc/trapfrozenc, SFD1 by errdiv0, IND by errind/trapfrozenind).  The claim is correct as written.  Recorded because the near-miss is the instructive part: a census that reports per-branch will make a correct union claim look wrong.

rows.title: dev_wdc.c ATAPI accounting: `consumed` counts helper CALLS, not successful pops -- over-counts when the input ring under-runs mid-access
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-06 from the `83df95c` pass 2 (panel_20260906_211839 + the codex run at regress/artifacts/retro_20260905/batch3a_wdc/pass2_seats/).  **DERIVED BY READING, NOT MEASURED, and the reachability half is explicitly NOT established.**

In the ATAPI accounting arm of `DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc)`'s `wd_data` read:

    int consumed = len == 4 ? 4 : (len >= 2 ? 2 : 1);

**`consumed` is computed from `len` ALONE.**  It counts the helper CALLS the arm makes, not the pops that
succeeded.  `wdc_get_inbuf()` returns `(uint64_t) -1` on an empty ring and returns BEFORE advancing the tail
-- verified by reading, the early return sits three lines above the advance -- so with `q` bytes queued a
width-`w` access pops `min(q, calls)`.  When the ring under-runs mid-access, `consumed` therefore over-counts
and `atapi_len` is decremented by more than the guest received.

*** THAT IS THE EXACT DEFECT #341 EXISTS TO FIX, QUOTED THREE LINES ABOVE THE EXPRESSION. ***  The comment reads *"account for what was actually CONSUMED from the buffer, not for what the guest asked for ... the count reported has to be the count that happened"* -- and the expression under it reports a count derived from the request.  #341 replaced `len` with this expression, which is correct whenever the ring holds enough bytes and wrong in exactly the residual case the same round was reasoning about.

**WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT FIXED IN-ROUND**, stated so nobody re-argues it: the stopping rule fixes a review finding in-round only if it is a MEASURED FALSE PASS or a WRONG RECORD.  The COMMENT was a wrong record and was corrected in place (L4, same commit).  The CODE question is a new defect with no witness: nothing here shows a guest reaching an under-run mid-access on the ATAPI path, and the over-read is already announced by the `warned_inbuf_overread` latch, so the silent-corruption claim is unproven.  **A round on this owes the rung-3 attempt** the lifecycle ruling requires.

**A SECOND OBSERVABLE IS WORSE THAN THE COUNT AND IS NOT ANALYSED HERE:** the arm accumulates with `odata += (wdc_get_inbuf(d) << 8)`, so a failed pop adds the sentinel's bits into the value the guest reads, not merely into the count.  Whether that is reachable, and whether the latch fires first, is the round's first question.

Codex noted `row_odd_step` and `row_odd_width` in `regress/diff_wdc_identify.c` already exercise the attempts-vs-pops distinction, so a detector may be closer than it looks.  It also found, separately, that `wdc_flood_probe.py`'s `overrun x2` omits the `r3` completion assertion -- a PRE-EXISTING coverage gap, not a stale expected value (row `wdcfloodprobe` already carries the probe's owed items).

rows.title: RULE QUESTION: does the addition licence authorise a zero-delta detector row that buys a distinguishing failure signature?
rows.witness: harness:table 15 measured the row's delta against its own mutant as zero (58/58 without it)
rows.hold_question: Does the ADDITION LICENCE authorise a row with ZERO measured delta whose benefit is telling you WHICH axis fired -- when removing it concentrates SFD1 coverage on a constant shared with two other rows, where a plausible edit silently reopens the axis and BASE does not notice?  codex ruled the attribution warrant does not transfer (the anchor rule repairs self-comparing oracles; row demand is per enumerated mutant, never per attribution need).  Rule for or against, and if for, say what the licence's wording should become.
rows.state_note:
*** A RULE QUESTION FOR THE 2026-09-09 ADJUDICATION, not a defect. ***  The carrier sends rule questions to the flagship seat at the next round boundary, because they change how future rounds run; this one was raised and ruled on by the pass-12 closing seat, and the ruling deserves the adjudicator rather than my acceptance.

**THE QUESTION: does the ADDITION LICENCE authorise a detector row whose only benefit is a DISTINGUISHING FAILURE SIGNATURE -- zero measured delta, but it tells you WHICH axis fired?**

**THE CASE.**  `#502` v19 added two rows to close the re-route trap side.  `trapfrozenuser` varies MODE and SFD1 together (PSR_FRZUSER = 0x03 clears both); `trapfrozensfd1` varies SFD1 alone.  Table 15 measured `trapfrozensfd1`'s delta against its own mutant as **ZERO** -- delete it and M_RRTRAPSFD1 is still caught, 58/58, by `trapfrozenuser`.

**MY WARRANT, AND THE RULING AGAINST IT.**  I claimed the anchor rule's principle one level down: a row varying two bits cannot say which one fired, so the single-axis row buys attribution.  codex (GPT-6 Astra, max) rejected it, citing the carrier: *the anchor rule repairs an oracle that compares a path with ITSELF*, which is not this situation -- the joint row already checks concrete vector and register expectations -- and *row demand is bounded 'per enumerated mutant, never per attribution need'*.  Its conclusion: **(iii) is wrong**, and (ii)'s claimed necessity for TWO rows is unsupported.  It was explicit that this does NOT extend the L2 chain and does not make the row vacuous; its verdict was CLOSE THE CHAIN.

**WHY THE ROW IS STILL IN THE TREE, and it is the same seat's own next paragraph.**  After removal, SFD1 coverage rests entirely on `trapfrozenuser`, whose `PSR_FRZUSER` is SHARED with `errpriv` and `errunimpl`.  Changing that constant from 0x03 to 0x0b would preserve THEIR intended routes while silently deleting the only SFD1-clear stimulus -- exception entry normalises both values to the same checked PSR and EPSR stays frozen, so **BASE alone would not notice**.  So the strict reading of the licence removes a row and creates a silent single point of failure on a shared constant.

**WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR IS ASKED.**  Either (a) the licence is right and the row goes, with the PSR_FRZUSER hazard handled some other way (a comment is memory, and this project's finding is that memory does not fire); or (b) a distinguishing failure signature IS a licensed benefit when the alternative concentrates an axis on a shared constant -- in which case the licence's wording should say so, since it currently does not.

**COST OF DEFERRING: none measured.**  The row is green, costs one session-free entry, and v21 is records-only (executable structure identical to the frozen v19 table 15 ran, verified with docstrings stripped), so table 15's scores still describe the shipped 59-row instrument and no re-table is owed either way.

**INDEPENDENT OF THE RULING:** any edit to `PSR_FRZUSER` owes a re-check of the pre-trap bit values and a repeat of both named mutant measurements.  That obligation stands whichever way this goes, and it is written into the probe beside the constant.

rows.title: alpha, i960 and riscv set cd.<arch>.irq_asserted with no consumer -- a real gap, but two are non-executing ports (scaffold cleanup) and the third is Alpha port completion
rows.witness: harness:source census, codex GPT-6 Astra at max, regress/artifacts/lcabadval/codex_irqasserted_20260906.txt
rows.state_note:
*** SEVERITY CORRECTED HIGH -> LOW THE SAME EVENING IT WAS FILED, BY THE PASS IT WAS FILED PENDING. ***  I filed this HIGH off ONE GREP while the investigation was in flight.  The census was right; the severity was not, and the correction is recorded rather than the row quietly re-graded.

**VERDICT (codex, GPT-6 Astra at max): REAL GAP in all three, and ALL THREE OF MY PREMISES HOLD.**  Six families set the flag, exactly three are consumed, and alpha/i960/riscv have no reader.  There is no alternate delivery mechanism for any of the three.

**BUT THE THREE ARE NOT ALIKE, AND THAT IS WHAT MOVES THE SEVERITY:**
* **i960 -- DEAD SCAFFOLDING.**  `cpu_i960_instr.c`'s instruction switch contains ONLY `default: goto bad;`. The FIRST instruction stops as unimplemented, so no boot, no timer programming, no driver wait is ever reached.  There is no guest to miss an interrupt.  `i960_exception()` is likewise a stopping stub.
* **riscv -- DEAD SCAFFOLDING.**  `cpu_riscv_instr.c` implements compressed NOP/ADDI only and the 32-bit branch goes unconditionally to `bad`.  `machine_test.c` DOES wire RTC -> interrupt controller -> CPU, so an asserted request really does end at the unused flag -- but this instruction subset cannot boot an OS or program that timer.
* **alpha -- A GENUINE HOLE, and the finding is that the PORT IS INCOMPLETE.**  `cpu_alpha_palcode.c` stores entry vectors and IPL (`PAL_OSF1_wrent`, `PAL_OSF1_swpipl`) and **`kentry` has no reader anywhere**; `PAL_OSF1_rti` appears only in the naming function with no execution implementation.  So delivery is missing at the CPU/PAL level, not merely at the flag.

**DISPOSITIONS:** removing the field and its stores is reasonable scaffold cleanup for i960 and riscv, and adding a dispatch check alone would achieve no usable capability in either.  For alpha the item is *track completion of the CPU/PAL/chipset path*, which subsumes `lcabadval`'s two interrupt stubs: **removing those exits still leaves both upstream forwarding and CPU delivery unfinished.**

*** AND IT CORRECTED MY CENSUS IN A WAY THAT DOES NOT CHANGE THE CONCLUSION BUT DOES CHANGE THE PICTURE: `cpu_dyntrans.c` ALSO delivers MIPS and SH interrupts, through DIFFERENTLY NAMED STATE. ***  My grep keyed on one identifier and so could not see them.  That is the correlate-not-the-class shape the carrier names -- the output was a plausible number either way -- and it is exactly the risk the brief disclosed about itself.

*** THE SHARPEST FINDING IS ABOUT MY BRIEF, NOT THE CODE: the seat named *"at least one numbered premise must be wrong"* AS THE UNSUPPORTED ASSUMPTION. ***  The three-question set closes with *WHICH IS WRONG?  Assume at least one is*, which is a good adversarial device and IS an unwarranted premise when the premises happen to be sound.  A seat that answers *none, and here is why the forcing assumption is unjustified* is giving the correct answer, and the template should say so rather than pressing for a defect that may not exist.  Filed against the template as `briefforcedwrong`.

Honest limit the seat stated and this row keeps: these are source-derived consequences, with no guest boot run, and "dead scaffolding" means the capability is absent rather than relocated.

entries.note: VERDICT: REAL GAP in alpha, i960 and riscv; all three premises correct as written.  Distinguished the three: i960 and riscv are DEAD SCAFFOLDING (neither can execute a second instruction -- i960's switch is only `default: goto bad;', riscv implements compressed NOP/ADDI and sends the 32-bit branch to `bad'), so there is no guest to miss an interrupt and the disposition is scaffold cleanup; alpha is a GENUINE HOLE at the CPU/PAL level (`kentry' stored with no reader, `PAL_OSF1_rti' named but unimplemented), so removing lcabadval's two interrupt exits still leaves forwarding AND delivery unfinished.  **Corrected my census**: cpu_dyntrans.c also delivers MIPS and SH interrupts through differently-named state, which a single-identifier grep could not see.  **And named my brief's forcing question as its own unsupported assumption** -- filed as briefforcedwrong.
