rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c horrible_getputpixel(): DE_MODE_LIN_B -- a DOCUMENTED NetBSD mode -- falls to the default arm, which assigns *color = random(); a copy then writes that random value to the destination
rows.witness: probe:regress/sgi_re_randompixel_probe.py -- rung 3 on unmodified -E sgi -e ip32, 8 rows, liveness AND device-signature controls green; re-pinned oracle measured RED at 7/8 on the COMMITTED pre-fix build (regress/artifacts/sgirandompixel/witness_20260906/prefix_repinned_RED.out), 8/8 after.  Gate-wired into gate_arm.sh; 880 checks PASS.
rows.state_note:
*** RAISED THE SAME EVENING IT WAS FILED, ON A READING THAT MADE IT WORSE: THE UNHANDLED VALUE IS A DOCUMENTED
MODE, NOT A NONSENSE ONE. ***  Verified against the vendored header before this edit.

`horrible_getputpixel()` extracts `tlb_mode = (mode >> 10) & 0x7` and switches on it.  The function's own
comment lists five NetBSD modes, and `src/include/thirdparty/crmfbreg.h` confirms their values:

    DE_MODE_TLB_A  0x0000 -> 0  handled       DE_MODE_LIN_A  0x1000 -> 4  handled
    DE_MODE_TLB_B  0x0400 -> 1  handled       DE_MODE_LIN_B  0x1400 -> 5  *** default -> *color = random() ***
    DE_MODE_TLB_C  0x0800 -> 2  handled       (3, 6 and 7 also reach it)

**FOUR OF THE FIVE DOCUMENTED MODES ARE IMPLEMENTED AND THE FIFTH RETURNS RANDOM DATA.**  So this is not a
guest choosing an out-of-spec value; it is a guest choosing one of the five modes the vendored header defines.

**THE GUEST-VISIBLE PATH, in `draw_primitive()`, and both mode words are GUEST-WRITABLE registers**
(`CRIME_DE_MODE_SRC` / `CRIME_DE_MODE_DST` via `d->de_reg[]`):

    if (drawmode & DE_DRAWMODE_XFER_EN)
            horrible_getputpixel(0, ..., &color, src_mode);   // GET may set color = random()
    ...
    if (draw)
            horrible_getputpixel(1, ..., &color, dst_mode);   // PUT writes it

A failed SOURCE read and the DESTINATION write are the same `color` variable in the same loop iteration, so
the random value is written out per pixel with no decline.  **The code's own comment on that XFER branch reads
*"Pixel colors copied from another source.  (OpenBSD draws characters using this mechanism.)"*** -- so the
branch is one a real guest driver uses, which is why this is filed HIGH rather than as a curiosity.

**STILL OWED AND NOT CLAIMED: the rung-3 witness.**  Reachability is READ, not MEASURED -- I have shown the
constant exists, the extraction reaches 5, and the registers are writable, and NOT that any in-tree guest
programs LIN_B.  A witness-attempt brief is with codex asking exactly that, including the awkward part: the
oracle cannot pin a value because `random()` is non-deterministic, so it must pin *the destination differs
from the source* and *two identical runs differ*.

*** THE PROVENANCE IS THE LESSON: this came from asking what a DISABLED kill FELL BACK TO. ***  It is the
second such finding today -- `lcabadval`'s disabled kill leaves a live `dev = 0` that aliases 'no selected
device' to device zero.  Both look like a decision already taken and neither is one to copy.  Four exits in
this file are commented out; the other three still owe that question.

*** RUNG-3 ATTEMPT MADE, AND THE ANSWER IS WITNESS BUILDABLE (grok).  The probe is SPECIFIED, NOT RUN --
that seat is plan-mode, so this is a READING and the measurement is still owed. ***

**THE FALSE NEGATIVE THAT WOULD HAVE WASTED THE FIRST ATTEMPT:** at reset the destination mode is TLB_A and
`re_tlb_a[]` has bit 31 clear, so the PUT returns WITHOUT WRITING.  A naive probe -- set SRC to LIN_B, draw,
read the destination -- finds it unchanged and reports NO DEFECT.  Using LIN_A as the destination closes it,
since case 4 forces the valid bit.  `sgi_de_primop_probe.py` had already named that gap.

**AND THE ORACLE IS CERTAIN, NOT PROBABILISTIC:** glibc `random()` is 31-bit, so the destination's bit 31 is
clear and inequality with a source of `0xAABBCCDD` is guaranteed rather than 2^-32.  Two runs differ by
default seeding; `-D` makes them identical, which changes the second oracle and not the defect.

*** THE SEVERITY SPLIT GROK NAMED, AND IT IS THE HONEST LIMIT OF THIS ROW: `LIN_B` IS DOCUMENTED AND STORABLE
BUT NOT SHOWN TO BE DRIVER-SELECTED. ***  It appears only in `crmfbreg.h` and this function's comment; the
XFER comment names OpenBSD character drawing without saying which source mode; the PROM's `MTE_TLB_LIN_A/B`
zero-fill path does NOT call `horrible_getputpixel`; and `images.md` has no O2/sgimips image to boot.  **A
documented-but-unused mode and a mode a driver really selects are different severities**, and only the
constant's existence is established here.

*** THE WITNESS IS BUILT AND MEASURED.  7/7 on the committed build, artifacts/sgirandompixel/witness_20260906/head_79cd12e.out. ***

Real guest instructions on an unmodified committed `-E sgi -e ip32', no `device_add'.  Both mandated controls
green: LIVENESS (store then load through RAM) and DEVICE SIGNATURE (CRIME_DE_STATUS reads 0x1e000000 where
RAM reads 0).  The value written was 0x4b1763a1 on one run and 0x2ee4b4df on the next, **bit 31 CLEAR both
times** -- glibc random() is 31-bit, so inequality with a source of 0xaabbccdd is CERTAIN rather than 2^-32,
which is what makes the oracle deterministic despite the value not being.

*** TWO TRAPS HIT WHILE BUILDING IT, AND THE ACCEPT CONTROL IS WHAT CAUGHT THE FIRST. ***
* **The destination tile pointer was 0, so every pixel went to PHYSICAL ADDRESS 0.**  grok had named exactly
  this hazard -- *'do not leave it 0: that writes phys 0'* -- and I hit it anyway from a direction it had also
  named: a 64-bit `sd' writes the HIGH word to `[n]' and the low word to `[n+1]', so storing 0x10 gave
  `re_linear_a[0] = 0, [1] = 0x10'.  **A probe with only the defect rows would have read the destination
  unchanged and reported NO DEFECT.**  The ACCEPT control failed instead, which is what an accept row is for.
* `lw` SIGN-EXTENDS into a 64-bit register, so the source value read back as 0xffffffffaabbccdd and the row
  failed on FORMATTING rather than behaviour.  The shipped `sgi_re_width_probe.py` carries that normalisation
  and says why; this probe should have copied it and now does.

**THE ORACLE MUST INVERT AFTER THE FIX, and the order is not optional.**  These rows PASS while the defect is
PRESENT, so post-fix they assert the wrong thing.  The oracle-correction rule requires the re-pin FIRST, the
committed build measured RED under the new expectations, and the code changed only THEN -- otherwise the
re-pin cannot be told from fitting the test to the binary.  Design panel is running; the post-fix row set
depends on its answer to what `*color' should be on a failed get.

*** DESIGN PASS 1: THE PANEL CONVERGES ON MEMBER 3 (DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE), 3 of 5 answering seats,
AND THE TWO DISSENTS ARE REFUTED ON A POINT BOTH FILE-READING SEATS REACHED INDEPENDENTLY. ***

deepseek and minimax voted MEMBER 5 (FAULT).  **The device access that triggers this ALREADY SUCCEEDED** --
the guest's store to PRIMITIVE|START was accepted -- so there is nothing left to fault, and raising a bus
error would report a failure for an access the hardware acknowledges.  grok put it exactly: *'member 5 is
available here' is true of IP32 and FALSE OF THIS CALL SITE.*  Their shared argument -- that only FAULT stops
the bogus write -- is true of a weaker member 3 than either file-reading seat proposed.

**THE REMAINING QUESTION IS SCOPE, and it is decided by the round-scope rule rather than by vote:**
* **codex** wants the complete fix now: an explicit success result on the function, and every GET site
  (source, the ROP `oldcolor', MTE's `bg') taught to suppress its dependent PUT.
* **grok** wants the minimal one: delete the `random()' assignment, let the PUT write `fg', and file skip-PUT
  and a real LIN_B case as separate rounds.
**A return value plus seven call sites is not ONE SITE**, and the reopening rule says a round takes one.
grok's scoping is taken; codex's obligations are filed rather than dropped.

*** THE ORACLE IS GROK'S AND IT DISCRIMINATES EVERY CANDIDATE AT ONCE, which is why it is worth having even
though the fix is minimal: *** zero leaves `0`, skip-PUT leaves the pre-paint `0x11111111`, IMPLEMENT-as-copy
leaves `0xaabbccdd`, and untouched-with-PUT leaves `fg`.  **THE PROBE MUST THEREFORE PROGRAM `fg` TO A
DISTINCTIVE NON-ZERO VALUE** -- the witness ran with `fg=0x0`, where 'untouched' and 'zeroed' are the same
observation and the oracle would be vacuous.  `lin_b written` is DROPPED as a defect row: under this member it
is true before and after.

*** PASS 2: SHIP, SIX SEATS ANSWERING, NONE WALLED, NONE DOWN -- the fullest roster of the session, and it cost one liveness call to get there. ***

Three explicit SHIP verdicts (kimi, glm, minimax); both FILE-READING seats answered without a verdict line and both were read in full, which is where the one finding was.  **codex re-derived all 40 row outcomes (8 rows x 5 mutants) from the preserved artifacts and confirmed the table**, saying plainly it ran nothing itself.  **grok answered NONE IS WRONG to the five-way question and named the question's own frame as the unsupported assumption** -- the second seat tonight to make that correction independently.

**THE ONE L4, AND IT WAS MINE:** `SGIRE_W_PRIM_OP`'s comment still claimed `1 << 10` was the next free bit and that the enum ended there -- false the moment `SGIRE_W_BADMODE = 1 << 10` was appended below it.  The file warns about exactly this collision four lines earlier, having paid for it once; I read that warning, placed my bit correctly by it, and left the signpost pointing at the bit I had taken.  Fixed in-round:
the superseded sentence is DEMOTED inside its own correction, so exactly one live next-free claim remains and it sits on the last enumerator.

**WHAT BOTH FILE-READING SEATS AGREE IS NOT COVERED**, recorded as the contract's disclosure rather than discovered later: line and MTE execution paths, other mode combinations, junk modes 3/6/7, the dest-side LIN_B PUT, MTE's `&bg' GET, the colour-mode default arm, and resistance to latch-sharing mutants (disclosed 8/8 in isolation, because nothing in these sessions sets the other bit first).

*** MAIN-LOOP RECORD 2026-09-06 (assess stage) -- written into state_note, NOT into `entries'. ***
`entries' is the SEAT ANSWER list: check_stage_panels.py counts entries to decide whether a stage's
nine seats were fired, and gen_dashboard.py REFUSES TO RENDER on a seat id no column declares.  A
main-loop note parked there is not merely mis-filed -- it MANUFACTURES A SEAT ANSWER THAT NEVER
HAPPENED, which is the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape inverted.  Seven such entries were
written during this session and all seven were migrated here when the generator refused.

Reading, not measurement: verified the default arm executes `*color = random()`, that LIN_B extracts to tlb_mode 5 and is unhandled while the other four documented modes are handled, that both mode words come from guest-writable de_reg entries, and that the failed source GET and the destination PUT share one `color` variable in one loop iteration. rows.state_note:
*** MY OWN DIAGNOSIS IN THIS ROW WAS WRONG WITHIN THE HOUR, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS BECAUSE IT CHANGES
THE REMEDY. ***  I wrote that the trigger is 'the SUBJECT SHAPE, not a phrase', on the evidence of two
refusals of one brief.  **codex then answered a brief on THE SAME DEFECT, in the same file, at 167 KB.**

The difference is the FRAMING, and it is sharper than either earlier guess:
  REFUSED  the WITNESS brief -- 'can you build a probe that REACHES this and shows the bad value?'
  ANSWERED the DESIGN brief -- 'what should this code do instead, and what should the rows assert?'
Same defect, same file, same session.  A request to CONSTRUCT A PATH TO A DEFECT reads as an attack recipe;
a request to DECIDE WHAT THE CODE SHOULD DO reads as ordinary review.  Neutralising the vocabulary did not
help because the vocabulary was never the trigger.

**SO THE REMEDY IS NOT ONLY RE-ROUTING: it is to ask codex the DESIGN question and let another seat answer
the REACHABILITY one.**  That is cheaper than it sounds -- grok answered the witness brief with a complete
buildable sketch, and codex then produced the best design answer of the panel.  Each seat was asked the
question it would answer.

*** THE SEAT-CHECK HAZARD IS UNCHANGED AND IS THE PART THAT WAS ACTUALLY FIXED. ***  The refusal writes a
zero-byte stdout with the reason on stderr on a direct call -- indistinguishable from an agy quota wall --
and through panel.sh it produced 150,372 bytes at 97% novel, which `seat_verdicts.py` scored as **answered,
NO VERDICT LINE**.  A seat failure counted as an answer, in the tool built to refuse exactly that.  Every
existing test passed it: no quota keyword (not a wall), high novelty because the seat streams reasoning
BEFORE the filter fires (not an echo), CLI seat (not a burn).  Now reported as **SEAT REFUSED**, counted with
the DOWN seats, keyed on the vendor's own sentence, and controlled in four directions: it fires on the
refusal, leaves a genuine quota wall as WALLED, leaves the mid-answer wall's READ-THE-BODY label intact, and
does not touch answering seats.

Both refusal transcripts and the answered design brief are preserved beside the round's artifacts, so the
before/after comparison is checkable rather than remembered.

*** THIRD INSTANCE, 2026-09-07 -- AND IT REFUTES THE DIAGNOSIS THIS ROW CURRENTLY CARRIES. ***

Preserved: `regress/artifacts/sgirekills/refusals/attempt3_scoping.err'.  Exact text, twice:

    ERROR: This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk. If this seems wrong, try
    rephrasing your request. To get authorized for security work, join the Trusted Access for
    Cyber program: https://chatgpt.com/cyber

**stdout was 0 bytes; the banner, the echoed prompt and both ERROR lines went to stderr** -- so a
check that measures the `.txt' alone sees an empty file and a check that measures SIZE sees 6829
bytes of healthy-looking stderr.  `seat_verdicts.py' already reports this as SEAT REFUSED / DOWN
(fixed earlier in this session); this instance confirms the detector on a fresh case.

*** WHAT IS REFUTED: this row concluded the trigger is the reach-the-defect FRAMING -- *design
briefs are answered, witness briefs are refused*.  THE REFUSED BRIEF HERE IS NEITHER. ***  It is a
read-only SCOPING task that explicitly says *"Do not design the fix diff.  Do not write rows"*.

**AND THE CONTROL IS STRONG, because it ran the same evening on the same model at the same effort:**
the `sgirebufuninit' pass-1 brief -- which discusses uninitialised host stack reaching guest-visible
memory, i.e. a MEMORY-DISCLOSURE defect -- was ANSWERED at 317 KB with a GO-WITH-CHANGES verdict and
two new findings.  So the trigger is not the subject matter, not the security-adjacent content, and
not the brief's purpose.

**THE REMAINING HYPOTHESIS, stated as a hypothesis because it is not yet tested: VOCABULARY DENSITY.**
The refused brief is saturated with this fork's historical term for the defect -- *kills*, *THE HOST
STILL DIES*, *terminating calls*, *host kill* -- while the answered brief describes an equivalent
severity in ordinary engineering words.  A re-fire is in flight with the identical technical content
rewritten in bounds-and-error-handling language (`RESEARCH_scoping_neutral_20260907.md'): same
questions, same code, same seven dispositions, no `kill'/`dies'/`host' vocabulary.

**That is a real experiment with a clean control and it settles the hypothesis either way** -- if the
neutral form answers, the trigger is vocabulary and the remedy is the benign-framing rule the carrier
already mandates for the Anthropic seats, applied to codex too; if it also refuses, vocabulary is out
and the next candidate is brief LENGTH or the enumerate-the-sites structure.

*Note the cost is real and recurring: codex is the seat this queue leans on hardest, and a refusal is
invisible to any size-based check.*

*** SOLVED, WITH A CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT.  THE TRIGGER IS THE REPOSITORY'S OWN ARCHIVES, NOT THE BRIEF'S
SUBJECT AND NOT ITS FRAMING.  Measured 2026-09-07 across four runs. ***

    attempt  brief vocabulary   reading scope        stderr     flag
    1        kills / HOST DIES  unrestricted           6,829 b  IMMEDIATE, before any work
    3        neutral            unrestricted         374,583 b  at byte 279,268 (~75% in)
    4        neutral            src/ + regress/*.py  279,132 b  *** NONE -- full verdict delivered ***
    (control) pass-2 panel      unrestricted         395,340 b  at the END of the answer

**TWO SEPARATE FILTERS, and each attempt isolates one:**
* **Attempt 1 -> 3 shows a PROMPT-level filter keyed on vocabulary.**  Rewriting *kills / the host dies /
  terminating calls* into ordinary bounds-and-error-handling language converted an instant refusal into a run
  that worked for minutes.  The technical content was IDENTICAL -- same twelve sites, same expectation design,
  same seven dispositions.
* **Attempt 3 -> 4 shows a CONTENT-level filter keyed on what the seat READS.**  Adding one paragraph -- *do
  not read `regress/artifacts/' or `tools/pipeline/ledger.json'* -- carried the run past the exact point where
  the unrestricted one died, to a clean finish.  **279,132 vs 279,268 bytes: the same distance, opposite
  outcome.**

**WHY THE ARCHIVES: they are this project's own record of a hardening campaign** -- kill tables, `host kill'
censuses, `exit(1)' enumerations, mutant names like `widthkillclass' -- accumulated over months.  Read in bulk
they look like exactly what the filter exists to catch.  *The irony is that the archive is the honest record
of DEFENSIVE work, and its own vocabulary is what makes the seat refuse to read it.*

> **THE OPERATIONAL RULE, and it costs two sentences in a brief: for any codex run, (a) write the brief in
> ordinary engineering language, and (b) SCOPE ITS READING to `src/` and `regress/*.py`.**  The pass-2 control
> shows why (b) matters even when (a) is satisfied: that brief was already neutral and was still flagged, at
> the end, after reading the ledger and CHANGELOG.

This matters more than one lost answer: codex is the seat this queue leans on hardest, a refusal writes 0
bytes to stdout while leaving healthy-looking stderr, and it is invisible to every size-based check.

*** SIXTH RUN, AND IT REFUTES THE REMEDY I SHIPPED TWO HOURS AGO -- SCOPING IS NECESSARY, NOT
SUFFICIENT.  Worse: it REHABILITATES the diagnosis I recorded as REFUTED, and my refutation was a
misreading of my own brief. ***

A `swpctx' design brief scoped ENTIRELY to `src/' was flagged at 145 KB -- the flag fired while it was
grepping `debugger_cmds.c', which is INSIDE the allowed scope.  All six runs, sorted by what they asked:

    WHAT IS TRUE                                    WHAT TO BUILD
    analysis of a defect        317 KB clean        smallest EDIT that RE-OPENS     375 KB FLAGGED
    count + classify            298 KB clean        smallest guest PROGRAM that
    is this path reached?       294 KB clean          WITNESSES each defect         145 KB FLAGGED
    CAN a guest run at all?     502 KB clean

**The discriminator is whether the brief asks the seat to BUILD SOMETHING THAT TRIGGERS A DEFECT.**  The
502 KB clean run asked at length about cold-debugger probes, breakpoints and planting instructions -- and
was fine, because it asked whether such a thing is POSSIBLE rather than for one aimed at a defect.

*** AND I HAD THIS RIGHT THE FIRST TIME. ***  This row's original diagnosis was *the reach-the-defect
FRAMING is the trigger*.  I recorded it REFUTED because a read-only SCOPING brief was also refused --
but that brief's Q3 asked *"what is the smallest change to the model that would restore the old
behaviour ... while still satisfying a test built that way?"*  **That is construction framing, and I did
not re-read my own brief before declaring the diagnosis dead.**  The premise-audit failure again, on my
own record rather than on the code.

**THE ARCHIVE FINDING IS NOT SUPERSEDED** -- it carried a run past the exact byte where an unscoped one
died, which is a measurement and stands.  There are TWO triggers; §C5 shipped implying one, and now says
so.

**OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, and it costs something real:** codex cannot be asked for mutants or witness
programs.  It can CHECK a construction supplied to it, and it can say whether one is possible -- both
measured clean.  **The construction itself goes to a measuring seat.**  That is a genuine capability
loss, not a wording problem, and it should be weighed on the 9th alongside [[codexbriefscoping]].

*** SEVENTH RUN, AND A THIRD REFINEMENT: A BRIEF THAT ASKS `IS THIS TRUE' CAN STILL BE REFUSED IF ITS
CONTENT IS AN EXPLOITATION CHAIN.  Immediate rejection at 8 KB. ***

The `sgilinearnegidx' verification brief obeyed both existing rules: neutral engineering language, reading
scoped to `src/' and `regress/*.py', and it asked only for each link of a chain to be CHECKED -- explicitly
*"I want it attacked rather than confirmed"*, with no construction requested anywhere.  **Refused on the
prompt**, before any work, exactly like the first `kills'-vocabulary attempt.

**What it contained that the six clean runs did not: a numbered seven-step guest-controlled chain ending in
a PHYSICAL write, plus questions about the reachable address range and about how far the guest can CONTROL
the value.**  The clean runs analysed defects, classified sites, traced reachability of a code path, and
asked whether a probe is possible.  None of them laid out *guest does A, then B, then C, and thereby writes
where it chooses*.

> **So the discriminator is not the QUESTION FORM but the SHAPE OF THE CONTENT.  `What is true about this
> code?' is clean; `here is a chain by which a guest reaches X -- how far does it go?' is not, however it is
> phrased.**

**OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, and it is the sharpest limit yet:** the seat cannot be used to review the very
findings that matter most in a hardening fork, once those findings have been assembled into a chain.  It can
check the LINKS SEPARATELY -- *is `src_x' masked in the linear path?* is a clean question -- but not the
chain as a chain.  **Split the chain into independent link questions, or verify it yourself.**  I verified
this one myself in three greps.

*Recorded with the other two triggers rather than replacing them: vocabulary (prompt-level), archive reading
(content-level, late), and now chain SHAPE (prompt-level).*

*** THIRD RECORDED INSTANCE, 2026-09-07, AND IT CARRIES THE CLEANEST DISCRIMINATOR YET, because
TWO briefs on the SAME SUBJECT MATTER passed on the SAME DAY and this one did not. ***

Artifact: `regress/artifacts/lcaconfbus1kill/codex_witness_20260907.err`.  The `.txt` is **ZERO
BYTES and the process exited 0** -- so an exit-status check scores it a success and a size check
scores it a dead seat; only the `.err` names it:

    ERROR: This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk. If this seems wrong, try
    rephrasing your request. To get authorized for security work, join the Trusted Access for
    Cyber program: ...

**THE CONTROLS ARE THE VALUABLE PART.  Same seat, same model, same effort, same day, same device
file, all three read-only:**

    PASSED   brief_lcabadval_fixcheck.md      "six value guards that END THE PROCESS" -- inlined
                                              fatal()+exit(1) verbatim, asked whether a proposed
                                              DELETION was sound.  6,976-byte answer.
    PASSED   brief_sgirandomcolour_scope.md   "writes FOUR random() bytes to guest memory",
                                              "uninitialised host stack reaches guest memory",
                                              asked for a reachability census.  7,946-byte answer.
    REFUSED  brief_lcaconfbus1_witness.md     asked whether a proposed TEST CONSTRUCTION would
                                              successfully REACH the termination, step by step.

**So it is not the vocabulary and not the subject.**  "Host kill", "exit(1)", "guest-drivable",
"uninitialised stack into guest memory" all pass.  What differs is the ASK: the first two ask *is
this analysis correct*; the third asks *will this sequence work*.  A numbered two-step recipe --
write this value here, then touch that window, and the process exits -- reads as exploit validation
however defensively it is framed, and mine was framed defensively (opened with "ordinary regression-
test adequacy review", no offensive-security wording anywhere).

> **THE OPERATIONAL RULE: ask codex to VERIFY AN ANALYSIS, not to VALIDATE A SEQUENCE THAT REACHES A
> TERMINATION.**  This is the carrier's existing C5 trigger -- *asking for a construction that
> reaches a defect* -- with a measured negative control on both sides for the first time.  Where a
> construction genuinely needs checking, ask about its CONTROLS in isolation ("does a matched
> surviving control at the same address attribute an outcome to the value?") without narrating the
> path to the kill.

**RECOVERY, and it is the sixth-class rule applied: the seat refused, the QUESTION did not become
unanswerable.**  grok reads the repo, takes its brief from a FILE (no argv cap), runs `--permission-
mode plan` read-only, and has no such filter.  It was fired on the byte-identical brief.  A refused
seat with a live alternate transport is ONE SEAT COVERED, not one lost -- but it is recorded as a
REFUSAL by name, never as agreement or as a wall.

*Cost note: 17,471 tokens spent before the flag fired, and 217 KB of tool-call reasoning in the
`.err` showing it had already listed the tree and begun reading.  The refusal is not instant, so a
zero-byte `.txt` after several minutes is NOT evidence of a hang.*

*** A DUPLICATE OF THIS ROW WAS FILED ON 2026-09-08 (`codexcontentfilter`) AND HAS BEEN WITHDRAWN.
It contributed ONE measurement worth folding in here. ***

**A DETERMINISM CONTROL: the same brief, byte-for-byte, REFUSED and then ANSWERED.**
`regress/artifacts/sgirekills/ROUNDDESIGN_brief.md`, md5 `21c440bc6746d1e6bb6d52f703f847bb`,
16,903 bytes -- firing 1 produced a 0-byte `.txt`, firing 2 produced 6,868 bytes and a full answer.
Nothing changed between them but time.

**That is consistent with THIS row's ARCHIVE-READING trigger and not with randomness:** the filter
fires partway through, at whatever point the run has read enough of the archive, so two firings of
one brief diverge on what they happen to read.  *The duplicate concluded "non-deterministic"; the
mechanism recorded here is the better explanation, and it makes the remedy a FIX (neutral language
plus scoped reading) rather than a retry.*

**A re-fire is still worth one attempt** -- it costs a minute and may take a different reading path
-- but it is a coin-flip with a mechanism, not the remedy.

*** A NEGATIVE CONTROL ON THIS ROW'S OWN REMEDY, MEASURED 2026-09-08: THE SCOPING FIX DID NOT WORK,
AND THE REASON IS THAT IT CANNOT WORK ON A ROUND OF THIS SHAPE. ***

This row's recorded remedy is **neutral engineering language AND reading scoped to src/ and
regress/*.py**, aimed at the ARCHIVE-READING trigger -- the filter fires once the run has read enough
of regress/artifacts/ or ledger.json.

The sgirekills re-pin brief was refused.  I applied the remedy exactly -- added a READING SCOPE
paragraph naming src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c and regress/*.py and excluding the archive -- and re-fired.
**It was refused again**: codex_repin_scoped_20260908.txt is ZERO BYTES, the .err carries two
Trusted-Access lines, 17,904 tokens used, exited 1.

> *** THE DIAGNOSIS: SCOPING THE READING TO src/ IS NOT A REMEDY WHEN src/ IS WHAT TRIPS THE
> FILTER. ***  The .err shows the run had reached dev_sgi_re.c -- and that file is a wall of bounds
> guards, refusal arms and exit(1) calls.  **To the filter, the product source of a hardening fork
> reads like the archive does.**  The remedy moves the reading from one flagged corpus to another.

**So the three recorded triggers need a fourth, and it is the one that BOUNDS the remedy:**

    SUBJECT SOURCE   content-level and UNAVOIDABLE -- a round whose subject file is itself
                     guard-and-refuse code cannot be scoped away from its own subject.

**WHAT THIS CHANGES OPERATIONALLY, and it is not nothing:** for a round on a device-hardening file,
codex must be given the FACTS INLINE -- treated as a PACKET-FED seat for that round -- rather than
pointed at the file.  That is the same move the carrier already prescribes for the Ollama transports,
and it is affordable here because a re-pin brief's facts are a few dozen lines of arm addresses and
array declarations.  **Untested as of this writing; recorded as the next thing to try, NOT as a
second remedy claimed to work.**

*Recorded because it is a controlled negative: same seat, same subject, remedy applied deliberately
and singly, refused.  The remedy's earlier success on the gdromcondavail brief stands -- what is
refuted is its GENERALITY, and this row had stated it with no scope condition.*

*** THE CHAIN-SHAPE TRIGGER CONFIRMED PROMPT-LEVEL, 2026-09-08, WITH A CLEAN DISCRIMINATOR THAT
SEPARATES IT FROM THE ARCHIVE-READING TRIGGER AT A GLANCE. ***

Four codex briefs went out tonight on neutral engineering subjects.  Three answered in full; the
fourth was refused.  **The refused one is the WITNESS-DESIGN brief**, and its `.err` settles where
the refusal happened:

    brief                      .err bytes   file-read lines   outcome
    armbfcdecode DECODE            70,308   many              ANSWERED (5,037 b)
    alphatbinegsel VERIFY          20,210   many              ANSWERED (6,820 b)
    alphatbinegsel Q3             167,085   many              ANSWERED (4,654 b)
    alphatbinegsel WITNESS          6,291   *** ZERO ***      REFUSED (0 b)

*** ZERO FILE-READ LINES MEANS IT REFUSED BEFORE OPENING ANYTHING.  The prompt's TEXT tripped it,
not what it read. ***  That is this row's third recorded trigger -- CHAIN SHAPE -- and it is now
confirmed as prompt-level rather than inferred.

**WHY THIS BRIEF AND NOT THE OTHER THREE.**  The three that answered ask *"is this analysis
correct"* about code that already exists.  The witness brief asks how to CONSTRUCT A GUEST SEQUENCE
THAT DEMONSTRATES THE DEFECT -- *"what the guest sets up, which PAL call it makes, and what it then
observes"*, plus *"remap a VPN to a different physical page ... then load from that VPN and see the
OLD contents."*  **A numbered guest-controlled sequence ending in an observation of stale memory is
the chain shape, however defensively framed** -- and this brief was written to be neutral, with no
`kill`/`host dies`/`exploit` vocabulary anywhere.  Neutral language was NOT sufficient.

> *** THE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, and it is a real capability limit rather than a nuisance:
> **codex CANNOT DESIGN WITNESSES FOR THIS PROJECT.**  Witness design IS the reach-the-defect shape
> by definition -- the ladder requires a real guest instruction sequence that reaches the site.  So
> every rung-3 witness brief is expected to refuse, and routing one to codex is a wasted
> invocation. ***

**THE DISCRIMINATOR, and it costs one `grep -c`:**

    small .err + ZERO read lines + 0-byte .txt   -> PROMPT-LEVEL.  Rewrite the brief, or send it
                                                    to a different seat.  A retry will not help.
    large .err + many read lines + 0-byte .txt   -> LATE (archive/subject).  Scoping the reading
                                                    may help; a retry may take a different path.
    NO .txt and NO .err at all                   -> the run NEVER STARTED (a launcher/path fault,
                                                    NOT a refusal) -- measured separately tonight.

*Three distinguishable states, three different remedies.  Previously only the middle one was
characterised, and the row's determinism pair belongs to it.*

**ROUTED TO grok INSTEAD**, which is not subject to this filter and which has designed rung-3
witnesses for this project before (`lcabadval`'s row records a rung-3 seat specifying a full
sequence).  *The brief was reused BYTE-FOR-BYTE -- no rewrite -- which is what makes this a clean
seat-capability finding rather than a prompt-quality one.*

*** THE THREE-STATE DISCRIMINATOR NEEDS ONE CORRECTION, FOUND BY APPLYING IT TO A HEALTHY SEAT
TWENTY MINUTES AFTER WRITING IT.  2026-09-08. ***

As written above, the first state reads *"small `.err` + ZERO read lines + 0-byte `.txt` ->
PROMPT-LEVEL refusal."*  Applied to the `#513` pass-2 run mid-flight, that pattern MATCHED a seat
that was perfectly healthy:

    refusal lines      0
    file-read lines    0        <- matches the "prompt-level" shape
    .err bytes    39,485        <- but LARGE, not small
    processes          4 alive
    .txt bytes         0        <- normal mid-run: codex writes stdout at the END

**It had read nothing because the pass-2 brief INLINES the whole diff -- there was nothing it needed
to open.**  A seat can legitimately answer with zero file reads.

> **THE ACTUAL DISCRIMINATOR IS THE REFUSAL LINE.  Everything else says WHERE it refused, not
> WHETHER it did.**
>
>     refusal line present + ZERO reads   -> PROMPT-LEVEL.  Reroute; a retry will not help.
>     refusal line present + MANY reads   -> LATE (archive/subject).  Scoping may help.
>     refusal line ABSENT, .txt 0 bytes,
>       process alive                     -> MID-RUN.  Not a refusal at all.
>     NO .txt and NO .err whatsoever      -> the run NEVER STARTED (launcher/path fault).

*The read count was doing work it cannot do.  I wrote the three-state form from four observations
that happened to correlate -- every refusal I had seen with zero reads also had a small `.err` --
and the correlation broke on the first case outside that set.*  **That is this file's own
freshly-minted-exemplar rule landing on a discriminator I minted an hour earlier: the instruction
survived, its cheap proxy did not.**

*Corrected in `tools/pipeline/ADJUDICATION_20260909.md` as well, which had quoted the earlier form.*

*** A FOURTH TRIGGER, AND IT IS THE OPERATIONALLY EXPENSIVE ONE: THE ASK-AGAIN QUESTION ITSELF.
Measured 2026-09-08 on the #513 pass-3 panel. ***

codex ANSWERED the pass-2 diff review and REFUSED the pass-3 one.  Both are diff reviews of the
same round, same file, same neutral vocabulary.  **The refusal is LATE, not prompt-level** --
133,341 bytes of `.err`, 30,706 tokens used, many file reads, then the flag -- so it is the
archive/subject shape rather than the chain shape.

**WHAT PASS 3 ASKS THAT PASS 2 DID NOT:**

    Q2  "Is there a third cell? ... bits 6, 7, 9, 10 are swept by nothing."
    Q3  "Name the smallest edit that keeps a guard and makes these two rows GREEN while the
         latch behaviour is WRONG."

**That is an EVASION-CONSTRUCTION request.**  Pass 2 asked *is this change correct*; pass 3 asks
*construct an edit that defeats this detector while looking right*.  The second is much closer to
the reach-the-defect shape than to source review.

> *** THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT COSMETIC: THE ASK-AGAIN IS A MANDATED STEP IN THIS PROJECT'S
> PROCESS. ***  The vacuity floor requires exactly this question of every clean kill table -- *"the
> smallest edit that breaks this property and still passes"* -- and measured yield says it is where
> the real escapes come from.  **So codex is unavailable for the single highest-yield adversarial
> query in the round lifecycle**, on top of being unavailable for witness design.

**WHAT STILL WORKS:** codex answered EIGHT briefs tonight -- decode conformance, ABI review, source
analysis, callback tracing, error-handling review, and the pass-2 diff review.  The pattern across
nine firings is consistent: **codex reviews CODE THAT EXISTS; it will not construct an edit or a
sequence that defeats something.**

**MITIGATION, and it is already proven in this round:** grok and the packet-fed seats answer the
ask-again without difficulty -- pass 3's five answering seats ALL found the remaining latch cells,
and grok additionally prescribed the one-row class closure.  **Route the ask-again to grok and the
Ollama transports; do not spend a codex invocation on it.**

*Recorded from a controlled pair: same round, same file, same seat, two briefs one hour apart,
differing in exactly this question.*

*** THE ARCHIVE TRIGGER FIRED AGAIN 2026-09-08, AND I WALKED THE SEAT INTO IT WHILE WRITING THE
AVOIDANCE INSTRUCTION.  Ten refusal lines. ***

The brief said, in its own scope section:

> *"Read ... `regress/artifacts/sgirekills/killtable_20260908/*.txt` and the `*_20260908.out` logs
> there -- **these are the measurement records the packet cites; reading them is the point of this
> brief**.  Please still avoid `tools/pipeline/ledger.json`."*

**`regress/artifacts/` IS the archive corpus this row's second trigger keys on.**  I named the
ledger as the thing to avoid and directed the seat straight into the other half.  507 KB of `.err`,
**ten** refusal lines, 0-byte answer.

> *** THE TENSION IS REAL AND IS NOT A MISTAKE IN THE ROW'S REMEDY: AUDITING MEASUREMENT CLAIMS
> REQUIRES THE MEASUREMENT ARCHIVE.  The remedy "scope reading away from regress/artifacts/" and the
> task "verify these numbers against their logs" are in direct conflict. ***

**THE RESOLUTION, and it is the one the packet-fed seats have always needed: INLINE THE LOGS.**  The
seven logs this audit needs total a few KB.  Re-fired as `PACKETAUDIT2_brief.md` with every one
inlined and an explicit *"DO NOT READ regress/artifacts/"* -- so the seat needs no archive access to
do the job.

**This generalises past codex:** a brief that asks a seat to check numbers should carry the numbers'
LOGS, not their paths.  The Ollama transports have always required that because they cannot read
files at all; here it is required for the opposite reason -- a seat that CAN read the archive is
refused for doing so.  *Same remedy, two different causes, and the file-reading seats' version was
not obvious until the filter made it necessary.*

*Recorded as my error rather than a seat failure: the brief was refused for exactly what it
instructed.*

*** THE ENTRY DIRECTLY ABOVE IS WRONG AND I AM CORRECTING IT WITHIN THE HOUR.  THE ARCHIVE-READING
BRIEF **ANSWERED**. ***

I recorded that the packet-audit brief was refused for directing the seat into `regress/artifacts/`,
and prescribed inlining the logs.  **The refusal count was 25 and the seat then produced an
18,687-byte answer** -- it retried and succeeded, reading the archive throughout and citing
individual log lines.  Meanwhile the INLINED re-fire sat at 2 refusals and a 0-byte answer.

> **SO A REFUSAL LINE IS NOT A TERMINAL STATE, AND MY OWN THREE-STATE DISCRIMINATOR SAYS SO
> WRONGLY.**  It reads *"refusal line present -> reroute; a retry will not help."*  **Measured
> false here: twenty-five refusal lines preceded a complete answer.**  The discriminating fact is
> the `.txt`, not the `.err` -- a non-empty answer means the seat got there whatever the stderr says.

**WHAT SURVIVES:** the two PASS-3 and WITNESS refusals were terminal (0-byte answers), so the
capability finding about the ask-again and witness-design shapes is unaffected.  What is refuted is
the inference that ANY refusal line means the seat is unavailable.

*Recorded here at length because I wrote the false version into this row, into the checkpoint and
into the adjudication packet within the last hour, and a correction that arrives quietly is worse
than the error.*

rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c: a DECLINED pixel GET still lets the caller perform its dependent PUT, so the destination is written with fg
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-06 from the `sgirandompixel' design panel, where **codex argued for it as part of that round
and grok argued for filing it -- and grok's scoping was taken**, because a return value plus every GET site
is not ONE SITE and the reopening rule says a round takes one.

After `sgirandompixel', `horrible_getputpixel()' leaves `*color' alone on a declined GET, so the caller's
own `uint32_t color = fg' stands and the PUT writes the FOREGROUND.  That is DETERMINISTIC, which is the
whole gain of that round -- and it is still a write of data the guest did not ask for.

**codex's form, recorded verbatim because it is the design if this is taken:** give the function an explicit
SUCCESS RESULT; *'unchanged `*color' is merely an output-parameter guarantee: callers must not consume it
following failure'*.  Cover ALL the GET sites -- the source GET, the `oldcolor' GET used by ROPs, and MTE's
`bg' GET.  **AND ITS WARNING, which is the sketch rule and is the reason this is not a one-liner:**
*'preserve coordinate advancement and stipple rotation when suppressing a pixel's PUT; an early `continue'
can bypass those updates'* -- anchors `src_x += step_x' and `Rotate the stipple pattern'.

The shipped detector already discriminates this: `lin_b is fg' expects fg TODAY, and under a skip-PUT fix it
would expect the PRE-PAINT instead.  So the oracle-correction rule applies again and the row set is known in
advance.

*** A SHIPPED ROW ACTIVELY REQUIRES THE BEHAVIOUR THIS ROW WOULD REMOVE.  Found by the codex seat
on the `sgirandomcolour` pass-2 brief, 2026-09-07. ***

`regress/sgi_re_randompixel_probe.py`'s **`lin_b is fg` expects FG rather than the destination's
prepaint** -- i.e. it asserts that the dependent PUT DID run after a declined GET.

> **So a general failed-GET/skip-PUT repair would make that existing row FAIL.**  An MTE-only repair
> would escape it; the general one collides with a shipped oracle.

**That is the oracle-correction rule's territory** -- the row's contract has to be adjudicated
explicitly before the code changes, and if it is re-pinned the re-pin must be measured RED on the
committed build first.  *Recorded here rather than acted on: the collision is the finding.*

rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c: DE_MODE_LIN_B is documented in crmfbreg.h and not implemented -- and implementing it as LIN_A-with-the-other-array was REFUSED for want of a warrant
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-06.  `horrible_getputpixel()' implements tlb_mode 0, 1, 2 and 4; **LIN_B extracts to 5 and
falls to the default arm**, which now declines.  `re_linear_b[]' exists, is written by the same width-checked
store path as `re_linear_a[]', and case 4 is four lines -- so the tempting fix is one more case.

*** THE PANEL REFUSED TO ENDORSE THAT, and the reasoning is the ADDITION LICENCE working. ***  codex: case 4
itself carries `TODO... probably not correct!'; and the MTE path that does select either array checks
`entry & 0x80000000' for validity and searches BY PAGE, while case 4 indexes DIRECTLY and FORCES validity.
**Symmetry between the two arrays is supporting evidence, not a transferred warrant for DE translation.**
Before implementing, obtain a DE address/validity reference or a hardware comparison using DISTINCT A/B
mappings.

It also caught that the witness probe programs only LINEAR_A, so *'merely changing its expected LIN_B result
to SRC_VAL would be unjustified'* -- the instrument would be asserting a behaviour nothing established.

rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c: the COLOUR-mode PUT default arm writes FOUR random() bytes to guest memory, and DE_MODE_TYPE_YCRCB -- a DOCUMENTED mode -- reaches it (verified: YCRCB appears 0 times in the file)
rows.witness: probe:regress/artifacts/sgirandomcolour/witness_20260910/HEAD_run1.out -- rung 3 (agy, the fallback measuring seat), 2/5 on the committed build 1ce8296 (both unsupported-type PUTs RED: host-PRNG bytes where the paint was), 5/5 on the fix with the same script, then 16/16 with the first eleven detector rows (fix_20260910/FIX519_detector_run3.out) and 19/19 with the fourteen (t2/BASE_19.raw, the final instrument on the final source)
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-06.  **FOUND BY GROK** on the `sgirandompixel' design panel, as a residual it explicitly said
to file rather than grow the round with: *'`default:' of the COLOUR-mode switch still does
`buf[n] = random()' and then writes those bytes.  Same class, different arm.'*

**VERIFIED BY READING before filing**: four `random()' calls at dev_sgi_re.c, anchor `buf[0] = random();',
in the colour-mode `default:'.  `sgirandompixel' removed the ONE in `horrible_getputpixel()'; these four
remain and are the reason `grep -c 'random()'` on that file is still non-zero after the fix.

Nobody else on that panel saw it -- not codex, not the packet-fed seats, not me -- and I had read the file
several times that evening.  The design is presumably the same member 3 (decline + latched announce), but
the observable differs: this arm fills a BUFFER rather than a single caller variable, so what a declined
fill should leave is its own question and the detector shape is not simply copied.

*** MAIN-LOOP RECORD 2026-09-07 (assess stage) -- written into state_note, NOT into `entries'. ***
`entries' is the SEAT ANSWER list: check_stage_panels.py counts entries to decide whether a stage's
nine seats were fired, and gen_dashboard.py REFUSES TO RENDER on a seat id no column declares.  A
main-loop note parked there is not merely mis-filed -- it MANUFACTURES A SEAT ANSWER THAT NEVER
HAPPENED, which is the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape inverted.  Seven such entries were
written during this session and all seven were migrated here when the generator refused.

SEVERITY RAISED MED -> HIGH, on a fact DERIVED rather than assumed.  The row said the fix
was *presumably* the same as [[sgirandompixel]]'s and that the observable differed.  **The reachability is now
established and it is the SAME documented-mode structure, not merely the same shape.**

Measured at HEAD, three commands:
  * the PUT colour switch implements exactly FOUR cases -- `DE_MODE_TYPE_' CI, RGB, RGBA, ABGR -- and its
    `default:' is `buf[0..3] = random()';
  * `crmfbreg.h' documents **FIVE** colour types; the fifth is `DE_MODE_TYPE_YCRCB  0x000000f0';
  * `grep -c YCRCB src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c' = **0**.  It is handled nowhere.

And it is reached by an ordinary register write: `color_mode = mode & DE_MODE_TYPE_MASK', mask `0xf0', so a
guest selecting YCRCB lands on the random arm directly.

*** SO THIS IS `#504's OWN SENTENCE AT A SECOND SITE: four of five DOCUMENTED modes work and the fifth
returns random data. ***  `#504` was graded HIGH on exactly that warrant, and this arm is arguably worse in
one respect -- `sgirandompixel' put a random value in `*color' for the CALLER to store, whereas this writes
four random bytes into the tile through `memory_rw(..., MEM_WRITE)' with no intermediary.

**WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and the severity should be read with it: NO WITNESS.**  Nothing here shows a guest
driver selecting YCRCB -- only that the model accepts it and answers with random data.  The rung-3 attempt
looks cheap for the same reason `#504's did (`regress/sgi_re_randompixel_probe.py' already programs this
code path; the colour type is a different field of the same mode word), and it is OWED before this ships.

**The GET side does NOT share the defect** -- its `default:' reads the raw 32-bit value rather than inventing
one, so this is a PUT-only arm.  That asymmetry is itself worth carrying into the design: the two default
arms of one function already disagree about what an unhandled colour type means.

Note this is a DIFFERENT defect from [[sgirebufuninit]] at the same lines: that one is about bytes NOBODY
assigns; this is about bytes assigned from `random()'.  A fix for either leaves the other standing.

*** READY TO RUN AS THE NEXT ROUND.  Three things established 2026-09-07 while `#505` worked in the
same function, none of which this row had. ***

**1. IT IS A DIFFERENT SWITCH FROM THE ONE `#504` FIXED, and the row should say so plainly** -- I nearly
recorded this as the `#499` symmetric-cell shape and it is not.  `#504` de-fanged the **addressing-mode**
default (`default: fatal("unimplemented dst_mode %i ..."); *color = random();`).  This row is the
**colour-mode** default of a different `switch` in the same function:

    default:buf[0] = random();  buf[1] = random();
            buf[2] = random();  buf[3] = random();
            // TODO.
            fatal("[ put: color mode = 0x%x ]\n", color_mode);
    }
    cpu->memory_rw(cpu, cpu->mem, tileptr + ofs, buf, bufdepth, MEM_WRITE, NO_EXCEPTIONS|PHYSICAL);

**There is no `break` and no decline: control falls straight into the write**, so four bytes of host
`random()` land in guest memory at a guest-chosen tile offset.  Same family as `#504`, same function,
different arm -- *related by idiom, not by the one-cell-repair pattern.*

**2. FULLY GUEST-REACHABLE, established by reading rather than assumed.**  `color_mode = mode &
DE_MODE_TYPE_MASK`, and `mode` is the caller's `src_mode`/`dst_mode`, read straight out of `de_reg[]`
from `CRIME_DE_MODE_SRC`/`CRIME_DE_MODE_DST` with **no filtering anywhere on the path**.  The four
implemented types are 0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30; `DE_MODE_TYPE_YCRCB` is **0xf0 and is documented in
`crmfbreg.h`** but unimplemented, so a guest selecting a real, named mode reaches this arm.

**3. A WITNESS IS ONE CONSTANT AWAY.**  `#505` built `regress/sgi_re_rgb_probe.py`,
a rung-3 probe that drives an XFER copy on an unmodified `-E sgi -e ip32` with both ladder controls and a
sibling accept row, and whose `setup()` now takes **both** src and dst modes.  Pointing its `dst_mode` at
`LIN_A | BUFDEPTH_32 | 0xf0` puts YCRCB into the PUT switch and reaches this arm.

  *** THE ORACLE IS THE HARD PART AND IT NEEDS SAYING BEFORE THE ROUND STARTS: THE DEFECT'S OUTPUT IS
  RANDOM, SO NO VALUE ROW CAN PIN IT. ***  `#504` hit exactly this and its answer is the precedent --

## THE DETECTOR -- convergent, and it is a DESTINATION CANARY, not "looks non-random"

Pre-fill the target bytes with a distinctive non-zero canary, execute ONE PUT with a declined mode,
read back, and **pass iff the canary is bit-identical** -- i.e. the oracle is *the store did not
happen*, not *the value is not random*.  A liveness control in the SAME script repeats with a
defined mode (RGBA or CI) and the canary MUST change; without it a dead PUT path greens the round.

*** THE HOLE, and three of the five seats were in it: DO NOT PIN THE TEST TO `0xf0` ALONE. ***
deepseek and kimi both proposed YCRCB `0xf0` as *the* test mode, kimi arguing it is the value a real
guest would plausibly select.  grok:

> *"A mutant `case 0xf0: put_ok = 0; break;` with `default:` still random would escape.  Use at
> least one UNDOCUMENTED value (`0x40` is the first hole) as the primary; `0xf0` can be a second
> vector, not the only one."*

**That is a real escape against the majority design.**  The documented mode is the most tempting
choice and the weakest one, because a mutant can special-case exactly it.

**FOUR MORE STRENGTHENINGS, one per seat, none of them duplicated:**
* **grok** -- vary `bufdepth` over at least {1, 4, 8}, so a mutant that skips the store only when
  `bufdepth == 4` dies.
* **minimax** -- make the oracle **CONJUNCTIVE**: the latch transitioned 0 -> 1 *during that pixel*
  (record the PRE-state) AND `memory_rw` was not called for it.  Either conjunct alone is escapable,
  and recording the pre-state defeats a mutant that pre-sets the latch at init.
* **kimi** -- assert the announce count is **exactly 1**, which is what actually pins the latch.
* **glm** -- assert the ADJACENT bytes are unchanged too, since the write is only `bufdepth` bytes
  at `ofs`; and run twice asserting identical transcripts.

**AND grok'S HONEST LIMIT ON ITS OWN ORACLE:** keeping `buf[i] = random()` while setting
`put_ok = 0` leaves the canary intact, so a destination-only oracle cannot see the leftover
`random()` calls.  It calls that *"a successful (b), not an escape, PROVIDED the patch also deletes
the four `random()` calls -- same edit, not a second oracle"*, and explicitly declines to make

## *** THE BLOCKING PREMISE THREE SEATS RAISED INDEPENDENTLY IS NOW SETTLED -- BY ME, IN TWO READS,
## AND IT SETTLES IN FAVOUR OF THE ROUND. ***

glm, kimi and deepseek each named the SAME single fact as the one that decides whether a witness
exists at all: **does the mode-register write path mask or reject `0xf0` (and the eleven
undocumented values) BEFORE they reach this helper?**  glm put the consequence sharply: if it does,
*"no witness exists, the round is documented-only, and '12 of 16' then describes host-reachable
states no real guest can reach."*

**THERE IS NO VALIDATION.**  `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_de)`:

    :1098  /*  Treat all registers as read/write, by default. ... */
    :1112  d->de_reg[regnr] = idata;              <- unconditional, unmasked

and the `switch (relative_addr)` below it reaches `case CRIME_DE_MODE_DST:` only to `debug()` the
value and `break` -- no mask, no rejection, no range test.  `draw_primitive()` then reads
`d->de_reg[(CRIME_DE_MODE_DST - 0x2000)/4]` straight back, and `horrible_getputpixel()` computes
`color_mode = mode & DE_MODE_TYPE_MASK`.

> **So a guest store of ANY 32-bit value to CRIME_DE_MODE_DST is kept verbatim, and bits 4-7 select
> among all 16 colour modes -- twelve of which reach the `random()` arm.  The witness is
> constructible and the round is NOT documented-only.**

*The file's own comment is the authority here, which is the strongest form: it is not that I failed
to find a validator, it is that the code states it treats these registers as raw read/write.*

**THE REMAINING UNSETTLED ITEM is smaller than it looked:** kimi asked whether `#504`'s witness
itself selected a declined mode.  That is a question about a shipped probe, answerable by reading
`regress/sgi_re_randompixel_probe.py`, and it is no longer load-bearing now that the register path
is settled.

*** THE CENSUS IN THIS ROW'S TITLE IS RIGHT ABOUT THE NAMED CASE AND UNDERSTATES THE SET BY TWELVE
TIMES.  Found by a codex ANALYSIS job 2026-09-08, VERIFIED here before recording. ***

The title says `DE_MODE_TYPE_YCRCB -- a DOCUMENTED mode -- reaches it'.  True, and it is ONE of
TWELVE values that do.

**MEASURED, not taken from the seat:**

    crmfbreg.h:328-333   CI 0x00, RGB 0x10, RGBA 0x20, ABGR 0x30, YCRCB 0xf0, MASK 0xf0
    dev_sgi_re.c:210     uint32_t color_mode = mode & DE_MODE_TYPE_MASK;      *** NO SHIFT ***

    domain of (mode & 0xf0):  16 values -- 0x00 0x10 ... 0xf0
    handled:                   4        -- 0x00 0x10 0x20 0x30
    UNHANDLED:                12        -- 0x40 0x50 0x60 0x70 0x80 0x90 0xa0 0xb0 0xc0 0xd0 0xe0 0xf0
                                            = ELEVEN UNNAMED ENCODINGS + the named YCRCB

**THE MISSING SHIFT IS THE WHOLE POINT.**  The constants look like a small enumeration -- 0, 1, 2, 3
scaled by 16 -- and reading them that way suggests four handled plus one named gap.  But the code
never normalises the field, so the switch compares raw masked values and every one of the sixteen
the mask can produce is a distinct case label.  *A derivation that assumes the obvious shift reads
exactly like a correct one, which is why this was enumerated rather than argued.*

> **THIS IS THE `asicbadaddr` SHAPE EXACTLY, and the carrier already records why it matters: a
> detector built from the wrong census walks the named value, covers a twelfth of the defect, and
> reports full coverage.**  A round that ships a row for YCRCB alone would do precisely that.

*** TWO REACHABILITY REFINEMENTS FROM THE SAME ANSWER, which the row did not have: ***

* **The producer does not filter.**  `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_de)` stores incoming register words without
  narrowing the colour-format bits, and `draw_primitive()` passes the stored mode to the pixel
  helper unnarrowed.  So the drawing-engine caller genuinely exposes all sixteen encodings.
* **The MTE caller constructs only CI or RGBA**, so NEITHER default is reachable through it.  That
  is a real distinction: the round's reachability argument belongs to the drawing engine only, and
  saying "the device reaches it" without naming the caller would be too strong.

*** AND A SECOND, SEPARATE OBSERVATION ABOUT THE BUFFER, recorded because it is NOT the same
defect and must not be folded in silently: `buf` is EIGHT bytes, not four. ***
`dev_sgi_re.c:307` is `uint8_t buf[8];` with the `#100` comment *"bufdepth can be 8 = 1<<((mode>>8)&3)"*.
The PUT `default:` assigns only `buf[0..3]` from `random()`.  **What the remaining four bytes hold,
and whether any bufdepth reads them, is NOT established here and is not claimed.**  It is written
down as an open question for the round rather than as a finding.

WITNESS brief twice -- the construction-shaped ask ("give the exact guest instruction sequence") is
content-filtered, see [[codexcyberflag]].  The identical subject in ANALYSIS form ("how many cases,
what is the domain, what does the default do") answered in full with a verdict line.  **The seat was

SCOPE CHECK, full denominator: seven call sites across two caller functions (four GETs, three PUTs), both argument-producing functions, two register-writer functions with six store statements, and the device initialiser.

**VERDICT: both claims confirmed.** (1) Twelve of sixteen colour-type encodings reach the default arm; nothing in the DE writer or draw_primitive() restricts the type field, and the function's earlier returns (coordinate bounds, tile-index bounds, addressing mode, tile-pointer validity) gate WHETHER a pixel op proceeds and never validate the colour type.  **Denominator correction worth keeping: a YCRCB-only check covers 1/12 of the default-arm encodings and 1/16 of the whole field** -- so a fix or detector built from this row's YCRCB framing covers one twelfth of the door and reports full coverage.

(2) Depth 8 IS reachable and CI is NOT restricted to depth 1: the DE writer preserves bits 9:8 and the helper evaluates `1 << ((mode >> 8) & 3)` without rejecting the fourth encoding.  The header names only three depth encodings and that naming imposes no runtime restriction.

*** AND IT CLOSED THE ONE QUESTION I COULD NOT SETTLE BY READING: THE CALLEE DOES COPY THE REQUESTED LENGTH. ***  memory_rw.c's RAM write is literally `memcpy(memblock + offset, data, len)`; a block-boundary crossing SPLITS the transfer and forwards the remainder rather than truncating; and the device-boundary clamping plus NO_EXCEPTIONS affect MMIO dispatch, not sanitisation of a RAM-write SOURCE buffer.  **The nearby zero-fill operations apply to READS.**  So there is no padding step that would render the uninitialised bytes harmless.

FLOOD CONFIRMED WITH ITS SCOPE: the colour-default diagnostic has no latch and no verbosity guard and execution continues into the write, so the DE line and rectangle loops can produce a per-pixel output flood -- but **MTE's current CI/RGBA construction does not reach the colour default**, so the flood is a DE-path property, not an MTE one.  The existing SGIRE_W_BADMODE latch guards the ADDRESSING diagnostic only.

*Its 'additional issue' -- the GET half consuming more bytes than it reads -- is ALREADY FILED as [[sgirebufuninit]], which names that exact path.  Recorded as independent confirmation, not as new.*

disabled kill (`//exit(1)'), also in `horrible_getputpixel()', also reached on a failed GET.  It returns

that round the two siblings AGREE on the value and DIFFER on the announce**: the mode arm now says so once,
and this one says nothing at all.

Whether that asymmetry should be closed is a real question rather than an obvious yes: a silent decline is
option-set member 2, and the pass-2 seat on that panel noted the tileptr arm *'safely suppresses a put, but a
get leaves foreground -- or the previous copied pixel -- in place'*, which is a DIFFERENT observable from the
mode arm's.  Sibling parity says name the asymmetry, not that every asymmetry is a defect.
