rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c horrible_getputpixel(): uint8_t buf[8] is never initialised and the guest picks how many of its bytes are used -- uninitialised host stack reaches guest-visible memory on PUT and *color on GET
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-07, found while writing the design brief for `sgirandomcolour' -- i.e. by reading the arm NEXT
to the one grok pointed at.  **This is a bigger defect than the row that led me to it, and it needs no
undocumented mode at all.**

`horrible_getputpixel()' declares `uint8_t buf[8];' and NEVER INITIALISES IT.  Verified: no memset in the
function, no initialiser, and the only memsets in the file are the device struct, `rop_used' and `zerobuf'.
The two fields that decide how much of `buf' is USED are decoded from the SAME guest-written mode register
and are INDEPENDENT of each other:

    uint32_t color_mode = mode & DE_MODE_TYPE_MASK;      /* bits 4-7  */
    int bufdepth = 1 << ((mode >> 8) & 3);               /* bits 8-9  -> 1, 2, 4 or 8 */

The colour arms fill a number of bytes fixed by the COLOUR type; the transfer length is `bufdepth'.  Nothing
anywhere makes them agree -- `grep -rn '>> *8) *& *3' src/devices/' finds the decode, its own #100 comment,
and the XFER siblings; NO GUARD.

**TWO REACHABLE UNINITIALISED PATHS, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS:**

* **PUT -- host stack INTO guest-visible memory.**  With the depth field = 3 (`bufdepth' 8) NO colour arm
  writes `buf[4..7]' -- not one of the five, including the correct ones -- and all eight bytes go straight to
  `memory_rw(..., tileptr + ofs, buf, bufdepth, MEM_WRITE, NO_EXCEPTIONS | PHYSICAL)'.  `DE_MODE_TYPE_CI'
  writes only `buf[0]', so CI at any depth above 1 leaks the rest.
* **GET -- host stack INTO `*color', which the caller then STORES.**  The read fills only `bufdepth' bytes,
  then RGB/RGBA/ABGR combine `buf[0..3]'.  Depth field 0 (`bufdepth' 1) with `DE_MODE_TYPE_RGBA' reads ONE
  byte from memory and builds a 32-bit colour from four.  `draw_primitive()' writes that to the destination
  in the same loop iteration -- **the identical caller-consumes-a-failed-read shape `sgirandompixel' just
  fixed one arm of**, reached here with every colour mode documented and implemented.

*** THE #100 COMMENT IS THE TELL, AND IT IS ON THE DECLARATION ITSELF. ***  It reads
`/*  #100: bufdepth can be 8 = 1<<((mode>>8)&3)  */' -- so a previous round worked out that the guest can
demand 8 bytes and GREW THE ARRAY to match, which fixed a stack OVERFLOW.  **It did not ask what fills the
bytes it had just added.**  The array is the right size and the contents are undefined.

SEVERITY: guest-reachable read of uninitialised host stack whose value becomes guest-visible.  In a loop the
stale bytes are usually the PREVIOUS pixel's, so the everyday symptom is wrong colours; on the first call in
a frame they are whatever the host stack held.  Both mode words are ordinary device registers reached by
ordinary stores, and all seven call sites pass one of them.

NOT YET WITNESSED -- filed at once so the finding is durable.  The witness is expected to be cheap because
`regress/sgi_re_randompixel_probe.py' already programs this exact path on unmodified `-E sgi -e ip32' and
needs only a different mode word: its `MODE_LIN_A = 0x1220' is LIN_A | depth-field 2 (`bufdepth' 4) | RGBA,
which is the MATCHED case and leaks nothing.  `0x1020' is the same line with depth field 0.

*** PASS-1 CORRECTION FROM THE GROK SEAT, VERIFIED AGAINST THE HEADER BEFORE BEING ACCEPTED.  MY PATH-A
EXEMPLAR WAS THE WEAKER ONE, AND A FULLY DOCUMENTED VEHICLE EXISTS. ***

The brief drove PATH A with mode `0x1320' -- depth field 3, `bufdepth' 8 -- and called it reachable.  grok:
*"BUFDEPTH in the header is 8/16/32 only -- field 3 is undocumented ... PATH A is live on documented `CI' +
`BUFDEPTH_16/32' (`0x1200'), not only on undocumented depth 8.  The brief's `0x1320' PATH-A vehicle is the
weaker one."*

**CHECKED, not taken on trust** -- `grep -n BUFDEPTH src/include/thirdparty/crmfbreg.h' returns exactly three:

    DE_MODE_BUFDEPTH_8   0x00000000   -> depth field 0 -> bufdepth 1 byte
    DE_MODE_BUFDEPTH_16  0x00000100   -> depth field 1 -> bufdepth 2 bytes
    DE_MODE_BUFDEPTH_32  0x00000200   -> depth field 2 -> bufdepth 4 bytes

**Field value 3 is documented nowhere**, so the brief's own vehicle relies on an undocumented depth -- while
`DE_MODE_TYPE_CI' assigns ONLY `buf[0]' and `DE_MODE_BUFDEPTH_32' transfers FOUR bytes, so `0x1200' leaks
`buf[1..3]' with **every field documented and CI being colour type ZERO**, the reset value.

*(Note the naming trap I had not spotted: the constants are in BITS and the code's `bufdepth' is in BYTES, so
`BUFDEPTH_32' is 4.  That is why `1 << ((mode >> 8) & 3)' maxes at 8 with only three constants defined.)*

**AND IT SETTLED Q1.3, WHICH I HAD EXPLICITLY LEFT OPEN: the destination is RAM, not a device.**  So `#95's
device-read pre-zero does not run AT ALL on either path -- not merely `does not cover the bytes past len'.
Both paths are therefore worse than the brief stated, not better.

**This is the premise-audit opener earning its place for the third recorded time.**  I asked seats to attack
the reachability premise; one did, and the correction STRENGTHENS the finding while WEAKENING the exemplar I
had chosen -- which is exactly the asymmetry the rule exists to surface.

grok's other two calls -- **do not join [[sgirandomcolour]]** (my Q6) and **talk HIGH down to MEDIUM** (my Q5)
-- are NOT actioned here.  They are adjudication questions and the panel is still running; the
provisional-adjudication rule says a ruling short of the roster is provisional on its face, so they wait for
the full six.

*** PASS-1 BRIEF DEFECT, RAISED INDEPENDENTLY BY ALL THREE PACKET-FED SEATS: I ASSERTED A PREMISE THEY
COULD NOT CHECK, AND SAID `SETTLED PREMISES: NONE CARRIED'. ***

No burns -- all three returned real verdicts on a 31 KB brief -- and all three named the same hole:
  * **minimax**: *"the load-bearing premise is NOT CHECKABLE and the brief states it confidently anyway ...
    That single fact -- the body of `cpus/memory_rw.c' -- is what would settle it, and the brief should not
    have stated it as confidently as it did."*
  * **glm**: *"reachability rests on one uncheckable premise"*; it treated every grep and scan output in the
    brief as uncheckable and said so.
  * **deepseek**: caught a SECOND one I had not noticed -- *"the brief's table for `default'/YCRCB assumes
    `fatal()' returns"*.  My PATH-A table lists the `default:' arm as filling `buf[0..3]' and then writing;
    **if `fatal()' exited, that arm would never reach the write and the row would be wrong.**

**BOTH RESOLVE IN THE FINDING'S FAVOUR, WHICH IS NOT THE POINT.**  Checked at HEAD: `fatal()' in
`src/core/debugmsg.c' is `va_start / va_debug / va_end' with **no exit and no early-out**, so the arm does
reach the write; and grok, a FILE-READING seat, settled the other by reporting the destination is RAM rather
than a device, so `#95's pre-zero never runs at all.

**THE DEFECT IS THAT I MADE A DOCUMENTED MISTAKE THE TEMPLATE WARNS ABOUT IN CAPITALS.**  `BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md`
section C is headed *"MANDATORY.  COPY FORWARD.  THIS IS THE ONE THAT GETS DROPPED"*, and my brief wrote
*"SETTLED PREMISES: none carried -- first brief of this campaign"*.  **That was true about the CAMPAIGN and
false about the QUESTIONS**: the template's own test is whether a seat could build an *if X then A, else B*
answer on the premise -- and deepseek built exactly that on `fatal()'.  The obligation is PER-PACKET and
BROAD, *whatever pass or round settled it*, and `fatal()'-does-not-exit was settled long ago; the carrier
records it costing the minimax seat its answer twice before.

**THE TRANSPORT PREAMBLE DID ITS JOB AND THE BRIEF DID NOT.**  `panel_ollama.py' asks a packet-fed seat to
NAME any premise it cannot settle instead of guessing, and all three did precisely that rather than
ratifying -- which is the behaviour that makes a packet-fed seat worth firing.  Score this as a BRIEF DEFECT,
never as three weak answers.

**FOR THE PASS-2 PACKET:** inline (a) `fatal()'s four-line body, (b) the `memory_rw' pre-zero site with the
branch that gates it, and (c) grok's RAM-not-device finding with its warrant.  All three are one or two lines
each and they are what these seats spent their answers asking for.

*** THE CLASS SCAN'S DENOMINATOR IS WRONG, AND THE WAY IT IS WRONG IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.  Codex seat,
pass 1, verdict GO-WITH-CHANGES. ***

The brief claimed SIX unpinned-length sites and FIVE stack-buffer write sites, and concluded that
`dev_sgi_re.c' is the only member of the class in the device tree.  **Codex found four write sites both of my
scanners missed**, and named the mechanism for each:

  * `dev_dec21143.c' descriptor writebacks (two sites) -- *"Nested argument commas defeat the scanner's
    splitting."*  **That is limit 1, which the brief DISCLOSED**, demonstrated on real sites.
  * `dev_dreamcast_maple.c' response writes (two sites) -- *"whose casts prevent recognition of the buffer
    argument."*  **That limit was NOT disclosed and I did not know about it.**

All four are SAFE (initialised via `store_le32', or cast forms that do fill the buffer), **so the CONCLUSION
survives and the DENOMINATOR does not.**  Those are different claims and the brief conflated them.

*** THE METHODOLOGICAL POINT IS SHARPER THAN THE COUNT, AND IT LANDS ON THE BRIEF'S BEST-LOOKING EVIDENCE: ***
*"Agreement between scanners sharing parsing limitations is not exhaustive corroboration."*  The brief
presented TWO independent scans agreeing as strong evidence of scope.  **They are not independent** -- both
split `memory_rw' arguments on commas with the same regex, so both are blind to the same call shapes.  Two
derivers that can fail the same way are ONE deriver run twice, and this project has already recorded that
exact lesson on the `sgirekills' count, where two agreeing greps both counted comment lines.

**Two of the brief's SAFE verdicts also need narrowing, per the same seat:**
  * **GBE** -- the divisor is nonzero and the transfer is bounded, but *"conversion still loops to 512 after a
    shorter read"*, which can consume unfilled bytes.  Codex declines to call it a demonstrated guest
    disclosure (the forwarded framebuffer prefix is smaller) but says it *"invalidates the blanket
    initialization-safety claim"*.  Correct: my check established the LENGTH bound and said nothing about
    consumption.
  * **PXG** -- `#207' bounds the later SRAM copy's SOURCE SPAN without bounding CONSUMPTION, and the initial
    SRAM copy is unchecked.  The enumerated 3080-byte PX maximum stands; what falls is treating it as proof of
    complete initialisation across BOTH branches.

**Consequence for this round: the scope sentence must be rewritten before pass 2** -- from *"the only member
of this class in the device tree"* to *"the only DEFECTIVE member among the sites these two scanners can
see, whose blind spots are nested-comma argument lists and cast buffer arguments"*.  The two new correctness
findings the same seat raised are filed separately as [[sgirergbroundtrip]] and [[sgimtedepth4dead]].

*** PASS-1 ADJUDICATION.  EVIDENCE BASIS: 6 of 9 -- six scriptable seats ANSWERED (0 walled, 0 down, 0
burns, novelty 93-100%); agy DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED on the measurement reserve; opus5 and fable5 HELD for the
2026-09-09 adjudication by standing owner directive.  The three absences are DIRECTED, not failures -- but the
provisional-adjudication rule still applies and this ruling is provisional on its face. ***

**THE FINDING SURVIVES ALL SIX.**  Nobody disputed that `buf' is uninitialised, that the two mode fields are
independent, or that `#95' fails to cover the paths.  What changed is the FRAMING, in three places, and every
correction came from a seat rather than from me.

**D1 -- Q6, ONE ROUND OR TWO: SEPARATE.  My proposal REFUTED, and refuted with a measurement.**  Three seats
said separate (grok, kimi, deepseek); kimi proved it: a shared *destination is deterministic across runs*
oracle is **VACUOUS for this row**, because `srandom(tv.tv_sec ^ getpid() ^ tv.tv_usec)' makes `random()' vary
per run while STALE-STACK REUSE UNDER A FIXED GUEST PROGRAM IS RUN-DETERMINISTIC -- so the buggy build PASSES.
Verified at `src/core/main.c:688-691'.  **I asked the panel not to let the convenience of one round drive the
answer, and it did not.**  ACCEPTED: two rounds.

**D2 -- Q5, SEVERITY: grok says MEDIUM, kimi says HIGH *conditionally*.  RESOLVED BY KIMI'S CONDITION, not by
counting.**  kimi: HIGH is defensible for this fork's mandate *'provided the entry carries the corrected
reachability framing ... Do not ship the entry with "no undocumented value anywhere" in it.'*  The row KEEPS
HIGH and the framing is corrected here.  grok's MEDIUM rests on disclosure impact, which is genuinely weak (4
stale bytes per pixel, usually prior pixels); kimi's HIGH rests on the fork's mandate and on this defect
falsifying `#95's *closes the whole class* sentence in the same batch that edited this array.  **That is the
stronger warrant for THIS fork**, and it is the one I take.  Recorded as a SPLIT, not as agreement.

**F1 -- A FALSE SENTENCE IN MY BRIEF, and it is NOT being edited.**  The brief says the paths are reached
*'with no undocumented value anywhere'*.  **False**: PATH A's MAXIMAL form (`bufdepth' 8) needs the
undocumented depth field 3.  Documented forms exist -- CI x BUFDEPTH_16/32 for PATH A, and PATH B entirely --
so the FINDING stands while the blanket phrase does not.  **The sent brief is left BYTE-UNCHANGED on purpose:
it is the frozen packet six seats reviewed, and rewriting it would falsify the record of what was asked.**
The correction lives here and goes into the pass-2 packet.

**F2 -- THE WITNESS IS NOT `ONE CONSTANT'.**  kimi: it needs a register plus the `step_x' twin, or ZERO extra
registers via a PUT-only RECT path.  My cost claim was optimistic; the PUT-only path is the cheaper design and
was not in the brief at all.

**F3 -- INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCE ON A NEW DEFECT.**  codex and kimi BOTH found the dead `if (depth == 4)'
without knowledge of each other.  Independent convergence is the one kind of agreement that IS evidence, so
[[sgimtedepth4dead]] ships with two witnesses to its existence.

**OWED BEFORE PASS 2**, from §C2 and the three packet-fed seats who each asked for it: inline `fatal()'s body,
the `memory_rw' pre-zero site with its gating branch, and grok's RAM-not-device finding with its warrant.

*** UNDER-HARVESTED REVIEW, CORRECTED 2026-09-07.  I READ THIS SEAT'S ANSWER FOR ITS NEW FINDINGS AND
STOPPED.  IT ALSO REFUTED FOUR OF MY CLAIMS AND **REJECTED MY WITNESS DESIGN**, AND I RECORDED NONE OF IT.
THIS IS THE UNREAD-REVIEW CLASS, ON AN ANSWER I HAD ALREADY OPENED. (regress/artifacts/sgirebufuninit/pass1_panel/codex.txt) ***

**1. MY WITNESS DESIGN IS REJECTED, and the reason is architectural rather than a detail.**  I proposed
painting a first pixel so `buf' holds KNOWN bytes, then reading a second at a mismatched depth and asserting
the result carries bytes from the first.  codex: *"Separate automatic objects have no architectural promise
of retaining each other's contents.  Register allocation, inlining, and intervening calls matter."*  And the
same objection kills the other direction: *"**Path A has the same problem:** observing an unassigned byte
does not guarantee that its value differs from the intended padding."*  **I flagged that risk myself in the
brief -- `an oracle of "the value is wrong" can pass by luck' -- proposed a fix for it, and did not record
that the fix was refused.**

**The prescribed measurement instead: an ATTRIBUTED INITIALIZEDNESS RESULT per direction** -- MemorySanitizer
or Valgrind Memcheck -- *"tied to the reviewed build, together with passing functional controls"*, with the
caveat that *"merely copying undefined bytes need not produce an immediate diagnostic"*, so instrumentation
coverage must be established rather than assumed.  **That is a different kind of round from the one I was
planning** and it is why this row is not next in the queue.

**2. `LIN_A cannot be refused' IS FALSE.**  I wrote that case 4 FORCES the valid bit so the arm is reached
unconditionally.  codex: *"remove 'LIN_A cannot be refused': its index guard can return before the buffer
code."*  `tile_nr = x >> 12; if (tile_nr >= 32) return;` -- an early return I read past.

**3. `THE WITNESS IS ONE CONSTANT CHANGED' IS FALSE.**  *"The existing probe uses its LIN_A constant for the
destination and matched control as well as a source case.  Changing that shared constant changes the
observation path and the control simultaneously."*  My cost estimate was wrong for the same reason kimi's
correction said so, and I recorded kimi's and not this one.

**4. `UNINITIALISED ON EVERY PATH' OVERSTATES IT.**  *"matched operations initialize every byte they
consume."*  The defect is the MISMATCHED pairs, not the buffer in general.

**5. MY `WORSE THAN I SAID' CLAIM ABOUT RAM IS WRONG.**  I recorded that grok's RAM-not-device finding makes
both paths worse.  codex: *"**RAM does not inherently make Path B worse:** a successful RAM read defines the
requested prefix through `memcpy'; the missing suffix is the same problem."*

**6. NOT ALL SEVEN CALL SITES TAKE THE GUEST MODE WORDS** -- *"the two MTE sites construct their own modes"*.
My reachability paragraph implies all seven.

**7. SEVERITY: MED, not HIGH.**  *"HIGH is not established by inheriting #95's severity."*  And it refuses
the downgrade too: *"'usually the previous pixel' and 'first call in a frame' are unsupported explanations of
stack contents.  They cannot justify downgrading this to a cosmetic rendering defect."*  **Both of my
severity arguments were unsupported, in opposite directions.**  Lowered to MED provisionally, with potential
host information disclosure recorded as unestablished rather than assumed either way.

*** THE PROCESS FAILURE IS THE POINT AND IT IS THE THIRD INSTANCE TONIGHT. ***  I opened this file, extracted
the two NEW defects and the census correction, and stopped -- because new findings are what I was looking
for.  **A seat that refutes your premises is easy to under-read precisely because its corrections are not
phrased as discoveries.**  The same failure hit the `lcabadval` answer (an eleventh site missed) and the
`alphaswpctxptbr` premises.  All three were answers already on disk.

*** THE STRONGEST REACHABILITY VEHICLE WAS IN THE KIMI ANSWER ALL ALONG, AND IT IS ALL-DOCUMENTED.
Harvested and verified 2026-09-07 (regress/artifacts/sgirebufuninit/pass1_panel/kimi.txt). ***

Everything above argues reachability from the DE path and concedes that PATH A's maximal form needs the
undocumented depth field 3.  **There is a third vehicle that needs nothing undocumented at all**, and it is
the one a real driver uses: `do_mte_transfer()' constructs its own modes with NO colour bits (so CI), because
the `if (depth == 4)' that would set RGBA is dead code -- see [[sgimtedepth4dead]], raised to HIGH on this.

CI fills only `buf[0]'; `MTE_DEPTH_16' and `MTE_DEPTH_32' are documented and give `bufdepth' 2 and 4.  **So
every MTE fill at those depths leaks 1 or 3 uninitialised bytes per pixel, with every value documented**, on
the path kimi names as used by `crmfb_fill_rect'.

**This also settles the `not all seven call sites take the guest mode words' correction** recorded above from
the codex seat: the two MTE sites construct their own modes -- and constructing them is exactly what makes
them leak.  The two corrections are the same fact seen from opposite sides, and I recorded one without
noticing it implied the other.

**AND BOTH FILE-READING SEATS INDEPENDENTLY REACHED THE DETECTOR REQUIREMENT:** the oracle must assert
VALUES, not determinism.  kimi's proof is the sharper one -- post-fix PATH B yields a deterministic value AND
the `bufdepth'-sized mutant yields the previous pixel's bytes, which are *also* deterministic under stack
reuse, so *"a determinism oracle CANNOT catch the mutant"*.  Two seats, two routes, one conclusion.

*** FOURTH UNDER-HARVESTED ANSWER, AND THE RICHEST PER BYTE: THE GROK SEAT'S 15 KB
(regress/artifacts/sgirebufuninit/pass1_panel/grok.txt).  IT ANSWERED THE OPTION-SET QUESTION WITH GREPPED IN-TREE PRECEDENT, NAMED
THREE MEMBERS I HAD NOT, ARGUED THE DISPOSITION I WAS LEANING TOWARD IS WRONG, AND FOUND THE MTE CHAIN
INDEPENDENTLY.  I HAD RECORDED ONLY ITS BUFDEPTH CORRECTION. ***

**1. THE MTE CHAIN, INDEPENDENTLY.**  *"16- and 32-bit MTE TLB fills therefore always run as CI + matching
bufdepth.  32-bit fill writes `bg''s low byte plus three uninit bytes.  Comment at :1322 says NetBSD
`crmfb_fill_rect' uses this."*  **So TWO seats found it and I missed it from both** -- and grok additionally
pinned the in-file comment naming the driver, which I had attributed to kimi alone.

**Its fix-order point is sharper than the one I recorded:** *"Do NOT join: fixing `== 4' to `== 32' changes
MTE 32-bit COLOUR semantics, which memset does not.  Memset would turn that path into 'low byte + zeros' --
defined, still wrong."*  I had noted that repairing the dead branch alone MASKS the leak; grok's is the dual
and it matters as much -- **the memset fix leaves the MTE path DEFINED AND STILL WRONG**, because the colour
semantics are a separate defect from the initialisation.  Neither fix subsumes the other.

**2. THREE OPTION-SET MEMBERS I DID NOT NAME**, and it reached them by grepping rather than reasoning:
    6.  `uint8_t buf[8] = {0};`  -- the C99 form, same observable as a memset
    7.  CLAMP THE TRANSFER to bytes filled (`len = min(bufdepth, filled)`) -- guest-visible difference: the
        OLD DESTINATION BYTES SURVIVE, which is neither zeros nor stale stack
    8.  IMPLEMENT the modes (YCRCB, 64-bit depth) -- and it refused this itself on the ADDITION LICENCE: no
        CRIME DE pixel-packing datasheet exists in `_scratchpad/`

**3. THE IN-TREE PRECEDENTS, WHICH IS WHAT THE OPTION-SET RULE ASKS FOR AND I DID NOT DO:**
    * **this function's own RGB PUT already pads with zero** (`buf[3] = 0`) -- in-function precedent for
      DEFINED PADDING rather than refusal;
    * `dev_dreamcast_maple.c' does `memset(buf, 0, 8)' then a partial fill then `MEM_WRITE' -- **the same
      shape, and the house answer there is zero the whole array**;
    * `dev_sgi_gbe.c' (`#196') renders an unimplemented colour type as BLACK -- defined zeros, no `fatal'
      flood;
    * MTE's own `zerobuf' is memset before its write, in this same file.

**4. IT ARGUES DECLINE IS THE WRONG DISPOSITION, AND THE REASON TIES BACK TO THE MTE CHAIN:**
*"`CI' + `BUFDEPTH_32' is a plausible 8-bit index in a 32-bit container (RGB already pads).  Declining it
would also break the MTE 16/32-bit TLB fill path, which ALREADY EMITS THAT PAIR.  No hardware evidence it is
illegal."*  **That is decisive against member 4** and I had not connected the two facts -- the very pair a
decline would reject is the one the model's own MTE path generates.

Its recommendation is **(1)/(6), full-object zero**, with the comment saying plainly that hardware padding is
unknown and this is defined behaviour rather than a CRIME model -- which is also what the codex seat
independently chose.

*** 5. AN APPARENT DISAGREEMENT I COLLAPSED, RESOLVED HERE BY READING BOTH RATHER THAN PICKING ONE. ***
I recorded codex's *"RAM does not inherently make PATH B worse"* as a correction of my summary.  grok says
the opposite in its heading: *"PATH B is worse than the brief said."*  **Reading both: they are not in
conflict.**  grok's point is that `#95' does not run AT ALL on a RAM destination, so nothing pre-zeroes
anything; codex's is that a successful RAM read still DEFINES the requested prefix through `memcpy', so only
the suffix beyond `bufdepth' is undefined -- which is the same defect either way.  **codex is right on the
technical point and grok is right about the brief's framing.**  Recording only one of them, as I did, loses
that.

*** THE THREE PRECEDENTS VERIFIED, AND THE THIRD IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN PRIOR RULING ON THE SAME
QUESTION.  Checked 2026-09-07 -- grok said `grep, not argument', so they were grepped. ***

    buf[3] = 0;                         dev_sgi_re.c, this function's own RGB PUT      CONFIRMED
    memset(buf, 0, 8);                  dev_dreamcast_maple.c, twice (:285, :330)      CONFIRMED
    *r = *g = *b = 0;                   dev_sgi_gbe.c #196                             CONFIRMED

**The `#196' comment is the decisive one and it is BY THIS PROJECT'S OWN SEATS:**

    default:/*  #196: (Codex/Fable) d->color_mode is guest-controlled; an
                unimplemented WID mode must not exit() the host (get_rgb is
                per-pixel, so don't fatal()-flood either) -- render black.  */
            *r = *g = *b = 0;

**That is the same question already answered**: a GUEST-CONTROLLED unimplemented colour mode, in a PER-PIXEL
helper, on a SIBLING SGI framebuffer -- and the ruling was DEFINED ZEROS, with the per-pixel property given
explicitly as the reason not to `fatal()'-flood.  It is the identical reasoning `sgirandompixel' used for its
latch, so the house doctrine is consistent across three rounds.

**SO THE DISPOSITION IS SETTLED BY TRANSFERRED WARRANT RATHER THAN BY PREFERENCE:** full-object zero, with a
comment saying plainly that hardware padding is unknown and this is defined behaviour rather than a CRIME
model.  Both file-reading seats reached it independently, and `#196' is a fourth vote from a round that
already shipped.

*This is the option-set rule working exactly as written -- `GREP THE FORK FOR AN EXISTING IDIOM; the tree's
own precedents are part of the design space'.  I did not do that; grok did, and it produced a better answer
than the argument I was assembling.*

*** FIFTH UNDER-HARVESTED ANSWER -- THE PACKET-FED SEATS.  glm's contains a DEFECT NOBODY ELSE FOUND
(filed as [[sgilinearnegidx]]) and a BETTER VERSION OF MY OWN #95 ARGUMENT. ***

**glm's `#95' warrant is stronger than the one I wrote and does not depend on reading the source:**
*"zeroing past `len' would itself be an OOB write on any caller with a tight buffer ... So every
MEMORY-SAFE implementation of `#95' zeroes at most `bufdepth' bytes, and PATH B's `buf[bufdepth..3]' are
stale under all of them, not merely the described one.  PATH A is a `MEM_WRITE' whose source is `buf'; a
write-side pre-zero cannot exist there without destroying the payload of every device write in the tree.
Survival against `#95' is OVER-DETERMINED, not lucky."*  My version rested on the pre-zero happening to be
gated on `MEM_READ'; glm's shows no memory-safe implementation could behave otherwise.

**And a correction to my own §3b:** I wrote that `#95' zeroes `buf[0..bufdepth-1]' unconditionally.  glm:
*"that is the device branch only -- the stronger case presented as fact, harmless to the claim."*

**minimax's witness-table point, recorded with its own arithmetic slip corrected:** it observes that the
witness table lists only RGBA mode words and omits the CI cases, which is fair -- CI leaks at any depth above
1 and no row drives it.  Its example value is wrong, though: it calls `0x1210' *LIN_A | depth 2 | CI*, and
`0x1210 & 0xf0' is `0x10' = RGB, not CI (`0x00').  **The observation stands and the constant does not.**

*** SHARPENED 2026-09-07 BY THE glm SEAT on the `sgirergbroundtrip` pass-1 panel (_scratchpad/panel_20260907_051055), and it is
wider than this row said. ***

    "per the code's own #100 comment a bufdepth of 8 makes every named PUT case transmit four
     uninitialized stack bytes to guest memory; a bufdepth-8 GET silently drops the high half;
     and with bufdepth 1 or 2 the RGB/RGBA/ABGR GETs read uninitialized buf[2..3]."

**THREE DISTINCT EXPOSURES, not one**, and the row had only the first:
  (a) bufdepth 8 PUT -- `buf[4..7]` are never written by ANY arm, so four uninitialised stack bytes
      go to guest memory through `memory_rw(..., MEM_WRITE)`;
  (b) bufdepth 8 GET -- the high half is read into buf and then silently discarded, since every GET
      arm reads at most four bytes.  Not a leak; a correctness gap;
  (c) **bufdepth 1 or 2 GET -- the RGB, RGBA and ABGR arms read `buf[2..3]` that `memory_rw` never
      filled.**  This is the one the row did not have, and it is the mirror of (a): a LEAK INTO THE
      GUEST'S OWN PIXEL VALUE rather than into guest memory.

**THE GUARD/BODY SPLIT IS WHY ALL THREE EXIST:** the colour type is bits 4-7 of the mode word and
`bufdepth` is bits 8-9 of the SAME word, read independently.  Nothing couples them, so a guest
selects a four-byte colour type with a one-byte transfer length whenever it likes.

*Recorded from `#505`'s pre-table GUARD-FIELD-vs-BODY-FIELD check, which found the same disagreeing
state independently and then DECLINED to row it -- the exposure is identical before and after that
round's edit (the shipped GET read three bytes, the fixed one reads three bytes), so a row there
would attribute a pre-existing defect to a round that neither created nor cured it.*

*** PASS-1 DESIGN AUDIT, 2026-09-07 -- BY grok, BECAUSE CODEX REFUSED THE BRIEF.
`regress/artifacts/sgirebufuninit/grok_pass1_20260907.txt`, 18 kB. ***

**VERDICT:** *"GO-WITH-CHANGES.  Zero-fill `buf` at its current declaration is the right fix for
THIS class and is the whole fix OF this class.  It is not the packing fix, it is not PUT-only, and
no single-access guest value of 0 can pin it.  S1 and S5 hold.  S2's decode holds.  S3's GET
overstates RGB.  S4's quotes exist and its site-count does not."*

**Q1/Q2 ANSWERED, and Q2's cost objection dissolved by a fact I did not have:** *"It is declared
AFTER the coordinate / `tlb_mode` / `tileptr`-valid early returns, so a zero-fill at that site is not
paid on declined pixels."*  So the per-pixel cost applies only to pixels that were going to be
transferred anyway -- which removes the reason to prefer a narrower site.

**Q3 ANSWERED, and it is the answer I asked for rather than the one I wanted:** *"no single-access
guest value of `0` can pin it."*  A value oracle cannot distinguish "filled with zeros" from
"happened to be zeros", which is what the brief suspected and what the round must now design around.

*** MY S3 WAS WRONG IN ITS EMPHASIS, AND grok's ENUMERATION IS BETTER THAN MY PROSE. ***  I led with
depth 8; the severe case is CI:

    PUT bytes transferred with no store:
                              depth 1   depth 2   depth 4     depth 8
      CI                      none      buf[1]    buf[1..3]   buf[1..7]
      RGB/RGBA/ABGR/default   none      none      none        buf[4..7]

**CI at depth 4 already transfers three unstored bytes**, which needs no unusual depth at all -- and
the MTE path forces CI (see [[sgimtedepth4dead]]).  *"emphasis on depth 8 is the weak vehicle."*

**S2 REFINED, and the refinement matters for how this is described:** on the MTE path the colour bits
are NOT a second guest field.  `src_mode`/`dst_mode` are built as `(tlb << 10) + (depth_field << 8)`
with no type bits, so `color_mode` is pinned at 0 (CI) unless the dead branch fires.  *"That is a
constant colliding with a guest depth, not two independent guest fields."*  The two-independent-fields
story is true of the DE path and false of the MTE path.

*** TWO NEW FINDINGS UNDER THE FOUND-SOMETHING-ELSE LICENCE: ***
  1. **`DE_MODE_PIXDEPTH_*` (bits 2-3) is never read by `dev_sgi_re.c` at all.**  A third mode field
     the device ignores entirely.
  2. **A WRONG RECORD IN PRODUCT CODE, verified by reading:** `dev_sgi_re.c:732` says
     `// bufdepth = 1, 2, or 4.` immediately above
     `int src_bufdepth = 1 << ((src_mode >> 8) & 3);` -- which yields **1, 2, 4 or 8**.  The `#100`
     round grew `buf[8]` precisely because the decode reaches 8, so this comment was already false
     when that round shipped.  **L4, cheap, and it belongs to whichever round next touches this
     file.**

**S4's SITE COUNT IS WRONG AND ITS QUOTES ARE NOT.**  I wrote that `memory_rw.c` zero-fills at three
sites; grok says the count does not hold and flagged in its own trace that *"GET versus PUT may not
share a `#95` path"*.  **That distinction is load-bearing and I had glossed it:** `#95` zero-fills a
READ buffer for `len` bytes on a FAILED access.  It therefore does nothing for a PUT (a write), and
on a successful GET it fills exactly `bufdepth` bytes -- never `buf[2..3]` beyond them.  **So the
transferred warrant is weaker than the brief claimed: `#95` establishes the fork's ETHOS for this
class, not a mechanism that already covers these calls.**

*Recorded as the round's own premise-audit result: of five settled premises, two survived intact, one
was refined, one had its emphasis corrected, and one had its supporting count refuted.*

*** A SECOND, INDEPENDENT AUDIT AGREES ON THE FIX AND GOES FURTHER ON THE ORACLE.  codex, via the
REWORDED brief (`codex_reworded_20260907.txt`) after the original was refused. ***

**VERDICT:** *"Zero-initialize all eight bytes at the existing declaration.  That completes the local
initialization repair in both directions, but does not establish correct pixel-format or MTE
behavior.  **No guest-visible value or write-count oracle can reliably prove initialization
occurred.**"*

**TWO SEATS, TWO TRANSPORTS, SAME FIX.**  grok: *"Zero-fill `buf` at its current declaration is the
right fix for THIS class and is the whole fix OF this class."*  codex: *"Zero-initialize all eight
bytes at the existing declaration."*  Both add the same caveat -- it repairs initialisation and does
NOT repair the packing/format defect, which is [[sgimtedepth4dead]]'s territory.  **The design is
settled.**

*** THE ORACLE IS HARDER THAN THE NEIGHBOURING ROUND ASSUMED, AND THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING.
***  grok said no single-access guest VALUE can pin it.  codex rules out the WRITE-COUNT oracle as
well -- and a write-count oracle is exactly what a seat proposed for [[sgirandomcolour]]
(*"observe ZERO MEM_WRITE calls from an unsupported PUT"*).  **That proposal survives for
`sgirandomcolour`, where the question is whether a write HAPPENS; it does not transfer to this row,
where the question is what the written bytes CONTAIN.**  Two rounds, one idiom, and it is valid in
only one of them.

**CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROUND'S SHAPE:** if no black-box guest-visible oracle can prove
initialisation, this round's detector cannot be a rung-3 probe of the ordinary kind.  The candidates
are an offline differential over the arms, or a `harness:` witness under the ladder's fifth term.
**That must be decided BEFORE the fix, not after** -- the round is otherwise a one-line edit with no
way to defend it.

**AND THE CEILING FOR THIS ROW IS NOW STATED CLEANLY** (same answer, Q1): *"initializing the buffer
changes neither the transfer length nor the call count.  Uninitialized bytes can happen to match the
expected initialized values, so even matching values PLUS matching counts cannot establish
initialization.  **Unexpected values can expose a failure; expected values cannot prove
definedness.**"*

That is the sharpest form of the limit and it settles the round's shape: **no guest-visible oracle
can prove this fix worked.**  The detector must be an offline differential or a `harness:` witness
under the ladder's fifth term -- decided BEFORE the one-line edit, not after.

*** FULL PANEL 2026-09-07 (`_scratchpad/panel_20260907_130159`).  SIX SEATS, ZERO DOWN, glm did
NOT burn for the second panel running. ***

**THE SPLIT, which is the thing for the adjudication:**
  * **grok: TAKE THE ROUND** -- *"zero-fill `buf` at the existing declaration; do not make the arms
    write `bufdepth` bytes; do not treat a guest 0 as proof of initialisation."*
  * **deepseek: NOT RATIFY as a correctness fix** -- *"zero-fill only converts uninitialized reads
    into defined-but-wrong bytes for CI depth>1; the independent assignment/transfer defect
    remains."*
  * **minimax: the symptom is handled but THE LICENCE IS UNSUPPORTED** -- *"no measured delta is
    offered."*

  *So the question is not whether to zero-fill.  It is whether zero-fill is a FIX or a SYMPTOM PATCH
  that leaves the real decoupling defect in place -- and whether the addition licence permits it with
  no measured delta.*

*** THREE SEATS INDEPENDENTLY FOUND A DEFECT IN MY PACKET, AND IT IS A CROSS-ROUND INTERACTION I HAD
NOT SEEN. ***  S3's REVERSE-DIRECTION sentence -- *"at depth 1 or 2 the read fills only that many
bytes and the multi-byte arms then read `buf[2..3]` regardless"* -- is **false of RGB as the file now
sits**.  grok: *"its GET sentence is false of RGB."*  glm: *"asserted in prose, not in the enumerated
table, and under the packet's own model it is wrong."*  minimax: *"S3's table is asymmetric -- write
direction enumerated, read direction mentioned in one sentence only."*

  **WHY: `#505` changed RGB GET from `buf[1..3]` to `buf[0..2]`.**  So post-`#505` an RGB read at
  depth 2 touches `buf[2]` and NOT `buf[3]`.  The sentence was true of the pre-`#505` file and I
  carried it forward into a packet written after the fix.  **My own two rounds interact and the
  enumerated table hid it, because I enumerated the WRITE direction and prosed the READ direction.**
  *A table beside a sentence invites exactly this: the table gets checked and the sentence does not.*

**THREE SEATS ALSO AGREE S4's WARRANT IS DEAD:** *"S4 is ethos, not precedent"* (deepseek, minimax);
*"its site-count and the `#95` transfer do not [hold]"* (grok).  I had already recorded `#95` as
weaker than claimed; the panel makes it unanimous.  **The addition licence therefore wants a MEASURED
DELTA for this one-line change, and none exists.**  That is now the round's blocking question rather
than the oracle.

**Q1 IS SETTLED AGAINST DEPTH-AWARE ARMS**, by two seats and for the same reason: *"depth-aware arms
would trespass on the neighbouring rows that own pixel semantics and would require hardware truth
this packet does not contain"* (kimi).  So the boundary with [[sgimtedepth4dead]] and
[[sgirandomcolour]] holds.

*** AND THE ORACLE QUESTION HAS ITS FIRST CONSTRUCTIVE ANSWER, from the kimi substitute: ***
*"The only honest definedness detector is an instrumented run (MSan/Valgrind class); any harness
witness is one-sided **UNLESS THE STACK BENEATH THE FRAME IS PRE-SEEDED**."*

  **That is actionable and nobody had proposed it.**  Every earlier answer said no oracle can prove
  definedness; this says a harness witness becomes TWO-SIDED if the frame's stack is seeded with a
  known non-zero pattern first -- then `0` means initialised and the pattern means not.  This fork
  already has an ASAN/UBSan tree (`build-asan/`), so the instrumented route is also available.
  **Both need checking before the round; neither was on the table an hour ago.**

*** THE CODEX SEAT REFUTED S4 AND THE OTHER THREE SEATS RATIFIED MY ERROR.  SETTLED BY OPENING
THE FILE, NOT BY COUNTING SEATS. ***

My S4 said `#95` *"fills a READ buffer for `len` bytes on a FAILED access"*.  deepseek, minimax and
grok all agreed and graded the warrant *"ethos, not precedent"*.  **codex went and read it:**

    memory_rw.c :492   if (writeflag == MEM_READ) memset(data, 0, len);
                :494   paddr -= mem->devices[i].baseaddr;      <- THE DEVICE DISPATCH

**`:492` is not in a failure branch at all.**  It prefills on EVERY device read, successful or not,
before dispatch and before length clamping -- its own comment says *"never hand back uninitialised
host memory to the guest.  Root-cause fix for the uninit-read class"*.  The failure-path fills are
`:215` and `:267`, the two that `return MEMORY_ACCESS_FAILED`.  **Verified here by reading all six
sites.**  codex's enumeration of six (215, 267, 492, 671, 683, 732) is correct and my 'three sites'
was wrong as well.

  > **SO THE WARRANT IS A PRECEDENT, NOT AN ETHOS: `#95` is exactly 'initialise storage before a
  > producer may assign only part of it'.**  That is this fix, one layer down.  The addition licence
  > is satisfied by TRANSFERRED WARRANT and the round does NOT owe a measured delta -- which
  > REVERSES the blocking question three seats had just created.

**THIS IS THE WRONG-FACT-COMES-BACK-CONFIRMED CLASS AT FULL STRENGTH.**  I stated a weakened S4 as a
SETTLED PREMISE; three of six seats confirmed it; one seat checked it.  The carrier's rule --
*unanimity on a brief-supplied fact is worth nothing; score agreement only where a seat re-derived
it* -- scores this exactly right, and I had written the premise-audit opener into the brief and
still stated S4 as settled rather than as a question.

*The sharper lesson: **a premise I had ALREADY CORRECTED ONCE, in the weakening direction, is the
most dangerous kind.**  It arrives wearing the clothes of a correction, so it reads as the careful
version and nobody re-checks it -- including me, who wrote it.*

**codex's other corrections, each verified before recording:**
  * **S1 is wrong.**  Not 'once per pixel from three callers': THREE execution paths, TWO caller
    functions, SEVEN direct call sites (LINE GET :817 PUT :863; RECTANGLE GET :878, GET :883,
    PUT :929; tiled MTE GET :1382 PUT :1387).  RECTANGLE does TWO GETs and a PUT per iteration, so
    'once per pixel' understates a fill's cost threefold on that path.
  * **S3's GET row corrected, agreeing with grok, glm and minimax** -- per-arm and per-width: CI
    consumes NO unassigned byte at any width; RGB consumes `buf[1..2]` after a 1-byte read and
    `buf[2]` after 2; RGBA/ABGR/default consume `buf[1..3]` and `buf[2..3]`.  **`#505` is why RGB
    differs** -- it now reads `buf[0..2]` and never `buf[3]`.
  * *** `-DNDEBUG` IS SET, so an `assert()`-based detector is a NO-OP in a normal build. ***
    Verified: `configure:313` sets `CFLAGS="-DNDEBUG $CFLAGS"`, and `src/devices/Makefile:9` carries
    it.  An initialisedness harness built on `assert` would be VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION -- the
    check-that-cannot-fail shape, arriving inside the detector for this very round.
  * **Q4, a coverage gap in the SHIPPED `#505` detector:** `rgb depth64` and `rgb tiled64` widen the
    *source read*; their destination stays a four-byte RGBA write, so **no row establishes
    initialisation of an eight-byte PUT's tail.**  Filed as [[sgireput8tail]] rather than fixed.

*** codex ASSESS 2026-09-08 -- ENUMERATED, not asserted, in BOTH directions. ***

**PUT -- uninitialised bytes actually transferred to guest memory:**

    CI          depth 2 -> 1 byte, depth 4 -> 3 bytes, depth 8 -> 7 bytes
    every other encoding (incl. RGB/RGBA/ABGR/YCRCB and the 11 undocumented)  depth 8 -> 4 bytes

    18 of 64 colour-type x byte-depth combinations, across all sixteen encodings the type mask
    allows.  (6 of 16 counting only the four handled types; 7 of 20 including YCRCB.)

**GET -- uninitialised bytes consumed by the recombination: 30 of 64.**

## TWO OF MY PREMISES WERE WRONG

* **`random()` INITIALISES its four bytes.**  So the `sgirandomcolour` arm does NOT leak
  uninitialised data -- it writes objectionable data.  Different defect, and the distinction is
  what keeps the two rows separable.
* **RGB's GET reads `buf[0..2]` only, never `buf[3]`** -- my brief said the arms recombine
  `buf[0..3]`, which is true of the others.
* and my "stale from a previous call" framing was loose: *"there is no persistent previous-call
  buffer in the language semantics.  Automatic storage becomes indeterminate again on each
  execution of the declaration."*

## *** A REACHABILITY FINDING I DID NOT ASK FOR: THE MTE PATH HITS THIS. ***

The tiled MTE constructs **CI/1, CI/2, RGBA/4 and CI/8**.  Its GETs therefore avoid the short-read
recombination -- **but its CI/2 and CI/8 PUTs are affected.**  *So this is not a hypothetical
combination space: an in-tree path already builds two of the leaking cells.*

## THE FIX, and it costs nothing on correct paths

    uint8_t buf[8] = {0};

*"It preserves the output of otherwise defined paths whose consumed bytes were already initialised.
PUT overwrites the same bytes before transferring them; GET overwrites the requested bytes before
recombination.  Transfer addresses and lengths remain unchanged."*  **That is the Q4 property --
no currently-correct path changes.**

## SEVERITY, BOUNDED RATHER THAN INFLATED -- which is what I asked for

**Both a guest-visible nondeterminism defect AND a bounded information-exposure one**, but *"source
inspection alone does not demonstrate secrets, another process's memory, or a reliable arbitrary
host-memory read."*  It is the emulator's own stack.

## SCOPE: two rounds -- AGREED, but NOT on the panel's reason

The `sgirandomcolour` panel ruled two rounds 5/5 because *"one oracle cannot distinguish a
CI/depth-8 regression from a YCRCB regression."*  codex agrees with the conclusion and **disputes
the argument**: *"One test suite can check multiple independent properties; one CI/depth-8
observation cannot establish YCRCB correctness."*

**And it sharpened the overlap the panel had called a half-fix.**  Zero-initialisation fixes the
four unwritten TAIL bytes of the default PUT at depth 8, and the default GET's short-read
recombination -- **it leaves all four `random()` calls and their PRNG-state effects intact.**  So it
is an overlap in *uninitialised-buffer behaviour*, not half of the random assignments.
**RECORDED HERE EXPLICITLY, as it asked**: if `sgirandomcolour` claims those tail/GET cases, its
scope overlaps this row and the two rounds must say so.

## *** THE ORACLE IS THE HONEST ANSWER I ASKED FOR, AND IT HAS A COST ***

*"A single ordinary run cannot reliably distinguish fixed from unfixed.  Uninitialised storage can
happen to contain zeros or a stable pattern ... Repeated identical output also does not prove
initialisation."*

**The instrument is MemorySanitizer**, which can tell an uninitialised zero from a deliberately
initialised one.  **THAT IS A NEW BUILD TREE:** `build-asan/` carries
`-fsanitize=address,undefined`, and **MSan is incompatible with ASan** -- so this round owes a third
sanitizer configuration, not a re-use.  *That cost is real and is recorded now rather than
discovered mid-round.*

INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION of both directions of this row, plus the piece it did not have: **the MTE depth mapping, derived from the live code rather than from `#509`'s comment.**

    MTE depth (bits)   helper colour type   helper bufdepth   unassigned bytes transmitted
     8                  CI                   1                 0
    16                  CI                   2                 1
    32                  RGBA                 4                 0
    64                  CI                   8                 7

*** THIS IS A LIVE CONSEQUENCE FOR `#509`, WHICH SHIPPED TODAY. ***  `#509` repaired the RGBA selection at depth 32 and that repair is confirmed present.  But the tiled MTE path still constructs **CI at bufdepth 2 and bufdepth 8**, and CI assigns only `buf[0]` -- so MTE transfers at 16 and 64 bits transmit 1 and 7 uninitialised host-stack bytes respectively.  `#509` was correct and scoped to the 32-bit cell by its own comment; this row owns the remainder, and the depth table is what makes the remainder concrete rather than hypothetical.

The full PUT initialisation census, which supersedes any per-arm reasoning:

    PUT arm          bytes assigned   depths transmitting unassigned bytes
    CI                     1          2, 4, 8  ->  1, 3, 7 unassigned
    RGB/RGBA/ABGR          4          8        ->  4 unassigned
    default (random)       4          8        ->  4 unassigned

And the callee question is closed: `memcpy(memblock + offset, data, len)` copies the requested length; block-boundary crossings split rather than truncate; NO_EXCEPTIONS and device clamping do not sanitise a RAM-write source buffer; the zero-fill paths are for READS.  **Nothing downstream makes these bytes safe.**

rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c: the RGB colour arms are OFF BY ONE BYTE POSITION -- PUT writes buf[0..2], GET reads buf[1..3], so a stored colour reads back shifted
rows.witness: probe:regress/sgi_re_rgb_probe.py
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-07.  **FOUND BY THE CODEX SEAT** on the `sgirebufuninit' pass-1 panel, under the standing
*"if you found something ELSE, say so"* licence -- it is not what that brief asked about.

**VERIFIED BY ARITHMETIC BEFORE FILING.**  The two arms disagree about which byte holds which channel:

    PUT  case DE_MODE_TYPE_RGB:   buf[0] = *color >> 24;  buf[1] = *color >> 16;
                                  buf[2] = *color >> 8;   buf[3] = 0;
    GET  case DE_MODE_TYPE_RGB:   *color = (buf[1] << 24) + (buf[2] << 16) + (buf[3] << 8);

PUT stores the top three bytes at indices **0,1,2**; GET recombines from **1,2,3**.  Storing `0x11223300'
gives bytes `11 22 33 00', which GET reads back as **`0x22330000'**.  A round trip through the model's own
RGB mode does not return what was written.

*** THE REASON THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE BUG: EVERY ANALYSIS THIS WEEK, MINE INCLUDED, CALLED THE FOUR
IMPLEMENTED COLOUR ARMS `CORRECT' AND TREATED ONLY THE `default:' ARMS AS SUSPECT. ***  The
`sgirebufuninit' brief says so explicitly -- *"NO colour arm writes buf[4..7] -- not one of the five,
including the four CORRECT ones"*.  codex's words: *"Calling all implemented color arms 'correct' is
unwarranted."*  It is right, and the phrase had been repeated unchecked across three documents.

WHICH SIDE IS WRONG IS **NOT** ESTABLISHED HERE and must not be guessed: RGBA uses 0,1,2,3 symmetrically on
both sides, and ABGR uses 0..3 reversed on both sides, so RGB is the only asymmetric pair -- but whether the
hardware packs RGB at the low three bytes or the high three is a DATASHEET question this row does not
answer.  A round taking it owes that reference, or a comparison against a real framebuffer dump.

NO WITNESS.  Reachability is not in doubt (RGB is documented and implemented) but nothing here shows a guest
driver round-tripping through it.

*** WHICH SIDE IS WRONG IS NOW SETTLED, AND NO DATASHEET WAS NEEDED.  THE ANSWER WAS ONE FILE AWAY, IN THE
CONSUMER OF THESE VERY BYTES.  Derived 2026-09-07, same day as the filing. ***

This row said the packing question needed *"a datasheet reference or a comparison against a real framebuffer
dump"*.  **It needed neither.**  `dev_sgi_gbe.c`'s tick reads the SAME tile memory these arms write and turns
it into host framebuffer pixels:

    color = (buf[i]<<24) + (buf[i+1]<<16) + (buf[i+2]<<8) + buf[i+3];

So the in-tree contract is unambiguous: **byte index 0 is the MOST significant channel.**  Against that:

    PUT  RGB    buf[0]=c>>24  buf[1]=c>>16  buf[2]=c>>8   buf[3]=0        AGREES with the consumer
    PUT  RGBA   buf[0]=c>>24  buf[1]=c>>16  buf[2]=c>>8   buf[3]=c        AGREES
    GET  RGBA   (buf[0]<<24)+(buf[1]<<16)+(buf[2]<<8)+buf[3]              AGREES
    GET  ABGR   (buf[3]<<24)+(buf[2]<<16)+(buf[1]<<8)+buf[0]              AGREES (deliberately reversed)
    GET  RGB    (buf[1]<<24)+(buf[2]<<16)+(buf[3]<<8)                     *** DISAGREES -- off by one ***

**THE DEFECT IS IN THE `GET' ARM, AND IT IS THE ONLY ARM IN EITHER SWITCH THAT DISAGREES WITH THE CONSUMER.**
Its sibling `GET RGBA' does the identical job one index lower and is correct, which is about as strong an
internal warrant as this tree offers.  The fix is the index triple: `(buf[0]<<24)+(buf[1]<<16)+(buf[2]<<8)'.

**WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE ROUND'S SHAPE:** it converts an open design question into a one-line fix with a
named oracle, and it supplies the detector's channel for free -- a PUT-then-GET round trip through RGB must
return what was written, which is a value oracle, not a survival one.

*The general lesson, and it is the option-set rule wearing another hat: I reached for an EXTERNAL authority
before asking whether the tree already answered the question.  `ls _scratchpad/*.pdf' confirms there is no SGI
or CRIME document here at all -- only MIPS manuals -- so the external route was not merely slower, it was
CLOSED, and the in-tree consumer was the only available oracle the whole time.*

*** A STRONGER ARGUMENT THAN THE CONSUMER ONE, AND IT NEEDS NO EXTERNAL REFERENCE AT ALL.  Enumerated
2026-09-07 by walking all four modes rather than reasoning about them. ***

The note above identifies the GET arm as wrong using `dev_sgi_gbe.c` as an oracle.  That argument stands, but
it depends on how GBE INTERPRETS an assembled value -- so here is the same conclusion from inside the
function, depending on nothing outside it:

    mode   PUT writes            GET returns    round-trips?
    RGB    11 22 33 00           0x22330000     *** NO -- expected 0x11223300 ***
    RGBA   11 22 33 44           0x11223344     yes
    ABGR   44 33 22 11           0x11223344     yes

**RGB IS THE ONLY MULTI-BYTE MODE THAT FAILS ITS OWN ROUND TRIP.**  And the two that pass do so using
OPPOSITE byte orders -- RGBA ascending, ABGR descending -- which proves the file can express either
convention correctly.  So this is not a disagreement about endianness or about what the hardware packs; **RGB
is simply inconsistent with itself**, and no datasheet is needed to say so.

**AND IT NARROWS WHICH SIDE:** `PUT RGB' writes the top three bytes to `buf[0..2]', exactly as `PUT RGBA'
does; `GET RGBA' reads `buf[0..3]' and is correct.  Since the two PUTs agree on `buf[0..2]', a correct
`GET RGB' must read `buf[0..2]' too.  **It reads `buf[1..3]'.**  The GET arm is the outlier by the file's own
internal evidence.

*** ONE THING THE ENUMERATION CORRECTED, AND IT WOULD HAVE READ AS A SECOND DEFECT: `CI' ALSO FAILS A NAIVE
ROUND TRIP, AND THAT IS CORRECT BEHAVIOUR. ***  `CI' is COLOUR-INDEX -- one byte -- so `PUT' storing only
`buf[0]' and `GET' returning only `buf[0]' loses the upper 24 bits BY DESIGN.  A round-trip oracle applied
blindly to all four modes would red on CI and manufacture a phantom defect.  **The detector must expect CI to
preserve ONE BYTE, not four** -- which is exactly the kind of row that looks like a bug and is a
misunderstanding of the mode.

**THE DETECTOR FALLS OUT OF THIS FOR FREE:** one PUT-then-GET row per mode, with RGBA and ABGR as ACCEPT rows
that must stay green (they are the de-escalation clause's accept side, already present) and CI pinned at one
byte.  The value oracle is the round trip itself -- no survival row, no exit-status channel, and nothing that
a message change could silence.

*** THE WITNESS DESIGN, AND IT CAN MEASURE WHICH ARM IS WRONG RATHER THAN INFERRING IT.  Derived
2026-09-07 from the XFER path. ***

Everything above identifies the GET arm by ARGUMENT -- the in-tree consumer, and the fact that RGB alone
fails its own round trip.  Both are sound.  **But the model makes the question directly measurable, and a
measurement beats two good arguments.**

`draw_primitive()` reads TWO INDEPENDENT guest registers:

    dst_mode = d->de_reg[(CRIME_DE_MODE_DST - 0x2000) / 4];
    src_mode = d->de_reg[(CRIME_DE_MODE_SRC - 0x2000) / 4];

and an XFER op **GETs with `src_mode` and PUTs with `dst_mode`** -- so the colour type of the read and of the
write are separately selectable by the guest.  That yields a 2x2 that ISOLATES the defective arm:

    src_mode   dst_mode   what it tests                       expected if GET RGB is the wrong one
    RGBA       RGBA       CONTROL -- both arms known good     destination == source
    RGB        RGBA       isolates the RGB **GET**            destination CORRUPTED
    RGBA       RGB        isolates the RGB **PUT**            destination == source (PUT is fine)
    RGB        RGB        the full defect, both arms          destination corrupted

**The predicted corruption is deterministic and computable in advance**, which is what makes this a value
oracle rather than an inequality: `GET RGB` builds `(buf[1]<<24)+(buf[2]<<16)+(buf[3]<<8)` from source bytes
`B0 B1 B2 B3`, giving `B1 B2 B3 00`.  So a source of `0xaabbccdd` copied through RGB lands as **`0xbbccdd00`**
-- a one-byte left shift with a zero fill.  A row can assert that exact value, not merely that something
changed.

**AND THE 2x2 IS THE DE-ESCALATION CLAUSE'S ACCEPT SIDE FOR FREE**: the RGBA/RGBA row and the RGBA/RGB row
must stay GREEN after the fix, so the accept rows the clause demands are the same rows that isolate the
defect.  No extra sessions.

**THE MODE WORDS**, from the same arithmetic as [[sgirebufuninit]]: LIN_A is bits 10-12 = `0x1000`, the depth
field is bits 8-9, the colour type bits 4-7.  With `BUFDEPTH_32` (field 2, `0x200`) so all four bytes
transfer:

    RGBA   0x1220     RGB   0x1210

`0x1220` is exactly what `regress/sgi_re_randompixel_probe.py` already programs, and its `copy lin_a` row
already performs an XFER copy and reads the destination back.  **So the witness is that probe's existing
session with one register changed** -- which is why this is the cheapest live item on the board.

*** ONE THING TO CHECK BEFORE TRUSTING THE 2x2, and it is the trap that caught the last round: does the XFER
path actually reach `horrible_getputpixel` twice, once per mode?  ***  The GET is guarded by
`drawmode & DE_DRAWMODE_XFER_EN`, and there is a SECOND `horrible_getputpixel(0, ...)` immediately above it
that reads the DESTINATION with `dst_mode` for the ROP path.  If that one also fires, three calls occur and
the 2x2's attribution is wrong.  **Enumerate the drawmode bits the session sets before building the rows** --
the previous round's witness failed twice on exactly this kind of unexamined session detail.

*** THE WITNESS OBJECTIONS THAT KILLED [[sgirebufuninit]]'s DESIGN WERE CHECKED AGAINST THIS ROW AND DO
NOT TRANSFER.  Checked 2026-09-07, not assumed. ***

The codex seat rejected `sgirebufuninit''s witness on two grounds.  Both were tested here:

* **"Changing that shared constant changes the observation path and the control simultaneously."**  True
  there, because `MODE_LIN_A' serves the destination, the matched control AND a source case.  **Not true
  here:** `setup(A, src_mode)' stores `DE_MODE_DST = MODE_LIN_A' (hardcoded) and `DE_MODE_SRC = src_mode'
  (the parameter).  Passing `0x1210' changes ONLY the source mode; the destination and the control keep
  `MODE_LIN_A' untouched.
* **"Separate automatic objects have no architectural promise of retaining each other's contents"**, and
  "observing an unassigned byte does not guarantee that its value differs from the intended padding".
  Decisive against an uninitialised-memory oracle.  **This row's oracle reads no unassigned byte at all:**
  a `PUT RGB' followed by a `GET RGB' on a KNOWN source is fully defined behaviour, and
  `0xaabbccdd -> 0xbbccdd00' is a deterministic byte re-index, not a stale-value comparison.

**So this row keeps a real value oracle while `sgirebufuninit' needs initializedness instrumentation** --
which is why the two rounds are different in cost by a wide margin, and why this one is next despite the
other's higher profile earlier tonight.

*Recorded here so the round that takes this does not have to re-derive whether a rejection aimed at a
neighbouring row applies to it.  A refutation is as transferable as a warrant, and needs checking the same
way.*

rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c do_mte_transfer(): `if (depth == 4)' is UNREACHABLE, so the MTE path ALWAYS constructs CI colour -- which makes every MTE fill at MTE_DEPTH_16/32 write 2 or 4 bytes with only buf[0] assigned.  The dead branch is the MECHANISM of [[sgirebufuninit]]'s strongest reachability, not a curiosity
rows.witness: probe:regress/sgi_mte_fill_probe.py
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-07.  **FOUND BY THE CODEX SEAT** on an unrelated brief, and VERIFIED at HEAD before filing.

    int depth = 8 << ((mode & MTE_MODE_DEPTH_MASK) >> MTE_DEPTH_SHIFT);

`MTE_MODE_DEPTH_MASK' is `0x00000300' and `MTE_DEPTH_SHIFT' is 8, so the extracted field is TWO BITS, 0..3,
and `depth' takes exactly the values **8, 16, 32, 64**.  The function then tests `if (depth == 4)', which is
therefore **never true** -- the guarded block is dead code.

codex's reading of what is lost: the dead block is *"its intended RGBA construction"*, so *"its helper calls
retain CI"* -- i.e. the transfer runs in colour-index mode where the author meant RGBA.  **That second half
is NOT verified here** and is the part a round would have to establish; what IS verified is that the branch
cannot execute.

*** IT ALSO REFUTES A PREMISE OF THE `sgirebufuninit' BRIEF, which is why it was filed rather than noted. ***
That brief asks whether callers constrain the (colour type, depth) pair.  Here is a caller that TRIES to and
FAILS SILENTLY -- so the model's own producer does not supply the pair its author intended.  Any round
reasoning about what callers guarantee must account for this one.

LOW because a dead branch cannot itself corrupt anything; the SEVERITY lives in whatever the missing RGBA
construction was supposed to do, which is unestablished.

*** RAISED LOW -> HIGH.  I FILED THIS SAYING `a dead branch cannot itself corrupt anything' AND THAT IS
WRONG: THE DEAD BRANCH IS WHAT MAKES THE MTE PATH LEAK.  Found in the kimi seat's pass-1 answer
(regress/artifacts/sgirebufuninit/pass1_panel/kimi.txt) -- which I had already opened and under-read -- and VERIFIED here. ***

    src_mode = (src_tlb << 10) + (((mode & MTE_MODE_DEPTH_MASK) >> MTE_DEPTH_SHIFT) << 8);
    dst_mode = (dst_tlb << 10) + (((mode & MTE_MODE_DEPTH_MASK) >> MTE_DEPTH_SHIFT) << 8);
    if (depth == 4) {                     <- DEAD: depth = 8 << field, so 8/16/32/64, never 4
            src_mode |= DE_MODE_TYPE_RGBA;
            dst_mode |= DE_MODE_TYPE_RGBA;
    }

**The constructed modes carry NO colour bits, so the colour type is 0x00 = CI.**  The only thing that would
make them RGBA is the dead branch.  So **the MTE path always runs CI** -- and CI's PUT arm fills ONLY
`buf[0]' while the transfer is `bufdepth' bytes.

    MTE_DEPTH_8  = 0  -> bufdepth 1   matched, no leak
    MTE_DEPTH_16 = 1  -> bufdepth 2   fills buf[0], writes 2  -> 1 uninitialised byte per pixel
    MTE_DEPTH_32 = 2  -> bufdepth 4   fills buf[0], writes 4  -> 3 uninitialised bytes per pixel

**All three are DOCUMENTED constants in `crmfbreg.h'.**  kimi: *"every MTE_TLB_A/B/C fill with MTE_DEPTH_16/32
leaks buf[1..3] per pixel (documented MTE_DEPTH values!).  This is the strongest reachability evidence:
PROM/NetBSD crmfb_fill_rect uses this path."*

**SO THE FIX ORDER MATTERS AND IS NOT WHAT I ASSUMED.**  Repairing `depth == 4' ALONE would switch the MTE
path to RGBA, which fills `buf[0..3]' -- accidentally masking the leak at depth 32 while leaving depth 16 (2
bytes, RGBA fills 4) and every DE-path case untouched.  **A round that fixes only this would look like it
fixed [[sgirebufuninit]] and would not have.**  That is the shape the vacuity floor exists to catch, arriving
before either round starts.

*** WHOLE-FUNCTION AUDIT, codex 2026-09-07 (regress/artifacts/sgimtedepth4dead/codex_audit_20260907.txt).  MY Q4 CONCLUSION IS PARTLY
WRONG AND THE SCOPE RULING IS FINER THAN `SEQUENCE, DO NOT SHARE'. ***

Verdict: *"Q1 is correct for the tiled transfer path.  Q4 is partly wrong: correcting the condition for
32-bit transfers leaves depth 16 in CI.  Additional defects exist; the current `zerobuf' chunk sizing is
bounded."*

**WHAT I GOT RIGHT AND WHAT I MISSED.**  I argued that repairing `depth == 4' alone would switch the path to
RGBA and MASK the leak at depth 32.  True for depth 32 -- and I stopped there:

    depth 32   -> RGBA both ways; four source bytes preserved, all four transmitted bytes initialised
    depth 16   -> STAYS CI: two bytes transmitted, ONE initialised          <- I missed this
    depth 64   -> STAYS CI: eight bytes transmitted, ONE initialised        <- I missed this entirely

**So the repair masks ONE of three leaking depths and leaves two.**  My sentence said it leaves "depth 16 and
the whole DE path"; depth 64 was not in it at all.

**And forcing RGBA at depth 16 would not help either:** *"its PUT would initialize four local bytes but
transmit only two.  Its GET would still decode four bytes after reading only two, exposing another helper
initialization problem."*  The colour type and the transfer width are independent, so no choice of colour
fixes a width mismatch.

**THE SCOPE RULING IS FINER THAN MINE.**  I said the two defects must be SEQUENCED rather than shared.
codex: *"The defects CAN share a change round, but successful 32-bit MTE behavior would then provide no
independent evidence that the shared helper defect was fixed.  For separate rounds, handling the helper
defect first avoids that masking."*  **So sharing is permitted and costs the independent evidence** -- which
is a vacuity-floor concern, not a reopening-rule one.  If separated, the HELPER (buf initialisation) goes

**CONFIRMED SAFE:** the `zerobuf' chunk sizing is bounded -- so the earlier reading of that path stands.

**RE-DERIVED, NOT NEW:** it independently found the RGB GET/PUT layout mismatch ([[sgirergbroundtrip]] --

rows.title: dev_sgi_gbe.c DEVICE_TICK: the tile-line conversion loop runs to 512 while memory_rw filled only `len' bytes -- an uninitialised read whose results are computed and then discarded
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-07.  **RAISED BY THE CODEX SEAT** on the `sgirebufuninit' pass-1 panel, as a narrowing of one of
my own SAFE verdicts, and VERIFIED at HEAD before filing.

`DEVICE_TICK(sgi_gbe)' reads one tile line into a stack buffer and then converts it to host framebuffer
pixels.  **The read length and the conversion bound disagree:**

    int len = tilex < width_in_tiles ? 512 : (partial_pixels * bytes_per_pixel);
    if (len > 512) len = 512;                                  /* OB-14 */
    cpu->memory_rw(cpu, cpu->mem, base + 512 * line, buf, len, MEM_READ, ...);
    ...
    for (int i = 0; i < 512; i += bytes_per_pixel) {           /* <-- 512, NOT len */
            ... color built from buf[i] .. buf[i+3] ...
            get_rgb(d, color, &fb_buf[fb_i], ...);
    }

`memory_rw' fills exactly `len' bytes.  The loop reads `buf[0..511]' **unconditionally**.  `len < 512' is
reachable: on the last tile column (`tilex >= width_in_tiles') it is `partial_pixels * bytes_per_pixel'.  So
`buf[len..511]' is read UNINITIALISED and fed through `get_rgb()'.

*** SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY AND MATCHING THE SEAT'S OWN HEDGE: THIS IS NOT A DISCLOSURE. ***  Only
`fb_len = (len / bytes_per_pixel) * 3' bytes are forwarded by `dev_fb_access', and `fb_len' is derived from
`len' -- so the pixels built from the uninitialised tail are COMPUTED AND DISCARDED.  codex said exactly this:
the smaller forwarded prefix *"prevents me from calling this a demonstrated guest disclosure; it nevertheless
invalidates the blanket initialization-safety claim."*  That is the right call and it is why this is LOW.

**What it IS: an uninitialised read of up to 511 bytes per tile line** -- undefined behaviour, and the kind of
thing an ASAN/MSan sweep is supposed to catch.  `build-asan/' exists and is kept clean, so a cheap first step
is to check whether a sweep already flags this and, if not, why not.

**The fix is one token: `i < len' instead of `i < 512'.**  Note the neighbouring OB-14 clamp shows someone has
already reasoned about this loop's bounds ONCE -- and bounded the READ while leaving the CONSUMPTION at a
literal.  That is the same shape as [[sgirebufuninit]] one file over: a previous round fixed the SIZE and did
not ask what fills, or here consumes, the difference.

NO WITNESS.  Reachability of `len < 512' is established by reading; nothing here shows a guest driving it.

one clause-(d) mutant I predict sweeps **59/59**: `implemented = true` -> `implemented =
(cpu->machine->ncpus < 2)' on the seven arms.  I could not build it (read-only seat; gates forbidden).  If

**IT IS THE CANONICAL CLAUSE-(d) SHAPE**: the guard is kept and its repair is CONDITIONED on a field the
guarded body reads -- `if (X)` -> `if (X && Y)` on the dominating predicate.  The floor says a clause-(d)
mutant that sweeps a detector clean is an **L2 breach, repaired in-round however late it is found**.

*** STATUS: PREDICTED, NOT MEASURED.  That distinction is the whole disposition. ***  The floor's L2 rule
fires on a MEASURED false pass; a prediction is a candidate.  grok said plainly it could not build the mutant
-- read-only seat, gates forbidden -- and did NOT dress the prediction as a score.  Recording it as owed rather
than acting on it is the honest reading, and recording it at all is what stops it becoming an unread review.

**WHY IT IS CREDIBLE ENOUGH TO MEASURE:** the same seat, in the same answer, correctly settled two other
premises by re-derivation -- that `machine->ncpus` has three assignment sites all preceding any device (so
`#503`'s DEVINIT snapshot is stable, which is what minimax had named as the settling fact and could not check
from the packet), and that `#502` delivers all seven classes at BOTH sites, i.e. it is NOT the `#499`
one-cell-repair shape that glm's arithmetic had suggested.  A seat that got two checkable things right in the
same answer has earned the build.

**TO MEASURE IT:** the mutant is one edit repeated on seven arms, scored against the shipped
`regress/m88k_exc_probe.py` (59 rows).  This is what the **agy measurement reserve exists for** -- it is the
only compile-and-measure seat not behind the Agent-tool transport, and Opus 5 / Fable 5 are held for the
2026-09-09 adjudication.  agy has no sandbox, so the brief must say: COPY the tree, build the COPY, never
write to GXEMUL-SEC, `rm src/cpus/*.o' first, and check `[ binary -nt source ]' because MAKE_RC has been
observed reporting 0 on a failed build.

**IF IT SWEEPS 59/59 it is L2 of the DETECTOR** -- `m88k_exc_probe.py`, not the product fix, which every seat
agrees is in the right place.  **If it does not sweep, the row closes as a measured non-finding** with the
score recorded, which is a result and not a waste.

*** SECOND, INDEPENDENT PREDICTION OF THE SAME HOLE -- FROM A DIFFERENT SEAT, ON A DIFFERENT MUTANT.
That is the one kind of agreement this project counts as evidence. ***

The `kimi-k3:cloud` substitute (the CLI being 403-walled) returned **NOT A CLEAN RATIFY** and predicted:

    *"a one-line deletion of `implemented = true;' on an unprobed exception class re-opens #502 exactly,
     and every probe row named in this packet stays green."*

**It is a DIFFERENT mutant from grok's** -- a bare DELETION on a class the probe never drives, where grok's is
a CONDITIONED repair (`implemented = (cpu->machine->ncpus < 2)`) on the seven arms.  Two seats, two shapes, one
conclusion: **the 59-row detector does not cover the `implemented' flag across the exception classes.**

**AND KIMI'S IS THE CHEAPER MUTANT TO BUILD AND THE HARDER ONE TO DISMISS**: a deletion needs no reachability
argument at all, and its premise -- that some exception class is UNPROBED -- is checkable by reading the probe's
row list against the switch's case labels, with no build required.  **That check should run BEFORE any mutant
is compiled**: if every class is probed, kimi's prediction dies on the spot for free; if one is not, the mutant
is written against that class and the measurement is aimed rather than speculative.

*Note the transport, per the doctrine: the substitute is PACKET-FED, so this is attack REASONING, not a repo
fact.  It cannot know which classes the probe drives -- which is exactly why it named the check rather than
asserting the answer.*

**TWO FURTHER CANDIDATES from the same seat, recorded here so they are not lost, and NOT actioned:**
* *"this commit makes an admittedly manual-inconsistent delay-slot path reachable by ordinary faults and the
  probe pins the wrong values green -- file it at minimum, L2/L3-candidate if the detector contract claims
  shadow fidelity."*  Whether the contract makes that claim is a reading of the probe header, not of this
  packet.
* the `#503` comment's *"two exits"* defence has a **program-order hole** -- connects run before the
  machine-layer exit -- which its own `-n 5` measurement cannot exclude.  **grok settled the ADJACENT premise**
  (no post-DEVINIT write to `machine->ncpus`) but not this one, which is about the ORDER of two init-time
  exits rather than about mutation.  The two seats are not in conflict; they checked different things.

*** THE FREE CHECK RAN, AND IT CONFIRMS THE PREMISE.  RAISED MED -> HIGH.  Measured 2026-09-07, no build
required -- exactly as predicted, the check settled it for nothing. ***

I said kimi's prediction was the cheaper one because its premise -- *some exception class is UNPROBED* -- is
checkable by reading the probe's rows against the switch's labels.  Run:

    implemented = true sites          11   (NOT the 7 the round's own narrative implies)
      on RESET                        line 700   <-- probe drives no such row
      on INTERRUPT                    line 705   <-- probe drives no such row
      on INSTRUCTION_ACCESS           line 710   <-- probe drives no such row
      on DATA_ACCESS                  line 715   <-- probe drives no such row
      on the seven fixed arms         lines 720-750, ALL probed

**SO THE MUTANT EXISTS AND ITS TARGET IS NAMED: delete `implemented = true;' at line 700, 705, 710 or 715.**
The probe's 59 rows drive bounds / div0 / error / misalign / ovf / priv / unimpl / sfu1 and the trap family;
**none of them drives RESET, INTERRUPT, INSTRUCTION_ACCESS or DATA_ACCESS**, so a deletion there is invisible
to every row -- which is the clean sweep, reached by the smallest possible edit.

**AND TWO OF THE FOUR ARE ORDINARY GUEST TRAFFIC.**  `DATA_ACCESS' and `INSTRUCTION_ACCESS' are page and bus
faults -- the commonest exceptions a real guest takes.  A regression that silently re-opened `#502` for those
would stop EVERY guest CPU on an ordinary fault, which is precisely the defect `#502` spent twelve passes
closing.  `RESET' and `INTERRUPT' are less obviously guest-driven and their reachability is NOT established
here.

*** THE PACKET-FED SEAT REASONED TO A CORRECT STRUCTURAL CONCLUSION IT COULD NOT VERIFY, AND SAID SO. ***  It
cannot read the probe or the switch; it inferred from the packet that a flag set per-class and a detector
driving some classes must leave others uncovered, and it named the check instead of asserting the answer.
That is the transport preamble working, and it is worth more than an unconditioned agreement from a seat that
could have checked and did not.

**WHAT REMAINS UNMEASURED, and it is the only thing left: THE SCORE.**  The premise is verified by reading;
whether the mutant actually scores 59/59 needs a build.  Do not record a breach until it is measured -- the
floor's L2 rule fires on a MEASURED false pass, and this row exists partly to keep that line sharp.

**grok's mutant is now the SECONDARY candidate**: it needs the conditioned form to be reachable, while this
one needs only a deletion on a line that is already there.  Measure this one first.

*** GRADING CORRECTED BY ME, WITHIN THE HOUR, BEFORE ANY REPAIR WAS ATTEMPTED.  I recorded this as a
CONFIRMED L2 FLOOR BREACH.  THE MEASUREMENT STANDS; THE GRADING DOES NOT, AND I SHOULD NOT HAVE ASSERTED
IT. ***

**WHAT I MISSED: the four uncovered arms are NOT part of `#502`'s fix.**  The probe's own docstring says so
in its second paragraph:

    `cpu_m88k.c`'s exception switch marks only RESET / INTERRUPT / INSTRUCTION_ACCESS / DATA_ACCESS
    `implemented`; every other vector below M88K_EXCEPTION_USER_TRAPS_START falls to a fallback ...

**That is a description of the PRE-FIX state.**  Those four flags are pre-existing upstream code.  `#502`
ADDED SEVEN (`git show` on the commit: exactly 7 `implemented = true` lines added), and the probe DRIVES all
seven.  So the detector covers the arms its round actually repaired.

**THE TWO READINGS, and I am not entitled to pick between them unilaterally:**

* **L2 FLOOR BREACH.**  Clause (d)'s DEPENDS-ON closure is *the predicates dominating the diff's edited
  lines, walked to the ENCLOSING FUNCTION BOUNDARY*.  The `switch (vector)` dominates all eleven arms and
  they share one function; `implemented` is the fix's own variable.  On that reading the four are inside the
  closure and a clean sweep is a breach.
* **CLAUSE-(e) COVERAGE DEBT.**  The four sites are not edited lines, existed before the round, and the fix's
  repair is not nulled by deleting a flag it never set.  On that reading the detector defends what its round
  changed, and the gap is debt on untouched code -- FILED, ranked, not repaired in a follow-up.

**WHAT IS SETTLED EITHER WAY, and it is the part that matters: THE COVERAGE GAP IS REAL AND MEASURED.**  A
one-line deletion at four sites in a shipped file is invisible to a 59-row detector, and two of those sites
(`DATA_ACCESS`, `INSTRUCTION_ACCESS`) are ordinary page and bus faults.  Nothing about the grading dispute
changes that number or that reachability.

**WHY I RECORDED IT WRONG:** the premise I verified was *four `implemented = true` sites are unprobed*, which
is true.  I then carried it straight to *therefore a clause-(d) breach* without checking WHICH SITES THE FIX
TOUCHED -- the one fact that decides the closure.  It took one `git show` to settle and I ran it only after
writing the grading down.  **That is the premise-audit failure this project's own brief opener exists to
prevent, committed by the person who writes the openers.**

*Raised as a rule question rather than resolved: it turns on the DEPENDS-ON closure's boundary for a fix that
adds instances of an EXISTING pattern, which is a class this project will meet again -- every de-fatalisation
round that extends a flag or a guard already present has the same shape.*
