rows.title: RULE QUESTION: a chain resting on an index or a bound should quote the DECLARATION of every variable in it -- raised by the withdrawal of a HIGH finding that was false because I never read a type three lines above the code I quoted
rows.state_note:
*** A RULE QUESTION FOR THE 2026-09-09 ADJUDICATION, RAISED BY THE FAILURE ITSELF.  See [[sgilinearnegidx]],
withdrawn at `a264a34`. ***

**THE FAILURE, stated plainly:** I filed a HIGH finding, escalated it to *a guest-chosen physical write
address*, wrote it into a commit message as a headline claim, and reported it as the session's most severe
result.  It was FALSE.  `tile_nr` is declared `unsigned int` at `dev_sgi_re.c:207`, three lines above the
code I quoted, so a negative `x >> 12` converts to ~4294967295 and the `>= 32` guard REJECTS it.

*** WHAT MAKES IT A RULE QUESTION RATHER THAN A LAPSE: I APPLIED THE DISCIPLINE AND IT DID NOT REACH. ***
I identified the link I doubted (whether `src_x` is masked in the linear path), verified it by grep, and ran
an `offsetof` rather than trust hand arithmetic about the struct layout.  **All three were aimed at links I
had already decided to question.**  The defeating fact sat in a declaration I never thought to read -- in a
range I had printed to my own screen earlier in the same session, while looking for something else.

**THREE QUESTIONS, in the order I think they matter:**

1. **Does the premise-audit instruction need a SELF-DIRECTED TWIN?**  It tells SEATS not to ratify my
   premises, and it works -- the carrier records it finding four wrong premises in one brief.  Nothing tells
   ME to enumerate the premises I never questioned, and that set is exactly where this lived.  **A premise
   you did not notice you were making is not audited by an instruction aimed at your reader.**  I think this
   is the more valuable of the two candidate remedies.
2. **Is the narrow mechanical rule worth a template line?**  *"A chain resting on an index or a bound
   quotes the DECLARATION of every variable in it."*  It is cheap, it is mechanical, it would have caught
   this in one line -- and it is minted from ONE instance, which this project's own freshly-minted-exemplar
   rule says makes its shape a hypothesis rather than a class.  **Restricting it to chains whose conclusion
   is a BOUND or an INDEX keeps the population small and recognisable**, which is the form I would propose.
3. **What does this say about C5?**  The chain-shaped brief asking for this exact chain to be attacked was
   REFUSED.  The same seat, asked the same subject WITHOUT the chain, put the refutation in its verdict
   line.  **So the refusal did not stop a bad question -- it delayed a correct answer by hours, and in that
   interval I escalated a false finding and committed it.**  That is new evidence [[codexbriefscoping]] did
   not have when it was filed: does it change that row's disposition, and does it warrant splitting every
   chain into LINK QUESTIONS by default rather than as a fallback?

**WHAT I AM NOT ASKING, because it would be the wrong lesson:** whether packet-fed seats are unreliable.
glm raised the asymmetry and was right that two guards disagree; what it could not do -- exactly as the
doctrine says -- is check a DECLARATION, because a type is a repo fact.  **The doctrine's warning is about
crediting such a seat with repo fact, and that is precisely the error I made on its behalf.**  The doctrine
came out of this correct; I did not.

*Queued in `fable_queue.md` section 6 with the other four rule questions, written out in full so the
adjudication can begin without reconstructing any of them.*

rows.title: #505's arm-attribution warrant is a claim about dev_sgi_gbe.c's scanout that NO row observes -- the detector runs the drawing engine only and has no framebuffer oracle
rows.witness: none
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-07 by `#505`'s own PRE-TABLE CLAIM->ROW check, which is what that check exists to produce.

`#505` chose the GET arm as the defective one on a warrant from a DIFFERENT DEVICE: `dev_sgi_gbe.c`'s
scanout composes a 32-bit tile pixel as `(buf[0]<<24)+(buf[1]<<16)+(buf[2]<<8)+buf[3]` and then
`CRMFB_MODE_TYP_RGB8` takes R,G,B from bits 31..24 / 23..16 / 15..8 -- so byte 0 is R and byte 3 is
unused.  **That is the strongest evidence in the round and NO ROW OBSERVES IT.**

The detector drives the drawing engine and reads the destination word back through the guest.  It never
reaches scanout, so it cannot tell a tree where DE and GBE AGREE on the container from one where they
have both been changed consistently and wrongly.

**WHAT A ROW WOULD NEED:** drive a DE draw in RGB mode, then make GBE scan the same tile out and compare
framebuffer bytes -- i.e. an oracle on `dev_fb_access` output rather than on a guest load.  That is a
different probe SHAPE, not another row in this one, which is why it is filed rather than added: the
round's own detector is above the floor without it.

*Recorded as an explicit no-row sentence rather than omitted, because the CLAIM->ROW check's rule is that
an added comment asserting an observable consequence owes a row OR an explicit statement that it has
none -- and an unrun check and an inapplicable one must not render the same.*

rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c: FOUR of the five GET arms compute `buf[i] << 24` on a uint8_t, which promotes to signed int -- for any byte >= 128 that is a signed left-shift overflow, i.e. UB, on all four arms
rows.witness: harness:regress/artifacts/sgirebufshiftub/ubsan_emulator_20260907.txt -- MEASURED 2026-09-07 under build-asan's -fsanitize=undefined, driving the shipped 10-row #505 probe through a stderr-capturing wrapper; positive AND negative controls in-band (ubsan_control_20260907.sh).  8 diagnostics, all left-shift.
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-07 by the **grok seat** under the found-something-else licence, on `#505`'s pass-1 panel
(`_scratchpad/panel_20260907_051055`).  Verified by reading before filing.

    uint8_t buf[8];
    ...
    *color = (buf[0] << 24) + (buf[1] << 16) + (buf[2] << 8);

`buf[i]` is `uint8_t`, which the usual arithmetic conversions promote to **signed `int`** -- not to
`unsigned int`, because `int` can represent every `uint8_t` value.  So `buf[0] << 24` for any byte
>= 128 shifts a 1 into or past the sign bit of a 32-bit `int`:

    0xaa = 170;  170 << 24 = 2,852,126,720  >  INT_MAX (2,147,483,647)

which is **undefined behaviour** in C99 6.5.7p4 (E1 << E2 where E1 is signed and the result is not
representable).  In practice gcc/clang produce the wrapped value everyone expects, which is exactly
why it has survived -- but `-fsanitize=undefined` reports it, and this tree HAS a UBSan sweep
(`gate_asan_sweep.sh`).

**IT IS PRE-EXISTING AND IT IS ON ALL FOUR ARMS**, not on the one `#505` edited: the RGB, RGBA, ABGR
and default GET arms all use the same `buf[i] << 24` idiom, and the shipped pre-`#505` RGB arm used
`buf[1] << 24` identically.  `#505` replaced one instance of the idiom with another instance of the
same idiom, which is the correct minimal-surgical choice: fixing the cast on ONE line would leave the
file internally inconsistent for no measured gain.

**DISPOSITION: FILED, not fixed in-round, and the seat that raised it agrees** -- *"Pre-existing on
every GET arm, not unique to RGB, not a reason to block."*  The stopping rule licenses an in-round fix
only for a MEASURED FALSE PASS or a WRONG RECORD, and this is neither.

**THE FIX WHEN IT COMES IS ONE CAST PER TERM** -- `((uint32_t)buf[0] << 24)` -- across all four arms in
one diff, which is the class-closure form rather than a cell at a time.  **OWED FIRST: whether the
UBSan sweep already reaches this function**, since if it does, the absence of a report is itself a
finding about the sweep rather than about the code.

*Note the shape: a seat asked about byte ORDER volunteered a defect about integer PROMOTION in the same
expression.  The found-something-else licence is where three of this session's filed rows came from.*

*** THE SAME DEFECT WAS RAISED AGAIN BY THE CODEX SEAT ON THE `sgirebufuninit` PANEL,
2026-09-07, AND I FILED IT AS A SECOND ROW (`sgishift24ub`) WITHOUT CHECKING THIS ONE. ***
The duplicate is merged here and deleted.  **grok had it first, on `#505` pass 1, under the
found-something-else licence** -- so this is the unread-review class one more time: the finding was
already in the ledger, and the round that re-derived it paid for it twice.

**WHAT THE SECOND RAISING ADDS, and it changes the disposition:** a CENSUS of the idiom, which
neither raising had.  Keyed on whether the shifted element carries a cast, over
`src/devices`, `src/cpus`, `src/core`:

    <ident>[..] << 24     111 total
      CAST                 25      e.g. cpu_alpha_instr_loadstore.c, `((uint64_t)data[3] << 24)`
      BARE                 86      in 22 files
        dev_px.c           20
        tmp_arm_rc.c       15
        dev_sgi_re.c        4      (a 5th grep hit is a comment, not code)

> **THE BARE FORM IS THE HOUSE IDIOM BY 86 TO 25, AND IT IS UPSTREAM'S** -- it sits in the CPU
> instruction decoders, and `cpu_mips_instr.c` carries both forms forty lines apart.  So
> `dev_sgi_re.c` is NOT an outlier, and repairing four sites in one device would be arbitrary.
> **The sibling-disposition check answers AGAINST a local fix**, exactly as it did for
> `sgireunmapped`.

**AND THE ROUND THIS DESERVES IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN EDIT.**  `build-asan/src/devices/Makefile:9`
already carries `-fsanitize=address,undefined`, and UBSan's shift check is in that set by default.
So *does it fire, on a path a gate already walks?* is answerable with a tool in the tree and no
source change at all.  If it fires, the finding is 86 sites and a tree-wide policy question for the
owner (`-fwrapv`?  cast the idiom?  accept and document?).  If it does not fire, find out why
before believing either answer.

*Verified before recording: `src/devices/Makefile:9` is `-fstrict-aliasing -fomit-frame-pointer
-fpeephole -fgnu89-inline -O3 -DNDEBUG` -- **no `-fwrapv`, no `-fno-strict-overflow`** -- so the
build gives the idiom no cover, and `#505`'s probe drives `0xaa` through it on every run.*

*Deriver, because my first TWO censuses were wrong -- one keyed on variable NAMES (a correlate,
which silently counted already-cast sites) and one whose bare-form count returned **0 while its own
sample output showed bare forms three lines below**:*

    T=$(grep -rhoE '[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*\[[^]]*\] *<< *24' src/devices/*.c src/cpus/*.c src/core/*.c | wc -l)
    C=$(grep -rhoE '\)[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*\[[^]]*\] *<< *24' src/devices/*.c src/cpus/*.c src/core/*.c | wc -l)
    echo "total $T  cast $C  bare $((T-C))"

*** OWNER DECISION 2026-09-07, asked with the four options on the table: MEASURE WITH UBSan
FIRST, THEN DECIDE.  The alternatives -- add `-fwrapv`, cast all 86 sites, or accept-and-document
-- were all declined PENDING the measurement. ***

**STEP 1, THE POSITIVE CONTROL, AND IT IS THE PART THAT MAKES THE MEASUREMENT MEAN ANYTHING.**
A silent run is ambiguous between *the code does not do this* and *this toolchain does not check
this* -- the pattern-that-matches-nothing shape, which this project has met five times.  So the
idiom was compiled STANDALONE with `build-asan`'s own flags, read out of its generated Makefile
rather than retyped:

    -fstrict-aliasing -fomit-frame-pointer -fpeephole -fgnu89-inline -O3 -DNDEBUG
    -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g

The control takes its byte from `argv` so `-O3` cannot constant-fold the shift away.  Measured, both
directions:

    byte 0xaa   ctl.c:13:18: runtime error: left shift of 170 by 24 places cannot be
                represented in type 'int'                                     <- REPORTS
    byte 0x02   stderr 0 lines                                                <- SILENT

> **SO THE CHECK IS PRESENT AND DISCRIMINATING IN THIS TOOLCHAIN, and a silent real run now MEANS
> the path did not execute the UB.**  Without this control it would have meant nothing, and the
> honest disposition would have been *uninterpretable* rather than *not reached*.

*Note what the control also settles: the UB is REAL rather than theoretical -- gcc's own sanitizer
calls it out by name at `-O3` with the fork's exact flags.  What remains open is REACHABILITY, which
is exactly the axis the row said bounds the severity.*

**STEP 2 is the shipped 10-row `#505` probe run against `build-asan/gxemul`** -- it drives
`0xaabbccdd`, so `buf[0] = 0xaa`, the very value the control reports on.  Both build-tree clearance
parts are checked before the run and it REFUSES to measure a stale or divergent ASAN tree.  Output
preserved at `regress/artifacts/sgirebufshiftub/ubsan_real_20260907.txt` -- a durable path, because a
number this row will cite must not live in `/tmp`.

*** TAKE 1 OF THE REAL RUN RETURNED **ZERO** AND THE ZERO WAS AN APPARATUS ARTEFACT.  I had the
control that makes a zero interpretable and then measured the WRONG STREAM. ***

    probe result   SGIRGB_RESULT=10/10  under the ASAN binary
    'runtime error' lines                0
    preserved file                    1310 bytes -- ten probe rows and nothing else

**The probe spawns `gxemul` inside a PTY.**  UBSan writes to the EMULATOR's stderr, which never
enters the probe's own stdout or stderr -- so what I captured could not have contained a diagnostic
whether or not one was emitted.  The 1310-byte file is the tell: an emulator run that had produced
any console output at all would be larger.

> **THE ZERO MEANT 'NO UBSAN OUTPUT ARRIVED HERE', NOT 'NO UB EXECUTED'.**  And it is worse than an
> ordinary miss, because the CONTROL had just certified that a zero would be meaningful -- the
> control certified the CHECK and said nothing about the PLUMBING, and I read its certificate as
> covering both.

*This is the carrier's own 'check that the apparatus selected something before reading what it says'
rule, met from a new direction: the apparatus selected the right FILES and the wrong STREAM.  It also
very nearly produced the most expensive kind of wrong record here -- a MEASURED-LOOKING NEGATIVE,
which would have closed the row as 'not reached' with a preserved artifact and a control behind it.*

**TAKE 2 uses `UBSAN_OPTIONS=log_path=...`**, which writes diagnostics to `<path>.<pid>` files
regardless of how the child's console is plumbed -- and it carries an **IN-BAND POSITIVE CONTROL**:
the known-UB binary is run through the SAME `log_path` mechanism first, and the script REFUSES to
interpret the emulator run if that control produces no log file.  *A measurement whose negative
result cannot be distinguished from a broken apparatus is not a measurement*, and take 1 is the
proof.

*** MEASURED: IT FIRES.  Owner decision was measure-then-decide; this is the measurement. ***

Take 3 drove the shipped ten-row `#505` probe against `build-asan/gxemul` through a wrapper that
appends the emulator's stderr to a file.  The probe itself scored **10/10** -- the emulator behaves
correctly -- and the run emitted **EIGHT** UBSan diagnostics, every one a left shift:

    5   dev_sgi_re.c:350:21   left shift of 170 by 24 places cannot be represented in type 'int'
    1   dev_sgi_re.c:353:21   left shift of 170 by 24 places
    2   dev_sgi_re.c:221:41   left shift of 32770 by 16 places

`:350` is **the line `#505` ships**.  `170` is `0xaa`, the probe's own first byte.

*** THE `:221` SITE WAS NOT IN MY CENSUS AT ALL, AND IT IS THE WORSE ONE. ***
`32770` is `0x8002`.  `:221-225` are `tileptr = d->re_tlb_{a,b,c}[tile_nr] << 16;` over
`uint16_t[256]` arrays -- and **bit 15 of a tile pointer is the VALID bit**.  So it is not that a
large value occasionally appears: **every VALID tile pointer has bit 15 set, so every tiled access
through this path is UB by construction.**  The RGB sites need a red channel >= 0x80; this one needs
only a tile that is marked present.

*** AND MY CENSUS WAS WIDTH-BLIND, WHICH IS WHY I MISSED IT. ***  I keyed on `<< 24` because that is
where a `uint8_t` overflows.  **The threshold moves with the shift**: a shift of N bits overflows
`int` once the value reaches `2^(31-N)`, so

    uint8_t  << 24    UB at >= 0x80        <- what I censused
    uint16_t << 16    UB at >= 0x8000      <- the same defect, invisible to that census
    uint8_t  << 16    max 0xff0000         <- SAFE, cannot overflow
    uint8_t  << 8     max 0xff00           <- SAFE

**So the class is defined by (operand's reachable maximum) x (shift width), not by the shift width
alone** -- the deriver rule again, and the third time today a census of mine keyed on a correlate.
Re-derived counts, bare (uncast) occurrences across `src/devices`, `src/cpus`, `src/core`:

    << 8    total 207   cast   8   bare 199    (mostly SAFE -- a byte cannot reach 0x800000)
    << 16   total 154   cast   8   bare 146    (UB wherever the operand is 16-bit and can set b15)
    << 24   total 126   cast  25   bare 101

*The `<< 8` population is large and mostly harmless, which is exactly why a raw shift-count census
is the wrong instrument: it over-counts the safe family and under-counts the dangerous one.*

> **SEVERITY SET TO `med`, and the axis is CONSEQUENCE rather than reachability.**  Reachability is
> total -- it fires on an ordinary probe run and, at `:221`, on every tiled access.  What holds it
> below `high` is that gcc emits the obvious shift at `-O3` today and no miscompilation has been
> observed; the harm is a standards violation the optimiser is entitled to exploit, not a measured
> wrong answer.  **That is a judgement about a compiler's future, which is exactly the kind of thing
> this project says to hand to the adjudication rather than settle in a round.**

**THE DISPOSITION IS NOW THE OWNER'S, WITH DATA.**  The three options the measurement was gating:
`-fwrapv` (one flag, defines all of them, changes codegen tree-wide and therefore every gate oracle
measured afterwards); cast the idiom (correct, matches the 25+8 sites that already do it, but a
large diff across upstream CPU decoders); or accept-and-document (cheapest, and now harder to
justify at `:221` than it was an hour ago).

*Apparatus note, because the number is only worth what the plumbing is worth: takes 1 and 2 both
returned a false or refused zero -- take 1 measured the probe's streams rather than the emulator's,
take 2 tried `log_path`, which GCC's libubsan silently ignores (measured: zero files, diagnostic
still on stderr).  The in-band control refused take 2 rather than letting it report.  Take 3's
control fires on `0xaa` and is silent on `0x02`, so the eight is discriminating in both directions.*

*** THE TITLE SAID "every GET arm" AND THAT IS FALSE.  Corrected 2026-09-07 after the `#509` pass-2 codex seat caught it while checking a DIFFERENT claim. ***  Read across all five arms:

    CI    :323  *color = buf[0];                                  NO SHIFT AT ALL
    RGB   :350  *color = (buf[0] << 24) + ...                     shifts buf[0]
    RGBA  :353  *color = (buf[0] << 24) + ...                     shifts buf[0]
    ABGR  :356  *color = (buf[3] << 24) + ...                     shifts buf[3], not buf[0]
    dflt  :359  *color = (buf[3] << 24) + ...                     shifts buf[3], not buf[0]

So the UB population is **four arms, two of them shifting a different byte**, and the CI arm is not a member.  *The defect is unchanged in substance and the enumeration was wrong in two directions at once -- it over-counted CI and mis-named the byte for ABGR and the default arm.*

*** A PATTERN IN MY OWN METHOD, WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT IS NOW FOUR FOR FOUR TODAY: EVERY

> **THE PRACTICE THAT FOLLOWS: a census that will be written into a durable record runs TWO

rows.title: tools/cxlaunch.sh: a codex seat check that could report a REFUSED seat as a clean run, and a wall-grep over stderr that matched the project's own ledger text
rows.witness: harness:controlled in four states on the day it landed -- refusal, echoed-source false positive, real wall, healthy answer; all four give the wanted disposition.
rows.state_note:
Built 2026-09-07 after the `lcaconfwidth` census was REFUSED by codex's content filter and my
launcher reported it as a completed run.  **Three defects, all mine, all found within an hour of
each other, and all of one family: a check that answers the same whether or not the thing it tests
is true.**

1. **The refusal check read the wrong stream.**  A content-filter refusal writes NOTHING to stdout
   and puts `ERROR: This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk.` on STDERR.  The check
   grepped stdout and printed `refusal hits: 0` on a refusal that had already destroyed 108,432
   tokens of completed work.
2. **The script exited 0 while holding `rc=1`.**  It captured codex's status, printed it, and ended
   on a successful command, so the harness reported the task COMPLETED.  Failure laundered into a
   clean completion -- the fourth instance of that class recorded here.
3. **The FIX introduced a third defect, measured on its first real run.**  Grepping stderr freely
   for wall text reported `wall: 3` on a HEALTHY seat, because **codex streams the source it reads
   into stderr** -- and all three hits were this project's own ledger prose about seat walls, one of
   them the line *"whose quotation of the pattern MATCHES"*.  That is the carrier's
   quoting-a-machine-read-marker rule, landing on a tool written by someone who had just read it.

> **THE DISCRIMINATOR: codex's OWN diagnostics are `ERROR:` at line start; everything else on stderr
> is echoed content.**  Anchor stderr tests on `^ERROR:`; grep stdout freely.  Exit 7 refusal, 8
> wall, 6 empty-with-neither, else `rc`.

**Controlled in four states**, and (b) is the one that matters: a stderr line containing *usage
limit* inside echoed source must NOT trip the wall check.

    a  ERROR: flagged...           -> REFUSED   (want REFUSED)
    b  echoed source w/ 'usage limit', good stdout -> answered  (want answered)
    c  ERROR: usage limit          -> WALLED    (want WALLED)
    d  ordinary reasoning, good stdout          -> answered  (want answered)

*** THE CLAIM I ORIGINALLY CLOSED THIS ROW WITH WAS FALSE, AND I MADE IT IN A ROW ABOUT CHECKS THAT
DO NOT CHECK.  Corrected within the hour, by reading `panel.sh` instead of assuming. ***

I wrote that *"`panel.sh` fires the same seat with its own check and has NOT been given this
discriminator."*  **It has had one longer than mine, and a better one.**  Its `check()` anchors error
sentinels to the **first 400 bytes** and its wall test to the **last 400 bytes**, with the reason in
its own comment: *"a review that merely quotes 'was retired' or 'usage:' gets mis-flagged (it did, on
the first live run)."*

**So the tree already held the lesson and I re-learned it by breaking it.**  The two discriminators
differ and both are sound:

    panel.sh    POSITION -- head/tail 400 bytes.  Transport-agnostic; works for any seat whose
                own status lands at the edges of the file, which is all of them.
    cxlaunch.sh FORMAT   -- codex's `^ERROR:` lines.  Sharper for codex, useless for the others.

*The honest ordering: `panel.sh`'s is the general one and mine is a codex-specific refinement.  A
future consolidation should take POSITION as the base test and add FORMAT where a seat's own error
prefix is known -- not the other way round.*

*Kept open for that consolidation, not for the phantom gap I invented.*

*** A SECOND SHAPE OF THE SAME CLASS, MEASURED ON MYSELF 2026-09-08: THE HARNESS REPORTED
"completed (exit code 0)" FOR A codex RUN THAT NEVER STARTED. ***

A background launch used a RELATIVE artifacts path.  The background shell's cwd was not
`GXEMUL-SEC`, so both halves failed:

    cat: regress/artifacts/alphatbinegsel/Q3_brief.md: No such file or directory
    bash: regress/artifacts/alphatbinegsel/codex_q3_20260908.txt: No such file or directory
    EXIT=1

and the task notification said **completed (exit code 0)** -- the WRAPPER's status, not the command's.
`codex` was never invoked; no `.txt` and no `.err` were created at all.

**The tell is the carrier's own three-state rule, and it is the state people forget:** log MISSING =
never started; log 0 bytes = started, mid-run or dead; log growing = alive.  A REFUSED codex run
leaves a 0-byte `.txt` AND a large `.err`.  **This left neither** -- which is how it is distinguished
from a refusal, and why a check that only looks for the refusal text would have called it a clean run.

Two things follow, and the second is the cheap one:
* **an explicit `echo "EXIT=$?"` after a backgrounded seat launch is what caught it.**  Without it
  the missing answer would have looked like a refusal or a wall.
* **use ABSOLUTE paths for every seat launch.**  The carrier already says the session cwd DRIFTS and
  mandates absolute paths for `panel.sh`; the same applies to any hand-rolled seat invocation, and a
  BACKGROUND shell does not reliably inherit the foreground `cd` at all.

dispatch switch has **no `case` for it** -- so a guest that calls it falls to the default arm,
which sets `cpu->running = 0` and stops the machine.

**NOT verified by me** -- recorded as the seat reported it, and a round on this owes the reading
first.  It is the same shape as [[alphaswpctxptbr]] (a PAL entry that does not do what its name
says) and plausibly the same family as the option-set work: an unimplemented PAL call is member 7
territory (IMPLEMENT) rather than a decline, because declining a context-flag operation leaves the
machine in a state the guest cannot reason about.

rows.title: precommit_check.sh validates the WORKING TREE, not the staged content, so it cannot see a staging omission
rows.witness: none

entries.outcome: CONFIRMED and WIDENED: the gate mixes staged FILENAMES with WORKING-TREE CONTENTS; section D is worse -- fully staging empties its input
entries.note: ASSESS (FILE-READING).  14,102 b.  Audited all 21 sections against their actual inputs, corrected two claims in my brief, and produced a SHIPPED instance plus a measured instance on this session own commit.

rows.state_note:
MEASURED on my own commit, 2026-09-07.  `2956c7e` committed regress/sgi_mte_fill_probe.py and NOT the check_probe_wiring.py MANIFEST entry that classifies it, so a fresh clone at that SHA reds with `UNCLASSIFIED'.  **precommit_check.sh reported PRECOMMIT_PASS 0 hard immediately before that commit**, because the working tree already carried the manifest edit -- it was simply never staged.

    git show HEAD:tools/pipeline/check_probe_wiring.py | grep -c sgi_mte_fill_probe.py  -> 0
    grep -c sgi_mte_fill_probe.py tools/pipeline/check_probe_wiring.py                  -> 1

> **A CHECK THAT VALIDATES A STATE OTHER THAN THE ONE THAT SHIPS CANNOT SEE A STAGING OMISSION.**  This is NOT the check-that-cannot-fail shape -- the gate failed eleven times tonight and every failure was real.  Its SUBJECT is one step to the left of the thing it guards.

*** IT INTERACTS WITH A POLICY THIS PROJECT ALREADY HOLDS, which is why it is a row and not a note. ***  The carrier forbids `git add -A' and directory adds, so every commit here stages by EXPLICIT PATH.  That is strictly safer against INCLUDING the wrong file -- the failure the rule was written for -- and strictly MORE EXPOSED to OMITTING the right one.  **Two rules pulling opposite ways, and only one of them has a checker.**

The same commit also missed its own pass-2 receipt (caught by section F) and the ledger row naming it (section L), both on the NEXT commit.  So the gate's coverage is real; what it cannot do is bind that coverage to the staged set.

**THE OBVIOUS FIX IS REJECTED ON ITS OWN RISK:** running the gate under `git stash --keep-index' would let a mid-run crash lose uncommitted work, and the gate takes ~2 minutes.  That is worse than the defect.  **The narrower candidate** is an existence check over the STAGED set for known file PAIRS -- a new `regress/*.py' and its MANIFEST entry; a `src/' change and a CHANGELOG round block -- in the check_cited_artifacts.py idiom (existence-only, forward-only from a cutoff).  NOT BUILT: it changes what every commit must satisfy, which is an owner decision, and owes two negative controls -- red on a probe staged without its manifest entry, green when both are staged.

*** CONFIRMED BY codex AND WIDER THAN I FILED IT.  THE GATE SELECTS FILES FROM THE INDEX AND
THEN READS THEIR CONTENTS FROM THE WORKING TREE. ***

    CHANGED=$(git diff --cached --name-only)      <- NAMES, from the index
    cmp -s "$SEC/$f" "$EST/$f"                    <- BYTES, from the filesystem

**There is NO indexed-blob reader -- no `git show :<path>` -- anywhere in the invoked checking
paths.**  `git ls-files` appears, but that tests index MEMBERSHIP, not content; L's `git show`
retrieves filenames from an existing COMMIT.  codex audited all 21 sections and marks 18 of them
false-green/false-reject on content: a working-tree correction can conceal an invalid indexed
version, and working-tree damage can reject a valid one.

*** SECTION D IS THE WORST AND IT IS THE OPPOSITE SHAPE: IT READS **UNSTAGED** ADDITIONS, SO THE
MORE CORRECTLY YOU STAGE, THE LESS IT CHECKS. ***

    ADDED=$(git diff -U0 | grep '^+' | grep -v '^+++')

**MEASURED ON THIS SESSION'S OWN COMMIT, and it is exact.**  At `#513`'s gate run the only
tracked-modified-but-unstaged file was `regress/sgi_de_primop_probe.py`, which is deliberately
kept OUT of every commit -- `git show --stat e302c98 | grep -c sgi_de_primop_probe` is **0**.  So
D's two green rows, *"no new file:line citations"* and *"no added occurrence counts"*, were
computed **entirely from a file that is not in the commit**, while 129 staged files were invisible
to it.  A fully-staged commit gives D the empty set and D reports green on it.

> **That is the check-that-cannot-fail family in its purest form: not a badly written assertion,
> but a check whose input goes to zero exactly when the thing it guards is done properly.**

*** A SHIPPED INSTANCE, found by codex in history rather than argued: commit `2956c7e` added
`regress/sgi_mte_fill_probe.py` while its own `check_probe_wiring.py` carried ZERO manifest
entries for that file. ***  An actual shipped invariant violation of this class.  (codex was
explicit that it did not verify historical gate OUTPUT -- the violation is established from the
commit contents, not from a green row.)

*** TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY BRIEF, BOTH LOAD-BEARING FOR SECTION J. ***
* I described J as comparing two tracked files.  **The project-root originals are OUTSIDE the git
  repository**; only the `GXEMUL-SEC/tools/` copies are in the index.  So J's
  `cmp -s "$ROOT/$_c" "$SEC/tools/$_c"` compares an UNTRACKED external file against a tracked
  copy -- and updating the external original and its working copy while omitting the copy from
  staging lets J pass while the commit retains the OLD carrier.
* **J's tracked-copy existence test is a bare `-f`.**  It does not verify index membership at all.

*** THE FIX IS NOT A FLAG, AND codex NAMED THE TRAP IN THE OBVIOUS ONE. ***  Blindly replacing
reads with `git show ":$path"` would inspect the WRONG version during the common before-staging
run, because *"nothing staged" normally means the index equals HEAD, not that the index is
empty*.  The shape it prescribes:

* **announce a SNAPSHOT MODE before the first pipeline invocation**, not at the late `CHANGED`
  assignment -- INDEX mode (membership, contents and checker selftests all from the candidate
  index; D switches to `git diff --cached -U0`) or WORKING-TREE PREVIEW (keep the useful
  before-staging audit; D keeps `git diff -U0`);
* keep the deliberately EXTERNAL inputs -- carrier originals, build trees, panel dirs -- and the
  historical git queries explicitly separate, since those are correct as filesystem reads;
* the helpers derive their paths from `__file__`, **so redirecting the shell's `ROOT` is not
  sufficient** -- a complete isolated index snapshot (a worktree) is the practical route, and it
  must carry unchanged dependencies too;
* byte comparisons need a deliberate decision about git filters and newline conversion (locally
  the carrier copies are LF and `core.autocrlf` is false).

**SEVERITY: this does not change what any product code does.  What it changes is what a GREEN GATE
MEANS**, on every round this project has recorded -- which is why it is filed high among harness
items rather than as a tidy-up.  It is a tooling change owing negative controls in both directions
(prove a staged-only defect REDS in index mode; prove a working-tree-only defect does NOT), so it
ships as its own harness round, never as a rider.

My first correction claimed it was lost and was written before I checked git; a wrong correction is worse than the error.  Source half proven COMMENT-ONLY by stripping comments and diffing (byte-identical).

*** PASS 2 ON `01a0339`, 2026-09-07 -- THREE SEATS AGREED ON A POINT THAT IS MEASURABLY FALSE, AND
MY BRIEF SUPPLIED THE FALSE PREMISE BY OMISSION. ***

All three landed seats independently called `s w32 pc` **a control, not a kill**, on the reasoning
that `s w32` already reds under non-execution because its expected value is NONZERO (`0x89abcdef`).
minimax stated the load-bearing assumption outright: *"r0 also retains its prior-row value (the row
before `s w32` is a UBFX row, not 0x89abcdef)."*

**THERE IS NO PRIOR-ROW VALUE.**  `run_word()` is:

    def run_word(iw, src=SRC):
        cmds = ["r1=0x%x" % src, "r0=0x0",
                "put w 0x%x, 0x%08x" % (CODE, iw),
                "pc=0x%x" % CODE, "step 1", "print r0", "print pc"]
        t, alive = session(cmds)

and `session()` does `pty.fork()` + `os.execv(BIN, ...)` -- **a FRESH emulator per row, with `r0`
explicitly zeroed before every word.**  So a word that does not execute leaves `r0 == 0x0`, and
`0x0` is EXACTLY the value `s w32` returned pre-fix.  The row is genuinely ambiguous between
*executed and returned the defect* and *never executed at all*, which is the ambiguity a pc control
exists to resolve.  **[THIS SENTENCE IS WRONG.  See the correction at the end of this note -- `s w32 pc` is an ATTRIBUTION control, the seats were right, and I refuted them on a mistake.]**, because all
three seats reasoned from the same false premise.

**THE DEFECT IS THE BRIEF'S, NOT THE SEATS'.**  I inlined the diff and the row list and did NOT
inline `run_word`.  That is the sketch rule -- *a brief that solicits evaluation of an edit must
inline the enclosing context, every exit path included* -- applied to a probe instead of a function,
and it is the second time this session a packet defect has produced confident agreement: the
carrier's rule is that **unanimity on a brief-supplied fact is worth nothing**, and here the fact
was supplied by ABSENCE, which is harder to notice than a wrong sentence.

*** deepseek's CLAIMED FLOOR BREACH IS AN EQUIVALENT MUTANT, so it is a RESULT and not a breach --
PREDICTED HERE, OWED A MEASUREMENT. ***  It proposes `width < 32` -> `width <= 32` and reports 14/14.
The score is almost certainly right and the DISPOSITION is wrong:

    at width 32   mask      = 0xffffffff          (the `width == 32` ternary arm)
                  1U << 31  = 0x80000000          DEFINED -- 1U is unsigned, 31 < 32, no UB re-opened
                  x & that  = nonzero for SRC
                  x |= ~mask  ==  x |= 0          NO OBSERVABLE CHANGE

So the mutant neither re-opens the defect (clause b) nor nulls the repair (clause d): it is
semantically equivalent, and this project has measured that exact shape before -- `#449`'s
guard-only widening was EQUIVALENT because the latch argument still masked to the original bits.
**A mutant that cannot fail is a result, not noise, and an equivalent mutant is not a floor breach.**
Recorded as PREDICTED; it is one build to settle and it is owed before the chain closes, because
this round's own rule is that a zero must carry its denominator.

**WHAT THE SEATS GOT RIGHT AND I ACCEPT:** `s w31` IS load-bearing (kimi and deepseek both, and it
is the row that pins SBFX at width 31 at all); the comment-only claim on `cpu_arm_instr.c` is
verified FROM THE DIFF by minimax (all four hunks inside comment blocks, the two `uint32_t mask =`
lines unchanged context), which is an independent confirmation of the strip-and-diff proof; and
kimi's warning that *"filed is not run"* for `ubsanshiftlane` is correct -- the disclosure claims a
UBSAN differential WOULD pin the two definedness escapes and no such receipt exists.

**NEXT: re-fire with `run_word` and `session` inlined.**  The adjudication packet carries the
correction, names the three seats' shared premise, and asks the parties to adjudicate their own
finding -- specifically whether `s w32 pc` is load-bearing once they can see that r0 is zeroed.

*** CORRECTION, SAME EVENING: I REFUTED THE PANEL AND THE PANEL WAS RIGHT.  grok -- the seat that
READ THE TREE -- settled it against me. ***

I argued above that `s w32 pc` is load-bearing because `run_word()` zeroes `r0` before every word in
a fresh emulator, so a non-executing word leaves `r0 == 0x0`, which is exactly the pre-fix failure
value.  **Every fact in that sentence is true and the conclusion does not follow.**  grok:

> *"A word that never ran leaves `r0 = 0` (the probe zeroes it).  That REDS `s w32`, it does not
> green it.  So this row does not stop a false pass of the value oracle.  What it does is ATTRIBUTE
> a red `s w32`: executed-and-wrong (pc advanced) versus never-ran (pc stuck or vectored).  `w32 pc`
> already does that for UBFX.  This is sibling parity, and it is correctly labelled CONTROL in the
> row note."*

`s w32` WANTS `0x89abcdef`.  Under BOTH failure modes -- never-ran and executed-with-the-defect --
`r0` is 0, so `s w32` is RED either way.  **Ambiguity in a row that is already failing cannot produce
a false pass**, and a detector row earns its place by turning red when something is wrong, not by
explaining why.  I conflated DIAGNOSTIC ATTRIBUTION with COVERAGE.

**AND THE ROW'S OWN NOTE ALREADY SAID SO.**  `s w32 pc` is labelled `"CONTROL: the SBFX word
EXECUTED"` in the probe.  The round shipped it correctly labelled and then argued in the ledger that
it was something else.

*** THE PROCESS LESSON, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN THE ROW: minimax's STATED PREMISE WAS FALSE AND ITS
CONCLUSION WAS RIGHT. ***  It wrote *"r0 also retains its prior-row value"* -- there is no prior-row
value, `run_word` zeroes it in a fresh session -- and it still reached the correct disposition, by a
different route than grok's.  I found the false premise, felt the refutation, and stopped.  **This
project's own rule is that a wrong reason can accompany a right conclusion and that neither credit
nor dismissal may rest on the reason alone**; the same file records a case where a flagship seat's
correction was itself false.  Checking the CONCLUSION costs one more paragraph and I did not spend it.

*This is the third correction-of-a-correction this session, and the rule keeps holding: a correction
carries more authority than the error it corrects, so it earns a SECOND reading rather than less of
one.  All three were caught, none shipped -- but all three were mine.*

**WHAT NOW STANDS, on five landed seats plus codex still streaming:**

* `s w32 pc` -- **ATTRIBUTION CONTROL**, sibling parity with `w32 pc`.  Correctly labelled, correctly
  shipped, and NOT a kill.  The round's prose implying otherwise is the thing to fix.
* `s w31` -- **LOAD-BEARING and not a duplicate of `w31`** (grok: it pins a SBFX-only `>= 31`
  bound-relax; kimi and deepseek independently).  This is the row that earned its place.
* **THE FLOOR QUESTION: grok CLOSES THE CHAIN** -- *"no in-rule clause-(d) mutant of `width == 32` or
  `width < 32` sweeps the 14-row detector except the two definedness escapes already disclosed."*
  That is a zero WITH its denominator, which is what the stop condition requires.
* **A FOURTH FALSE PROSE CLAIM, caught independently by glm AND grok**: the diff says *"the SBFX rows
  are exactly the ones whose expected FAILURE value is also EXACTLY ZERO."*  Too wide.  **UBFX `w32`
  also returned exactly `0x0` pre-fix** -- this round's own witness table says so -- and only
  `s w32` has that property among the SBFX rows.  The asymmetry argument that justified adding a pc
  control was therefore wrong in its stated form, while the row itself is fine as a control.
* **deepseek's `width <= 32` "floor breach" is an EQUIVALENT MUTANT** (my analysis, and grok's
  closure implies it): at width 32 the mask is `0xffffffff`, `~mask` is 0, so `x |= ~mask` is a
  no-op and `1U << 31` is defined -- no UB re-opened, nothing observable changed.  Not a breach.
* **glm's second finding is refuted by an EXISTING MEASUREMENT MY BRIEF FAILED TO INLINE.**  It says
  deleting `x |= ~mask` is green against every row the packet names.  That mutant was built during
  the previous pass with a pre-registered prediction and measured **10/11, killed by `s mid` alone**
  (`regress/artifacts/armbfxwidth32/M_nosext.raw`) -- `s mid`'s field is `0xde`, whose bit 7 IS set.
  glm could not know that; **the brief inlined the two disclosed escapes and not this measurement.**
  Third packet defect of mine this session, same shape: a premise the seats needed and I withheld.
rows.hold_question: What should `bfi` do when msb < lsb?  Its width = msb - lsb + 1 spans -30..32, so 465 of the 1024 pairs give a strictly NEGATIVE shift count (496 is the msb < lsb population, i.e. width <= 0; the other 31 give width 0, which is defined) -- undefined by the same C99 clause as the too-large one.  ARM calls that encoding UNPREDICTABLE, and this fork's standing position is that an unpredictable GUEST encoding must not produce undefined behaviour in the HOST.  A codex pass examined 13 comparable decisions and found the tree answers this class INCONSISTENTLY: no-op has bitfield precedent, conditional UND has decoder precedent, cpu_arm_instr_loadstore.c:204 picks another defined result for an UNPREDICTABLE halfword load, and #312's own comment argues AGAINST halting.  It said plainly that nothing examined settles bfi uniquely.  AND THE OBVIOUS ROUTE IS WRONG AS WRITTEN: X(und) expects arg[0] to hold a PC OFFSET and bfi's holds a REGISTER POINTER.  #510 therefore fixes the three WITNESSED sites and leaves bfi alone rather than inventing a policy.

SIX SEPARATE ROUNDS -- no merger has sufficient evidence. ***

    one fix design : return/cache permissions according to the actual translation contract
    one oracle     : observed access disposition matches independently specified page permissions

**The ordering ruling matters more than the grouping:** codex put **`alphaswpctxreg` FIRST**, on the
ground that it is the only one with verified behaviour AND a decisive witness (a returned register
value), and it labelled that *"a confidence judgment, not a claim that it has the greatest potential
severity"* -- which is the rung-versus-severity distinction the ladder already insists on, arrived at
independently.

*** AND IT REFUTED A GROUPING HYPOTHESIS I HAD FLOATED: "the claim that `alphapteprot` prevents all
guest paging is not established by this review." ***  I had suggested the page-walk row might be a
prerequisite for testing the others; that is not supported, and scheduling on it would have been
scheduling on an assumption.  `alphafaultclaim` and `alphavmkill` may be reconsidered together only
after proving they share a file, one fault-handling repair and one fault-delivery oracle --
*"correcting a comment and preventing termination do not establish that grouping."*

*** codex ASSESS, 2026-09-08: THE MECHANISM IS CONFIRMED AND THIS ROW'S FRAMING IS REFUTED.  The
defect is bigger than the one filed. ***

**CONFIRMED:** every successful walk returns `2`.  `memory_alpha.c` ends the three-level walk with
`// TODO.` then `return 2;`, and the kernel direct-map and zero-PTBR bootstrap arms return `2` as
well.  **The only PTE checks are `ALPHA_PTE_VALID`; `flags` is unused.**  There is no
protection-dependent successful return anywhere.

*** BUT "SO `memory_rw` CACHES EVERY WALK" IS THE WRONG DIAGNOSIS, AND THE CONTRACT IS DOCUMENTED
RATHER THAN UNWRITTEN. ***  `src/include/memory.h`:

    0    MEMORY_ACCESS_FAILED       denied or failed
    1    MEMORY_ACCESS_OK           success, READ-ONLY
    2    MEMORY_ACCESS_OK_WRITE     success, READ/WRITE
    256  MEMORY_NOT_FULL_PAGE       suppresses whole-page caching

with the prose authority spelled out in `memory_arm.c`.  **Both 1 and 2 are cacheable** -- the
consumer passes `ok - 1` as the cache's write permission, so `1 -> host_store = NULL` and
`2 -> host_store = host_page`.  *Caching a read-only mapping is legitimate; the defect is claiming
READ/WRITE for every page.*

## *** AND CHANGING THE RETURN TO 1 WOULD NOT BE ENOUGH -- BOTH PATHS ACCEPT THE PROHIBITED STORE ***

* **fast path:** `host_store` is installed, so the store never reaches a check;
* **slow path:** `memory_rw` supplies `FLAG_WRITEFLAG` but **rejects only a ZERO translation
  result**.  Alpha returns 2, so the RAM path performs the write; and the physical backing helper in
  `core/memory.c` has no guest-PTE protection check either.

> **So the repair is request-time ENFORCEMENT plus permission-dependent cache metadata -- not a
> one-line return change.**  A round that only edited the return value would ship a fix that
> measures clean on the fast path and still writes through the slow one.

**THE IN-TREE IDIOM EXISTS AND WAS FOUND BY GREPPING, as the option-set rule requires:**

    M88K   rejects writes when accumulated permissions contain PG_RO, then
           return (accumulated_flags & PG_RO)? 1 : 2;          memory_m88k.c
    ARM    computes permission from the descriptors and mode, requires access > writeflag,
           returns that permission, else takes the permission-fault path.  memory_arm.c

*** IT CROSS-CONFIRMED A DIFFERENT OPEN ROW ON THE WAY: [[alphafaultclaim]]. ***  *"There is no
implemented Alpha MM-fault dispatch here.  `ALPHA_KENTRY_MM` and `ALPHA_MMCSR_*` have definitions
but no consumers; `kentry` entries are initialized and assigned, never used to dispatch.  The
comments claiming the translator or caller 'already signalled' a fault are unsupported by the
implementation."*  **That is `alphafaultclaim`'s claim, established independently by a seat that was
not asked about it.**

**Q5 -- IT IS OBSERVABLE, so the documented-only escape does NOT apply:** the channel is guest RAM
CONTENTS -- a prohibited write changes bytes that should not change.  *"'Protection is unmodelled,
so nothing can observe the error' does not follow: memory contents remain observable."*

**Q6 -- ITS OWN SEVERITY WORDING, which is careful and which I am adopting rather than
paraphrasing:** an *"Alpha MMU protection-fidelity gap with observable guest-memory correctness
consequences"*, substantial for software relying on page permissions -- and explicitly **NOT** host
memory corruption and **NOT** a host security-boundary failure.

*** TWO CAUTIONS ON ITS OWN EVIDENCE, both of which I am recording rather than glossing: ***
* **It corrected a premise I had inlined from another seat.**  The `DM_EMULATED_RAM` registration is
  the RAM-MIRROR branch in `dev_ram.c`; base RAM is created through `memory_new` in `core/emul.c`.
  The conclusion (2 is cacheable) is unaffected, but the premise as I stated it was wrong.
* **IT CITED THE ALPHA ARCHITECTURE MANUAL BY URL, AND THAT MANUAL IS NOT IN `_scratchpad/`.**  The
  fifteen PDFs there include no Alpha reference.  So the Table 17-3 citation is **NOT locally
  verifiable**, and under this project's rule -- born from `#357`/`#362`/`#365` shipping page numbers
  that came from model output -- it must not be quoted as an established architectural fact.  *The
  SOURCE findings above stand on their own; only the architectural authority is unverified.*

**A ROUND TAKING THIS OWES AN ALPHA ARCHITECTURE MANUAL**, exactly as `armbfcdecode` owes DDI 0406.

*** TWO CONCRETE MEMBERS OF THIS CLASS, FOUND BY THE grok PASS-2 SEAT ON `#511` AND VERIFIED, 2026-09-07. ***

    dev_uninorth.c:70-72   for (dev=11; dev<32; dev++)  if (idata & (1 << dev)) break;
    dev_v3.c:164-166       for (dev=24; dev<32; dev++)  if (relative_addr & (1 << dev)) break;

Both reach `dev == 31`, so both evaluate `1 << 31` = 0x80000000 -- **a signed overflow in a 32-bit
int, C99 6.5.7p4**, the same defect `#511` repaired in `dev_lca.c`.  Both are PCI IDSEL scanners:
the same idiom, in three chipsets, and only one had been noticed.

**THE ONE-TOKEN REPAIR IS THE SAME (`1U << dev`)**, and each site needs the same check `#511`
needed: what is the type of the left-hand operand of the `&`, and does the truth value move?  In
`#511` that operand was a plain `int`, so the `&` happened at 32 bits and nothing observable
changed; **neither of these two has been checked, and the answer may differ** -- `dev_uninorth.c`
ands against `idata`, which in that handler is likely 64-bit, and that is EXACTLY the case where the
old sign-extension and the new zero-extension give different masks.  *Do not assume `#511`'s
conclusion transfers; it turned on a type.*

**WHY THIS ROW GAINED THEM RATHER THAN A NEW ROW:** it is already the filed home for the class and
already marked HONESTLY PARTIAL.  These make the partiality concrete.

*Provenance worth keeping: my own sibling census for `#511` MISSED both, because it excluded
literal `1` as "the ordinary bitmask idiom".  `1` has the most headroom and is therefore the only
literal that overflows at the maximum shift a `< 32` loop produces -- the exclusion removed exactly
the population it should have kept.*

*** THE TYPE CHECK EACH SITE OWED IS DONE, AND THE TWO SITES DIVERGE -- ONE REPAIR IS
BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING AND THE OTHER IS NOT.  A THIRD SITE WAS FOUND IN THE PROCESS, ON THE LINE
ABOVE, THAT NEITHER SEAT NAMED. ***

**`#511`'s conclusion turned on `tag` being a 32-bit `int`, so the `&` happened at 32 bits and the
bit pattern was unchanged.  That reasoning must be redone per site, and it does not give the same
answer twice.**

**(A) `dev_uninorth.c:70-71` -- THE REPAIR CHANGES BEHAVIOUR, AND FIXES A REAL DEFECT.**

    :56    uint64_t idata = memory_readmax64(cpu, data, len | MEM_PCI_LITTLE_ENDIAN);
    :70    for (dev=11; dev<32; dev++)
    :71        if (idata & (1 << dev))

`idata` is **`uint64_t`**, and it is the same variable at both lines (one block, declared at `:56`,
used at `:71`).  So the `&` is `uint64_t & int`:

    OLD at dev==31:  `1 << 31' is int, 0x80000000, NEGATIVE  ->  sign-extends to 0xffffffff80000000
    NEW at dev==31:  `1U << 31' is unsigned, 0x80000000      ->  zero-extends to 0x0000000080000000

**Those masks differ, and `idata` really can carry bits 32..63** -- it comes from
`memory_readmax64` with the access width, and is stored whole into `d->cur_addr` (a `uint64_t`).
**So under the CURRENT code a guest write with any bit in 32..63 set matches spuriously at dev==31
and the scan breaks on the wrong device.**  The `1U` repair does not merely remove UB there; it
corrects a guest-visible mis-decode.

*This is exactly the case the `#511` pass-2 seats warned about in the abstract -- glm, minimax,
deepseek and the kimi substitute all raised the wider-operand sign-extension scenario -- and it is
REAL here even though it was not real in `#511`.*

**(B) `dev_v3.c:164-165` -- THE REPAIR IS BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING.**

    :161   relative_addr &= 0xfffff;
    :162   relative_addr |= ((d->lb_map0 & 0xfff0) << 16);
    :164   for (dev=24; dev<32; dev++)
    :165       if (relative_addr & (1 << dev))

`relative_addr` is `uint64_t` (the `DEVICE_ACCESS` macro), so the same sign-extension happens -- but
by `:164` its **bits 32..63 are all ZERO**: `:161` masks to 20 bits and `:162` ORs in a value that
cannot exceed bit 31.  The extra ones in `0xffffffff80000000` therefore meet only zeros, and the
result is identical either way.  **Still worth repairing -- the shift itself is UB regardless of what
the `&` does with it -- but nothing observable moves.**

*** (C) A THIRD SITE, ON `dev_v3.c:162` ITSELF, WHICH NEITHER SEAT NAMED AND MY OWN CENSUS ALSO
MISSED. ***

    :63    uint16_t  lb_map0;
    :162   relative_addr |= ((d->lb_map0 & 0xfff0) << 16);

`lb_map0` is `uint16_t`, which INTEGER-PROMOTES to `int`; `0xfff0` is an `int`; so the `&` yields an
`int` and the `<< 16` is a signed shift.

    0xfff0 << 16 = 0xfff00000 = 4293918720      INT_MAX = 2147483647      OVERFLOWS

**It overflows whenever bit 15 of `lb_map0` is set** -- i.e. for half the values the register can
hold -- and `lb_map0` is GUEST-WRITABLE at `:212` (`d->lb_map0 = idata`).  Repair: `0xfff0U`, or
cast the operand.

*My census could not see this one either, for a different reason than the `1 << 31` misses: the
shift count here is a CONSTANT (16), so a filter keyed on "shifted by a VARIABLE" -- which mine was
-- excludes it by construction.  **Two filters, two blind spots, both of my own choosing.**  The
honest form of this row remains what it already said: HONESTLY PARTIAL.*

**STATUS: three verified members, none repaired.**  Each is a one-token change but (A) has a
guest-visible consequence and therefore owes a witness of its own, while (B) and (C) are
language-level repairs.  They are NOT bundled: (A) is a defect round, (B)/(C) are hygiene.

THE THREE C99 FORMS ARE KEPT SEPARATE, which is what makes the list usable: (a) negative count, (b) count at or beyond the promoted operand width, (c) signed left-shift result not representable. **This row was minted for form (c) alone** -- the plain-`1' family -- and the census shows (a) and (b) are the larger and more serious populations.  It also adds a fourth C99 clause this row never mentioned: left-shifting a NEGATIVE signed operand is undefined, which is what makes MIPS DSLL a member.

TOP THREE BY THE SEAT'S RANKING: ARM X(bfi) ([[armbfiwidth]], already filed), MIPS X(ext) and MIPS X(dext) for DEXTM/DEXTU ([[mipsextshift]], already filed).  **So the two rows filed earlier today from a different brief are exactly the census's own top three**, reached independently.

NEW MEMBERS THIS ROW DID NOT KNOW ABOUT, worth naming because they are guest-driven: MIPS X(ror) and X(rorv) (rorv takes an UNMASKED register value as its count -- forms a AND b, and the subtraction can overflow too, which is worse than the EXT family); MIPS X(dsll) (signed 64-bit left operand); dev_irqc.c `1 << idata' with **completely unvalidated guest idata**; dev_mb89352.c `1 << d->reg[BDID]' with a stored byte reaching 255; dev_dec21143.c `d->mii_bit - 13'; and FOURTEEN operators in the PPC condition-register edits.  The two PCI IDSEL scanners this row already named (dev_uninorth.c, dev_v3.c) are confirmed.

*** AND SEVENTEEN TEMPTING FALSE POSITIVES ARE NAMED WITH THEIR WARRANTS, which is a RESULT and not an absence -- it stops the next census re-finding them. ***  Among them: net.c's broadcast mask is clamped to 8 (the sibling I checked by hand today and reached the same answer); ordinary DEXT's decoder really does produce 1..63; MIPS INS's middle shifts enumerate to 0..31 even for reversed fields; the ARM load/store rotations guard a nonzero count; M88K's `imm16' is uint32_t despite holding a sign-extended value; the MIPS TLB probe's -1 takes the other branch before the shift; Alpha's high-part INS/EXT/MSK have explicit zero/64 handling; and the PMAG-JA pixel shift is compiled out.

AND ONE FINDING THAT IS NOT A SHIFT DEFECT AT ALL, filed separately as [[ppcrldiclzero]]: the census records X(rldicl)'s shift counts as SAFE and then reports that the handler ALWAYS WRITES ZERO for an unrelated reason.  *A census that only reported its own class would have walked past it.*

rows.title: a UBSAN differential would pin the shift-UB class that a guest-value probe provably cannot see
rows.witness: none
rows.state_note:
Filed 2026-09-07 from `#510`'s pass 2.  Full record in OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md under the same id.

grok showed two one-line regressions that re-open real UB and score FULL MARKS on a 12-row guest-value probe, and the reason is STRUCTURAL: both are DEFINEDNESS repairs, and definedness has no guest-visible value on a non-trapping host.  `1 << 31' and `1U << 31' give the same mask after the `- 1'; with a correct 32-bit mask `x |= ~mask' is `x |= 0'.

**build-asan already carries `-fsanitize=address,undefined`** -- established AFTER I wrote "unchecked" about it in the probe header, one grep from the answer.  So the class IS pinnable, as a DIFFERENTIAL: fixed source produces no shift diagnostic, the `1U'->`1' mutant produces one.

**Not bolted onto #510**: a second binary and a STDERR oracle is a new measurement lane, and #510's pass 2 had already run.  A lane added after a pass is a lane nobody reviewed.

Covers the same species at [[lcashiftub]], [[sgirebufshiftub]], m88k_rot:513, cpu_mips_instr.c:1757 and the two is_userpage sites -- EIGHT sites across three CPUs, none directly visible to a value oracle.

*** THE FILED QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER COMES WITH A FREE VEHICLE: THE PROBE SHIPPED FOR
[[lcaconfbus1kill]] ALREADY EVALUATES THIS EXPRESSION ON EVERY RUN. ***

This row asks *"whether a UBSan sweep already flags it, and if not, why not."*  Both halves settled
by reading, 2026-09-07.

**UBSAN IS PRESENT.**  `build-asan/Makefile:9` carries
`-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g`.

**BUT THE SWEEP CANNOT REACH THIS SITE, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT.**
`gate_asan_sweep.sh` runs, per machine type and subtype:

    timeout 25 stdbuf -o0 -e0 "$bin" -V -E "$t" -e "$s" "$DUMMY" </dev/null

That is a **CONSTRUCTION** sweep -- it builds each machine and lets it start.  The shift lives in
`DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_pci_conf)`'s device-scan loop, which runs only when a guest performs a PCI
CONFIG-SPACE ACCESS.  **Constructing `alphabook1` never executes that loop**, so no amount of
sweeping flags it.  *This is the witness-ladder distinction one level down: rung 2 (construction)
cannot reach an access-path defect, which is exactly what the ladder says about registration
proving presence and not reachability.*

*** AND THE VEHICLE ALREADY EXISTS, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH ACTING ON. ***
`regress/lca_confbus_probe.py` (shipped 2026-09-07 as the witness for [[lcaconfbus1kill]]) drives a
guest `ldq` into the PCI config window with `ioc_conf == 0`.  That takes the `bus == 0` branch:

    for (dev=0; dev<21; dev++)
            if (tag & (0x800 << dev))
                    break;

Its control read uses `relative_addr == 0`, so `tag = (relative_addr >> 5) & ~0xff` is **0**, the
`if` is never true, and **the loop runs all 21 iterations** -- evaluating `0x800 << 20` at the last
one.  `0x800` is `2^11` and a plain `int`, so `0x800 << 20` is `2^31`: **signed overflow, C99
6.5.7p4, undefined behaviour, on every single run of that probe.**

> **SO THE MEASUREMENT IS: run the existing `lca_confbus_probe.py` against `build-asan/gxemul` and
> read stderr for a UBSAN shift diagnostic.  No new probe, no new row, no new apparatus.**  The
> expected diagnostic names `dev_lca.c` and a left-shift of a signed value.

**NOT RUN YET** -- a probe run must not overlap the codex census currently in flight.  Queued.

**IF IT FIRES**, this row gains a measured witness and its one-token repair (`0x800U << dev`) can be
graded properly.  **IF IT DOES NOT**, that is itself a finding about
[[ubsanshiftlane]] -- it would mean the ASAN build is not reporting a shift UB that is provably
evaluated, and the whole proposed UBSAN differential lane rests on an assumption that does not hold.
**Either outcome is worth the one run**, which is the argument for doing it before designing the lane.

*Found while answering this row's own filed question rather than by looking for it -- and note the
irony the row already recorded: this loop is the file's OWN graceful-degradation precedent, cited by
[[lcabadval]] as a transferable warrant.  The safe path contains the UB.*

*** MEASURED 2026-09-07.  THE UBSAN DIAGNOSTIC FIRES, NAMING THE FILE, LINE, COLUMN, VALUE AND
SHIFT COUNT.  Artifact: `regress/artifacts/lcashiftub/ubsan_HEAD_20260907.raw`. ***

    GXemul> step 5
    fffffc0001040000:  243f0102    ldah  t0,0x102
    fffffc0001040004:  a4410010    ldq   t1,16(t0)
    fffffc0001040008:  a4810000    ldq   t3,0(t0)
    fffffc000104000c:  a4210008    ldq   t0,8(t0)
    fffffc0001040010:  a4620000    ldq   t2,0(t1)
    dev_lca.c:125:21: runtime error: left shift of 2048 by 20 places cannot be
                      represented in type 'int'
    GXemul> print t2
    0xffffffffffffffff

**`2048` is `0x800`; `by 20 places` is the final loop iteration; `dev_lca.c:125` is exactly
`if (tag & (0x800 << dev))`.**  The diagnostic lands on the guest `ldq t2,0(t1)` -- a real guest
instruction through real address decode on an unmodified `alphabook1`, with the empty-slot signature
`0xffffffffffffffff` printed immediately after.

**NO NEW APPARATUS WAS BUILT.**  This is `regress/lca_confbus_probe.py`, shipped earlier the same day
as the witness for [[lcaconfbus1kill]], run against `build-asan/gxemul` instead of `build/gxemul`.
The control read takes the `bus == 0` branch with `tag == 0`, so the scan loop runs all 21
iterations and reaches the overflow every time.

*** AND THE FIRST MEASUREMENT WAS A FALSE NEGATIVE OF MY OWN MAKING, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN THE
RESULT. ***  Run 1 reported NO diagnostic and I nearly recorded that as a finding against
[[ubsanshiftlane]].  The cause: **I grepped the PROBE's stdout, and a UBSAN message goes to the
EMULATOR's stderr**, which lands in the probe's internal pty buffer and is never echoed.  That is
*exactly* the defect I had fixed hours earlier for the `bus attrib` row -- a green row whose evidence
never reaches the artifact -- recurring one level out, on the harness rather than the row.

> **A PROBE ONLY SHOWS YOU WHAT IT CHOOSES TO PRINT.  When you are looking for output the probe was
> not written to surface, dump the buffer -- do not grep the summary.**  Re-run from a frozen COPY
> in `/tmp` (the shipped probe is not edited for a measurement) with the full buffer echoed, and the
> diagnostic was in the first ten lines.

*The wrong answer REASSURED, which is this project's recurring signature: "no diagnostic" is exactly
what a clean build looks like.*

*** THE LANE'S PREMISE IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT: THE ASAN BUILD DOES REPORT SHIFT UB AT RUNTIME,
WITH FILE, LINE AND COLUMN. ***  This row proposed a UBSAN DIFFERENTIAL to pin the shift-UB class
that no guest-value row can see, and rested on the untested assumption that `build-asan` would
actually emit such a diagnostic.  **It does**, and the message is precise enough to key an oracle on
(`dev_lca.c:125:21`, the value, the shift count, and the type).

**So the differential shape is viable as filed:** fixed source emits no diagnostic for that site, the
`1U`->`1` mutant emits one.  What this measurement does NOT establish is the other half -- that the
diagnostic DISAPPEARS once the site is repaired -- which needs the repaired build and is the
two-direction control the lane owes.

*One incidental observation, recorded and NOT filed: the same run ends with `LeakSanitizer: detected
memory leaks -- 3211582 byte(s) leaked in 21 allocation(s)`.  The session ends via `exit(1)` from the
kill under test, so leaks at abrupt termination are expected and this is not evidence of a defect.*

*** codex, `#511` PASS 2: "INVOKING THE EXISTING PROBE ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT" -- AND IT IS RIGHT,
WHICH CHANGES THIS ROW'S DESIGN. ***

*"The shipped `lca_confbus_probe.py` `session()` and the top-level evidence-printing code captures
emulator output but does not score or generally print shift diagnostics.  Future wiring must
explicitly expose and check that evidence."*

**That is exactly the defect I hit by hand earlier the same day** and recorded as an apparatus
lesson: the probe captures the whole pty buffer but PRINTS only the rows it chooses, so a UBSAN
message is present in memory and absent from the artifact.  My working measurement used a frozen
COPY in `/tmp` with the buffer dumped -- **not the shipped probe.**

> **SO THIS LANE'S RECIPE IS NOT "point the existing probe at build-asan".**  It owes an explicit
> SCORING step: a row whose oracle is the presence or absence of a shift diagnostic in the captured
> buffer, printed into the artifact so a later reader can check it.  Without that the lane would
> pass by construction -- a green run that never looked.

*That is this project's check-that-cannot-fail shape, and it would have been built into the lane's
first version if codex had not named it.*

**THIS IS THE UNREAD-REVIEW CLASS, BUT NOT THE VERSION THE CARRIER DESCRIBES.**  That class is about
PANEL ANSWERS NOBODY OPENED -- a seat file sitting in a panel dir.  Every instance here is different and
worse: the knowledge was in **committed files** and **open queue rows**, i.e. in the two places this
project treats as its own memory.  Instance 4 is the sharpest, because the duplicate row PASSED THE
PRECOMMIT GATE and would have sat in the queue indefinitely as a second entry for one defect.

**THE COST IS NOT ONLY TIME.**  Instance 1 and 2 consumed a codex invocation on questions a committed
artifact had already answered -- against a standing directive to spend codex on the queue.  And a
duplicate row inflates the backlog the owner is trying to prioritise, which is the opposite of what
[[queueunrated]] is for.

*** WHAT MAKES IT A CLASS RATHER THAN CARELESSNESS: THE INVESTIGATION IS WHAT HIDES THE RECORD. ***
In every instance I reached the finding by READING SOURCE, and a source reading gives no signal that a
row exists.  The record lives under a row id I would only search for if I already suspected the answer.
Instance 3 is the clean demonstration: I derived the `(once)` gap from the probe, wrote it up as new,
and the row `randompixdiagonce` had been filed EARLIER THE SAME DAY under a name I would never have
guessed from the code.

**PROPOSED STRUCTURAL FIX, and it is deliberately two things because they catch different halves:**

* **(a) WRITER-SIDE, mechanical -- a duplicate check on ADDED ledger rows.**  When a commit adds a row,
  compare its title's content words against every open/in-work row's title and REPORT the nearest
  matches for a human to dismiss.  It cannot auto-reject (titles are prose and near-misses are real
  rows), so it warns; the value is that it fires at the moment of filing.  Forward-only from a cutoff,
  the `check_cited_artifacts` idiom.  **Owes two negative controls -- a genuine near-miss pair must NOT
  be reported as a duplicate, and an actual duplicate MUST be -- so it ships as its own harness round,
  not as a rider.**
* **(b) READER-SIDE, a habit with a command -- before investigating a device or a probe, list what is
  already open against that FILE.**  This is the half that would have caught instances 1, 2 and 5,
  which were never going to be caught at filing time because I never filed them.  The command is one
  line and the artifacts directory is the other half of it:

      grep -l "<file>" regress/artifacts/*/*.txt
      python -c "...print rows whose title or note names <file>..."

**HONEST LIMIT: (b) IS PROSE, AND THIS FILE'S OWN FINDING IS THAT PROSE DOES NOT FIRE.**  I am not
claiming it will.  It is recorded because (a) genuinely cannot catch instances 1, 2 and 5 -- there is no
filing event to hook -- and saying "no structure reaches this half" is more useful than pretending a
habit is a control.  If a later session finds a mechanical trigger for the reader side, that supersedes
this.

*Severity med, not high: nothing shipped wrong.  Every instance was caught, four of them within the
hour, and the one that reached the ledger was withdrawn the same day.  The cost is wasted effort and an
inflated backlog, not a defect in the emulator.*

*** A NEIGHBOURING RECORDS CLASS, MEASURED 2026-09-08: A MULTI-ROUND COMMIT LEFT ALL FOUR OF ITS
ROWS WITHOUT COMMIT ATTRIBUTION, AND ONE OF THEM ALSO KEPT A STALE STATE. ***

`7a41b3f` shipped `#505 #506 #507 #508`.  Afterwards:

    sgirergbroundtrip  #505   state STILL `open', commits None, witness None   <- worst
    lcaconfwidth       #506   commits None
    alphaswpctxptbr    #507   commits None
    alphapfnoffset     #508   commits None

**The `commits` gap is a records defect with no measured decision cost yet.**  The `state` gap DID
cost one: I read `sgirergbroundtrip` as an open med defect while scoping the `sgirandomcolour`
round in the same file, and began designing around a defect `#505` had already fixed.  *Those are
different fields and should not be conflated into one severity.*

**HOW BOTH WERE FOUND, and the order matters:** the state gap by ACCIDENT (opening the source while
scoping something else); the three commit gaps by then asking the general question --
*"which non-closed rows are named by a CHANGELOG round-block heading?"* -- which is a precise query
because the heading format is fixed (`# \`#NNN\` <rowid>: <title>`).  It returned **7 candidates,
of which 4 were legitimate `in work` rows and 3 were real gaps**, so the query needs
row-by-row verification and is not a population claim.

**NO CHECKER IS PROPOSED.**  The carrier's escalation discipline applies: the commit-attribution
gap has consumed zero decisions, and a check that fires on legitimate `in work` rows would be
switched off.  *If a stale STATE ever consumes a second decision, that is the trigger to revisit --
and this note exists so the count is findable.*

**THE DEFECT: an ACCEPTED write to one register arms a host kill in a DIFFERENT function.**

`DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_ioc)`, `case LCA_IOC_CONF`:

    d->ioc_conf = idata;
    /*  Only bit 0 is implemented so far, the PCI bus 0 vs
        bus non-0 selection bit.  */
    if (idata & ~1) {
            fatal("TODO: Write to unimplemented bit of IOC_CONF: 0x%" PRIx64 "\n", ...);
            exit(1);
    }

**`0x1` PASSES that guard.**  `idata & ~1` is 0, so the write is accepted, stored, and the arm's own
comment describes bit 0 as the implemented selector.

`DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_pci_conf)` then consumes it:

    bus = d->ioc_conf & 1;
    if (bus == 0) {
            for (dev=0; dev<21; dev++)
                    if (tag & (0x800 << dev))
                            break;
            if (dev >= 21) {
                    /*  fatal("[ LCA: No bus 0 device? TODO ]\n");
                    exit(1);  */
                    dev = 0;
            }
    } else {
            fatal("TODO. Non-zero bus.\n");
            exit(1);
    }

So: **guest writes 1 to IOC_CONF (accepted), then performs any PCI configuration-space access, and
the host process exits.**  Two guest accesses, both to registers the model implements, neither of
them rejected.

*** WHY IT IS ITS OWN ROW AND NOT PART OF [[lcabadval]]. ***  Every kill `lcabadval` covers is a
guard REFUSING a value it does not recognise.  **This one fires on a value the guard ACCEPTS**, in a
different function, on a later access.  The acceptance and the kill are separated in both code and
time, which is why a per-arm audit of `lca_ioc` walks straight past it -- as mine did, twice.

*** AND THE SEAT'S FRAMING NEEDED CORRECTING, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH RECORDING. ***  grok wrote
that this exit becomes *"newly reachable from a CONF extra-bit write that also sets bit 0; today
that write dies in the CONF guard first."*  That is true of an EXTRA-BIT write (e.g. `0x3`), and it
made the kill sound like a CONSEQUENCE of adopting option A.  **It is not: `0x1` alone reaches it
today, with no fix applied.**  A widens which CONF values arrive here; it does not open the door.
The door is open now.  *Checked by reading both arms rather than by accepting the seat's sentence --
which is this project's own rule, and the seat was right about the site while being wrong about the
timing.*

**THE IRONY, and it is a design signal rather than a joke:** the `bus == 0` branch is the file's own
graceful-degradation PRECEDENT -- a commented-out `fatal()`/`exit(1)` with `dev = 0;` substituted --
and [[lcabadval]] cites that very loop as a transferable in-tree warrant.  **The `else` five lines
below it is a bare kill.**  Same function, opposite dispositions, no comment explaining why.

**REACHABILITY, stated honestly rather than assumed.**  Bit 0 is a bus SELECTOR, so a guest reaches
this by selecting a bus the model does not implement and then doing config access -- plausible for
firmware or an OS that probes beyond bus 0, and trivially reachable by a probe.  **Whether any
shipped guest on `alphabook1` actually does it is NOT established here**, and the row does not claim
it.  What is established is that no guard stands between an accepted write and the kill.

**WITNESS: a rung-3 probe is available and most of it already exists.**  `device_add(machine, "lca")`
is `ST_ALPHABOOK1` ONLY (`machine_alpha.c`), and `regress/lca_confwidth_probe.py` ALREADY drives a
guest `stq`/`ldq` at `LCA_IOC_CONF` (`0xfffffc0180000020`, K0SEG | physical) on unmodified
`alphabook1`.  This row needs one more session: `stq 0x1` to CONF, then a PCI config-space access.
**Three traps that probe already paid for:** debugger `dump` skips `DM_DEFAULT` handlers; a debugger
`put d` of a killing value IS a host kill but is NOT a guest instruction, so it does not witness; and
HAE at window offset 0 silently succeeds, so a miss control must not use `LCA_IOC_BASE+0`.

**DISPOSITION, not yet adjudicated:** it is the same de-fatalisation family, but the option set
differs because the kill is not a value refusal -- the honest members here are DECLINE THE CONFIG
ACCESS (return without dispatching, with a latched announce) or IMPLEMENT bus != 0.  **Note the
architecturally correct error path is blocked for the same reason grok gave on the sibling row:
`LCA_IOC_STAT0`/`STAT1` have no case at all and hit the `default:` arm's `exit(1)`, so LCA cannot
report a device error through the register the header designates for it.**

sev HIGH: a guest-drivable host kill, reached by two ordinary accesses with no rejected value
anywhere on the path.

**CONFIRMED:** S2 reaches `bus = d->ioc_conf & 1` for ANY access in the window -- no `switch` on
`relative_addr`, no `len` test, no `writeflag` test that can skip it, no early `return`; the only
`writeflag` use before it is filling `idata`, which is not a guard.  `len` is first used AFTER the
kill.  And `ioc_conf` has **exactly two readers**, so nothing else can be armed by S1.

*** FOUR CORRECTIONS THAT CHANGE THE CONSTRUCTION: ***

1. **MY LIVENESS CONTROL IS MISLABELLED.**  `ioc rt` proves the WRITER (`lca_ioc`'s CONF arm)
   round-trips `0x1`.  **It says nothing about S2's window.**  PCI_CONF liveness is the armed
   session's unique message (the handler ran) PLUS the control surviving (the same access is not an
   unconditional kill).  A positive signature is available if wanted: an empty-slot read returns
   `0xffffffffffffffff`, where unmapped returns 0.
2. **S2 MUST BE A READ, NOT A WRITE.**  Both reach the kill, but an empty-slot WRITE makes
   `bus_pci_data_access` print `[ ... write to non-existant device ... ]` -- so the CONTROL would
   carry a second `fatal()` on stderr.  An empty-slot READ of reg 0 is the architectural ID probe
   and is silent.
3. **A TIGHTER VARIANT: ONE PROCESS, not two sessions.**  control `ldq` (survives), then S1, then
   the armed `ldq` (dies) -- **only `ioc_conf` changes between the two loads.**  Separate sessions
   are still adequate, but this removes the residual that two processes could differ in something
   that ran before the debugger prompt.
4. **KEEP IT ON `step`.**  `continue` would make the `lca_interrupt_assert`/`_deassert` stubs a
   confounder -- and `cpu_dyntrans.c` skips interrupt delivery while single-stepping anyway.

*** THE CONTRACT LIMIT, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE FOR THE FIX ROUND: THIS IS A WITNESS OF
THE `exit(1)`, NOT A DETECTOR OF THE REPAIR. ***  grok: *"'Host survives, session completes' greens
for a silent `return 1` that skips `bus_pci_*` and `memory_writemax64`, for a latched announce, AND
for falling through into existing `bus_pci` with `cur_bus=1` (empty type-1 also survives)."*  So the
post-fix oracle cannot discriminate between fix members, and a round that ships one must build a row
that can.  **Post-fix caution in the same breath: if someone later implements type-1 by falling
through to `bus_pci_setaddr(bus=1, ...)`, empty bus 1 is a non-killing miss today, so the witness
goes green -- do NOT read that green as "type-1 is modelled."**

**WHY OFFSET 0 IS THE RIGHT CONTROL ADDRESS, which I had asserted without warrant:** it is not
HAE-like (HAE is an exact-address `break` in `lca_ioc`; `lca_pci_conf` has no per-offset special
case).  On the ARMED session the offset is irrelevant -- `bus == 1` exits before `tag`/`dev` are
used.  On the SURVIVING control, `tag == 0` matches no IDSEL bit, so the `dev >= 21` body runs --
**and that body is already the commented-out kill with `dev = 0;`** -- then an empty-slot read
returns `(uint64_t)-1` without exiting.  `0x18` (the NetBSD `| 0x3 << 3` encoding) yields the same
`tag`/`reg` and is equivalent.  **Do NOT use `relative_addr = 0x800000`**, which talks to the
registered `i82378zb` at device 7.

*** AND grok FOUND THE DESIGN ARGUMENT SITTING FIVE LINES ABOVE THE DEFECT: the `dev >= 21` arm is
ALREADY DE-FATALISED, in the same function, and the surviving control USES that path. ***  *"If that
`exit(1)` were still live, the control would die and you would misread PCI_CONF as unconditionally
fatal.  The file already contains the decline precedent the `else` lacks."*  That is the strongest
available warrant for declining here, and it is one function away from the kill.

Also confirmed: FAULT (member 5) is unavailable -- `memory_rw.c` delivers a failed device access as
an exception only under `MEM_MIPS`/`MEM_M88K`, and this path always `return 1` on the live path, so
the kill is `exit(1)` and not `return 0`.  And `lca_isa`'s `ofs > len` kill is a DIFFERENT window
(`LCA_PCI_SIO`), not reachable from `0x1e0000000`.

*** CROSS-REFERENCE, AND A CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN NOVELTY CLAIM.  [[lcabadval]] ALREADY
ENUMERATED THIS KILL ON 2026-09-06. ***

Its eleven-kill census for dev_lca.c lists **line 134, class BUS, condition `bus != 0`, i.e.

filed this row saying only lcabadval mentioned lca_pci_conf without reading how.  **Sixth

**WHAT THIS ROW GENUINELY ADDS, stated narrowly:** the census records the MECHANISM; it does not
record that **`0x1` PASSES the CONF guard**.  That is what makes the kill reachable with no rejected
value anywhere on the path -- an accepted write in one handler arming a terminating branch in
another -- and it is why the disposition differs from lcabadval's six value guards, whose kills all
fire on refusal.  Plus the witness design, now reviewed SOUND by grok.

**KEPT AS A SEPARATE ROW** because it has its own disposition (decline the config access, or
implement bus != 0) and its own witness, and because folding it into a row named for VALUE GUARDS
would hide it -- which is the census's own closing lesson: *a row named after one class hides the
members of the others.*

*** AND THE CENSUS NAMES SOMETHING PLAUSIBLY WORSE THAN THIS ROW, WHICH I SHOULD SAY OUT LOUD RATHER
THAN LEAVE IN A TABLE: the two INTERRUPT STUBS at :73 and :85. ***  `lca_interrupt_assert` and

these two need only that an interrupt is asserted."*  That is member 7 (IMPLEMENT) of the option

*** THE RUNG-3 WITNESS EXISTS AND THE DEFECT IS MEASURED, 2026-09-07.  regress/lca_confbus_probe.py,
artifact regress/artifacts/lcaconfbus1kill/witness_HEAD_20260907.raw, sentinel LCACONFBUS_DONE. ***
