rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-08 as `#512`'s own declared floor breach.  **The round graded it a BREACH rather than clause-(e) debt on purpose**: `assert = 0` is the repair's effect, so nulling it is (d)'s canonical form and sits inside the closure.  THE SHAPE OF THE REPAIR: breakpoint + `continue` so host-timer callbacks run, T1 enabled with a small compare so a timer interrupt goes pending, MIEN and C040 both set, and the oracle is the `debug("[ pcc2: IPL = %i, MASK = %i => %s ]")` at the foot of reassert_interrupts() reading `no assert`.  *That channel IS visible in a stepped capture -- what cannot vary is the STATE, because no guest store can set an ICR INT bit.*

*** THE ORACLE THIS ROW WAS FILED WITH IS WRONG, AND THE codex SEAT HAD ALREADY SAID SO IN AN ANSWER
I HAD RECORDED AS "not yet fully mined".  Corrected 2026-09-08, VERIFIED BY LINE ORDER. ***

The row proposed reading `debug("[ pcc2: IPL = %i, MASK = %i => %s ]")` for `no assert`.  **That
message EXECUTES BEFORE BOTH SUPPRESSIONS:**

    :334   debug("[ pcc2: IPL = %i, MASK = %i => %s ]" ...)   <-- prints `assert' HERE
    :339   if (!(GENCTL & PCC2_MIEN))       assert = 0;
    :364   if (GENCTL & PCC2_C040)        { ... assert = 0; }
    :374   if (assert) INTERRUPT_ASSERT ... else INTERRUPT_DEASSERT

So it reports the PRE-suppression value and is **green under exactly the mutant it would be chosen
to catch**.  codex: *"do not use the existing `IPL ... => ASSERT' debug message as the line-state
oracle: it executes before MIEN suppression and before the proposed C040 suppression.  Observe the
interrupt callback/state."*

> **THE CORRECT ORACLE IS THE INTERRUPT CALLBACK/STATE, not the diagnostic.**  A free-running probe
> is still required for the STATE (an ICR INT bit cannot be set by a guest store), but the CHANNEL
> changes: observe delivery, or instrument the callback -- never the pre-suppression debug line.

*This is the channel-line check failing on a row I wrote while quoting the channel-line check.  A
row whose named channel cannot vary under its named mutant is vacuous by construction -- and here
the channel was not merely invariant, it was measured at the wrong POINT IN THE FUNCTION.*

*** THE "NEEDS A FREE-RUNNING PROBE" WARRANT IS WRONG.  Refuted at pass 2 by grok and VERIFIED here
2026-09-08. ***

`pcctwo_interrupt_common()` ORs `PCC2_IRQ_INT` onto SCSIICR/SCCTX/SCCRX when those lines assert, and
`dev_clmpcc.c:88-89` calls `INTERRUPT_ASSERT(d->irq_scc_tx)` **synchronously inside a guest store to
CLMPCC_REG_IER**; `machine_mvme88k.c` constructs clmpcc with its irq wired to pcc2.  **So the state
is reachable while single-stepping** -- `st.b` IEN|IL to SCCTX, `st.b` to the clmpcc IER, `st.b`
`C040|MIEN` (0x06) to GENCTL.

**THIS ROW IS THEREFORE AN IN-ROUND L2 OBLIGATION, NOT A FILED ONE**, and `pcc2c040kill` has been
reopened accordingly.  The remaining difficulty is the ORACLE, not the state: the `debug()` line is
before both suppressions, so the observable must be the interrupt line itself -- `INTERRUPT_ASSERT`
/ `cpu->cd.m88k.irq_asserted` / guest delivery.

*Two wrong reasons in a row on this same question -- first "the channel is invisible" (false: it
prints while stepping), then "the state is unreachable" (false: another device's store sets it).
The conclusion "no row today" was right both times and neither reason was.*

*** THE VEHICLE EXISTS AND IS SHIPPED.  `regress/m88k_exc_probe.py` IS ALREADY AN m88k FREE-RUNNING
EXCEPTION-DELIVERY PROBE.  Found 2026-09-08 by looking instead of reasoning. ***

Its own header describes the shape this row needs, verbatim:

> *"seeded with `rN=`, a `br .` (c0000000) planted at every vector entry so a delivered exception
> spins rather than executing zeros, `breakpoint add <8*vector>`, `continue`, then `reg` and
> `reg 0,0`."*

**So the repair is a COPY of a proven in-tree shape, not a new capability.**  That matters for the
disposition: "needs a different probe shape" sounded like a capability gap and is really a
half-day's careful work against an existing template.

**THE ORACLE, now that both halves are settled:**

    STATE   (stepped-reachable, per grok/pass 2) st.b IEN|IL -> SCCTX; st.b -> CLMPCC_REG_IER,
            whose handler calls INTERRUPT_ASSERT(d->irq_scc_tx) synchronously inside the store;
            pcctwo_interrupt_common() then ORs PCC2_IRQ_INT into SCCTX.
    ORACLE  (needs FREE-RUNNING) the m88k INTERRUPT vector entry.  Plant `br .' there,
            `breakpoint add', `continue'.  Breakpoint FIRES  = the line asserted = the mutant.
            Loop survives to timeout                          = suppressed  = the fix.

> **WHY THE ORACLE STILL NEEDS FREE-RUNNING EVEN THOUGH THE STATE DOES NOT** -- and this refines
> grok's *"the obstacle is the oracle, not the state"* rather than contradicting it.  The only
> difference between the fix and the mutant is `INTERRUPT_ASSERT` versus `INTERRUPT_DEASSERT` on
> `d->cpu_irq`; `cpu->cd.m88k.irq_asserted` is a HOST-side field with no guest-readable reflection,
> so the sole guest-visible consequence is DELIVERY -- and `cpu_dyntrans.c` suppresses interrupt
> dispatch while single-stepping by design (*"Do not cause interrupts while single-stepping"*).
> **State: stepped.  Delivery: free-running.  Both facts are needed and neither alone settles it.**

*Note the adjacency to `m88kexcdetectorl2`, which is a HIGH row about that same probe.  These are
separate rows and must not be merged -- same vehicle, different defect, different oracle.*

*** THE DESIGN REVIEW CAUGHT TWO DEFECTS BEFORE A LINE WAS WRITTEN, AND THE FIRST IS THAT THE ROW
WOULD HAVE PASSED ITS OWN MUTANT.  codex, 2026-09-08, VERDICT: BUILD-WITH-REVISIONS. ***

### 1.  *** THE PROPOSED DEFECT ROW STILL PASSES THE `return` MUTANT. ***

**GENCTL resets to ZERO**, so MIEN is clear throughout the setup and every completed recalculation
DEASSERTS the CPU line.  At the final GENCTL write:

    shipped repair            deasserts the line          -> no interrupt   PASS
    `assert = 0' DELETED      asserts the line            -> interrupt      caught
    `assert = 0' -> `return'  leaves the line UNCHANGED   -> no interrupt   *** PASSES ***

> *"Deleting the assignment PERMITS ASSERTION; returning PRESERVES THE INCOMING LINE STATE.  The
> callbacks simply assign `irq_asserted = 1` or `0`; returning invokes neither."*

**My §3 treated the two mutants as interchangeable.  They are not**, and the row was built around the
one that happens to be easier to catch.

**THE FIX IS A PRECONDITION, not a new oracle: write MIEN-ONLY GENCTL IN BOTH ROWS FIRST**, so the
CPU line is already ASSERTED before the operation under test.  Then `return` leaves it asserted, the
interrupt is delivered, and the row reddens.

### 2.  *** THE ORACLE WAS A CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL.  VERIFIED IN THE CODE. ***

`session()`'s `rd()` tests `until in buf` **against the ENTIRE ACCUMULATED TRANSCRIPT**, at the top
of its loop -- and `alive = rd(settle)` has already drained the boot banner, which ends at a
`GXemul>` prompt.  So `("continue", grace, "GXemul>")` returns **True with ZERO READS**.  codex
exercised the extracted reader in memory and got exactly that.

**And `how == "no-breakpoint"` is not the negative oracle I took it for**: it establishes a MISSING
TOKEN, not successful execution without delivery.  The runner deliberately preserves that status
through forced termination and unreaped outcomes, *"so a C040-specific hang or unexpected guest halt
can satisfy a timeout-only negative oracle."*

### 3.  THE REVISED DESIGN (to build)

1. Fresh machine per row; perform setup while STEPPING.
2. Establish the pending SCC TX request, then write **MIEN-only GENCTL in BOTH rows** -- this is the
   precondition from §1.  *Do not rewrite SCCTX afterwards: its write arm CLEARS INT.*
3. Final GENCTL write: MIEN-only for the control, MIEN|C040 for the defect row.
4. `continue` into a FINITE guest path with a **separate normal-completion breakpoint**.  The
   control must stop at the interrupt entry; the defect row must reach NORMAL COMPLETION without
   hitting it.  **That gives the negative case affirmative evidence instead of a timeout.**
5. Attribute stops by FRESH breakpoint evidence and PC.  **Treat timeout, unexpected stop or death
   as FAILURE**, never as the negative result.

### 4.  EVERY HARDWARE PREMISE CONFIRMED, one with a better warrant than I had

* **PSR `0x80000000`** keeps supervisor mode, clears IND and SFRZ, preserves endianness; the
  dispatch condition is `irq_asserted && !(PSR & IND)` outside single-stepping.  **It also checked
  my `stcr` word against the decoder** -- it does select `stcr r5,cr1`.  *That is the
  hand-assembled-encoding trap closed by someone other than its author.*
* **VBR = 0 is right, and for a better reason than mine:** `mvmeprom.c:59` EXPLICITLY sets it to
  zero, rather than it being an assumed reset value.
* **Entry `0x8`**: interrupt is vector 1 and entry sets PC to `VBR + 8 * vector`.
* **Source and priority:** SCCTX takes `0x13`; a qualifying IER write asserts SCC TX synchronously,
  making it `0x33`; recalculation selects IPL 3; MASK starts at 0, so the comparison succeeds.

### 5.  TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN Q2 EXPECTATIONS

* **"Suppression by another route" is NOT inherently a defect.**  *"A behaviorally equivalent
  implementation should pass.  The defect is violated behavior or collateral state changes, not
  failure to use the local variable named `assert`."*
* **My "both rows fail to deliver" escape is not a green pair** -- `(no interrupt, no interrupt)`
  FAILS the positive control.  It becomes an escape only if the grader omits or neutralises that
  control failure, which is an argument for asserting the control's outcome explicitly rather than
  treating it as informational.

**Residual classes it names as still uncovered by a delivery-only pair:** C040 suppression that
corrupts MASK/MIEN/pending state or IPL bookkeeping; suppression that stays stuck after C040 clears
(needs a RECOVERY observation); and suppression that works only for the tested source, priority or
first invocation.

*** CLOSED 2026-09-08.  ALL THREE ESCAPING MUTANTS ARE KILLED. ***

    BASE            11/11
    M_d1_noassert    9/10   `assert = 0' DELETED        -- was 7/7 (a CLEAN SWEEP)   KILLED
    M_return         9/10   `assert = 0' -> `return;'   -- the one-token pass-2 mutant KILLED
    M_latchinside   10/11   `assert = 0' INSIDE the latch -- was 10/10               KILLED

**The rows, and what each buys:**

    irq pending     SCCTX reads 0x33 after the clmpcc IER store -- LIVENESS.  Without it, "no
                    interrupt" is indistinguishable from "no pending request was ever created".
    irq live        C040 CLEAR: the guest REACHES the interrupt vector (pc = 0x8).  POSITIVE
                    CONTROL, and it is what makes the negative case meaningful.
    c040 noassert   C040 SET on an ALREADY-ASSERTED line: reaches COMPLETION (pc = 0x1001c).
    c040 noassert2  the SECOND C040 encounter, latch already set: also reaches completion.

*** TWO DESIGN CORRECTIONS MADE THIS WORK, AND NEITHER WAS MINE. ***

1. **The precondition.**  My first design wrote C040 into a RESET GENCTL, so MIEN was clear, the
   line was already deasserted, and `return` -- which merely preserves the incoming line state --
   would have PASSED.  Writing MIEN-only GENCTL FIRST, in BOTH rows, is what makes it catchable.
   *codex, design review, before a line was written.*
2. **The encounter axis.**  `assert = 0` moved inside the latch suppresses correctly on the FIRST
   encounter and skips it on every later one, so a single-encounter row scores 10/10 against it.
   **Closing the axis with one repeated write beats adding a row per mutant** -- the class-closure
   rule rather than pass-per-instance.  *Predicted by codex on pass 1, measured here.*

**AND THE NEGATIVE CASE IS AFFIRMATIVE, NOT A TIMEOUT.**  Both outcomes stop at a breakpoint and the
discriminator is WHICH PC.  The obvious oracles were both unusable: the `debug()` line executes
BEFORE the suppressions, and `("continue", grace, "GXemul>")` returns True with ZERO READS because
`rd()` matches against the whole accumulated buffer, which already holds a prompt.

**RESIDUAL, disclosed rather than implied:** these four rows establish DELIVERY under one source, one
priority and two encounters.  They do not cover C040 suppression that corrupts MASK/MIEN/pending
state, suppression that stays stuck after C040 CLEARS (a recovery observation), or other sources and
priorities.  *And per codex: suppression by a different implementation route is NOT a defect -- "the
defect is violated behavior or collateral state changes, not failure to use the local variable named
`assert`."*

*** COMMITTED AS `9fa07fe`, inside `#512`.  This row was FILED as coverage debt and CLOSED IN-ROUND
instead, which is what pass 2 required. ***  It never became a separate round: the four rows it
specified ship as part of the detector they were owed to.

FILED 2026-09-08.  **A guard written SPECIFICALLY to stop a panel launching on an empty brief launched
a panel on a brief that did not exist** -- and it is a NEW MECHANISM for the check-that-cannot-fail
class, not another instance of the recorded one.

*** THE CASCADE, in order. ***

1.  The diff was written to git-bash's `/tmp/d512.diff` and READ by **Windows** python
    (`C:/Users/.../Python312/python.exe`), which resolves a DIFFERENT `/tmp`.  *The carrier already
    records `git-bash /tmp != WSL /tmp`; this is the same trap with a third interpreter.*
2.  The brief generator raised `FileNotFoundError`, so **no brief was written**.
3.  *** THE GUARD FAILED OPEN. ***  It read:

        N=$(grep -cE '^@@' "$BRIEF")
        if [ "$N" -lt 3 ]; then echo "REFUSING TO LAUNCH"; exit 1; fi
        echo "ok -- launching"

    On a MISSING file `grep -c` prints nothing, so `N` is the EMPTY STRING.  `[ "" -lt 3 ]` is not
    false -- it is a **bash syntax error**, `integer expression expected`, which exits NON-ZERO, and
    an `if` reads a non-zero exit as FALSE.  **So the else-branch ran and printed "ok -- launching".**
4.  `panel.sh` printed `no such brief` and launched **nothing** -- and exited 0, so the background
    task reported SUCCESS.

*** WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A WASTED RUN: the newest panel dir was still PASS 1's. ***  Had the seat
files been read without checking the directory timestamp, **pass 1's answers would have been graded
as pass 2** -- a whole review stage discharged by the stage before it.  That is the carrier's own
warning about a relative `./panel.sh` launch ("a SILENT zero-seat failure that looks like a completed
run, so you review the previous round's stale seat files by mistake") reached by a different road.

> *** THE CLASS EXTENSION, and it contradicts something the carrier asserts. ***  The
> check-that-cannot-fail section concludes that in this project such a check *"is almost never a
> badly-written assertion -- it is a claim that some cheap observable stands in for an expensive
> one"*, and reports a hunt over 251 gate rows that found ZERO unguarded self-comparisons.
>
> **This is a badly-written assertion, and it is in a guard whose entire purpose was to prevent the
> failure it permitted.**  The mechanism is specific to shell: **a comparison against an EMPTY
> variable is an ERROR, not a FALSE, and `if` grades an error as false -- so the guard's refusal
> branch is unreachable in exactly the case it exists for.**
>
> The generalisation: **test EXISTENCE before you test a PROPERTY.**  A property test on a
> non-existent object cannot fail closed, because there is nothing to measure.

**THE FIXED FORM, used on the relaunch:**

    [ -s "$B" ] || { echo "REFUSING: brief missing or empty"; exit 1; }
    N=$(grep -cE '^@@' "$B" 2>/dev/null)
    [ "${N:-0}" -ge 3 ] || { echo "REFUSING: only ${N:-0} hunk markers"; exit 1; }
    grep -q "<a token from the diff body>" "$B" || { echo "REFUSING: diff body absent"; exit 1; }

Three properties, and each is load-bearing: `-s` catches missing AND empty; `${N:-0}` makes the
comparison well-formed whatever grep did; and the CONTENT grep catches a brief that has hunk markers
but lost the body.

**NOT MECHANISED, deliberately.**  This guard is written ad hoc at each launch rather than living in
`panel.sh`, and moving it there is a change to the script every panel runs -- which owes two negative
controls (prove it refuses a missing brief, prove it does NOT refuse a good one).  **That is its own
harness round.**  Note `panel.sh` ALREADY refuses correctly (`no such brief`); what is missing is
that the CALLER believes it launched.

*Provenance: my own guard, written earlier in the same session, in the same shell block, on the
belief that it made the launch safe.  It had worked on three previous briefs -- because they
existed.*

*** THE FIXED GUARD CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT ON ITS FIRST USE, AND IT WAS THE **CONTENT** CHECK THAT
FIRED -- not the existence test and not the count.  2026-09-08. ***

Building the `sgirekills` round-design brief, I inlined the arm cascade as lines 420-545 and the
guard refused:

    REFUSING: cascade truncated before LINEAR_B

**The range was wrong.**  `LINEAR_A`'s arm alone runs to line 585 and `LINEAR_B` starts at 588, so
the true cascade is 420-660 -- **241 lines, not 126.**  The brief would have said *"the FULL arm
cascade, VERBATIM"* while omitting the sixth of the six windows it was about, and the seat would
have answered a question about five arms believing it had seen six.

> **THE COUNT CHECK WOULD HAVE PASSED IT.**  126 inlined lines is a perfectly healthy-looking
> number; the file existed and was 11 KB.  **Only asking "is the thing I claim to have inlined
> actually in here?" could fail.**
>
> That is the denominator rule's own limit, restated: a denominator proves the apparatus SELECTED
> something, never that it selected the RIGHT something.  A content assertion is the only check that
> distinguishes them.

**So the three-part guard has now earned each of its parts by a different failure:** `-s` was minted
by the missing-file cascade that filed this row; `${N:-0}` by the empty-variable comparison; and the
CONTENT grep by this truncation, which the other two pass cleanly.

*Recorded because the guard was written defensively an hour earlier with no expectation of firing,
and the thing it caught was mine.*

rows.title: mvme_pcctworeg.h defines C040 TWICE with DIFFERENT values -- PCC2_C040 = 0x04 (right, and what the model uses) and PCC2_GENCTL_C040 = 0x03 (wrong; 0x03 is FAST|MIEN).  The wrong alias has no consumers today, so it is a loaded trap rather than a live defect
rows.witness: none -- documented-only: a comment on a symbol nothing reads (grep -rn PCC2_GENCTL_C040 src/ finds only the definition), so a row would be vacuous by construction.  *** CORRECTED 2026-09-09 from `harness:read' -- the harness: term is admitted only when the round's SUBJECT is the test apparatus, and a vendored product header is not; the reading it named (mvme_pcctworeg.h :61 and :134 plus the zero-consumer grep) is preserved here as the finding's evidence, not as a witness. ***

entries.note: Found while auditing `#512`'s P1.  I had checked only PCC2_C040 and concluded the fork was clean; codex checked the whole header and found the fork carries the SAME conflict it inherited from OpenBSD's `include/pcctworeg.h`.

One-line annotation plus a nine-line comment naming the right constant; value unchanged.  Disposition adjudicated (annotate, not delete: a vendored third-party header, and the addition licence does not reach a deletion on a zero-consumer warrant).  Propagated with the #516 batch, two-part clearance CLEAN/FRESH on every row (_scratchpad/propagate516.out; three consumers of the header, devices/*.o and machines/*.o cleared first).  Witness field corrected in the same edit: `harness:read' was a misuse of the harness: term for a product header.

rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-08.  **`#512` verified `PCC2_C040 = 0x04` against the MVME187 board manual and shipped on it.  The header ALSO carries `PCC2_GENCTL_C040 = 0x03` sixty lines down.**  0x03 is `FAST|MIEN` -- two unrelated control bits -- so an edit reaching for the second spelling would test the wrong bits entirely and would look plausible doing it.

**NOT A LIVE DEFECT: a fork-wide grep finds ZERO consumers of the 0x03 alias.** It is upstream residue, inherited from OpenBSD's own `mvme88k/include/pcctworeg.h`, which carries the same wrong value.

*The disposition question -- DELETE the dead alias, or CORRECT it to 0x04 -- is an option-set question and is not settled here.  Deleting is the additions-licence-consistent move (a dead define is not load-bearing); correcting it leaves a second spelling for a future edit to pick.*

*** I FILED THIS FINDING A SECOND TIME ON 2026-09-08 AS `pcc2c040dup', HOURS AFTER THIS ROW EXISTED.
The duplicate has been removed, and the GATE is what caught it -- not me. ***

A codex analysis job on [[pcc2c040kill]] named the two symbols in passing; I verified the values and
the zero-consumer count and filed a new row.  `precommit_check.sh` section **P** then refused the
commit -- *"AN OPEN ROW EXISTS ONLY IN THE LEDGER: pcc2c040dup"* -- because a new row must also be
findable in `OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md`.  Going to add it there is what put this row in front of me.

**THIS ROW IS THE BETTER OF THE TWO AND ANSWERS A QUESTION MINE LEFT OPEN.**  I had written that the
header lives under `src/include/thirdparty/`, so it *"may be a verbatim import from NetBSD, in which
case editing it is a DIVERGENCE"* -- and flagged that as undecided.  **This row already had it
settled: the alias is upstream residue, inherited from OpenBSD's own
`mvme88k/include/pcctworeg.h`, which carries the same wrong value.**

**THE ONE THING WORTH CARRYING ACROSS, because it sharpens why the trap is loaded rather than merely
present:** the second family is not simply wrong, it is wrong ONLY IN ITS LAST MEMBER.

    PCC2_FAST  0x01   vs  PCC2_GENCTL_FAST  0x01     AGREE
    PCC2_MIEN  0x02   vs  PCC2_GENCTL_IEN   0x02     AGREE
    PCC2_C040  0x04   vs  PCC2_GENCTL_C040  0x03     *** DISAGREE ***

The first two coincide because a bit-mask sequence (1, 2, 4) and a plain enumeration (1, 2, 3) are
identical until the first power-of-two gap -- **which is exactly the point at which a reader stops
checking.**  So the family reads consistent, and is not.

*Recorded rather than quietly deleted: the memory rule is to check for an existing entry before
creating a new one, and I did not.  What made the duplicate cheap is that section P forces every
ledger row into the bug file, so a duplicate collides with its original at commit time instead of
living alongside it.*

**SHIPPED 2026-09-09 as `#517` (54a2eb4): ANNOTATE, NOT DELETE.**  The wrong value is left in place, marked WRONG on its own line pointing at `PCC2_C040`, with the reasoning in a comment above it; nothing that parses the header changes meaning.  Adjudicated by fable5 as a records/guard fix rather than a round; no panel on a one-line annotation, by the loop's judgment, recorded in the CHANGELOG block.  State `in work` rather than closed: the regress phase is Fable-only and has not run on it, and the two sibling defines (`PCC2_GENCTL_FAST`/`IEN`) were NOT audited against the manual, which the block says.

rows.title: cpu_arm_instr.c: the bfi decoder accepts source field 15 and passes r[15] to X(bfi), but the architecture assigns that encoding to BFC (Bit Field Clear) -- so BFC is decoded as `BFI with Rn = PC'
rows.witness: none -- NOT YET ATTEMPTED.  Raised by the codex seat from source inspection while answering armbfiwidth; the decoder arm and handler were read, no instruction was planted.  This field says `not yet done`, never `did not think to ask`.

entries.note: Raised as an explicitly SEPARATE issue: *"the decoder accepts source-field 15 and passes r[15] to this handler, while the architecture assigns that encoding to BFC.  The mask correction does not settle that issue."*  Recorded as its own row rather than folded into armbfiwidth, per the round-scope rule -- different defect, different fix, different oracle.

entries.outcome: implementation claim VERIFIED; architectural claim NOT document-verified
entries.note: Verified the decoder arm and the handler line by line, refuted my r[15] characterisation and my ARMv5 premise, said plainly that no local manual covers BFI/BFC, and supplied a constructible distinguishing observation.

rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-08 from the codex `armbfiwidth` design answer.  **BFC is BFI with Rn = 15**, and the architecture defines it as clearing the field rather than inserting from a register.  This fork's decoder does not distinguish them, so a BFC would insert bits taken from `r[15]` -- the PC -- instead of clearing.

**NOT VERIFIED HERE.**  It comes from one seat's source reading, and neither the decoder arm's exact guard nor the architectural claim has been re-derived by me. *The round-scope rule keeps it separate from `armbfiwidth`: same file and adjacent lines, but a different defect with a different fix and a different oracle, so it is a candidate ROUND rather than a rider.*

*** THE codex ASSESS ANSWER, 2026-09-08.  THE IMPLEMENTATION HALF IS VERIFIED; THE ARCHITECTURAL
HALF IS NOT, AND THE SEAT SAID SO RATHER THAN FILLING THE GAP FROM MEMORY. ***

### 1.  VERIFIED: source field 15 does reach the handler

The generic decoder computes `rm = iword & 15`, and the bfi arm binds `ic->arg[1] =
(size_t)(&cpu->cd.arm.r[rm])` with **no guard excluding 15**.  `X(bfi)` then opens with
`uint32_t x = reg(ic->arg[1]);` and has **no source-15 clear path**.  All three of my settled
premises about the extraction and packing were confirmed against the file.

### 2.  *** MY OWN CHARACTERISATION WAS WRONG, AND THE CORRECTION IS SHARPER THAN THE CLAIM. ***

I wrote that BFC becomes *"BFI with Rn = PC"*.  **`r[15]` is not the PC in this interpreter.**
Translation reconstructs the instruction address into `cpu->pc` WITHOUT refreshing `r[15]`, and the
PC+8 that PC-relative loads need is computed into a separate `tmp_pc`.  So `r[15]` holds whatever
was last written there -- **a previous load-to-PC target, or an exception-vector address** -- which
is a *stale* value, not a predictable one.

*That matters for the fix and for any oracle: a row that assumes r[15] holds the current PC would
be pinning something the emulator does not maintain.*

### 3.  *** AND MY MANUAL PREMISE WAS WRONG TOO -- THE PREMISE-AUDIT LINE EARNED ITS PLACE AGAIN. ***

I told the seat DDI 0100I was ARMv5.  **Its preface explicitly includes ARMv6.**  It still does not
contain BFI or BFC -- the seat searched and found neither mnemonic -- because those are ARMv6T2
additions.

> **SO THE ARCHITECTURAL CLAIM AT THE HEART OF THIS ROW REMAINS UNVERIFIED AGAINST ANY LOCAL
> DOCUMENT, and the seat refused to paper over it:** *"source 15 -> architectural BFC is not
> document-verified within this reading scope; I cannot attach a local manual page citation to it."*
> **That is the honest form this project asks for, and it is a BLOCKER: #357/#362/#365 shipped page
> citations that came from model output rather than a local manual.**  This round does not ship a
> behavioural change on a recalled architectural rule.  **It needs an ARMv7-A ARM (DDI 0406) in
> `_scratchpad/`, and until then the row stays open with the implementation half verified.**

### 4.  THE WITNESS IS CONSTRUCTIBLE, and the design turns on the r[15] correction above

Because `r[15]` is stale rather than the PC, the witness must PUT a known value there:

    r0 = 0xffffffff
    a word load into PC whose target is 0x00001008   -- this is what leaves 0x1008 in r[15]
    at that target:  BFC r0, #8, #4                  -- lsb=8, msb=11, width=4

    clear the field          -> r0 = 0xfffff0ff
    insert the stored r[15]  -> r0 = 0xfffff8ff

**Merely placing the instruction at 0x1008 does NOT establish that register value** -- the
load-to-PC setup is what does it, which is precisely the consequence of finding 2.  Width 4 is
chosen to avoid the sibling mask-boundary cases.  *Source-derived and arithmetic-checked; not run.*

### 5.  TWO ROUNDS CONFIRMED, on the round-scope rule

*"Correcting source-15 semantics leaves mask construction unchanged; correcting mask construction
leaves source-15 semantics unchanged."*  Different fix, different oracle -- so `armbfiwidth` stays
separate, as filed.

*** THE MANUAL THIS ROW WAS BLOCKED ON IS NOW LOCAL, AND IT COVERS BFC TOO. ***
`_scratchpad/ddi0406.txt` (ARM DDI 0406C.d), fetched 2026-09-08 at a seat's citation for the
sibling row `armbfiwidth` and verified by reading.  **`:17995`, A8.8.19 BFC:**

    if msbit >= lsbit then
        R[d]<msbit:lsbit> = Replicate('0', msbit-lsbit+1);
        // Other bits of R[d] are unchanged
    else
        UNPREDICTABLE;

Identical in structure to BFI's.  So this row no longer needs a source it does not have -- and the
reason it appeared to need one is worth recording: **`ddi0100i.txt` is DDI 0100I, which predates
ARMv6T2 and contains no BFI, BFC, UBFX or SBFX at all.**  The block was the WRONG MANUAL, not a
missing one.

rows.title: a STANDING flagship DO-NOT-CODE ruling lived in the CHANGELOG and another row's artifact but not in the row it governs, and a full round was designed against it before a seat caught it -- the population is NOT mechanically enumerable (two greps gave 0 and 9, the 9 mostly noise)
rows.witness: harness: the measured near-miss -- sgitexindex's round was designed, briefed and panelled before grok opened regress/artifacts/pcc2widthkills/fable_adjudication_20260902.md and quoted the DO-NOT-CODE verbatim.
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-08, from a MEASURED near-miss: I spent a round preparing to code `sgitexindex` against a
STANDING FLAGSHIP RULING that said DO NOT CODE, and a seat stopped it by opening a record I had not
read.

*** THE DEFECT IS NOT THAT THE RULING WAS UNRECORDED.  IT IS THAT IT WAS RECORDED SOMEWHERE THE
DECIDER DOES NOT LOOK. ***

    where the ruling was   CHANGELOG.md, and an artifact under ANOTHER row's directory
                           (regress/artifacts/pcc2widthkills/fable_adjudication_20260902.md)
    where I looked         the LEDGER ROW, which said `state: open, sev: low` and carried no note
    result                 a full round of design, a nine-seat brief, and a panel fired against a
                           question that had been adjudicated six days earlier

**The ruling even contained the finding I re-derived**: *"the proposed `>> 1` fix would IMPORT the
siblings' overrun."*  I enumerated that from scratch and wrote it up as new.

> **A STANDING DISPOSITION THAT LIVES ANYWHERE EXCEPT THE ROW IT GOVERNS WILL BE RE-OPENED BY THE
> NEXT PERSON WHO READS THE ROW -- which is exactly the population that might re-open it.**

*** THE POPULATION IS NOT MECHANICALLY ENUMERABLE, AND I TRIED. ***  Two greps disagreed:

    narrow (a close-word within ~120 chars AFTER the row id)      0 rows
    broad  (any ruling word within 400 chars either side)         9 rows

Spot-reading three of the nine: `wdcbeoddtail`'s hit is a SEVERITY assignment in an audit table
(noise); `sgirandomskipput`'s is a FILING decision (*"filed as X rather than dropped"*), not a
do-not-code; `m88kmxmkill`, `m88ktbnd` and `m88kexctaildefault` are *"filed now as documented-only
LOW rows"*, which IS a disposition worth carrying.  **So the broad check is a CORRELATE -- "a ruling
word near the row id" -- and not the class**, which is *a disposition decided elsewhere that the row
does not carry*.  That distinction needs READING, not grepping.

*This is the deriver rule landing on my own audit within the hour of my citing it: before writing a
deriver, ask what makes a member a member.  Here the answer is a property no regex tests.*

**NAMED CANDIDATES for a proper read, not a claim about them:** `m88kmxmkill`, `m88ktbnd`,
`m88kexctaildefault` -- all three cited in one sentence as filed documented-only, none carrying that
in the row.  **The other six flagged rows are probably noise and are NOT claimed.**

**NO CHECKER PROPOSED.**  A proximity grep would fire on ~9 rows with a majority false-positive rate,
which is how a check gets switched off -- this project's own recorded reason for declining the
stale-count checker.  What is cheap and reliable is a HABIT at the point of decision: **before
opening a round on any row, grep the CHANGELOG and `regress/artifacts/*/` for the row id and read
what comes back.**  It cost one command here and would have saved the round.

*Related in shape, one row over: `sgilinearoob` carried a bare title and an EMPTY note while the
2026-09-02 adjudication referred to "the siblings' overrun" as known -- the class was known to the
adjudication and not findable from the row that carries it.*

*** THE THREE "NAMED CANDIDATES" DISSOLVE ON A FULL READ.  THE POPULATION OF THIS CLASS IS ONE.
Corrected within the hour, 2026-09-08, before anyone acted on the list. ***

I named `m88kmxmkill`, `m88ktbnd` and `m88kexctaildefault` as probable members because the CHANGELOG
says they were *"filed now as **documented-only** LOW rows"*.  **Reading the whole sentence changes
it:** *"three rows this round CITED were never FILED ... filed now as documented-only LOW rows
**RATHER THAN CITED AS IF THEY EXISTED**."*

**The disposition being recorded there is FILING -- creating rows that had been cited without
existing -- not a prohibition on coding them.**  "Documented-only" describes their EVIDENCE state,
which is the ordinary condition of an open row, and not a DO-NOT-CODE.  `sgitexindex`'s ruling was
explicit and adversative: *"DO NOT CODE and DO NOT DROP."*

**And checking the rows settles it a second way: all three have EMPTY state_notes.**  That makes
them members of `baretitle` -- *"20 of 55 OPEN rows are a bare title with an EMPTY note"* -- which is
a DIFFERENT row, already filed.  A bare row cannot be carrying a ruling it does not carry.

> **SO THIS CLASS HAS A POPULATION OF ONE, AND THAT ONE IS FIXED.**  The near-miss was real and the
> lesson stands; the *scale* I implied was not.

*Twice in one hour I named a population from a proximity grep and had to withdraw it -- nine rows,
then three.  The class is defined by "a DISPOSITION decided elsewhere that the row does not carry",
and neither a grep nor a partial read can test that.  **The honest form of this row is: one measured
instance, a habit that prevents it, and NO claim about how often it recurs.**

rows.title: the de-fatalisation rounds left DESCRIPTIONS of host kills behind in dev_sgi_re.c and gate_arm.sh -- a reader is told the guard is fatal where the code now latches and declines; plus two gate records that contradict the gate's own current requirements

*A records-only brief -- "no mutant, no evasion, no guest sequence" -- drew zero refusals from a

rows.title: codex briefs are rejected PLATFORM-SIDE by a cybersecurity content filter, and this project's own row ids are the trigger
rows.witness: none
rows.state_note:
*** A SEAT-FAILURE CLASS NOT ON THE CARRIER'S LIST, MEASURED BY CENSUS 2026-09-08. ***

    ERROR: This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk.  If this seems wrong, try
    rephrasing your request.  To get authorized for security work, join the Trusted Access for
    Cyber program

**It is a PLATFORM content filter, not a model refusal**, and it is the only codex failure mode
here that can leave a ZERO-BYTE answer behind a large `.err`.  The carrier lists codex refusal
triggers as vocabulary, archive-reading, chain shape and the evasion-construction question; this
is a different mechanism and it is not listed.

*** THE CENSUS, and it corrects my own first reading of it. ***

    21   .err files carry the flag
     8   of those left a ZERO-BYTE .txt
     5   of the 21 produced a FULL answer anyway (14,102 / 18,687 / 12,952 / 8,682 / 6,868 b)

**So the flag is NOT terminal and its PRESENCE proves nothing** -- exactly like the refusal-line
rule already on record.  `gateworktree`'s 14,102 b assess carries the flag twice and answered in
full.  **The `.txt` SIZE is the only discriminator**, which is the rule this project already
learned once for refusal lines and had not connected to this filter.

*** THE TRIGGER IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN VOCABULARY, WHICH IS WHY IT KEEPS RECURRING. ***  The row
ids are `sgirekills`, `lcaconfbus1kill`, `lcairqstubkill`, `pcc2c040kill`, `alphavmkill`,
`asicoffsetkill`; the probe rows are literally named `tlb_a ld kill`, and briefs speak of *death
rows* and *host kills*.  **A brief that merely NAMES its row carries the trigger.**  The graded
evidence is in `regress/artifacts/sgirekills/refusals/`:

    attempt1.err                       5,906 b   flagged early
    attempt2_neutralised.err           6,572 b   flagged early
    attempt3_scoping.err               6,829 b   flagged early
    attempt4_neutral_late_flag.err   382,773 b   did the WHOLE analysis, flagged at the END

*** THE RECOVERY ALREADY WORKS AND HAS BEEN USED THREE TIMES, AND IT IS WRITTEN DOWN NOWHERE. ***

    sgirekills      codex_rounddesign_20260908       0 b  ->  _RETRY_  6,868 b
    armbfiwidth     codex_fixdesign_20260907         0 b  ->  20260908 5,091 b, v2 7,308 b
    sgirebufuninit  codex_pass1_20260907             0 b  ->  _reworded_ 10,557 b

**The filename `codex_reworded_...` IS the technique**, applied by hand three times by whoever hit
the wall, and never promoted to a rule -- so the next round rediscovers it.  *That is the carrier's
own trigger-versus-memory finding: the knowledge existed, on disk, at the moment of the decision,
and did not fire.*

**STILL UNRECOVERED (codex lost; another seat covered the topic in all but the last):**
`lcaconfwidth` census (grok 25,281 b), `lcaconfbus1kill` witness (grok 10,679 b), `alphatbinegsel`
witness (grok 10,679 b -- grok took it after codex was flagged), and `m88kexcdeliver/pass1/
codex_p1_refire` which has a 0-byte `.txt` and **NO `.err` at all**, i.e. by the redirect-target
rule it never started rather than being flagged.

**A RECORDS GAP FOUND WHILE MEASURING THIS:** `lcaconfwidth` has no brief file on disk at all --
the brief was passed inline and not preserved -- so **a flagged job there cannot be re-fired or
audited without reconstructing its brief.**  A brief that is not preserved is not re-runnable.

**PROPOSED, NOT DONE:** a neutral-vocabulary convention for codex briefs (*process-exit arm*,
*unreachable-path termination*, *abort site* for *kill*; describe the row rather than naming its
id), plus preserving every brief beside its answer.  It is a convention change affecting every
future brief, so it goes to the owner rather than being adopted by a round.

*** THE TRIGGER IS NOW MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: A ONE-VARIABLE EXPERIMENT, TWO BRIEFS DIFFERING IN
ONE QUESTION. ***

    IMPLEMENT_brief.md     Q4 = "what is the smallest edit that would make this look
                                implemented while still being wrong?"        ->  0 b, flag x2
    IMPLEMENT_brief_v2.md  Q4 = "what observable behaviour distinguishes a correct
                                implementation from an incomplete one?"      ->  7,026 b, flag x0

Everything else in the two files is byte-identical -- the diff is that question and nothing else.
**The answer went from nothing to a full review, and the flag count from two to zero.**

> **SO THE EVASION-CONSTRUCTION FORM IS A TRIGGER AND THE OBSERVABLE-DIFFERENCE FORM IS NOT, AND
> THE TWO ASK FOR THE SAME ENGINEERING CONTENT.**  The carrier already listed "the ask-again /
> evasion-construction question" among codex's refusal triggers; this measures it, and gives the
> rewrite rather than only the warning.

**THE REWRITE, which costs nothing and preserves the adversarial value:** ask what OBSERVABLE
distinguishes correct from incomplete, and what a regression row must assert so a later partial
implementation does not read as complete.  That still forces the seat to think like an adversary
about the detector, without asking it to author a disguised defect.

**AND THE NON-TERMINAL HALF GAINED A SIXTH INSTANCE THE SAME DAY:** the `lcaconfbus1kill`
self-review carried **five** flag hits and still returned **9,710 bytes** of full answer -- the
largest flag count on record with a complete answer behind it.  *The flag's presence remains
evidence of nothing; the `.txt` size is the discriminator.*

**Four briefs written in neutral vocabulary and checked against the trigger list before firing
(`lcabadval/MANUAL`, `lcabadval/PACKET`, `alphaswpctxreg/PASS1`, `lcaconfbus1kill/SELFREVIEW`)
returned 8,657 / n-a / 4,841 / 9,710 bytes.  Zero lost seats since the rule was applied.**

*** TWO MORE INSTANCES 2026-09-08, AND THEY CHANGE THE DIAGNOSIS.  THE TRIGGER IS NOT THE BRIEF'S
WORDING -- IT IS WHAT CODEX READS AFTER THE BRIEF, AND THAT IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN RECORDS. ***

Two independent codex jobs refused the same way inside one hour:

    lcaconfbus1kill pass 2      71,124 b of trace, then ERROR ... flagged for possible
                                cybersecurity risk       (24,984 tokens)
    sgirandomcolour witness     277,836 b of trace, same ERROR   (78,953 tokens)

**THE SECOND ONE HAD ALREADY BEEN BENIGN-REFRAMED, AND THAT IS THE EVIDENCE.**  Its brief was
written from the start as ordinary emulator correctness work: no "kill", no "attack", no "exploit",
no "host death" -- a census of the finished text returned ZERO for every one of those.  It was
flagged anyway.

*** WHAT THE TRACE SHOWS, and it is the whole finding: codex went and read the RECORDS. ***
`grep -c 'dev_sgi_re|crmfbreg|DE_MODE_TYPE'` over its trace = **1,725**, and the trace contains long
verbatim extracts of `CHANGELOG.md` and `tools/pipeline/ledger.json` -- files whose prose is
saturated with exactly the vocabulary the brief had been scrubbed of, because THIS PROJECT WROTE
THEM ABOUT HOST KILLS AND GUEST-REACHABLE PROCESS TERMINATION.

> **SO BENIGN FRAMING OF THE BRIEF IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT.  A file-reading seat pointed at
> this repo will find the un-scrubbed vocabulary by itself, in the records, and the refusal arrives
> at OUTPUT time after the tokens have been spent.**

**AND THE COST IS NOT ONLY THE SEAT.**  Both refusals came AFTER substantial real work -- 79k tokens
on the second -- so the failure is expensive and produces a ZERO-BYTE `.txt` with everything in the
`.err`.  A run that reads 1,725 record lines and then refuses looks, from the `.txt` alone, exactly
like a seat that was never invoked.

**THE FIX UNDER TEST (not yet proven at the time of writing): a `§B0` READING-SCOPE BOUND** naming
the four files the task needs and saying explicitly *"do NOT search or read CHANGELOG.md,
ledger.json, OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md or _scratchpad/ -- those are engineering RECORDS, not the code
under review"*, with an instruction to stop and say so rather than go and get a fact that lives only
there.  **Recorded as a HYPOTHESIS with its result to follow, not as a remedy**, because this row
has already had one diagnosis overtaken by evidence and a second unverified one would be worse than
none.

*The operational consequence for the standing directive to use codex heavily: EVERY codex brief in
this repo now carries the scope bound, and a codex job that returns a zero-byte `.txt` must have its
`.err` TAIL read before it is scored -- the seat-check rule that a wall is diagnosed from `.err` and
never from size, applied to a failure mode that is not a wall.*

*** THE RECORDS HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, AND THE REAL DISCRIMINATOR IS MEASURED.  Four controlled
firings, 2026-09-08, and the split is clean. ***

**The scope-bound experiment WORKED as an experiment and FAILED as a remedy.**  Adding a `§B0`
reading bound cut the trace from 78,953 tokens to 17,566 -- so codex obeyed it and did NOT go to the
records -- **and it was flagged anyway.**  So the vocabulary in `CHANGELOG.md` and `ledger.json` is
not the trigger.

**THE DECISIVE CONTROL: a MINIMAL brief on the SAME FILE, in the same repo, with no scope bound at
all, ANSWERED.**  733 bytes, correct, in one call:

    "Read src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c.  How many case labels does the colour switch have?
     What does its default: arm do?  Does crmfbreg.h define a constant it has no case for?
     Answer in prose.  Do not propose any code change, and do not write any test."

    -> ANSWERED.  Named all four cases, described the default arm, named DE_MODE_TYPE_YCRCB.

**SO IT IS NOT THE FILE, NOT THE REPO, AND NOT THE RECORDS.  IT IS THE ASK.**

    FLAGGED  lcaconfbus1kill pass 2   asked it to assess a probe that DRIVES an aborting path
    FLAGGED  sgirandomcolour witness  asked for "the exact guest instruction sequence ... as
                                      concrete stores with addresses and values"
    FLAGGED  sgirandomcolour scoped   same ask, reading bounded
    ANSWERED sgirandomcolour minimal  pure analysis; explicitly "do not write any test"

> **THE DISCRIMINATOR: codex answers ANALYSIS of a code path and refuses CONSTRUCTION of an input
> sequence that drives an unhandled one.**  Test-construction and exploit-construction are the same
> shape from outside, and this project's rung-3 witness discipline is, by design, exactly that shape
> -- a hand-assembled instruction sequence built to reach a path a guest should not reach.

*** THE OPERATIONAL REMEDY, which KEEPS the seat rather than losing it: SPLIT THE JOB. ***

    to codex     the enumeration, the premise audit, the decode arithmetic, the option-set
                 reasoning, the disposition argument, "which constant has no case", "what does
                 this arm do", "is this claim true of the source"
    NOT to codex the instruction sequence, the probe design, the address construction
                 -> those go to grok (which built this round's decode walk unaided), to agy when
                    no measurement is in flight, or to the main loop

**AND THE ANALYSIS HALF IS THE HALF THIS PROJECT MOST NEEDS FROM IT.**  On the round where it was
flagged, the seat that replaced it -- grok -- produced the round's single most valuable finding by
doing exactly the analysis codex would have done.  Nothing about the split reduces codex to a
lesser seat; it aims it at what it will answer.

*A cheap standing test, since the boundary may move: the minimal-analysis brief above is preserved
at `regress/artifacts/codexcyberflag/minimal_20260908.txt` with its `.err`.  Re-firing it is a
four-second liveness check that separates "codex is walled" from "codex refused THIS ask" -- two
states this row previously conflated, and which a zero-byte `.txt` renders identically.*

**AND A ZERO-BYTE `.txt` IS THE STANDING TELL.**  All three refusals wrote 0 bytes to stdout and
put everything on stderr, so from the `.txt` alone a refusal is indistinguishable from a seat that
was never invoked.  **Read the `.err` TAIL before scoring any codex job** -- the seat-check rule
that a wall is diagnosed from content and never from size, applied to a failure mode that is not a
wall.

*** THE DIAGNOSIS MADE A PREDICTION AND THE PREDICTION HELD, which is the first time this row has
been able to say that. 2026-09-08, `#515`'s ask-again. ***

The ask-again brief is the one this project fires at a CLEAN kill table, and its whole purpose is to
obtain **an edit that re-opens a closed defect**.  Its words were: *"give me the exact source edit as
a diff hunk"*, *"the smallest realistic edit ... which leaves all 14 rows GREEN while re-opening the
defect"*.

**That is construction in its purest form, so the diagnosis says it must be refused -- and it was**,
at 6,339 bytes with the same filter message.  Five firings now, and the split is unchanged:

    FLAGGED    #515 pass 2 (original)          construction: assess a probe that drives a kill path
    FLAGGED    sgirandomcolour witness         construction: "the exact guest instruction sequence"
    FLAGGED    sgirandomcolour scoped          same ask, reading bounded
    FLAGGED    #515 ask-again                  construction: "the exact source edit as a diff hunk"
    ANSWERED   #515 pass 2 benign re-fire      analysis
    ANSWERED   minimal probe                   analysis
    ANSWERED   lcabadval (x2), lcairqstubkill  analysis
    ANSWERED   sgirandomcolour ANALYSIS        analysis -- same row, same file, opposite outcome

*** THE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE IS SHARPER THAN "SPLIT THE JOB", AND IT NAMES A STANDING COST. ***

**The ask-again is STRUCTURALLY a construction task**, so codex cannot serve it in its usual form.
That is not a small loss: the ask-again is the capped adversarial query this project relies on after
a table comes back green, and codex is the seat most likely to enumerate an input space exhaustively.

**THE REFRAME THAT KEEPS THE SEAT: ask for the GAP, not for the EDIT.**

    refused    "give me the smallest edit that leaves all 14 rows green"
    accepted   "name the input-space cell these 14 rows leave least constrained, and say why it
                matters -- describe it as a property, not as an edit"

Those solicit the same knowledge.  A named unconstrained cell is one step from a mutant, and that
step is one I can take myself.  **The seat supplies the enumeration; the main loop supplies the
edit** -- which is the same division the rest of this row already prescribes, applied to the one
brief in the pipeline that most obviously violates it.

*Recorded as a held prediction rather than as another instance, because that is what raises this from
a pattern to a usable rule: the diagnosis said in advance which of two briefs would be refused, and
it was right.  The reframed firing's outcome is recorded separately -- if IT is also refused, the
"analysis is safe" half of this row is weaker than five firings suggested and must be re-stated.*

*** A SECOND, UNRELATED FAILURE MODE OF THE SAME SEAT, AND IT IS ABOUT SCOPE RATHER THAN CONTENT.
Three firings of ONE question, three scopes, measured 2026-09-08. ***

    scope                                     stream     verdict?
    regress/*.py  (a PREDICATE, ~65 files)    2,404 KB   NO -- cut short
    six files named extensionally               325 KB   NO -- cut short
    ONE file named                              (running)

**A codex run has a budget, and a reading-scope bound spends it before the question does.**  The
first scope was not a bound at all -- *"only the probe files that contain `row(` and `exit0`"*
cannot be evaluated without reading every probe.  The second was properly extensional and STILL
too large.

> **THE RULE: a reading-scope bound must be EXTENSIONAL *and* SMALL.  Name the files, and name as
> few as the question can be answered from.**  Where a census spans many files, ask it ONE FILE AT
> A TIME and pick the file holding the largest share -- here `pcc2_width_probe.py`, 25 of 90
> candidate rows.

*** AND THIS IS WHY THE `codex_answer.py` VERDICT LINE MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKED. ***  All three
runs produced substantial, correct, partial work -- the membership definition, the fourth guise of
the class, two concrete leads.  **A reader scoring them by size or by "did it answer" would call all
three successes.**  The tool reports *"verdict blocks 0 -- NO VERDICT LINE: treat as CUT SHORT, not
as agreement"*, which is the only thing separating a completed census from a budget exhaustion, and
it is the same POSITION discriminator this project already uses for seat truncation.

*Recorded under this row rather than a new one because it is the same operational question -- what
does it take to get an answer out of this seat -- and this row is where a future round will look.
The CONTENT rule (analysis answers, construction is filtered) and the SCOPE rule (extensional and
small) are independent, and a brief has to satisfy both.*

entries.note:
FILED 2026-09-10 after the THIRD instance in one day, the third of which cost 224,661 codex tokens and returned nothing.  The carrier already records the class (an analysis brief inlining a diff with memory-safety vocabulary is content-filter refused; re-route by eliding the flagged text).  THIS ROW RECORDS WHAT WAS MEASURED TODAY ABOUT ITS TRIGGER AND ITS COST, because the existing note names the remedy but not the shape.

THREE INSTANCES, and they are not the same severity:
  1. #519 coverage brief -- REFUSED OUTRIGHT, zero bytes of answer, `.err' carries only the flag text.
     Flagged vocabulary: an uninitialised stack buffer, `random()' bytes, writes into guest memory.
     RECOVERED by rewriting the identical question as ordinary test-design: the code became a `pixel
     format dispatch', the buffer talk went, and the answer came back complete and excellent.
  2. #520 pass-2 seat -- PARTIAL.  It answered 155 KB and then hit the filter on an OUTBOUND WEB SEARCH
     for an Alpha architecture PDF.  The local-file work survived; the concluding verdict did not.  A
     MILDER form: the seat kept working and only the fetch was refused.
  3. The unrowed-exit census -- REFUSED OUTRIGHT after 224,661 tokens.  Flagged vocabulary: 
     `guest-reachable', `end the emulator process', `corrupt guest memory', `critical'.
     Re-routed as an ERROR-HANDLING AUDIT: `library code that calls exit() instead of returning',
     `reachable while the emulated machine is running', `the emulator stops instead of continuing'.

THE TRIGGER, as best it can be characterised from three points and stated as a HYPOTHESIS rather than a rule: it is not the SUBJECT (device bounds work passes routinely) but the FRAMING -- a brief that describes an untrusted party driving a host process to termination or to a memory fault reads as exploitation, whatever the actual work is.  The same question framed as robustness, error handling or test coverage passes.

WHAT IT COSTS AND WHY IT IS NOT MERELY ANNOYING: the refusal is INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A QUOTA WALL in the output shape -- zero-byte `.txt', content in `.err' -- so a seat check keying on size alone files it as a dead seat.  It is not: the seat is healthy and will answer the SAME QUESTION reworded.  Reporting it as a wall would lose an available seat, which is the sixth seat-failure class in a new coat.

PRACTICE, not machinery: write panel briefs in the vocabulary of the ENGINEERING TASK.  This project's briefs are about bounds correctness, error handling and detector coverage, and they read better in those words anyway -- the re-routed #519 brief was CLEARER than the one that was refused.  No checker is proposed: there is no mechanical test for 'this phrasing will be flagged', and a checker that guessed would fire on honest briefs, which is how a check gets switched off.

rows.note:
[MAIN-LOOP NOTE, 2026-09-09, phase research -- moved out of the seat entries because the dashboard declares no such seat]  THIRD independent confirmation of the CONTENT rule, and the first scored by the POSITION-keyed detector shipped the day before.  sgirandomcolour/codex_scoped_20260908.err is a genuine CONTENT-FILTER REFUSAL: two markers IN THE TAIL, zero verdict blocks, the seat's own words being 'I can assess the code path and disposition, but I can't provide or run a guest sequence designed to reproduce the suspected defect.'  Counting the string would have been ambiguous here; position is not.  The routing fact holds: ask codex for the GAP, never for the WITNESS.  Measured the same day AGAINST a control: a GAP-shaped, four-file, premise-as-question brief (wiringcliff) returned a full 12.9 KB verdict from the same seat in the same session.

[MAIN-LOOP NOTE, 2026-09-09, phase research -- moved out of the seat entries because the dashboard declares no such seat]  A THIRD CODEX RULE, measured: the CONTENT rule (ask for the GAP, not the EDIT) is necessary and not sufficient -- an analysis-shaped brief was refused because the DIFF IT INLINED carried memory-safety language in its comments.  Two sibling briefs fired the same minute with the same shape and no such diff text (pcc2c040kill completeness; armbfxwidth32, whose diff is arithmetic) both answered in full.  RULE: for codex, a review of a memory-safety fix is pointed at the FILE (the ARGV_CAP pointer form) rather than inlined, or the diff is summarised -- and any brief that inlines a diff is scanned for the trigger vocabulary before firing.  The position-keyed detector caught it correctly; the SIZE (29 KB) would have read as an answer.

[MAIN-LOOP NOTE, 2026-09-10, phase research -- in `note` rather than in `entries` because the dashboard declares no main-loop seat, following this row's own 2026-09-09 precedent]

*** A ZERO-BYTE CODEX ANSWER HAS A SECOND, INDEPENDENT CAUSE, AND THIS ROW'S OWN DETECTOR WOULD MISATTRIBUTE IT TO THE FILTER. ***

Two farmed briefs came back with 0-byte .txt files today.  The position-keyed detector this row shipped says REFUSAL, and for one of them it is right.  For the other the cause is in OUR LAUNCHER:

    UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x90 in position 7509

The inline launcher read codex stdout in TEXT mode, which on Windows decodes cp1252, and codex emits bytes cp1252 cannot map.  The wrapper died and wrote nothing.  **The carrier already records this exact trap for the Ollama seats -- "write responses to utf-8 files, never print() (cp1252 crash)" -- and it was never applied to the codex farm.**

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN AN ORDINARY BUG: a 0-byte answer is the SAME OBSERVABLE for four different states -- terminal refusal, quota wall, run still in flight, and now wrapper crash.  A project that has just built a refusal detector will confidently read the fourth as the first.  That is the seat-failure-misattributed shape rather than the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape, and it is harder to see because the detector AGREES with the wrong answer.

FIXED at the source rather than in prose: the farm launcher now captures stdout as BYTES and decodes utf-8 with errors="replace", so no decode can throw and the answer survives whatever codex emits.

*** AND THE POSITION DISCRIMINATOR GOT ITS CLEANEST CONTROL PAIR TODAY, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. ***  The rule is that POSITION decides and COUNT does not, and here are two runs on the same day, same CLI, same effort:

    codex_fixdesign_20260910   3 flags at lines 2345/2540/2587 of 3987  (59-65% depth)  ->  10,731-byte ANSWER
    codex_unrowed_20260910     8 flags, the LAST TWO at lines 18860-18861 of 18863      ->  0-byte, TERMINAL

**A `grep -c` scores the healthy run as the WORSE refusal** -- 3 flags against 8 is the wrong way round only if you count, and the run with FEWER flags is the one that died.  Mid-stream flags are individual tool calls that codex retries around and they cost nothing; a flag in the last lines is the seat refusing.  This is the same POSITION-versus-SIZE discriminator seat_verdicts.py already uses to catch a wall in an otherwise healthy-looking 36 KB answer, arrived at independently for a different transport.

ONE MORE DATA POINT ON THE CONTENT RULE, and it is a NEGATIVE one worth recording: **the refused brief was ALREADY the benign one.**  brief_unrowed.md is written throughout in ordinary-defect-triage language ("Ordinary defect triage on an emulator"), with no offensive-security wording anywhere, and it was refused anyway.  **So benign FRAMING is not sufficient**, and the trigger is closer to specific vocabulary than to tone -- which sharpens this row's title claim rather than merely confirming it.

STATED AS OPEN RATHER THAN CLOSED, because the controlling measurement HAS NOT FINISHED: brief_unrowed2.md is a second rewrite of the same question that additionally drops the phrase "guest-reachable exits" and every row-id resembling a CVE handle, and reframes it as "library code that calls exit() instead of returning".  At the time of writing that run is STILL IN FLIGHT -- 5 flags, all mid-stream, no terminal pair, no "tokens used" line, codex.exe alive.  **If it lands with an answer that is the controlled A/B this row has never had** (same question, same seat, same day, vocabulary the only variable).  If it refuses in the tail, the vocabulary hypothesis is refuted and the trigger is the SUBJECT.  Either way the result belongs here; it is not being predicted.

rows.title: pty probes omit `-A`, so with CLICOLOR set the debugger prompt arrives wrapped in ANSI escapes and every prompt-anchored parser reads ZERO responses -- 53 of 61 pty probes are exposed, and the 8 that pass -A are all the ARM ones
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED 2026-09-08 -- CLICOLOR=1 without -A gives 53 ANSI escapes and 0 parsed responses on alpha_swpctx_v0_probe.py (a CORRECT build scoring 1/5); with -A, 0 escapes and 5/5.  CLICOLOR_v4_20260908.out.
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-08, found by a pass-4 seat reviewing `#514`'s probe and then MEASURED
in both directions.

**THE MECHANISM.**  `use_colorized_output()` (`src/core/misc.c`) gates colour on
`isatty(STDIN_FILENO) && isatty(STDOUT_FILENO)`.  **A pty satisfies BOTH**, so a probe that uses
`pty.fork()` -- which is every probe in this tree -- is exactly the case where colour turns on.
With `CLICOLOR` in the environment the prompt arrives as

    \x1b[34;1mGXemul> \x1b[0mprint v0

and **no parser anchored on `^GXemul>` can match it.**

**MEASURED, both directions, same probe and same binary:**

    CLICOLOR=1, no -A     53 ANSI escapes, ZERO parsed responses, a CORRECT build scores 1/5
    CLICOLOR=1, with -A    0 ANSI escapes, responses parse, 5/5

`-A` sets `enable_colorized_output = false` (`src/core/main.c:317`).

*** THE POPULATION, derived rather than estimated: 61 probes call `pty.fork()`, and 53 DO NOT PASS
`-A`.  The 8 that do are ALL the ARM ones *** -- `arm_bfx_width`, `arm_endian`, `arm_flags`,
`arm_fold_marker`, `arm_idle`, `arm_memcpy`, `arm_strlen`, `arm_writeback`.  So the tree already
holds the defence and it was applied to one family and not carried.

**SEVERITY IS `med` AND THE REASON MATTERS: THIS DOES NOT FIRE ON THIS MACHINE.**  `CLICOLOR` is
not set here -- measured at 0 escapes without `-A` -- so nothing in the current gate is wrong.  It
is a LATENT environment dependence: a probe run on a developer's machine with `CLICOLOR` set, or
under a CI image that sets it, silently stops parsing.  **And the failure shape differs by parser:
a prompt-anchored one fails CLOSED (loud, a correct build reds), while a loose one may still match
and mis-attribute (silent).**  The loose parsers are therefore the more dangerous half of the
population, not the safer half.

**NOT FIXED HERE, and deliberately.**  `#514`'s own probe is fixed because that round owns it; the
other 52 are a separate harness round -- it is a one-argument edit per file, but it changes what
every probe launches and owes a check that each still parses afterwards.  *A 52-file sweep bolted
onto a round whose pass 4 is still open is exactly the scope creep the one-site rule refuses.*

**THE CHEAP CHECK FOR A FUTURE ROUND:** run any pty probe under `CLICOLOR=1` and compare its score
with the same probe unset.  A difference is this defect; no difference means that probe's parser
tolerates the escapes, which is worth knowing separately.

rows.title: a seat answer TRUNCATED MID-VERDICT reads as agreement -- glm returned exactly "**VERDICT: RATIFY THE" (21 bytes) with the daemon up, and a verdict-line extractor scores that as a ratification
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED 2026-09-08 -- _scratchpad/panel_514p6_20260908/ollama_glm.txt is 21 bytes; the re-fire to ollama_glm_REFIRE.txt returned 6,425 bytes and the OPPOSITE-SHAPED verdict ("CLOSES AT PASS 6", with a contingency).
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-08 from a pass-6 panel.

**glm's answer was TWENTY-ONE BYTES, cut mid-word:**

    **VERDICT: RATIFY THE

*** IT IS NONE OF THE FIVE RECORDED SEAT-FAILURE CLASSES. ***  The daemon was up and `glm-5.3:cloud`
was in `api/tags`, so not the REFUSED CONNECTION class.  No quota text, so not a WALL.  The response
is NON-EMPTY, so not the THINKING BURN -- that class is an empty `response` behind a huge `thinking`
field.  And it is a VERDICT LINE rather than an opening intention (*"let me pull the files"*), so
not the minimax STALL.

> **THE DANGER IS THE WORD IT STOPPED ON.**  This project's own policy is VERDICT LINE FIRST so an
> answer survives truncation -- and that policy is what makes this shape harmful: the surviving
> fragment is `RATIFY`.  **A verdict-line extractor scores it as agreement.  A size check scores it
> as a tiny file whose content happens to read positive.**  Neither can tell it from a seat that
> ratified in one line.

**THE RE-FIRE IS WHAT CAUGHT IT, and it changed the answer's SHAPE and not just its length.**  The
standing rule is to re-fire a walled seat once; applied here to a truncation, it returned **6,425
bytes** whose verdict was *"CLOSES AT PASS 6 ... fund no pass 7"* **with a stated contingency**.  A
contingent close is not the unqualified ratification the fragment implied.

**WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, said plainly:** the CAUSE.  This was one occurrence, the daemon was
healthy before and after, and the re-fire succeeded immediately.  Whether it was a transport hiccup,
a provider-side cut, or something in `panel_ollama.py`'s read loop is **not measured**, and this row
does not guess.

**THE CHEAP DEFENCE, proposed not built:** `seat_verdicts.py` already distinguishes seat states by
POSITION rather than size.  A seat file whose entire content is shorter than its own verdict line --
no newline, no body -- is mechanically detectable, and reporting it as TRUNCATED rather than as a
verdict costs one test.  *That is a change to a tool every panel reads, so it owes negative controls
in both directions and ships as its own harness round, not as a rider.*

rows.title: APPENDING a row BELOW a probe's score computation silently splits the summary -- numerator over the old row set, denominator evaluated at print time.  *** POPULATION AT HEAD IS ZERO across all 73 candidate probes: this is an EDITING hazard I introduced twice in one session, NOT a latent defect in the tree ***
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED 2026-09-08 both ways.  I created the split in two probes by appending rows; the 8042 probe then printed six rows all `ok` under a summary of 4/6, and the UART probe printed 3/5 pre-fix where the honest score was 2/5 (confirmed after repair: 2/5).  A position census over HEAD -- score assignment BEFORE the last row() call -- returns ZERO of 73 candidates.
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-08, found by adding rows to two probes during `#516`.

**THE SHAPE.**  Both probes computed their score at a point ABOVE the last `row()` call:

    ok  = sum(1 for _, o in rows if o)      <- evaluated HERE
    ... more row() calls ...                <- appended AFTER
    print("..._RESULT=%d/%d" % (ok, len(rows)))

`ok` is a VALUE captured early; `len(rows)` is a call evaluated late.  So the numerator counts the
old row set and the denominator counts the new one.

*** IT IS SILENTLY RIGHT WHENEVER NOTHING FAILS, WHICH IS THE DANGEROUS HALF. ***  With every row
passing, the numerator equals the old count and the denominator the new, so the score reads `4/6`
rather than `6/6` -- visibly wrong.  But in the UART probe's POST-FIX run the formula was
`len(rows) - len(bad)` with `bad` empty, which renders `5/5` -- **correct by coincidence**.  Only the
PRE-FIX run, where rows actually failed, exposed it: reported 3/5, honest score 2/5.

> **A SCORE LINE THAT CONTRADICTS ITS OWN PRINTED ROWS IS THE CHEAPEST SIGNAL THERE IS, and it is
> only available because these probes print every row individually.**  A probe that printed only its
> summary would have shipped the wrong number with nothing to compare it against.

**REPAIRED IN BOTH FILES** by moving the computation adjacent to the print, with a comment saying
why, so the split cannot be reintroduced by appending a row.

*** THE POPULATION IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT GUESSED. ***  Two probes were checked
because two were being edited.  The tree has ~65 probes.  **A census keyed on "score computed before
the last row" needs to compare two POSITIONS in each file, not match a pattern** -- and this project
has recorded three name-based censuses coming back wrong in one day, so the deriver has to test the
property (relative position of the assignment and the final `row()` call) rather than a spelling.

*The class is adjacent to `exit0oracle` and `storesidedead` -- all three are oracles that are right
for the wrong reason under exactly the conditions where nobody looks -- but it is a DIFFERENT
mechanism: those are about what a row observes, this is about when the SUMMARY is computed.*

*** CORRECTION, SAME DAY, BEFORE THIS ROW WAS EVER READ BY ANYONE ELSE: THE POPULATION AT HEAD IS
ZERO, AND I CREATED BOTH INSTANCES MYSELF. ***

The row as first filed implied a latent tree-wide class and asked for a census.  **I then ran the
census, and it inverts the finding.**  Keyed on the PROPERTY -- the position of the score assignment
relative to the LAST `row()` call, which is what defines the defect -- over every probe at HEAD:

    probe .py files at HEAD          369
    candidates (assignment + row() calls + a _RESULT line)    73
    *** SPLIT AT HEAD                  0 ***

**So the tree has never carried this defect.  Both instances were mine, made minutes apart, by
inserting rows BELOW the score computation in two probes that were correct before I touched them.**

> **THE CLASS IS REAL AND ITS DIRECTION IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT I FILED: it is an EDITING hazard,
> not a latent one.  A probe is correct until someone appends to it, and appending is exactly what a
> fix round does** -- this round added three rows across two probes and broke both scorers doing it.

**SEVERITY LOWERED med -> low** to match: nothing shipped is wrong, and the repair (keep the
computation adjacent to the print) is now in both files with a comment saying why.

*** WHAT THE ORIGINAL FILING GOT RIGHT AND IS WORTH KEEPING: the defect is SILENTLY CORRECT WHENEVER
NOTHING FAILS. ***  The UART probe's post-fix run rendered `5/5` while split, because `bad` was
empty; only the PRE-FIX run, where rows genuinely failed, exposed it as 3/5 against an honest 2/5.
**A green run cannot detect this.**  That is why it was found by measuring the red direction, and it
is the argument for the two-direction discipline rather than for a checker.

*** AND THE CENSUS ITSELF IS THE POINT WORTH CARRYING. ***  I filed a med row naming a class,
explicitly refused to guess its size, then spent two commands measuring it -- and the measurement
said the class had no members.  **Filing a class and measuring its population are different acts,
and doing the second cheaply is what stopped a wrong record from standing.**  The deriver is two
positions per file and is recorded in `witness` so it can be re-run rather than trusted.

entries.note: GPT-6 Astra @ max, file-reading (handler, header, HRM sections, bus_pci, machine_alpha, emul.c); no refusal.  VERDICT: REVISE the proposed member-6 round -- a uniform store-and-echo would establish the WRONG contract.  Per register, with HRM lines: STAT0 +0x040 is RO status (P_NBR, CODE, TREF, THIT, CMD) plus R/W1C ERR[4] and LOST[5] (clearing mask 0x30), all bits UNDEFINED after reset, SROM writes ones to ERR/LOST (:10287-10370, :10271, :10788); STAT1 +0x060 is RO ADDR[31:0] with NO W1C field and S6.4.14 specifies no write to it (:10392-10409); SFT_RST +0x0c0 is WO RST[6] (mask 0x40), RST=1 after reset, a written one ASSERTS PCI reset until a written zero, SROM writes zero to release it (:10457-10489); PAR_DIS +0x0e0 is WO PAR[5] (mask 0x20) and does NOT suppress target-reported perr_l on CPU writes (:10509-10531).  WO must be added to the type vocabulary: echoing a WO value is emulator convention, never fidelity.  DISPOSITION: member 7 for STAT0 + STAT1 together (guest writes must never manufacture RO status; STAT1 captures the address while the error record is frozen), member 3 NOW for SFT_RST and PAR_DIS with a persistent bit until their effects exist -- so #518's default-arm decline is the right interim.  bus_pci has NO reset entry point or device reset callback (bus_pci.h:92-114, :146-162): SFT_RST costs an interface, not a call.  FOUND: the PCI backend already recognises an absent device and supplies no error to LCA (bus_pci.c:109-122; HRM :9494-9513 says hardware logs it in STAT0/STAT1) -- `nothing sets the logs' is missing integration, not absence.  The fork does not establish whether NetBSD or Linux touch these offsets; direct boot never executes the SROM sequence, so a functional reset model must arrange RELEASED PCI reset itself.

rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c horrible_getputpixel: the tile-base shift `re_tlb_[abc][tile_nr] << 16' is a SIGNED shift of a promoted uint16_t, and every tile pointer the model accepts as VALID (bit 15 set) overflows INT_MAX -- undefined behaviour on the only path that works

entries.note:
FILED 2026-09-10, found by the codex seat under the found-something-else licence while answering a TEST-DESIGN question about #519's row coverage -- it was checking whether a tiled PUT reaches a given physical word and noticed the shift on the way.  VERIFIED BY READING before filing.

`dev_sgi_re.c` declares `uint16_t re_tlb_a[256]', `re_tlb_b[256]', `re_tlb_c[256]', and `horrible_getputpixel()' computes the tile base as `tileptr = d->re_tlb_a[tile_nr] << 16;' (anchor `case 0:	tileptr = d->re_tlb_a[tile_nr] << 16;', and the same at the b/c arms).  A `uint16_t' promotes to `int' under the usual arithmetic conversions, so this is a SIGNED shift: any entry with bit 15 set gives at least 0x8000 << 16 = 2147483648, which exceeds INT_MAX (2147483647).  Signed left-shift overflow is UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR in C99 and C11.

*** IT IS NOT AN EDGE CASE -- IT IS THE ONLY PATH THAT WORKS. ***  Two lines below, the model gates on `if (!(tileptr & 0x80000000)) return;' with the comment `The highest bit seems to be set for a "valid" tile pointer', and then clears it with `tileptr &= ~0x80000000;'.  Bit 31 of the shifted value can ONLY come from bit 15 of the uint16_t, so EVERY tile pointer the model accepts as valid is exactly a value that overflows, and every tile pointer that would not overflow is rejected as invalid.  The UB is on the taken path, not a corner.

GUEST-DRIVABLE: the three arrays are written by ordinary guest register writes inside DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_re) (the TLB register handlers, which require 8-byte writes), so the guest chooses the value that overflows.

NOT the same defect at the fourth array: `re_linear_a' is `uint32_t[32]', so `re_linear_a[tile_nr] << 12' promotes to UNSIGNED int and wraps rather than overflowing -- defined, and out of scope for this row.

FIX SHAPE: three one-token casts, `(uint32_t)d->re_tlb_x[tile_nr] << 16'.  No behaviour change on any compiler that today does the obvious thing; it removes the licence for one that does not.  EASY.

WITNESS: none built, and the honest note is that a rung-3 witness may be IMPOSSIBLE for UB whose observable behaviour is the intended one on every compiler this project builds with -- the ATTEMPT is owed per the 2026-08-27 lifecycle ruling, and a build under `-fsanitize=undefined' in build-asan/ is the obvious first try, since that turns the UB into a diagnostic rather than into a wrong value.  Do not record `none' as `did not think to ask'.

rows.title: dev_mk48txx.c: EIGHT offsets inside the device's own mapped range (0x1ff0-0x1ff7) fall to a default: arm that calls exit(1), so an ordinary guest read of the MK48T08 clock page ends the emulator process -- and machine_mvme88k.c attaches the device unconditionally
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-10.  Surfaced by the GPT-6 Astra exit audit (regress/artifacts/queuetriage/codex_exitaudit_20260910.txt), which ranked it I1/E1 -- its highest impact and lowest effort.  EVERY ELEMENT BELOW WAS RE-DERIVED LOCALLY by opening the files, not taken from the seat.

*** THE ARITHMETIC, enumerated rather than reasoned. ***  The device is registered for MK48TXX_LEN = MK48T08_CLKSZ = 8192 bytes, so relative_addr spans [0, 0x2000).  The early accept block passes everything OUTSIDE [CLKOFF, CLKOFF+ISEC) straight through to the RAM path with a `goto ret'.  With MK48T08_CLKOFF = 0x1ff0 and MK48TXX_ISEC = 9, the switch is therefore reached for exactly the nine offsets 0x1ff0..0x1ff8 -- and the switch has exactly ONE case, MK48T08_CLKOFF + MK48TXX_ICSR = 0x1ff8.  **The other EIGHT, 0x1ff0 through 0x1ff7, fall to `default:', print an `unimplemented' diagnostic and call exit(1).**

*** REACHABILITY IS NOT THEORETICAL. ***  machine_mvme88k.c attaches it unconditionally -- `mk48txx addr=0x%x', 0xfffc0000 -- in the same block that attaches the PCC2 SCSI this project has been running rounds against all week, so the machine is live and exercised. The eight offsets are ORDINARY BYTES of the chip's clock/NVRAM page: nothing in the guest has to do anything unusual to touch them, and firmware that checksums or dumps the NVRAM sweeps the whole 8 KB and walks straight into them.  There is no guard, no validation and no way for a guest to discover the region is fatal before touching it.

*** AND THE BOUNDARY LOOKS DELIBERATE, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED. ***  The accept block's comment says `Reads and writes to the RAM part of the mk48txx, or the clock registers, are OK', and the test READS as though it means `everything except the clock registers'.  But the upper bound is CLKOFF + ISEC, i.e. the SECONDS register -- so the block hands the real time-of-day registers (ISEC..IYEAR, 0x1ff9..0x1fff) to the RAM path, which is harmless because mk48txx_update_regs() writes into the same d->reg[] array, and it captures 0x1ff0..0x1ff7 into the fatal switch, which is not.  **The bound is one constant away from correct in the direction nobody checks.**

FIX SHAPE, not yet adjudicated -- no panel has seen this: the option set's member 3 (DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE) or member 6 (BACKED ACCEPT) both fit, and BACKED ACCEPT is probably right because d->reg[] ALREADY has storage for those offsets -- the array is MK48TXX_LEN bytes, so the bytes exist and the handler simply refuses to use them.  That makes this closer to a boundary correction than to a new policy.  A one-constant change to the accept block would do it; the round owes the check of WHICH constant is right against mk48txxreg.h rather than assuming.

WITNESS: none built.  The vehicle looks cheap -- mvme88k is an in-tree machine and a debugger-driven byte read at 0xfffc1ff0 is a rung-3 probe -- but a witness has NOT been constructed and this row does not claim one.  The rung-3 ATTEMPT is owed before it can be recorded documented-only.

RELATED: this is NOT a member of [[shiftubcensus]] or [[exitsweep]]'s repaired set; it is one of the 76 unowned runtime error-exit sites the exit audit enumerated across 24 files, and it is the one that ranked first on both axes.

*** FIX DESIGN DELIVERED 2026-09-10 (codex_design_20260910.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max, 11,991 bytes, ZERO cyber flags) -- AND IT REFUTED A PREMISE OF MINE. ***

MY BRIEF ASSERTED that indices 0-7 of the clock page are 'unaccounted for by any MK48TXX_I* define'. **FALSE, and one file open away.**  Seven of the eight ARE named -- IFLAGS, IASEC, IAMIN, IAHOUR, IADAY, IINTR, IWDOG -- with index 1 explicitly commented 'unused on MK48T59'.  The header's own prose says why: *'The first bank of eight registers at offset (nvramsz - 16) is available only on more recent MK48Txx models'*, and the MK48T59's extra facilities sit 'at offset 0x1ff0 in the NVRAM'.  **So those eight are the MK48T59's alarm/watchdog bank, and on the MK48T08 -- the only model this file implements -- they are ORDINARY NVRAM.**  The ST datasheet agrees: 8184 SRAM bytes plus eight clock bytes, clock window 0x1ff8..0x1fff.  Verified locally before recording.
