rows.title: cpu_ppc_instr.c X(rldimi): the rotate loop's post-decrement leaves sh == -1, so the insert mask always runs to bit 63 instead of 63-SH -- the instruction OVERWRITES the 64-SH destination bits the architecture requires it to PRESERVE, for every SH != 0
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-10 from the [[ppcrldiclzero]] witness's sibling audit.  MEASURED, not read.

The handler rotates with a `while (sh-- != 0)' loop, which ALWAYS exits with sh == -1 because the post-decrement runs once more than the body.  The mask loop then terminates on a condition involving 63 - sh, i.e. 64 -- always.  The architecture requires the mask to END AT 63-SH (the rldimix RTL and its prose, '1 bits from bit MB through bit 63 - SH').

MEASURED with the destination seeded to 0 and an all-ones source:
    SH=8    got 0xffffffffffffffff   want 0xffffffffffffff00
    SH=32   got 0xffffffffffffffff   want 0xffffffff00000000
    SH=0    got 0xffffffffffffffff   want 0xffffffffffffffff   -- the one safe case

**This is the standard bitfield INSERT.**  A compiler using it to splice a field destroys everything to the right of that field.  Live for every SH != 0.

*** THE DURABLE REPAIR IS NOT TO PATCH THE 63 - sh EXPRESSION. ***  That loop idiom is shared by rldicl, rldicr AND rldimi; rldicr survives only because it never reads sh again.  **Any future edit that reaches for sh after the rotate loop in any of the three will be wrong the same way.**  Save sh before the loop instead.

Same reachability and the same gate blind spot as [[ppcrldiclzero]]: 64-bit CPUs only, and no gate instantiates one.

*** DESIGN REVIEW 2026-09-10 (ppcrldimimask/codex_design_20260910.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max, 14,947 bytes, ZERO cyber flags): THE DEFECT PREMISE IS EXACT AND **MY PROPOSED REPAIR IS INSUFFICIENT**. ***

The post-decrement reading is confirmed exactly: the loop's final test evaluates the old value zero and then decrements to -1, **and this happens even for SH=0**, so the mask always covers architectural bits MB..63.  The rldimix RTL requires MASK(MB, 63-SH).

**BUT 'SAVE sh BEFORE THE LOOP AND KEEP THE MASK LOOP' -- which I filed as the durable repair -- LEAVES TWO MORE DEFECTS.**  Both come from the manual's own mask definition, which makes BOTH endpoints inclusive and WRAPS through bit 63 to bit 0 when the beginning exceeds the end:
  (1) the existing loop compares the INCREMENTED position against the inclusive endpoint, so where it terminates normally it **stops one bit early**;
  (2) it **never wraps**, so other operand combinations run past bit 63 and evaluate invalid shift counts -- an undefined-behaviour defect hiding inside the wrong-value one.

THE PRESCRIBED REPAIR is therefore four coordinated changes rather than one: preserve the decoded `sh', rotate with a separate counter (`int n = sh; while (n-- != 0)'), advance the mask position modulo 64 (`m = (m + 1) & 63'), and terminate on the position AFTER the endpoint, modulo 64 (`m != ((64 - sh) & 63)').

*A round that had taken my one-line framing would have shipped a fix that is still wrong at the endpoint and still undefined on the wrapping cases, and its detector -- built from the same framing -- would very likely have passed it.*

*** THE GATE CLAIM WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE.  I WROTE IT INTO THREE ROWS, A CHANGELOG BLOCK AND TWO COMMIT MESSAGES BEFORE A SEAT CHECKED IT (wiringcliff/codex_ppcgate_20260910.txt). ***

**I CLAIMED: 'no gate in this tree instantiates a 64-bit PowerPC CPU at all, so the whole 64-bit-only instruction group is invisible BY CONSTRUCTION.'  THE FIRST HALF IS FALSE.**  Gate 9 (gate_asan_sweep.sh) enumerates EVERY advertised machine type and subtype -- including bareppc, testppc and macppc/g5, all of which default to the PPC970 -- so 64-bit PowerPC CPUs ARE constructed by a gate today, and have been all along.

**THE CORRECT AND NARROWER FINDING: NO GATE CHECKS THEIR INSTRUCTION RESULTS.**  Gate 9 is a CONSTRUCTION check with no PowerPC result oracle; the two PowerPC gates both drive `macppc -e g4', an MPC7400, which is 32-bit, and their probes select it EXPLICITLY rather than by default.  So the defects were invisible because nothing EXECUTES these instructions and inspects the answer -- not because nothing builds the CPU.

*** THAT DISTINCTION IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN WITNESS LADDER, ONE LEVEL UP, AND I WALKED PAST IT. ***  The ladder's whole rung-2 clause says machine CONSTRUCTION proves presence and NOT reachability, and is a reproduction only for defects that construction itself executes.  I applied that rule carefully to witnesses all day and then made exactly the error it warns about when reasoning about GATES.  A gate that constructs a CPU is a rung-2 gate; these defects need a rung-3 one.

THE PRESCRIBED CLOSURE IS SMALLER THAN MY FRAMING SUGGESTED: wire the existing 19-row regress/ppc_rldicl_probe.py into gate_ppc.sh, asserting its score AND its completion sentinel.  That closes the missing instruction-result check.  **It does NOT close all 64-bit PowerPC coverage**, and the seat says so explicitly rather than letting the round claim it does.

*** DESIGNED 2026-09-10 (ppcrldimimask/codex_repair_20260910.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max, ZERO cyber flags).  MY PREMISES HELD AND MY CHARACTERISATION OF THE DEFECT WAS HALF OF IT. ***

CONFIRMED: `sh' is `-1' on exit for EVERY decoded SH including zero (the final test reads the old value, decrements, and exits), the rotate body IS a correct ROTL64, and the mask loop therefore always stops at `m == 64' and selects bits `MB..63'.  The architectural mask is `MASK(MB, 63-SH)', INCLUSIVE of both endpoints and WRAPPING -- RTL at `ppc_pem_32and64_2005.txt:29908' (`m <- MASK(b, ~n)'), endpoint prose at `:29909', mask definition at `:6879'.

*** THE ROW'S TITLE DESCRIBES ONLY THE NON-WRAPPING HALF.  The defect has TWO directions: ***
  * `MB <= 63-SH' (non-wrapping) -- it OVERWRITES the low SH destination bits that must survive;
  * `MB > 63-SH' (wrapping) -- it OMITS the required insertion into positions `0..63-SH', leaving
    those destination bits UNCHANGED.
A repair tested only on non-wrapping encodings fixes one and leaves the other.

**AND SAVING SH IS NOT ENOUGH -- THREE MORE EDITS ARE NEEDED, which is why my sketch was rejected.**  The comparison happens AFTER the increment, so the stopping position is the endpoint's SUCCESSOR, and the counter must be circular:

        int m, n = sh;                       /*  1: keep SH  */
        while (n-- != 0) { ... }             /*  2: consume the copy  */
        do {
                tmp |= ((uint64_t)1 << (63-m));
                m = (m + 1) & 63;            /*  3: circular increment  */
        } while (m != ((64 - sh) & 63));     /*  4: successor, modulo 64  */

**Changing only one of edits 3 and 4 does not repair the loop.**  A partial repair that saves SH and sets the bound to 24 at `MB=40, SH=40' while keeping `m ++' walks 40..63 and then enters the body with `m == 64', evaluating `(uint64_t)1 << -1'.  *** That is UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR, and the seat declined to call it an infinite loop on the ground that doing so would assign DEFINED behaviour to an undefined program -- which is the correct discipline and is what my brief's question got wrong. ***

WORKED CASE, usable as a row: `rldimi r4,r3,40,40' = instruction word **0x7864422e**, with `r3 = 0xffffffffffffffff' and `r4 = 0': the repaired loop visits 40..63 then 0..23, 48 iterations, mask **0xffffff0000ffffff**, which is also the correct result.  **The original handler produces 0x0000000000ffffff.**

MUTANT, one character, defined result: `64` -> `63` in the repaired bound.  `rldimi r4,r3,0,0' = **0x7864000c**, `r3 = ~0', `r4 = 0' gives correct `0xffffffffffffffff' and mutant `0xfffffffffffffffe' -- it drops the inclusive endpoint, architectural bit 63.

The seat validated its replacement against an independent bit-membership oracle over **40,960 cases** (every SH/MB pair x ten source/destination pairs), max loop count 64.  **It could NOT compile or run the emulator** -- no native compiler, and WSL returned `E_ACCESSDENIED' -- so this is a READING plus an offline model, not a measurement of this tree.  A measuring seat still owes the build.

rows.title: cpu_ppc_instr.c X(rlwimi): the 32-bit rotate is performed at 64-bit width in the 64-bit build, so HIGH-HALF source data leaks into the low 32 bits -- its two siblings truncate to uint32_t first and this one never does
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-10 from the [[ppcrldiclzero]] witness's sibling audit.  MEASURED, not read.

The handler takes its operands as MODE_uint_t and then rotates with a shift pair using 32-sh.  cpu_ppc.c defines DYNTRANS_DUALMODE_32, so the file is compiled TWICE and MODE_uint_t is **uint64_t** in the 64-bit build.  The architecture specifies a 32-bit rotate over the LOW half of the source -- **the high half plays no part whatsoever** -- but the right-shift pulls bits out of the high half straight into the low 32 bits, which is exactly where the mask lives.

MEASURED, source 0xAAAAAAAA0000000F, destination seeded 0x5A5A..., shift 4, full mask:
    got 0x5a5a5a5aaaaaaaf0    want 0x5a5a5a5a000000f0
The 0xAAAAAA is high-half data the architecture says cannot reach there.

ATTRIBUTION IS PINNED BY TWO COMPANION ROWS: rlwinm on the SAME source and shift is CORRECT, because it casts to uint32_t before rotating, and rlwimi at SH=0 is correct because the ternary short-circuits the rotate entirely.  **So the defect is the missing truncation in this one handler, not the shape of the rotate expression.**

*A row testing this is VACUOUS unless the source's two halves DIFFER: the seat's own first draft used an all-ones source, under which a 64-bit rotate and a true 32-bit one agree bit for bit, and it corrected the row rather than shipping it green.*

ADJACENT, NOT A DEFECT BUT WORTH RECORDING so a round does not rediscover it: rldic, rldcl and rldcr are NOT IMPLEMENTED AT ALL -- the decoder's default swallows them.  rldic in particular is documented and compiler-emitted.

*** DESIGN REVIEW 2026-09-10: THE WIDTH PREMISE HOLDS AND **TRUNCATION ALONE IS NOT THE FIX**. ***

Casting the source to `uint32_t' before the rotate is necessary and not sufficient.  The prescribed repair splits the combined declaration -- `uint32_t tmp = (uint32_t)reg(...)' with the destination kept at the mode-dependent width -- **and additionally handles the WRAPPING mask**, because the manual's mask wraps when the beginning exceeds the end: `if (mb > me) ra = (ra & 0xffffffffULL) | ((uint64_t)tmp << 32);' AFTER the rotation and BEFORE the existing mask loop.

*** AND A NEW FINDING THAT CONTRADICTS THE EARLIER SIBLING AUDIT: `rlwinm' AND `rlwnm' ARE NOT UNIVERSALLY CORRECT. ***  The witness measured them green on the cases it drove and the audit recorded them as correct; the design review says that is true of those cases and not of the handlers.  **A measured-green sample is not a proof of correctness**, which is this project's own reading-versus- measurement distinction cutting the other way for once -- the measurement was right about what it measured and the GENERALISATION from it was mine.  Re-check both before either is called clean, and do not let this row's fix be copied to them on the strength of the audit.

*** THE GATE CLAIM WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE.  I WROTE IT INTO THREE ROWS, A CHANGELOG BLOCK AND TWO COMMIT MESSAGES BEFORE A SEAT CHECKED IT (wiringcliff/codex_ppcgate_20260910.txt). ***

**I CLAIMED: 'no gate in this tree instantiates a 64-bit PowerPC CPU at all, so the whole 64-bit-only instruction group is invisible BY CONSTRUCTION.'  THE FIRST HALF IS FALSE.**  Gate 9 (gate_asan_sweep.sh) enumerates EVERY advertised machine type and subtype -- including bareppc, testppc and macppc/g5, all of which default to the PPC970 -- so 64-bit PowerPC CPUs ARE constructed by a gate today, and have been all along.

**THE CORRECT AND NARROWER FINDING: NO GATE CHECKS THEIR INSTRUCTION RESULTS.**  Gate 9 is a CONSTRUCTION check with no PowerPC result oracle; the two PowerPC gates both drive `macppc -e g4', an MPC7400, which is 32-bit, and their probes select it EXPLICITLY rather than by default.  So the defects were invisible because nothing EXECUTES these instructions and inspects the answer -- not because nothing builds the CPU.

*** THAT DISTINCTION IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN WITNESS LADDER, ONE LEVEL UP, AND I WALKED PAST IT. ***  The ladder's whole rung-2 clause says machine CONSTRUCTION proves presence and NOT reachability, and is a reproduction only for defects that construction itself executes.  I applied that rule carefully to witnesses all day and then made exactly the error it warns about when reasoning about GATES.  A gate that constructs a CPU is a rung-2 gate; these defects need a rung-3 one.

THE PRESCRIBED CLOSURE IS SMALLER THAN MY FRAMING SUGGESTED: wire the existing 19-row regress/ppc_rldicl_probe.py into gate_ppc.sh, asserting its score AND its completion sentinel.  That closes the missing instruction-result check.  **It does NOT close all 64-bit PowerPC coverage**, and the seat says so explicitly rather than letting the round claim it does.

*** DESIGNED 2026-09-10 (ppcrldimimask/codex_repair_20260910.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max, ZERO cyber flags), AND IT FOUND A SECOND DEFECT AT THIS SITE THAT I HAD NOT SEEN.  MY 'ONE-TOKEN CAST' PREMISE IS REFUTED. ***

The width contamination is confirmed exactly as filed: for `1 <= SH <= 31' the erroneous expression's low word is `correct_rot32(L, SH) | ((H << SH) & 0xffffffff)', and the existing low-word mask can select those bits.  `SH == 0' bypasses the shift expression and is clean.

*** THE SECOND DEFECT: WHEN `MB > ME' THE ARCHITECTURAL MASK WRAPS ACROSS THE 64-BIT BOUNDARY AND COVERS THE ENTIRE HIGH HALF, so RA's high 32 bits must be REPLACED with the rotated word -- and this implementation preserves them unconditionally. ***  `ROTL32(x, y)' is defined as rotating `x || x', the low word DUPLICATED (`ppc_pem_32and64_2005.txt:17143'), and the rlwimi RTL at `:29989' combines that with `MASK(MB+32, ME+32)'.  The wrapping mask visits `MB+32..63, 0..ME+32' -- which includes every architectural position `0..31'.

    MB <= ME   high 32 mask bits all ZERO  -> preserve old RA      (what the code does)
    MB >  ME   high 32 mask bits all ONE   -> replace with rot word (what the code never does)

**So the repair is narrowing AND a high-word insertion**, and it must sit after the rotation and before the loop mutates `mb':

        uint32_t tmp = (uint32_t)reg(ic->arg[0]);
        MODE_uint_t ra = reg(ic->arg[1]);
        ...
        tmp = sh ? ((tmp << sh) | (tmp >> (32-sh))) : tmp;
        /*  A wrapping MASK(MB+32, ME+32) includes the high word.  */
        if (mb > me)
                ra = (ra & 0xffffffffULL) | ((uint64_t)tmp << 32);

In the 32-bit compilation the conversion back to `MODE_uint_t' discards that high half, so the existing behaviour there is unchanged.

MUTANT, one character: `>' -> `<' in the new condition.  `rlwimi r4,r3,0,31,0' = **0x506407c0**, `r3 = 0xaaaaaaaa0000000f', `r4 = 0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a' gives correct `0x0000000f5a5a5a5b' and mutant `0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5b' -- the low-word insertion succeeds and the high-word replacement is skipped.

TERMINATION PROVED rather than assumed: both fields are masked `& 31', `mb' is reset to 0 on reaching 32, positions are `(b+k) mod 32', and ME is processed after `((ME-b+32) % 32) + 1' bodies -- between 1 and 32.  Every shift count `31-mb' is in range.

ROUND SCOPE: **TWO rounds, not one**, with [[ppcrldimimask]].  Same file and family, but one repairs operand lifetime and a circular inclusive traversal while the other repairs source width and a missing high-word insertion, and validating the second needs word-duplication and high-half expectations that lie outside the doubleword detector's contract.

Validated offline over **655,360 cases** (every SH/MB/ME at both widths x ten operand pairs).  **Not compiled** -- the seat had no native compiler and WSL returned `E_ACCESSDENIED'.

rows.title: cpu_mips_instr.c X(ext): EXT requires a properly sign-extended 32-bit source and nothing checks it -- a SECOND restriction, independent of the shift-count range that [[mipsextshift]] closes
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-10 from the [[mipsextshift]] design review (mipsextshift/codex_guards_RETRY_20260910.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max), which found it while answering a question about something else and said so explicitly: *"The proposed range checks do not address that separate condition."*

MIPS64 Volume II states the restriction on EXT's page (mips64_volII.txt:746) and reflects it in the instruction's operation section (`:750'): the source register must hold a properly sign-extended 32-bit value.  `X(ext)' reads `uint32_t rs = reg(ic->arg[1]);' -- it TRUNCATES to 32 bits and asks nothing about the upper half, so a 64-bit register holding a value that is not a sign-extension of its low word is accepted and extracted from silently.

**WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY RATHER THAN FOLDED INTO [[mipsextshift]]:** that row's guards are a DECODE-time predicate over two instruction fields, decidable when the instruction is translated. This one is a RUN-time property of a register value, so it cannot be checked in the decoder at all and needs a different fix shape.  Same instruction, different site, different mechanism -- the round-scope rule's same-fix-design condition fails.

SEVERITY IS LOW AND THE REASON IS WORTH RECORDING: this is UNPREDICTABLE-on-violation like the range case, but unlike the range case it causes **no undefined behaviour in the host** -- the truncation is well-defined C.  The cost is a wrong guest answer in a state a correct guest does not reach, not a host fault.

NOT MEASURED, no witness, and it inherits [[mipsextshift]]'s blocker: EXT is MIPS32 Release 2, so no machine in this tree has yet been named that executes it.

rows.title: dev_dreamcast_maple.c maple_do_dma_xfer(): the DMA address is advanced past the command list and the file flags its own uncertainty about it in a comment -- `// TODO: Should the DMA address be updated?'
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-10, split out of [[mapledmaaddr]] so that row can proceed.  **The two are on DIFFERENT SITES and only one of them is that round's.**

`maple_do_dma_xfer()' walks the command list accumulating `addr += datalen_cmd * 4;' per command, and at its tail -- immediately before asserting SYSASIC_EVENT_MAPLE_DMADONE -- does:

        // TODO: Should the DMA address be updated?
        d->dmaaddr = addr;

So an advancing cursor IS modelled, and the author recorded that they did not know whether it should be.  **The comment is the finding**: this is not a defect anyone has established, it is an unresolved semantic question sitting in shipped code with no test either way.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: real Maple hardware behaviour for a read of the DMA address register after a completed transfer.  No Dreamcast or Maple documentation is present in `_scratchpad/` -- checked by `ls`, not assumed -- so this needs a source obtained first, on the vmesbcp2 / 21066 / ddi0406 precedent where a seat's citation was fetched and then VERIFIED LOCALLY rather than trusted.

**TWO EARLY RETURNS LEAVE THE FUNCTION BEFORE THE TAIL** and are part of the same question: the `!d->enable' path and the `addr & 0x1f' alignment refusal both return without touching `d->dmaaddr', so after an aborted transfer the field holds the PROGRAMMED address while after a completed one it holds the advanced address.  Whatever contract is settled has to cover both.

*** DO NOT LET THIS BLOCK [[mapledmaaddr]]. ***  That round deletes a terminating call in the register's READ arm, which is a pure reporter of this field -- it neither creates nor resolves the question above, and the same unverified address is ALREADY handed to the DMA engine on every transfer whether or not a guest ever reads it back.  The dependency runs the other way: whatever is settled here becomes the expected value of that round's disclosed after-DMA row, which is why that row is written to pin the READ ARM'S contract rather than to certify the advanced value.

*** ARITHMETIC CORRECTED 2026-09-10 (mapledmaaddr/codex_readarm_20260910.txt) BEFORE ANYONE BUILT ON IT. ***  This row first described the advance as `addr += datalen_cmd * 4' per command.  **That is one of three terms.**  Each descriptor advances the local cursor by 8 bytes of control words, 4 bytes of command word, and `4 * datalen_cmd' of data, so the committed value is

        C = (P + SUM over descriptors of (12 + 4*D_i))  mod 2^32

Two consequences for whoever settles the hardware contract: **the sum is modulo 2^32, so "advanced" does not imply numerically larger**, and `C != P' is not guaranteed in general -- so a test asserting merely that the value CHANGED is weaker than it looks.

**AND THE EARLY-EXIT DESCRIPTION IN [[mapledmaaddr]] WAS WRONG in a way that matters here:** an early return preserves the field's ENTRY value, which may be a PRIOR transfer's cursor -- it does not restore a programmed address.  The `!d->enable' test also precedes the alignment test, so a disabled and unaligned address never reaches the alignment diagnostic.  Any contract settled for this row has to cover the entry-value case, not just "programmed" versus "advanced".

Also relevant to the eventual policy: an alternative length calculation from the CONTROL word sits COMMENTED OUT beside the executable one, so the file records that its author considered a second arithmetic and chose this one.

rows.title: cpu_ppc_instr.c X(rlwinm) and X(rlwnm): a WRAPPING mask (MB > ME) selects the whole high half under the manual's RTL, and both handlers zero it instead -- but the manual CONTRADICTS ITSELF on this point and the dispute is unresolved
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-10 from the [[ppcrlwimiwidth]] design review (ppcrldimimask/codex_repair_20260910.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max).  **It arrived as a refutation of MY OWN premise**: I had told the seat that these two siblings are the CORRECT idiom that `rlwimi' fails to follow.  They are correct about the low word and, on the RTL reading, wrong about the high one.

THE MECHANISM, verified locally by reading both the decoder and the handlers rather than taking the seat's word:
  * the decoder (`case PPC_HI6_RLWNM: case PPC_HI6_RLWINM:') builds a **32-bit** mask with a correct wrap -- `mask |= ((uint32_t)0x80000000 >> mb); ... mb ++; mb &= 31;' -- so the LOW word is right including the `MB > ME' case;
  * `X(rlwinm)' holds `tmp' as `uint32_t' and ends `reg(ic->arg[0]) = tmp;'.  **Assigning a uint32_t into a 64-bit register ZERO-EXTENDS**, so the high half is unconditionally 0.

Under the RTL the high half is not free to be zero: `ROTL32(x, y)' is defined as rotating `x || x' -- the low word DUPLICATED (`ppc_pem_32and64_2005.txt:17143') -- and `MASK(MB+32, ME+32)' with `MB > ME' wraps to cover `MB+32..63' AND `0..ME+32', the second range including every architectural position `0..31'.  So the high half should receive the rotated word.  Worked case from the seat: `rlwinm' with source `0xaaaaaaaa0000000f', SH=0, MB=31, ME=0 gives RTL `0x0000000f00000001' against the tree's `0x0000000000000001'.  The same applies to `rlwnm' when the register shift's low five bits are zero.

*** THE REASON THIS IS FILED AS A DISPUTE AND NOT AS A DEFECT: THE MANUAL CONTRADICTS ITSELF, AND THE SEAT SAID SO ITSELF RATHER THAN LETTING ITS READING STAND UNQUALIFIED. ***  `ppc_pem_32and64_2005.txt:30065' asserts blanket upper-half CLEARING for `rlwinm', which conflicts with that instruction's own RTL and with the general duplicated-rotation / wrapping-mask definitions when `MB > ME'.  The seat followed the RTL and flagged the conflict; **this row does not adopt either reading.**

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, in preference order: a second PowerPC manual in `_scratchpad/` (three more are present -- `ppc_oea_book3_v201', `ppc_pem32_rev2_2001', `ppc_vea_book2_v201' -- and none has been consulted on this point); then real hardware behaviour; then what other emulators and compilers assume.  **Compiler output is the strong practical argument either way**: if compilers emit wrapping-mask `rlwinm' expecting the high half cleared, the tree's behaviour is what software depends on whatever the RTL says.

*** DO NOT LET THIS BLOCK [[ppcrlwimiwidth]]'s NARROWING HALF. ***  That round's FIRST defect -- high-half SOURCE bits leaking into the low word through `tmp >> (32-sh)' at 64-bit width -- is independent of this dispute and is wrong under every reading.  Only its high-half INSERTION half depends on how this resolves.

rows.title: harness: the #522 witness's rldimi oracle returns ZERO for every wrapping mask and its mask32 omits the high half -- so the two filed sibling rows rest on oracles that cannot certify their own repairs
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-10 from the [[ppcrldimimask]] design review, which named the defect and the line; **both halves were then verified locally by opening the file before this was written.**

`regress/artifacts/ppcrldiclzero/opus_ppc_rldicl_witness_20260910.py' is a COMMITTED artifact of `#522' (`e777ff0').  Two of its model oracles are wrong for WRAPPING masks:

  * `want_rldimi()' computes `m = mask_b_63(mb) & mask_0_e((63 - sh) & 63)' -- the INTERSECTION of `bits mb..63' with `bits 0..63-sh'.  That is the correct mask when `mb <= 63-sh'.  When `mb > 63-sh' **the two ranges are disjoint and the intersection is EMPTY**, so the oracle returns the untouched destination for every wrapping encoding.  Its own docstring shows how it happened: it cites the manual's PROSE (*"1 bits from bit MB through bit 63 - SH"*), which describes the non-wrapping reading, rather than the `MASK' definition that wraps.
  * `mask32()' is documented *"confined to the low 32 bits"* and sets only `1 << (31 - b)'.  Its companion `rotl32()' correctly returns the DUPLICATED `(r32 << 32) | r32', so the model has the duplication and then masks it away -- the high half a wrapping word mask requires is never selected.

*** THIS DOES NOT INVALIDATE `#522'. ***  That round is `rldicl', which uses neither oracle, and its 190-cell census and 24-row detector are untouched.  The exposure is FORWARD: [[ppcrldimimask]] and [[ppcrlwimiwidth]] are filed on measurements this witness produced, and **the wrapping encodings are exactly where both repairs do their new work** -- so an uncorrected oracle would score a correct repair as wrong, or agree with a repair that fixes only the non-wrapping half.

**THE SHAPE IS ONE THIS PROJECT HAS NAMED BEFORE: a check that cannot fail.**  A wrapping-mask row scored against `want_rldimi()' compares an implementation that omits the wrap against an oracle that omits the wrap, and passes.  *The oracle and the defect share the same misreading of the same sentence.*

OWED BEFORE EITHER SIBLING ROUND MEASURES ANYTHING: correct both oracles to the wrapping `MASK' definition, and add a row at a wrapping encoding that is RED on the committed build -- the order discriminator, so the correction cannot be mistaken for fitting the oracle to a repair.

rows.title: cpu_ppc.c update_cr0(): the comparison width is chosen from the CPU MODEL width (cpu->cd.ppc.bits) rather than from the current operating mode, so a 64-bit CPU running with SF=0 records 64-bit condition bits
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-10 from the [[ppcrldimimask]] design review, which raised it as a limitation on its own repairs rather than as the thing it was asked about.  **Verified locally by opening the function.**

`update_cr0()' branches on `if (cpu->cd.ppc.bits == 64)' and compares `(int64_t)value', else `(int32_t)value'.  `cpu->cd.ppc.bits' is a property of the configured CPU MODEL and does not change while the guest runs.  The manual requires the comparison to follow the current MODE (`ppc_pem_32and64_2005.txt:6357'), which on a 64-bit implementation is selected by the MSR SF bit and CAN change at run time.

So on a 64-bit CPU executing in 32-bit mode, a record-form result whose low word is negative but whose full 64-bit value is positive records GT where the architecture requires LT.

**SCOPE IS THE WHOLE RECORD FORM, NOT ONE INSTRUCTION**: every `_dot' handler in the tree routes through this one function, which is why it is filed on its own rather than inside either PowerPC rotate row.  The seat's own statement of the consequence is the honest bound to carry forward: *those repairs do not establish correct record-form behaviour on a 64-bit CPU operating with SF=0.*

LOW because reachability is unestablished in the sharpest way: it needs a 64-bit PowerPC CPU running with SF clear, and this tree has no gate that executes ANY 64-bit PowerPC instruction and checks the result -- see [[wiringcliff]].  A round here owes the mode plumbing first, and should check whether `cpu->cd.ppc.bits' is consulted this way anywhere else.

Amendment 2 (model the main-loop hat on `closure.by`, with roster validation) is ratified in the same decision and is tracked as `closurebyroster` -- ratified, not deferred. THE REAL CARRIER IS `ledgerclosureby`, whose title is "closure.by holds the WRONG KIND of value on two rows, and a role distinction THE ROSTER DOES NOT MODEL on ten more" -- i.e. it already covers both halves of this amendment (the main-loop hat and roster validation). state_semantics._WHY: The ledger's schema had NO WRITTEN SEMANTICS. That single absence is the cause behind six mis-counts in one session, two file-reading seats reading OPPOSITE conventions into one closure string, and five seats agreeing on only 4 of 11 rows they were asked to state-check. A field every round ranks and closes from was never defined.
state_semantics._THE_QUESTION_state_ANSWERS: Is anything still owed on this row, and who acts next?
state_semantics._TENSE: *** `state` IS PRESENT-TENSE; `closure.note` IS PAST-TENSE. *** The note is an EVENT LOG of what happened to a STAGE ('CLOSE (assess)' closes the assess stage). `state` asserts what the ROW still owes. **They are independent BY DESIGN** -- 23 rows share the string `CLOSE (assess)` across three states, and that is the ledger working correctly, not a defect: rows that experienced the same stage event legitimately differ in what else they owe. NEITHER can be derived from the other, and both attempts to do so have been measured wrong.
state_semantics.closed: Nothing outstanding; the claim was discharged BY WORK. Mechanical companions, era-scoped: commits, closure.by, and witness if closed on/after 2026-08-19.
state_semantics.dropped: Nothing outstanding; the claim was retired WITHOUT work, with the reason. Confusing this with `closed` is the es438 class -- both mean 'nothing owed', and misstating WHY is what misleads a future reader.
state_semantics.held: Something outstanding, waiting on a NAMED party or event, and carrying the QUESTION it is held for (standing rule). `open`/`held` WITH commits is normal here.
state_semantics._NOT_DERIVABLE_FROM: closure.note, entries, or stage coverage. Establishing a row's state requires a SUBSTANCE READ -- commits, gates, holds, filed questions -- which is what `asicbadaddr` was closed from and is the template.
state_semantics.open: Something outstanding, UNCLAIMED -- the complement of `in work`'s 'actively claimed'. No named party is required (that is `held`) and no work is under way. *** THIS DEFINITION WAS MISSING FROM THE BLOCK UNTIL 2026-08-25, AND `open` IS THE SECOND-LARGEST STATE IN THE LEDGER (46 of 216 rows). *** It appeared only inside `held`'s prose. Found by the fable5 adjudicator when asked to ratify the block -- it was told plainly that ratification was not wanted and to check the premises, and the gap is what that instruction bought. A checker built on the block as written would have misclassified a fifth of the ledger while reporting full coverage, which is this project's own 'a detector built from the wrong census reports full coverage' class wearing schema clothes.
state_semantics._RETROACTIVE_OR_FORWARD_ONLY: *** THE FIRST DRAFT SAID FORWARD-ONLY FLAT, AND THAT WAS HALF RIGHT IN THE LOAD-BEARING HALF. *** The split is by LAYER, and the block's own _TENSE ruling decides it: **the MEANING binds retroactively; only MECHANICAL CHECKS are forward-only by date.** `state` is PRESENT-TENSE, and a present-tense field has no era -- a false state is false NOW. 'Pre-adoption rows are read charitably' would preserve the exact defect this block exists to end (the es438 reader reads 'not done' off shipped, witnessed work TODAY) and would keep the ledger permanently bilingual. Forward-only enforcement follows the boilerplate-check precedent: a rule that retro-fails the archive gets disabled, and a disabled rule protects nothing. *** THE DISHONESTY WORRY DISSOLVES ONCE THE LAYERS ARE SEPARATED: `state` is a LIVE FIELD, NOT HISTORY. *** Correcting it rewrites no history -- `entries`, notes and `commits` are untouched. The migration is the warranted in-place repair already used twice on 2026-08-25: correct the state cell and attach a warrant note naming the row's OWN evidence. NO BULK REWRITE -- the round's central finding stands (state is NOT derivable; five seats agreed on only 4 of 11 rows), so every remaining row gets a substance read.
